2009-1.sentence: ADHD in a child is rarely a solo act: anxiety and learning trouble often join the room as the child, parent, and teacher keep trading “can’t sit still” for “won’t try,” so stomachaches and decoding failure stay unseen. Treat the relational loop—who is scared, who is ashamed of reading—or the stimulant win will leave the pair still organizing around avoidance.

2009-2.sentence: Adolescence is the stage of massive synaptic pruning plus falling glucose/oxygen use and smaller EEG amplitude, so insight work should stay modest while impulse and planning are still being remodeled. Support the ego’s new capacities; deep uncovering outruns a mind that can look adult in spots and still cannot hold a plan.

2009-3.sentence: In borderline relatedness the same person cannot stay both needed and dangerous, so after a fight the coworker is no longer a mixed figure but an all-bad persecutor and a brief psychotic story fills the gap. Sleep and cooling the abandonment storm let the good and bad pieces sit in one relationship again, which is why the plot talk can vanish without a primary psychotic illness.

2009-4.sentence: Denial is at work when the floor treats metoclopramide as “just nausea medicine” and then calls psychiatry for the tongue thrust and torticollis as if they were conversion. Naming the defense lets the consult stop interpreting the neck and instead reverse the D2 blockade that produced the dystonia.

2009-5.sentence: Thomas and Chess’s difficult child already brings intense mood and irregular sleep and meals into the visit, and the parents and clinician start repeating that same high-volume, poorly timed rhythm—talking over each other, rushing transitions, leaving the room dysregulated. The work is to notice that two-person replay and slow the tempo rather than treat the loudness as badness or low IQ.

2009-6.sentence: Pervasive insomnia is a vertical split: the daytime self still only has old passive death wishes, while the unsleeping night self is agitated, hopeless, and already holding the firearm. The person never left the chair, but the part that could wait for morning has gone offline, which is why this sleep collapse predicts emergent suicidality more than male sex or age over 65.

2009-7.sentence: Haloperidol laryngospasm is the ego losing its most basic jobs—airway, voice, and voluntary control of the neck—in one acute dystonic burst. Benztropine is the anticholinergic that hands those functions back; lorazepam, propranolol, amantadine, and bromocriptine do not restore that motor self-control.

2009-8.sentence: The MMPI-2 has a hard stop: it maps major areas of psychopathologic functioning, not organicity, unconscious conflict, a cognitive battery, or a scored mental status. Ending the consult there is the same discipline as ending a session on time instead of asking the test to finish work it cannot rush.

2009-9.sentence: The useful trial comment is naming the staring spells and spike-and-wave as childhood absence, not as a gabapentin, phenytoin, or carbamazepine problem. Valproate is an adequate first medicine only after that seeing-the-syndrome step, including asking about morning myoclonus that still keeps valproate on the table.

2009-10.sentence: Fiduciary means the relationship’s job is to be based on trust, not on justice, a fee, acting as the patient’s agent, or a complete note. When a kickback tempts a treatment, that trust is the function being spent.

2009-11.sentence: Mother’s hospitalization and missed medicine drop this patient with schizophrenia onto Erikson’s earliest task—can daily functioning be trusted to hold—not onto insight or identity work. Supportive therapy’s goal is to restabilize that functioning and strengthen existing defenses, not to raise self-awareness, agree for self-esteem, or only fix the environment.

2009-12.sentence: Higher-level histrionic organization has a working conscience: seductiveness is subtly appealing rather than raw impulse, overestimated intimacy, or uncontained transference heat. That same guilt-and-limit capacity lets the patient reflect, keep reality testing, and feel mixed about the flirtation when you set a frame.

2009-13.sentence: The late-life ego that used to shift sets and hold a plan now stalls because the basal ganglia loops that time and sequence action never quite recover after small-vessel hits. Urinary urgency and a cautious gait are the body showing a developmental capacity that arrived decades ago and is now arriving late, or not at all, while recognition memory still works because the mesial temporal store was not the first to fail.

2009-14.sentence: The trunk that locks into lordosis and spasms at a sudden noise is repeating what cannot be put into words: antiglutamic acid decarboxylase antibodies have stripped GABA’s quieting, so unremembered threat lives in axial muscle instead of a story. EMG that spares distal nerve and a serum GAD antibody tell you the unrepresented state is central and autoimmune, not a peripheral cramp-fasciculation or myokymia you can dismiss as local wiring.

2009-15.sentence: When you hand hospital staff the General Health Questionnaire and ask them to tick their own distress, you are recruiting them to become the expert on themselves and you to become the distant tally clerk who never interviews. Notice the countertransference pull to trust a paper screen as if it were a Present State Examination or SADS sitting with you, when the GHQ only knows what the subject is willing to write.

2009-16.sentence: Number needed to treat is a competence mirror: five patients treated for one extra remission (40% versus 20%) is a number you can hold without inflating your worth or collapsing when the other four do not remit. Idealizing a p-value or a 95% interval as the prize misses the self-esteem that comes from knowing exactly how many people you must treat to produce one additional positive outcome.

2009-17.sentence: The wish to feel something in ten superficial wrist cuts collides with a death wish she half-owns (“easier if I were dead”), and recent alcohol abuse is the drive that melts the last prohibition so the cut can go deeper than she meant. Sexual-abuse history, borderline traits, or having never cut ten times before do not outrank that chemical disinhibition when you decide who needs the locked door tonight.

2009-18.sentence: Caffeine is the world’s everyday mood-altering substance; an ego that already cannot tolerate affect will use coffee, energy drink, and cola to prop alertness and then wonder why anxiety and insomnia will not settle. Screening only alcohol, nicotine, opiates, and benzos leaves the coping strategy that is actually running the day unnamed, so impulse control and sleep hygiene get treated as if they failed on their own.

2009-19.sentence: The fluent lecture about cars and computers is a vertical split: one stream of mind stays in the chair and talks facts, while the stream that would feel the other child’s face, pause, and trade turns is not online. That is not a shy child hiding; it is a mind that left the interpersonal field without leaving the room, so friendship fails even though language is intact.

2009-20.sentence: Lithium carbonate is not only an ion; it is the reliable adult who stays after a suicide attempt and becomes a chemical secure base the patient can protest toward instead of dying. Prescribe it as proximity you can count on—blood levels, clinic visits, the same bottle—so the person does not have to use death to regulate when the mood drops.

2009-21.sentence: The caretaker and the 0.25 mg of risperidone together produced the rigidity and extra confusion: two people plus a neuroleptic made a dyad the Lewy body brain cannot metabolize. Stop treating the pair as “patient plus drug error” and read the new parkinsonism as the relationship announcing that this cortex cannot hold dopamine blockade the way other dementias can.

2009-22.sentence: When OCD arrives in bursts with bipolar mood, do not excavate every contamination thought as if the ego can use uncovering; support first, stabilize sleep and mood, then decide how much ritual talk this mind can metabolize. Technique follows prognosis: episodic, mood-tied rituals need containing structure more than interpretation until the bipolar swing is quieter.

2009-23.sentence: Case-control starts with the damaged baby (Ebstein’s anomaly) and looks backward for the pill, so good and bad are already split: the “case” mother is the bad object and the control mother is the good one you hope was unexposed. The design itself holds the pair—anomaly vs no anomaly—and asks which relationship to a psychotropic made the difference, which is why it fits a rare heart lesion better than a cohort you wait years to watch.

2009-24.sentence: Choosing clozapine after other antipsychotics fail is suppression in action: the team names the suicide risk, then deliberately puts it aside long enough to run ANC checks and stay with the one drug that actually lowers death. That is not denial of schizophrenia; it is the ego using a weekly lab ritual to keep dying thoughts from running the treatment.

2009-25.sentence: When parents bring the invisible friend into the consult as a problem, they are already asking you to join a two-person drama about who is allowed to play. Name the friend as ordinary preschool make-believe so the family does not have to enact a medical crisis around a healthy 4-year-old’s companion.

2009-26.sentence: The needle on the tray can split the recovering heroin user: one part sits for labs, another is already back in the vein. Treat the craving as a classically conditioned flash, not as proof they secretly decided to use, so the split can be talked about instead of acted.

2009-27.sentence: Amphetamine can blow out the ego’s hold on reality testing, so flashing computer messages feel like real threats and a knife feels like self-care. Until that state settles, you contain agitation and weapon talk; you do not interpret the messages as if the observing ego were still online.

2009-28.sentence: Pramipexole-driven gambling and hypersexuality do not wait for a planned ending; the dopamine agonist has already removed the brake. The work is a firm limit—name the drug, stop or change it, and do not treat the new appetites as a character flaw you can interpret away while the agonist is still on.

2009-29.sentence: Delirium tremens at 36 hours after the bleed is not a moment for a trial comment about drinking or insight. Psychological mindedness returns only after benzos, vitals, and seizure care restore a mind that can hear a remark.

2009-30.sentence: Binge–purge can live in a split: the person sits in clinic while another part is already at the toilet, and the ECG’s QT and T-wave changes are the body keeping the score. Do not treat those cardiac findings as abstract labs; they are the dissociated purge arriving in the tracing.

2009-31.sentence: When the student says schizophrenia means “split personality,” the room is already repeating Bleuler’s original split-of-associations versus a popular identity-split; the resident who only snaps “wrong” joins that split instead of holding both histories. Name the enactment: you and the student are dividing Bleuler from DID the way the word itself got divided in culture.

2009-32.sentence: Asking yesterday’s breakfast is a recent-memory probe; treating the blank as “they’re not trying” is denial of the clock you just set with attention tasks. Humor about a forgotten bagel can hide the same defense: joking away that recent memory failed after digits were intact.

2009-33.sentence: At three weeks, sleep and appetite already took the 20 mg citalopram as a feed; hiking the dose or stacking lithium/mirtazapine now can feel like a demand that the remaining dysphoria prove the pill is poison. Waiting at the same dose is the relationship move: the medicine is still being metabolized as hope, not as a verdict.

2009-34.sentence: The limit that grows preschool vocabulary is not SES, daycare count, or extra languages—it is how much talk is directed at this child, a frame of time and address caregivers either hold or outsource. Naming that boundary ethically: word growth is not a fee the family pays with status, but minutes of speech they can still give.

2009-35.sentence: Late arrivals and one-word CBT answers are data on alliance, the factor most tied to outcome—not on whether you recited the manual. A trial comment—“does this work even feel like yours?”—tests if they can see their part in the stall instead of only taking more homework.

2009-36.sentence: Eight admissions, three weeks max in board-and-care, garbage-can meals: this is not a termination you can rush with a clinic slot or a family lecture. ACT is the limit that goes to the street; clozapine, CBT, or ECT cannot end the cycle if the frame still expects him to arrive and stay.

2009-37.sentence: Alogia here is speech that names almost nothing—white, things, I am—so the interviewer’s job is to hold the dread of an empty mind without stuffing it with extra questions. You contain (take in the raw feeling and give it back in a thinkable form) the poverty of thought by reflecting how little can be said, rather than chasing a hidden sentence that was never formed.

2009-38.sentence: Premature ejaculation so often hits as a competence injury: the man feels he cannot last long enough to be a good lover, so shame, not desire, starts running the bedroom. A self-psychological stance mirrors that he is still a sexual person whose timing failed him, instead of confirming the collapse of self-esteem that makes him avoid partners.

2009-39.sentence: Personality change plus early backward falls and dysphagia is progressive supranuclear palsy stripping motor and frontal capacities, not a midlife wish colliding with a prohibition. Name the neurologic loss so family guilt (“we should have set firmer limits”) does not get treated as if character were the disease.

2009-40.sentence: Oxytocin is the animal signal that a mother’s caregiving can feel worth idealizing: the infant’s presence lights a biologic “I can do this” rather than a mere hormone trick. Teach that bonding still needs a caregiver who can be used as a competent, soothing other; the peptide does not replace that selfobject function.

2009-41.sentence: In Charles Bonnet syndrome the blind field is a nameless void; formed people and animals arrive as if the mind evacuated emptiness into pictures it can almost think. Contain the fear of “going mad” by naming macular-degeneration hallucinations with preserved insight, so the images become a known sensory leftover instead of a nameless dread.

2009-42.sentence: Charcoal cannot bind lithium because the ion is not a carbon-loving organic pill; the overdose stays in the body until kidneys or dialysis move it. The un-absorbable salt is the point of the emergency: you do not pretend the usual gut ritual metabolized what never attaches.

2009-43.sentence: The wish is to keep last night’s terror and confusion inside the story of the self; herpes encephalitis plus seizures have stripped the hippocampus’s capacity to bind that wish, so the prohibition is not repression but missing memory—no EEG change, intact clock drawing, and “I slept well.” Treat the amnestic gap as an ego-function failure, not a forbidden impulse the patient is refusing to confess.

2009-44.sentence: The frame is diagnostic honesty: you do not treat cartoon-soldier visions as a psychosis ticket that would lock the patient into antipsychotics and a schizophrenia narrative. Conversion hallucinations stay childish and fantastic so the symptom can speak without becoming a second diagnosis you then have to “manage” with drugs and a locked unit.

2009-45.sentence: Quetiapine 12.5 mg bid is not a permanent feed that proves the nursing-home patient still needs chemical control after the hitting stopped. OBRA’s every-three-month taper attempt is the relationship’s limit: you keep offering less pill so staff cannot use the antipsychotic as proof the resident is still dangerous.

2009-46.sentence: Naltrexone’s baseline and eight-week LFTs mark a time you cannot rush: the liver has to declare whether the anti-craving drug is tolerable before you call the trial a success. Ending or holding the prescription waits on that second lab, not on the patient’s wish to be “done” with alcohol or with being monitored.

2009-47.sentence: A five-year-old who says Mom is watching from the sky after the crash is using the only insight his age allows—not a trial interpretation of denial you would offer an adult. Psychological mindedness here is the child’s concrete afterlife story; you listen for play and sleep, you do not confront him as if he should already see death the way you do.

2009-48.sentence: The double bind is class and loyalty as a third in the room: go to college (become someone else) and do not spend the family’s money (stay our child). Betty cannot obey both messages without betraying either mobility or the household that cannot afford her leaving.

2009-49.sentence: The cocaine crash on the ward is an identity-versus-role-confusion crisis: the pill and the high had been doing the work of “who I am,” and two days off stimulant the ego is left with despair, sleep, hunger, and vivid dreams. Asking for double portions is the leftover oral claim on the hospital as a stand-in self after the borrowed energy is gone.

2009-50.sentence: Weekly unexpected panic with a clean medical workup is often an unremembered state repeating in the body: no scene, just a storm. Fluoxetine first-line is not “covering the trauma”; it quiets the autonomic replay so something that never had words can later be thought instead of only felt.

2009-51.sentence: The migraine patient recruits you to be the rescuer who aborts *this* attack—sumatriptan—not the long-haul preventer who offers propranolol, valproate, or topiramate. Your countertransference urgency to “just stop it” is the same pull; name it so you do not confuse one dose of a triptan with a prevention plan.

2009-52.sentence: Lifetime prevalence is a snapshot of people who *ever* had the illness; it is a bigger, older self-story than point or 12-month rates. Knowing that definition is a competence/mirroring move in journal club: you do not inflate your (or the field’s) self-esteem by comparing numbers that are not the same kind of “how common.”

2009-53.sentence: Lithium was the first psych drug whose wish (calm, evenness) had to collide with a prohibition you can measure in blood. The level is the conflict made concrete: take enough to treat, not enough to poison kidney and thyroid.

2009-54.sentence: The small lid and the pupil that gapes more in the dark are the symptom’s meaning: sympathetic tone dropped at the superior cervical ganglion, not a pons, midbrain, or third-nerve story. The body is showing a cut fight-or-flight cable, not asking you to treat a brainstem stroke.

2009-55.sentence: The neighbor-poisoning conviction sits on a collapse of basic trust (Erikson’s first task): the world next door is no longer safe enough to leave, so the day is spent at the window and the night is spent awake. Empathy without arguing the delusion is how you become a usable other—someone who can be leaned on while trust in the neighbor, and in one’s own perception, is still wrecked.

2009-56.sentence: Hippocrates’ four humors (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile) moved “mental disease” out of a purely moral ledger—sin, vice, a harsh conscience that must be punished—and into a bodily imbalance that a physician could treat. Black bile as the ancestor of melancholia is the historical reminder that we still risk treating depression as a character defect rather than a state that needs care.

2009-57.sentence: Megadosing pyridoxine to “fend off Alzheimer” is a concrete, almost childlike bid to control aging when the adult capacity to bear an uncertain future has not quite come online. The burning dysesthesias of B6 neuropathy then become the body’s reply: a sensory lesson that this magical prophylaxis cannot stand in for a more grown-up way of facing cognitive decline.

2009-58.sentence: Jung’s introversion/extroversion names how a person holds good and bad: energy turned toward inner objects and inner scenes, or toward people and events outside. Calling a quiet patient “introverted” in Jung’s sense is only fair if you mean that inward object-world, not that they have split off the outer other as dangerous or worthless.

2009-59.sentence: In bulimia nervosa the mind that asks “will therapy work?” can usually use a structured, here-and-now method more than deep uncovering: CBT targets regular eating, binge–purge cycles, and rigid food and shape rules. Save exploratory or psychoanalytic work for later, if at all; first give a technique with evidence this ego can actually use.

2009-60.sentence: A forensic fee that is a percentage of the plaintiff’s award ties the psychiatrist’s worth and “ideal expert” shine to the size of the win, so the evaluator needs the examinee to be damaged. Flat, hourly, or retainer pay keeps self-esteem in competence and honesty, not in mirroring a victory.

2009-61.sentence: The mid-session drift is not just boredom; it is the hour pouring a raw, unnameable feeling into you so it does not have to stay inside the patient (Bion’s evacuation). Your first job is to sit with that sleepy, wandering state long enough to name it in yourself—containment—before you speak, apologize, or cut the session short.

2009-62.sentence: An 8-year-old’s school performance has a real time-limit: you cannot substitute a toddler Denver screen or a broad developmental battery for what the child has actually learned. The WRAT respects that limit by measuring current reading and arithmetic achievement rather than rushing past the school-age task.

2009-63.sentence: After a lithium overdose, insight will not reverse a cerebellar lesion; the lasting story of the toxicity is incoordination, dysarthria, and a wide gait. Psychological mindedness still matters for why the overdose happened, but the cerebellum is the structure that may keep a permanent mark.

2009-64.sentence: A 24-hour crash into anxiety, insomnia, tremor, and a tonic-clonic seizure is the body enforcing a limit no one held: lorazepam was stopped too fast. The frame here is a planned taper and emergency holding of withdrawal, not treating the seizure as a random event or a stimulant crash.

2009-65.sentence: ECT is offered as a last, powerful feed for severe psychotic depression, but patients often experience it as a treatment that also takes something—memory. Cognitive impairment is the side effect that most often limits how fully someone can accept that bargain.

2009-66.sentence: Denial splits the story: a “voice change” and a little faintness on standing are treated as separate nuisances while one vocal cord, miosis, dry skin, and a full bladder already show widespread autonomic failure. Naming Shy-Drager (multiple system atrophy) means refusing that split and seeing the orthostatic drop and the immobile cord as one illness.

2009-67.sentence: Assuming the addicted colleague's seizure is alcohol or butalbital withdrawal (and not meperidine) already repeats a two-person cover story: we keep treating the prescriber as a withdrawer so we do not have to name opioid diversion. Name meperidine, renal clearance, and nor-meperidine toxicity in the room instead of joining the system’s “just another sedative taper” enactment.

2009-68.sentence: The nighttime GHB “recovery” liquid is a chemical vertical split: the lifter leaves ordinary waking life so growth-hormone pulses can bulk muscle while they are not there. Ask about that liquid specifically, because nandrolone stays in the body as a steroid, whereas GHB knocks consciousness out and then spikes GH.

2009-69.sentence: One week after his wife dies he still works and shows up socially, so the ego can still hold grief, sleep, and appetite without a full collapse. On this older rule, two months of the same anhedonia is the point where that remaining strength is no longer enough and major depression is diagnosed.

2009-70.sentence: Early dementia’s lost hours are not stored as a story the family can tell on a scan; they return as failed orientation, recall, and calculation when you sit and do the mental status exam. MRI or EEG can wait; what cannot be remembered has to be elicited in the interview, not imaged.

2009-71.sentence: The teen who sleeps eighteen hours, eats when awake, and looks dull recruits you to become the parent who keeps shaking him—or the doctor who feels bored and writes him off. That countertransference dullness belongs to Kleine–Levin (normal NREM/REM, long sleep, hyperphagia), not to narcolepsy or apnea; do not enact the withdrawal by stopping the workup.

2009-72.sentence: First-line fluoxetine is the field’s conscience for adolescent major depression: only this SSRI is fully sanctioned. Starting sertraline, citalopram, or venlafaxine first is a quiet gap in that rule—easier for the prescriber, less justified for the kid.

2009-73.sentence: Knowing the day and year is a school-age ego function that usually arrives around six, after running, jumping, and a pincer grasp have already settled; it is calendar orientation, not adult insight. If that dating skill is still missing at six despite chance to learn it, you are looking at a capacity that never quite arrived, not at a child who is merely “being difficult.”

2009-74.sentence: The AIMS is a timed, structured look at tardive movements the patient may already feel in the lips and fingers; you cannot rush that rating into a casual glance. Naming the involuntary motion on the scale is a limit that ends the fantasy that the body will quietly “adjust” if we just wait.

2009-75.sentence: Early SSRI nausea and diarrhea are raw gut alarm the patient cannot yet think; they evacuate the pill after two doses instead of bringing the feeling into words. Containment here is naming the GI effect as expected, not nameless poison, so the serotonin can stay in the body long enough to become usable.

2009-76.sentence: When dementia meets a bedside light and the patient screams “fire,” the self is no longer being mirrored as a person who can locate danger; infection can shatter that remaining competence overnight. A urinalysis is the first restoration of self-esteem: treat the delirium so the person is not left only with panic and a lorazepam wipe.

2009-77.sentence: Hours of lock-checking are the wish to be perfectly safe colliding with a harsh inner ban on any leftover risk; the ritual is the compromise, not the cure. First-line CBT (exposure and response prevention) puts that collision on the table so the prohibition can be practiced against, rather than endlessly obeyed.

2009-78.sentence: Asking the closest relative or the attending to sign off after you have already found the 88-year-old incompetent is denial of the durable power of attorney already on the chart. The assigned decision maker is the legal container; bypassing them is acting out the wish that family feeling, not the document, should decide agitation treatment.

2009-79.sentence: Cigarettes had been silently “feeding” CYP1A2 so the same 10 mg of haloperidol stayed a tolerable partner; stopping smoking turns that dose into poison and the body answers with rigidity, tremor, or akathisia. Ask what the pill now means after the smoke-free ward: not more illness, but a relationship to neuroleptic that suddenly flooded the motor system.

2009-80.sentence: IPT’s sick role is a formal truce in the caregiver’s fight: the wish to stop giving collides with the inner ban that rest equals selfishness, and naming depression as illness lets the wish stand without a moral trial. The diagnosis is not a label for its own sake; it is permission to occupy the sick role while the role dispute (care of the parent) is worked.

2009-81.sentence: Hot, dry, dilated, constipated, visually hallucinating—the paranoid patient’s body stops being a usable self-mirror and cohesion collapses into anticholinergic delirium, not “worse schizophrenia.” Calling this toxidrome instead of NMS protects remaining self-esteem and competence: you do not pile on more dopamine blockade when the self is already unmoored by atropinic poisoning.

2009-82.sentence: The request for DBS recruits you to become the missing steady hand—the one who can write and feed—so notice the pull to rescue or to recoil from the tremor. The usual target is the ventral intermediate thalamus for essential tremor, not the subthalamic nucleus of Parkinson surgery; stay in that limited role rather than becoming the doctor who will fix the whole person.

2009-83.sentence: The MCO’s push to send home a still-suicidal patient can repeat an unspoken expulsion—what cannot be remembered as abandonment gets enacted as a premature discharge. Keep the person in hospital as long as medical safety requires; the frame is to hold the overdose intent in the dyad rather than let the insurer’s pressure complete the trauma in the body.

2009-84.sentence: Whether PTSD follows the fire tracks how close and how severe the exposure was—the trapped, injured survivor faces a bigger developmental overload than the relative who only heard the story. Childhood history and support matter less here than whether the ego’s current capacity was simply outgunned by proximity and dose of trauma.

2009-85.sentence: A standing risperidone order can function as a moral shortcut: the team’s conscience is soothed by “doing something” about frightening hallucinations while the patient’s Lewy-body rigidity and falls absorb the cost. Hold the guilt in the room—name that protecting gait and cognition is the ethical act, not quieting voices with a D2 blocker that this brain cannot tolerate.

2009-86.sentence: Adolescence is Erikson’s identity-versus-role-confusion work; a loaded gun in the house turns a still-forming self into a one-decision tragedy. The most identity-preserving prevention is not a lecture or a hotline but removing firearms so the identity crisis cannot end in a completed act.

2009-87.sentence: The black-box finding is an increase in suicidal ideation on SSRIs versus placebo, not completed suicide, QT change, or bleeding. That ideation can be the adolescent’s first words for despair that the pill both stirs and, with close follow-up, finally lets them say out loud.

2009-88.sentence: Four months after the spouse’s cancer death, self-blame and “I should have died instead” sit in Klein’s depressive position: he is trying to repair a loved object he feels he destroyed, not merely “normal grief.” Antidepressant plus psychotherapy holds that guilt so it can become mourning rather than a demand that he be punished in her place.

2009-89.sentence: Peek-a-boo is object permanence: the hidden face still exists, so reunion can be trusted. Culture and identity enter only as the particular face that disappears and returns—the game still measures that one cognitive hold, not race or class as a third in the room.

2009-90.sentence: Amphetamine euphoria is dopamine dumped into the nucleus accumbens; two people then organize around that spike—the user chasing the rush, the other person managing the crash. The relational pattern is the pair living inside that accumbens burst, not a lone “addict brain” acting in a vacuum.

2009-91.sentence: Invite the quiet members to say what they actually felt when the room went still, so the patient can use the group as a secure base instead of treating silence as proof of abandonment. Consensual validation is proximity-seeking done in words: comparing the rejection story with other people’s inner states until the distortion loosens.

2009-92.sentence: Tramadol plus fluoxetine is not just a drug interaction; it floods the body with serotonin so the patient cannot hold a calm, “good enough” bodily state and instead lives a split of flushing, diarrhea, tremor, and hyperreflexia. Treat the combination as a relationship that went toxic—stop both contributors, support the ego with cooling and benzos, and only later restore one clean antidepressant object.

2009-93.sentence: This length-dependent, sensory-greater-than-motor, sympathetic alcohol neuropathy is a mind that needs support, not uncovering: burning feet and lost ankle jerks will not yield to interpretation of drinking. Technique is concrete—stop alcohol, replace thiamine, treat pain, and work the addiction as a deficit in self-care rather than a conflict to decode.

2009-94.sentence: Natalizumab blocks integrin so lymphocytes cannot stick to endothelium; any new cognitive or behavioral change on it is a frame issue first—think PML and hold the infusion, not a session about meaning. The psychodynamic job is containment of terror while you protect the medical boundary: this monoclonal is not a metaphor until infection is ruled out.

2009-95.sentence: The back pain, fever, paraparesis, saddle numbness, and incontinence after IV methamphetamine is pus in the epidural space—the body evacuating danger it could not metabolize, not a conversion to interpret. Kleinian urgency here is repair in action: get imaging and neurosurgery before you sit with the guilt or the need to punish the using self.

2009-96.sentence: The delayed shuffling, masked face, and apathy weeks after carbon monoxide coma are the symptom doing the work of a second death: the person looks recovered, then the basal ganglia announce that the original hypoxia is still unfinished. Parkinsonism here is not random movement noise; it is the nervous system insisting the near-death still organizes gait, expression, and initiative.

2009-97.sentence: This sits on Erikson’s generativity-versus-stagnation work of midlife: she is re-choosing what faith she will pass on, not dissolving who she is. The guilt that she is “acting against her moral beliefs” is the cost of that adult identity revision, which is why DSM codes a religious or spiritual problem rather than an identity disorder.

2009-98.sentence: Mother’s “our disease” and answering for the boy is a fused conscience: his colitis pain and her worry are treated as one moral unit, so he never gets a private “I.” Minuchin calls that enmeshment—boundaries so thin that guilt and caretaking replace a separate self.

2009-99.sentence: Acculturation is a developmental achievement: how far this second-generation patient has taken in a new culture’s ways of healing, not a racial stamp or a frozen ethnicity. Cultural identity therefore changes with that arrival of belonging, so you ask about degree of acculturation instead of assuming group membership equals ethnic identity.

2009-100.sentence: The tapes-through-the-wall story is already a relationship to help: therapy as a leaky, persecutory feed rather than a sealed hour. Asking for the perceptions that led to that discovery treats the belief as data in the bond, not as a cue to force a pill or to prove the office is safe.

2009-101.sentence: The pediatrician holds the developmental limit: at three, speech should be intelligible enough that family and strangers can understand, so “don’t worry, hearing is normal” would abandon the child. Expressing concern is the frame—naming that most three-year-olds can make themselves understood and that further work is required.

2009-102.sentence: Twelve-step facilitation enacts the addiction as a disease you stop fighting alone: acceptance and surrender to help beyond oneself become the couplet in the room. That is a two-person repetition of “I cannot control this,” unlike CBT, MET, or dynamic therapy, which keep more of the fight inside the patient’s will.

2009-103.sentence: Calling this “just a migraine” after seeing papilledema is denial: the mind waves away the venous-sinus emergency so the headache can stay ordinary. The CT contrast study is the reality the defense was keeping off the table.

2009-104.sentence: Distractibility arrives as nameless dread—raw noise the mind cannot yet name—until the WAIS attention/concentration subtests contain it as a score. Evacuating the complaint into “they’re just unfocused” skips that containing work and leaves the feeling unthinkable.

2009-105.sentence: A prior postpartum psychosis is not only a statistic; it is a collapse of the self’s competence after birth, when the new mother needed mirroring that she could still hold a mind. Idealizing “this delivery will be different” without planning around that history starves self-esteem of a realistic scaffold.

2009-106.sentence: A trial comment—“the oral meperidine is simply weaker milligram for milligram than the IM shots”—tests whether she can see her part in the panic as pharmacology, not as craving. If she can use that, psychological mindedness is intact; if she can only hear accusation, insight has not arrived yet.

2009-107.sentence: The low K+, low Cl−, high bicarbonate, and high amylase with normal lipase mark a limit: the purging cannot be rushed into “we’ll talk about it later.” Termination of the binge-vomit cycle has to respect a body that will not wait for insight.

2009-108.sentence: The cholinesterase inhibitor will not give childhood memories back; wanting it to is the transference wish that you become the parent who restores what was lost. Your countertransference urge to “fix” visuospatial skill or reverse the dementia is that same recruitment—stay with reducing agitation, not with being the miracle.

2009-109.sentence: Valproate raising lamotrigine is the conscience of the pair: it punishes a “usual” start dose as if speeding were a moral offense. The slower, halved titration is the sanctioned gap—permission to go on, but only after the resident pays the extra guilt-work of checking the interaction.

2009-110.sentence: Telling the patient to keep usual sodium while starting lithium is already a two-person scene: the pair is rehearsing who will be blamed when a crash diet or a salt binge later “makes” the level toxic. If the clinician frames sodium as a rule the patient must not break, the next missed meal becomes an enactment of who failed whom, not a pharmacokinetic fact.

2009-111.sentence: Condensation is the dream’s vertical split: teacher, parent, and supervisor occupy one image so the dreamer can sit in the seminar chair and still not feel all three wishes at once. The single figure lets the self leave the conflict without leaving the room.

2009-112.sentence: The right parietal lesion that makes her call the flaccid left arm “yours” turns the exam into a relationship: the paretic limb is offered as if it were the psychiatrist’s body, not a need she must own. The pill or the consult then risks becoming proof that someone else must carry the deficit she cannot claim.

2009-113.sentence: Naming primary autism as the infant’s first state is adult denial of what the newborn already does: attend to faces, voices, and cross-modal cues that start attachment. The consultation that watches gaze and vocal turn-taking undoes that denial by treating the infant as already a partner, not a sealed-off mind.

2009-114.sentence: The best malpractice shield is not the no-harm contract or the withheld risky drug; it is the two-person pattern of talking through benefits, harms, and how to reach the team. Suit risk drops when both people have already practiced staying in the relationship after a bad outcome is named.

2009-115.sentence: A reading-disabled 11-year-old who also has inattentive ADHD cannot use uncovering; the ego is already overloaded by lost materials, missed multistep directions, and unfinished work. Technique stays supportive: scaffold attention and reading load first, then add insight only if school function actually holds.

2009-116.sentence: Acute myasthenic crisis is an ego-strength emergency: affect talk and fancy immunotherapy wait until the patient can breathe and clear secretions. Mechanical ventilation first restores the most basic impulse-control analog—keeping air moving—so later plasma exchange or IVIG can be used without the mind drowning in panic and hypoxia.

2009-117.sentence: Fast slurred speech, bad gait, 35 CSF lymphocytes, protein 110, and high gamma globulin are not “age plus atrophy”; they mean a treatable infection (neurosyphilis) is carrying the forgetfulness. The symptom’s job is to stop the team from attaching to a hopeless-dementia story and instead hunt the reversible inflammatory cause.

2009-118.sentence: The wish to treat temporal arteritis as “just a headache” collides with the prohibition against delay: the ophthalmic artery can occlude and steal the eye. The repetition is the amaurosis curtain—act on steroids/workup now, or the drive to see loses to the blocked vessel.

2009-119.sentence: MS depression is not a badge of lesion load or interferon virtue; it is a collapse of self-esteem and felt competence that still answers to antidepressants. Mirror the low mood as real depression, treat it, and the patient’s idealizable rehab self can come back online instead of being swallowed by fatigue.

2009-120.sentence: When a cholinesterase inhibitor no longer holds the Alzheimer patient, memantine is the next secure-base drug: it partly blocks NMDA so glutamate storms do not rip the person further from caregivers. Proximity regulation here is pharmacologic—damp excitotoxicity so the patient can still use another person to stay oriented.

2009-121.sentence: Internuclear ophthalmoplegia (the adducting eye stalls, the abducting eye nystagmus) is a concrete hit to reality testing: the world literally doubles and tilts, so the first ego job is naming the finding as a medial-longitudinal-fasciculus lesion, not as “I’m going crazy.” Affect tolerance then means sitting with a probable multiple-sclerosis diagnosis without either denying the diplopia or flooding into catastrophe before the MRI and the rest of the exam are in.

2009-122.sentence: Free erythrocyte protoporphyrin is a child’s-development test, not a metaphor: it flags lead before the still-myelinated, still-learning brain pays with attention, language, and impulse control. The developmental task for the adults is to treat peeling paint and microcytic anemia as injuries to a growing nervous system, not as a child’s “willfulness.”

2009-123.sentence: Cocaine’s rank as the most powerfully reinforcing drug of abuse already writes the session: the pair can start chasing the next hit of certainty, the next clever formulation, the next “why they keep using.” Name that two-person loop—clinician and patient both pulled by the same steep reward curve—before it becomes another unpaid, illegal, medically dangerous run.

2009-124.sentence: Empathy here is taking in the patient’s inner state (“everyone thinks I am lazy; I am exhausted”) without dumping it back as your own imagined day in their shoes—that swap is identification, not contact. In Kleinian terms, you metabolize what they project (the lazy/exhausted split) and return it as their experience seen from inside, not as your sympathy or your trial of their position.

2009-125.sentence: Paroxetine was offered as a good object against depression and instead joined the body as a bad one: SIADH, sodium 117, headache and lethargy. Confirming that with urine osmolality keeps the story medical—do not split the pill into “the helpful SSRI” versus “mysterious decline” until the concentrating urine proves the relationship that is actually harming them.

2009-126.sentence: A 36-year-old with migraine and a posterior-cerebral-artery infarct after oral contraceptives cannot use deep uncovering of “why me” until the vascular fact is held: estrogen plus migraine is the likely mechanism. Technique is supportive first—stop the pill, name the stroke risk in plain language—and only later, if ego can bear it, work the meaning of losing vision or independence.

2009-127.sentence: A crossover trial is a two-person bargain: the participant and the protocol take turns holding drug and placebo, so each person becomes their own comparison. If you treat “double-blind” as the design rather than the mask, you miss the sequence that actually builds the result.

2009-128.sentence: Intellectual disability does not invent a private catalog of mental illness; the same mood, anxiety, psychosis, and behavioral syndromes still arrive, only later or harder to hear. What often never quite arrives is a reliable way to name those syndromes instead of folding them into the cognitive deficit.

2009-129.sentence: Daytime alcohol is doing night-shift work the circadian clock will not: forcing sleep after a duty cycle that wrecked alertness. Relieving the night shift first withdraws the symptom’s job before you load on disulfiram, naltrexone, or an antidepressant.

2009-130.sentence: Forced medication is a technique choice that suspends autonomy—the patient’s right to refuse this antipsychotic after a capacity talk. Uncovering “why they refuse” comes after you know whether this ego can still hold a specific informed no.

2009-131.sentence: Reproductive hormone collapse is the body splitting off fertility so the starving self can keep a rigid good-control / bad-appetite split. The amenorrhea is not a side note; it is how the relationship with food holds good and bad apart.

2009-132.sentence: Psychoeducation is containment: the family is handed facts, meds, sleep, and problem-solving so they stop receiving the patient’s projected chaos as if it were their own failure. Calm guidelines invite depressive concern—repair and support—rather than a paranoid hunt for who caused the schizophrenia.

2009-133.sentence: Flattened pitch and wrong stress are a speech-motor loss, not a mood or affect problem, so do not treat the person as emotionally empty because the music of speech is gone. If you hear “cold” or “dead,” check whether you are reacting to dysprosody rather than to what they actually think and feel.

2009-134.sentence: A young executive’s 4 a.m. hour-long unilateral pain with tearing, runny nose, and drooping lid is not an Erikson work-identity crisis acting out in the body. Name it as cluster headache so the intimacy-versus-isolation story of “stress at the brokerage” does not delay oxygen or other attack treatment.

2009-135.sentence: Late-life depression more often uses a psychotic story—poisoned food, ruined family—to give shape to collapse, instead of the early-onset confession of worthlessness. Ask what the delusion is doing: it may be holding terror that the person cannot yet say as ordinary sad mood.

2009-136.sentence: Three weeks after the crash, “spirit leaving the body” is a young adult’s not-yet-integrated way of surviving horror, not a finished identity split. The developmental task is to keep the self in one piece through the acute window, before a month turns the same numbness and dreams into PTSD.

2009-137.sentence: Ibuprofen can feel like a morally clean “just Advil” loophole while it blocks lithium clearance and invites toxicity. Name the conscience split: the patient may hide the NSAID because needing lithium already feels like a failing, then present with tremor or confusion as if they did nothing wrong.

2009-138.sentence: She can want and climax alone, so you are not meeting low desire; you are meeting a no to the husband as initiator. Notice if you become the gynecologist who found “nothing wrong,” or the husband who keeps approaching—both recruitments miss the aversion itself.

2009-139.sentence: Marginalization—no living allegiance to the native culture and no real uptake of the host one—leaves the adolescent without a story of belonging, so the unrepresented exile is acted in the body as suicide risk, alcohol, and other substances. In the dyad that same gap shows up as a kid who cannot “remember” either home, only the felt deadness of standing between two groups and belonging to neither.

2009-140.sentence: Early full remission is the DSM name for a conscience that has held: no drinks and no dependence criteria for six months, but not yet a year—so the superego is not allowed to declare the patient “cured.” Writing that specifier keeps guilt and pride from jumping the clock; sustained full remission is a later moral achievement, and any leftover criteria would make it only partial.

2009-141.sentence: In childhood-onset schizophrenia the ego functions that should arrive in latency—stable reality testing, play that stays play, a school self that can recover after a bad week—never quite lock in, so the course is typically chronic and unremitting rather than episodic. The developmental point is not a later “break” after a formed personality, but a psychotic process that occupies the years when those capacities were supposed to consolidate.

2009-142.sentence: In healthy people over 65 the executive capacities that plan meds, money, travel, and a household do not show a significant life-cycle decline; slowness on a new phone app is not the same as loss of that organizing function. Treat the 72-year-old accountant’s extra learning time as a speed change, not as proof that judgment and planning failed to hold.

2009-143.sentence: Festination—the involuntary speeding-up of a short shuffling gait as the patient “runs after” the center of gravity—recruits you into hurrying, catching, or over-directing, as if the pair must accelerate together. Name that pull in yourself so you do not treat Parkinson gait like astasia-abasia, drunken staggering, or Huntington chorea, and so you do not rush the interview the way the legs are rushing.

2009-144.sentence: Choosing gabapentin for the seizure in this OCP-triggered porphyria picture (soft abdomen, tachycardia, arm weakness with lost biceps/triceps jerks, psychosis) is a competence move: you do not prop self-esteem on a “stronger” AED like phenytoin or valproate that can worsen the heme crisis. The mirroring the patient needs is a clinician who can hold the frightening body without offering a drug that further dismantles it.

2009-145.sentence: Without object constancy—the inner sense that the same person stays whole when the schedule shifts—the clinician who changes an appointment is no longer a mixed, reliable other and becomes a dismissive controller. The wish to cling and the wish to attack then have nowhere to live except in the accusation that the office is persecuting them.

2009-146.sentence: The chin-touch that stops the leftward head turn is a sensory trick of cervical dystonia, not a limit the patient can talk themselves past or a conversion that will melt at termination. Interpreting the right sternomastoid spasm as rushed affect delays botulinum toxin, which is the treatment that actually interrupts the motor loop.

2009-147.sentence: A baseline EKG before any child starts a tricyclic holds the unthinkable cardiac collapse in a tracing so it can be thought, not evacuated into “we’ll check if they get chest pain.” Waiting for symptoms, monthly checks only in known arrhythmia, or a six-month delay leaves that nameless dread uncontained at the moment the drug is first given.

2009-148.sentence: The reprimand that follows the rule-break is a two-person sequence: staff deliver an aversive stimulus contingent on that response, and the pair then see the behavior drop—that is punishment, not a vibe in one mind. Calling it extinction, positive reinforcement, or negative reinforcement blurs who did what to whom after the violation.

2009-149.sentence: Malpractice is a four-part frame: duty, negligence, causation, and actual harm to the patient—not the physician’s ignorance, impaired judgment, or a missing consent form standing alone. When the missed lab is caught and no injury occurs, the attachment-style protest of “you abandoned me” may be real in the room, but the legal claim still lacks harm.

2009-150.sentence: In pregnant mania, the pill is not a way to split off the agitation into the fetus: carbamazepine, lithium, and valproate carry heavier teratogenic meaning than the choice of haloperidol. Treating the unsafe, sleepless mother with Haldol keeps the fetal body from becoming the container for adult mood instability.

2009-151.sentence: An aging liver that clears antipsychotics more slowly is also a weaker ego for affect and impulse: the same milligrams that a younger patient can metabolize become a flood the older patient cannot hold. Start low so the person can still test reality and ride out agitation without the drug itself becoming the next insult to coping.

2009-152.sentence: Wanting to stay on valproate through a first-trimester window is often denial dressed as stability: the neural-tube risk is set aside so the familiar mood stabilizer does not have to be mourned. Name the defense and the folate/teratogen fact together so planning a switch is grief work, not a sudden rupture.

2009-153.sentence: Friedreich ataxia’s recessive GAA expansion already enacts a two-person story: parents who look well and a teenager who cannot walk, so the room fills with unspoken blame and rescue. Slow the workup so the family is not forced to reenact “who failed whom” while reflexes vanish and gait worsens.

2009-154.sentence: Modeling only works inside a frame you hold: the child watches peers enjoy the bike, but you decide when watching ends and when a graded try is allowed. Do not collapse into forcing the climb or abandoning the hour; the limit is the safe seat from which someone else’s fun can become theirs.

2009-155.sentence: Diphenhydramine’s anticholinergic storm (hot, dry, blind, full bladder, quiet gut) can be the pill as poison: sleep was supposed to soothe, and the OTC tablet instead takes the body hostage. Treat the toxidrome and the relationship to the sleep aid so the next “harmless” bottle is not another demand to be knocked out.

2009-156.sentence: Low CSF serotonin in intermittent explosive disorder is a limit you cannot rush: the pause between spark and outburst is thin, and remorse after the blast does not restore that pause overnight. Therapy and meds aim at buying a second of delay, not at ending sessions as if the serotonergic brake were already in.

2009-157.sentence: At 12 months the baby can treat a parent’s face as a trial comment—“is this play structure safe?”—and then use that look to decide whether to climb. That is early psychological mindedness: they already check another mind before they can name their own fear.

2009-158.sentence: Kagan’s inhibited infant is stuck on Erikson’s autonomy-versus-shame task: novelty feels like a test they will fail, so they freeze rather than try. That same shame-anxiety line is why early behavioral inhibition tracks later anxiety disorders, not ADHD, learning, mood, or conduct.

2009-159.sentence: No postictal fog means the stare did not serve as a retreat the child has to climb back from; consciousness snaps back because the event was a brief absence, not a complex partial withdrawal. If teachers report sleepiness or confusion afterward, the “stare” is doing a different job and you should not call it absence.

2009-160.sentence: The little-finger/ulnar-ring numbness and wasted hypothenar is the body localizing an ulnar lesion from a truck driver’s repeated grip, not a vague left-hand complaint. Mapping those two fingers keeps the finding from being swallowed into “stress tingling” and points to the nerve that is actually being crushed.

2009-161.sentence: On the TAT the patient dumps inner figures into the picture—who is attacking, who must be repaired—so you hear paranoid-schizoid threat versus depressive concern without them owning it as theirs. That is projective identification onto the scene: the story carries the split so they do not have to feel it as their own.

2009-162.sentence: Bupropion can hold sexual desire as a good, alive part of the pair when the patient is not depressed, instead of splitting sex off as the bad object the way sertraline, duloxetine, or venlafaxine often do. The pill’s meaning is “desire is allowed in this relationship,” not another antidepressant that makes the partner the enemy of libido.

2009-163.sentence: Name the mismatch between “I’m fine about my sibling’s drinking” and the crack of anger in the voice; that is confrontation, not interpretation of hidden meaning. Use it only if this mind can hear the affect without collapsing—otherwise stay with support and let the feeling stay unnamed until the ego can hold it.

2009-164.sentence: Avoidant and schizoid both sit far from people; the relational difference is that the avoidant still wants closeness and is organizing around feared rejection, not around no appetite for others. Treat the pattern as two-person: invitations declined are about expected humiliation, so the work is safety of contact, not “teaching” social skills to someone who never desired them.

2009-165.sentence: A double-blind trial is the research analogue of a secure base: neither patient nor rater can use “I know I’m on the pill” as the person they lean on to decide how they feel. If that knowledge leaks, hope and allegiance become the regulator, and the rating of agitation is no longer the patient’s own signal.

2009-166.sentence: Direct conditioning after this man’s own crash means the ego now treats driving as danger he cannot yet titrate; panic and job-threatening avoidance show affect and impulse regulation are overloaded. Technique is graded exposure that rebuilds reality testing (“the car is not the collision”), not insight about why he “chose” to stop driving.

2009-167.sentence: The hop to irrelevant topics when a loss appears is resistance: the mind leaves the feeling without leaving the chair, a vertical split rather than frank hostility or thought-disordered derailment. Name the leave-taking gently—“we were at the death, then work details arrived”—so the split can close without shaming the patient for disappearing.

2009-168.sentence: Hyperactivity fading by adolescence while inattention and disorganization stay means the room may still fill with late work, lost papers, and interruptions even as the body sits still. That leftover mess can become an enactment: you chase, they scramble, and the old ADHD pair repeats unless you treat the remaining symptoms as the task, not as willful chaos.

2009-169.sentence: Overnight insomnia is the defense of acting out: when orientation and recall have already failed, the delirious body stays awake as if staying up could fend off the ward. A hypnotic is then used because that enacted all-night protest, not clouding or slow reaction time, is what wrecks the next day’s care.

2009-170.sentence: Major depression in the 15-to-44 years is the illness that takes the person out of work and family roles that used to hold them, so the symptom’s job is disability, not only low mood. That is why it outranks schizophrenia, bipolar illness, substance use, and GAD as the leading cause of lost function in that age band.

2009-171.sentence: Long-term HAART let patients with HIV grow into an older adult body that earlier cohorts never reached, so stroke risk arrives as a late-life capacity rather than childhood-like HIV dementia. Abrupt aphasia and one-sided weakness are that new developmental task and must not be read as anxiety or a leftover opportunistic encephalitis.

2009-172.sentence: Bupropion on nicotinic receptors is a sanctioned gap in the smoker’s conscience: the pill, not grit, occupies the receptor the cigarette used to own. The superego can then stop treating every craving as a moral failure while dopaminergic or serotonergic stories stay beside the point.

2009-173.sentence: Once the 18-month-old can use a word for an absent parent, you are recruited as the one who understands a symbol, not only as a body in the room. The countertransference is to feel brilliantly spoken-to and to forget that stuffed-animal play, turn-taking, or trial-and-error is a different job than this leap into language.

2009-174.sentence: Maple syrup urine disease splits the newborn in the first days: the initially well infant versus the suddenly lethargic, poorly feeding, twitching baby, before good and bad can be held in one caregiver. The failed object is milk itself once branched-chain amino acids cannot be cleared, unlike later PKU or Tay-Sachs.

2009-175.sentence: The patient drops an unspoken identity into you and then walks away, leaving you holding a secret the spouse now wants named—that is projective identification, putting an unwanted bind into someone else. Depressive concern means you keep the patient’s name unsaid rather than dumping the awkwardness by confirming who they are.

2009-176.sentence: At 150 mg of sertraline, OCD often still means the same contamination ritual has not been given a high enough SSRI trial, so raising to 200 mg is staying with one treatment relationship instead of swapping pills in frustration. The next dose is the intervention; adding bupropion or jumping to clomipramine treats your impatience, not the unfinished sertraline trial.

2009-177.sentence: This item sits on trust versus mistrust: the body may be failing (a clot in the lung) while the patient offers the familiar story of “another panic attack.” You earn basic trust by checking oxygenation and sudden dyspnea before you treat the feeling as only anxiety.

2009-178.sentence: Velocardiofacial (22q11) loads the ego so heavily—heart repair, palate/speech trouble, learning problems—that reality testing is the function most at risk for a first psychotic break. Williams or Prader-Willi do not carry that same hit to the apparatus that tells inner from outer.

2009-179.sentence: Wraparound keeps the child near the people who already function as a secure base so aggression does not get solved by sending them away to a hospital or residence. The goal is proximity and a usable home team, not a new placement that treats separation as treatment.

2009-180.sentence: The wish is to be steered through every task while the doctor is gone; the prohibition is against a loud, entitled protest, so the distress stays panicky, withdrawn, and politely timed to the vacation. That collision—need for a caretaker versus not daring to rage—is dependent, not the storm of a borderline abandonment scene.

2009-181.sentence: When carbamazepine induces the enzymes that clear methadone, the body can reenact withdrawal—yawning, rhinorrhea, gut pain, craving—as an unremembered state: the opioid deficit is lived, not thought. Treat the pharmacokinetic hit as a bodily repetition of loss; restore methadone levels so the dyad is not left managing raw withdrawal as if it were “relapse character.”

2009-182.sentence: In a school-age child, irritability is often nameless dread that has not yet become thinkable sadness; the household and classroom get the raw evacuation of a depressive affect that cannot be named. Containment here means asking about anhedonia, sleep, appetite, and energy so the argumentativeness can be metabolized into a mood diagnosis rather than left as opposition.

2009-183.sentence: NMS is a collapse of the body’s competence system: after dopamine blockade, rigidity, fever, and rising CK say the self can no longer regulate itself. Stopping the antipsychotic and adding a dopamine agonist is a mirroring of agency—you restore the missing dopaminergic signal so the patient is not left idealizing “more neuroleptic” as rescue.

2009-184.sentence: A ~3 Hz, irregular, terminal intention tremor on finger-to-nose is the cerebellum’s timing capacity arriving late: the reach starts, then the correction never quite lands. That is a developmental failure of on-line adjustment, not essential, physiologic, or rest tremor—name the late-arriving error so the exam is not collapsed into “just shaky.”

2009-185.sentence: In an otherwise typically developing preschooler, hitting often does the work the sentence cannot: it discharges a conflict the child cannot yet put into words. Limited verbal ability is the meaning of the aggression—build language and pause at the trigger so the fist is not left as the only available speech.

2009-186.sentence: On the WCST, perseverative errors recruit you into being the unchanging rule: the patient keeps sorting by the old category while you feel the urge to over-explain or to give up. Stay with the scored switch-cost rather than becoming the new deck yourself; the clinical point is cognitive inflexibility, not your countertransference wish to rescue the sort.

2009-187.sentence: The conscience can demand a pill for a problem that is already resolving, as if doing nothing were negligence. Transient global amnesia wants observation, not memantine, olanzapine, or lorazepam, because the moral task here is to tolerate a scary blank without medicating it away.

2009-188.sentence: Payday and methamphetamine have already become a two-person scene: money arrives, the old ritual knocks, and both of you can start treating the paycheck as the dealer. Stay with the cue long enough and the craving usually fades in intensity; rushing to rewrite payday as if it were still the high is the enactment.

2009-189.sentence: Denial here is not a speech about drinking; it is the empty fridge while Korsakoff memory loss keeps the body from registering that it is starving. A nutritious diet is the confrontation that actually matters, because thiamine and calories, not an NSAID or a cholinesterase inhibitor, are what slow the slide toward alcohol-related dementia.

2009-190.sentence: Nausea after valproate is a raw evacuation: the body dumps the drug before anyone can think about mood. Contain the GI side effects first—dose timing, food, hydration—so the feeling can become a side-effect conversation instead of a sudden stop.

2009-191.sentence: Retentive encopresis is a body that will not finish on command; you cannot terminate withholding with an SSRI or a couch. Psychoeducation and laxatives accept the limit: the colon has to empty on a schedule before anyone can talk about the accident as meaning.

2009-192.sentence: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder is a monthly collision of a wish to stay even and a prohibition that arrives with the luteal crash. Fluoxetine treats that timed conflict; pyridoxine, diazepam, lithium, and bupropion do not hit the same cycle.

2009-193.sentence: Young-adult smokers often use nicotine to prop up a shaky sense of being impressive or “together,” so the highest-prevalence years are also years of hunting for a chemical mirror that says they belong. Screening every young adult about cigarettes, vaping, and other nicotine is asking whether self-esteem is being outsourced to a product rather than to real competence.

2009-194.sentence: In individual DBT the psychiatrist is the relationship that both feeds and withholds: warmth is given, but the “pill” of care is never a substitute for the patient doing the next skill. Nurture without a demand to self-help becomes poison; a demand without nurture becomes a dead prescription.

2009-195.sentence: Power analysis is undoing in numbers: before the trial, you ritually calculate the sample size needed to detect a defined effect given known variances so you will not later have to pretend an underpowered null was truth. Skipping that step is denial dressed as “we’ll just see what we get.”

2009-196.sentence: The blank, slowed, hyperreflexic post-hip-surgery patient can name frustration but may not see that periventricular white-matter disease, not only “depression,” is stealing spontaneity. A trial comment—“part of this blankness may be the brain’s wiring, not only your mood”—tests whether they can use that split insight.

2009-197.sentence: Amantadine for antipsychotic parkinsonism is a frame decision: you hold the limit that the neuroleptic stays if it is working, and you add a second agent rather than abandon the first at the first cogwheel. Who holds that limit is the psychiatrist, not the patient’s wish to be “off everything” or the ward’s wish for a quieter gait.

2009-198.sentence: Hypochondriasis locks the ego onto disease as the object; affect about death and bodily failure is not tolerated as feeling, so it is converted into a hunt for the hidden illness. Impulse to check and seek reassurance crowds out the capacity to sit with uncertainty after a negative workup.

2009-199.sentence: LSD and mescaline turn up 5HT2A so the usual inner “someone is with me” signal goes haywire and proximity no longer soothes. The resident’s job is to become a temporary secure base—voice, lighting, and stay-near presence—until that receptor storm settles and the patient can use another person to regulate again.

2009-200.sentence: Superior-division MCA occlusion hits contralateral face-and-arm more than leg and drives gaze away from the weak side; the body is acting out a wish to look toward the intact half and a prohibition against using the damaged field. The stroke consult is the collision made visible: motor drive toward the world, blocked in the very territory the artery no longer feeds.

2009-201.sentence: Motivational interviewing first mirrors the OCD patient’s competence—naming what washing still “works” for—before anyone asks them to stop. Idealizing the therapist as the one who “gets it” rebuilds self-esteem enough that exposure can later be chosen rather than assigned.

2009-202.sentence: Clang associations recruit you into a rhyming partner: “bright / light / flight / right” asks you to chase sound instead of meaning, safety, or sleep. Notice the countertransference pull to finish the couplet or smile at the cleverness; that is the transferential bid to become an audience, not an examiner.

2009-203.sentence: The “special / needs really good treatment” handoff is an unremembered split already repeating in the referral itself. Anticipate splitting—holding both doctors as all-good or all-bad—rather than probing old boundary crossings or promising extra gentleness that enacts the same unrepresented demand.

2009-204.sentence: Neglect, not hitting or a parent’s schizophrenia, is the most common reason parental rights end: the child’s capacity to expect a mind that keeps them fed and followed medically never quite arrived. Child work starts from that missing developmental provision—supervision as a function that failed to consolidate—not from a later abuse narrative.

2009-205.sentence: Histrionic affect is loud, but the superego—the inner prosecutor that says “I am late, I am failing, I am unlovable”—is often what just exploded. Ask him what happened before the rage so conscience can be examined instead of discharged as a divorce edict.

2009-206.sentence: Knee extension lives on the femoral nerve, and Erikson’s industry-versus-inferiority is the matching psychosocial task: can this body still do the work of standing up from a chair. Weakness here is not just a root; it is a threat to competence, so name the femoral lesion and the competence fear together.

2009-207.sentence: Emergency medicine’s high substance-use rate is not only access; the symptom medicates a self that must stay hyper-awake, decisive, and never collapse. The drug (or drink) is doing night-shift containment that the person cannot ask a colleague for.

2009-208.sentence: The 2-year-old with the car next to the truck is in an enactment of “we share a space without sharing a mind yet.” If you push cooperative play too soon, you repeat the adult demand that the toddler join a game the psyche is not ready to staff.

2009-209.sentence: Macrocytic anemia plus late-life apathy is B12 until proven otherwise; the “leaving without leaving the chair” can be metabolic, not a vertical split of self. Order the vitamin B12 level so you do not treat a deficient brain as if the person had dissociated from her own initiative.

2009-210.sentence: HSV encephalitis recruits you as the person who must smell danger first: fever, seizure, drowsiness, and temporal T2 change feel like “this house is fouled.” Your countertransference urgency is useful—treat for herpes while you wait, rather than becoming the family member who only argues about the odor.

2009-211.sentence: An APP mutation does not wait for the usual age of decline; it writes early Alzheimer disease into the family line before the person has “earned” dementia by living long enough. Conscience wants a moral story—lifestyle, neglect, punishment—but amyloid precursor protein is a protein verdict, not a character one.

2009-212.sentence: The wish is still for a quick dopaminergic lift; the prohibition is not to hand a divertible stimulant to an adolescent who already sold someone else’s pills. Atomoxetine treats ADHD without feeding that collision, so the drive can be named in therapy instead of being swallowed or sold.

2009-213.sentence: When desipramine “does nothing,” the unrepresented part is what the body is actually doing with the drug—missed doses, fast metabolism, an interaction—not a remembered scene. A blood level turns that mute repetition into a number you can think with, instead of another month of unexplained nonresponse.

2009-214.sentence: The condemning voice is raw, undigested badness dumped into the child’s mind rather than held until it can be thought as depression. Containment means you name major depressive disorder and stay with the irritability and guilt instead of evacuating the problem into oppositionality or childhood-onset schizophrenia.

2009-215.sentence: Clozapine can feel like the last ideal object for treatment-resistant psychosis; rushing the dose is a bid for instant repair of a shattered self. Slow titration is respect for the brain’s limits: seizures are what happens when that idealization outruns the cortex’s capacity to regulate.

2009-216.sentence: Circumstantiality still gets to the point; it just cannot close without first unloading weather, traffic, and breakfast. A trial comment—“you took the long way, and then you said sleep”—tests whether they can see that extra loop as theirs, not as the world’s necessary inventory.

2009-217.sentence: Reporting a driver with progressing dementia is a termination of a freedom, and you cannot rush past the state’s legal clock by inventing half-limits like daylight-only or no-highways. Check the statute first; talking with the patient is the work, but unilateral “just be careful” is a wish that the lost capacity will wait.

2009-218.sentence: A BAC of 0.425 g/dL in a stuporous patient is not a moment for uncovering seizures, DTs, or the meaning of the drink. Support the brainstem first: respiratory failure is the immediate concern while pulse and blood pressure still look deceptively ordinary.

2009-219.sentence: Blunted affect is something two people feel together: the face goes still and you start working harder to keep the room alive. Hallucinations, thought insertion, and control delusions are additions; this negative symptom is a missing interpersonal signal, not a story the patient is telling you.

2009-220.sentence: Hyperkalemic periodic paralysis and paramyotonia congenita are sodium-channel mutations that were there from the start; the channel never quite learned a quieter way to reset after rest or cold. Development here is electrical, not psychological: the weakness arrives on a timetable the muscle already inherited.

2009-221.sentence: The anesthesiologist’s falling asleep in the OR, weight gain, and unrefreshing nights look like a conscience problem—overwork, burnout, a sanctioned gap in self-care—but the harsher verdict is medical: breathing-related sleep disorder. Guilt about “not refueling” can hide apnea; a negative urine screen does not absolve the airway.

2009-222.sentence: After the sandbags you can feel recruited as the person who should have stopped the heroics, while the body only reports what the nerve can still do. Weak initiation of abduction and external rotation points to the suprascapular nerve, not axillary or long thoracic; name that finding before you inhabit the guilt.

2009-223.sentence: When the fight lives only in the dolls, it is often an unrepresented state: something that cannot yet be remembered in words is being repeated in play. Name the dolls’ anger without pinning it on the child so the scene can become thinkable instead of a forced confession.

2009-224.sentence: Trial competence is a frame problem, not a diagnosis: the court cannot proceed if the person cannot even understand the charges. Psychosis, old hospitalizations, or M’Naughten-style questions about wrongfulness do not by themselves collapse that frame.

2009-225.sentence: Copropraxia looks like a rude message, but it is a tic: an intrusive obscene gesture that is not answering the room. Do not treat it as a parapraxis or a wish; Tourette’s motor burst arrives before meaning does.

2009-226.sentence: The M’Naughten rule asks whether illness wrecked knowledge of the nature of the act or that it was wrong—whether the moral faculty could still judge. Durham, irresistible impulse, and the Model Penal Code test other parts of the mind; this one is knowing, not stopping the impulse.

2009-227.sentence: Little Albert’s fear is a manufactured pairing of a stimulus with a loud noise, not a symbol the infant needed. Nonmaleficence forbids installing that phobia so classical conditioning can look true.

2009-228.sentence: Sublingual buprenorphine is a partial mu agonist with a ceiling, so the person does not have to hunt the street for the next dose. That is attachment in pharmacology: a reliable object that stays put and quiets frantic seeking.

2009-229.sentence: The IQ of 65 and the sixth-grade academic ceiling are not a private deficit sitting inside one adolescent; they live in the daily couple of student and teacher, parent and child, consultant and school. If the adults keep treating him as if he should keep pace with typical seventeen-year-olds, the two of you recreate the same mismatch: he fails, they push, and nobody names the shared work of matching demand to adaptive skill.

2009-230.sentence: Piaget tracked the process of arriving at an answer, not the pile of facts, because that is how industry is built: the school-age child learns how to work a problem, not just whether the answer is right. When you only score content, you miss the psychosocial task sitting on the table—can this mind use a method, or is it still waiting to be told what is true.

2009-231.sentence: The lucrative investment offer is a test of the frame, and the live third in the room is status: older successful businessman, younger male psychiatrist, money as the language of who is on top. Decline the deal and stay curious about the seduction—he is asking whether you can be bought, rivaled, or turned into a junior partner instead of a therapist.

2009-232.sentence: Gerstmann after left angular gyrus embolus—finger agnosia, right-left errors, agraphia, acalculia—is a mind that cannot name or locate parts of the body it still inhabits. That is a Kleinian nightmare in flesh: the self is split into unnameable fragments, and the frustration is not “mood” but the inability to gather the pieces back into one person who can write and calculate.

2009-233.sentence: Inactive CYP2A6 raises cotinine per unit of nicotine and blunts tobacco addiction, so the drug itself is a less reliable “good object”—it does not deliver the same hit. Protection here is metabolic, not moral: the relationship to the cigarette never gets organized because the enzyme never clears the drug into the usual craving cycle.

2009-234.sentence: An acute MS flare needs methylprednisolone, not interferon, glatiramer, azathioprine, or baclofen—this is support first: put out the inflammatory fire before you ask the nervous system to reorganize. Uncovering and disease-modifying strategy come later; in the relapse the mind and the cord can only use a high-dose steroid and rest.
