2009-235.sentence: The isolated voice is often a two-person move: the preschooler puts the fear into a sound so a caregiver can hear it and help settle it. Anxiety is the shared climate that makes that scene, not a one-mind break into schizophrenia.

2009-236.sentence: An alpha-2 agonist such as clonidine or guanfacine lowers the arousal that makes tics fire, so the patient can still use another person as a secure base. First-line here means start with that attachment-friendly damper, not a D2 antagonist that can flatten relatedness while it quiets motor output.

2009-237.sentence: Clonidine turns down the noradrenergic surge of opioid withdrawal so the ego can keep affect and impulse in range. Detox is not only receptors; it is whether the person can tolerate craving without acting it out.

2009-238.sentence: The sudden headache, vomiting, small pupils, and weak abducens on both sides are the hydrocephalus talking after the bleed, not a stroke or a second rupture. Consciousness fails when CSF cannot leave the ventricles, so call neurosurgery for the pressure, not for a psychiatric “leaving.”

2009-239.sentence: The husband’s “everything is fine” is already the enactment: the two of you are living the denial instead of naming the infant-risk. Involuntary admission interrupts that cover story when she feels an “evil force” and cannot keep the baby safe.

2009-240.sentence: Reliability is the frame rule for a scale: the same rater, or another trained rater, must get the same score on a second look. If the withdrawal instrument will not hold still, you are treating noise as if it were a clinical fact.

2009-241.sentence: Sullivan's interpersonal psychiatry treats anxiety as a signal that relatedness is threatened, so ego strength is the capacity to stay in contact without collapsing into panic or rage. Security operations—his word for the automatic ways we manage that anxiety—are the patient's coping, not a character defect to shame.

2009-242.sentence: The limp arm is conversion as a defense: the mind knocks the limb offline so the rage impulse never reaches a punch. That is primary gain—the symptom itself reduces inner conflict; it is not a performance for disability papers.

2009-243.sentence: Echolalia turns the interview into an enactment: the patient cannot author speech, so your words bounce back parrot-fashion and you become the only speaker in the room. Name that two-person freeze as catatonic, then look for the rest of the motor picture rather than arguing content with a mute mind.

2009-244.sentence: Substance-related disorder, not schizophrenia or mania, is the most common psychiatric finding in people who assault others—so technique starts with intoxication, withdrawal, and access, not uncovering childhood rage. Insight work on a wet brain is theater; support, detox, and risk containment come first.

2009-245.sentence: After the affair he can hold only a bad object: she must hurt exactly as he hurts, and there is no mixed picture of a loved wife who also betrayed him. That revenge plan is not a delusion you treat on a locked unit; send him back to law enforcement because the threat is specific and the mind is organized around punishment, not psychosis.

2009-246.sentence: Serotonin and its metabolites stay relatively steady with age, while dopamine and acetylcholine fall—so late-life apathy or parkinsonism is not a serotonin story. Think of 5-HT as the more durable social-regulatory tone: the older patient can still use another person as a secure base even when motor and memory systems are fading.

2009-247.sentence: A no-self-harm contract is a one-person charm; the legally protective act is the two of you actually thinking the risk together—ideation, intent, plan, means, attempts, intoxication, stressors, and reasons for living. Write that conversation down so the work is not “I extracted a promise” but “we named what could kill them and what still holds them.”

2009-248.sentence: Haloperidol can quiet Huntington chorea (and the agitation that rides with it) so the body stops broadcasting collapse every few steps. That is a self-esteem intervention in neurologic clothing: fewer falls and fewer paranoid accusations mean the patient is less forced to live as a ruined, accused self.

2009-249.sentence: The crawling ache at bedtime is a raw, unthinkable urge that gets evacuated by pacing—walk it out of the mind so sleep can start. Bromocriptine, a dopamine agonist, is the usual pharmacologic container here: it holds restless legs syndrome long enough that the feeling becomes a treatable symptom instead of a nightly nameless dread.

2009-250.sentence: Thunderclap pain and a stiff neck dump unmetabolized terror into the room until someone can name the vessel. Anterior communicating artery aneurysm is that name: once angiography locates the bleed source, the catastrophe becomes a thinkable, operable fact instead of nameless dread.

2009-251.sentence: Late-life “depression” that is mostly hypersomnia and unrefreshing sleep in morbid obesity often means the night is failing the self, not that the character is weak. Polysomnography is the honest mirror: it shows whether apnea is stealing competence and mood, so you treat sleep rather than idealize another antidepressant.

2009-252.sentence: After a myocardial infarction, depression—not mania, panic, albumin, or even ejection fraction in this comparison—is the strongest predictor of death, so the trial comment is about their part: withdrawal from rehab, anhedonia, hopelessness. Psychological mindedness here is seeing that the sad, guilty, sleepless self is not a side note to the infarct but a risk factor you can name and treat.

2009-253.sentence: Acute inflammatory polyneuropathy will not wait for insight: demyelination with conduction block, prolonged distal latencies, and areflexic legs is a hard stop on time. The wish to keep treating this as anxiety or “secondary gain” is the defense; the limit is that the nerve will not remyelinate on your schedule.

2009-254.sentence: Projective identification is not just “they dumped a feeling on you.” The patient disavows a helpless, unhelpable self and then recruits you—via insistence that no clinician can understand—to live that identity in countertransference. If you start believing you are uniquely incompetent, you are wearing their discarded representation, not discovering a new fact about your skill.

2009-255.sentence: The finding is not more genetic loading or “minority risk”; it is greater vulnerability to the same stressful events once class already depletes reserve. A harsh superego—the inner judge that says poverty is a character defect—lets the system treat exposure as deserved rather than as a load the ego cannot metabolize.

2009-256.sentence: An overvalued idea is a wish for certainty about the defect colliding with a prohibition that still works: when challenged, the person can admit it may not be true. The symptom (hours of mirrors, social avoidance) holds both the drive to be rid of the imagined flaw and the remaining grip of reality testing that a delusion would have already surrendered.

2009-257.sentence: Phenelzine plus meperidine is not a “bad reaction” you remember later; hyperpyrexia, hypertension, and coma are the unrepresented interaction written into the body when the MAOI history never made it into a thinkable story. What cannot be held in the chart—old antidepressant, meperidine for chest pain—gets repeated as autonomic catastrophe instead of as a sentence someone said out loud.

2009-258.sentence: At nine months the Erikson task is still basic trust: can the world meet my rhythm, or do I bang alone? Attunement is the parent falling into “kaaa-bam” on the upswing and the stroke, turning motor exuberance into a shared beat that says you are not a closed circuit.

2009-259.sentence: Kohut’s move is empathic validation: you first show that the patient’s experience of being unseen is real, not a tantrum to be confronted. A missed callback can land as a selfobject failure—the therapist briefly stops being the mirroring presence that holds the self together.

2009-260.sentence: IPT leaves the childhood split alone and treats today’s lunch table as the live relationship problem. You help her use the friendships she already has as good objects she can actually lean on, instead of treating every coworker as a rejecting other.

2009-261.sentence: Carbamazepine induces CYP3A4 and can chew through a previously solid 10 mg of haloperidol. The returning voices are the blood level falling, not a new internal collapse of the mind.

2009-262.sentence: Alzheimer disease is the most common dementia after 65, and it unravels the autobiographical self that lets a person stay a continuous someone. Repeating questions and lost bills are the cortex failing the late-life task of holding a life story together.

2009-263.sentence: An AA sponsor is not the meeting chair or the chip-passer; they are one experienced member who guides the program one-to-one. That pairing sits on Erikson’s generativity: someone further along offers care so the newcomer can rebuild an adult identity without alcohol.

2009-264.sentence: Lithium can flare psoriasis even when mood is finally quiet. The plaques are not a symbolic protest; they are the salt acting on keratinocytes that the patient then has to wear on the skin.

2009-265.sentence: Adult menstrual and sexual function is a late developmental achievement; strong D2 blockade can shove it back into amenorrhea, low desire, and galactorrhea. Clozapine is the antipsychotic that mostly leaves that later-arriving HPG capacity standing.

2009-266.sentence: CLAS is the institution’s external conscience: you do not get a sanctioned pass to send someone home in a language they cannot read. The required act is patient-related materials in the patient’s native language, not a brochure about how diverse you hope to become.

2009-267.sentence: At 3 a.m. you are being recruited to become the person who finally shuts the ward up, and that feeling pushes you toward quetiapine, diphenhydramine, or a benzodiazepine. This item wants zolpidem first for insomnia in a 78-year-old with dementia, so name the countertransference hunger to over-sedate before you reach for an antipsychotic.

2009-268.sentence: In Capgras the face is seen, but the warm recognition that should attach to father never arrives, so the mind solves it by calling him an impostor. What cannot be felt as “this is my father” gets repeated as a stranger standing in his place.

2009-269.sentence: The idea of the father kicking the puppy is allowed; the rage, horror, and grief are not. Isolation of affect is that split: the drive-laden feeling is cut away so the story can be told as if it were weather.

2009-270.sentence: An advance directive is a conversation two people can still have while the patient is competent, not a monologue you start after life support has already changed the pair. Talk when both of you can still think together about future decisions.

2009-271.sentence: Flooding works only if the therapist stays a secure base: someone close enough that the patient can protest, borrow calm, and not flee the 15-minute talk. The unknown staff are the feared crowd; you are the person the patient uses to regulate while they stay in the room.

2009-272.sentence: MDMA can feel like instant ego strength—easy warmth, less shame, more closeness—until the body shows the cost: bruxism, sweats, heat, anorexia, and a harder time reaching orgasm. The jaw clench is the ego’s leftover job: holding tension the drug borrowed and then dumped.

2009-273.sentence: Alcohol splits the mind: the suicidal line is there, but the person who can name a plan, use judgment, or make a pact is not in the chair yet. Observe and reevaluate when he is sober so you interview the whole mind, not the intoxicated fragment.

2009-274.sentence: A lithium level of 4.5 with creatinine 3.0, diarrhea, twitching, and stupor is not a mood-frame problem; the medical frame comes first. Emergent hemodialysis is how you keep the patient alive so any later talk about the overdose can actually happen.

2009-275.sentence: Pictures of the nanny let the child keep a good object in mind and feel sad, which is Klein’s depressive concern: missing someone without having to hate or erase them. A quick replacement nanny would be a manic patch—plug the hole instead of letting the child repair the loss.

2009-276.sentence: An elevated mean corpuscular volume often holds the drinking the interview cannot hold: one self says “not that much,” the other self is already in the blood. Treat the MCV as the split made visible, then ask about alcohol without forcing the patient to choose a single story on the spot.

2009-277.sentence: This mind is not ready to uncover danger alone; it still borrows the mother’s face as an auxiliary ego at the curb. Technique follows that: you support the referencing function first, and you only interpret once the child can appraise the street without scanning her expression.

2009-278.sentence: Lithium can sit there like a moral obligation—the “good bipolar patient” never stops the mood stabilizer—even when it lengthens seizures and leaves the person postictally confused. A less rigid conscience holds lithium when it protects mood and lets it go for ECT when the protocol, level, kidneys, and hydration say the combination is no longer clean.

2009-279.sentence: Lorazepam is the benzodiazepine whose absorption actually arrives whether you give it by mouth or intramuscularly; diazepam by IM often never quite makes it into the bloodstream. Think of it as a developmental capacity: in an airway-watched, agitated patient you pick the drug whose effect shows up, not the one whose pharmacokinetics stall like a late milestone.

2009-280.sentence: Serotonin syndrome—restlessness, myoclonus, lower-limb hyperreflexia, diaphoresis, shivering, tremor, confusion—means this nervous system cannot use more uncovering of serotonergic tone. Technique is support: stop stacking agonists, treat the hyperreflexic storm, and only later ask what the added drug was meant to reach.

2009-281.sentence: The antidepressant becomes a third object in the room—rescuer, poison, proof of weakness—not a neutral chemical. Optimal work holds the good and bad of the pill inside the same treatment relationship so the patient does not split “real therapy” from “just meds.”

2009-282.sentence: Aspirin is the agent most likely to slow further infarcts in vascular dementia; each new stroke severs another route by which this person could still use a caregiver as a secure base. Protect the vessels and you protect remaining proximity-seeking; another lacune can leave them unable to find or use the very person who still regulates them.

2009-283.sentence: The exam is already a two-person event: she cannot feel her feet or her position in space, and you are the one who has to name that B12-related proprioceptive loss instead of chatting only about “memory.” Macrocytic anemia plus dorsal-column signs is the pair you make together—your hands on vibration and position sense, her body answering—so the deficiency does not stay a silent interpersonal miss.

2009-284.sentence: Competence is the part of the mind that can stay in the chair while you list risks, benefits, and alternatives; dissociation is the vertical split where that part clocks out even though the body signs. If she cannot hold the information long enough to choose freely, you do not have informed consent—you have a signature from the absent half.

2009-285.sentence: Ego strength here is the child’s capacity to sit with a twitch without the whole treatment collapsing. Stimulants have been shown to reduce tics in comorbid ADHD, so you do not treat the first motor jerk as a reason to abandon impulse control and school function.

2009-286.sentence: Denial would file Todd’s paresis and aphasia under “just postictal soup” and throw away the map. The transient right-arm weakness and speech loss localize the focus; you keep the deficit in view instead of wishing the seizure had no address.

2009-287.sentence: A variable-ratio slot machine is already an enactment: the house and the gambler are living the old “maybe this pull” scene instead of talking about the hunger. Unpredictable payouts keep the pair repeating the lever press long after talk would have named the loss.

2009-288.sentence: Double depression changes the frame: years of dysthymia plus a new major episode with hopelessness and suicide talk is not a Tuesday-afternoon “mild dysphoria” visit. You hold time, safety, and the limit on leaving him in bed with a chronic-only diagnosis while the acute risk is in the room.

2009-289.sentence: A triptan is not a neutral abortive here. After a myocardial infarction it can feel like a demand to make the headache vanish now, while the coronary bed is being asked to vasoconstrict. Name the CAD limit out loud so the pill is neither poison nor proof that you refuse to help.

2009-290.sentence: An alcohol blackout is anterograde amnesia while the person stays awake. Split-off hours can be dumped into you as if you were there and they were not. That is projective identification: they park the missing night in the interviewer so they do not have to own what they did while conscious.

2009-291.sentence: Adoption designs fail when adoptive and biological parents resemble one another, so “genes versus home” never fully separates. The child then carries two sets of similar objects, and good and bad get assigned to nature or nurture to keep one parent pair clean. Ask about selective placement before you split the finding that way.

2009-292.sentence: Billing a missed visit is ethical only when the fee sits in the contractual agreement you both already accepted. That is the industry-versus-inferiority task: a written rule, not a last-minute scolding about whether the excuse was good enough. Keep the fee in the frame so it is competence, not punishment.

2009-293.sentence: Lateral medullary stroke in a 56-year-old who smokes with diabetes and hypertension is a vascular event, not “anxious dizziness.” Class and smoking history sit in the room as a third: do not let the consult become a story about panic in people who “don’t take care of themselves.” Hoarseness, ipsilateral face pin loss, and veering left keep the body, not the stereotype, in charge.

2009-294.sentence: Paroxetine still leans on muscarinic receptors, so anticholinergic load can stall bowel, memory, and a mind that never quite got a sturdy adult filter. Late-life cognition is a developmental capacity that can slip backward under extra acetylcholine blockade. Choose another SSRI when constipation and mild cognitive impairment are already in the picture.

2009-295.sentence: The mean is doing a job the mode will not: it lets the long-stay outliers pull the “typical” stay toward the tail so the rare catastrophe speaks for the whole ward. Report it only if you want those few marathon admissions to dominate the story; otherwise the median stays nearer the brief stays everyone actually lives.

2009-296.sentence: The adolescent is recruiting you as the adult who will finally certify an identity and end the uncertainty. Feel that pull to name it, then refuse the role: most people first recognize a same-sex orientation in adolescence, and your job is to stay curious rather than become the labeler.

2009-297.sentence: Mesial temporal sclerosis—hippocampal atrophy plus T2 hyperintensity—is doing explanatory work the failed drugs cannot: it locates the seizures in a scarred memory circuit instead of in “nonadherence.” Once the MRI names the lesion, the team can stop treating the patient as morally stubborn and start talking about epilepsy surgery.

2009-298.sentence: The proud announcement is a wish for recognition colliding with an old prohibition against needing anything from you. Offer congratulations first: that gratifies the wish in reality so you do not enact the critic by going silent, interpreting the need, or auditing the grades.

2009-299.sentence: Amphetamine leaves a urine trace for only one to two days, so the body cannot testify about last week. When the patient’s timeline and the screen disagree, treat that gap as unrepresented time rather than as a confession—the assay is a short witness, not a memory.

2009-300.sentence: Genetic anticipation means the next generation gets earlier onset or worse illness, so the child cannot lean on a still-well parent as a secure base for as long. Name the pedigree pattern aloud: the attachment system is being asked to hold more illness, sooner, in the person who still needs caretaking.

2010-1.sentence: Telling the worker the exam is not confidential is the secure-base move: you name who actually holds you so they are not lulled into treating you like their doctor. Proximity to the employer’s request is the frame; if you hide that, they will protest later as if you betrayed a treating alliance you never offered.

2010-2.sentence: Getting the phone number and address first stops the enactment: you refuse to become the helpless listener while command hallucinations keep running the scene. Location is how you leave the two-person panic and put a real body on a map instead of trading threats about police or quizzes about drugs.

2010-3.sentence: Digit span is the mind still here: six numbers held and handed back before they fall through. Immediate recall is not yesterday’s dinner or school history; it tests whether attention stayed in the chair or left without standing up.

2010-4.sentence: Levodopa is the feed that idiopathic Parkinson disease still answers; the one-sided tremor and bradykinesia say the nigrostriatal system is starving unevenly, not globally poisoned. When the pill works on that asymmetric onset, it is proof of a remaining dopamine relationship, not the mute wall of vertical gaze palsy, early dementia, or failed levodopa.

2010-5.sentence: Stopping the neuroleptic and adding a dopamine agonist undoes the blockade instead of denying the fever and rigidity. Bromocriptine or another agonist is the opposite of more phenothiazine: you give back what the D2 lockout took, not more poison.

2010-6.sentence: Rett disorder asks whether anyone can still see the child’s part after the regression: the lost hand use, midline wringing, and decelerated head growth after a good first 18 months. A trial comment is developmental, not blaming—“she had skills, then they went”—so the picture is MECP2-era Rett, not late autism or Fragile X.

2010-7.sentence: The 1974 DSM-II revision that dropped homosexuality is a frame decision: the profession, not the patient, decides what counts as illness and what stays off the chart. Read that change as an ethics of the limit—who holds the diagnostic boundary—rather than as proof that an identity was ever a disease or that a later edition made it vanish.

2010-8.sentence: Valproate’s neural-tube risk is not a side note; it is the symptom-cost the drug is already writing into a future pregnancy. Name that meaning out loud: the same molecule that steadies mood or seizures can interrupt folic-acid–dependent closure of the tube, so contraception and folate become part of what the prescription is doing.

2010-9.sentence: MELAS shows a developmental capacity that arrived and then will not stay: after seizures begin around age nine, motor and sensory skills that should be consolidated drop out for days to weeks as mitochondrial energy fails. The changing MRI and hemicranial headaches are the same story in tissue—stroke-like episodes that migrate because the child’s brain never gets a stable metabolic floor.

2010-10.sentence: Poststroke depression is the most common psychiatric presentation, so the first technical choice is support, not excavation. This mind is already working with a damaged substrate; uncovering conflict while the patient is withdrawn from rehab usually costs more than naming the mood, treating it, and keeping the person in the room with therapy.

2010-11.sentence: Needle exchange is a two-person deal: you stay in the relationship while the patient is still injecting, instead of making abstinence the price of contact. Harm reduction here is interpersonal work—you and the patient build a pattern that reduces HIV and hepatitis risk together, rather than you holding a one-person demand they cannot yet meet.

2010-12.sentence: Therapeutic index measures safety: how close the useful dose sits to the toxic one, which is why some drugs need a person and a lab as a secure base. Serum levels are attachment technology—the clinician and the assay keep the patient near enough to the medicine without crossing into harm when hydration, interactions, or adherence shift.

2010-13.sentence: Valproate works here because it can carry the whole generalized syndrome—myoclonus plus GTCS—without needing a second agent. Ego strength is that same capacity: the brain, and the person, can hold a surge of activity without fragmenting into a second, worse solution. Narrow-spectrum drugs like carbamazepine or phenytoin fail both jobs; they can worsen myoclonus the way a brittle defense worsens the affect it cannot contain.

2010-14.sentence: In autism the social cue is often not registered, so there is nothing to turn away from. Dissociation is a later, more expensive move: the child leaves the scene while still in the chair. PTSD, depression, and social phobia still track faces; they just cannot stay with what they see.

2010-15.sentence: Herpes simplex is already in the geniculate ganglion, then it lights up as Bell’s palsy. That is an enactment: the old viral partner returns as a one-sided facial crisis instead of remaining a silent guest. The pair has been living together for years; the palsy is the relationship becoming visible.

2010-16.sentence: Insurers pay most often for patient self-harm, not for sex, fraud, or a missed side effect. Denial is the defense that makes this statistic: if the wish to die is treated as noise rather than the central risk, the chart looks calm while the danger stays live. Thorough suicide documentation is suppression done right—you keep the threat in view instead of wishing it gone.

2010-17.sentence: Kraepelin’s gift was course: some psychoses remit between mood episodes, others grind into deficit. Self-esteem in a young psychiatrist often hangs on an idealized ancestor who can tell those stories apart. You borrow his longitudinal eye so you do not confuse a recoverable illness with one that will need a longer, humbler frame.

2010-18.sentence: Most homicide is ordinary rage, jealousy, and intoxication, not paranoid psychosis. The countertransference trap is to become the expert who locates the danger only in Axis I, because that role feels safer than facing a non-ill person who can still kill. Stay with threats, weapons, and the story of the slight; do not recruit yourself as the one who “explains it away” as illness.

2010-19.sentence: Fragile X is a CGG triple-repeat on FMR1, not a moral verdict on the family. Guilt about “passing something on” belongs in genetic counseling, not in the karyotype.

2010-20.sentence: A cluster attack is a 60–90 minute autonomic storm: one-sided retro-orbital pain, tearing, rhinorrhea, and pacing. Reality testing stays intact; affect tolerance does not, so you abort the bout instead of coaching him to sit still through it.

2010-21.sentence: When a caregiver sometimes yields after saying no, that occasional yes is intermittent reinforcement. The child keeps seeking the person as a regulator because the slot machine still pays, which is why the behavior resists extinction.

2010-22.sentence: Repeating the same plan to a relative who cannot encode it is already an enactment: you are living the memory failure instead of measuring it. A 10-item word-list learning task names the hippocampal problem the conversation keeps bumping into.

2010-23.sentence: A securely attached 4-year-old who bargains for one more story is using language to delay a ordinary conflict, not leaving the room in a split. That is development doing its job: words instead of collapse or triangulation.

2010-24.sentence: Narcissistic exploitativeness treats the other person as a selfobject, a function to be used, not a mind with a claim. The coworkers who finish his work are proof of entitlement, not partners in a relationship.

2010-25.sentence: Denial is the move here: the drinker treats stopping as if GABA tone will just hold, so last-drink time never gets asked. The generalized seizure hours to a few days later is the nervous system refusing that story; phenytoin will not rewrite the timeline.

2010-26.sentence: Psychological mindedness on this list means noticing your own part: leaving lithium on during ECT is how you help write the cognitive fog. A trial comment to the team is enough—“If lithium stays, we will not know what is illness and what is the treatment.”

2010-27.sentence: You hold the frame first: a private room, names, each step named before it happens, no one entering unasked. Legal talk, referrals, and guilt work wait until safety is actually restored; rushing them is another loss of control.

2010-28.sentence: The daughter brings the infidelity talk as something to evacuate—get rid of it with risperidone 0.5 while donepezil stays. Containing it means you sit with the raw dread of a fading spouse, keep regular visits, and let the fluctuating Alzheimer accusation become thinkable instead of a pill.

2010-29.sentence: Your capacity exam for this refusal can be finished today; competency cannot. Only a judicial hearing ends or limits that legal status, and no petition, neuropsych battery, or attorney letter can rush that ending.

2010-30.sentence: The unrepresented state lives on the skin: hours of washing to excoriation instead of a memory that can be told. Fluvoxamine 200 to 300 mg daily is the dose that can quiet that loop enough for the fear of making others sick to become words, not ritual.

2010-31.sentence: The family already cast this adolescent as clumsy; after the grand mal they recruit you as either the next adult who shrugs off the morning jerks or the one who names juvenile myoclonic epilepsy. Notice if you feel pulled to over-reassure so they stop looking frightened, or to over-investigate so you never have to sit with their shame about dropped objects.

2010-32.sentence: Declarative memory is the hippocampus-and-parahippocampal-gyrus job of keeping facts you can tell; when that fails, the self that “knows things” goes dark even if procedural skill still works. The wound is to competence: the patient can still do, but cannot hold a name or a morning’s discussion, so self-esteem collapses around being unable to be a reliable knower.

2010-33.sentence: The wish is to be the one therapist who holds the adolescent and the family at once; the prohibition is the dual-relationship rule that those two jobs cannot occupy the same person. The symptom of saying yes is a compromise: you gratify the rescue wish and then leak confidentiality across rooms you were never meant to sit in together.

2010-34.sentence: Indiscriminate warmth after early foster-care disruption is not extra love; it is a child who cannot wait for a selective attachment to ripen. Reactive attachment disorder here is a limit problem: closeness with strangers comes cheap because the capacity for one enduring other cannot be rushed on the school’s timetable.

2010-35.sentence: Transient global amnesia dumps a raw “why am I in the hospital” that will not become a story; the patient evacuates it by asking again instead of thinking it. Your job is containment: you hold the repeating question and the intact recognition of family so the blank last two hours stay thinkable and do not turn into nameless dread.

2010-36.sentence: Group therapy is the frame that refuses the schizoid bargain of perfect fantasy friends and no real ones. The other members, the clock, and the room are the ethical limit: relatedness has to happen with actual people, not only inside the elaborate inner cast.

2010-37.sentence: Content validity is the test of whether each item actually maps onto the construct—rapport, history, risk, MSE—not whether the form merely looks like an interview exam. A trial comment works the same way: you listen for whether the patient can use it as their own part of the story, or whether you only scored face validity.

2010-38.sentence: Calling this “somatoform pain” when the tongue is large and percussion myoedema is sitting there is denial: you refuse the medical fact because a tidy psych label is less frightening. Name the hypothyroidism first; then you can talk about mood and aching without using a diagnosis as a cover.

2010-39.sentence: Each visit and each negative scan functions as a demand and a proof of need: the body must be gravely ill or the care would not be deserved. Insight is poor here, so do not argue the hypochondriasis away; offer a regular appointment as a reliable feed rather than another hunt for the hidden lesion.

2010-40.sentence: Methadone is the first medication here because it is a steady selfobject: it replaces the crashing opioid supply and lets a fragmenting self feel held again. Clonidine can blunt noradrenergic noise, but it does not restore that idealized, regulating presence the way methadone does in combined heroin–alcohol withdrawal.

2010-41.sentence: Secondary gain is the distinguishing motive in malingering; factitious disorder is after the sick role itself. Contain that raw mix—money, disability talk, fear of being seen as a fake—until a thinkable wish can be named, instead of evacuating the consult as “just malingering.”

2010-42.sentence: Codeine has already called time: pinpoint pupils, hypoventilation, and blue lips mean the respiratory limit is not a negotiation. Airway and naloxone come first because you cannot interpret an overdose until breathing is restored.

2010-43.sentence: The staff’s “drug-seeking” story is a trial comment you can test with them: can they see their own part—fear of being used—without dumping it onto the patient? Methadone maintenance covers withdrawal, not cancer pain, so the useful interpretation is of the team, not of the request: give more opioid because tolerance is real.

2010-44.sentence: The frame is the set of limits that keep the work a treatment: time, fee, place, confidentiality. Homemade cookies near termination are a modest, one-time crossing of that frame; stretching the hour, café sessions with a borderline patient, investment tips as payment, and “anger means you’re fired” are violations that serve the therapist’s need, not the work.

2010-45.sentence: The Rorschach is the least structured test: an inkblot with almost no instruction becomes whatever the patient needs it to be—feed, poison, demand, or proof they are seen. MMPI, WAIS-III, TAT, and sentence completion still hand the patient a story, item, or stem; the blot hands them a blank and asks who they are with you.

2010-46.sentence: The young patient (and sometimes the ED) can use suppression—pushing the fear of stroke out of awareness on purpose—because the whole-field heat-wave vision, vertigo, dysarthria, bilateral acral and perioral tingling, then occipital headache is a story that has ended before. Name the pattern basilar migraine (brainstem aura) so the defense does not have to do the neurology for you.

2010-47.sentence: If the team keeps asking only for first-grade, grandma’s summer, the first sled ride, or a TV gag, they are enacting “prove you remember us”—a two-person repetition of reunion, not a memory exam. Semantic memory is the shared calendar fact: the town parade is every July 4th; that is knowledge, not a scene with you.

2010-48.sentence: Factitious disorder is organized around assuming the sick role, not around money, a hidden “real” diagnosis, or beating the doctor. The cultural third is the hospital’s hierarchy of worthy patients: illness as identity when other identities feel unlivable.

2010-49.sentence: Nonmaleficence sits on Erikson’s generativity: you already hold the power to change a body, so the adult task is to refuse the move that would injure even when the wish to “do something” is loud. Beneficence is the wish to give; nonmaleficence is the pause that keeps that gift from becoming an assault.

2010-50.sentence: Reduced hippocampal volumes mean the organ that files new memory is shrinking, so the past cannot be retrieved as a story. What cannot be remembered returns as repetition in the body and the family: the same question, the same search, the same agitation, lived instead of told.

2010-51.sentence: One rejection letter and the student recruits you as the next admissions office: you will either bless or crush the whole future. Name the distortion—overgeneralization and all-or-none thinking—so you stay a therapist who thinks with the student, not another verdict.

2010-52.sentence: Point prevalence is a still photograph: the proportion of a population with the disease at one specific time, not a lifetime sentence. A rigid conscience wants a lasting verdict; this statistic only says who met criteria on that date.

2010-53.sentence: A prion is a protein that never arrived at a livable fold, then teaches other proteins the same failed shape. In fatal familial insomnia the developmental capacity for sleep does not consolidate; rest itself never quite arrives, and the nervous system unravels around that missing function.

2010-54.sentence: The record has to show why you rejected alternative ways of responding—hospitalize, restrain, send home—because every choice is also an ending of the other paths. You cannot rush that limit: write the reasons you did not take the unused roads, so the note holds the stop as well as the plan.

2010-55.sentence: Give thiamine before glucose so the confused, ataxic, ophthalmoplegic state can become thinkable instead of pouring more fuel into Wernicke’s metabolic fire. That is containment: you metabolically hold the raw collapse so it is not evacuated into worse neuronal death.

2010-56.sentence: Those rapidly shifting, shallow emotions are a bid for mirroring: the self feels real only when the room lights up. Idealizing the audience props self-esteem that does not hold from the inside, which is why histrionic affect looks theatrical and does not last.

2010-57.sentence: The violent startle and spontaneous myoclonus of spongiform encephalopathy are not a forbidden wish breaking through a prohibition. Cortex is being destroyed; do not interpret the jerks as conflict when the finding points to prion disease.

2010-58.sentence: Rapport is the first shared good object: ease, compassion, and quiet expertise let the patient bring pain without splitting you into useless or persecutory. You hold both sides of the relationship so the interview can stay one person talking to one person.

2010-59.sentence: Develop discrepancy is the right dose of technique: set the wish to drink beside the wish to parent instead of confronting denial. This mind uses support that makes the gap visible; a hard uncovering attack usually hardens resistance.

2010-60.sentence: Cognitive slowing with untreated HCV, normal ammonia, and no HIV is not a psychic conflict dressed as fog. Name HCV infection of brain; do not force a wish-versus-prohibition story onto a virus in parenchyma.

2010-61.sentence: A random-assault survivor often still has a self that can use you as a mirror: someone who sees their courage as they approach the memory, rather than as a collapsed ideal. That leftover self-esteem is why graded exposure can land as competence work instead of another shattering.

2010-62.sentence: When you hold three words across a few minutes, you are not only scoring short-term memory; you are briefly the person who might forget them too. Notice if you rush the delay or over-coach—countertransference often wants to rescue the exam so neither of you feels dumb.

2010-63.sentence: Interferon can pour cytokine heat into a mood that never found words, so suicidal ideation is the body finishing a sentence the mind never wrote. Treat that SI as already-present despair looking for a chemical amplifier, not as a side-effect trivia fact.

2010-64.sentence: A six-year-old exploring genitals in the tub is ordinary phallic-stage curiosity, not a dissociative reenactment of abuse. Shame from the adult is what splits the child from the body; a calm privacy rule keeps the experience thinkable and owned.

2010-65.sentence: Fever plus lead-pipe rigidity means the ego’s body-regulation has failed after an antipsychotic push: affect, muscle, and autonomic control collapse together. That is not a coping problem you talk through; it is NMS, and you stop the drug before anyone tries to “contain” it psychologically.

2010-66.sentence: Ambivalence after a near-lethal overdose, a thin “I am sorry,” and no regret for surviving is raw dread that cannot yet be thought—Bion’s nameless stuff looking for a container. Inpatient hospitalization is that container: you hold the impulse in a locked frame until it can become a feeling instead of another evacuation.

2010-67.sentence: Lithium’s common ECG finding is benign T-wave flattening, and that is a limit you cannot rush past: the heart can look a little “tired” on the tracing without meaning the myocardium is failing. Name the T waves as a known, usually reversible lithium effect so the patient’s fear of a dying heart can become something you both can think about instead of an emergency that ends the medicine.

2010-68.sentence: Valid consent for brain surgery in intractable OCD is the reasonable-patient standard: what most patients would want to know, not what you or the most panicked person would pick. Technique follows capacity here—give material risks, benefits, and alternatives in ordinary language; this mind may need support more than a full uncovering of every theoretical catastrophe.

2010-69.sentence: Kohut’s self psychology is not drive conflict or Erikson’s epigenetic stages; it is the need for empathic interaction with self-objects, people who lend cohesion when the self wobbles. When the resident misses a real accomplishment, the hurt is often a selfobject failure: the patient needed to be seen, not analyzed as vanity.

2010-70.sentence: Neck pain radiating down the arm plus gait change and urinary incontinence is a cord-compression clock; MRI of the cervical spine cannot wait for a prettier story about anxiety. Some limits are anatomic: once the cord is being squeezed, insight work and urodynamics are too late.

2010-71.sentence: After a myocardial infarction, sertraline is the antidepressant that holds the cardiac risk without asking a damaged heart to carry TCA quinidine-like effects, SNRI pressor load, or MAOI diet rules. Contain the post-infarct despair—hold the raw “my pump failed, I am finished” feeling—long enough that it can become thinkable rather than evacuated into a risky drug.

2010-72.sentence: Double-blind exists to kill examiner-expectation bias: if the rater knows who got drug versus placebo, hope and loyalty leak into the scores. The research frame is an ethic of not knowing on purpose; you hold that limit so the data, not your wish to look effective, decides the result.

2010-73.sentence: Klein’s depressive position is the capacity to see a loved person as both good and harmed, then feel guilt and want to repair. A trial comment that names the patient’s own fury and the wish to make it right tests whether they can use that insight instead of only punishing themselves.

2010-74.sentence: A fixed belief that undercover agents will kill him is a delusion: an unshakable idea that bypasses testing, not a mis-seen object or a made-up memory. Erikson’s last-stage task is integrity versus despair; when that work collapses into terror of being hunted, the mind trades a bearable life review for a persecutory story.

2010-75.sentence: Normal pressure hydrocephalus is wet, wobbly, and wacky—gait first, then thinking, then sphincter—without the headache or papilledema of high pressure. The assigned cultural-third lens does not live in this triad, so stay with the finding: do not call it Alzheimer until you have asked whether walking failed before memory did.

2010-76.sentence: Parent management training works because the child’s oppositional battles are often a bid for a coherent response when praise and limits have gone missing. Mirroring here is not flattery; it is the parent noticing competence and setting a firm frame so self-esteem is earned, not extracted by winning the fight.

2010-77.sentence: Citalopram helped the mood, but morning headaches plus clonazepam-triggered crash point to sleep apnea, not a need for more sedation. The symptom is doing double duty: it looks like residual anxiety while it is actually a blocked airway asking not to be covered with a benzodiazepine.

2010-78.sentence: Nonfluent aphasia after a middle-cerebral-artery stroke usually spares comprehension enough that “Close your eyes” still works, while speech, repetition, and a hospital narrative do not. Attachment is regulation through another person; the consult becomes a secure base when you use a one-step command the patient can actually do, instead of demanding talk they cannot produce.

2010-79.sentence: Horizontal nystagmus plus paranoia and ataxia is a PCP-level assault on ego strength: reality testing, impulse control, and affect tolerance all fail at once. You contain first—low stimulation, vitals, safety—because you cannot interpret a mind that cannot hold a thought.

2010-80.sentence: Voices arguing about the patient in the third person recruit you into the same triangle: two others deciding who he is while he listens. Notice the pull to become the third voice—the one who judges, sides, or silences—before you start documenting Schneider.

2010-81.sentence: Venlafaxine raising blood pressure can be the body saying what the history still cannot: norepinephrine climbing when words for threat never formed. Titrate and check the cuff, and also ask what the pressure is carrying that never got a story.

2010-82.sentence: Alexithymia is the compromise when a wish and a prohibition collide: feel it and you risk acting; name it and you risk knowing. Chest tightness and sleeplessness keep the drive in the soma so neither desire nor guilt has to take the floor.

2010-83.sentence: Language development is the old Asperger–autism split because words are how a child first gets a usable mirror. Delayed speech starves that mirroring; phrase speech on time still lets competence and self-esteem grow even when interests stay narrow.

2010-84.sentence: IPT’s middle phase stays on current relationships because that is intimacy versus isolation in real time, not in the transference. The promotion-versus-friend dispute is the psychosocial task: can two adult needs sit in one week without one person disappearing.

2010-85.sentence: Akathisia is the body screaming that dopamine blockade has become unlivable; the pacing and “crawl out of my skin” feeling is not anxiety you talk through first. Propranolol quiets the adrenergic surge so the patient can stay inside their own motor system instead of using restlessness as an exit.

2010-86.sentence: A ten-year-old who can wait for a dollar every third clean already has a working delay: the mind can count and hold the rule without a parent standing there. Fixed-ratio training is scaffolding that capacity, not magic—drop the schedule too fast and the internal counter collapses.

2010-87.sentence: The conference podium turns the audience into a live conscience: tremor and tachycardia become proof that the trainee is about to be found wanting. Atenolol, taken shortly before exposure, lowers that bodily exhibit so the superego cannot use the heart as a gavel.

2010-88.sentence: Admission is not the hour to excavate death anxiety; the mind that just lost home needs information, not uncovering. Naming the living will as optional paper—not a demand to refuse treatment—keeps the work supportive and inside what an eighty-year-old in transition can use.

2010-89.sentence: At nine, right and wrong still live in the adult who will punish, not yet inside a whole object that can be loved and survived. Kohlberg’s consequence stage means good and bad are held by the teacher’s hand, not by an internalized pair the child can argue with.

2010-90.sentence: Blepharospasm steals the developmental job of looking: the lids slam the world shut so driving, reading, and faces drop out. Botulinum toxin is the intervention that returns the capacity to keep the eyes open; talk does not reopen a lid the muscle has locked.

2010-91.sentence: Learned helplessness is operant: after the environment stops pairing effort with any change in outcome, the person stops emitting the response that used to look like trying. The “symptom” is not laziness; it is a learned shutdown of agency that once protected them from more failed attempts.

2010-92.sentence: The interruption lands on the same Erikson ground as the hour itself: can this pair still hold trust after the adult world barged in. Spend the leftover minutes on what the wait felt like, not on making the clock whole, or you skip the developmental repair the rupture just asked for.

2010-93.sentence: AACAP still wants a distinct period of abnormal mood with episodic symptoms, not a temperament that is always loud, frustrated, or culturally “too much.” If you collapse chronic irritability into bipolar I, you pathologize a child’s identity and environment instead of naming a true mood episode.

2010-94.sentence: Beneficence is the ethical name for acting when the patient cannot yet hold concern for their own body—the Kleinian move from “get this persecutor off me” to someone who can later repair. Paternalism is justified only while you are containing danger they cannot metabolize; it is not a license to stay the all-good parent after capacity returns.

2010-95.sentence: The adoption design shows a biological parent’s alcohol dependence raising risk in the child even when the adoptive home is shared—that is the disease model’s claim about inheritance, not a moral stain. Hold the good and bad of that fact: genes load the gun, but the current relationship and the bottle still have to be worked with as lived objects.

2010-96.sentence: Zaleplon is a short-acting hypnotic for sleep-onset only; it does not invite a long night of sedation or a deep dive into why they cannot let the day go. Support the mind that cannot yet surrender to sleep; do not uncover the night with a long-acting sedative when the clinical job is simply to start sleep.

2010-97.sentence: The depressive position is two-person work: you and the patient stop taking turns as the all-good or all-bad partner and practice staying in the room after a disappointment. Comfort with “the good with the bad” is not a solo insight; it is what happens when neither of you has to split the relationship to keep it from feeling ruined.

2010-98.sentence: Vertical-gaze slowing plus axial rigidity and falls is progressive supranuclear palsy, not garden-variety Parkinson disease, and the stay-at-home anxiety is often proximity-seeking after the body stopped being a secure base. Treat the fear of leaving as attachment protest to a failing motor system, not as a free-floating phobia you can talk away.

2010-99.sentence: Reduced REM latency is a lab marker of depression, not a reason to diagnose from a sleep study alone. Ego strength still lives in the daytime: can the patient tolerate affect and hold a schedule when early REM and early-morning awakening shred the night.

2010-100.sentence: Acculturation is keeping family recipes while taking up American ballroom dancing—heritage and host culture both stay live, which is not assimilation’s wipe-and-replace. In the room, culture is a third person: ask which practices still feed identity instead of assuming the dancing means the old self is gone.

2010-101.sentence: First you engage the adolescent and family to shrink drug-seeking, not extract an abstinence vow that often just dumps the “bad addict” into the kid. That is Kleinian repair: help them hold a using teen who is still their child, instead of splitting into persecutor-parent and evacuated-bad-object patient.

2010-102.sentence: First-time cannabis panic with pounding heart and fear of dying gets lorazepam, not an SSRI, antipsychotic, or naloxone. Ego strength is down: the patient cannot hold the surge, so a short-acting benzo is temporary affect-control until reality testing and the body come back.

2010-103.sentence: Complex partial seizures take the mind offline for minutes—automatisms, unresponsiveness, then amnesia—so this is not a moment for uncovering conflict. Stabilize the frame, get a witness history, and treat the circuit; insight work waits until the cortex is back in the room.

2010-104.sentence: The ED group is running on missing bodies; this physician is using caffeine intoxication—rambling speech, flush, palpitations—to stay the extra pair of hands. Two people made the pattern: the director notices the activation, and the stimulant is covering a schedule neither of them named as unsustainable.

2010-105.sentence: Mirtazapine’s alpha2-adrenergic antagonism lets norepinephrine and serotonin rise; H1 blockade then sedates and stimulates appetite. Attachment-wise, the pill becomes a reliable night presence—sleep and food return first so the person can use another human as a secure base later.

2010-106.sentence: In children the most common cause of delirium is central nervous system infection, which shreds attention and reality testing overnight. Ego strength here is not character; it is a febrile brain that cannot hold a thought still until you treat the infection.

2010-107.sentence: Corticobasal ganglionic degeneration can split the body from ownership: the alien left arm rises while the person does not claim it, with right-greater atrophy, rigidity, and apraxia. That is a neurologic dissociation, a vertical split—the limb acts and the self is not in the chair with it.

2010-108.sentence: A negative therapeutic reaction is getting worse after an accurate, well-timed interpretation, not after a clumsy one. The self that needed to stay small cannot yet take in being understood; the insight lands as a blow to the old way of earning love.

2010-109.sentence: Control is this man's wish after the infarct: if he can interrogate every test and pill, he is not a passive body on the floor. The team answers the questions and pulls him into the plan so the wish can work in reality instead of colliding with a staff prohibition that would turn him into a defiant, refusing patient.

2010-110.sentence: Bilateral parotid enlargement is not just a gland finding; it is the body advertising a secret purge the patient cannot say. The swelling does work for the person: it lets vomiting stay unnamed while still marking the anorexia as a binge-purge pattern you must treat, not simple restriction.

2010-111.sentence: Winnicott's holding environment is the developmental capacity that arrives when parenting is consistent and reliable enough that the infant does not have to organize the world alone. If that safe context never quite arrives, later transitions feel like falling, and treatment starts by restoring predictability rather than interpreting content.

2010-112.sentence: The conscience that says “do not be dramatic” is a dangerous luxury when myasthenia plus fever produces clammy fatigue and a failing airway. Mechanical ventilation first is the ethical override: you do not let guilt about “overreacting” delay the tube while IVIG, steroids, or plasmapheresis wait their turn.

2010-113.sentence: Serial sevens recruit you as the examiner who will either stay with the patient's effort or grow impatient and fill in the numbers. Watch that countertransference: irritation at the slow 100-minus-7s is data about concentration, not a cue to abandon the task or treat it as a memory test.

2010-114.sentence: Khat chewing held a good object in East African work and social life: the leaf was concentration, belonging, and stamina, not “a drug.” If you only hear the bad object of stimulant misuse, you split the immigrant from the plant that organized his long hours and you lose the alliance you need to assess dependence.

2010-115.sentence: Atomoxetine is not a bigger bang in the cleft; it is a selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor, so the therapeutic action sits at NET, not at an alpha-2 agonist, SERT, dual pumps, or dumping dopamine. If you catch yourself wanting the drug to “do more,” that is the old wish for a stimulant-style flood—name the pump and you stop treating a fantasy.

2010-116.sentence: Turner syndrome puts a body-third in the room: short stature, delayed puberty, cardiac history, and a verbal-over-performance IQ split that does not match the expected girlhood script. The social immaturity is not “just personality”; it is identity work around a karyotype that will not produce the usual pubertal passport, so you name Turner before you name autism.

2010-117.sentence: This couple is stalled on intimacy versus isolation: vestibular pain has become the third party that keeps sex, and mutuality, off the table. Nortriptyline titrated slowly treats the vestibulodynia; couple conflict work is not the first move when touch itself still hurts.

2010-118.sentence: After prolonged deprivation, Stage 4—deep slow-wave sleep—is what restores the functions the shorter nights stole; Stages 1–2, even REM, do not carry that homeostatic debt. You cannot talk someone out of needing that depth, and you cannot rush the rebound: the limit is physiologic time, not will.

2010-119.sentence: A useful trial comment is: the fear is choking, not calories or shape—so this is specific phobia after one panic-while-eating episode, not an eating disorder or panic disorder. If they can see that the avoided pasta is a feared sensation in the throat, they have enough mind to work the phobia instead of shrinking the plate forever.

2010-120.sentence: The harsh superego—your inner rule-maker—wants to bar the spouse at the door in the name of purity and confidentiality. The grown-up frame is yes if the patient wishes, plus a later private hour: conscience that can make a sanctioned exception without handing the whole interview to the couple.

2010-121.sentence: Desipramine plus cocaine is two noradrenergic engines on one immature brake: the blood-pressure system cannot yet wait out withdrawal without stacking a TCA and a stimulant. Hypertension is the body saying the capacity to delay gratification never quite arrived, so catecholamines do the waiting for him.

2010-122.sentence: An adverse life event that cannot be put into words often does not become a story; it becomes a bipolar depressive episode. What cannot be remembered as loss is repeated as anergy, so you treat the mood and still name the job loss as the unrepresented hit.

2010-123.sentence: Bilateral anterior cingulate infarction steals initiation, so the awake, tracking patient recruits you to become the missing will. Notice the countertransference pull to chatter, lift, or decide for him; that urgency is you filling a cingulate that no longer starts anything.

2010-124.sentence: Crushed methylphenidate tablets leave talc in the lung because the pill was used as a selfobject: a borrowed burst of competence injected when esteem collapsed. The granulomas are the body keeping the record of a self that needed the tablet’s shine more than an airway.

2010-125.sentence: Numbing and then a surge of arousal is the old fight between a wish to vanish and a drive to stay ready after the knifepoint robbery. Call it acute stress disorder while it is still inside a month; the clock, not the flavor of dissociation, is what keeps it from being PTSD.

2010-126.sentence: Varicella zoster virus waited in the dorsal root ganglion until immunity thinned, then ended latency as a unilateral vesicular belt. Time and limits work like that: you cannot rush a dormant infection, and you also cannot pretend the childhood chickenpox chapter is closed forever.

2010-127.sentence: Bupropion before ECT is an evacuation: the cortex cannot hold the planned seizure, so the charge dumps too early and the treatment cannot be thought through. Holding the drug off the list is containment—you keep the threshold nameable with the anesthesiologist instead of letting a premature fit speak for everyone.

2010-128.sentence: The limit you hold is time, not another consult: functional blindness after a witnessed murder is expected to lift in days or weeks if you do not install a chronic-patient frame. Colluding with endless lesion-hunting or a sick role keeps the eyes in the job of not seeing; naming a short course lets the symptom finish and leave.

2010-129.sentence: A trial comment to the parents—that the new sibling took the old place and the accidents came back to reclaim it—lets them see the child's part without calling it delay or acting out. That is psychological mindedness in a three-year-old's language: normal regression after a successful toilet training, not a new diagnosis.

2010-130.sentence: The split is doing work: pills live in one office and meaning in the other, so anger never has to sit in one relationship. The psychiatrist's job is to evaluate need, prescribe, and keep regular contact with the therapist so the patient cannot park the conflict in the gap.

2010-131.sentence: St. John's wort (Hypericum perforatum) induces the enzymes that clear cyclosporine, so graft protection falls while the patient feels they are taking something 'natural.' The herb is doing psychic work: it lets the person reclaim a piece of the body from the transplant clinic without naming the wish to be off the drug.

2010-132.sentence: Cyclothymia names the frequent few-day highs (inflated self, little sleep, racing thoughts, no marked impairment) and week-long downs (worthlessness, hypersomnia, hyperphagia) that never become bipolar II rapid cycling or a personality war. The swings keep the motor running—about twenty turns a year—without the cost of a full episode or a borderline label.

2010-133.sentence: This sits on Erikson’s trust-versus-mistrust task: the intravenous heroin user already expects to be treated as a “drug seeker,” so the pair either rebuilds basic trust or repeats abandonment. Name the cord emergency—spinal epidural abscess at T5 with a sensory level at the nipples—and you show that this body still gets believed.

2010-134.sentence: Object relations is about holding two versions of a rule in one mind without splitting them into all-good and all-bad. The Wisconsin Card Sorting Test asks exactly that: keep yesterday’s category and today’s category together; vascular-frontal injury dumps the old rule and perseverates.

2010-135.sentence: By about age 3 the child is moving from Klein’s paranoid-schizoid world of split part-objects toward a more whole self that can be loved and worried about. Core gender identity usually locks in on that timetable—not at 18 months, when the self is still in pieces.

2010-136.sentence: Tics live in a two-person field: shame, watching, and family alarm can amp the motor and vocal bursts as much as the basal ganglia do. When antipsychotics and alpha-2 agonists have already failed that shared pattern, tetrabenazine is the next move you make with a tic specialist, not another round of “try harder” at home.

2010-137.sentence: This mind cannot use uncovering right now; the work is support of a body in crisis. Prochlorperazine blocked dopamine and produced acute dystonia—wry neck, eyes stuck up and right—so you give diphenhydramine, not an interpretation and not more neuroleptic.

2010-138.sentence: Conjoint marital therapy asks for ego strengths the violent partner does not have in the room: impulse control, affect tolerance, and a shared reality that the other person is not property. Put them together and you get an enactment of coercion, not treatment; start with private individual work and safety.

2010-139.sentence: The open mouth, dysarthria, rigidity, and tremor are the body asking for a medical secure base, not an adolescent using argumentativeness as separation protest. Urinary copper excretion is the lab that lets you stay close to the real danger—Wilson disease with liver injury—instead of treating the parent or the teen as the problem to regulate.

2010-140.sentence: A harsh treatment conscience says you must never drop the clozapine that kept schizoaffective illness quiet for a year. Fever, dehydration, confusion, and rigidity sanction a break in that rule: stop clozapine now, because NMS or toxicity is not a moral failure to treat psychosis.

2010-141.sentence: Combativeness in Alzheimer disease often means the daughter's adult capacity to hold a parent has been exceeded, not that the 80-year-old can still learn from time-outs or a changing schedule. Assessing caregiver burnout names the developmental mismatch: the child-as-parent is exhausted, and that exhaustion is the intervention target if home care is to continue.

2010-142.sentence: Morning headache, vomiting, ataxia, falls, and diplopia are the posterior fossa speaking: a medulloblastoma blocking CSF, not a four-year-old's stomach or a wish to stay home. The symptom's job is to force imaging, not to carry a family conflict.

2010-143.sentence: Attribution is the story you tell about why something happened—internal, global, stable, or not—and that story sits on Erikson's identity task: who I am if this event is my fault forever. Causal explanations of events and personal experiences are not attachment styles or raw sensory meanings; they are the identity-work that can lock a resident into “I am incompetent” after one fail.

2010-144.sentence: Amphetamine had been a cheap selfobject: it mirrored energy and competence until the crash. Dysphoria and anhedonia after the high usually need 2 to 4 months to ease, so the empty, unmirrored self is not a one- or two-week dip you can pep-talk away.

2010-145.sentence: Mature object relations means this mourner can hold love and anger toward the same lost person without collapsing, so STPP can work the real collision: the wish to stay fused with the dead versus the prohibition on rage, guilt, and letting go. Supportive therapy soothes that conflict; STPP interprets it, which is why those patients outperform supportive care in complicated grief—and why male gender, age, and meds do not pick the winner.

2010-146.sentence: The opening line recruits you as the spouse’s enforcer—the person who will complete an evaluation someone else already decided. Asking “How do you feel about that?” refuses that transference role and puts the patient’s own affect, not the spouse’s mandate, in the chair; dates, the spouse’s treatment history, and joking that your spouse advises you too all keep you as the spouse’s stand-in.

2010-147.sentence: When meds have failed and there is no safely resectable focus, the team is being asked to become the person who will finally “cut out” the bad part—pallidotomy, cerebellar DBS, or STN stimulation all gratify that destroy-the-focus fantasy. Electrical stimulation of the vagus nerve is the procedure that treats refractory epilepsy without enacting that wish: you modulate a cranial nerve and leave cortex and basal ganglia intact.

2010-148.sentence: Levodopa/carbidopa bought movement and then invited visual hallucinations as a third party in the room; olanzapine, risperidone, and ziprasidone answer by attacking dopamine and, with it, the motor self you just restored. Quetiapine is the interpersonal compromise: treat the hallucinations without stealing the Parkinson patient’s remaining mobility.

2010-149.sentence: Late-onset schizophrenia clusters in women, often after the late-life attachment field thins—widowhood, grown children gone—so persecutory ideas and voices can become a grim substitute for a regulating other. That is not a statement that the illness is hopeless or treatment-refractory, and it is not a prodrome that only starts after sixty; the demographic is the attachment clue.

2010-150.sentence: A first seizure at fifty-eight that starts focal and then generalizes is the body writing a story the patient cannot remember: cortex being invaded, classically by glioblastoma multiforme. Alcohol withdrawal does not march from a focus, TLE is a chronic syndrome not a first event in this age, and SAH announces itself as thunderclap plus meningeal catastrophe—not this motor sequence.

2010-151.sentence: Clock drawing fails when construction and executive sequencing cannot hold the wish to stay oriented against the brain’s prohibition on new learning. Alzheimer dementia turns that collision into a visible symptom: the hands and numbers will not stay where the person still wants them to go.

2010-152.sentence: Rapid cycling shreds the selfobject function of lithium as a reliable stabilizer the patient can idealize and lean on. Each extra pole in a year is another failed mirroring of competence: the drug that should restore a coherent self keeps missing, so self-esteem collapses into “nothing works.”

2010-153.sentence: Tinnitus plus abdominal pain plus metabolic acidosis is aspirin evacuating nameless dread through the body instead of putting the overdose into words. Containment here is naming salicylate toxicity out loud so the ringing and the acid become thinkable facts, not raw panic dumped into the ED.

2010-154.sentence: Ethnicity, unlike race or SES, is the shared history the work cannot rush past if you want a real ending with this person. Asking about ancestry, beliefs, and the language at home honors a limit: identity is not a demographic you assign and then terminate the conversation.

2010-155.sentence: Papilledema with OCPs and a noncontrast CT that looks “normal” tests whether you can see your own part: you almost called it pseudotumor. A trial comment—“this could be sagittal sinus thrombosis, not idiopathic pressure”—uses insight to keep looking instead of settling for the reassuring empty scan.

2010-156.sentence: The frame for a five-year-old after a move is time and a holding limit, not a report that development was lost. Transient thumb-sucking and accidents are regression inside a still-maturing child; you hold the hour and the story rather than treating earlier behaviors as a broken milestone.

2010-157.sentence: The CRAFFT car question is not small talk; it asks whether the teen will let a substance sit in the driver's seat of a real body. Naming that risk out loud can feel like a demand or a feed: you are offering protection, and they may hear you taking away the high or calling them needy.

2010-158.sentence: Cortical atrophy pulls the brain away from the skull and stretches bridging veins, so a minor bump can leave a chronic subdural that looks like new apathy or forgetfulness. Good and bad stay poorly held in that gap: the family sees “just getting old,” and the clot sits as a silent bad object until you name the bleed.

2010-159.sentence: If agencies match adoptive homes to the birth parents’ education or temperament, the study cannot split genes from environment; resemblance is already mixed. That is a Kleinian mess of insides and outsides: what looks like the child’s inherited “bad” or “good” may be a placement that already resembled the original object.

2010-160.sentence: Frotteurism is the urge to rub against a nonconsenting stranger, often on a crowded train, and the distress does not make the act a medicine. Treat any later SSRI or antiandrogen as a limit you two negotiate, not a chemical fig leaf that proves the patient is either poisoned or finally “fixed.”

2010-161.sentence: Supervision belongs in the opening frame, same as fee and time: the patient deserves to know a third person already sits in the room. Hiding the attending until they ask is not kindness; it is you holding the confidentiality limit for your comfort instead of theirs.

2010-162.sentence: Naming deficits after cueing point to cortical language loss, not the give-up-and-slow-down of depression. If you keep treating only the lifelong mood and skip that anomia, you and the family are already in an enactment: repeating “it’s just the depression” instead of facing a new brain.

2010-163.sentence: Calling this a “bad migraine” is denial: you shove aside hemorrhage into an oligodendroglioma so you do not have to treat a suddenly sleepy young adult with bilateral Babinski signs as a crash. Denial buys calm for a minute and costs the scan.

2010-164.sentence: A score without validity is an evacuation: you dump a number that never named the actual feeling, so the resident is left with nameless dread dressed as data. Validity is containment—the instrument holds what it claims (depression, not “vibes”) until that experience can be thought.

2010-165.sentence: Praise and an upcoming vacation work as a mirror: someone else briefly holds this person’s worth, so mood lifts and the sweet binge can pause. Fear of rejection is the same self-esteem system with the mirror gone—intimacy feels like a drop, not a relationship.

2010-166.sentence: Flumazenil can reverse alprazolam at the GABA-A receptor; it cannot make the patient see their part in emptying the bottle. After the airway is safe, one trial comment—“what was happening that you needed this much?”—tests whether they can use insight or only the antidote.

2010-167.sentence: Oppositional defiant disorder lives at the limit: “no,” bedtime, and adult time are endings the child cannot yet metabolize, so anger and blame arrive instead of a stop. You do not rush that capacity with a lecture; you hold a firm, boring frame until “stop” is thinkable.

2010-168.sentence: On a blot or TAT card the patient can park a bad object—persecutor, fragment, bizarre link—without having to keep good and bad in one relationship the way interview requires. That is why projective testing can catch a subtle psychotic process the mental status still packages as “a bit guarded.”

2010-169.sentence: Tranylcypromine plus 1.5 g of 5-hydroxytryptophan is not more treatment; it is more uncovering than this serotonergic system can use. When colorful hallucinations, confusion, and myoclonus appear, the technique is support: stop the combination and contain serotonin syndrome, not push the MAOI higher.

2010-170.sentence: If the room keeps treating months of hand wasting, fasciculations, brisk reflexes, and extensor plantars as “deconditioning” or a psychiatric story, that is an enactment: you and the system are repeating the old medical habit of talking while the motor neurons die. Name ALS in the room instead of living the delay.

2010-171.sentence: Nicotine is the most commonly abused substance in schizophrenia because it can hold a vertical split: the person stays in the chair while a piece of agitation, anhedonia, or cognitive fog leaves. Ask about cigarettes and vaping as the cheap self-stitches that keep that split from tearing open on the ward.

2010-172.sentence: Privilege belongs to the patient, not to the judge, the psychiatrist, or the DA who wants the chart. That is the frame: the resident does not mail records on a subpoena alone, because handing over the file as if it were yours is a boundary break dressed as cooperation.

2010-173.sentence: Past violent behavior predicts future violence better than anger, weapons, or which defense you name on the board. Acting out is the defense here: the person discharges the impulse in assault instead of thinking it, so you take the history of what they already did, not the feeling of the hour.

2010-174.sentence: Split treatment is still one relationship: you write the prescription while another clinician holds the hour, and the two of you are making the care together. You keep full responsibility for the patient, not a 50/50 pill-only slice, so you must talk, consent to communicate, and own safety as if the therapy were in the room with the meds.

2010-175.sentence: Bupropion’s dopamine boost can flood a mind that already struggles to keep inner noise from becoming outer fact—uncovering more drive is the opposite of what that ego can use. Stay supportive: track hallucinations, sleep, and activation rather than asking the patient to “work through” the energy the drug just added.

2010-176.sentence: Childhood-onset schizophrenia still hits the same attentional, learning, and abstraction systems adults lose—so ego strength is already thin before identity has even coalesced. Do not ask that child to “process” the psychosis; measure whether they can still hold a thought, delay an impulse, and test reality as school and peers change around them.

2010-177.sentence: An overvalued idea of adultery sits between doubt and delusion: the spouse is still used as a regulator, but closeness now means scanning for betrayal. Ask how certain they are and whether they can entertain being wrong—that is the attachment test, not the content of the jealousy.

2010-178.sentence: A no-show one month after bipolar hospitalization is not a cultural identity crisis in the room; it is a break in the holding arrangement. Call, say you are concerned, and ask why they missed—so the patient learns absence still brings a person, not a letter threatening discharge.

2010-179.sentence: At three-and-a-half, dressing in mother’s clothes is social learning on the initiative-versus-guilt stage: she copies the same-sex model she sees reinforced. Social learning does not need a triangular Oedipal plot or a genital self-concept—just watching Mom and being rewarded for looking like her.

2010-180.sentence: PCP intoxication is an unrepresented state: the body is repeating what cannot be thought—agitation, heat, and possible rhabdo—so you treat the soma first with aggressive hydration, not insight. Keep the room quiet and the vitals watched; interpretation waits until the mind can actually hold a sentence.

2010-181.sentence: The body is recruiting you as the examiner who must map the lesion, not as the anxious bystander who just names “shoulder.” C5–C6 weakness of abduction, internal rotation, flexion, and adduction of the extended arm is upper-trunk work; your countertransference urge to shrug and move on is how the plexus gets missed.

2010-182.sentence: Reliability is the group’s conscience about scoring: different raters must land near the same number, even if that number is not yet the “true” value. A delirium scale that wanders with the rater is a sanctioned moral gap—we pretend we measured the patient when we only measured our own looseness.

2010-183.sentence: At fourteen the developmental job is still school, peer work, and keeping the day organized—not proving that the elders are “not real.” Treat the declining grades as the capacity that is slipping; leave the culturally held visions intact unless function, not cosmology, is what failed.

2010-184.sentence: The new profanity, irascibility, and six-month collapse of conscientiousness are not a character upgrade; they are the frontal lobe taking the brakes off the person he used to be. The symptom is doing the work of an injured executive system: impulse without the old internal editor.

2010-185.sentence: Erikson’s young-adult task is intimacy versus isolation; prison already isolates him, so taped razor blades buy a hospital leave—an external escape, not a plea to be known. That is malingering: a clear secondary gain, not the identity work of factitious illness or the identity diffusion of borderline personality.

2010-186.sentence: Two or more voices conversing once counted as a Schneiderian first-rank shortcut: the diagnosis could stand without extra Criterion A company.
