The cultural third in the chart is the DSM era itself—an older exam voice still speaking in the room—so you treat the finding as psychosis to assess, not as a timeless identity of “schizophrenia-lite.”

2010-187.sentence: The frequent pairing of autistic disorder with mental retardation is the clinic’s reminder not to dump every limitation into one diagnosis—that is a paranoid-schizoid move, splitting the child into “just autism” so no one has to face the extra damage. Depressive concern, Klein’s capacity to stay with mixed reality and try to repair, means you actually measure IQ, language, and adaptive skill and then help the family grieve and plan for both.

2010-188.sentence: Dementia with Lewy bodies cannot hold a single, stable picture of the person: vivid children in the house on some days, a nearly intact mind on others, plus mild rigidity. Object relations here is that split—good days and haunted days sit side by side in one body, and the work is to keep both halves in the same relationship rather than calling it late schizophrenia or a one-way Alzheimer decline.

2010-189.sentence: Pennies, a piggy bank, and a cow only become a test of abstract reasoning if the patient can leave the concrete objects and find a shared idea. If they cannot, uncovering metaphors and deep interpretation will bounce; this mind needs supportive, structured work until categorization itself comes back online.

2010-190.sentence: Methadone had been functioning as a reliable selfobject—something outside that kept the self from fragmenting into craving and shame. When HIV antiretrovirals yank the level down or up, the patient does not only get withdrawal or sedation; they lose the mirrored sense of competence that a stable dose had been providing, so treat the interaction before you treat them as “nonadherent.”

2010-191.sentence: Menninger’s triangle—here with the therapist, there with partners, then with early caregivers—is raw until someone names the link. That naming is interpretation: Bion’s containing, taking the evacuated fear that everyone is disappointed and returning it as a thinkable pattern instead of another nameless dread.

2010-192.sentence: Pregnancy is a hard limit: valproate is off the table, and you cannot wait for a leisurely lithium or carbamazepine titration while she is restrained, grandiose, and at 33 weeks. Haloperidol is the honest ending of that fantasy of a perfect mood-stabilizer restart—treat the mania now, then rebuild the longer regimen with obstetrics when the mind can use time again.

2010-193.sentence: A trial comment that tests insight is: “I hear the pain and the diagnosis—what I have to write down is what you still cannot do at work, at home, and in public, week after week.” If they can help you name missed days, failed tasks, and lost roles, they are already doing the real work of a disability exam: translating inner life into degree of functional impairment, not into a sadder story.

2010-194.sentence: That glance at mother’s face is the infant borrowing a conscience: he will not treat the stranger as safe until she sanctions it with a smile and a nod. Social referencing is early morality made visible—permission lives on her face before it lives inside him.

2010-195.sentence: Witnesses will recruit you as the neurologist who must call this a seizure, and your countertransference urge is to over-treat the jerks so you do not “miss epilepsy.” Stay with the sequence they actually saw: faintness and pallor, collapse, a few bilateral jerks, then flushing—that is vasovagal syncope, not a bid to make you the crash-cart doctor.

2010-196.sentence: The humiliation they expect is often never a story they can tell; it lives as a freeze in the throat, so they stay mute in groups while still wanting friends. Avoidant personality disorder is that unrepresented shame enacted in the room: they treat your slightest frown as the criticism they cannot remember having survived.

2010-197.sentence: The calm line “my significant other dumped me” is a compromise formation: the wish to be held collides with a ban on looking needy, so feeling is stripped out. Confrontation is the first move—you name the split between words and affect—before you interpret the buried wish.

2010-198.sentence: St. John’s wort (Hypericum perforatum) often arrives as “just a natural mood tea,” a cultural third that makes a serotonergic herb feel unlike a drug. Name the plant and the SSRI together so that identity story—“I don’t take chemicals”—does not quietly build serotonin syndrome.

2010-199.sentence: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy is not only white-matter holes on T2 MRI; it knocks a 43-year-old out of the work of caring for a household and other people. That is Erikson's generativity task in the 40s—staying useful to those who come after you—and the JC-virus lesions make stagnation a neurologic injury, not a midlife attitude problem.

2010-200.sentence: Generativity is the 40-to-60 job: feeling useful by protecting people who come after you, not mastering intimacy or making peace with death. Hold the hour as that developmental work—do not turn empty-nest doubt into extra visits, a rushed diagnosis, or a fee that implies midlife meaning is an emergency you must fix.

2010-201.sentence: Recurrent unsuccessful efforts to control use is the DSM-IV dependence criterion; role failure, fights, and legal trouble stay on the old abuse list. The drug has become the regulator the person reaches for first—proximity to a chemical 'secure base' that soothes, even while every stop attempt fails.

2010-202.sentence: Osteoporosis is the anorexia complication least likely to reverse after weight is restored; lipids, thyroid labs, and arrhythmias more often quiet down. You and the patient make the next pattern together: name residual bone loss as a shared medical fact so rehab does not become another two-person war over the plate and the scale.

2010-203.sentence: Clang associations are a thought-process break: speech follows rhyme and sound, not the question you asked. That mind cannot use uncovering yet—stay supportive and concrete, because interpreting conflict while words are already chaining by noise only piles more fragments on.

2010-204.sentence: The 2008 meta-analysis put long-term psychodynamic psychotherapy ahead of CBT, DBT, supportive, and family therapy for personality disorder plus chronic mixed illness. Years of a steady therapist can function as a selfobject: reliable mirroring of competence so esteem is borrowed until a more stable self can hold.

2010-205.sentence: The outbursts are raw beta-elements—unthinkable rage after the TBI—evacuated into staff as “I just see red.” Propranolol does not interpret the anger; it contains the autonomic surge so the feeling can become thinkable instead of only discharged.

2010-206.sentence: Atypical depression with rejection sensitivity and two failed SSRIs is a limit you cannot hurry past with another serotonergic trial. Tranylcypromine names that limit: some MAOI-responsive patterns need a different capacity, not more of the same ending.

2010-207.sentence: A trial comment is whether she can see the low desire as part of her own depression—anhedonia, insomnia, fatigue, appetite loss—rather than a standalone sexual disorder. If she can use that, the DSM-IV-TR mapping is a symptom of a major depressive episode, not hypoactive desire or arousal disorder.

2010-208.sentence: The harsh inner judge can treat post-viral tingling and areflexia as moral failure—“I should push through”—when the body is declaring Guillain-Barré, acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy. Conscience does not get a sanctioned gap here: weakness after a URI with slow conduction is medical, not a character verdict.

2010-209.sentence: The family recruits you as either reckless prescriber or withholding savior when they invoke the black-box warning on quetiapine in this 82-year-old with dementia. Name the feeling they put in you, then tell the truth: atypical antipsychotics increase mortality, and that risk is weighed against benefit—not denied or inflated.

2010-210.sentence: Calling it neurasthenia can already be an enactment: patient and clinician repeating a cultural script of exhaustion instead of thinking undifferentiated somatoform disorder. Stay with what the body is doing—fatigue, aches, poor concentration—rather than living the old label as if it were the whole relationship.

2010-211.sentence: A malpractice payout with no admission of fault is institutional denial: cash moves, and the story stays “nothing was wrong.” The National Practitioner Data Bank still files that settlement, so the defense erases guilt-talk, not the report.

2010-212.sentence: Parity treats the psychiatric prescription as the same feed as insulin, not as a luxury demand or a slightly shameful extra. Justice is the principle that lithium or an antipsychotic is not a second-class meal just because the organ is the mind.

2010-213.sentence: Ventral tegmental area cells dump dopamine into the nucleus accumbens; a late refill or a cancelled hour can hit that circuit like a missed meal. Hold time, money, and the prescription as the frame—you are sitting next to a pathway that treats the next dose as proof you will still be there.

2010-214.sentence: Freud parked genital focus plus the opposite-sex-parent wish in the phallic stage, not in latency or the later genital stage. Insight is whether they can try on that comment as a map of rivalry and desire, not as a police report about last Tuesday.

2010-215.sentence: Cataplexy ends muscle tone on a laugh while the person stays awake; that limit will not wait for more insight. Clomipramine holds the body at the ending you cannot rush by will.

2010-216.sentence: Left face numbness, nystagmus, hiccups, and falling left after abrupt vertigo is a lateral medullary (Wallenberg) stroke, not a moral collapse. A harsh conscience will call the stagger weakness of character; the lesion is in the lateral medulla, and guilt does not live there.

2010-217.sentence: Meperidine plus an MAOI is the pair that can kill; the developmental task is the late-arriving capacity to stop and scan the whole list before the impulse to “just give something for pain.” Until that pause is reliable, the old reflex to reach for meperidine stays in charge.

2010-218.sentence: The extra chromosome 21 in Down syndrome is not a metaphor; it keeps making amyloid precursor protein, so Alzheimer pathology shows up decades early. The “symptom” of premature dementia is what that extra APP gene is doing for the brain, not a random overlay on intellectual disability.

2010-219.sentence: Ego psychology sits on Erikson’s industry-versus-inferiority task: envy and rage at someone who seems more competent get handled by defenses, not by drive discharge. Name the defense—devaluation, denial, projection—and you are watching how the person tries to stay industrious without collapsing into inferiority.

2010-220.sentence: HSV in the temporal lobe can split personality, memory, and smell/taste while the body never leaves the chair—that is a neurologic vertical split, not a chosen trance. The olfactory and gustatory hallucinations are the uncus announcing that the self has come apart at the medial temporal seam.

2010-221.sentence: CATIE found second-generation antipsychotics were no more effective than first-generation ones; most patients still quit. Ego strength here is the capacity to stay on a drug through weight gain or akathisia without treating “newer” as a magic increase in coping.

2010-222.sentence: Dissociative fugue is flight used as a defense: the person leaves the name and the past so the trauma does not have to be felt. Repression then seals the autobiography, which is why the history cannot be recalled even after the traveling stops.

2010-223.sentence: The condolence call can already be an enactment: you and the spouse are living the old rescue instead of naming the loss. Stay with the spouse's feelings; explaining the five-year treatment or offering to treat the family repeats the rescue you could not finish.

2010-224.sentence: The concert lobby is the frame: confidentiality is the limit you hold when no one asked you to speak. Walk past unless the patient greets you first; initiating contact, steering your spouse away, or making introductions spends the patient's secret in public.

2010-225.sentence: Nicotine replacement is a feed; the wrong vehicle becomes a poison the mouth, skin, or nose cannot take. Lozenges give the dose without chewing around upcoming braces, a patch on psoriasis, or spray and inhaler into stuffed, allergic airways.

2010-226.sentence: Muscle is a limit you cannot talk past: atorvastatin plus gemfibrozil already crossed it, and the slightly high creatine kinase is the body saying stop. Name statin-induced myopathy before you treat the aches as mood, worry, or a need for more steroid.

2010-227.sentence: Rapprochement is the toddler's first insight: I went too far, I am separate, I can come back. The work is the reunion after that brief rupture with the parent, not peer life, adolescent renegotiation, or simply checking in before a risk.

2010-228.sentence: At four the psychosocial task is initiative: I reach, I try, I want. In Prader-Willi the drive is hunger the child cannot master—infant hypotonia, then foraging and tantrums—so the stage looks like failed will rather than Down, Williams, Fragile X, or Angelman.

2010-229.sentence: Plasma homocysteine gives the young stroke a metabolic name, so the person is not left with a story that just says “this came from nowhere.” The elevated level is doing work: it turns a terrifying blank into a lab finding you can chase, treat, and share with family instead of carrying as a private omen.

2010-230.sentence: The automatic thought is a fast defense: it slams the door on other meanings so the patient never has to sit with not-knowing. Eliciting and testing that thought is how you stop the defense mid-sentence and ask whether incompetence is fact or just the mind’s first shield.

2010-231.sentence: After a bipolar postpartum psychosis, the mood stabilizer is not only chemistry. It can feel like a second feed the mother did not choose, or like proof she cannot hold the baby without a third party in her bloodstream. Name that relationship to the pill early, or the same person who needs lithium most will experience it as poison or as a demand she already failed.

2010-232.sentence: Imipramine’s plasma level is the part of treatment that does not leave the chair when the patient (or you) has already checked out of the subjective story. Dose and “I took it” can split from what is actually in the blood; the level is the vertical split made visible, so you treat the number instead of arguing with the narrative.

2010-233.sentence: In REM sleep behavior disorder the dream is not remembered; it is staged. That is an enactment: punching and kicking live the scene instead of watching it. Synuclein inclusions mark the brainstem losing the lock that keeps dream from becoming action, so the bed becomes a theater the sleeper cannot leave.

2010-234.sentence: World War II forced psychiatry to stay close to men who fell apart under fire, and DSM-I is that proximity written as a manual. The categories offered a secure base: a shared language so the returning soldier was held as a reaction to war, not left unclassified and alone.

2010-235.sentence: A threatened court commitment is coercion, not a real choice, so the signature is not informed consent. Suicidality already taxes affect tolerance and impulse control; stacking a legal threat on top does not restore ego strength, it just produces compliance.

2010-236.sentence: ERP works by habituation: the feared cue stays present, the ritual is blocked, and the anxiety curve falls on its own. That is a supportive-behavioral dose, not uncovering; you do not interpret the contamination fantasy while the patient is still flooding.

2010-237.sentence: Lithium plus an SSRI can jointly lower the seizure threshold; the pair is the risk, not either drug alone. Watch the relationship in the body the way you would watch a tense dyad: tremor, confusion, vomiting, or a first seizure means the combination has become toxic.

2010-238.sentence: Inattentive ADHD clusters with learning disorders, anxiety, and somatic complaints more than with ODD or conduct. School failure and stomachaches often carry what the child cannot organize as attention; treat the learning problem, not just the daydreaming.

2010-239.sentence: The rehab team is recruiting you to become the one who smashes the chipper stance and forces mourning. That is countertransference: their anxiety about denial. Support the tetraplegia patient's existing coping and do not confront the medical realities until function, not the team's discomfort, requires it.

2010-240.sentence: An MMSE of 23 sits below the usual 24 cutoff and only suggests dementia or mild cognitive impairment, not a diagnosis. Ego functions of memory, orientation, and language need history, function, and a medical workup before you treat the number as a verdict.

2010-241.sentence: Paramyotonia that worsens with continued exercise and cold is a sodium-channel problem, not “nerves.” The self takes a hit to competence: the body fails in the middle of effort, so the person starts to doubt they can finish anything hard.

2010-242.sentence: Fluoxetine is the one with real data for binge–purge cycles. Think of it as a chemical container: it holds some of the raw fullness and shame so they do not have to evacuate it through vomiting.

2010-243.sentence: Formication, picking, oral stereotypies, and paranoia mark stimulant intoxication, not a leisurely come-down. The high has no built-in ending; the nervous system slams a limit when the user will not.

2010-244.sentence: Leaving the public place stops the panic, so escape is negatively reinforced: relief teaches the next flight. A trial comment is whether they can see their own part—that the relief, not the street, is training the attacks.

2010-245.sentence: Midlife friendship is less bound to being the same age; the old schoolyard frame of “same cohort only” loosens. Who counts as a real friend is a limit question: closeness and reliability, not birth year.

2010-246.sentence: Minimally conscious state means inconsistent command-following, a gesture, or a word—not coma and not reliable awareness. Families will treat that flicker as a full return of the person; you hold the bond without inflating a thumbs-up into recovery.

2010-247.sentence: Suppression is the parent putting fear on a shelf on purpose so she can call the neighbor and get to the hospital. The affect is not gone; it is parked until the kids are covered and she can feel it.

2010-248.sentence: The after-meal cigarette is a cue, not a character flaw: the plate, the coffee, the chair already 'ask' for nicotine. Name the trigger so the craving is a learned pairing you can swap, not proof he cannot quit.

2010-249.sentence: OCD and tic disorders travel in the same families; the circuit for urge-and-repeat is shared, not a later-life mood or panic add-on. Ask the child about motor and vocal tics because the familial story is a developmental line, not a coincidence.

2010-250.sentence: You are being hired as the court's eyes on now, not as biographer or crime-scene mind-reader. If you feel pulled toward old charts or the alleged offense, that is countertransference: you are sliding into advocate or detective instead of testing current grasp of charges, roles, and consequences.

2010-251.sentence: Severe lithium toxicity with impaired consciousness, neuromuscular irritability, and seizures is not a problem you can 'tough out' with fluids or a cleaner conscience. Hemodialysis is the sanctioned exit: the toxin stays until you actually take it out of the blood.

2010-252.sentence: Rapid cycling—four or more syndromal mood episodes in a year—shows up more in women; the cycling capacity is sex-linked, not a lithium side effect or late-onset story. Watch the calendar in female patients so the pattern is named before the year fills with episodes.

2010-253.sentence: Bringing unconscious conflict into awareness is what the hour is for: the scheduling change is not just logistics, it is the old authority fight arriving as “you are harsh.” Once that collision can be named, the patient has a chance to think it instead of only living it with you.

2010-254.sentence: The Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scale (VABS-II) does more than score dressing and toileting; it takes a caregiver’s raw “this child cannot manage a body” and turns it into named, thinkable domains. Once that dread is contained in numbers and skills, you can plan supports instead of only evacuating panic as “retardation.”

2010-255.sentence: Insufficient data to pick CBT, a medication, or both for panic means you cannot hide behind a “best” first move; you have to see what actually steadies this patient’s self when unexpected attacks hit. The subway-avoidance is a collapsing sense of competence—choose the pill, the person, or both by what restores a usable, mirroring other, not by a ranking table.

2010-256.sentence: Venlafaxine already leans on serotonin and norepinephrine; only at the highest recommended doses does dopamine reuptake join the fight, adding a push of wish and energy. That extra dopaminergic edge can collide with the old prohibition—more drive, same guilt—so watch whether high-dose titration livens the patient or just revs a conflict they then have to punish.

2010-257.sentence: Labyrinthitis writes itself in the canal: nystagmus that fades with visual fixation and grows when the eyes turn toward the quick phase is a peripheral hit the patient cannot narrate. If you hunt MS, Wallenberg, or a CPA tumor first, you are looking for a story with a lesion while the vestibule is already repeating what has no words.

2010-258.sentence: Preschool animism is expected work, not a diagnosis: the toy bear gets to be “alive” so the child can practice leaving and being left without losing the object. When a 4-year-old says the stuffed animal is sad alone, you are hearing symbolic play come online—ask about language and reciprocity, not whether the bear needs a prescription.

2010-259.sentence: Pain and temperature drop out while vibration and joint sense stay because the spinothalamic tracts live in the anterior two-thirds of the cord and the dorsal columns do not. That split is the anterior spinal artery talking after a decompression insult: it feeds the anterior cord, and the posterior spinal arteries still keep proprioception online.

2010-260.sentence: The gym ‘bulk-up’ gift is doing GABA-B work, not muscle work: GHB drops alertness and heart rate while a routine urine screen stays blank. The body is advertising the drug’s real job—coma and bradycardia—so you treat airway and watch, not anabolic side effects.

2010-261.sentence: Saying whether Mr. X is even in the practice already breaks the frame: confidentiality covers the fact of treatment, not only what is said in the room. The limit you hold is a sentence that neither confirms nor denies, so a colleague’s curiosity does not become an unauthorized consult.

2010-262.sentence: After seventy, oxidative (phase-I) clearance is a late-life loss, so long-acting oxidatively metabolized benzos—diazepam, flurazepam, clorazepate, chlordiazepoxide—accumulate. Lorazepam needs only conjugation, a capacity that usually remains, which is why it is the safer LOT choice in that aging liver.

2010-263.sentence: IPT works the psychosocial task in front of the person—here a role transition—not unconscious conflict, automatic thoughts, or repressed memory. Erikson would name the same job: renegotiate identity and generativity after a life-structure change, in current relationships, not in the buried past.

2010-264.sentence: The essential finding is not theatrical switching; it is extensive inability to recall personal information, the stretch of life that never got a continuous ‘I.’ What cannot be remembered as one story is repeated as another self, so lost time is trauma showing up as a gap rather than a narrative.

2010-265.sentence: The frame here is public-health, not a polite consult: tuberculous meningitis with a sixth-nerve palsy, hoarseness, and CSF glucose of 29 means airborne isolation and a reportable disease, even if the patient arrived as “just another drinker with a headache.” You hold that limit so stigma about alcohol dependence does not delay the tap, the isolation room, or the call to the health department.

2010-266.sentence: The parents’ startle is a harsh conscience scanning the playroom for pathology; the child’s “monster will never catch us” is ordinary preschool private speech, not a command hallucination. Let the child keep the monster in the toys so the real-world rules stay light enough to play with.

2010-267.sentence: Caffeine blocks the adenosine receptor and lets dopamine run hotter, so the room can feel as jittery as the patient’s pulse. Notice if you are being recruited as the colleague who shrugs “it’s only coffee” while sleep, tremor, and anxiety keep climbing.

2010-268.sentence: Autonomy is not a pamphlet dump; it is matching diagnosis, options, and risks to what this ego can actually hold without flooding. If you outrun their affect tolerance or reality testing, you have performed informed consent on paper and left them alone with the choice.

2010-269.sentence: Nightly clonazepam, now 5 mg after a spouse’s death, has become the stand-in for the person who used to make sleep feel safe. A slow taper is a planned separation: you stay as the secure base while the pill stops pretending it can replace a lost attachment.

2010-270.sentence: After one surge of cramps and palpitations in the OR, the surgeon rearranges the world so help is always nearby—no ED call, no crowds, no noisy rooms. That is agoraphobia without panic: using proximity to safety to regulate the body instead of trusting the setting to be survivable.

2010-271.sentence: Intrafamilial violence hits the ego’s shock absorbers hardest because the person who should help the child metabolize terror is often the source of it. Affect tolerance and reality testing then have to grow inside a home that keeps rewriting what “safe” means.

2010-272.sentence: Fluoxetine’s long half-life is the pharmacologic version of a slow taper: it covers a mind that cannot yet sit with the raw rebound of stopping paroxetine. Use that long tail as support, not as an invitation to excavate every anxiety that surfaces during washout.

2010-273.sentence: Painful monocular loss, faded color, an afferent pupillary defect, and a swollen disc that then remits is a two-person story: the eye and the CNS keep writing the same demyelinating chapter. Stay in that partnership—optic neuritis now, multiple sclerosis later—rather than treating the recovered vision as a closed case.

2010-274.sentence: A prior alcohol or other-drug abuse history is the finding that should raise concern, not daily alprazolam, potency, or rebound after a taper. Denial here is not “I have no anxiety”; it is treating physiologic dependence as if it were proof of character, so the real risk factor gets waved away.

2010-275.sentence: Hair-pulling often coexists with a mood disorder, so the pill is not just anti-urge chemistry—it can feel like the only proof someone believes the depression behind the patches. If the antidepressant is offered as feed for a depleted self rather than as a demand to stop pulling, the relationship around the medicine stays usable.

2010-276.sentence: Conversion can split motor control off from awareness: the teen’s legs fail while the person stays in the chair, not faking and not fully owning the paralysis. Rehabilitative treatment works because it invites the body back into function without forcing the split to confess.

2010-277.sentence: Starting hydrochlorothiazide next to lithium is already a two-person enactment: primary care treats the blood pressure as if it lived in a separate body from the bipolar illness. Name that split before the level climbs, or the teams will keep repeating “my organ, your organ” while the patient metabolizes both.

2010-278.sentence: Arcuate fasciculus damage leaves fluency and comprehension standing while repetition will not come, no matter how hard you drill. That is a hard limit: the white-matter bridge is gone, so you stop asking the circuit to close and you work around the gap.

2010-279.sentence: The surgeon cannot keep the hospital’s ordinary demands inside as thinkable disappointment; he evacuates them as persecution so they will not become nameless dread. Containment here means holding the raw betrayal-feeling long enough to ask what happened, without agreeing that peer review was an attack.

2010-280.sentence: Toluene years live in cerebellar atrophy, white-matter change, ataxia, neuropathy, and a mind that cannot tell the story. What was never remembered as “I was dissolving myself” returns as rhabdomyolysis and renal failure instead of a narrative.

2010-281.sentence: The wish to call day-five fluctuation “just a seizure” or “another rupture” collides with the prohibition against missing delayed vasospasm after left MCA aneurysmal bleed. The drive is to settle the anxiety; the task is to treat the spasm window as the real conflict.

2010-282.sentence: A self-help group is not there to remodel personality or harvest insight; it mirrors competence while people practice not drinking. Self-esteem grows from “I did the next right behavior,” not from being idealized as newly analyzed.

2010-283.sentence: A trance is not “spacing out.” It is evacuation: the mind dumps a raw, unthinkable feeling so it never has to become a thought. Bion would say nobody contained the dread—held it and named it—so the patient leaves the scene in altered consciousness instead of remembering it.

2010-284.sentence: Longer awakenings are not just “bad sleep.” They are the night doing extra work: checking the body, the bladder, the empty house. Ask what the waking is for before you chase more hours of unconsciousness.

2010-285.sentence: A no-show fee is ethical only after the rule has actually arrived—told in advance, in words the patient can use. Surprise billing is not a frame; it is a parent who invents the law after the child already broke it.

2010-286.sentence: Central pontine myelinolysis is the pons paying for an overzealous correction of sodium 99. That is a superego move in the body: the deficit must be punished into normal, and the myelin is what gets stripped.

2010-287.sentence: Ask for the patient’s explanation of the illness or you will be recruited as the knowing outsider who already named it. That is the cultural formulation’s job: keep their story in the room so your countertransference does not write the chart first.

2010-288.sentence: Liaison is teaching, not another consult note. Staff often use denial—they refuse the feeling the patient is dumping on the ward—and a brief lesson names that feeling so it does not have to become a fight.

2010-289.sentence: Once you name carbamazepine’s 10–15% early maculopapular rash and the SJS/TEN warning signs, the pair is already in an enactment: a two-person replay of “will you treat my danger as real, or will you minimize it?” The rash report two weeks later is not just a side-effect callback; it tests whether the warning was theater or a live contract you both keep.

2010-290.sentence: Adult inattention is the ADHD piece most likely to stay, and a harsh superego—the inner judge—often misreads missed deadlines as laziness rather than a remaining attentional deficit. Treat that moral verdict as the problem in the room: guilt is doing diagnostic work that belongs to history of childhood onset, not character.

2010-291.sentence: Idiopathic Bell’s palsy knocks out the whole ipsilateral face, including forehead, because CN VII never finished a clean day’s work of carrying affect onto the face. Pain behind the ear, tearing, and hyperacusis mark a sudden loss of a developmental capacity: the face as the child’s first signaling organ, not a brainstem stroke or a sensory nerve story.

2010-292.sentence: The topographical model (conscious / preconscious / unconscious) is not furniture; it names what a memory is doing for the person. A childhood address can sit preconscious—available after a prompt—while a conflictual wish stays unconscious so it can only arrive as a dream, a slip, or a defense.

2010-293.sentence: The MCMI-III is built to map personality patterns; Erikson would ask which psychosocial task never quite settled—identity versus role confusion, or intimacy versus isolation. Use the inventory to sharpen that question, then still decide whether the longstanding instability is a failed identity consolidation, not a one-off mood week.

2010-294.sentence: After recurrent depression remits, staying on the same antidepressant dose is the frame: the agreed holding structure, not a taper that quietly says “you should need less.” Cutting the dose to chase a fantasy of independence trades the working alliance for a relapse you both then have to explain.

2010-295.sentence: Vomiting in the purging subtype is evacuation: the patient treats food, calories, and even the body as a persecutory object that must be forced out. That is Kleinian projective identification in the gut—push the bad thing into the bowl—and the potassium follows it, so hypokalemia is the metabolic signature of that emptying.

2010-296.sentence: Café-au-lait spots at birth plus later neurofibromas and Lisch nodules (iris hamartomas) name one mutation, NF1, not TSC-1 or ATM. The family has to hold both pictures of the same child—the marked skin and the still-developing mind—without splitting the kid into “just spots” versus “ruined.”

2010-297.sentence: Rotter’s internal locus is not “I caused everything”; it is the expectation that my act will reach a valued goal. Until that expectancy is even a little believable, stay supportive and behavioral; heavy uncovering of why they feel powerless will only confirm that luck and other people run the show.

2010-298.sentence: In late-life depression the clock of thought—information-processing speed—can come back when mood remits; motor dexterity, visuospatial skill, and performance IQ are less likely to snap back. Hold the frame around time: slower answers now are a treatable state, not a new identity as “demented,” so you do not drop the hour or the hope just because the visit runs long.

2010-299.sentence: The stamped-envelope question tests judgment: can they choose a safe, socially fitting act in a made-up bind. Insight is whether they see their own part; if they cannot even pick a decent hypothetical action, a trial comment about motive will bounce—stay concrete until judgment is back online.

2010-300.sentence: Gradual personality change, hygiene collapse, anomia, and grasp/suck reflexes point to frontotemporal dementia, not Alzheimer or Lewy body disease. Meds here are not a feed that restores the old self; they are often experienced as a demand on a frontal system that no longer holds the “who I am” object, so you treat the family relationship and safety, not a pill as proof you can give the person back.

2011-1.sentence: Digit span is not a trivia quiz; it asks whether the mind can hold a raw string of six numbers before memory turns it into a story. When attention flickers, the finding is that holding function failing—the numbers never get inside long enough to be remembered.

2011-2.sentence: Heavy smoking in schizophrenia often sits on identity versus role confusion: nicotine is a cheap, reliable self that does not demand intimacy. Irritability after admission is that fragile identity losing its only dependable regulator, not a personality surprise.

2011-3.sentence: A right posterior cerebral artery infarct takes the left half of the world from both eyes—left homonymous hemianopsia—so the person keeps walking into what the cortex no longer represents. The bumping is the field cut lived in action: unseen space becomes collision instead of a complaint about vision.

2011-4.sentence: Ethnicity is the developmental we-ness that ties common ancestry to a shared story, not the surface markers of race, language, or religion. Asking which communities the patient belongs to treats identity as a living task, not a box you can infer from the face.

2011-5.sentence: Blows to the abdomen in pregnancy attack a third who cannot yet speak; the violence is written on the body when it cannot be named in the room. Unexplained abdominal pain and a fearful partner visit are that unrepresented assault repeating until someone asks in private.

2011-6.sentence: After eight good ECT treatments you are recruited to be the rescuer who can finally stop, or the parent who disappears the moment the crisis lifts. Maintenance ECT for at least ten weeks is staying in the relationship after the dramatic save, instead of acting out the wish that the work is finished.

2011-7.sentence: Whipple disease (Tropheryma whipplei, PAS-positive macrophages in CSF) often arrives as “memory clinic” while fat malabsorption, fever, and hyperpigmentation sit in the waiting room. The conscience of the work is refusing that sanctioned gap: do not treat a failing mind as a private moral failing when the gut is the organ that is dying.

2011-8.sentence: Clarification is not a clever paraphrase; it is a secure-base move: you put their wish into words so they can feel held before anyone reaches for a pill. The last psychiatrist’s brief, med-only visits were a failed proximity—no listening, no regulation through another mind.

2011-9.sentence: DSM-IV-TR was built from data re-analyses and field trials, not from a priori theories of etiology. That is ego strength at the level of a nosology: tolerate not knowing the cause, keep reality testing on symptoms and impairment, and change the manual when the field data say so.

2011-10.sentence: Old Asperger criteria allowed social-communication trouble and restricted interests without an early delay in spoken language and communicative gestures; that delay marked autistic disorder. In Bion’s terms, words and gestures are how a mind contains raw experience so it can become thinkable—when those arrive late, the dread stays more nameless.

2011-11.sentence: Phototherapy can treat winter depression in bipolar II, but only with vigilance and careful titration of dose and time. Light is not a free lunch at termination of darkness: the frame has a limit, because too much too fast can shove the patient into hypomania.

2011-12.sentence: The Wisconsin Card Sort Test asks whether the patient can drop a dead rule after feedback and take a new one—that is executive set-shifting, not naming or word-list memory. Psychological mindedness is the same muscle: can they use a trial comment (the tester’s “wrong”) to see their own stuck strategy and change it.

2011-13.sentence: Hold the frame at one week: maternity blues is a time-limited lability, not a license to skip safety, bonding, or follow-up just because she “has no complaints.” Name the limit out loud—crying without persistent sad mood or psychosis is expected now, but if sleep, attachment, or reality testing break, you escalate, you do not wait for her to ask.

2011-14.sentence: Penicillin is not a polite suggestion here; it is the relationship’s medicine for neurosyphilis when CSF lymphocytes, protein, and reagin antibodies sit next to a young stroke. Offering aspirin or warfarin instead treats the clot story and withholds the antibiotic the patient actually needs—the pill as proof you recognized the infection, not as a demand that she “try something for circulation.”

2011-15.sentence: The sick role is the prize: assuming the patient identity soothes something that ordinary life does not, even when no lawsuit, narcotic, or disability check is on the table. That is not malingering’s external incentive and not hypochondriasis’s fear of disease—it is a defense that keeps the self organized around being cared for as ill.

2011-16.sentence: In the phallic period the child clocks the parental couple as a pair that exists without the child, and the seminar can start living that triangle: the resident, the theory, and the excluded “other.” That is an enactment if the group talks about oedipal curiosity while acting as if someone in the room is the leftover third.

2011-17.sentence: Lewy body dementia splits the night from the day: REM sleep behavior has the person fighting in a dream while the body never left the bed, and daytime fluctuations plus visual hallucinations do the same vertical split while sitting in the chair. Do not collapse that into ordinary Parkinson’s just because levodopa/carbidopa once helped the rigidity.

2011-18.sentence: Insecure attachment tracks the caretaker who does not answer hunger, distress, or reunion—not the job, the adoption papers, or a temperament mismatch. Ego strength in the infant grows when someone reliably metabolizes those signals; unresponsiveness plus poor-quality daycare leaves the baby with no place to put the affect.

2011-19.sentence: A loaded gun in the house is not a secure base; it is a lethal object sitting where attachment should regulate panic. Ask about firearms and lock them away so the resident, partner, or parent can be the person who holds the affect instead of a trigger.

2011-20.sentence: Directed masturbation plus couples therapy is the dose of uncovering this complaint can use: the couple’s bed, not a couch. Yohimbine, tramadol, a group, or psychoanalysis would treat a different mind than anorgasmia that lives between two people.

2011-21.sentence: Neglect is the most common maltreatment because it is a two-person failure: no one keeps showing up with food, school, medicine, or eyes on the child. Abandonment, sexual abuse, ritual abuse, and physical abuse are louder; the prevalent pattern is the caregiver who simply does not complete the care.

2011-22.sentence: The hour-long orbital stab with tearing and congestion is the syndrome speaking; high-flow oxygen answers that attack, not a mood stabilizer. Lithium and valproate belong later as prevention; ibuprofen and indomethacin treat a different headache.

2011-23.sentence: Hold the good and the bad in the timed APAP curve, not in the friend’s rescue story or the ten empty packs. N-acetylcysteine follows the serum N-acetyl-p-aminophenol level over time on the nomogram, not first transaminases, ultrasound, or lactate.

2011-24.sentence: The pull is a vertical split: the child leaves the rising tension without leaving the chair. CBT names that exit negative reinforcement because the urge drops after the hair comes out, which is not a reward, extinction, punishment, or positive reinforcement.

2011-25.sentence: The ECT course has already become an enactment: everyone is crowding treatments as if more shocks, faster, will undo the depression, and the dense retrograde amnesia is the relationship paying the bill. Widening the interval between ECT sessions is the two-person correction—you stop living the urgency and give the hippocampus a chance to keep recent memory.

2011-26.sentence: The cousin is doing the attachment work the interview asked of the patient: proximity to a vivid other instead of staying with you as a secure base for a yes-or-no about mania. Tangentiality is that departure—the story never comes back—so the patient regulates closeness by talking about someone else rather than risking a direct answer.

2011-27.sentence: Ego strength here is staying with a local ulnar lesion at the elbow instead of spinning a bigger story when the fourth and fifth digits go numb and the intrinsics weaken. Reality testing holds if you map sensation and finger spread to the ulnar nerve and do not treat it as a neck, radial, or median problem.

2011-28.sentence: Rapprochement is the toddler’s ethics of the frame: mother is the one who holds time and location, and the child keeps checking where she actually is. The 18-month-old’s marked worry about separation is not regression into symbiosis; it is the work of using a real parent as the limit while still wanting to roam.

2011-29.sentence: Insight starts with naming the body: confusion, oculomotor signs, ataxia, and dysarthria are Wernicke, not a puzzle to interpret first. Give thiamine before glucose so the trial comment is medical—you see the deficiency, you do not chase the mental status with a neuroleptic.

2011-30.sentence: The familial OCD–tic link is a Kleinian pair: the tic discharges what cannot be held, and the compulsion tries to repair it. A genetic tie to tic disorders, not PANDAS or panic, means the family may be living both the fragmenting burst and the need to put the pieces back.

2011-31.sentence: Memantine is not another “smart pill” in the donepezil–galantamine–rivastigmine–tacrine AChE family; it is an NMDA antagonist that damps glutamate noise so remaining cortex can still think. Name the receptor in the room. If you lump memantine with the cholinergics, you are treating a wish for one magic enhancer, not the two different synapses actually on the list.

2011-32.sentence: An 8-to-12-year-old with depression more often brings a stomachache than adult-style hopelessness, anhedonia, or hypersomnia. Stay near the body first: name the pain, keep school going, and do not force uncovering of despair the child’s mind cannot yet put into words.

2011-33.sentence: Niacin deficiency (pellagra) can put depression, apathy, and memory loss in the same person as a scaly rash on sun-exposed skin—one missing vitamin speaking through skin and mind. Do not split “psych” from “derm”: the bad object here is a hole in nutrition, not a purely inner persecutor.

2011-34.sentence: The developmental move is to let the patient use a current AA member as a third, not to become the parent who drives, hints, waives the copay, or makes care hostage to a signed card. That is how a reluctant adult grows a capacity to borrow another recovering ego instead of remaining fused with—or defiant toward—you.

2011-35.sentence: Ask how the family actually reads with the child. That scene shows whether learning lives under a harsh “do it or else” conscience or under a shared, usable voice the child can take in. Discipline history and diagnoses matter later; the reading pair is where guilt or pride about letters is being installed right now.

2011-36.sentence: Six admissions, nonadherence, housing loss, and many specialists sit on Erikson’s trust and identity tasks: this mind cannot yet keep clinic, meds, and “who I am in town” inside without a team that comes to the person. Assertive community treatment is the scaffolding for those stages; weekly supportive hours or MET alone assume a self that is already there.

2011-37.sentence: Essential tremor shows up when the hands try to do something—hold a cup, write—so the finding is not just “old age shaking”; it is a public announcement that purposeful action is no longer reliable. That is what the symptom is doing for the person: it turns competence into a visible, embarrassing negotiation every time they reach.

2011-38.sentence: Chromosome-17 frontotemporal dementia (MAPT) lays down tau inside neurons; the circuits that usually keep impulses in check are the ones dying. Denial then does the rest of the work: the person simply does not register the disinhibition and lost empathy that everyone else can see.

2011-39.sentence: When someone says exercise is pointless until the back is gone, the pair can start living that rule instead of treating it: that is an enactment, a two-person repetition of “nothing counts until pain is erased.” Group CBT’s actual target—function despite pain—is the move that stops that scene.

2011-40.sentence: Naming alprazolam at 2 mg four times a day is the wish for instant quiet; the blank first-attack history is the colliding prohibition against being seen as a seeker. Substance abuse lives in that collision: the drug is requested as medicine so the craving never has to be named.

2011-41.sentence: In CBT, feelings of devaluation—not anergy or anhedonia—are what keep major depression going. Often that “I am useless” line is not a new thought at all; it is an old verdict that never became a memory, so it keeps repeating as a body-and-mind shutdown.

2011-42.sentence: The many-site complaints after a negative workup recruit you either as the doctor who dismisses the body or the one who chases another specialist. Regular scheduled visits with a physical exam refuse both roles: you stay a steady, examining presence instead of proving or disproving the lump in the throat.

2011-43.sentence: Hospital protocol that names chlordiazepoxide is a rigid conscience; chronic hepatitis is the sanctioned exception that lets you break the house rule without being reckless. Lorazepam still works because it skips oxidative CYP metabolism and leaves the liver via glucuronide conjugation, so you treat withdrawal without stacking more hepatic work on a damaged organ.

2011-44.sentence: What arrives in separation anxiety is not generic clinginess but a specific mental picture: while we are apart, something catastrophic will happen to me or to my caretaker. Other childhood anxieties can look like the same tears at the door; this one is organized around harm-to-the-dyad, not around social scrutiny or a grab-bag of worries that only happen to quiet near mom.

2011-45.sentence: The body is drawing a horizontal line: mid-thoracic sensory level, lost vibration and joint position in the feet, brisk legs, bilateral plantar responses, and a bladder that has stopped cooperating. That package is acute transverse myelitis doing its job as a cord-level alarm, not a length-dependent polyneuropathy and not an anterior-spinal infarct that would spare dorsal-column position sense.

2011-46.sentence: Trust versus mistrust starts before speech because the newborn already comes equipped: face preference, voice tracking, and cross-modal matching that let a caregiver become a recognizable person. Attachment is not something you install after a mythical autistic phase; those built-in perceptual skills are how the infant recruits a reliable other in the first months.

2011-47.sentence: Chess and Thomas watched the same children at 3 months, 2, 5, and 20 years, which is a prospective cohort: you start with a defined group and follow temperament forward into later psychiatric trouble. That design is how you test whether an early trait actually predicts later illness, rather than guessing backward from the kids who already got sick.

2011-48.sentence: In Capgras the loved person is split: the face is recognized, but the feeling of “this is my father” is ripped off and dumped into an impostor. Klein would call that projective identification in delusional form—the bad or dead version of the object is evacuated into a look-alike so the mind does not have to hold love and threat in one father.

2011-49.sentence: Fluoxetine is the “good object” they can name; the forgotten serotonergic partner is the split-off bad object still in the bloodstream. Serotonin syndrome (fever, myoclonus, restlessness) is what happens when both halves of the pair are acting at once and nobody is holding them as one dangerous combination.

2011-50.sentence: Citalopram’s long half-life lets the patient use suppression: they know they skipped pills and can wait, because levels fall slowly. Paroxetine and venlafaxine do not grant that pause; the same lapse becomes electric-shock sensations, so the body refuses the defense.

2011-51.sentence: Disulfiram is already an enactment: instead of talking about the wish to drink, you and the patient install a chemical stand-in for failed acetaldehyde dehydrogenase. One drink then lives the punishment in the body—flush, nausea, shock—rather than putting the conflict into words.

2011-52.sentence: The left arm has left without leaving the chair: no swing, rigidity, slow finger tapping, while the rest of the gait still tries to walk. That vertical split of the motor self is Parkinson disease, not a mind that dissociated—do not treat the unused limb as “just not paying attention.”

2011-53.sentence: Between eight and eleven, ego strength shows up as internalization of parental values: the rule holds when no adult is watching. That is impulse control moving inside; altruism and abstract rights come later and should not be demanded yet.

2011-54.sentence: Catastrophe skips to termination—“I failed, so I never graduate”—and tries to end the story in one sentence. Listing evidence for and against failing out of college is the CBT limit: stay in the hour, do not soothe or excavate childhood, and do not let the exam become a premature goodbye.

2011-55.sentence: The trial comment here is not “you are fighting the medicine,” but “your neck and eyes locked because D2 blockade outran acetylcholine, and diphenhydramine at the muscarinic-1 receptor will put that balance back.” If the patient can take that in—see the dystonia as a receptor event they did not choose—they can use the injection as information instead of as proof they are being attacked.

2011-56.sentence: The frame after an adequate, tolerated immediate-release methylphenidate trial is not a scramble into clonidine, atomoxetine, or desipramine; it is staying inside first-line stimulant logic and trying mixed amphetamine salts. Holding that sequence is the limit: you do not declare the whole class a failure just because one molecule did not work.

2011-57.sentence: Flat face is not an empty tank; the pleasure that actually drops in schizophrenia is social interaction, the live give-and-take with another person. A pill can feel like feed or poison, but it cannot substitute for that missing social reward—so do not treat the face as if the meal, the song, or the drug high were gone too.

2011-58.sentence: Diarrhea after an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor is the body saying what the failing memory cannot: acetylcholine is flooding the gut. That is an unrepresented state—experience that never becomes a story—so you read the stool and the dose, not a search for a forgotten trauma, as the thing being repeated.

2011-59.sentence: Adult opsoclonus-myoclonus-ataxia is a collision: the wish to look and reach stays online while an immune prohibition slams the brainstem and cerebellum, usually in the service of hunting breast carcinoma. The eyes and limbs keep firing the impulse; the hidden tumor turns that impulse against the self.

2011-60.sentence: Secure preschool attachment shows up as empathy and altruism: the child can feel another’s distress and still offer a toy, because the caregiver remains a usable base. That is not a split-off self leaving the room; it is one mind that can stay with both need and the other person’s need.

2011-61.sentence: Early refills and “I just need a few more” for pain relievers are often already an enactment: you and the patient are repeating a two-person scene of demand and supply instead of naming the use. Pause the pad and ask what the extra dose is doing in the relationship—soothing, binding, or testing whether you will become the next source.

2011-62.sentence: Interviewing all parties is the forensic version of a secure base: the child and each parent get a fair proximity to the evaluator, not just the parent who hired you. Skip one side and you become an attachment figure for the retaining parent’s protest, not a neutral assessor.

2011-63.sentence: Reactive mood in atypical depression means the ego can still take in a good object and briefly lift—affect tolerance is not locked in melancholic shutdown. That flicker of lift after a friend or good news is a strength sign, not proof the depression is “not real.”

2011-64.sentence: The enuresis alarm asks the child and family to stay with wet nights until the signal becomes internal; that is more uncovering of a habit loop than desmopressin’s overnight cover. Lower relapse is the payoff of building a mind that can wake itself, not a drug that holds the symptom while camp week passes.

2011-65.sentence: Months after whole brain radiation, the leukoencephalopathy can look like the patient “checked out” of the relationship—apathy, slow thinking, unsteady gait—when the white-matter hit is doing the withdrawing. Name the delayed radiation injury with the family so you do not treat the pair as if they are jointly refusing care.

2011-66.sentence: Valproate holding lamotrigine in the blood is a Kleinian squeeze: one drug projects its load into the other until the level climbs and the rash risk is in the room. Titrate slower and lower so you repair the pair instead of acting as if each medicine lives in its own paranoid-schizoid silo.

2011-67.sentence: Lateral medullary stroke (Wallenberg) is the body holding two maps at once: ipsilateral face numbness beside contralateral limb findings, plus hiccups, nystagmus, and falling toward the lesion. If you collapse that into one “good” story—just Ménière’s, just midbrain—you drop the bad object, the brainstem, out of the relationship with the exam.

2011-68.sentence: Talking about an advance directive while the patient is competent is mirroring: you reflect a whole self that can still choose, not a collapsed one on a vent. Wait until life support or “only if they ask,” and you stop idealizing their agency and treat competence as something the family or the admission desk can lend them.

2011-69.sentence: Competence to proceed is a current-functioning question—can this defendant understand the courtroom and assist counsel today, Dusky-style—not what psychosis did at the time of the offense. The evaluator’s wish to settle guilt collides with the legal prohibition against turning a CST exam into a stealth insanity or mens rea interview.

2011-70.sentence: Activated charcoal will not bind lithium; the ion will not attach to that dark slurry no matter how much you want a procedure to hold the danger. Treat the medical team and serial levels as the actual secure base, and stop using charcoal as a substitute attachment when the molecule will not stay.

2011-71.sentence: Venlafaxine is the SNRI most likely to raise blood pressure, especially after a dose increase you and the patient negotiated together. Hypertension here is not a one-person side effect; it is the body’s comment on a treatment alliance that kept pushing noradrenergic tone without checking the cuff.

2011-72.sentence: Preparation is the moment the patient can name marijuana’s cost to school, money, and mood and commit to a plan without having changed use yet. The old cancelling was a vertical split—the using self left the room while the body stayed booked; showing up consistently means those parts are in the same chair long enough to plan.

2011-73.sentence: Harm avoidance is ego work under load: the person treats novelty as danger and clamps down on impulse before it can be tested. A serotonin-transporter polymorphism can tilt that temperamental brake, but it does not tell you whether this patient can still reality-test and stay in the exam room when anxiety rises.

2011-74.sentence: Davanloo treats the defense as the problem in the hour, not as a polite delay. When the patient smiles, intellectualizes, or goes vague, you name that maneuver and hold them to the feeling it is covering, rather than chasing Oedipus, a preset termination date, or an interpersonal formulation.

2011-75.sentence: The overdose is already an enactment: the patient and the system are living a lethal bid for care instead of putting despair into words. Warm dry skin, dilated pupils, quiet bowel, and a QTc of 589 msec name the TCA, so the team must hold the body first and not replay abandonment by missing the ECG.

2011-76.sentence: The frame includes the pill schedule; missed paroxetine is a broken appointment with the receptor. You hold the limit by naming discontinuation (dizziness, shocks, vivid dreams) rather than treating a two-day gap as moral failure or as proof the depression has instantly returned.

2011-77.sentence: A blunted TSH after TRH was once offered as a lab proof that the depression was “real,” as if the patient needed a hormone slip to justify need. The relationship task now is to use that historical finding without making the assay a demand that suffering show up on a stimulation test.

2011-78.sentence: At 81 the motor ego has already thinned: initiation, dress, and gait no longer arrive on time. Carbidopa/levodopa is the first treatment because it restores that late-life capacity; dopamine agonists, anticholinergics, selegiline, and entacapone ask an aging brain for more than it can safely give.

2011-79.sentence: Staff’s “she’s getting back at us” story is a sanctioned gap in morality: incontinence is recoded as a moral offense so the unit can feel righteous instead of late. Timed voiding, independent of requests, treats the bladder and the memory deficit, and it also stops punishing an 82-year-old for urgency she cannot hold.

2011-80.sentence: Childhood-onset schizophrenia usually creeps in; you cannot rush a developing ego to produce the crisp, adult-style break that later-onset illness often shows. The gradual course is itself a limit: school drop-off and thinning relatedness may be the illness arriving before well-formed delusions ever do.

2011-81.sentence: The remembered train-and-panic scene is the manifest dream: the version the mind can hold after sleep has done its work. Dream work has already contained the raw wish and dread—Bion’s nameless feeling made thinkable—so what you hear at the seminar is the evacuated night, not the latent content.

2011-82.sentence: Suicide or attempted suicide is the allegation that most often lands in court, and it hits the psychiatrist’s self where competence and the wish to be a protecting ideal live. Careful documentation of thoughts, intent, plan, means, and the why of your decision is also a self-object function: it mirrors that you thought, so you can survive the patient’s despair without collapsing into omnipotent rescue or frozen shame.

2011-83.sentence: In CBT, humor is licensed when it loosens a distorted cognition—one error equals total incompetence—so a new perspective can enter. The wish to be flawless and the prohibition against looking foolish collide in that all-or-nothing thought; a well-timed joke lets the collision become thinkable instead of another humiliation.

2011-84.sentence: Norming is when members stop using avoidance of difference as their group defense and can show who they actually are. Early silence and waiting for the leader is suppression of conflict; once that thins, experiential learning can start because disagreement is no longer treated as a threat to the group’s skin.

2011-85.sentence: Bradylalia is not just a motor lag; it can feel like the session itself is starving you of a reply. The slow words become a demand for patience, and if you fill the silence too fast you are treating the delay as poison instead of as the depression speaking.

2011-86.sentence: Burning, shock-like neuropathic pain is a real limit, not a debate about whether the patient is “psychogenic.” Hold the frame: name the pain type, treat the nerve injury, and do not make the patient prove they deserve relief.

2011-87.sentence: Chronic opioids commonly drop testosterone; low desire and flat energy are not only “resistance” to insight. A trial comment can name both: the hormone change is real, and it still matters how they use the low drive as a story about themselves.

2011-88.sentence: A verbal IQ far above nonverbal is doing work: words cover what the hands and spatial mind cannot hold. The split is the signal to look further, not a trophy for being “smart enough.”

2011-89.sentence: Appetite suppression and sleep loss on a stimulant land on the child’s daily industry: can they eat, rest, and still do schoolwork. That is an Erikson industry-versus-inferiority problem, not just a side-effect checklist.

2011-90.sentence: Nystagmus that worsens with fixation and has a vertical component is a brainstem finding, so the ethical limit is not “reassure and discharge.” You hold time and workup until central disease is off the table.

2011-91.sentence: She is treating the household food as poison, not as a meal. A family meeting puts the contested feed on the table so you do not answer that fear with risperidone or a clearance stamp.

2011-92.sentence: A neologism is a private word that lets the thought out without using the shared one. Ordinary language would make the idea too public; the invented term is a small repression of the common name.

2011-93.sentence: Most serotonin sits in the gastrointestinal tract, so an SSRI often speaks first as nausea or loose stool. If you and the patient argue only about whether the pill is “working in the brain,” you are already repeating the split instead of naming the gut.

2011-94.sentence: Fragile X is a CGG triple-repeat expansion that silences FMR1. Language and social development stall because the synapse never got the protein it needed.

2011-95.sentence: The note has to show you could stand the anxiety of not restraining or over-intervening. Write why you rejected those other responses so the chart records judgment, not only a risk label.

2011-96.sentence: The Stroop asks the patient to name ink color and leave the written word alone. The examiner’s rule is the regulating other; the printed color-word is the pull toward the easier, more familiar cue.

2011-97.sentence: Writer's cramp is a two-person problem: the hand only locks when it is in a demand-relationship with the page, the boss, or the audience, not when it is idle. Botulinum toxin is the treatment that interrupts that motor conversation at the neuromuscular junction so the writing pair can work without the grip becoming the protest.

2011-98.sentence: A ten-year sentence on an adult child often lands as a verdict on the parent: the conscience may treat the conviction as proof of failed rearing and collect the debt as low mood and middle insomnia. That is adjustment disorder with depressed mood, not major depression—the sadness is a guilt payment timed to the courtroom, not a free-standing episode.

2011-99.sentence: APA ethics treat the erotic transference as never fully discharged: you remain the doctor in the patient's inner courtroom even after the last session. A date request from a former patient is recruitment into that leftover role, not informed consent—so sex with current or former patients is not allowed.

2011-100.sentence: Four sessions of a monopolizer turn the group into a hanging jury: members stop listening and start punishing, which is how a group conscience goes rigid. Cohesiveness—the felt we that lets people stay in the room—is what that moral rallying against the talker quietly kills.

2011-101.sentence: Primary process is mentation aimed at drives and wish fulfillment: images collapse time so the wish can be had now, without the adult rules of logic. In supervision the dream of unlimited parental gold is recruiting you as the wish-granter; name the wish, do not file it as a plan.

2011-102.sentence: Lymphocytes, near-normal glucose, and only a modest protein rise are the CSF's way of saying this is usually enteroviral—most often Coxsackie—not a sugar-eating bacterium. The finding does work for the consultant: it keeps you from treating a viral meningitis like meningococcus while you still manage the agitation and headache.

2011-103.sentence: Telepsychiatry asks for a developmental capacity that many psychiatrists never quite grew: staying present with a person when the body is not in the room. Reluctance is not only logistics; it is a late-arriving comfort with a new way of being with someone, and until that capacity arrives the platform sits unused.

2011-104.sentence: Restless legs at rest is the body announcing that nighttime competence has slipped: you cannot even keep still without walking it off. Pramipexole, a dopamine agonist, is first-line because it restores that quiet self-regulation; carbamazepine, clonazepam, fluoxetine, and oxycodone do not rebuild that function the same way.

2011-105.sentence: Socratic questioning is containment: you hold the raw “I am incompetent” long enough for it to become a thought you can examine, not a feeling that has to be evacuated as fact. Exposure, free association, guided imagery, and motivational interviewing do other jobs; they do not turn the automatic thought into something thinkable the way a good question does.

2011-106.sentence: What the adolescent cannot keep in mind—that two methadone tablets plus sertraline can stack into apnea—gets repeated in the body as slowed breathing. Sertraline can inhibit methadone clearance; the “pharm party” is the unrepresented interaction showing up in the emergency department rather than in a conversation.

2011-107.sentence: Hydrochlorothiazide collides two aims: the wish to lower blood pressure and the prohibition against pushing lithium into toxicity. Aspirin, fluoxetine, propranolol, and aminophylline do not raise the lithium level the way this thiazide does, so the conflict is pharmacokinetic, not just clinical preference.

2011-108.sentence: The CPT’s frame is simple: press for every letter except X. Missing the F is a failure of attention to that rule, not impulsivity, disinhibition, registration, or recall—those would be hitting X or never encoding the letter at all.

2011-109.sentence: Fluoxetine is working, so the pill is no longer just a demand for more complaints—it is also a feed that actually soothed the depression and anxiety. Terazosin treats the night sweats without yanking that feed away, which keeps the relationship from becoming another trial that “proved” medicine is poison.

2011-110.sentence: The cape-like pain/temperature loss with preserved touch is syringomyelia doing a job: it hands you a real, crossing-fiber lesion instead of a two-year-old wreck you cannot settle. Do not let the delayed timing talk you into malingering when the dissociated sensory pattern names a syrinx.

2011-111.sentence: Fourteen sits on Erikson’s identity-versus-role-confusion task: she has to know who she is and where she is before any story of the rape can be hers. Grounding puts her back in the ED as herself; playing along with the friend’s house, or sedating her, leaves identity parked in a false scene.

2011-112.sentence: Little Hans’s horse phobia is castration anxiety with a costume: the boy’s conscience, his emerging superego, converts the forbidden Oedipal wish into a single avoidable animal. Stay off the street and you never have to feel guilty about wanting mother or rivaling father.

2011-113.sentence: Treat the late-luteal crash as a monthly developmental stress test, not “just PMS.” The same ego that regulates mood mid-cycle can lose that capacity when ovarian steroids swing, and the drop can reach major-depressive severity.

2011-114.sentence: In SLE the common psychiatric picture is depression or cognitive dysfunction, not mania or florid psychosis—the disease most often dulls and saddens the self rather than inflating it. Object-relationally, the body becomes a bad object inside: the organ that once held the person now attacks thinking and mood.

2011-115.sentence: Ask about alcohol in private, as a routine fact, before you interpret what “just partying” means. Uncovering motives too soon only thickens the cover story; first you need an ego that can stand the most common adolescent drug being named.

2011-116.sentence: A late-but-solid sleeper is often a delayed clock, not a child who “won’t” go to bed. Melatonin is a zeitgeber that resets circadian timing; treat it as development of the sleep system, not a power struggle you interpret.

2011-117.sentence: Neuroticism, extraversion, openness, agreeableness, and conscientiousness are ordinary ranges, not hidden wishes. High conscientiousness can mean dependable, not obsessional; do not decode a Five-Factor score as if it were a symptom.

2011-118.sentence: Some endings are anatomic, not transferential: medulloblastoma is the common childhood CNS solid tumor, classically posterior fossa. You cannot rush past lineage and location into metaphor; neuroblastoma is usually not a primary brain tumor.

2011-119.sentence: Winnicott’s job is not to erase frustration or keep primary maternal preoccupation forever; it is to notice the child’s push to explore. Contain the toddler’s mix of excitement and fear so curiosity becomes thinkable instead of raw dread the parent has to evacuate.

2011-120.sentence: Flumazenil is not a clean undo when the history is incomplete. In a benzodiazepine-dependent patient it can rip off GABA cover and precipitate a withdrawal seizure; the ethical limit is not to reverse what you cannot safely take away.

2011-121.sentence: Late life sits on Erikson’s integrity-versus-despair task: staying a whole person while the body gets less reliable. Antidepressants—on top of benzodiazepines—are the other class most tied to falls after sixty, so a nighttime tumble after a med change is the body announcing that autonomy is under threat, not just a pharmacy footnote.

2011-122.sentence: The suicide attempt is doing work the patient could not say: it turns “I could not reach you” into a crisis that cannot be ignored. Abandonment is the legal name for that same rupture—vacation without coverage—so the act is both a plea and an indictment of the missing covering clinician.

2011-123.sentence: What never quite arrived in this adolescent is a reliable brake: the capacity to pause between feeling and act. The reported cluster with serotonin dysregulation, suicidality, and aggression in borderline youth is impulsivity, not merely anger—so safety planning has to treat the missing delay, not only the mood.

2011-124.sentence: An objective inventory lets a strict inner judge fill in boxes instead of free-associating in front of you. The Millon Clinical Multiaxial Inventory (MCMI) is that structured adult personality measure; Rorschach, sentence completion, and word association leak, and the WCST is not a personality test at all.

2011-125.sentence: The subacute ataxia plus anti-Yo recruits you as the detective who must find the hidden tumor before the cerebellum is gone—your countertransference is urgency, not reassurance from a normal MRI. Order a CT scan of the chest next; mild CSF pleocytosis and a clean brain scan do not close the cancer hunt in a long-time smoker.

2011-126.sentence: When there is no hallucination or delusion to hold the breakdown, the story gets lived as blank decline—unrepresented collapse rather than a named psychotic plot. Deteriorative disorder is separated from schizophrenia by the absence of prominent positive symptoms, so do not retrofit a frank psychosis onto a deficit-only course.

2011-127.sentence: Moral treatment is a fight between two drives: the wish to be held and occupied, and the wish to collapse into chaos. Pinel’s daily schedule of work and learning is the compromise—libido gets a job so the hospital does not become a stage for unrestrained impulse.

2011-128.sentence: The enactment is already running: mother and doctor both treat methadone as a poison, repeating the old story that help itself will harm the baby. Name the pair—methadone maintenance is the evidence-based hold, not another abandonment dressed up as purity.

2011-129.sentence: The cancel splits the hour: one self sits in the chair, another is already back with the unavailable father. Interpret that transference out loud so the two states can meet instead of the patient leaving the treatment to stay loyal to the old absence.

2011-130.sentence: ICU “psychosis” is delirium: attention fragments and the person leaves without leaving the bed. That is a vertical split from a sick brain, not a new identity you interpret—you fix the cause so the mind can stay in one piece.

2011-131.sentence: Picking mirtazapine for the gut-sensitive, sleepless, thin patient can become an enactment: you soothe appetite and sleep while both of you quietly dodge the SSRI diarrhea that actually happens less on mirtazapine. Say the trade—less diarrhea, more sedation and weight—so the prescription is a choice, not a rescue.

2011-132.sentence: Calling for MRI after a deteriorating head injury can be denial: we wait for the prettier picture while an acute epidural hematoma expands. CT is the defense that faces the blood now instead of wishing the posterior fossa or white-matter detail would save the hour.

2011-133.sentence: Clozapine is not only the last-line antipsychotic here; for a patient who gets more paranoid and then uses cocaine, the pill can feel like a feed that quiets the voices enough to make abstinence imaginable. If the resident treats clozapine as a demand for blood draws and compliance, the patient hears poison, not help—and the coke returns when the relationship around the tablet goes cold.

2011-134.sentence: A first focal-onset seizure that secondarily generalizes at 58 is a brain that may be carrying glioblastoma, not a mind ready for uncovering work. Keep the stance supportive and concrete: image, neurology, and containment of panic, because digging for meaning while the cortex is under a mass is technique that outruns what this ego can use.

2011-135.sentence: A self-help group is two (or twenty) people practicing a new interpersonal pattern: they interrupt drinking together, they do not excavate childhood. The goal is overcoming maladaptive behaviors—the room becomes a living lab where the old drinking dyad is replaced by a sober one, not insight into psychodynamics or a personality overhaul.

2011-136.sentence: Prolonged caregiving without a secure base keeps the attachment system on high alert, and that protest is written into neuro-immuno-endocrine function—HPA axis, sleep, and the skin flare of psoriasis. Stress does not mutate Mendelian genes or rewrite the genome; it uses the other person’s absence (or presence) to turn the endocrine and immune dials.

2011-137.sentence: Needle exchange is harm reduction: you meet a mind that cannot yet tolerate abstinence and you shore up ego strength—impulse control, reality testing about overdose and infection—without demanding an identity change first. Supply, access, and demand strategies fight the drug market; this one fights death while the patient is still using.

2011-138.sentence: Toluene’s subcortical demyelination steals the scaffolding of competence: headaches, lability, and confusion make the self feel unmirrored and incompetent, which the anxiety then tries to paper over. Do not idealize “just anxiety” or a personality problem; the MRI lesions are why self-esteem and affect regulation are collapsing.

2011-139.sentence: Age less than 35 is the suicide risk that belongs to schizophrenia, not to the general population, because the drive to live and the wish to erase a new, shaming identity collide before a workable self has formed. The early course is not just statistics; it is a young ego still arguing with a diagnosis it cannot yet metabolize.

2011-140.sentence: Tuskegee failed on the risk:benefit ratio because investigators used denial: they called untreated syphilis “observation” so they would not have to feel they were harming Black men. Denial here is not forgetting facts; it is keeping the harm out of awareness so the study can continue.

2011-141.sentence: When both tolerance and withdrawal to Internet use can develop, the consult is already an enactment: more time, better gear, then anger and dysphoria when the connection is cut, and you two are living that chase instead of naming it.
