Ask about loss of control and forced disconnect as the relationship, not only as checklist items.

2011-142.sentence: The red-glass exam is the frame: one meter, glass over the right eye, six cardinal gazes, and you hold that limit so the double images can speak. Those images localize a right medial rectus palsy; skipping the protocol is how you lose the finding.

2011-143.sentence: Most hypnosis is not an authoritative pill you swallow; it is an invitation to use inner resources for adaptive coping, like being offered a feed rather than a command. Persuasion and orders from on high treat the trance as poison or demand; the usual technique treats it as something the patient already has.

2011-144.sentence: Refractory epilepsy marks a limit you cannot rush: drugs have already failed, and the cortex will not become seizure-free because you wish it. Electrical stimulation of the vagus nerve is the next honest ending of the medication chapter, not a shortcut around that ending.

2011-145.sentence: The daughter's request to keep the patient home can hide her own exhaustion, so burnout is the part of the story that needs to be seen, not another behavior plan. A trial comment—“How are you holding up with this?”—tests whether she can use that insight, or whether time-outs and restraints will just get dumped on an already depleted caregiver.

2011-146.sentence: A lithium tremor is not a vanity complaint; it attacks the feeling of a competent body when the cup shakes in the hand. Propranolol is the concrete repair of that self-esteem wound—restore the steady hand first, then talk about living with lithium.

2011-147.sentence: Panic turns a heartbeat into nameless dread: a raw sensation that the mind cannot think, so it gets evacuated into another ER visit. CBT’s job is containment—rename palpitations as a misfired alarm, not a dying heart, until the feeling becomes thinkable instead of something to dump.

2011-148.sentence: Late-onset schizophrenia clustering in women is often grief or isolation that never found words, then returned as a persecutor in the room. The body and the dyad carry what cannot be remembered as loss; do not treat it as childhood schizophrenia that simply waited until after sixty.

2011-149.sentence: The wish is an unbroken night; the prohibition is a brain that now fragments sleep, so the fight shows up as longer awakenings, not more REM or more slow-wave. “I barely slept” is that collision spoken in the morning, not a complaint that subjective quality or deep sleep somehow increased.

2011-150.sentence: Those few bilateral jerks after pallor and a tight collar are not a seizure capacity that finally arrived; they are an old baroreflex that got too loud. Carotid sinus syncope is the developmental story: a reflex that should stay quiet overfired, then the limbs twitched as the lights came back on.

2011-151.sentence: Intense mood is not just “a difficult kid.” It is a signal the child is using to move the environment: get you closer, get you to stop the novelty, get the world back on a predictable clock. Thomas and Chess’s difficult temperament clusters that intensity with irregular sleep/feeding and withdrawal from new situations, so the job is to name the signal without treating the child as a character defect.

2011-152.sentence: Aspirin toxicity can recruit you into the role of the one who “should have known” and now must rescue: tinnitus, abdominal pain, and mild metabolic acidosis arrive as a body-language confession you are asked to decode fast. Notice the pull to become either the all-seeing parent or the scolding one; the antidote is a calm, specific salicylate workup rather than a moral interrogation in the ED.

2011-153.sentence: Trazodone’s rare priapism warning is a superego moment: you either give the patient a sanctioned, shame-reducing script or you leave them alone with a private catastrophe. Counsel plainly—if an erection lasts too long, it is an emergency, not a character failing—so conscience can protect the body instead of silencing it.

2011-154.sentence: Those morning whole-body jerks that drop objects are the drive leaking through: a sudden motor discharge the adolescent and family have been trying to prohibit by calling it clumsiness. Juvenile myoclonic epilepsy (4–6 Hz irregular polyspike-and-wave) names the conflict medically so you can treat sleep and alcohol as real precipitants rather than as willpower failures after the first grand mal.

2011-155.sentence: Cortical brain death leaves no shared memory of the person, so the adult child and the dissenting nurse repeat the lost relationship in the unit: they keep the body “alive” as a stand-in for a goodbye that cannot be thought. Meet family and staff separately first; the polarization is the unrepresented grief, not a debate you win by confronting hope.

2011-156.sentence: Klein put the infant’s earliest objects—breast, mother, the split good/bad other—at the center, earlier than Freud’s later Oedipal theater. When a patient floods the team with idealization then condemnation, they are evacuating raw bits they cannot yet think; your job is to contain that (hold it, name it) so it can become a thought instead of a war.

2011-157.sentence: The locus ceruleus is where the self borrows chemical quiet: opioids shut down cAMP-dependent phosphorylation there so the noradrenergic alarm does not fire. Pull that borrowed soothe away and the self cannot hold itself—sweating, tachycardia, and panic are the LC firing without the mirror that once kept it still.

2011-158.sentence: DSM-IV-TR parked compulsive skin picking in Impulse Control Disorder NOS because the field had not yet asked the patient to see the picking as something they could watch. A trial comment—what happens in the second before your fingers move—tests whether they can use that insight or only discharge tension.

2011-159.sentence: Extinction is an ending you cannot hurry: you withdraw the unconditioned stimulus and wait while the conditioned response dies of neglect. The association weakens only after the expected catastrophe keeps not arriving; rushing that interval is just more pairing in disguise.

2011-160.sentence: The MMPI-2 Lie scale catches denial dressed as virtue: the person endorses social-desirability items and erases ordinary faults. That is not a pretty personality; it is a defense that says nothing bad about me can be seen, so you do not interpret the clinical scales until you name the lie.

2011-161.sentence: The SSRI meta-analyses show more depressed youths respond to medication than spontaneously report suicidality, so the pair of you can live a false calm: the pill is working, so we stop asking. That is an enactment: the system acts as if silence equals safety instead of asking about suicidal thinking directly.

2011-162.sentence: A no-harm contract has no significant empirical support, and it can invite a vertical split: the patient signs while another part stays suicidal. They leave without leaving the chair—the signature is dissociated compliance, not a whole person agreeing, and it lets both of you stop looking.

2011-163.sentence: ALS can look like a nervous breakdown until wasting and fasciculations show the body is failing, not the will. Ego strength here is affect tolerance: helping the person stay oriented to that motor-neuron fact without collapsing into panic or denial.

2011-164.sentence: A bizarre delusion was once enough, by itself, to name schizophrenia—an official shortcut that treated one break with shared reality as the whole diagnosis. Limits still matter: you cannot rush a current assessment by borrowing that DSM-IV-TR exception as if time and criteria had not changed.

2011-165.sentence: Metformin is not just a metabolic add-on; it is a trial comment in pill form: “the valproate-plus-atypical combination is working, and the weight is also real.” Insight is whether the patient can use that comment instead of hearing only criticism of appetite or willpower.

2011-166.sentence: IPT starts by mapping current social connections, not childhood or unconscious conflict, because the work lives in the living network. Holding that frame means you do not drift into character analysis when the task is grief, role change, dispute, or thin support.

2011-167.sentence: Exaggerated startle and stimulus-triggered myoclonus in a rapidly deteriorating older patient point to spongiform encephalopathy, not a medication that failed to soothe. The pill-as-relationship trap is offering more sedative as feed when the body is signaling a fatal prion illness.

2011-168.sentence: Dusky competence is understanding the proceedings and assisting counsel; failing the second prong is not the same as insanity or an irresistible impulse. Projective identification—pushing an unbearable state into the other so they feel it—shows up when the defendant cannot work with the attorney and the court starts to carry the panic instead of testing those two capacities.

2011-169.sentence: Codeine is a mu agonist that can flatten respiratory drive the same way it flattens the ache the person was trying not to feel. Pinpoint pupils and blue lips are the body saying the mute button went past sleep into hypoventilation.

2011-170.sentence: WAIS-IV Vocabulary is the ethical baseline: it estimates who this mind was before the dementia, so you do not treat today’s Trails or WCST score as the whole person. Hold that limit. Without it you either over-pathologize a still-verbal patient or miss a real drop.

2011-171.sentence: Fluoxetine lengthens ejaculatory latency so arousal can be noticed instead of discharged in a rush. That pause is a trial comment the body can use: stay with the surge, name it, then finish rather than flee.

2011-172.sentence: Middle-phase IPT keeps the work inside current relationships—the role dispute this week—not transference or childhood archaeology. The limit is the clock: you do not rush an old wound into insight on IPT time.

2011-173.sentence: The axillary nerve used to carry abduction and the small patch of feeling over the deltoid; after the shoulder jumps out, that function is evacuated as wasting and a numb lateral badge of skin. Name the nerve so the raw loss becomes a thinkable lesion, not nameless dread in the arm.

2011-174.sentence: The observing ego is the bit of self that can turn an unconscious drive into a sentence: I felt small, then I wanted to attack. Mirroring that sequence builds competence—watching the drive—rather than needing the supervisor to be a flawless ideal.

2011-175.sentence: After a cluster of seizures the usual cortical brake on drive is offline, so aggression and forbidden wishes arrive as paranoia and hallucinations instead of as thoughts you can argue with. Interictal psychosis in this timeline is that collision resolving over days as inhibition comes back online—not mania, not a new schizophreniform illness.

2011-176.sentence: Psychosis and mania leave families with terror that has no story, so they repeat it as blame, hovering, and sleepless nights. Multifamily psychoeducation that provides knowledge and direct guidance gives the illness words and a map, so the group can think instead of only living the unrepresented panic.

2011-177.sentence: In biofeedback you are recruited as the trainer who rewards a small drop in muscle tension or a rise in finger temperature—the screen is the other who says yes. That is operant conditioning: the autonomic signal changes because a contingent reward follows it, not because a paired bell (classical conditioning) made it happen.

2011-178.sentence: If this mind can make a story from an ambiguous TAT picture, it can probably use uncovering of unconscious drive and conflict. Reach for the TAT when you need those themes; the SCID and MMPI-2 will inventory symptoms and traits but will not show you the wish.

2011-179.sentence: The reading problem lives between two people: the child who cannot map speech sounds to letters and the adult who either slows down to phonemes or shames the child as lazy. Name the deficit as phonological functioning so the dyad practices sound-structure together instead of arguing about IQ, vision, or oculomotor skill.

2011-180.sentence: You cannot rush the end of the drinking; motivational interviewing holds that limit by refusing advice and confrontation. Develop discrepancy—the gap between the valued self and what alcohol is costing—and let the patient’s own timeline close it.

2011-181.sentence: Offer a trial comment that names the mismatch: work is slower even though pleasure and mood are intact, so the mind may be missing a body cause rather than “just getting old.” If they can use that idea, B12 is the test that respects their part—checking a reversible deficiency instead of folding the complaint back into bipolar illness or valproate/bupropion.

2011-182.sentence: A day of headache and irritability after twenty minutes of confusion threatens the athlete’s sense of competence—the self that feels real when it can play. Hold that self with a clear one-week hold rather than rushing back to restore the idealized player the moment confusion lifts, or sending them for MRI/CT when the exam is already normal.

2011-183.sentence: Three diagnosis groups on one mood scale can feel like nameless dread: maybe the labels are noise and you should just pick two and t-test. ANOVA is the container: it holds all three means at once so the question stays thinkable instead of being evacuated into pairwise tests, chi-square, or clustering.

2011-184.sentence: Ease, named pain, compassion, a look at insight, and shown expertise loosen the patient’s first defense—often a stiff, judging distance that keeps the doctor from mattering. Rapport is what fills that space once they can suppress (hold back, not bury) the fear of being exposed, instead of needing reflection or transference as the main tool.

2011-185.sentence: The pair in the room can already be living a hopeless script: staff treat the crisis as “personality,” “anxiety,” or “just alcohol,” and the patient’s despair is sent home unspoken. Name the mood disorder as the most common diagnosis among those who complete suicide so the work stays a suicide assessment, not an enactment of dismissal.

2011-186.sentence: The frame here is not to turn church-shopping and guilty doubt into OCD or bipolar when the rest of the mental status is clear and she will not act against her morals. Hold the limit as a religious or spiritual problem: explore meaning and supports without medicalizing her faith, and do not report or medicate a crisis of affiliation.

2011-187.sentence: The split ring finger is the body drawing a map: median territory at the wrist, not a neck root and not a vague “anxiety tingle.” Treat that line as communication, not decoration — the patient is asking you to believe a nerve, not a mood.

2011-188.sentence: The most frequent extra problem in autism is intellectual disability, not epilepsy or a second “psychosis” label. Social mute and low IQ can look like the same storm; the symptom of failing self-care may be cognition doing the work you keep attributing to autism alone.

2011-189.sentence: A two-year-old after a cold still cannot name “worst headache of my life”; fever and flop are the whole vocabulary. Enterovirus is the usual meningeal visitor at that age — the language for pain has not arrived, so you treat first and sort virus from bacterium after.

2011-190.sentence: Object relations says the mind is stocked with pictures of self and other; self psychology asks what those pictures do for esteem. When the therapist stops mirroring, the inner other flips from idealized protector to cruel rejecter — same furniture, different job: holding the self together.

2011-191.sentence: The street offense is a collision: a wish to stay free and untreated versus a community that wants punishment. Mental health court is the compromise formation — it aims the same defendant at treatment rather than jail instead of pretending the drive or the prohibition disappeared.

2011-192.sentence: You cannot rush an MAOI off the board before the knife; the washout is a real time limit, not a suggestion. Fentanyl is the opioid that usually respects that limit; meperidine, tramadol, dextromethorphan, and amitriptyline do not — they force a serotonergic ending you did not schedule.

2011-193.sentence: A number given before seven is often an evacuation: the family dumps nameless dread—“is something wrong with this mind?”—into a score that cannot yet hold still. Wait until IQ is actually stable, then contain that anxiety as a thinkable fact instead of a verdict.

2011-194.sentence: Assertive community treatment is a conscience that leaves the office: the team is available around the clock because the patient’s own observing ego will not reliably show up for clinic. The risk is a harsh superego in a van—compliance as moral duty—rather than a sanctioned gap that lets staff go to the person when guilt and insight are not enough.

2011-195.sentence: The Nuremberg Code is a developmental milestone that arrived after catastrophe, not on schedule: research only grew a working conscience once subjects had already been treated as material. Informed consent is that late-arriving capacity—do not enroll the hospitalized patient as if the milestone never had to be learned.

2011-196.sentence: Those silent, colorful children are unrepresented cortex, not a memory: posterior cerebral artery ischemia can release formed visual images the mind cannot historicize, so they replay as pictures. Do not treat the scene as a trauma narrative or as Lewy-body psychosis when language, memory, and the motor exam are intact.

2011-197.sentence: The parents are recruiting you to become the family diagnostician who already “knows” because the older brother has ADHD. A matching teacher report is the third that breaks that transference; without it you are only confirming the story they brought you.

2011-198.sentence: A dollar every third unprompted cleanup is a fixed-ratio schedule: the reward is tied to a counted number of responses, not to the clock. The child’s “I did it myself” still rides on that FR-3 bargain until the habit can stand without the bill.

2011-199.sentence: Isolation of affect keeps the memory intact while the feeling is shoved out of the self—Klein would call this projective identification: the horror is parked in you so he can stay bland. Your visible upset is the evacuated piece; name the split, do not swallow it as if the feeling were only yours.

2011-200.sentence: ADHD here is a developmental lag in the child's own brakes, not a failure of will. Parent behavioral management is the adult becoming a temporary external executive—clear cues, consistent consequences—until that capacity arrives more fully.

2011-201.sentence: Polymyositis is the body failing at hip and thigh lift, not a disguised protest about standing up in life. The symptom's job is medical: it asks you to work up proximal weakness, not to interpret chair-rise as resistance.

2011-202.sentence: Infants under three cannot recruit you with words, so they recruit you with an injury that does not match what a baby can do. Countertransference will pull you toward the caregiver's story or toward rage; hold the protector role and get pediatrics and safeguarding in the room.

2011-203.sentence: A dinner-table monkey at four and a half is ordinary preschool play, not a crime against reality. The worry to watch is a rigid parental conscience that treats imagination as lying; if the play is friendly and the rest of development is on track, you loosen that rule, you do not pathologize the child.

2011-204.sentence: Skepticism about “talking about the past” is happening now, in the hour, as a test of whether you will lecture, go silent, or stay with him. The frame is the alliance: explore what in this session makes partnership feel unsafe before you sell the method or call it resistance.

2011-205.sentence: Asking for S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAMe) is often a bid to change mood without taking on the identity of a psychiatric patient. SAMe is a methyl donor with modest antidepressant signal, so the wish is not empty—but it still needs the same bipolar, severity, and interaction screen you would give any mood treatment.

2011-206.sentence: Severe factitious illness often rides with borderline personality because the need to be held is acted out on the body instead of said. That is acting out: the ward becomes the theater of care-seeking and rage, while the wish to be dependent stays out of words.

2011-207.sentence: Bilateral papilledema with a clean contrast CT and a bland lumbar puncture is the body announcing pressure without a mass—pseudotumor cerebri. The opening pressure and the threatened optic nerve are the meaning; the headache is only the messenger.

2011-208.sentence: Competency to stand trial is presumed unless someone raises it, so the court treats the defendant as an ordinary partner in the process until protest appears. Your job is the secure-base check: can this person understand the charge, the roles, and work with counsel—not a ritual finding of sanity or mens rea.

2011-209.sentence: Stimulant cues light glutamate projections into the reward circuit, so the craving is a chemical hijack, not a failure of will. Ego strength here is affect tolerance: noticing the surge when the old block or peer appears, and not having to chase the next hit.

2011-210.sentence: Twice-weekly binge–purge at a normal weight is bulimia nervosa, and the referral already recruits you as the one who will watch the body. Watch the countertransference—disgust, fascination, or an urge to police food—because that is the old audience being installed in the room.

2011-211.sentence: 22q11 deletion does not just raise a number; it leaves a hole in the mind's filing system, so the first break of schizophrenia often arrives as a body and a relationship that suddenly cannot be trusted. What cannot be remembered as a gene or a developmental scar is repeated as withdrawal, suspiciousness, and odd percepts in the adolescent dyad.

2011-212.sentence: Lorazepam 2 mg IM, with a repeat at 45 minutes, is the adult capacity that this intoxicated patient never quite has in the moment: a frontal brake that can wait, listen, and not throw the tray. You are not treating a character; you are lending a late-arriving inhibitory function until the brain can hold it again.

2011-213.sentence: Kindling means later depressive episodes fire without a stressor, as if the conscience no longer needs an external crime to levy the sentence. The mind has learned to punish itself on a hair trigger; guilt now arrives as weather, not as a response to a real loss.

2011-214.sentence: Bilateral facial palsy from Borrelia burgdorferi sits on Erikson's trust-versus-mistrust edge: the face that greets the world suddenly will not work on either side. The developmental task is to keep faith with the body and the medical team while Lyme, not conversion, is named and treated.

2011-215.sentence: A few beers and occasional cannabis with friends, while school and attachments hold, is typical adolescent use: the symptom is doing affiliation, not self-destruction. It marks belonging at the party more than a hole in self-esteem or a hidden family war.

2011-216.sentence: The MAOI crisis on tranylcypromine—headache, vomiting, palpitations—is a paranoid-schizoid emergency: the body is treated as a bad object that must be stopped, so you halt the drug and give nifedipine first. Repair comes later; first you contain the hypertensive storm instead of debating whether to keep the antidepressant going.

2011-217.sentence: Go/no-go is a test of the ego's brake: tap once when asked, hold still when the second tap arrives. Executive functioning is that pause between impulse and action, the same pause a distractible inpatient loses when a line or button is sitting there to be pulled.

2011-218.sentence: Selective mutism is not a language hole; it is a solution that keeps the child's voice at home, where it feels safe, and locks it at school. The silence is the symptom's job: it avoids the feared audience rather than proving the child cannot speak.

2011-219.sentence: Ordinary grief still lets longing and even a sense of the dead person's presence do their work; early, heavy depressive symptoms mean the anger of the loss has already turned inward. That is turning against the self: the 80-year-old is attacking the surviving self instead of mourning the spouse.

2011-220.sentence: A sodium of 95 mEq/L is an emergency, but the pons cannot survive a sudden leap back to normal any better than an ego can survive forced, overnight change. Over-rapid correction risks central pontine myelinolysis: the myelin strips when you correct faster than the tissue can adapt.

2011-221.sentence: Financial stress is not a moral verdict on parents; it is a load that thins affect tolerance and impulse control while several children still need care. Abuse risk rises when the caregiver's ego is depleted by rent, job loss, and exhaustion, not because two-parent homes or older teens are the usual setting.

2011-222.sentence: Traditional ECT can become an enactment of wipe-and-reset: the team seizes the whole brain and the patient pays in confusion and memory. Magnetic seizure therapy's bid is to keep the seizure while sparing more cortex, so the treatment does not have to erase the mind in order to treat the depression.

2011-223.sentence: The team can use denial—the mind simply refuses to register a cause that is sitting in the med list—and treat the new gloom, anxiety, and fog as “just hepatitis C.” Interferon-alpha is the named culprit; name it so the affect can be treated instead of waved away.

2011-224.sentence: A lost prescription is a little crisis in the relationship to the pill: feed, poison, demand, or proof that someone still has to take care of you. Asking what they would do samples judgment—whether they would call, wait, borrow, or double-dose—not whether they remember the pharmacy’s name.

2011-225.sentence: The ethical frame here is who holds the limit: the child, the teacher, or a diagnosis that stops the homework war. Reading disorder is the commonest learning disability; naming it keeps the team from turning a phonologic problem into a character flaw.

2011-226.sentence: A trial comment that names both pieces—third-nerve palsy plus equal face-arm-leg weakness on the other side—lets the team see their own half-look at “just a hemiparesis.” That crossed midbrain picture points to a perforating branch of the posterior cerebral artery, not a cortical middle-cerebral stroke.

2011-227.sentence: You cannot rush a crisp story out of someone whose job, in a compensation case, is to stay blurry. Vaguely defined, shifting symptoms are the tell; the consulting limit is to record the fog, not to write the plot they will not give.

2011-228.sentence: Patient-satisfaction scores arrive as a raw evacuation—nameless dread dumped onto the survey—until someone contains them, meaning holds the feeling long enough to think. Continuous quality improvement is that containing function for accrediting agencies: turn the complaint into a process you can map, not a smear you pass along.

2011-229.sentence: Depression in a kid is not only sad mood; it is a collapse of the self’s mirroring function—the inner sense of being seen as worthwhile—so food and withdrawal start doing the job applause and play used to do. When that self-esteem system stays hungry, later obesity often tracks the old depressive injury more than anxiety or restriction ever would.

2011-230.sentence: A left ACA infarct writes the unremembered event into the contralateral foot and leg: the body repeats a vascular story the patient cannot narrate. You treat that paresis as the memory you can examine, not as a metaphor you invent.

2011-231.sentence: The late-maturing prefrontal cortex is the brake on a wish that adolescence still floors: drive arrives first, prohibition arrives later. That is why a 15-year-old can name a future in a calm room and still chase the impulse when the wish is hot.

2011-232.sentence: When eight people remitted at 1 mg and two needed 5–10 mg, the median is the dose that still feels like a competent, typical self—not the mean, which lets the two outliers inflate what “normal” looks like. Reporting the median protects the clinic’s self-esteem as a realist: most people needed the small dose.

2011-233.sentence: Viral encephalitis plus diphenhydramine is raw beta-elements—unthinkable confusion—evacuated into paranoia instead of being contained, that is, held long enough to become a thought. Name the delirium so the ward can metabolize the dread instead of treating the evacuation as a personality.

2011-234.sentence: Huntington’s CAG story asks for support first: this mind is losing cortical control, so deep uncovering of irritability will not restore a dying striatum. Technique follows prognosis—name the autosomal-dominant illness, then keep the work concrete and containing.

2011-235.sentence: Frotteurism is not a clumsy exam technique; it is using the stool-and-slit-lamp setup as a cover so a forbidden sexual object can be taken without naming the wish. Object relations here is crude: the patient is split into a pair of knees-plus-crotch, not a person who can refuse, so the doctor never has to hold both “healer” and “predator” in one mind.

2011-236.sentence: Sedative-hypnotic (and alcohol) withdrawal can kill with seizures and delirium; cocaine, opioids, PCP, and MDMA withdrawal are miserable, not typically lethal that way. The moral trap is a harsh conscience that treats “just stop” as virtue while ignoring GABA downregulation—guilt about using is not a substitute for a taper.

2011-237.sentence: Contemplation is “it may be a problem… I’ll think about it”: he can see the alcohol and still not choose. You are being recruited as either the scolding wife or the enabler who lets him off the hook; stay the third person who names ambivalence without becoming either.

2011-238.sentence: Kant’s gift is the ethical frame: treat the person as an end, never only a means—hence capacity, reasons, and refusal even when the team wants the pill. Dissociation would be treating the refusing patient as a body that left the room while the “good patient” stays in the chair; Kant keeps the whole person in the consult.

2011-239.sentence: Rogers v. Commissioner: after incompetence, you still cannot force antipsychotics in a non-emergency unless a court-approved substituted-judgment plan says what that patient would have wanted. Ego strength here is yours: tolerate the wait and the paperwork instead of impulsively medicating because the ward is loud.

2011-240.sentence: Oxcarbazepine induces CYP3A4 and can drop combined oral contraceptive levels; bupropion, lithium, lorazepam, and fluoxetine do not do that job. The collision is a wish to treat mood versus a wish not to risk pregnancy—name the interaction out loud so the conflict does not get enacted as a surprise pregnancy.

2011-241.sentence: HIV-associated dementia lives in unrepresented tissue: white-matter rarefaction, microglial nodules, and multinucleated giant cells do the remembering the cortex cannot. The memory complaint is not a forgotten scene; it is the virus repeating itself as apathy, gait, and a mind that will not hold a thought.

2011-242.sentence: Déjà vu is a paramnesia: the mind evacuates a nameless surge of familiarity into a false “I have been here,” then has to contain it as a known illusion. Help the patient name that mismatch—felt certainty versus intact insight—so the oddness becomes thinkable instead of a spooky discharge.

2011-243.sentence: A clouded sensorium is not a personality flaw; it is the self’s organizing function failing, so attention and orientation no longer hold you together. Before you mirror “voices” as psychosis, restore that competence: a mind that cannot stay awake is medical until proven otherwise.

2011-244.sentence: DBT’s telephone consultation is a developmental crutch: a brief coach in the gap where a reliable inner parent never quite arrived. The call is not extra therapy; it is practice holding the urge until distress-tolerance can live inside the patient.

2011-245.sentence: The spiritual language in AA can function as a container for craving, but the outcome data do not make a spiritual awakening the engine of abstinence. Treat “higher power” as one possible meaning of the ritual, not as the required mechanism—and do not force a religious story on someone who needs a different one.

2011-246.sentence: Bupropion can light up an amphetamine immunoassay, and the screen will recruit you into the role of cop if you treat the strip as confession. Feel that pull toward accusation, then stay the clinician: confirm meds and timing before you write a story about secret stimulants.

2011-247.sentence: Hopelessness is not just a mood score; it is a collapsed conscience that has already sentenced the future as unforgivable. A remote overdose still matters because the old verdict—"I do not deserve to go on"—can sit quiet for years and still be the rule the patient lives by.

2011-248.sentence: The EMG pattern (tibialis anterior and posterior, spared conduction) localizes a damaged L5 root; the rest of the limb is still working. Do not dump the whole catastrophe into "back pain" or "neuropathy." Keep the bad part named and limited so repair of the root, not a smear of dread across the whole body, can happen.

2011-249.sentence: The feared object is a specific stretch of steep road, not a bad self or a persecuting other. That is why this stays a specific phobia: good and bad are not split across relationships; they are parked on one concrete situation the patient can route around.

2011-250.sentence: Mirtazapine blocks presynaptic alpha-2-adrenergic receptors so more norepinephrine and serotonin can come through, and the H1 block often turns sleepless, nauseated nights into something thinkable. Until then the body just evacuates the state as insomnia and no appetite; the drug is a chemical container, not a personality change.

2011-251.sentence: Pheochromocytoma's catecholamine bursts feel like panic, but they are a clock you cannot interpret away. Do not rush a psychological ending on a tumor; the "attacks" stop when the source is removed, not when insight is complete.

2011-252.sentence: The wish is to protect a colleague (and oneself) by promising silence; the prohibition is the duty not to leave patients with an impaired physician. A PHP's floor is structured monitoring—not confidentiality from the board or free treatment—because the conflict gets managed in a program, not in a private pact.

2011-253.sentence: An advance directive lets a still-capable self choose a surrogate before mania steals judgment, which is a bid for mirroring: you treat the well patient as a competent author, not a future ward. Guardianship, conservatorship, a guardian ad litem, and a representative payee are court or money substitutes that arrive after capacity is gone, so they cannot hold that self-esteem.

2011-254.sentence: The 1994–2004 data put completed suicide highest in Caucasian American men in their 60s, so the pill after bereavement can feel like feed, poison, or proof that he is allowed to need care. Watch how he uses the antidepressant, the alcohol, and the new firearm as objects that either restore or annihilate that need.

2011-255.sentence: Calling for a CT or MRI first can be denial: treating temporal arteritis as if it were a brain mass so you do not have to act on the ESR of 96 and the threatened eye. The indicated move is temporal-artery biopsy (and steroids now), not lumbar puncture or EEG, because delay is how the defense costs vision.

2011-256.sentence: Pretend play hinges on using one object to represent another, so a trial comment can land: “The block is Grandma’s phone.” If the child can play with that idea, you are seeing the start of psychological mindedness, not just language, peer cooperation, or following rules.

2011-257.sentence: The five-week fluoxetine washout before phenelzine is the frame: you hold the clock so serotonin syndrome does not become the treatment. That limit is ethics in action, not fussiness; one week or three weeks is too short because fluoxetine’s long half-life still occupies the synapse.

2011-258.sentence: Family psychoeducational therapy cuts schizophrenia relapse by working Erikson’s intimacy-versus-isolation task: the household learns expressed emotion and early warning signs instead of abandoning or engulfing the patient. Exposure, IPT, DBT, and TFP do not carry that same relapse data for this illness.

2011-259.sentence: Disruptive behavior is the ticket that gets the child into the room, not the diagnosis. The outburst can be doing work for the child—protest, rescue-seeking, or a way to make an unbearable classroom feeling land on someone else—so you still have to ask what the fighting is accomplishing before you treat the referral label.

2011-260.sentence: General paresis of the insane was syphilis of the brain: Treponema pallidum turning wish, fear, and reality-testing into psychosis and a staggering gait. Fever therapy with malaria was a desperate collision of the drive to cure with a prohibition against doing nothing while 20 percent of asylums filled with a treatable infection.

2011-261.sentence: A sponsor is not a pamphlet; it is a living other who can hold what the alcoholic cannot yet put into words. Unrepresented craving and shame get repeated in the body as the next drink unless they are spoken into a relationship that can stay when the story is ugly.

2011-262.sentence: Lithium is the one to hold before ECT because it can worsen postictal confusion and prolong seizures—you are not being recruited as the withholding parent, you are protecting the brain during a seizure. Notice the countertransference pull to keep every mood stabilizer going so you do not feel like you abandoned a bipolar patient; the team still stops lithium.

2011-263.sentence: Hypocretin (orexin) from the lateral hypothalamus is the wake-keeper; when those cells die, sleep and REM crash the gate without permission. That is a biological gap in regulation, not a guilty conscience falling asleep on duty—do not moralize cataplexy as weakness.

2011-264.sentence: A prolactin of 354 ng/ml on olanzapine is not “just the med” until pregnancy is off the table. Insight here is practical: can she and you see that the first move is a pregnancy test, not an MRI of a pituitary you have not ruled out another life for.

2011-265.sentence: Postpartum psychosis does not wait for insight to ripen. The hard limit is the infant’s life: infanticide can arrive before the mother can think, so the job is hold and protect, not wait for her to “settle.”

2011-266.sentence: In women the path from first drink to alcohol dependence is telescoped—the window for thinking shrinks. Alcohol then evacuates what cannot be contained: raw dread gets dumped into the body instead of named.

2011-267.sentence: Mirtazapine’s H1 histamine blockade restores sleep and appetite when self-esteem is too thin to tolerate activating side effects. That is concrete mirroring: the drug meets a depleted self with food and rest before you ask for more grit.

2011-268.sentence: Supportive therapy gratifies dependency on purpose: you do some of the holding so the patient need not pretend they can. Watch the enactment—the two of you living “I cannot function unless you do it”—and name that rather than only filling out more forms.

2011-269.sentence: Binge eating disorder usually does not keep a normal weight because nothing cancels the intake. Bulimia’s typical defense is undoing—vomit, restrict, exercise—to erase the binge; without that ritual, the body records what the mind will not metabolize.

2011-270.sentence: Small, short-duration motor units on needle EMG mean the remaining muscle fibers cannot sustain a full contraction. The symptom’s meaning is myopathic dropout, not a bad nerve: conduction stays normal while the muscle itself fails.

2011-271.sentence: A child who passes the false-belief marble task can hold two minds at once: what they know and what the other doll still believes. That capacity is your green light for more uncovering work; if the patient cannot yet imagine a mind that is wrong, stay supportive and name states rather than interpret hidden motives.

2011-272.sentence: Until she can feel that the boyfriend-as-attacker is outside the room, every other person—including you—can still fuse with the persecutory object, the dangerous other she expects to hurt her. Safety first splits “then” from “now” so a good-enough helper can exist beside the bad one instead of collapsing into him.

2011-273.sentence: rTMS is aimed at prefrontal cortex because that is the late, planning surface that depression has taken offline. You are not chasing mood in the thalamus or motor strip; you are asking the thinking-ahead cortex to come back on duty so affect does not run the whole show.

2011-274.sentence: Nortriptyline is one of the few antidepressants whose blood level actually maps onto both efficacy and toxicity, so the number is part of the treatment frame. Checking it before you raise the dose keeps you from treating your hope, her report, or a class stereotype as if they were the drug.

2011-275.sentence: Carbohydrate-deficient transferrin is the lab that best tracks heavy drinking when the story of abstinence and the work identity are still at odds. Erikson’s task here is integrity of the self-account: CDT is a quiet third witness so shame does not have to be the only auditor.

2011-276.sentence: A self-help group keeps the shared problem—the drink, the illness—as the task and does not treat the group itself as the patient. That is the point of the symptom there: it organizes belonging and practical hope, not exploration of who is angry at whom in the room.

2011-277.sentence: Risperidone’s evidence for youth explosiveness is the field finally catching up to a developmental truth: reactive rage is often a late or missing brake, not a fully formed “choice.” You are treating a capacity that never quite arrived—frustration tolerance and delay—so the pill is scaffolding a mind that still cannot hold the surge long enough to think.

2011-278.sentence: Buspirone’s 5-HT1A action is a slow, non-punitive anxiolytic: it does not knock the patient out or hand them a forbidden bottle. For a conscience that already treats benzos as a moral failure, that receptor story can be the sanctioned gap—relief without the guilt of “getting high.”

2011-279.sentence: Antisocial personality recruits the group into prey and predator: you will feel used, and the other members will feel unsafe. That is the transference you are refusing to host—an outpatient process group cannot survive becoming the crime scene.

2011-280.sentence: Unaware tongue retraction and lateral movements on long-term thioridazine is tardive dyskinesia announcing itself; this is not a mind that needs more uncovering. The technique is conservative: taper thioridazine and start low-dose risperidone—support the body first, because insight into involuntary movements will not reverse them.

2011-281.sentence: The pair is the point: sublingual buprenorphine works, and naloxone barely absorbs there, so the two of you can keep the intended agonist effect only if the film is used as prescribed. Crush it and inject it and the unused partner—naloxone—suddenly shows up and ruins the high; the formulation encodes a relationship of trust versus misuse, not a one-person pharmacology story.

2011-282.sentence: Familial hypokalemic periodic paralysis after a military test dumps potassium and strength together; the cadet’s mind is not attacking the body in Klein’s sense. What looks like collapse is channelopathy, not projective identification—name the potassium of 2.8 so you do not treat a medical nucleus as a split-off bad object.

2011-283.sentence: Holding the same antidepressant dose after remission is like keeping a reliable good object present instead of splitting it into a “needed when sick” half and a “disposable when well” half. Cutting the dose the moment they feel better treats the medicine as a bad, contaminating object they must eject, and the relationship to treatment then fragments the way the mood history already did.

2011-284.sentence: Boundary crossings sit in Erikson’s intimacy versus isolation: the task is a live, situation-specific judgment about closeness, not a rigid rule that pretends intimacy is either always safe or always forbidden. Treating every gift or extra minute as automatically exploitive skips that assessment and leaves the pair isolated behind a wall of policy.

2011-285.sentence: Hypokalemia after purging is not only a lab; it is the body carrying a cultural third about thinness, control, and which appetites a young woman is allowed to keep. Ask about vomiting and diuretics as identity work in the room, not as a private vice you pretend not to notice.

2011-286.sentence: Idiopathic Bell palsy is a peripheral seventh-nerve hit that takes forehead and lower face together; the developmental analogue is a capacity that never quite arrived as a clean split between “central spare-the-forehead” and “peripheral whole-face.” Do not call it brainstem stroke or zoster unless the exam and vesicles say those later-arriving differentiations actually showed up.

2011-287.sentence: Reframing turns “lazy” and “controlling” into a family trying to negotiate independence, which is what the fight was doing for them all along. The symptom was a crude job description; positive language lets the same work happen without the insult.

2011-288.sentence: When the toddler makes the teddy bear alive, you are being recruited as the adult who either joins the play or kills it with a lecture. Animism is the child’s transference onto the stuffed animal; your countertransference is the urge to correct it instead of using it.

2011-289.sentence: Warfarin can feel like the more conscientious move after a stroke, as if antiplatelets were a moral shortcut. For a lacunar infarct with a normal echo, a normal EKG, and only mild carotid narrowing, aspirin plus dipyridamole is the prevention that matches the vessel, not the guilt.

2011-290.sentence: Creatinine clearance falls in ordinary aging even when the person still looks sturdy. Dose as if the kidney were still a young secure base and a renally cleared drug will pile up while you keep waiting for a “real” creatinine crisis.

2011-291.sentence: Handing the neighbor a treatment plan makes the two of you a clinical pair, even at a party. Advising cognitive-behavioral therapy with named providers is that step; a card, a resource list, or a general remark about the economy is not.

2011-292.sentence: Psychomotor attacks can look like the mind leaving the body, but this is not a split in consciousness. A TSC-1 mutation ties the seizures and the school trouble to the same skin lesion of tuberous sclerosis.

2011-293.sentence: Housebound depression can look like ego collapse until the body writes the diagnosis on the skin. Hyperpigmentation, weight loss, and cold intolerance point to Addison disease: lost cortisol, not lost will.

2011-294.sentence: Avoidance is the defense in play: he will not talk about the crash so the horror stays out of the room, while the dreams and the “spirit leaving the body” still leak through. At three weeks that cluster is acute stress, not PTSD.

2011-295.sentence: Karyotyping is you and the lab looking at chromosomal structure itself, not mapping cDNA or cloning some cytoplasmic fantasy. The enactment is treating the genome as a smear on a slide: the work is to see the actual chromosomes, not to keep hybridizing metaphors while the karyotype sits unread.

2011-296.sentence: Wearing-off is a clock problem: levodopa’s usable time ends before the next dose, and a COMT inhibitor (catechol-O-methyltransferase) holds that interval by slowing levodopa’s peripheral breakdown. You are not regenerating dopaminergic neurons or bargaining away dyskinesia; you are keeping the dosing frame honest so the patient is not abandoned in an off-period.

2011-297.sentence: Methadone at 60–100 mg is the dose range that actually feeds the mu-opioid system enough to cut illicit use; 5–40 mg is a starvation ration dressed up as treatment. If morning withdrawal and craving keep winning, the pill is still a tease, not a holding environment.

2011-298.sentence: A no-show fee is ethical only after you have named the limit out loud, in advance—the APA annotation is notice, not insurance permission or a secret penalty. Ending an hour the patient never used is still an ending; surprise billing turns the limit into a slap.

2011-299.sentence: A 17-year-old who looks “argumentative” with an open mouth, dysarthria, rigidity, tremor, and high transaminases cannot use a trial comment about attitude until you have checked urinary copper excretion for Wilson disease. Insight work on personality change is the wrong instrument when copper is chewing the basal ganglia and the liver.

2011-300.sentence: Conjoint marital therapy is the wrong first technique in active domestic violence: it asks the couple to uncover the fight in the same room where coercion already lives. Start with individual work, meds if needed, and group only if it is safe; joint sessions can worsen the prognosis by putting the victim back under the partner’s gaze.

2012-1.sentence: Transference is the old feeling landing on you; ego strength is whether she can feel the abandonment terror after one reschedule and still test it against the actual frame. Explore the conviction instead of rushing to soothe it, so impulse and affect get a chance to stay thinkable.

2012-2.sentence: Gage’s frontal injury tore the circuitry that lets a person use another mind as a secure base instead of dumping impulse into the room. After frontal TBI, proximity-seeking turns reckless—purchases, boundary breaks—because the patient can no longer hold you in mind as a brake.

2012-3.sentence: Cluster headache is a 45-minute ipsilateral storm (tearing, rhinorrhea, pacing at 3 a.m.), and the household often becomes a second clock: someone stays up, fetches oxygen, absorbs the panic. Name the autonomic attack so the pair can stop treating each night as a shared emergency ritual.

2012-4.sentence: Meds in autism can blunt aggressiveness; they will not restore gaze, prosody, or pragmatics, so do not treat the core social deficit as something to uncover. Support first: map transitions, pain, sleep, and communication load before you reach for interpretation or a pill.

2012-5.sentence: Advising sits at the supportive pole: you temporarily loan a organizing other when grief has split the good object from the day’s tasks. Hold off interpreting dependency until sleep and meals are back; the relationship needs a usable good object before it can metabolize mixed feelings.

2012-6.sentence: Calling thunderclap pain plus vomiting “panic” is a hole in the work’s conscience: subarachnoid hemorrhage is the diagnosis the scan is asking you to own. Anxiety can be real and still be the alarm, not the disease.

2012-7.sentence: After sertraline 200 mg, duloxetine 90 mg, and phenelzine 90 mg have failed, the will-updating is recruiting you into shared hopelessness: you become the doctor who agrees nothing works. Feel that pull, then still offer ECT—the modality with the highest chance of remission—instead of matching the despair with another pill trial.

2012-8.sentence: Do not promise a colleague more privacy than a state physician health program and the medical board can actually keep. That monitoring frame is what stops the addiction from being enacted as a two-doctor secret instead of a named, followed recovery.

2012-9.sentence: “Doctor, you believe this is happening” is a wish that you join the assassin-and-rape scene; the prohibition is that you must not certify it as fact. “It sounds terrifying” stays with the affect and refuses both the collusion and the cold rebuttal.

2012-10.sentence: Depression and alcohol dependence are already acting together on suicide; a t-test pretends only one predictor is in the room. Regression analysis is the method that keeps both independent variables in the model instead of collapsing a two-factor problem into a one-variable duel.

2012-11.sentence: Spasticity is the stretch reflex with the brake cut: glycine and GABA drop in quantity, uptake, and turnover. Lost inhibition is failed suppression of motor discharge the cord can no longer hold back.

2012-12.sentence: Oculogyric crisis after haloperidol 5 mg bid can make the body feel stolen—“can’t see,” stuck looking up—and that terror is not a reason to raise the antipsychotic. Give benztropine 1 mg IV now so the patient can re-own the body; oral diphenhydramine or more haloperidol asks for more affect tolerance than this moment has.

2012-13.sentence: Childhood abuse can split panic off from memory: the body floods with dying-fear while the mind never names what happened. Panic disorder is that split in action—palpitations and escape without a story attached.

2012-14.sentence: Adolescence is when a trial comment can land: “You failed the cut, not the self.” Insight here means they can see their own harsh standard and still keep a goal that is sized to a real body.

2012-15.sentence: The old one-year opioid-dependence rule is a clock you cannot charm: maintenance methadone waits for a history that is long enough, not a wish that is loud enough. Ending chaos on day thirty does not rewrite that limit.

2012-16.sentence: Offering an antidepressant for “depression-related low energy” can feel like feed—proof someone finally believes the patient is sick. Inclusion body myositis (quadriceps, finger flexors, normal CK) is not a mood; the pill cannot lift a thigh that the muscle has already lost.

2012-17.sentence: Prazosin for combat nightmares is a frame decision: you treat the night so the day can hold, not so the veteran can keep the horror as a private duty. Holding that limit means you do not leave the alpha-1 blockade to “just talk it out.”

2012-18.sentence: IPT’s sick role is a cultural third: depression gets named as illness so class-and-duty talk (“I should snap out of it”) stops running the hour. Permission to recover is not laziness; it is a temporary identity that makes getting well the job.

2012-19.sentence: Contamination is the common OCD pattern because dirt is the mind’s stand-in for a bad object that must be kept out of the self. Hours of showering and avoiding the grandchildren are Kleinian projective identification in soap-and-water form: the feared mess is put into the world, then washed so the person can feel clean enough to stay related.

2012-20.sentence: Fludrocortisone is not just salt retention; it is a concrete feed that keeps blood volume up so standing does not empty the body. When Parkinson drugs already feel like a demand or a poison, this mineralocorticoid can land as proof someone is still willing to hold the patient upright instead of chasing more levodopa.

2012-21.sentence: Suppression is the ego’s deliberate pause: you keep the family fight in awareness and park it until after conference. That is not repression (the conflict is not banished from mind) and not denial (you already know it hurts); it is a conscious, time-limited diversion so thinking can stay online.

2012-22.sentence: “Best interests of the child” is the legal frame, but the consult is already an enactment: two adults are fighting through you instead of holding the child’s anxiety. Your job is to stop living their custody war and name the child’s needs so the court hears functioning, safety, and care, not the parents’ old script.

2012-23.sentence: Prolactin stays quiet only while tuberoinfundibular dopamine keeps a tonic brake on the lactotrophs; D2 blockade lifts that brake and amenorrhea arrives. The body then dissociates desire from the rest of the person—libido drops while the patient sits in the chair, as if sexuality left without anyone standing up.

2012-24.sentence: Frequent small sips of water ask the ego to tolerate dying without heroic tubes: comfort, not TPN or IV hydration, matches failing reality testing around “starvation.” Family panic is the impulse to reverse cachexia; your ego strength is holding that affect so the 91-year-old is moistened, not medicalized.

2012-25.sentence: She used the family and the phone call as a secure base—another person to down-regulate after the imipramine overdose—and the medical resident is now offering a second, false secure base: “750 ng/mL combined imipramine–desipramine is not cardiotoxic, so ship her.” You hold proximity by insisting on the EKG and continued ED or ICU monitoring; that is the adult who stays in the room until the heart, not the story, is actually safe.

2012-26.sentence: You and the intern can quietly agree that a young stroke “doesn’t fit,” and that shared shrug is the interpersonal pattern: two people making the case less medical so neither has to name meningovascular syphilis. Acute neurosyphilis most often shows up as stroke; the work is to keep that fact in the room with the other clinician instead of splitting neurology off as someone else’s problem.

2012-27.sentence: These parents can use a trial of ordinary curiosity more than they can use uncovering for trauma, a Denver screen, or a lecture on paternal ADHD and ODD. Start by exploring what the tantrums mean to them; if the mind in front of you is the parents’ anxiety, support and clarification beat premature technique.

2012-28.sentence: The ED can recruit you as the person who “knows these alcohol patients,” and your countertransference—irritation, fatalism, the wish to move on—is the cue that you are being invited to become the neglectful other. High-dose vitamin B1 (thiamine) is what prevents Wernicke’s confusion, ataxia, nystagmus, and ophthalmoplegia; give that fact before you give the feeling a story.

2012-29.sentence: In autism, a lot of distress never becomes a memory or a sentence; it is repeated as the same action until the environment answers the same way. Behaviorism is that answer: one consistent consequence for one target behavior, so the foster home becomes a predictable other when words cannot hold the state.

2012-30.sentence: Notice the pull to become wiser than the chart—the opposing lawyer’s “you will not be asked for an independent legal opinion” is a compliment that tests whether you can see your own part. You are a fact witness: what you observed and treated, not an expert on the work claim; if you cannot use that limit as a trial comment to yourself, you will start testifying as if you were hired to win.

2012-31.sentence: Around age three, a child can put a birthday or a fall into words after it is over—so time is no longer only now. That new capacity cannot be rushed: until language can hold a past event, you cannot treat the child as if they already have a narrative you can simply interview.

2012-32.sentence: Pyridoxine (B6) in famine or megadose both chew the same nerves, so the body cannot tell starve from flood. Hold that paradox as Bion’s container would: turn nameless burning feet into a thinkable fact instead of evacuating it as “just another vitamin story.”

2012-33.sentence: Contemplation is the smoker’s bid for a mirror that says the knowing self is real, without demanding a quit date that would collapse self-esteem. If you rush them into preparation, you withdraw the idealizable helper and they defend the pack as the last thing they still control.

2012-34.sentence: Neurasthenia’s fatigue, worry, and somatoform complaints often land as an anxiety disorder in U.S. coding—and the room may already be enacting that: you hunt for a lesion while they offer a body. Name the two-person loop or you will treat the category instead of the fear that keeps arriving as exhaustion.

2012-35.sentence: DBT starts with mindfulness because without noticing the urge, the usual defense is acting out—doing the cut instead of knowing the feeling. Practice observing first so suppression and crisis skills have a mind to land in, not just another behavior to stack.

2012-36.sentence: A posterior cerebral artery infarct can leave midline-reaching hemisensory loss, then thalamic pain that light touch turns into fire. The analgesic you offer is not only chemistry: it can feel like proof you believe the pain, or like a demand that they stop asking the body to speak.

2012-37.sentence: Hold the alcohol clock as the treatment frame: accusatory voices after a week off heavy drinking do not authorize a lifetime schizophrenia or schizoaffective chart. Citalopram, sertraline, and quetiapine nonadherence plus medical clearance still do not make this delirium tremens or MDD with psychosis; you protect her from a chronic-psychosis identity until the substance-induced window is honestly closed.

2012-38.sentence: Once hospital discipline lasts more than 30 days, the hospital—not the doctor—must report the adverse professional-review action to the National Practitioner Data Bank. That filing is the professional limit: hallway coaching stays inside the staff office; a formal privilege restriction does not.

2012-39.sentence: The suicide threat is doing work: it makes the parents drop the demand, not express a plan to die. Sending her home names that meaning, so you treat coercive rage in a euthymic, logical child instead of using the ED or a locked unit as the parents’ new giving-in.

2012-40.sentence: At home the parents may be caught in projective identification—they feel the “bad, suicidal girl” has been put into them and they surrender. A teacher report is the third mind that checks whether that all-bad object is only a family creation or whether the same split lives at school.

2012-41.sentence: Do not crown the “better” parent or let the child pick a referee; that makes you the extra adult who splits the couple. Explore why they cannot share one limit, because the outburst is living in the gap between two disciplines.

2012-42.sentence: This child does not need insight, mindfulness, or a lecture on how maladaptive she has been. She needs supportive technique: parents ignore the scream, keep the rule, and stop the negative reinforcement that used to cancel the demand.

2012-43.sentence: After a spouse dies, the surviving partner’s inner couple—good memories held with the pain—needs a living other who can take the spillover. Quality social support is that third object: someone who can hold both the beloved and the rage at being left, so the widow does not have to split the marriage into all-saint or all-void.

2012-44.sentence: Amphetamines dump catecholamines into the synapse; the rush is a chemical stand-in for a caregiver who suddenly arrives. That flood can feel like a secure base in a bottle—until the crash, when the attachment system protests the same way a child does when the parent walks out.

2012-45.sentence: Dissociative amnesia hits episodic memory: the lived scenes of “what happened to me with you,” not how to ride a bike or what a chair is called. Two people often keep that gap in place together—the patient cannot recall, and the other quietly agrees not to ask, so the relationship never has to hold the scene.

2012-46.sentence: Manganese chews the globus pallidus and striatum, the circuits that start and stop movement, and the person can look parkinsonian while still sitting in the chair. Dissociation is the psychic twin of that lesion: a vertical split, motor and feeling go offline without the self leaving the room.

2012-47.sentence: The MMPI-2 is the inventory that has actually been checked in adolescents, elders, and ethnic-minority groups, so it can carry the ego’s report across those frames. Ego strength here is not “insight”; it is whether the person can sit with a long, structured test without the answers collapsing into culture-bound noise.

2012-48.sentence: Start with sex education: menopause, desire, and aging bodies are facts, and naming them undercuts the wife’s quiet denial that she is still a sexual person. Her offer that he find a younger woman is reaction formation dressed as generosity—she turns shame about not feeling sexy into a “kind” push-away.

2012-49.sentence: The pair is already in a fight about whether the TCA is a tool or a poison: the patient lists dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, and urinary retention, and the doctor still wants a tricyclic. Naming desipramine as the first choice is how you stop that enactment—the two-person replay of force versus refusal—because this secondary amine is the least anticholinergic of the list, so you are treating the depression without making the body prove the patient’s fear.

2012-50.sentence: Alexia without agraphia after a cortical PCA infarct is a hard limit on insight: the patient can write a sentence and still cannot read it, because the right homonymous field and the splenium disconnect vision from language. A trial comment has to honor that split—ask them to write, then show them their own words—so you are testing whether they can use what they produced, not whether they will admit a deficit.

2012-51.sentence: The transplant is over and the hospital is ending; the anxiety is about leaving a frame that held him through bone marrow transplantation, not a new personality or a full major depression. Adjustment disorder with anxiety names that limit: sleep and discharge fear after an uneventful BMT are a mind catching up to a finish line you cannot rush.

2012-52.sentence: When a depressed patient treats CBT like the only real pill, the therapy brand becomes feed, proof of being a good patient, or a demand you must swallow. Meta-analyses that other psychotherapies match CBT let you offer a relationship that works, not a single patented capsule.

2012-53.sentence: The ethical frame here is whose definition of a healthy self you enforce in the room: Western esteem built on inner attributes and self-defined goals, or non-Western esteem built on contribution to the group and harmony. If you treat caregiving and not burdening relatives as only guilt or dependence, you have already broken the frame by scoring their culture as pathology.

2012-54.sentence: Psych was called for anxiety while the legs go weak and the reflexes disappear; that consult is already an enactment—the system repeating “this is nerves” while nerve conduction velocities slow. Acute polyneuropathy (think Guillain-Barré physiology) is the medical fact you name so you do not live out somatization with the team instead of sending the patient to neurology.

2012-55.sentence: Fluvoxamine’s short half-life makes missed pills a body event within a day or two—dizziness, irritability, zaps—so “I’ll catch up later” is denial: the mind treats the absence as harmless while the receptor occupancy is already gone. Fluoxetine would have forgiven the same lapse; this molecule does not.

2012-56.sentence: Exposure and response prevention is an ego-strength drill: the patient touches the contaminant and then holds the urge to wash long enough for anxiety to crest and fall. You are building affect tolerance and impulse control, not arguing the germs away.

2012-57.sentence: By about 48 hours after the last drink the alcohol-soaked calm has left the chair even though the patient is still sitting in it—a vertical split between a present body and a CNS that has lost its sedative. That is when the unthinkable arousal (tremor, autonomic storm, seizure risk) peaks, so you time the watch to the last drink, not to how “with it” they look.

2012-58.sentence: Clozapine is the only atypical that consistently beats typicals in psychosis, and it only works as a two-person treatment: weekly blood, agranulocytosis talk, the clinic that keeps showing up. The superior efficacy is not a solo receptor story; it is a relationship that can hold the labs and the risk together.

2012-59.sentence: “What do you think will happen if you don’t undertake this treatment?” asks whether the patient can still use you as a secure base—someone to think danger with—rather than only name the date or the doctor. Competence here is proximity-plus-thought: can they stay close enough to the relationship to picture the consequence of walking away.

2012-60.sentence: A corrective emotional experience is Bion’s container in ordinary clothes: you take in the expected scolding, metabolize it, and hand back acceptance plus a limit the old parent never offered. The patient then has a thinkable feeling instead of nameless dread that they will be attacked for every mistake.

2012-61.sentence: The ulnar nerve at the elbow is a limit you cannot talk past: numbness in the fourth and fifth digits that wakes the patient is anatomy, not a feeling you interpret first. Slowed conduction velocity across the elbow names the bottleneck; if you skip that mapping, you treat a capacity that will not recover on insight alone.

2012-62.sentence: Phenelzine plus an over-the-counter cold remedy that spiked the pressure to 210/118 is not a moment for a trial comment about “what this headache means.” Insight here is seeing the patient’s part in the mix-up, then choosing nifedipine and medical backup instead of lorazepam or a migraine drug that would miss the crisis.

2012-63.sentence: Activity monitoring is a frame: you hold the hour-by-hour log and the mastery/pleasure ratings so “I do nothing” can be checked against the day, not argued. The psychiatrist sets that task the way one sets a fee or a session time—the limit is the record, not a pep talk.

2012-64.sentence: Periodic limb movement disorder recruits you as the night witness: brief, stereotypic, nonepileptiform toe-extension jerks in non-REM sleep that the patient may never feel. Countertransference is the pull to treat restless legs or “anxiety in the legs” when the finding is the movement itself, not a wish you are being asked to soothe.

2012-65.sentence: After a recent attempt, what cannot yet be narrated as a full story often returns as the next act; suicide-focused CBT is the treatment shown to cut later attempts in depressed adults. You walk the circumstances and the thoughts in words so the body does not have to repeat the unrepresented state.

2012-66.sentence: Six weeks after a parent’s sudden death, pangs of grief are the wish to find the parent colliding with the fact of loss; that conflict is ordinary bereavement. Persistent avoidance of death reminders marks traumatic grief—the mind refusing the collision rather than letting the wish and the prohibition meet.

2012-67.sentence: Ordering a fasting lipid panel before the first atypical antipsychotic treats the patient's bodily self as worth protecting, not as a metabolic afterthought. Safety here is a competence move: you are saying their heart and pancreas matter as much as their psychosis.

2012-68.sentence: Cocaine can infarct the anterior spinal artery while the posterior columns stay online, so pain and temperature drop out and vibration stays. Ego strength here is reality testing: treat the incontinence and mid-thoracic sensory level as cord, not as a panic story about a clumsy leg.

2012-69.sentence: Sexual side effects on citalopram can feel like the pill stole a piece of closeness, so the patient starts to pull away from you and the treatment. Offering bupropion is a secure-base move: you stay with the depression work without asking them to sacrifice desire.

2012-70.sentence: The therapeutic alliance is not a nicety; it is what the treatment is doing for the person—making it safe enough to stay. Technique and transference interpretations only work if that bond is already carrying the load.

2012-71.sentence: Regular scheduled visits with the primary doctor answer the trust-versus-mistrust question: someone will be there even when the workup is empty. That appointment is the treatment for somatoform illness, not a courtesy before the next scan.

2012-72.sentence: A young woman with post-flu exhaustion and a day-long crash after housework is easy to recode as depression or personality, and that gendered dismissal is the third person in the room. Name chronic fatigue syndrome so her energy economy is not treated as a character flaw.

2012-73.sentence: REM sleep behavior disorder is the night version of evacuation: the dream is not held inside as a thought, so punching and shouting dump the nightmare into the bedroom. Clonazepam does the containing work the motor system failed at—it keeps the dream from being projected onto the mattress and the partner.

2012-74.sentence: Carbamazepine first looks like a reliable good object—mania quiets and drowsiness proves it is actually in the body—then, around week four, autoinduction of the epoxide pathway makes the liver chew the drug faster and the mania returns. The split is pharmacokinetic, not moral: the same relationship that helped is now metabolizing itself away, so you raise the dose or change the object rather than accusing the patient of leaving.

2012-75.sentence: DSM-III’s explicit criteria and five axes were a technical decision about how much uncovering a field could safely do: operational lists support reliable talk when deep formulation would scatter. Use that same gauge with a patient—if the mind needs a shared checklist more than a rich story, stay at the DSM-III level of work and do not force interpretation it cannot use.

2012-76.sentence: GHB is a two-person toxin: friends bring a relaxed, talkative companion who then becomes drowsy, nauseated, and labile, and you are now the other person who must hold the airway they cannot. The interpersonal pattern is literal—the drug that made the night feel close can drop respiratory drive, so your job is not to interpret the high but to stay with the body until consciousness stops swinging.

2012-77.sentence: Among youth antidepressants, fluoxetine has the best risk-benefit ratio in pooled trials, which in attachment language means it is the most usable secure base: close enough to help, less likely to worsen the very danger you are trying to regulate. Pair it with a real person—psychotherapy, parents, a clinic that answers—because a pill cannot protest separation or hold the adolescent when mood drops.

2012-78.sentence: Piaget mapped how a child learns about and understands the world, and the stages are a limit you cannot terminate early: concrete operations will not become formal thought because you wish the consult over. Meet the seven-year-old at the level the mind actually has, then stop pushing abstraction the way a good ending stops when the hour—and the capacity—are done.

2012-79.sentence: Window-banging is evacuation: the anxiety about meds is dumped into the nurses as nameless dread instead of being held long enough to become a thought. The request card is containment in Bion’s sense—an incompatible, reinforced act that turns the raw feeling into something you can wait with and name.

2012-80.sentence: Dextromethorphan is not a party trick; it is a chemical shortcut to dissociation, the mind’s way of leaving the body when feeling is too much. The ED visit is the morning after that split—confusion and ataxia as the price of a self that briefly refused to stay put.

2012-81.sentence: Severe mania is identity flooding: grandiosity and sleeplessness dissolve the ordinary “who I am” that Erikson’s identity task is supposed to hold. Combined antipsychotic plus lithium or valproate is the fastest way to restore a self that can do that work again.

2012-82.sentence: In hypochondriasis the feared disease is a bad object parked in the body; the doctor’s clean workup cannot be taken in as a good object. Keep one consistent relationship so good and bad findings can live in the same room instead of each visit becoming a hunt for the hidden killer.

2012-83.sentence: Calling this conversion would be a Kleinian dodge: dumping the pain into “all in the mind” instead of owning a real CN IX lesion. Glossopharyngeal neuralgia asks for the depressive position—repair, not projection—because the lancinating tongue–pharynx–ear pain with swallow and speech triggers is the nerve, not a fantasy.

2012-84.sentence: Attraction that blurs the patient’s best interest is a superego emergency: conscience has gone offline and the wish is driving. Supervision is the first use of a borrowed conscience; telling the patient or shrinking the hour just hands them your guilt.

2012-85.sentence: Cue-triggered craving is recruiting you as bartender and accomplice: the bar, the smell, the old route all ask you to become the person who says yes. Name the nucleus accumbens as the reward hub, then say the feeling in you—urgency, rescue, or contempt—is data about the pull, not a reason to pour.

2012-86.sentence: The guilt is doing a job: it keeps the 14-year-old from treating independence as a crime against the parents he still loves. Those harsh parental introjects—inner copies of mom and dad that went quiet in latency—wake up when he pushes back, so he argues and then pays a moral tax.

2012-87.sentence: Insanity work asks whether reality testing held at the moment of the act, not whether schizophrenia is old or whether he took his pill today. "What were the voices saying?" tests if command content, not duration of illness, can show he could not know wrongness when the assault happened.

2012-88.sentence: Ideas of reference already pull you into a two-person scene: the newscaster is "talking about me," so you become either the confirming audience or the one who denies the message. Ask if the link is literal and personal; if you start arguing the news, you are living the conviction instead of examining it.

2012-89.sentence: The e2/e3 report can split the mind: one part hears "protected," another still waits for Alzheimer disease as if the gene were a verdict. Hold both: APOE e2/e3 lowers population risk with age, and no genotype tells this person whether they will leave themselves.

2012-90.sentence: After a fall and sinking consciousness, CT is the scan that can see blood now, when waiting for MRI would split the team between "watch and wait" and "this is an emergency." You keep the good object of careful psychiatry and the bad fact of possible bleed in the same plan: stabilize, then CT the 70-year-old who is going down.

2012-91.sentence: The central nucleus of the amygdala is the output hub that turns a cue into freeze, flight, and autonomic surge; uncovering “why you are afraid” is wasted if that circuit is still firing as if the hallway were a predator. Support first: name the body as alarm, not confession, then later you can look at the meaning of the cue.

2012-92.sentence: Carbohydrate-deficient transferrin (CDT) is the lab that most reliably flags recent heavy drinking; MCV and SGOT lag or wander. In the room, class and shame are often the third party: the patient may “pass” as abstinent while the marker tells a story they cannot afford to own yet.

2012-93.sentence: Family psychoeducation, not structural or paradoxical family therapy, is what PORT found cuts schizophrenia relapse. Klein would say the family is being asked to hold split-off terror and rage without dumping it back as blame—that is containment: taking in the projected mess and returning it as usable information.

2012-94.sentence: Myotonic dystrophy explains the grip that will not let go, ptosis, and early cataracts; this is not myasthenia’s fatigable weakness. Ego strength here is reality testing: the mind must accept a progressive muscle disease instead of treating slowness as laziness or “depression only.”
