2012-95.sentence: Outpatient groups for schizophrenia aim at social skills development, not diving into unconscious or delusional themes. Dissociation is the vertical split—the person leaves without leaving the chair—so you rehearse a greeting to a supervisor in the room where they can stay present.

2012-96.sentence: A pulse of 200 that settles after Valsalva (bear down) is paroxysmal atrial tachycardia, not a panic attack you two “co-created.” The relational trap is the pair agreeing the body is “just anxiety” so neither has to face a treatable arrhythmia.

2012-97.sentence: That 400 ng/ml after 50 mg of desipramine is not “she cannot tolerate starting a pill.” Her CYP450 cannot clear the drug, so the body floods with anticholinergic and adrenergic noise and she uses the phone to pull you close as a regulator. Answer the call as attachment work: you become a secure base by naming the toxicity, cutting the dose, and staying reachable while her level comes down.

2012-98.sentence: Before you treat the silence as a psychological poison or a demand for interpretation, ask whether the child can hear. Hearing is the feed that makes speech possible; if that channel is blocked, advice about novelty, empathy, or MMR meaning will miss the actual deprivation.

2012-99.sentence: Polydipsia plus mild confusion is hyponatremia until proven otherwise, and the treatment frame is the water limit you hold when the patient’s thirst will not. You keep the clock, the I’s and O’s, and the sodium—not the fantasy that more drinking will settle the mind.

2012-100.sentence: Normal scans with bilateral papilledema still leave her needing you close enough to measure opening pressure; lumbar puncture is the proximity that imaging refused. The dull daily headache is a bid for a real examination of intracranial pressure, not more distance from the bedside.

2012-101.sentence: Naltrexone and disulfiram both tax the liver, so ego strength here is whether this person can use serial enzymes and the no-drink rule without collapsing into “the medicine is attacking me.” You dose the constraint to their affect tolerance: monitor LFTs, name the shared hepatotoxicity, and do not start either drug if they cannot partner with that watch.

2012-102.sentence: A step-parent in the home is an epidemiologic risk, not a symbol to interpret first. Support and safety come before uncovering family romance: document the bruises, separate inconsistent stories, and protect the child rather than exploring what the new adult “means.”

2012-103.sentence: High-dose fluphenazine is never a one-person event: the pair often escalates the dose together until the body answers with rigidity, fever, and a rising creatine kinase. CK is how you stay in the relationship with that body instead of arguing with the mental status.

2012-104.sentence: The 3½-year-old is taking in father's penis as a whole object he can look at and name, not as a persecutory part that has to be hidden. "Why is it so fat?" is ordinary genital curiosity, not a Kleinian catastrophe that requires you to hunt for a molester.

2012-105.sentence: An ataque de nervios is the moment the family field cannot hold good and bad in one piece, so the mix dumps out as shaking, shouting, and feeling out of control. That same unheld mix is why these patients so often also meet criteria for major depression, GAD, or PTSD.

2012-106.sentence: Integrity versus despair is the late-life task, and a slower information-processing speed is the clock you have to make peace with. Language, long-term memory, and simple pattern recognition can still hold; despair starts when the person treats extra seconds as proof they are finished.

2012-107.sentence: The paranoia, hypertension, and substernal pain are one sympathomimetic story, not a new identity as a psychotic patient. A urine toxicology screen keeps the chest and the voices in the same sentence so you do not invent a first-break out of cocaine or amphetamine.

2012-108.sentence: Fidelity is the promise that someone who knows the work will still be there; vacation without coverage breaks that promise in the frame. The patient is left holding the treatment alone, which is abandonment dressed up as time off.

2012-109.sentence: Those fully formed, silent, colorful children are Lewy-body cortex filling a failing visual-attentional field; the image is doing the work of a mind that cannot hold a stable scene. Mild rigidity and fatiguing finger tap tell you the same circuit is slipping motorically, so the visions are a perceptual patch, not a late-life wish for company.

2012-110.sentence: Lithium plus ECT can leave the patient unable to think the treatment: prolonged seizures, postictal delirium, and a fog that blocks any trial comment. Holding or cutting the lithium is the psychologically minded move—protect the mind that has to notice what the seizure did, not just the mood it treats.

2012-111.sentence: Call depersonalization a disturbance of perception and you keep the frame honest: the patient is watching the self from outside, not believing a delusion that must be reported or certified. Insight stays inside the hour—“I know this is not literally happening”—so you treat panic and the body, not thought content.

2012-112.sentence: The well twin’s dread that shared genes mean shared illness is nameless until you hold it: concordance is not destiny. A two-hit model—genetic load plus an environmental second hit—turns that raw certainty into something thinkable instead of evacuating it as “I am next.”

2012-113.sentence: Transient global amnesia is a hard stop on encoding: fluent speech, intact identity, and a six-hour inability to keep the next sentence. You cannot rush a hippocampus that will not write; the day ends without a record, and the following morning the capacity simply returns.

2012-114.sentence: The frame is the prohibition—fixed time, fee, cancellation, confidentiality—set against the wish to be special, late, unpaid, or endlessly available. When those rules stay consistent, the collision shows up as material instead of becoming an extra session or a broken boundary.

2012-115.sentence: REM is already running in utero, which means a self-state exists before anyone can offer a mirror or an ideal. Caregivers later borrow that built-in activation when they delight in the infant; they do not create the first “I am here” signal.

2012-116.sentence: A rare outcome recruits you into the hero who will “prove the cause” by waiting for new cases that may never arrive. Case-control lets you stay the clinician-epidemiologist instead of the person who needs thousands of incident events to feel useful.

2012-117.sentence: On the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test the rule has already changed, but the person keeps dealing the old set. That is an unrepresented shift: the body-mind repeats the last strategy because the new contingency never became thinkable, only felt as wrongness after each card.

2012-118.sentence: The capacity to bounce back from a small slight is a developmental achievement, not a moral one. If caregivers never supplied timed, accurate empathy, that resilience never quite arrives, and ordinary feedback still lands as a collapse of the self.

2012-119.sentence: Short REM latency means dream sleep barges in before the night has done its delaying work. In depression the conscience that should hold the line until morning lets forbidden, self-attacking material onstage early—and then wakes the patient at 4 a.m. to continue the trial.

2012-120.sentence: Avoidance is the defense: the person never stays long enough for fear to update. D-cycloserine only helps if the exposure actually happens; it does not replace facing the cue, it just makes the unlearning stick once the defense is set aside.

2012-121.sentence: Checking TSH before lithium is not just a lab ritual. It is a first statement of the relationship: this salt can feed stability and can also poison the thyroid, so you measure the organ you may injure before you ask the patient to swallow it.

2012-122.sentence: The frame here is medical: new depression and cognitive change plus inflamed joints on a previously stable prednisone dose is lupus until proven otherwise, not a therapy hour about stress. You hold the limit by ordering the workup for disease-induced cerebritis instead of attributing it to corticosteroid toxicity or psychological strain.

2012-123.sentence: Finding meaning in the loss is a sign of psychological mindedness: the mourner can look at their own grief and use it, not only suffer it. A trial comment that lands is something like, “You are trying to keep them inside you without staying frozen in the day they died.”

2012-124.sentence: APA ethics draw a hard termination line: no sexual relationship with a current or former patient, period. Time, marriage, supervision, and “no exploitation” do not reopen the door, because the old transference does not expire when the last session ends.

2012-125.sentence: When the lesion is the proximal axon, myelin repair is not enough and the body cannot convert raw threat into a thinkable illness. That is nameless dread in neurologic form: the team has to contain respiratory and autonomic collapse until the feeling—and the prognosis—can be named.

2012-126.sentence: CB1 receptors packed in the hippocampus knock out short-term memory, so the self cannot keep a coherent story of the last hour. Without that inner mirror of what just happened, competence and self-esteem wobble even if mood and reality-testing look intact.

2012-127.sentence: Psychogenic blindness is a compromise: a wish not to see something forbidden collides with a prohibition against admitting that wish, so vision itself becomes the battlefield. Evoked potentials still fire because the pathway is intact; the conflict is in looking, not in the optic nerve.

2012-128.sentence: Therapeutic privilege can be a Kleinian move: the doctor takes in the patient's panic and then withholds the risk, as if the patient were too fragile to hold both hope and danger at once. Depressive concern would name that anxiety and still tell the truth; paranoid-schizoid thinking splits the news into poison and keeps the patient in the dark to 'repair' them.

2012-129.sentence: This adolescent is not splitting the nose into an all-bad object that must be endlessly remade; it is a real, dated hockey injury he wants returned to ordinary. When good and damaged can sit in one face, rhinoplasty often lifts quality of life instead of feeding a new preoccupation.

2012-130.sentence: The MMSE has a ceiling effect in a former history professor: easy items never reach the height where his actual decline lives. The complaint is the meaning—lost keys and lost names in a mind built for lectures—not a screen that still looks 'normal' because it never asked him to work that high.

2012-131.sentence: Progressive supranuclear palsy steals the small motor adjustments ego uses to stay upright: upward gaze fails, the neck locks in extension, and axial rigidity makes rising from a chair and short-step gait treacherous. Falls are not only neurologic; they are a daily hit to affect tolerance when the body no longer partners with intention.

2012-132.sentence: Clomipramine is the TCA that actually holds OCD over the long haul because serotonin, not just norepinephrine, loosens the ritual's grip. The wash or check had been a homemade secure base; with relapse prevention the person can lean on people again instead of on proximity to the sink.

2012-133.sentence: Supportive therapy is a two-person bargain: you and the patient agree to leave standing the defenses that are currently holding the hour together. Accepting those defenses is how you stay in a usable relationship instead of turning care into a fight about insight.

2012-134.sentence: Haloperidol 5 mg IM is the limit once PCP has already blown past a quiet room and talk: you hold safety for staff and patient rather than waiting for a cooperative frame that does not exist. Soft restraints and oral diazepam or zolpidem are not that limit; intramuscular antipsychotic is how you stop an escalating, hallucinating assault on the room.

2012-135.sentence: A five-year-old still thinks a wish can move the world, so “I hate you” and Mom’s crash feel like one event. That is age-appropriate egocentric causality, not a precocious conscience and not a break with reality.

2012-136.sentence: Family systems count who actually soothes, feeds, and stays—the grandmother and the neighbor belong if they function as attachment figures. Working families share those attributes of care and reliability more than they share a blood-and-roof structure.

2012-137.sentence: The parent–teacher split is already an enactment: homework chaos at home and adequate attention at school are two relationships producing two different kids. You do not pick a villain; you treat the rating discrepancy as expected data about setting and dyad.

2012-138.sentence: Nightmares, peri-event detachment, and silence with friends at one week is acute stress disorder, not PTSD. The assault lands on Erikson’s intimacy task: she cannot risk telling anyone, so isolation replaces the ordinary reach for another person.

2012-139.sentence: Horner syndrome after neck trauma is the body saying the sympathetic chain on that side has been interrupted: lid droops, pupil stays small in the dark, and the face does not sweat. The triad is not a generic “droopy lid”; it is the face advertising a broken fight-or-flight wire you must not miss.

2012-140.sentence: Aripiprazole’s D2 partial agonism is a stabilizer, not a sledgehammer: it occupies the receptor and still lets some dopamine through. That property can spare a patient the prolactin crash of a full antagonist when the ego is already working hard to tolerate a medication change.

2012-141.sentence: Mefloquine can split the mind without the person leaving the chair: anxiety, agitation, and persecutory delusions arrive as a drug effect, not as “schizoaffective coming back.” Treat the antimalarial as the dissociative trigger first; do not rewrite a decade of stability as travel stress.

2012-142.sentence: Atrial fibrillation and the brain have already collaborated on one embolic MCA stroke; warfarin is how you stop that two-person pattern from repeating. Aspirin-plus-dipyridamole or ticlopidine treats the artery conversation, not the atrium that is throwing clot.

2012-143.sentence: Both IPT and CBT stay in the here and now: they use the current relationship field—work conflict, withdrawn friends—as the secure base for change. Neither asks you to excavate childhood or interpret transference as the main tool.

2012-144.sentence: Sleep paralysis is the same REM machinery that made the sleep-onset dreamlike state: the body is still locked while the mind is already awake. The pill-or-sleep story here is narcolepsy’s package—irresistible sleep, hypnagogic imagery, and paralysis—not apnea or restless legs.

2012-145.sentence: A fitness-for-duty exam is not a treatment alliance, so the frame has to be spoken before you take a history: who asked for the report, and what will leave the room. If you wait until after the resident has talked, you have already borrowed a confidentiality you cannot keep.

2012-146.sentence: Preadolescent girls usually pull ahead of same-age boys in height and secondary sexual development; that lag is the timetable, not a failure of the boy. Name the stage so the family stops treating a normal sex difference as a contest they have already lost.

2012-147.sentence: Once use is compulsive, the drink is less a chase of high than a flight from withdrawal, craving, and shame—negative reinforcement doing the work. That is suppression of dysphoria in action: the next dose is how the patient keeps the bad feeling from arriving, not how he seeks a good one.

2012-148.sentence: The lucid interval after a temporal blow is the epidural hematoma buying time while arterial blood from the middle meningeal artery fills the space. The “I woke up, I am fine” stretch is the finding doing its worst work: it hides rising intracranial pressure until vomiting and lethargy declare it.

2012-149.sentence: Couples work sits on Erikson’s intimacy-versus-isolation task: can two people stay in a we without collapsing into blame or flight. Pointing the camera at the relationship problem, not at whose family of origin is worse, is how you keep that task in the room.

2012-150.sentence: Normal adult alpha is a posterior, intermittent, eyes-closed rhythm; it is the cortex showing an organized waking background, not a lesion signature. Treat it as evidence the mind can still assemble a coherent state—do not read a reactive posterior alpha as the seizure or the unremembered event you came looking for.

2012-151.sentence: The silverware ritual and chewing look like a compromise: a brief wish to rearrange the kitchen collides with a prohibition that cuts consciousness off. Complex partial seizures do the cutting for her—lip smacking, one-to-two-minute uninterruptible automatisms, and amnesia—so you treat cortex, not a fugue of forbidden desire.

2012-152.sentence: Checking the already-taken-off orders is undoing: she tries to cancel a death-wish that her conscience still treats as causal after her brother’s tularemia. The superego will not accept “I wished it and he died” as coincidence, so she keeps rewriting the chart until the fantasy of harm feels reversed.

2012-153.sentence: Handing over the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) recruits you as someone who will believe her numbers without first putting words on them. If you treat the score as the whole truth, you skip the transference question: what she can say to a scale that she cannot yet say to you.

2012-154.sentence: A trial that excludes comorbidity cannot be rushed into “this is what we do here”; that is a limit on generalizability, not a personality flaw in the paper. External validity dies when the study population is not the population you treat—placebo, attrition, and regression toward the mean bruise internal stories, not the outside world.

2012-155.sentence: A golden-brown Kayser–Fleischer ring plus low ceruloplasmin is copper, not a metaphor you can interpret away. Insight here means seeing that dysarthria, wing-beating tremor, and unexplained liver disease are Wilson’s, so the trial comment is a lab order, not a defense interpretation.

2012-156.sentence: The “bumps” and picking keep a fragile sense of a salvageable body when dermatologists refuse to mirror the defect as real. First-line fluvoxamine treats the body-dysmorphic loop; pimozide would idealize an old delusional-parasitosis script and leave self-esteem still hitched to the next scrape.

2012-157.sentence: GABA-A is how alcohol swallows raw terror before it can be named: nameless dread gets dumped into chloride channels instead of held in a mind. That is evacuation, not containment—the feeling is quieted by sedation and ataxia, so nobody has to think it.

2012-158.sentence: Preparation means they already call truancy a problem and are picking tactics, which is still one step short of walking through the school door. That is suppression: they can park the wish to skip long enough to name a Monday plan, without having to deny the wish is there.

2012-159.sentence: Insight is the hinge: they can still entertain “maybe this is fear, not a tumor,” which is what keeps hypochondriasis from becoming a somatic delusion. If you keep ordering another scan to soothe your own doubt, that is an enactment—the two of you are living the hunt for a perfectly certain body instead of talking about the terror.

2012-160.sentence: After the stimulant looked like poison to the tic circuit and the tics stayed, an alpha-adrenergic agonist (clonidine or guanfacine) is the next trial that can quiet both ADHD arousal and Tourette movements. Offer it as a calmer feed, not as proof the child is broken or as a demand that the tics disappear on schedule.

2012-161.sentence: A working-memory test that only checks immediate recall is unfinished until it also measures attention, the capacity to hold digits while something else tries to pull you off. That is the frame in cognitive form: someone has to hold the limit so the material does not leak the moment a distraction arrives.

2012-162.sentence: The rat is the conditioned stimulus: a once-neutral thing that now carries the fright that belonged to the noise. A trial comment that builds insight is “your body learned the rat means danger,” so the child can see the pairing instead of treating the fear as a fact about rats.

2012-163.sentence: Competency is about today’s capacity, not yesterday’s voices or tomorrow’s verdict. You cannot rush a defendant past the Dusky questions: do they understand the charge, and can they work with counsel? Illness history, meds on the crime day, and right-versus-wrong belong to other exams.

2012-164.sentence: Pramipexole, a dopamine agonist, can loosen the ego’s brakes on impulse: gambling, spending, sex. The person still “knows” the risk; the wanting just outruns judgment. Ego strength here is impulse control, not insight.

2012-165.sentence: Buprenorphine is a mixed opioid agonist/antagonist: it occupies mu receptors enough to quiet craving, then blocks a full agonist from flooding in. That is a pharmacologic split—relief without the old high—so induction still waits for withdrawal or you precipitate it.

2012-166.sentence: After suicide or homicide, the early grief looks familiar, then dysphoria stays. The system often enacts a two-person repetition: you get recruited to prosecute, acquit, or explain the death instead of sitting with the unanswerable. Name that pull so the interview does not become a courtroom.

2012-167.sentence: Chronic heavy drinking quietly empties magnesium and phosphate while the person uses denial: “I’m fine, I just need a drink.” Denial is not lying; it keeps the depleted body off the mental screen until tremor and vomiting force the labs. Order Mg and Phos even when the story minimizes.

2012-168.sentence: Catatonic excitement is excessive purposeless motor activity that does not track you—you are not the stimulus. Countertransference may rush in as “they’re ignoring me” or an urge to over-control the floor. You are being recruited as a bystander to a motor storm, not as a failed interpreter.

2012-169.sentence: Skipping MRI after a first convulsion that started in the right arm is a quiet moral shortcut: EEG or labs feel diligent while you leave a late-life mass unlooked-at. Conscience here is the duty to image the hemisphere that announced itself, not to settle for a cheaper test that cannot show the lesion.

2012-170.sentence: Imaginal exposure is already a two-person enactment: you and the patient are crossing the bridge in the office instead of walking to a real one. Name that bargain out loud so the image stays a rehearsal, not a collusion that forever postpones the actual height.

2012-171.sentence: School-age is when the IQ of 68 meets reading groups and number facts, and the child can look present while the academic self goes offline. That is a vertical split: the cooperative classmate stays in the chair and the failing learner leaves without anyone calling it dissociation.

2012-172.sentence: Bill Wilson did not lecture Dr. Bob; he lent ego strength—impulse control and affect tolerance around craving—when the surgeon’s own coping had collapsed into drink and withdrawal. AA starts as one person borrowing another’s capacity to stay sober until that capacity is internalized.

2012-173.sentence: After the mother’s limit, the twelve-year-old runs to grandmother to restore proximity and calm—using a second attachment figure as a regulator. Triangulation is that secure-base shopping: the child recruits the grandmother so the dyad never has to hold the protest.

2012-174.sentence: Failed antidepressant trials plus obesity, acne, and hirsutism are not a one-person mood story; the body is joining the conversation with cortisol. Ecchymoses are the interpersonal clue you cannot ignore: the clinic pair must treat Cushing’s bruising as a third party in the room, not another SSRI failure.

2012-175.sentence: School-age minds first assimilate: they fold the penguin into the old “bird” schema before they rewrite the schema. Do not push uncovering or sudden accommodation; support the existing construct until it can stretch without collapsing.

2012-176.sentence: Alprostadil, given transurethrally or into the corpus cavernosum, makes erection a local prostaglandin event, not a verdict on whether the partner is “good” tonight. Treat the vascular failure first so the couple stops using every limp episode as proof the relationship is bad.

2012-177.sentence: Stopping shaving and toothbrushing is not a conversion symptom; it is realistic avoidance of trigger zones in trigeminal neuralgia, those seconds-long V2/V3 jolts set off by light touch. Interpret the frown as pain, not as a wish to punish the face or the examiner.

2012-178.sentence: The basketball-card hoard is a drive in work clothes: competitive wish and father-identification get bound into collecting, ranking, and showing the rare cards. Erikson’s industry versus inferiority is the stage where that wish either becomes competence with dad and peers or turns into “my grades prove I am less.”

2012-179.sentence: Contemplation in motivational enhancement is a self-esteem problem: part of the person still needs the drink as a stabilizer, part wants a more coherent self. Mirror the split and evoke their own reasons; a push into action feels like a narcissistic slight and they cling harder.

2012-180.sentence: This is identity work, not a date: she shadowed the resident’s stores to try on the therapist’s self, Erikson’s identity versus diffusion lived as a shopping route. Interpret the longing to identify; confront, test, or transfer her and you confirm she will be “fired” for needing a model.

2012-181.sentence: The Halstead-Reitan Battery is the one instrument here that maps damaged circuits instead of personality style. A TAT or Rorschach will spin a story about the injury; WAIS and MMPI-2 can look 'off' without telling you which domains actually failed.

2012-182.sentence: Repeated respiratory illness can freeze a child's lesson that air hunger equals dying. Panic disorder is that lesson never updating—the adult still treats a tight chest as catastrophe instead of a body signal that can be named and waited out.

2012-183.sentence: Physostigmine crosses the blood–brain barrier and puts acetylcholine back where the antimuscarinic stole it. The flushed, dry, delirious picture is not a psychosis asking for chlorpromazine or more atropine; it is a cholinergic vacuum asking to be filled.

2012-184.sentence: Lock the door and you are recruited as the only doctor they can have—that is the necessaries doctrine, not charity. Notice the countertransference that they forfeited care; the duty exists because they cannot walk out and seek it themselves.

2012-185.sentence: A harsh conscience—yours or the patient's—may treat methylphenidate as a moral shortcut for 'laziness' in early HIV-associated dementia. Use it while drive can still be borrowed; later the same stimulant becomes frankly toxic, so the permission has a clock.

2012-186.sentence: Bilateral hippocampal and parahippocampal injury erases the ledger where a wish can become a memory. The person still wants the story of why they are here; amnesia is the anatomic veto—the trace cannot land.

2012-187.sentence: An unexplained intracranial injury is often the only language the infant has for what cannot be remembered or named. Head trauma is how the unrepresented scene—the blow that nobody will narrate—gets repeated in the body and then in the consult dyad that wants to look away.

2012-188.sentence: “My apple” is not greed; it is the child discovering a self that is not mother’s. The protest marks a developmental arrival: two minds, two owners, one fruit.

2012-189.sentence: By thirty-six hours the lost heroin is no longer a story; it is a two-person crisis in the room—sweats, yawns, bargaining, the urge to “just give something.” That is an enactment: you and the patient are living the absence instead of timing it.

2012-190.sentence: Absorption is a developmental capacity: attention can finally stay inside one imagined scene the way a child stays inside play. Hallway noise drops out not because the mind splits, but because that hold has arrived.

2012-191.sentence: When methylphenidate “fails,” a harsh conscience wants a moral upgrade—atomoxetine, an antipsychotic, something that feels like punishment for noncompliance. Mixed amphetamine salts stay with the same drive problem; they do not treat the child as if inattention were a character defect.

2012-192.sentence: Refeeding sits on Erikson’s first task: can the body take in care without collapsing. A phosphate crash two days into high-calorie feeds is trust vs. mistrust written on the myocardium—too much offered, too little intracellular store to metabolize it.

2012-193.sentence: The Nuremberg Code names consent as the first ethical act, not a formality after the protocol is already written. For the inpatient you want to interview, that rule is doing protective work: it keeps “research subject” from collapsing into “patient who cannot refuse.”

2012-194.sentence: A prior suicide attempt carries the highest standardized mortality ratio because the death-drive has already found a method, not just a mood. In Kleinian terms this is a failed repair: the attack on the self was enacted rather than held as depressive concern, and the next attack is statistically closer.

2012-195.sentence: Function lives in the household you can watch at 7 a.m., not in the kinship chart. Ask who actually resides together, because those interaction patterns are the current attachment field that is shaping the school refusal.

2012-196.sentence: New confusion days after an SSRI in a 70-year-old with Alzheimer disease is a medical emergency first, not an invitation to interpret the dementia. Order electrolytes before you uncover anything: hyponatremia is the finding that can drop consciousness, and this mind cannot use insight work until sodium is safe.

2012-197.sentence: Salt craving, hyperpigmentation, weight loss, and apathy are the adrenal cortex failing, not a depressed object world. Name adrenocortical insufficiency out loud so the “depression” stops being treated as a purely psychic bad object while cortisol stays unreplaced.

2012-198.sentence: The Child Behavior Checklist is the broad-band scale with age- and gender-based norms, so teacher “ADHD” and parent “worry” can sit on the same page. That split is your first test of psychological mindedness: can the adults see that the child is one person, not two competing diagnoses?

2012-199.sentence: Writer’s cramp is a task-specific dystonia, so the honest limit is the overactive writing muscles, not a request to keep producing pages through pain. Botulinum toxin holds that limit at the neuromuscular junction; lorazepam or baclofen just blurs the diagnosis into “tension” and leaves the secretary still writing inside a cramped hand.

2012-200.sentence: A failing liver cannot oxidize most benzodiazepines, so diazepam, clonazepam, alprazolam, and clorazepate stack up as the organ sets the metabolic limit. Lorazepam is conjugated by glucuronidation instead, which is how you respect that limit rather than arguing with it.

2012-201.sentence: Alcohol is doing a job for antisocial personality: it shortens the already thin pause between impulse and act, so deceit, aggression, and rights-violations run with less friction. The drinking is not a separate “addiction personality”; it is an amplifier of the same externalizing pattern that usually started before the bottle.

2012-202.sentence: IPT refuses the transference field—the place where the patient would dump unwanted bits of self into you via projective identification, that is, making you feel and act the leftover part. It stays with depressive concern for real others: role transition, role dispute, direct advice, and repair of actual relationships instead of analyzing who you have become in the room.

2012-203.sentence: From the first minutes of life the infant already orients to the human voice over other sounds, so attachment is not a later luxury you “create” with the right toy. Talking, reading, and singing are using a preference that is wired at birth, not waiting for a social smile to prove the baby is ready.

2012-204.sentence: After an SSRI trips a brief mania, the pull is to become the doctor who “unmasked bipolar” and lock in a lifelong label. Hold the countertransference: this episode meets substance-induced mood disorder, not bipolar II, until a spontaneous syndrome shows up off the drug.

2012-205.sentence: When melancholia has emptied the man of speech, food, and thirst, the body is doing the remembering he cannot put into words. ECT is the intervention that reaches that unrepresented state first: it interrupts the somatic freeze so a mind can start to exist again.

2012-206.sentence: ADHD is a developmental claim about a capacity that should show up wherever the child has to hold attention and inhibit impulse. If the trouble lives only in one classroom, you have not yet seen a missing function; you have seen a setting that cannot hold him.

2012-207.sentence: A posterior cerebral infarct can steal a visual field and leave the patient half-blind to what he owes the world. The harsh conscience still judges the missed objects as carelessness, while the cortex that would show him the other half of the scene is silent.

2012-208.sentence: Before you sit with the defendant, name the jurisdiction’s insanity test, or you will split: clinician in one room, legal actor in another. The first step is to know which standard (M’Naghten, ALI, or the local statute) will decide whether mind and crime can even be linked.

2012-209.sentence: Stopping cigarettes on a smoke-free unit removes CYP1A1/1A2 induction, so the same clozapine dose floods the system and can seize him. That is an ego-strength problem in pharmacology: the coping habit (smoking) was also the enzyme that kept the drug inside a tolerable range.

2012-210.sentence: Klein would ask whether the mourner can still keep the dead person as a whole object—loved and missed—rather than a persecuting absence. Cross-cultural rituals that look “too long” or too concrete can be depressive-position repair, not pathology; they widen what counts as ordinary grief.

2012-211.sentence: MBT sits on Bowlby's attachment theory: the therapist is a secure base you use to notice your own mind, not a Kleinian container you fill with split-off good and bad. When a late callback becomes “she is rejecting me,” you do not decode a hidden object; you slow the certainty and ask what made the attachment figure feel gone.

2012-212.sentence: Cluster A isolation is Erikson's trust-versus-mistrust left unfinished: other people never became safe enough to approach, so withdrawal is the compromise. Social withdrawal is the signal symptom; catatonia, loose associations, and command voices would mean the task has already collapsed into frank psychosis.

2012-213.sentence: The bilingual schoolroom is a cultural third: a public language and audience the child cannot yet risk a voice inside. Start with graded behavioral exposure that raises tolerance for speaking there; do not open with an SSRI, a benzo, or an Oedipal play hour as if the silence were a private family secret.

2012-214.sentence: The Trail-Making Test asks the ego to hold a sequence in mind while the eyes scan and the set switches—attention, visual search, and cognitive sequencing in one run. Intact naming or a word list (Boston Naming, CVLT) does not prove that executive glue is still there.

2012-215.sentence: Peritraumatic dissociation is the ego stepping out of the scene—numbing affect and reality-testing so the mind does not have to stay inside the crash. That immediate uncoupling, more than ordinary fear or rumination, marks a mind that could not bind the event and raises later PTSD risk.

2012-216.sentence: Lithium is a high-demand technique: it needs kidneys that can still clear a narrow-window salt. After 65, falling renal clearance is why valproate is chosen more often—not because valproate wins head-to-head, but because the aging body cannot safely hold lithium's job.

2012-217.sentence: Validating what this family already does well is the Engagement stage of family psychoeducation: you are recruiting two more people as partners, not installing a protocol on them. If you skip that join and jump to relapse drills, the parents and the 25-year-old with schizophrenia start making a new pattern together—compliance theater instead of a working alliance.

2012-218.sentence: The “hyper,” one-hour sleep, and irritability after 80 mg of prednisone are a steroid storm, not a character you have to interpret first. Gradual taper is the treatment; naming it as mania and piling on quetiapine or valproate can be a defensive enactment—acting instead of removing the cause.

2012-219.sentence: Cisplatin is the agent that left large-fiber position and vibration gone distally and color-changing pain in the fingers and toes. After orchiectomy and chemo, the pill and infusion can feel like leftover poison in the body—proof the cure still occupies him—so name the neuropathy plainly rather than treating the numbness as only “anxiety.”

2012-220.sentence: DSM-IV-TR Asperger disorder is marked off from autistic disorder by age-appropriate language acquisition, not by nicer social skills or absent clumsiness. An old chart that never put words to early language leaves that history unrepresented, and the adult then repeats the gap in the interview as mute social oddity you cannot quite name.

2012-221.sentence: The stomachache and the refusal to sleep alone are the compromise: the child wants the parent nearby and also wants to be a big kid who goes to school. Separation anxiety is that collision in the body—proximity is the wish, independence is the prohibition, and the symptom lets both stay.

2012-222.sentence: Lithium sat at 0.8 for a decade; the new antihypertensive raised it to 1.5 by cutting renal clearance, and nausea, tremor, and ataxia followed. Competence here is not “being a good bipolar patient”—it is protecting a working self by catching the interaction before the body, not the mood, takes the hit.

2012-223.sentence: The aphasia and hemiparesis arrive as nameless dread: a body event that has not yet become a thinkable stroke until someone holds last-known-well and the clock. Your job is containment in Bion’s sense—taking in the raw panic so it can become a plan, which here is intravenous thrombolysis inside the window, not aspirin while you wait for the feeling to settle.

2012-224.sentence: Withdrawal has a pace you cannot hurry; a short-half-life benzodiazepine ends coverage the way an abrupt termination ends a session, before the nervous system has metabolized the loss. That drop is why grand mal seizures become more likely—the brain is left without a long-acting hold once the pill is gone.

2012-225.sentence: Psychological mindedness starts when he can hear the thought “I am a failure as a husband” as his construction, not as a fact the affair proved. CBT’s first useful comment targets that assumption of personal failure, not the marriage history, so he can see his own part without drowning in the parents’ divorce.

2012-226.sentence: Counting to 100 is a homemade frame: a time rule he invents to keep the contamination worry from flooding work. PET still lights the caudate because a private ritual is not a real limit—the circuit keeps firing as if no one is holding the hour.

2012-227.sentence: A child’s story is co-authored; you do not know the attachment field until you hear the people who feed, soothe, and set the rules. Parental interviews are therefore mandatory—not optional labs or a play hour—because the relationship that holds the child is part of the examination.

2012-228.sentence: Doubling lithium is acting out: she changes the dose instead of saying the bipolar illness still feels unbearable. The diarrhea, tremor, and disorientation are the body answering that bypass—lithium will not be undone by more of itself.

2012-229.sentence: Acetylcholine-receptor antibodies sit in the neuromuscular cleft and cancel a message the nerve already sent. That is an enactment: nerve and muscle are living a blocked conversation instead of a working one, and the consult often repeats it as “is this just psychiatric fatigue?”

2012-230.sentence: Hopelessness is a verdict: the future has already been tried, found guilty, and denied parole. That inner sentence, not remorse or anxiety, is what the cognitive model treats as the suicide-risk signal.

2012-231.sentence: Discrepancy is a developmental arrival: he can now see the gap between wanting closeness and inviting fury. Brief psychodynamic work uses that newly arrived observing capacity rather than waiting for a full transference reconstruction.

2012-232.sentence: The head-banging is anger at the occupied grandparents and the new baby, turned against the self so attachment can stay clean. The symptom is doing the job of punishing his own body instead of risking the relationship.

2012-233.sentence: SSRIs beat TCAs on the best-documented point: fewer people drop out because of side effects. That is an industry-stage problem: you cannot keep doing the work of getting well if TCA sedation and anticholinergic fog make you leave the job.

2012-234.sentence: Saying the alphabet backward from Z tests concentration: can the self hold a sequence and run it against the grain. A miss is a live hit to competence, not a date, a proverb, or breakfast recall.

2012-235.sentence: Hallucinations on a stimulant are not just a “side effect to watch.” They are the wish for more drive, more focus, more go colliding with a brain that can no longer tell signal from threat. Stop the drug now; the prohibition is physiological, and you do not interpret voices you just chemically turned on.

2012-236.sentence: The bond is not poetry. It is the adult’s body between the infant and danger when the infant cannot yet represent danger in words. What cannot be remembered as “I was kept safe” is later repeated as cling, freeze, or a clinic that suddenly feels like a cliff.

2012-237.sentence: Incorrect treatment is the claim that most often arrives, and it often arrives after you were recruited to be the one who “just sends them home.” Notice the pull to be the brave discharger or the anxious jailer, then document the assessment, the alternatives, and the limit you actually held.

2012-238.sentence: Elevated IgG in both CSF and serum points toward sarcoidosis, a systemic story, not MS as a private CNS file. The frame here is diagnostic honesty: you do not let one CSF number become a diagnosis you cannot later unsay.

2012-239.sentence: Akathisia is the body shouting what the patient may not yet be able to name. Before you add propranolol or switch the antipsychotic, try one trial comment: “This restlessness started with the medicine, not with your character.” If they can use that, you have a partner; if they only pace, treat the receptor first.

2012-240.sentence: Thiamine before glucose is not a superstition. The hypoglycemia is the obvious alarm; Wernicke’s is the quieter one the drinking has been doing for the person, blotting out a brain that could not be fed. Give the cofactor so the rescue does not finish the injury.

2012-241.sentence: Covert obstructionism is delayed agency: the child never quite got a safe way to say no out loud, so stubbornness and lost forms do the refusing. Name the old DSM type—passive-aggressive—then ask what direct protest would cost this adult if it finally arrived.

2012-242.sentence: Gender, class, and an abusive partner sit in the room as a third: they already limited her choices, so do not import a script that she must be secretly devastated by the abortion. Track what actually predicts later depression—pre-pregnancy depression—rather than moralizing her reported relief.

2012-243.sentence: Integrity is Erikson’s last task: looking back and finding the life, including the misses, still worth having been lived. After sixty-five that verdict is the opposite of despair, not a denial of grief.

2012-244.sentence: Nervios is not a worse object or a sinful self; it is how many Puerto Rican and other Latin American patients locate depression in the nerves—jittery, sleepless, aching. Ask what “nervousness” means in her family before you translate it into emptiness or shame.

2012-245.sentence: Do not read a half-face as conversion until the forehead and the ear have spoken. Equal forehead and perioral weakness plus mastoid pain and hyperacusis is Bell’s palsy—peripheral VII—not a split-off rage parked on the cheek.

2012-246.sentence: A mixed manic/depressed episode puts you both in two weathers at once: racing, irritable, and hopeless in the same hour. Lithium often fails that mix, and the dyad then enacts “nothing works” unless you name the mixed state instead of bargaining for a cleaner mania.

2012-247.sentence: This mind is already running hot: easy fatigue plus feeling keyed up means the ego is burning fuel just to keep worry from spilling. Do not go hunting childhood meaning first; stabilize sleep, tension, and the day's tasks, then decide later whether this person can use any uncovering at all.

2012-248.sentence: The entorhinal cortex is the doorway for new memories; once cells die there, the clock on recent learning does not rewind because someone is motivated. Treatment has to honor that limit: you work with what still encodes, and you do not treat forgetting as resistance.

2012-249.sentence: Simple schizophrenia is the old name for a picture built only of deficit: blunting, withdrawal, no rich inner story to interpret. A trial comment that asks them to see their own part will bounce; you need to test whether any observing ego is left before you treat silence as hidden meaning.

2012-250.sentence: She has already put the baby in the room as a third: “what is best for my baby” is maternal identity speaking, not just a medical preference. Methadone maintenance for the whole pregnancy holds that third without asking her to prove virtue by going cold turkey.

2012-251.sentence: Lithium has no metabolite, so the toxic dose is still lithium itself, sitting in water, waiting for a kidney or a dialysis membrane. That is why hemodialysis works: you can take the actual ion out instead of waiting for the body to “process” a breakdown product that does not exist.

2012-252.sentence: The yelling and hitting after detention can be doing a job: carrying mood, trauma, psychosis, or ADHD that the conduct label is hiding. Evaluating additional psychopathology first treats the outburst as a message, not as the whole person.

2012-253.sentence: At 66 this sits on Erikson’s integrity-versus-despair work: looking back and deciding whether the life was livable, or whether it should end. Amitriptyline turns that despair into a sodium-channel problem, so you get the EKG first; you cannot interpret the suicide as meaning until the QRS is not widening.

2012-254.sentence: The family’s alarm at pajamas in the street is a superego scene: public exposure as a moral emergency. Delirium is the opposite of conscience—waxing-and-waning attention and picking at the gown are not guilt, they are an organ failing in real time.

2012-255.sentence: The 2003 New Freedom Commission named a late developmental task for the whole care system: treat mental health as vigorously as physical health, the way a child finally holds two parts of the self in one mind. Separate schedules and split reimbursement are the earlier stage, when those capacities never quite arrived in the same visit.

2012-256.sentence: An aryl sulfatase mutation is not a memory; it is an unrepresented state written into myelin as sulfatide piles up and white matter fails. The gait, neuropathy, and lost skills are the body repeating what no one can narrate: a gene that never became a story.

2012-257.sentence: Seasonal affective disorder recruits you as the missing light: fall-winter hypersomnia and appetite increase, then spring returns and the transference to the sun lifts. Light therapy works here because the treatment is the longed-for object, not because you became a more inspiring clinician.

2012-258.sentence: The old affair is already in the room: the patient presents a phantom venereal disease, the spouse says it was years ago and forgiven, and the three of you are living the confession again. That is an enactment of psychotic depression—mood-congruent guilt made into a body crime—not a fresh infection or a new hypochondriacal hobby.

2012-259.sentence: Shame after a binge is the signal that the episode already happened; denial is what kept the hand moving until the plate was empty. Name the loss of control in the room so binge-eating disorder is a pattern you can discuss, not a blackout the patient has to hide.

2012-260.sentence: If they can say, "I still jump at engines and I keep canceling drives," they have enough mind to try a comment: the body is treating every highway as the accident. Sertraline is the first-line medicine for that leftover hyperarousal when three months of talk has only half-helped.

2012-261.sentence: The EMG limit is the same as a session limit: you keep asking the neuromuscular junction to fire, and it fails—decreased amplitude with repetitive motor nerve stimulation. You hold that finding; you do not stretch the test until a tired muscle "proves" myasthenia gravis.

2012-262.sentence: Risperidone at 6 mg can feel like a needed feed that also poisons: mood and paranoia lift while masked facies, cogwheel rigidity, drooling, and slowed thinking arrive. Lower the antipsychotic first so the pill stays a help, not a demand that the patient stay stiff to stay well.

2012-263.sentence: Absence is not repression of a thought; the 3 Hz spike-and-wave burst blanks awareness for a few seconds of stare and blink. Do not treat the pause as a child "spacing out" on purpose when the EEG names a seizure.

2012-264.sentence: The wish is a cheaper fill; the prohibition is that the generic must still be the same drug in the blood. FDA bioequivalence is that compromise: not cost, not a new efficacy trial, just proof the parent compound and the copy land alike.

2012-265.sentence: MDMA’s night-after picture—mydriasis, hypertension, dehydration, a CPK bump—hits the self’s need to feel mirrored and enlarged at the party, then dumps the body into a crash when the borrowed glow is gone. The stimulant–serotonin rush is a chemical stand-in for an idealized, high-wattage self; what you are treating in the ED is the flesh paying for that inflation.

2012-266.sentence: Behavioral work contains the panic by naming the sequence—cue, surge, avoidance, relief—so the raw rush becomes a map instead of nameless dread you can only evacuate by fleeing. Attention to situational maintainers is the container: you hold the unthinkable feeling long enough to turn it into a chain you can interrupt.

2012-267.sentence: Low ceruloplasmin in Wilson disease is a hard stop: the liver and the mind share a deadline you cannot talk past. Impulsivity and lability here are not a character you can hurry into insight; copper has already set a clock the family already watched run out at thirty.

2012-268.sentence: Lorazepam first-line for catatonia—immobility, posturing, echopraxia—treats a developmental capacity that has gone offline: the body can no longer use gesture as thought. You do not start with lithium or a neuroleptic as if mood or psychosis were still the available language; the motor self has to come back online before talk can arrive.

2012-269.sentence: Sagittal sinus thrombosis with papilledema, opening pressure of 80 cm H2O, bloody last-tube RBCs, and a high D-dimer/FDP is the conscience of the workup: you do not get a pass because the noncontrast CT is clean. Calling it pseudotumor or migraine would be a sanctioned gap in duty—relief from the harder diagnosis at the patient’s risk.

2012-270.sentence: Libidinal-stage theory fails clinically because adult reconstructions are idiosyncratic: each telling evacuates a messy past into a tidy oral/anal/genital story that will not hold still. Bion’s problem is containment—the raw developmental mess has to stay thinkable; a stage label is often just a way to dump the dread into a sequence that never was consistent.

2012-271.sentence: Uncontrollable shock empties the animal of a felt sense that effort works—self psychology’s competence pole, the ordinary pride that “I can still do something.” Antidepressants reverse those escape deficits, which is why the paradigm is useful: they restore trying, not just mood labels.

2012-272.sentence: The verbal self arrives early and loud; the nonverbal toolkit—visual-spatial organization, reading faces and tone—never quite comes online. That is the nonverbal learning disability profile that tracks with Asperger, not dyslexia or a global IQ drop.

2012-273.sentence: He is trying to keep two attachments alive at once: the parental Colombian object and the new marital one. Integration names that strain—heritage held, not discarded—unlike assimilation (drop the old) or separation (refuse the new).

2012-274.sentence: You will feel recruited to become the skeptic who unmasks a faker; that countertransference belongs more to factitious disorder and malingering. Conversion is the limp that is not produced on purpose—no secondary-gain plot, no hunt for the sick role.

2012-275.sentence: A harsh conscience wants a prohibition: one dinner wine must now be a dementia toxin because the parents had dementia. The data do not license that sermon—if the pattern stays one drink and mood stays remitted, you do not rewrite a lifelong habit into a crime.

2012-276.sentence: Late-life baroreflexes no longer buffer a stand-up; that capacity has thinned, so orthostasis is the enemy. Among these TCAs, nortriptyline is the secondary amine that least knocks blood pressure down—skip doxepin, amitriptyline, and imipramine.

2012-277.sentence: An intention tremor plus broken rapid alternating movements is the cerebellum failing at its actual job: timing and smoothing a movement the cortex already chose. The clumsiness is not “nerves”; it is the ipsilateral cerebellar hemisphere dropping the last milliseconds of the plan.

2012-278.sentence: Erikson’s intimacy task is mutuality: two people stay related without one using the other. A boundary crossing can still serve the work; a violation is when the clinician’s need (status, sex, money, or a private audience) exploits the patient and isolates them from a safe professional relationship.

2012-279.sentence: Residential care is indicated when home cannot function as a secure base for sobriety—when the people who should hold proximity are the ones offering the drug. Lack of family support is not a character flaw; it means the attachment environment itself is the relapse cue, so the person needs a substitute holding setting.

2012-280.sentence: This laughter is not play or joy; a hypothalamic hamartoma can fire gelastic seizures and, sitting on the tuber cinereum, also drive precocious puberty. The face smiles while the girl feels nothing funny—development has been hijacked at the hypothalamus, not in her mood.

2012-281.sentence: Bilateral electrode placement is a two-person (really two-hemisphere) bargain: more antidepressant punch, more retrograde amnesia. You and the patient decide together whether wiping autobiographical time is worth the bilateral efficacy, then watch orientation and life-story memory as the relationship’s scorecard.

2012-282.sentence: A sixteen-year-old trying on a masochistic heterosexual scene in fantasy is doing ordinary sexual-identity work: the mind rehearses desire before it has to live it. Excitement plus anxiety is the ego sampling a script, not a verdict of future paraphilia or proof of abuse.

2012-283.sentence: Twelve-step facilitation treats showing up at AA as an ego win: the patient already tolerated the social-anxiety spike and still walked in. You shore up that capacity instead of analyzing the strangers, chasing craving, or backing off the meeting.

2012-284.sentence: Asking for a stimulant after four hours of sleep is a wish to override the body’s limit rather than restore the eight-hour baseline. Dyssomnia NOS names that collapse; treating it as ADD would collude with the demand to stay up.

2012-285.sentence: A post–lumbar puncture headache that worsens sitting upright is CSF leak physics, not meningitis theater or migraine. Believe the positionality: lie the patient down and treat the leak, do not chase fever or oxygen as if it were something else.

2012-286.sentence: Williams syndrome (7q11.23) gives cocktail-party sociability plus real visuospatial weakness and high anxiety. Support the fear and the spatial deficit; do not interpret the friendliness as sturdy relatedness you can uncover.

2012-287.sentence: Abstract reasoning is the move from “both are round” to “both are fruits”—part to whole class. Same muscle as holding a whole person instead of one concrete feature.

2012-288.sentence: Assaults cluster at change of shift because the holding environment—the staff who know the patient’s state—briefly disappears. Treat handoff like a toddler’s caregiver swap: make the outgoing and incoming minds one continuous object.

2012-289.sentence: Telling the limits of confidentiality at the first visit is conscience put on the calendar, not a speech you give after you have already leaked. The safeguard is the superego made procedural: the rule sits in the room before anyone is tempted to treat privacy as a personal favor.

2012-290.sentence: Propranolol is the usual first reach for essential tremor, but asthma is a hard veto on a nonselective beta blocker. Primidone is the honest next drug: you treat the action tremor without asking the bronchi to pay for a calmer hand.

2012-291.sentence: Habeas corpus is the court walking into an enactment: the hospital is already living “we can hold you” instead of arguing the hold in the open. The writ does not treat the patient; it forces the system to show the body and the legal basis, now.

2012-292.sentence: Hypnosis for IBS works as a borrowed regulator: another person’s voice becomes a temporary secure base for gut arousal the patient cannot dampen alone. The trial signal is not “nice support”; it is a structured other that the enteric nervous system can actually use.

2012-293.sentence: Last observation carried forward is an ego that cannot stand an empty cell: when the participant leaves, the last number is asked to keep functioning as if nothing dropped out. That preserves a complete table, but it is a coping trick, not proof the missing visits would have looked the same.

2012-294.sentence: The fencing posture is a frontal-lobe motor signature; you do not call it “behavioral” from a hallway story. Video-EEG is the frame that holds the limit: brief, stereotyped, clustering nocturnal spells stay seizures until the tracing says otherwise.

2012-295.sentence: Rizatriptan is an abortive 5-HT1B/1D agonist, and it only works if the patient can still say “this is my usual migraine” at the first warning instead of waiting for the pain to prove they deserve a pill. Offer a trial comment: “You delay until the attack is undeniable; taking rizatriptan early is you using your own read of the pattern, not waiting for the headache to make the decision.”

2012-296.sentence: A 29/30 MMSE can become denial: the number is used to push the engineer’s failing finances and travel planning out of awareness because the score “looks fine.” The limitation is that the MMSE may miss very mild cognitive impairment, so treating the total as reassurance is the defense, not a better screen.

2012-297.sentence: The dopaminergic system is the last to mature, so adolescent reward can feel like a feed arriving before prefrontal control can metabolize it. Any dopamine-facing pill or story then lands as proof of need (“my drive is too big”) or as poison (“you are trying to kill the only lively part of me”), depending on whether we frame late DA maturation as deficit or as unfinished development.

2012-298.sentence: At twenty-seven the Erikson task is intimacy versus isolation, and NF-2—merlin-gene mutation with bilateral vestibular schwannomas—can make hearing loss and ataxia feel like a secret that keeps a partner at arm’s length. The gene names the tumors; the stage names the risk that she pulls back from closeness rather than let someone live with a body that keeps delivering new masses.

2012-299.sentence: Age and cohort sit in the room as a third: many older adults were taught that grief is private and respectable, so standard DBT skills miss the extra target of emotional constriction. When they describe bereavement only in practical terms, you are meeting a generational rule that feeling too much is unseemly, not a failure of mindfulness or distress tolerance.

2012-300.sentence: Completed-suicide risk stays elevated versus other adoptees after a birth mother’s suicide; that is a developmental load the child did not choose and adoption does not cancel. What may arrive late, or only with help, is the capacity to hold that history as vulnerability rather than as a script—so the parents can watch for risk without treating every mood as fate.

2013-1.sentence: Financial incentive is not attachment. Attachment would be using the sick role to keep a caregiver close—the “psychological need to feel cared for”—and that points toward factitious illness, not malingering. Name the pending disability check as secondary gain so you do not confuse a bid for money with a bid for a secure base.

2013-2.sentence: Spasmodic torticollis is a cervical dystonia, not a neck that “won’t face” someone; do not interpret the turn until you have treated the circuit. Botulinum toxin is the treatment with the best evidence here, and it works by weakening the overactive muscles rather than by resolving a split between good and bad objects.

2013-3.sentence: Introjection is swallowing the other person whole—taking in a parent’s contempt so it now lives as the patient’s own voice. This mind can use some uncovering: when you show that the phrase is borrowed, you loosen an internalized object instead of only supporting the self-attack.

2013-4.sentence: The school–parent–clinic loop can become an enactment: adults are already living a sexual-danger story instead of talking about ordinary five-year-old curiosity. Peeking and bathroom play among peers, without coercion or distress, is normal sexual development; treat the adults’ panic so the child is not assigned an abuse script he does not have.

2013-5.sentence: Recurrent suicidal behavior in schizophrenia is often acting out: putting a death wish into action rather than holding it in words. Clozapine has the strongest evidence for cutting that behavior, so you treat the impulse at the receptor while you keep naming the wish instead of only managing the aftermath.

2013-6.sentence: Confusion, apathy, and lost tandem gait after gastric bypass can look like collapsed ego strength—poor reality testing and no coping—but the mind is starving for thiamine. Give thiamine for this Wernicke picture before you interpret the “change” as a psychological failure to metabolize loss.

2013-7.sentence: He parks the sadness in karma—past deeds as deserved punishment—so the man sitting with you never has to own a treatable depression. That is a vertical split: he stays in the chair, but the part that could accept care leaves into fate, and arguing Buddhism versus Taoism will not bring that part back.

2013-8.sentence: Sensate-focus work—exercises to heighten sensory awareness, not intercourse or vibrators—asks whether they can notice their own tightening and hurry instead of performing. A trial comment lands here: if they can say “we turn touch into a test,” they have enough psychological mindedness to use Masters and Johnson rather than just follow a homework sheet.

2013-9.sentence: EMG biofeedback can operantly shape muscle tension; night terrors and night sweats will not answer the same way. The limit is time and capacity: forehead and shoulder tightness can be trained down session by session, and you cannot rush a function the paradigm cannot condition.

2013-10.sentence: The CPT scores vigilance by whether attention stays put or blanks while the body remains at the desk. Those omission and commission lapses are a small vertical split: the child leaves the target without leaving the chair, which the MMSE, CVLT, TAT, and WISC-IV are not built to isolate.

2013-11.sentence: Dextromethorphan intoxication blows through ego strength: reality testing goes (“walking on air,” paranoia, hallucinations) and impulse control goes with the tachycardia and agitation. Withdrawal from cocaine, cannabis, or opioids does not produce this mix; the ego is flooded, not emptied.

2013-12.sentence: Alcohol plus alprazolam strips the last useful defense, suppression—the conscious hold on impulse—so the argument at the party becomes action. LSD, MDMA, cocaine, and cannabis do not potentiate that benzo disinhibition the same way; the pair dissolves the brake, not the wish.

2013-13.sentence: Hostility is not a private feeling; it is already being enacted — lived out — in tense interactions and in the vascular bed, where blood pressure tracks the fight. Studying Type A or depression will miss the more consistent finding: anger that is acted rather than thought keeps the pressor system on duty.

2013-14.sentence: Nonmaleficence here is a frame limit, not a personality trait: you do not accept a seriously ill 10-year-old as your patient when your last child work was twenty years ago. Holding that limit — and naming it — protects the child from treatment that would look like care and still be unsafe.

2013-15.sentence: Marked individual differences in executive function first show in the preschool years, when waiting, shifting, and recovering from frustration become visible tasks. That is the developmental window where you can start to see who can hold a plan in mind and who still needs the adult as an external prefrontal cortex.

2013-16.sentence: A blood alcohol of 178 does not close the case; an older drinker after a recent crash can harbor a chronic subdural that only later declares itself as an isodense crescent deforming the cortex. Confusion here has a time course you cannot rush: weeks of slow bleed, not a night of intoxication.

2013-17.sentence: MMPI-2 validity scales do not prove the test is a good test; they show the patient's test-taking attitude — how much they are guarding, exaggerating, or answering at random. Before you interpret a clinical scale, ask whether they can look at their own spin, or whether the profile is mostly a performance.

2013-18.sentence: At forty the Erikson task is generativity: making something work. He treats sleep as a production job — lie still, try hard, manufacture rest — and that work-ego in bed is exactly psychophysiological insomnia. The symptom means effort has invaded the one function that only arrives when effort stops.

2013-19.sentence: The rumination is doing a job: it turns sleep into a performance, so the bed becomes a workplace instead of a cue for rest. Stimulus control names that bargain—go to bed only when sleepy, and leave if you are working the insomnia instead of sleeping.

2013-20.sentence: A new fine tremor after corticosteroids can recruit you into the alarmed witness who treats every shake as anxiety or withdrawal. Name the drug first: steroids amplify physiologic tremor, so your job is not to interpret the hands until you have timed the dose.

2013-21.sentence: An illusion is a real sound—here the rustling leaves—misheard as a call, as if the world were addressing him by name. That is conscience using a stimulus: the mind borrows the wind to make a summons, not a voice from nowhere.

2013-22.sentence: Sixth-grade work at seventeen, after delay already visible in second grade, is the picture of mild intellectual disability: school skills arrive, just years late and thinner. Do not stop at the grade equivalent; check whether conceptual, social, and practical capacities ever caught up.

2013-23.sentence: Fluoxetine is the antidepressant whose milk levels, peaks, and gradients are actually mapped, so the data can hold a mother’s fear of poisoning the infant. The drug’s job in the dyad is often that containment: a known exposure instead of an unknown one.

2013-24.sentence: Clarification is the most insight-oriented move because it puts two versions of the self in the same sentence—what is claimed and what is done. That is identity work: the patient has to own the gap rather than take advice, praise, or more story.

2013-25.sentence: C-6 radiculopathy is not “arm pain as a story.” It is a dermatome with an address: biceps, biceps reflex, and thumb. Treat the root first; metaphor can wait until the C6 circuit is actually intact.

2013-26.sentence: A high-stakes treatment (bad risk–benefit) tightens the capacity exam because the object can kill or save. That is depressive concern, not a rubber stamp: can this mind hold both danger and help, or is the psychiatrist being handed the whole decision as savior or attacker?

2013-27.sentence: The SCL-90-R keeps many bad parts on one page—somatic, anxious, interpersonal—so you do not split the patient into a single “good” or “bad” diagnosis. It is a holding map: mixed objects stay mixed until you see which relationship actually hurts.

2013-28.sentence: An inhibited toddler’s mind startles at novelty; that is a temperament, not a defense you interpret away. Lead with support and graded exposure, not uncovering—this ego needs a safer runway before you ask it to fly.

2013-29.sentence: DID and PTSD are not a one-person museum of alters. The two of you will remake the old danger or the old rescue unless you name it: amnesia and hypervigilance live between people, not only inside states.

2013-30.sentence: An MCA infarct puts a clock on the work: last-known-well is the frame, and you hold the time limit, not the family fantasy that “we can wait.” Face-arm deficit, aphasia, or neglect is the clinical alarm that the window is already closing.

2013-31.sentence: A request for a memory pill can be a feed: proof that someone is doing something about the forgetting. An upgoing plantar response plus nonfluent speech is not asking for that feed; it is asking you to work up a vascular lesion instead of offering donepezil as comfort.

2013-32.sentence: Calling the pulling a nervous habit is minimization: the alopecia stays in view while the diagnosis stays out. Fluoxetine for at least twelve weeks, titrated to a maximal approved dose, treats trichotillomania as a real impulse, not a shrug.

2013-33.sentence: Card sorting can become an enactment: you keep stating the new rule and the two of you live out I will not shift instead of naming the rigidity. The Wisconsin Card-Sorting Test is built to catch that perseveration after feedback says the old category is wrong.

2013-34.sentence: Clock-watching and a locked jaw strip competence: the body will not take an order to sleep. Biofeedback for chronic insomnia gives a bit of mirroring back — the patient can see the arousal and practice turning it down.

2013-35.sentence: One possible bad physics score is not yet a fact, but the mind evacuates: raw dread is dumped as expulsion and family exile instead of being held as a grade. Catastrophic thinking is that uncontained spray; the therapist's if-you-failed question is trying to make the dread thinkable.

2013-36.sentence: PMDD has a built-in stop time: the week after menses is when the storm is supposed to end. That follicular quiet is the limit that separates a luteal-timed syndrome from a mood disorder that never clocks out.

2013-37.sentence: A trial comment can land here: “The ESR and the two-day prednisone response mean the shoulders were announcing inflammation, not a character flaw.” If they can use that, they stop hunting for a psychological sin and can stay with the medical story.

2013-38.sentence: Erikson’s generativity is not a moral exam you fail when the kids leave; the conscience can bless creative community projects as real care for the next generation. A rigid superego that only counts childrearing or career status will keep midlife feeling like dereliction.

2013-39.sentence: A one-week BDI-2 sweep gives point prevalence: who screens hot right now, not who will get ill this year. Watch the pull to become the campus parent who treats that snapshot as destiny; the instrument is a census, not a transference verdict.

2013-40.sentence: Restart fluoxetine, the regulator that already worked, rather than a new molecule that barges into tacrolimus and cyclosporine. Attachment here is practical: keep the known secure base and do not introduce a stranger that can knock the graft off its levels.

2013-41.sentence: Dragons at the desk plus rambling, off-topic answers are a collapse of reality testing, not garden-variety inattention. Early-onset schizophrenia means this ego cannot yet organize thought or filter fear; support structure first, do not interpret the dragons as metaphor.

2013-42.sentence: After temazepam and zolpidem scrambled an already mild dementia, this is not a mind for more sedation-as-uncovering. Ramelteon is the supportive move: nudge the melatonin clock and leave cognition alone.

2013-43.sentence: In the middle of IPT you and the patient keep tightening one agreed link: this supervisor fight, this dip in mood. That is the work of the intermediate phase—strengthening the connection between interpersonal events and symptoms—not restarting the inventory or racing toward goodbye.

2013-44.sentence: Asking bupropion to guarantee methamphetamine abstinence is denial: pushing away the fact that no pill can stand in for craving, cues, and lapse. Bupropion may lower relapse risk; it does not erase the work of staying off meth.

2013-45.sentence: Fever, new paranoia, and a focal seizure are not a request for an antipsychotic first; they are HSV-1 announcing itself in temporal cortex. Treat the encephalitis, not the story the inflamed brain is telling.

2013-46.sentence: Phenelzine plus oxycodone is already an enactment: the procedure team and the long-stable MAOI patient lived the forbidden mix instead of naming the interaction. Delirium, myoclonus, and 196/122 are the body finishing that conversation in the ED.

2013-47.sentence: Slapping a schizophrenia label on a first break is an enactment: the unit repeats the chronic-psychosis script before anyone has talked. Confusion plus poor memory of recent events is the clue that this may still be brief psychotic disorder, not a life sentence.

2013-48.sentence: A 4–8 Hz postural shake that runs in the family will not hurry into Parkinsonism or a psychogenic flourish just because you want a neater ending. Essential tremor sets its own limit: it shows when the limb is held still, and it does not owe you rest tremor.

2013-49.sentence: Name neurofibromatosis type 2 out loud so bilateral VIII schwannomas, meningiomas, and cataracts become one thinkable illness instead of a pile of scares the patient has to dump on you. That is containment: you hold the raw dread of a multi-tumor syndrome until it can be thought as coordinated neurology, not evacuated as one isolated symptom after another.

2013-50.sentence: This 15-year-old with death wishes needs supportive structure and FDA-approved escitalopram, not an uncovering hunt for the meaning of every irritable comment. Ask about suicide directly first; insight work waits until the mind can use it without more despair.

2013-51.sentence: Contingency management lets the methadone clinic stay one whole object: take-home doses arrive when attendance and groups are real, and they shrink when they are not. That keeps the patient from splitting the program into the kind dispenser and the cruel rule-maker.

2013-52.sentence: Threatening involuntary stay unless the manic patient “chooses” admission uses closeness as a club and wrecks informed consent. Attachment needs a secure base; here the psychiatrist offered proximity only as a trap, so the signature is not a free yes.

2013-53.sentence: An infant and each caregiver co-build a bond; that is why multiple attachments form and why their strength can differ. The daycare protest is a two-person pattern with that teacher, not proof the child has only one slot and the parents lost it.

2013-54.sentence: Late-life integrity still shows as grace and etiquette with strangers while Alzheimer dementia quietly takes names and ADLs. The social polish is the last hold on “I am still myself,” not evidence that the mind is intact.

2013-55.sentence: Bilateral internuclear ophthalmoplegia is the medial longitudinal fasciculus failing, not the psyche converting anxiety into double vision. That crossed adduction weakness plus abducting nystagmus is the brainstem’s way of announcing multiple sclerosis before anyone should reach for conversion.

2013-56.sentence: Alexithymia is not a missing heart; feelings never become words, so they stay as headache or chest tightness. In Kleinian terms those affects stay unmentalized and get evacuated into the body instead of becoming concern you can think about and repair.

2013-57.sentence: Residual effects mean treatment A is still acting when you start B, so the second period is no longer a clean answer. A washout is the research frame trying to keep the first drug from speaking for the second.

2013-58.sentence: Oxcarbazepine induces enzymes and can quietly strip an oral contraceptive of its job. The ethical frame is to name that interaction before she starts the pill, not after a surprise pregnancy holds the limit for you.

2013-59.sentence: Atomoxetine blocks the norepinephrine transporter; it is a quieter feed than a dopamine-releasing stimulant. For someone who fears being handed a drug of misuse, that NET action can feel like help without the demand to get high.

2013-60.sentence: Metastatic lung carcinoma is the most common brain tumor at sixty-five because lung cancer seeds the brain; new headache or personality change is that seed, not a late-life attachment crisis. Do not treat the new irritability as a relationship problem until imaging has asked about the lung.

2013-61.sentence: Methadone is holding this woman's ego together: impulse control and affect stay usable because the receptor is not in withdrawal. Pregnancy is already a huge demand on coping; ripping the methadone out (or chasing it with naloxone) would smash that stability for both of them.

2013-62.sentence: Fetal thyroid hormone is not a mood story; it is construction material for cortex and myelination. If that hormone is missing in utero, the brain never gets built, and you get severe intellectual disability rather than a later, reversible delay.

2013-63.sentence: The legal split is already an enactment: the prison must treat “psychiatric” illness, but substance use is left as crime, not care. So opioid or alcohol treatment is not a constitutional right the way Estelle-style medical care is; programs often include it, but the court never required it.
