2013-64.sentence: Pramipexole dumps dopamine into the seeking system and the casino becomes the dumped-in object: greed lives outside him, not as a thought. The spouse is doing the depressive work—seeing the wreckage—while he stays in a paranoid-schizoid binge of luck and loss.

2013-65.sentence: A small, apt disclosure lets the patient meet a mixed human object instead of a blank screen or a twin who “has been there too.” You are modeling how a good-enough other survives feeling, which is what builds alliance—not credentials, politics, or shared faith.

2013-66.sentence: Neurofibrillary tangles mean tau (and mixed Alzheimer-type) pathology in progressive supranuclear palsy and often in dementia with Lewy bodies—this mind is losing hardware. Uncovering fantasy will not clear tangles; you support orientation, motor risk, and antipsychotic sensitivity, not insight.

2013-67.sentence: Schizophrenia here is not only a broken mind; it is a two-person field collapsing, as the family becomes the last audience while the patient starts relating to cars, the television, and unseen others instead of them. Those flapping, waving arms are the body joining the same withdrawal: movement that no longer answers another person.

2013-68.sentence: Ankle clonus plus hyperreflexia without rigidity is serotonin syndrome talking through the cord after citalopram 40 mg met bedtime trazodone; the gut, fever, and nystagmus are the same storm, not NMS. Lorazepam is not the 'antidote story'—it quiets the agitation while you stop both serotonergic drugs and wait for the body to stop firing.

2013-69.sentence: A melatonin agonist is useful in delayed sleep-wake phase because it names night for a clock that has slid later; the 'symptom' is the phase itself, not a failure to sleep once the night finally starts. Give it as a time cue, not as a knockout pill for nightmares, narcolepsy, night terrors, or restless legs.

2013-70.sentence: Separation anxiety is a collision: the wish to stay glued to the parent meets the demand to go to school, and the mind solves it by flooding with danger-to-family. Generalized anxiety is the usual roommate because that same prohibition against risk then spreads to grades, bodies, and the world.

2013-71.sentence: Back on the unit the smoke-free frame held clozapine levels; home cigarettes can feel like a selfobject, the thing that restores calm and competence after discharge. Hydrocarbons induce CYP1A2, so heavy smoking drops the clozapine that was holding the self together and the early paranoia is a pharmacokinetic insult, not 'the drug failed.

2013-72.sentence: In a patient over 65 on cardiac and pain meds, each new interaction is more raw stimulation the brain cannot metabolize into a clear plan. Bupropion’s advantage over SSRIs here is fewer drug–drug collisions, so you contain the depression without evacuating the problem into another pharmacokinetic mess.

2013-73.sentence: Caregiver alcohol abuse predicts elder abuse because the helper’s own limit has already failed: intoxication collapses the pause between rage and action. Time and sobriety cannot be rushed in that person, so you do not wait for “insight” before arranging a private safety interview.

2013-74.sentence: Globus pallidus DBS is hardware for a motor circuit, not a comment the patient can use. Psychological mindedness starts after the twist lessens: can they notice what the dystonia was doing in the family, or do they only track voltage and pulse width?

2013-75.sentence: COPD, not pregnancy or cirrhosis, is the risk that should hold the ECT frame: you do not proceed until airway and recent exacerbations are known. The psychiatrist owns that limit even when the depression is screaming for a date on the schedule.

2013-76.sentence: The pill, the pediatric visit, the headache: each can function as a feed that keeps the child and parent glued together so school drop-off never has to happen. Name the medicine as optional so it does not become proof that only a body crisis justifies staying home.

2013-77.sentence: Buprenorphine’s ceiling on respiratory suppression lets you stop pretending methadone taper is equally “safe enough.” Denial here is the wish that all opioids are the same; the partial agonist is the fact that undoes that story.

2013-78.sentence: When a two-year-old feeds a stuffed animal from a toy cup, you and the parent may start narrating a whole inner life that is not yet there. That is an enactment: the adults are living a preschool script while the child is still just discovering that one thing can stand for another.

2013-79.sentence: In obstructive sleep apnea the airway keeps collapsing while the person stays “asleep,” so the fight for air never becomes a thought—only morning headache, night sweats, and falling asleep at the desk. That is a vertical split: the body leaves the room into hypoxia without the patient leaving the chair, so do not file the sleepiness under depression or hygiene until you have asked about snoring, pauses, and unrefreshing sleep.

2013-80.sentence: The binge-purge cycle in bulimia often props up a self that cannot borrow steadiness from another person; fluoxetine plus CBT is the combination that has actually been studied, not oxcarbazepine, ondansetron, or bupropion (which you avoid because of seizure risk). Fluoxetine does not “cure willpower”; it can quiet the drive enough that the patient can use the therapist as a mirror and rebuild competence without needing the purge to restore self-esteem.

2013-81.sentence: A brief, discussable hug after a death is a boundary crossing: the wish to soothe and be soothed collides with the rule that we do not touch, and you let both sides of that conflict stay in the room. It is not a boundary violation (exploitation) and not an enactment you hide; name the hug in the next session so the drive does not get acted again instead of thought.

2013-82.sentence: Cervical myelopathy—neck stiffness, limb weakness, brisk reflexes, clonus, upgoing toes, incontinence—does not wait for the depression to lift or the meds to be “optimized.” Ending and limits live in the cord here: some capacities cannot be rushed or interpreted away, so falls and new urgency on the unit are a stop sign, not more psychomotor retardation.

2013-83.sentence: Craving after alcohol withdrawal is raw stuff that wants to be evacuated into a drink; naltrexone blocks the opioid reward so the urge can sit in the session long enough to become a sentence instead of a relapse. Therapy contains the feeling; naltrexone is the pharmacologic container—not disulfiram’s punishment, not lorazepam’s short-term hush, not ondansetron’s maybe.

2013-84.sentence: The lithium frame is yours even when primary care writes the thiazide: that diuretic raises lithium and can turn a stable older bipolar patient into tremor, dystonia, hyperreflexia, ataxia, and confusion. Ethics here is who holds the limit—you check the new antihypertensive before you rewrite the mood story.

2013-85.sentence: Isolated erotomania sits in delusional disorder, so a trial comment about longing or status will not land as metaphor; the patient treats coded interviews as evidence, not as a wish they can look at. Psychological mindedness is exactly what is missing: they cannot see their own part in constructing the romance, only the other person’s alleged love.

2013-86.sentence: Wanting off fluoxetine the moment sildenafil tames the sexual side effect is often denial: the third episode is treated as if it never happened. Keep the fluoxetine while it works; the defense is against needing a maintenance drug, not against the orgasm delay itself.

2013-87.sentence: Topiramate is a quieting feed: it clamps voltage-gated sodium channels, blocks kainate at AMPA, and potentiates GABA-A so the brain is less allowed to fire. In the relationship, the pill can feel like a demand to be smaller—calmer seizures, flatter words, less appetite—proof that control has to come from outside.

2013-88.sentence: After long deprivation, Stage 4 non-REM (deep slow-wave sleep) is the vertical split that restores: the person stays in the bed while the cortex drops into delta and leaves ordinary awareness. REM will wait; the organism first pays the debt of being gone without being gone.

2013-89.sentence: Skipping a power analysis is already an enactment: the team repeats a wish that the psychotherapy module will “show itself” without recruiting enough patients to see a defined effect. Name the two-person pattern—hope plus avoidance of variance, alpha, and sample size—before you randomize.

2013-90.sentence: In acute refeeding for severe anorexia nervosa, starvation is an unrepresented state: hunger, fear, and control live in the body and cannot yet be remembered as a story. Coaching, support, and reinforcement at the meal are the first language; interpretation of family or core beliefs comes after the soma can stay in the room.

2013-91.sentence: The cocaine crash is a drive collision in miniature: the wish for more dopamine rush keeps firing after the drug is gone, and the prohibition is not moral so much as biological—the depleted reward system simply cannot pay the bill. Fatigue, hypersomnia, and low mood are the wish collapsing into its opposite once the stimulant no longer props it up.

2013-92.sentence: A superior homonymous quadrantanopia is Meyer’s loop speaking: temporal optic radiations carry the upper-field fibers, so a temporal lesion punches a “pie-in-the-sky” hole. The symptom is not vague “brain damage”; it is a map of which fibers left the lateral geniculate and looped through temporal white matter.

2013-93.sentence: Hyperactivity is the piece that most often quiets with age, and that can recruit you into a false transference of “this kid grew out of it.” Your countertransference—relief that they sit still—can hide that impulsivity and inattention are still asking you to be the external brake they never fully internalized.

2013-94.sentence: Dusky competence is not “sounds lawyerly.” The defendant must consult counsel with a rational understanding and hold a factual and rational grasp of the proceedings. A delusion that the judge is an alien agent can leave vocabulary intact while the belief itself is doing the work of making the courtroom unusable as a real legal space.

2013-95.sentence: Long-term nursing-home care sits at a late developmental stage—chronic dependency after independence fails—and U.S. funding never quite grew a dedicated adult payer for that stage. Medicaid becomes the last-resort parent; Medicare covers the earlier, time-limited rehab chapter, not years of custodial care.

2013-96.sentence: Dialysis dementia (historical aluminum encephalopathy) is the toxin doing the thinking: progressive confusion, memory loss, and seizures after years of dialysis, with a bland exam and empty labs. Do not assign the decline to conversion, dissociation, or depression when the syndrome is the old dialysate metal writing itself on cortex.

2013-97.sentence: This sits on identity vs role confusion: the mind can split off unbearable pieces of self so they never have to be owned as one continuous “I.” High hypnotizability is the same talent for absorption that lets dissociative disorder park memory and feeling offstage when identity cannot hold them together.

2013-98.sentence: The MAOI–fava-bean rule is an object-relations problem in food form: tyramine is the “bad object” that cannot be held safely once MAO is blocked. Teach the patient that fava beans (and other high-tyramine foods) are not a moral failing of appetite; they are a concrete split you keep out of the relationship so the antidepressant can stay a good object.

2013-99.sentence: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome after repeated IM haloperidol dumps raw danger into the body—rigidity, 101.6°F, CK 4000—as if the mind cannot think the threat and so the soma must. Diuresis (and anticoagulation when indicated) is repair in the Kleinian sense: you do not attack the wrecked body further; you flush myoglobin risk and clot risk so the damaged self can be mended rather than evacuated.

2013-100.sentence: Child abuse is the moment you stop being a private container and become a public one: the raw terror cannot stay inside the usual confidentiality frame. You metabolize nameless dread into a report—words, a duty, a safety plan—so the adolescent is not left to evacuate the danger alone by going back to the same house.

2013-101.sentence: Primary process is the mind before the clock: unconscious thoughts that do not keep logical connections, so a supervisor can be a parent and a train at once. You cannot rush that material into secondary process; termination and the hour only work if you let illogic exist long enough to be named rather than tidied.

2013-102.sentence: Increased sleep fragmentation after 65 is a trial comment waiting to happen: can the patient see awakenings as their own physiology plus treatable extras, not as a failing will? Psychological mindedness here is noticing the night’s breaks without collapsing into “I am broken,” so you can still hunt pain, nocturia, and meds instead of only mourning youth.

2013-103.sentence: TADS sets the treatment frame: for moderate-to-severe adolescent depression you do not offer fluoxetine alone or CBT alone as if either were a complete contract. Combination therapy is the limit you hold—medication plus CBT—because half a frame leaves the family with an underpowered plan when school collapse and suicide risk are already in the room.

2013-104.sentence: The plea for a pill after cirrhosis can recruit you into a punitive rescuer—disulfiram as the ‘make it hurt so they stop’ object—or a magical one who will erase drinking with fluoxetine. Acamprosate is the less theatrical choice: you stay the physician who protects a damaged liver instead of acting out the patient’s disappointment as either punishment or a mood-drug shortcut.

2013-105.sentence: In DBT, ‘dialectical’ means holding two truths at once—this pain is real and this behavior cannot continue—and looking for a synthesis rather than picking a side. That is the opposite of an unrepresented split: what cannot be thought as both/and gets repeated as self-harm after rejection until someone helps the patient stand in the middle.

2013-106.sentence: Fluctuating arousal is the tell that the ego’s grip on wakefulness and attention is failing hour by hour, not that a slowly eroding Alzheimer network has simply gotten worse. Track that waxing and waning at the bedside; apraxia, poor short-term memory, even visual hallucinations can belong to either illness, but a consciousness that comes and goes is delirium until proven otherwise.

2013-107.sentence: School-age speed of learning rides on prefrontal cortical pruning: unused connections are cut so the remaining circuits can work with more precision. The child’s self still needs your mirroring of real competence—‘you can plan this homework’—because pruning is refinement, not a finished executive self, which is why impulse control still wobbles.

2013-108.sentence: Decentration is an ego gain: the child can now stand outside his own wishes and see two parents as separate people with their own conflict. That frees him from the old magical bargain—‘if I am good they stay’—so sadness and anger can be felt without being used as proof that he caused the divorce.

2013-109.sentence: Working memory is how you keep a needed other in mind when they are not in the room. D1 agonism aims at that holding function in prefrontal cortex; D2 blockade can quiet hallucinations and still leave the person without a secure cognitive base.

2013-110.sentence: Envy is the wish; the prohibition is that you must not be the envious one. Projection dumps the impulse on the sibling so the wish stays alive while the conscience stays clean.

2013-111.sentence: Do not treat ring-and-little-finger night paresthesias as a body memory of something unspeakable until you have ruled out a local nerve. Nerve conduction studies ask whether the ulnar nerve is actually injured at the elbow, not whether the dyad is repeating an old injury.

2013-112.sentence: Sex can recruit you into a transference story: this patient is a typical depressive, so bipolar is someone else's problem. Equal male and female rates in bipolar disorder are the reminder to stay the diagnostic clinician, not the character the gendered script wants.

2013-113.sentence: After you have helped produce NMS, the harsh conscience wants a brain-level atonement: more dopamine tinkering, more central heroics. Dantrolene's job is skeletal muscle relaxation, which is the unglamorous moral act of treating rigidity where it actually lives.

2013-114.sentence: Anaclitic depression is Spitz's name for what happens when a needed caregiver is suddenly gone and the infant's capacity to use that person has already formed. The collapse in feeding, sleep, and liveliness is a developmental achievement that then has nowhere to go.

2013-115.sentence: The “3” is already doing a job: it keeps some wish to change alive without forcing a full goodbye to alcohol. Asking why not a 1 pulls that leftover concern into words—liver, a relationship—so the patient hears their own reason instead of yours.

2013-116.sentence: Cyclosporine can steal the very self the transplant was meant to save: tremor, fear, and hallucinations smash the late-life task of integrity, the work of still feeling like one person. Name the drug early so the ward does not treat a toxic break as a failure of character or of the new kidney.

2013-117.sentence: The outbursts show up when a parent says “chores” or “no,” not with siblings, so the fight is a two-person signal, not a free-floating illness. Parent management training has the evidence because it changes the adult’s response—the actual arena—rather than medicating a child who can still play.

2013-118.sentence: Skipping BUN and creatinine before lithium is an enactment: you and the patient live out manic “we can ignore the body” instead of talking about risk. Checking the kidneys first is the frame that keeps the salt from becoming a shared dare.

2013-119.sentence: Covert sensitization pairs the hot fantasy with an aversive fantasy so the mind supplies its own punishment without a shock box. That is a planned use of undoing: the person rehearses spoiling the urge in imagination so they do not have to act it out.

2013-120.sentence: The family dumps nameless dread into a normal head CT and wants you to turn it into “the brain is fine.” Negative predictive value is the containing thought: how much residual danger remains after a negative scan in an 80-year-old with sudden seizures, hallucinations, and aggression.

2013-121.sentence: NMDA opening will not happen on glutamate alone; glycine has to occupy the co-agonist site before the channel will work. D-cycloserine is a glycine-site partial agonist, so the lesson is a hard limit: you cannot rush plasticity by flooding one ligand when the receptor still needs its second key.

2013-122.sentence: The coffee-shop job holds two wishes at once: to become the physician the parents already named, and to refuse that career without having to say no. Identity is the task because the depression is the collision of those wishes, not a failure of intimacy or of later generativity.

2013-123.sentence: Phenytoin can steal the body the patient uses to feel intact: gingival hypertrophy, hirsutism, and cerebellar ataxia are not just side effects, they are daily insults to appearance and competence. The seizure drug that should restore control also unmirrors him, so follow-up has to name the self-esteem hit, not only the nystagmus.

2013-124.sentence: Clomipramine is the most serotonergic TCA and still the pharmacologic standard when OCD washing will not yield. You will be recruited as the one who finally sanitizes the world or as the one who dares leave dirt on the hands; that pull is countertransference, and it is data, not a reason to skip the drug.

2013-125.sentence: The five-mile radius is the fear living in the body because it never became a memory that could be told. Exposure CBT is the treatment that asks the unrepresented panic to happen in graded drives rather than only in the locked-down map of home.

2013-126.sentence: Intellectual disability is the most frequent comorbidity in autism because a large share of these children never quite get the cognitive equipment that later skills assume. Limited speech is not the IQ; adaptive testing still has to ask which capacities arrived, arrived late, or did not arrive.

2013-127.sentence: A positive serum VDRL is a screen, not a verdict, and conscience here means you do not authorize penicillin desensitization until you know whether the brain is involved. The next sanctioned step is cerebrospinal fluid FTA-ABS: confirm neurosyphilis before you override an allergy or start a dangerous drug.

2013-128.sentence: Eighteen sits on identity versus role confusion, and phencyclidine (PCP) blows that task apart: clouded sensorium, labile euphoria, and vertical nystagmus mark a self that cannot hold still. The nystagmus is the bedside signature that this is PCP, not LSD or MDMA playing at identity.

2013-129.sentence: The Lewy body on that biopsy is not decoration; it is the symptom’s name, an alpha-synuclein inclusion that turns a vague decline into Parkinson disease. What the finding does for the workup is stop you from calling it Alzheimer, Huntington, or ALS when the inclusion already chose the diagnosis.

2013-130.sentence: Declarative memory is the capacity to look back and say what happened today; recalling daily events is that trial comment made to oneself. Priming, skills, and classical conditioning can run on without insight; the day’s story cannot.

2013-131.sentence: School-age grief has a clock you cannot rush: intense crying and questions about the death are work, not pathology. Unresolved grief shows as a limit that will not close—clinging to parents in separation anxiety or a lasting freeze-out of peers.

2013-132.sentence: On a monoamine oxidase inhibitor, fentanyl is not comfort; it is a poison the relationship can deliver if you treat the pill as mere analgesia. Phenelzine plus fentanyl can kill, so the prescription itself becomes the demand you must refuse.

2013-133.sentence: The first limit you hold is medical reality, not the consulting-room hour: referral for further medical evaluation comes before psychoanalysis, a splash of haloperidol, supportive ego-bolstering, or CBT for “cognitive errors.” Confidentiality of the cancer fear does not cancel the duty to work up reflux and indigestion as possible gastric disease.

2013-134.sentence: Cade lifted lithium from a gout-and-uric-acid story and put it in mania; teams still replay that origin by treating the salt as a leftover instead of the prototypical stabilizer. That is an enactment: attending and resident live the “old drug, not a real treatment” script rather than naming lithium.

2013-135.sentence: The crack-house is a conditioned stimulus; classical conditioning rings craving before the ego can vote. Walking another block is suppression—pushing the urge aside on purpose—and it fails at the doorway because Pavlov already owns the street.

2013-136.sentence: In the emergency department, ego strength starts as safety, so affect can be tolerated without flooding and reality testing can come back online. Psychosocial interventions that establish safety from further trauma do that work; benzodiazepines, a same-day SSRI, single-session EMDR, and group debriefing do not.

2013-137.sentence: Lithium’s anti-suicide effect is independent of mood leveling; it keeps the lethal self from driving while the rest of the person is still in the chair. Dissociation is a vertical split—the person leaves without leaving—and lithium is the stabilizer that stitches those sides together better than lamotrigine, valproate, olanzapine, or oxcarbazepine.

2013-138.sentence: The handshake at the synapse is two-sided: nerve releases acetylcholine and muscle must receive it. Antibodies against acetylcholine receptors break that meeting, so fatigable weakness is a failed relationship at the receptor, not an attack on myofibrils or voltage-gated calcium channels.

2013-139.sentence: Emergency intramuscular medication is a last-ditch use of staff as a regulating other when the patient’s attachment system has collapsed into fight and no words or proximity can settle him. Documenting imminent danger is what keeps that hold from becoming a takeover: you are saying the body cannot be left unheld, not that psychosis alone voids consent.

2013-140.sentence: Lithium is both poison and feed here: Ebstein-risk chemistry that has also been the only object that kept her from catastrophic relapse. After neuroleptic malignant syndrome she treats antipsychotics as an attempted killing, so staying with lithium is staying with the known, survivable relationship rather than switching to valproate or carbamazepine, which are worse fetal toxins, or to lamotrigine, which has not held her mania.

2013-141.sentence: She parks the terror in her ex-husband—that is projection, putting an inner change onto someone outside—while she still knows the story “sounds crazy.” New replacement of objects, insomnia, and work decline need a medical and neurologic workup first; interpreting the projection as the diagnosis would miss an organic process announcing itself as Capgras-like certainty.

2013-142.sentence: Latency lines up with industry versus inferiority: the school-age child’s job is competence, and the 8-year-old’s falling self-esteem is already an enactment in which adults keep proving he cannot do the work. If the evaluation only catalogues deficits, the clinic joins the same two-person script instead of naming skills, effort, and what still works.

2013-143.sentence: Fatigable ptosis, esotropia, and diplopia after two minutes of upgaze are the neuromuscular junction failing in real time, not conversion and not “sleepiness.” The edrophonium test briefly boosts acetylcholine at that junction; a positive response names myasthenia before you chase a thoracic CT for thymoma.

2013-144.sentence: Reality testing and role functioning are still standing—he is in class, with family, in organized sport—so the ego’s crack is impulse control and affect tolerance, not a first mania or PCP break. Exogenous anabolic steroids punch that hole: more gym, more irritability, threats, without needing a new personality story.

2013-145.sentence: Higher CYP3A4 activity in many African American patients is not a personality trait; it is a metabolic fact that can make a prescribed 3A4 substrate vanish faster than you expected. Think of the enzyme as a noisy attachment figure: if you do not stay close enough to check levels, response, and the inhibitor/inducer list, the treatment relationship loses its secure base and the patient protests with relapse or “nonadherence.”

2013-146.sentence: Subacute spongiform encephalopathy (prion disease) shows up as a two-person emergency: startle myoclonus, ataxia, and a collapsing EEG force you and the family into the same startled, inattentive field. Do not treat the dyad as if one mind were merely “confused”; name the shared pattern—rapid decline plus unrevealing CT/CSF—so the work stays neurologic rather than becoming an argument about cooperation.

2013-147.sentence: Group work can use more therapist transparency and self-disclosure because the here-and-now already has many observers; a brief, real statement can support members who cannot yet use deep uncovering. Keep self-disclosure as technique, not confession: enough presence to regulate the room, not so much that you steal the hour from exploring what the late arrival is doing to the group.

2013-148.sentence: CBC monitoring on clozapine is about neutrophils, not hemoglobin theater; agranulocytosis is the medical fact that will recruit you into the role of either a reckless parent or a jailer. Watch your countertransference: if you skip a required ANC because the patient “looks fine,” you have become the figure who denies danger rather than the one who holds the frame.

2013-149.sentence: Ropinirole, a dopamine agonist, can drop sudden sleep attacks into a body that cannot narrate the change—family reports the near-miss because the patient may not represent it as a medication effect. Treat the unremembered nap at the wheel as a repeated state, not a character flaw: ask what started when the agonist started, then take the keys until the body can stay awake.

2013-150.sentence: An effectiveness trial asks whether a new atypical works in the messy clinic, not whether a handpicked sample can show a clean signal. Psychological mindedness here is the researcher’s: can they see their own wish for a pretty efficacy design and still choose the design that includes comorbidity, missed doses, and ordinary follow-up?

2013-151.sentence: Consent is the frame’s hard stop: you cannot discuss the spouse’s medication questions until the patient authorizes it, no matter how worried the caller sounds. Time and confidentiality cannot be rushed; the first sentence is that you need the patient’s permission, not an invitation to explain the change.

2013-152.sentence: Lewy body dementia dumps raw, unmetabolized experience into the room—fluctuating attention, visual hallucinations, parkinsonism, and antipsychotic EPS sensitivity—before the mind can bind it into a story. Containing means naming that cluster so staff stop evacuating the terror with more neuroleptic and can think about the syndrome instead.

2013-153.sentence: Delirium tremens shreds the self’s usual scaffolding: orientation, skin integrity, and a competent body all fail at once, so insects on the skin and 200/132 blood pressure are not metaphors. The mirroring job is medical first—hold the person together with benzodiazepines and fluids—because you cannot restore self-esteem until the self can stay in one place.

2013-154.sentence: If you treat twenty-five-year sadness about a child who died of leukemia as pathology, you and the system are enacting a demand that grief finish on schedule. The living pattern is the pressure to call function-preserving, sleep-intact mourning “complicated” instead of letting it remain a durable bond.

2013-155.sentence: Mirtazapine’s alpha-2 blockade is the opposite of repression: it lifts the presynaptic brake so norepinephrine and serotonin can come into awareness rather than stay locked downstream. You are not blocking reuptake; you are undoing the autoinhibitory “don’t feel that yet” signal.

2013-156.sentence: After the snake, the hike itself becomes a poison-pill: exposure is not help, it is proof that danger is coming. Specific phobia is the relationship to the cue—cling to the parents, refuse the trail—not a demand for a systemic treatment of “anxiety.”

2013-157.sentence: The limit you hold is the cannabis history itself: age at first use, how often, and whether it preceded the psychosis—not a polite skip because the teenager (or the family) treats it as ordinary. Confidentiality covers the chart, not the fact; you still name cannabis as the adolescent exposure tied to later schizophrenia.

2013-158.sentence: Looking down on purpose is a late-arriving skill; in progressive supranuclear palsy that voluntary vertical gaze drops out while the older doll's-head reflex still drives a full range. Early falls, rigidity, and no tremor mean the newer overlay failed—the brainstem hardware was never the missing piece, which is why the MRI can look unremarkable.

2013-159.sentence: Paradoxical insomnia is the night doing psychic work: the patient needs the story of under two hours even when latency is ten minutes, sleep lasts seven hours, and efficiency is 90%. The complaint is a misread of rest, not a factitious show for the lab, so you treat the conviction rather than a missing two hours.

2013-160.sentence: The tears are something to put into you; containment means you hold them—“this has been very difficult”—instead of tossing the pain back as who ended it or get back out there. Asking how they are coping tests whether depressive concern is available yet: can they bear the loss and still look after themselves.

2013-161.sentence: Acamprosate works on glutamate, quieting the excitatory rebound that keeps shouting for a drink after the last one is already gone. The tablet is not a character test; it damps leftover craving so the person can stay abstinent long enough for the talking treatment to land.

2013-162.sentence: Cocaine withdrawal can raise prolactin and cause galactorrhea with no antipsychotic and no seizure, so you do not dig for a hidden neuroleptic confession. Stay supportive and concrete: name the cocaine, finish the usual prolactin workup, and leave the milk uninterpreted until the chemistry is explained.

2013-163.sentence: The teacher-child pair can still hold a “good” version of this student: live explanation lands, and the IQ of 92 is not the problem. Achievement and adaptive scores drop once the work is asked of the child alone, so the learning disability is the split between competence inside a holding relationship and collapse when the page has to stand in for the teacher.

2013-164.sentence: Five years of methadone maintenance is a hard-won adult capacity: the opioid system finally stays regulated without daily chaos. Ciprofloxacin (a CYP3A4/1A2 inhibitor) takes that capacity away overnight, so the same dose becomes lethargy, obtundation, and respiratory depression—development reversed by one enzyme.

2013-165.sentence: Bitemporal hemianopia is the visual signature of a chiasmal hit, usually a pituitary mass squeezing the crossing nasal fibers. Central vision can still work, which is why the person keeps missing cars from both sides while looking “straight ahead”—the finding is a hole in the periphery, not blindness.

2013-166.sentence: Blood-injection-injury phobia sits on Erikson’s autonomy-versus-shame task: first the body revs (anxiety, blood pressure up), then it surrenders control. The second stage is hypotension—a vasovagal faint—so the needle is escaped by losing vascular autonomy rather than by fighting or fleeing.

2013-167.sentence: In bipolar illness after 65, the mixed episode does a job: it packs racing thoughts and agitation together with guilt and hopelessness so no one can treat “just mania” or “just depression.” The finding is more mixed episodes, not more clean manias or more substance comorbidity.

2013-168.sentence: Frontotemporal dementia knocks out the frontal brake, so a wish (cruel laughter, odd oral rules) no longer collides with a living prohibition—it just happens. The later contamination/food refusal is drive without a flexible conscience: germs become a concrete ban after memory is still intact and language and attention have already slipped.

2013-169.sentence: A resident’s competence can wobble when one antipsychotic is written in milligrams and another in hundreds, as if the bigger number were the “real” drug. Potency is only the relative dose needed for a given effect, so you restore self-esteem by saying milligram size is not efficacy—not by pretending the confusion never happens.

2013-170.sentence: The pair may already be in an enactment: intercourse has become a pass/fail test, she “fails” lubrication, and he presses for completion. Sensate focus breaks that two-person script by taking intercourse off the table so they stop living the old anxious pattern and can notice actual sensation.

2013-171.sentence: Humor here is a defense with extra mental room: the school-age child can hold two meanings at once, see the forbidden or silly second meaning, and laugh it into a safer form. Understanding double meanings in jokes is that new capacity; preschoolers still need language to stay more literal.

2013-172.sentence: You are not being a chauffeur; you stay in traffic until tachycardia and sweating fall so the ego can learn the fear wave is tolerable. Classical conditioning paired traffic with terror; remaining until that arousal fades rebuilds affect tolerance instead of letting avoidance run the day.

2013-173.sentence: A fetish can work like a vertical split: arousal is parked in a nonliving object so the person does not have to feel whole, mixed, human desire in the room. The object is concrete and controllable—that is dissociation dressed as lust, which is why fetishism is defined by that nonliving focus when it causes distress.

2013-174.sentence: A trial comment only lands after lorazepam 2 mg has brought the cocaine hyperarousal down enough that the adolescent can actually think. Psychological mindedness needs a cortex that is not flooded; you do not hunt insight while they are still tachycardic and scanning the room.

2013-175.sentence: Varicella zoster does not wait for insight: once it reactivates in a dorsal-root ganglion, the T4 band of vesicles is already a deadline, not a metaphor. Time is the limit here—antivirals help most in the first 72 hours, and lingering to “see how it evolves” is how postherpetic neuralgia gets a head start in a 75-year-old.

2013-176.sentence: After methylphenidate fails a real trial, offering dextroamphetamine is not a rejection of the child; it is another attempt to feed a nervous system that still cannot organize attention. Watch what the switch means in the family: some hear a better-fitting stimulant, others hear “you need a stronger pill,” which is a demand unless you say out loud why amphetamine is the next evidence-based step and not a verdict.

2013-177.sentence: Nonmaleficence is the frame that holds when a helpful impulse wants to outrun the risk: primum non nocere means the first job is not to add injury. Beneficence wants to treat; this principle is the brake that makes you name the harm, the interaction, and the safer option before you act.

2013-178.sentence: Fever, dystonia, tremor, and confusion after haloperidol can look like neuroleptic malignant syndrome, but the body also speaks infection—and you do not decide which story it is from the bedside alone. Cerebrospinal fluid evaluation is the limit you hold: skip the LP and you treat a syndrome while missing meningitis.

2013-179.sentence: Taijin kyofusho locates the danger in what leaks into the other person—gaze, face, odor—as if a bad part of the self will be put into them and injure them. That is projective identification in cultural clothing: the feared scene is not “I will be shamed,” but “I will contaminate you, and then I cannot repair it.”

2013-180.sentence: Supportive work stays in the present so you do not reenact the old scene of an unavailable adult disappearing into the patient’s childhood while the rent and the insomnia go unaddressed. Working primarily now is the technique: you sit in today’s crisis with the patient instead of becoming the next person who talks over it.

2013-181.sentence: Valproate does not step out of the room when you add lamotrigine. It stays and blocks glucuronidation, roughly doubling the level and the rash risk. A vertical split is treating the new tablet as if it lives in a different body from the divalproex already sitting there.

2013-182.sentence: Reading disorder is the most common learning or communication problem among children in special education, so the first ego job is staying with the page when a word will not decode. Affect tolerance here is holding the shame of that stall without calling the whole self stupid or tossing the book.

2013-183.sentence: Alcohol had been the secure base: proximity on demand, a chemical other that quieted tremor and fear. A typical benzodiazepine detox lasts three to five days so that stand-in can be withdrawn while the body protests the loss without seizing.

2013-184.sentence: Insight on this consult is seeing the monoparesis, not the fever and confusion everyone already named. West Nile can hit anterior horn cells; the flaccid weak limb is the trial comment that distinguishes it from garden-variety viral encephalitis.

2013-185.sentence: The frame is who holds the meaning: a professional interpreter, not a cultural spokesperson who closes the case. Nervios in Hispanic American communities names stress in the nerves; you still ask what this patient's nerves do, or confidentiality and curiosity both collapse into a group slogan.

2013-186.sentence: In major depression the clock from sleep onset to REM onset shortens; the dream gate opens too early. A medicine that lengthens that latency can feel like a feed that restores a night boundary, or like a demand that the body stop proving how depleted it is.

2013-187.sentence: Denial is at work when the scan’s story is treated as one more hypertensive event: the mind refuses the fact of recurrent cortical bleeds so the future stays simpler. Amyloid angiopathy names what denial is keeping out—lobar hemorrhages that will likely return, not a deep basal-ganglia stroke from years of high pressure.

2013-188.sentence: The pulmonary wish is to keep aminophylline on board; the mood wish is to keep lithium in range. Those aims collide because aminophylline (like theophylline) speeds lithium clearance, so the trough falls and the old mania or depression can walk back in.

2013-189.sentence: A WISC-IV full-scale IQ of 60 is only half of competence; self-esteem in this child lives in what they can actually do at home and school. The Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales, 2nd ed. (VABS-II) is the mirroring instrument: it asks caregivers whether daily function matches the low score before you call it intellectual disability.

2013-190.sentence: After a graft, the idealized body—the one that did not need a stranger’s organ—is gone, and self-esteem often crashes into guilt about depending on family and pills. That is why major depression, not PTSD or a brief psychosis, is the most common psychiatric illness after transplant: the self cannot yet feel like a whole person again.

2013-191.sentence: The wish is that ECT will wipe out emptiness, rage, and abandonment the way it can lift a melancholic episode. Borderline personality disorder is a negative predictor because the prohibition remains: the machine treats the major depression, not the characterologic storm that will still be there when the seizure is over.

2013-192.sentence: The fights are the couple’s way of repeating what they cannot yet put into words: how they already survive some hours without attacking. Solution-focused homework—“what are you doing differently when you are not arguing”—pulls that unrepresented stretch of peace into speech so they do not have to keep living it only as the next explosion.

2013-193.sentence: Once a preschooler can hold two minds at once, you stop being a mind-reader and become a person they can test, surprise, and recruit. The countertransference shift is the work: you feel less like a container of their thoughts and more like someone whose thoughts they are now tracking.

2013-194.sentence: Synesthesia after LSD is a sensory mash-up, not a moral verdict, but the conscience still wants a story: “I did something forbidden and now the world is broken.” Name the finding first so guilt does not turn a crossing of senses into a crime.

2013-195.sentence: Shooting is the most common completed method in the United States, so the developmental task is not abstract: the adult capacity to plan and obtain a firearm arrived, and it can be used against the self. Ask about access because that capacity is already there.

2013-196.sentence: Cisplatin’s distal sensory polyneuropathy can become a body-language for what chemo is doing to the self: the feet no longer report the floor, so the person feels unheld by their own body. The tingling is toxic, not symbolic first, but it can also say “I cannot stand on this treatment.”

2013-197.sentence: Conviction needs both actus reus, the act, and mens rea, the guilty mind; that is Erikson’s industry-versus-guilt problem in court. The work is to keep those two tasks separate so a psychotic hospital stay does not get collapsed into either automatic guilt or automatic excuse.

2013-198.sentence: ODD after “no” is often a fight over who gets to be the authority in the family, including whose class, gender, or parenting style counts as legitimate “no.” Ask whether the tantrum is only at home: that tells you if the child is opposing a particular adult identity, not the whole social world.

2013-199.sentence: Working memory is the bench where a thought, a person, and the next step stay in mind at once. When that bench fails in schizophrenia, fragments get shoved into you by projective identification—you are made to hold the thread they cannot, as if the split-off bits of mind were now your job.

2013-200.sentence: TCA blockade of cardiac fast sodium channels is a wish and a ban in the same beat: the pill that was supposed to quiet the mind also stalls the heart’s depolarization. A wide QRS is that collision made visible—desire for relief colliding with a prohibition so concrete the action potential itself cannot fire.

2013-201.sentence: At eleven, “best friend” means feeling cared about: care has to exist as a named fact, not only as recess or a group project. After trauma, that fact often never gets represented, so need is repeated in the body or dumped into the adult instead of being located in a peer who actually holds the child.

2013-202.sentence: Bilateral CA1 neuron loss—whether in mesial temporal epilepsy or Alzheimer dementia—takes out the historian who binds an episode into a story. You get recruited as the external hippocampus: holding sequence and names the patient cannot store, and the feeling in you is the pull to become their missing memory.

2013-203.sentence: Periodic limb movements punish from below awareness: the legs jerk, sleep fragments, and the waking self only owns the fatigue. That is a superego (the inner prosecutor) with no charge sheet—penalty without a thought the patient can confess.

2013-204.sentence: This adult never developed the capacity to weigh a greater-than-50% chance of right-arm paralysis against freedom from seizures, so a guardian’s insistence cannot stand in for a mind that did not arrive. Court order is the frame when someone else is choosing a disabling resection the patient cannot authorize.

2013-205.sentence: Percent carbohydrate-deficient transferrin (CDT) can do a job the interview cannot: it holds the fact of recent heavy drinking when shame makes the history shrink. Use it as a quiet third, not a gotcha, so the lab carries the truth long enough for you both to talk about withdrawal risk instead of arguing about ounces.

2013-206.sentence: At thirty-five the Erikson task is still intimacy versus isolation: staying through the night with another person, not just surviving the day. Cluster headache yanks the patient out of sleep with unilateral orbital pain, lacrimation, and rhinorrhea, so the body keeps breaking the pair just when closeness is supposed to hold.

2013-207.sentence: A self-report form such as the Beck Anxiety Inventory or the Taylor Manifest Anxiety Scale lets the patient name somatic fear in their own words instead of performing it for a rater. That is the meaning of the instrument: it gives anxiety a place to sit on paper so it does not have to live only in the exam room.

2013-208.sentence: Raynaud disease leaves the fingers cold, white, then blue—as if the bad, lifeless bit of the body has been split off and abandoned at the periphery. Thermal biofeedback asks for a depressive-position repair: the patient practices bringing warmth back into what was treated as dead tissue, rather than cutting it away with sympathectomy or clamping vessels with propranolol.

2013-209.sentence: This sixteen-year-old can still hold a whole object: shy interest in real classmates plus an hour every few weeks with images of women and heterosexual sex. The websites are a part-object rehearsal, not a split into “good friends versus deviant sexuality,” so the curiosity itself is not abuse, addiction, or orientation confusion.

2013-210.sentence: Those five-minute orbital stabs with rhinorrhea and red conjunctivae are paroxysmal hemicrania: raw pain dumped into the face before it can be thought. Indomethacin is the container here—it stops the evacuation so the attack becomes a diagnosable, treatable event instead of nameless dread behind the eye.

2013-211.sentence: Those missing-time splices and the hostile calls she cannot own mark a self that cannot stay in one continuous hour; integration is a capacity that will not be rushed by a new marriage or by your wish for a single narrator. Treat the gaps as a hard limit: you work with whoever is in the room today, and you do not demand that one person remember the old girlfriend’s voicemails before the work has earned that continuity.

2013-212.sentence: Compliance rises when someone can take in a trial comment and see their own part—panic about the kidneys, not “being difficult”—instead of only fighting the diuretic. A good C-L service is psychological-mindedness on the ward: one usable interpretation of the refusal, then the medicine actually gets taken.

2013-213.sentence: The frame here is who holds the limit on suffering: the typical “bad death” fear is dying in pain, not the hospital, delirium, or unfinished life review. Your ethical job is to name that fear plainly and keep analgesia and honesty in the room rather than outsourcing the end to vague reassurance.

2013-214.sentence: Asterixis plus high ammonia is recruiting you to become the interpreter of a “confused personality,” and your countertransference may be to argue with her or to feel useless. Bilateral triphasic waves say the opposite: this is a liver-brain storm, not a transference you should analyze until the ammonia comes down.

2013-215.sentence: School age is Erikson’s industry versus inferiority: the child is building personal worth through competence at reading, games, and making things work. “I am stupid” is that stage speaking; the developmental task is a real skill that can be mastered, not more parental love or a premature identity crisis.

2013-216.sentence: Sensitization is the conflict written into the reflex: the wish to stay safe collides with a nervous system that now treats a subthreshold twinge as the original harm. The startle is not “irrational fear” in the everyday sense; it is a learned overshoot in which even a whisper of sensation is forbidden to be ordinary.

2013-217.sentence: Stopping lamotrigine and going to emergency care is also a selfobject function: you hold the patient’s worth by treating a facial rash plus sore throat and fever as SJS/TEN until proven otherwise, not as a nuisance to be waited out. Dose holds, diphenhydramine, and a dermatology callback all say “we can still titrate you”; the emergency stop says your body is not expendable for mood stability.

2013-218.sentence: Goldwater sits on Erikson’s identity vs. role confusion: a psychiatrist who never examined the entertainer still claims “alcohol abuse,” as if a public role were enough to name a person. The ethical move is to refuse that shortcut so identity stays something earned in an exam, not conferred by a news desk.

2013-219.sentence: Pramipexole as first-line RLS treatment names the urge as a dopamine-circuit symptom, not a character flaw of restlessness. The walk that briefly relieves evening legs is the body trying to complete a motor loop; the dopamine agonist does that job so the person does not have to pace all night to feel whole.

2013-220.sentence: The abdomen as the typical injury site in pregnant partner violence is a fact that can open insight: the blow is aimed at the pregnancy, not “just another argument bruise.” A trial comment after you see her alone—“it looks like the baby was the target”—tests whether she can use that observation without you diagnosing her partner from the hallway.

2013-221.sentence: Arbitrary inference is concluding with no evidence or against the evidence, and you cannot rush the patient past that habit by arguing the conclusion. The limit is time plus capacity: stay with the missing data until they can tolerate not-knowing, rather than filling the gap with a finished story.

2013-222.sentence: Increased ECT-induced frontal delta activity as a correlate of response is the treatment writing itself on the EEG, not a personality trait proving you “needed” shock. The seizure is not poison or proof of damage; the frontal slowing is the relationship’s measurable feed that the brain took the dose.

2013-223.sentence: The 13-year-old who asks the same morning questions is asking you to hold the clock and the story, not to become another parent who answers forever. Anxiety is the usual partner of ASD, so you keep confidentiality while you still call school about bullying—the child is not the only informant, and you do not hand the limit to whoever is loudest.

2013-224.sentence: The emergency bay can already be in an enactment: staff treat the obese 26-year-old’s headache as noise while the swollen discs are the finding. Idiopathic intracranial hypertension is that two-person pattern—dismiss her body, miss the raised pressure, and risk her vision.

2013-225.sentence: Pinning every surge on coffee or a bad thought is rationalization: the ego invents a cause so the attack is not random. Panic disorder still needs at least some unprovoked attacks that peak in minutes; if a neat trigger covers every episode, you are watching a defense, not the diagnosis.

2013-226.sentence: Speech in the ICU is not ego strength: he can answer a simple question and still cannot hold the facts or the affect of prolonged ventilation. A living will or a durable power of attorney carries the wish when reality testing fails; a DNR or DNI slip is a later order, not the paper that tells the team what he already decided.

2013-227.sentence: Lifelong rapid ejaculation can be a vertical split: the genitals finish while the person has already left the bed without standing up. Paroxetine is the antidepressant most likely to delay that reflex, buying seconds so he can stay in the act instead of climaxing and vanishing.

2013-228.sentence: Anti-Yo means Purkinje cells are dying, so gait and limb coordination—a skill that once arrived—falls apart in weeks. Order CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis next; the antibody points to an occult cancer undoing that cerebellar capacity, not to serial antibody titers.

2013-229.sentence: Looking to the partner before speaking is not politeness; it is the symptom doing work—keeping the room safe by not naming the threat. Private, concrete questions about domestic violence take that job off the patient’s mouth so the couple’s story cannot keep the violence hidden.

2013-230.sentence: A securely attached toddler seeks contact eagerly because the parent is still a usable base, not a source of poison or demand. Reunion is the “dose”: proximity is taken in, distress metabolizes, and play can start again.

2013-231.sentence: Calling it hypochondriasis first is a defense: denial of the body so nobody has to sit with a real lesion. The most important differential is a medical condition, because ruling that out is what keeps the consult from becoming a shared wish that the abdomen is “only” in the mind.

2013-232.sentence: The apnea test is not a metaphor; it is the limit that says the brainstem no longer drives breathing. Families and teams need that named finding so grief is not asked to do the work of a neurologic exam.

2013-233.sentence: Derealization is the attack doing a job: the room goes unreal so the surge of fear does not have to be fully inhabited. Ask whether it is recognized as an odd inner state; if it is held as fact, you are no longer in a panic attack.

2013-234.sentence: Nitrous oxide lets the dentist evacuate what cannot be thought—numbness of limb standing in for a feeling that never got a name. The neuropathy is the leftover of that evacuation: the body keeps the uncontained bits after the gas has done its brief containing.

2013-235.sentence: Isolation of affect, intellectualization, and reaction formation keep feeling off the table so the hour stays a problem to solve rather than a relationship that will end. Suitability for uncovering therapy is limited until time, fees, and termination can be felt as losses, not just procedures.

2013-236.sentence: Compulsive sexual behavior is a drive collision: the erotic wish and the prohibition keep repeating as acting instead of as conflict you can talk about. Twelve-step groups hold both sides at once—the craving and the rule—better than diving into psychodynamic work before the enactment is contained.

2013-237.sentence: Peek-a-boo works because object permanence lets the infant keep a picture of the caregiver when the face vanishes. That returning, delighted gaze is early mirroring: the self stays coherent because the other is expected to come back, not gone forever.

2013-238.sentence: When one member names hopelessness and suicide and another immediately feels the same, that is contagion: the suicidal state has jumped bodies instead of staying named as one person's pain. Universalization can still be useful—you are not the only one—but the work is to hold the shared bad feeling without inviting a comparison of methods.

2013-239.sentence: After two failed antipsychotics, the psychosis is still being put into everyone around the patient; that is projective identification: unwanted fragments live in staff and family instead of in the patient's mind. Clozapine is the drug that can shrink that unheld psychosis enough for depressive concern—worry about the damage—to even become possible.

2013-240.sentence: Slurred speech, nystagmus, ataxia, and hypoactive reflexes mean inhalants have soaked the cerebellum and cortex; this is not a night for uncovering motives. Stabilize first, ask about aerosols and solvents, and keep the technique supportive until the brain can use more than a quiet room.

2013-241.sentence: Atenolol is the least interpersonal landmine here: it does not recruit the old pair of “my body is failing and you keep giving me something that makes me worse,” the way reserpine or methyldopa can revive depression or hydrochlorothiazide can drop sodium again. You and the patient are choosing a blood-pressure drug that will not restage lethargy as proof that treatment is dangerous.

2013-242.sentence: A mid-chest band, leg numbness, and new incontinence are the nervous system screaming for a secure base: get the MRI of the spine before you soothe anyone with “we’ll watch it.” Attachment work here is proximity to the right scanner, not waiting until the sphincter protest is complete.

2013-243.sentence: Schizotypal personality already shows the same thin ego functions that fail in schizophrenia: reality testing is leaky enough for odd beliefs and unusual percepts, but not shattered. That family history is the heritable marker that those particular ego muscles—reality testing and the stimulus barrier—run thin in this pedigree.

2013-244.sentence: This sits on Erikson’s first task, trust versus mistrust: hostility is often the last available protest when the room already feels unsafe. Name and validate the affect first so the patient can feel met rather than managed; logic, threats, or a needle only confirm the mistrust.

2013-245.sentence: Content validity is the instrument’s theory of the illness: skip depressed mood and you have already written a different disorder. Spending-spree items smuggle in a manic object, so the form measures another conflict than the one it claims to name.

2013-246.sentence: The psych consult is projective identification: the team parks fever, weight loss, ataxia, and months of memory loss in “depression” so they do not have to hold HIV. Depressive concern is ordering the HIV test and staying with what it means, not splitting the body off as a mood case.

2013-247.sentence: The “defect” is a split-off bad object parked on one feature so the rest of the self can stay clean and lovable. Fluoxetine can quiet the checking enough that the patient can start to see the face as a relationship problem, not a surgical one.

2013-248.sentence: Cape-like loss of pain and temperature will recruit you to become the skeptic who calls it functional and walks away. Syringomyelia is the central-cord lesion that explains that pattern; naming it keeps you from living out the dismissive doctor they already expect.

2013-249.sentence: Your training-superego — the inner examiner — will demand a quick major-depression label and a prescription before you have asked what the illness means. Inquiring what the patient believes explains the symptoms is how you keep conscience from turning into a rigid Western script.

2013-250.sentence: The flattery is projective identification: she lodges an idealized erotic self in you, and you start to feel special as if the fantasy were about your actual person. Consultation is the repair move — you take the projection back instead of acting from that mutual glow.

2013-251.sentence: The dance-night “ecstasy” story is already a cultural third: belonging and risk sit in the room before the labs do. MDMA still hits serotonin neurons; do not let the club identity (“just a party drug”) erase that specific toxicity.

2013-252.sentence: This is an industry-versus-inferiority problem: you either know what the liver does to an oral dose or you guess. First-pass effect is presystemic elimination — gut wall and liver strip drug before it reaches the rest of the body — so a route change is a competence move, not a hunch.

2013-253.sentence: Valproate is doing two jobs at once: it holds the mother's bipolarity and it quietly writes risk onto the fetal neural tube. Naming that conflict early lets the wish for stability stay in the room without pretending the fetus is not already in the bargain.

2013-254.sentence: The feared object tells you which developmental task never quite arrived: being seen by others versus being trapped without an exit. Social anxiety is a later-arriving self-in-the-gaze problem; agoraphobia is a panic-of-no-escape problem, even if both people avoid the same store.

2013-255.sentence: Maturation of the prefrontal cortex is how the inner brake grows: the adolescent slowly gets a cortex that can say no before the body already said yes. Think of it as a late-arriving conscience-hardware, still patchy when peers light up the reward system.

2013-256.sentence: When you ask how an apple and an orange are alike, you are recruiting yourself as the one who decides whether the mind can leave the concrete surface. A concrete answer can pull you into irritation or over-teaching; that feeling is countertransference to a mind that cannot yet join you in the category.

2013-257.sentence: Conduct disorder on top of ADHD is not extra fidgeting; it is aggression that has never been remembered as pain and so keeps getting enacted as fighting, theft, and rule-breaking. The worse adult prognosis is the unrepresented injury repeating in the body and the relationship instead of becoming a story.

2013-258.sentence: Drink-refusal skills and emergency plans in CBT are a structured fight with the wish to drink colliding with the prohibition against it. You are teaching the patient to meet that drive at the bar door instead of discovering the conflict only after the first sip.

2013-259.sentence: Caregivers keep a self together by feeling useful and competent, not by being forced into one heroic person or an even split. Your job is to shore up that competence—who can dose meds, who can give respite, what actually calms agitation—so the family’s work actually improves the patient’s care.

2013-260.sentence: A cluster attack already has a clock: about forty minutes, then it ends whether anyone is ready or not. High-flow oxygen is the abortive that meets that limit now; dexamethasone and topiramate belong later, as if you tried to rush a termination that is not this hour’s job.

2013-261.sentence: A prior suicide attempt is the fact you have to hold, not a feeling you can talk away into “hopelessness” or family history. Contain it—keep the raw dread thinkable—by asking method, intent, rescue, and what treatment followed, instead of evacuating the risk into a softer predictor.

2013-262.sentence: Adult partner violence is not a mandated police report the way child abuse is, so you do not seize the frame by calling the cops or ordering him to leave tonight. You hold the limit by listening and mapping safety, threats, and what he wants next—without blaming him or pretending this is rare in gay relationships.

2013-263.sentence: Waxing and waning alertness after sertraline is not “deeper depression” the patient needs insight into; it is delirium until proven otherwise. Check serum electrolytes first, because an SSRI in a 65-year-old often means SIADH hyponatremia, and a sertraline level or DST will not name that.

2013-264.sentence: The hated boss in his head was an unrepresented state: a felt “mean” figure with no room for another mind. Mentalization is noticing the gap—the real voice in the office versus the one inside—so the old scene is no longer only repeated as hatred.

2013-265.sentence: The anxious pulmonary patient will try to make you the instant soother—the one who hands over alprazolam, clonazepam, or propranolol so the dread drops now. Your countertransference is the urge to comply; naming that pull lets you stay the doctor who offers buspirone, a 5-HT1A agonist that calms without stealing respiratory drive.

2013-266.sentence: Left anterior cerebral artery infarction hits the medial frontal lobe and paracentral lobule, so the right leg fails while the hand and face are spared—and the self goes quiet. Abulia is a competence injury: this person needs you to mirror remaining agency, not to treat passivity as consent or as a personality.

2013-267.sentence: The forbidden tyramine bite is the wish; the MAOI diet is the prohibition; the hypertensive crisis is the collision as norepinephrine floods alpha receptors. Phentolamine, a parenteral alpha-blocker, is the brake on that surge—not dantrolene, bromocriptine, or a benzodiazepine standing in for the wrong emergency.

2013-268.sentence: Mild pediatric anxiety is doing a job: it keeps the child off the stage and recruits adults to remove the danger. Psychotherapy alone is first-line because the work is to find what the worry is protecting, not to start an SSRI or a benzodiazepine before that meaning has been heard.

2013-269.sentence: At forty-seven this mania sits on generativity versus stagnation: the wish to keep producing recovery by stacking lithium, divalproex, clonazepam, olanzapine, and bupropion. Lithium is the agent that most often turns ECT into delirium, so the adult task is to stop holding every drug and let one treatment work.

2013-270.sentence: The incapacitated patient dumps the unbearable decision into you—that is projective identification, putting a feeling into another person so they will carry it. Beneficence here is depressive concern, not omnipotence: seek a surrogate and treat in the patient’s interests rather than deciding alone from the paranoid-schizoid stance of “I know what is best.”

2013-271.sentence: Caudate atrophy is what boxes out the frontal horns, and it is also the lost brake on impulse and affect. Chorea and the new irritability are the same striatal failure showing up in muscle and in mood.

2013-272.sentence: CBT for panic leaves a method the patient can still run after termination: cue logs, interoceptive exposure, and walking back into avoided places. Pills do not install that skill, which is why relapse rises after they stop and CBT’s advantage appears at discontinuation.

2013-273.sentence: Selective mutism is avoidant behavior, not opposition or a language lesion: the child splits a safe home object from a dangerous school audience. Silence protects the speaking self rather than handing it to strangers who feel like bad objects.

2013-274.sentence: After 65 the vascular and autonomic scaffolding that once buffered a TCA’s alpha-1 blockade is thinner, so orthostatic hypotension and falls become the developmental risk. SSRIs are preferred not for stronger antidepressant force but because they ask less of a standing reflex that no longer arrives on time.

2013-275.sentence: Low-dose imipramine treats the pain–depression circuit instead of another workup that functions like a moral exam. The preferred act is not more investigation or an opioid; it is a TCA that can quiet both the abdomen and the self-attack that keeps the pain on trial.

2013-276.sentence: Laryngeal dystonia after a dopamine blocker is an airway emergency, not a symptom to interpret in the moment. Give intramuscular benztropine now; meaning waits until the patient can breathe.

2013-277.sentence: Duty is the piece that never formed: a lecture Q&A does not hire you as that family’s doctor, so your referral is information, not a treatment contract. The lawsuit still wants a parent-doctor, but malpractice needs an actual treating relationship before Deviation or Direct causation even get a vote.

2013-278.sentence: Heroin withdrawal (yawning, lacrimation, myalgias, diarrhea) smashes suppression—the ordinary “I can ride this out” lid—so suicidal talk rushes in as a bid to end the body-pain now. Treat the opioid withdrawal first; the death-wish often shrinks once the autonomic storm is named and medicated.

2013-279.sentence: You and the patient may already be living the posterior-column failure: both keep walking as if the floor is known while B12 deficiency has stolen vibration and position sense. That is an enactment—repeating “it’s just unsteadiness or aging” instead of checking the cord, the nerves, and the cognition together.

2013-280.sentence: This sits on industry versus inferiority: the young lawyer treats sufficient sleep as slacking on the high-profile case, so the ego never clocks out. Sleep paralysis with a sensed intruder is the body forcing a stop the career-self will not grant; the first treatment is sleep, not prazosin.

2013-281.sentence: N-acetylcysteine is doing the work the missing clock cannot: when acetaminophen timing is unknown, you start NAC rather than wait for a tidy Rumack-Matthew plot. The antidote covers the gap so hepatocytes are not sacrificed to a better history.

2013-282.sentence: The 4-per-second generalized spike-and-wave of childhood absence epilepsy is dumped into the teacher as “this girl will not pay attention”—projective identification, meaning the blank second is put into the adult so the child is not seen as briefly gone. Depressive concern starts when you repair that misread: it is a seizure, not a character flaw.

2013-283.sentence: Buying shares turns you from the person who holds both the hopeful and the predatory parts of the patient into a partner who needs the business to win. Once money and care occupy the same object, the “good doctor who believes in recovery” and the “investor who benefits” cannot be kept apart in one mind.

2013-284.sentence: Bupropion SR 100 mg BID already worked, but this is not a mind that can absorb more uncovering of “maybe another AD will be fine.” Taper and watch: the technique matches a nervous system that has already shown it cannot spare extra seizure-threshold risk.

2013-285.sentence: Hematemesis, renal tubular acidosis, CPK 3120, and brain atrophy land in the room as a pair of people deciding whether the story is “mystery medical” or “glue and solvents.” If you skip products the patient does not call drugs, the two of you collude in the same not-naming that kept the inhalant use going.

2013-286.sentence: Those 4–6 Hz irregular polyspikes of juvenile myoclonic epilepsy show a brain that loses its morning grip when sleep is cut. Attachment here is concrete: a roommate, parent, or you becomes the secure base that protects the sleep schedule so the myoclonus does not escalate into a convulsion.

2013-287.sentence: After CABG, an SSRI can help mood partly because it inhibits platelet function—the same antiplatelet push the surgeons already want. Ego strength is the body’s: can this patient tolerate extra bleeding risk on aspirin or a P2Y12 inhibitor, or is the depression treatment itself a hit the clotting system cannot absorb.

2013-288.sentence: A contracted missed-visit fee is containment: the rage or shame of the empty hour gets a named rule instead of being dumped as “you don’t care” or “I don’t exist.” The APA stance only holds if you put that container in the contract first, so the feeling can be thought rather than evacuated by a surprise bill.

2013-289.sentence: The ex-girlfriend leaving him is a blow to self-esteem, and the plan to “teach her a lesson” is an attempt to restore a grandiose, competent self by force. Your job is still the Tarasoff duty: inform the police that he poses a potential danger, rather than treating the threat as only a narcissistic rant.

2013-290.sentence: The 13-year-old’s development still depends on a home that does not throw children across rooms; “no medical injury” does not make the rage safe. You tell the 22-year-old that you must report to child protective services, because protection cannot wait for insight into why the story arrived today.

2013-291.sentence: Hypnosis after trauma works when a harsh inner critic can briefly stand down and allow focused attention instead of scanning for danger. In hypnotizable people it can safely decrease pain and stress; it is not a moral shortcut that “makes half of patients worse.”

2013-292.sentence: Recurrent “unexplained” visual loss and old hemiparesis recruit you into the conversion-hysteria role—the doctor who treats the body as a message. Bilateral cortical blindness, spasticity, extensor plantars, and the angiogram/MRI point to sickle cell vaso-occlusion, so you stay the neurologist, not the interpreter of symbols.

2013-293.sentence: In patients over 65, alcohol dependence is less common, but the same “few drinks” after a fall can be the body repeating unmourned loss without a story attached. The adverse consequences are more serious—falls, drugs, isolation—so you treat the drinking as high-stakes even when the narrative is thin.

2013-294.sentence: A 5-year-old who just learned to walk and talk steadily can lose those skills overnight when post-measles acute cerebellitis inflames the cerebellum. Normal MRI and tox do not make it a medulloblastoma or PML; the developmental capacities arrived, then a post-infectious attack knocked them offline.

2013-295.sentence: Descriptive diagnostic criteria turn a culture-war about “what kind of person this is” into a shared checklist: symptoms, duration, impairment, exclusions. The manual is the third in the room so two residents stop arguing identity and start counting what the patient actually does.

2013-296.sentence: Engagement and differentiation running together is Erikson’s identity-versus-role-confusion on a group scale: members need a “we” and also a special seat next to the leader. Competition for time is not failure of bonding; it is the group trying on both belonging and a distinct self at once.

2013-297.sentence: The nightcap is doing a job: it buys sleep onset by cutting REM, the stage that usually runs the night’s emotional replay. Sedation is not rest; as the alcohol wears off, fragmentation returns and the mind never got its dream work.

2013-298.sentence: This is countertransference: leftover urgency to save the alcoholic parent is now aimed at this patient, so “we are making progress” is the psychiatrist’s wish, not the work. A trial comment starts with that pull to convince rather than another lecture on quitting.

2013-299.sentence: Duty to other hospitalized patients is the frame after an assault: the ward’s safety limit outranks keeping this admission “therapeutic.” Arrest and transfer say the community of remaining patients holds the boundary, not the assailant’s treatment preference.

2013-300.sentence: Ego strength here is reality testing under a scary story: a cohort follows vaccination first, then watches for autism, instead of grabbing a case history that feels causal. Delay and comparison groups are the adult alternative to a single vivid sequence that “proves” harm.

2014-1.sentence: The mother's "kaaa-bam" is not just cute noise; it is a timed feed of rhythm that says I am with your body, not merely watching it. Attunement here is the pill-as-proof-of-need: she matches his stroke so he feels his pleasure is receivable, not a demand she has to dodge.

2014-2.sentence: Twelve-step facilitation recruits you as sponsor-stand-in: someone who names the disease and then steps aside so a Higher Power can hold what he cannot. Notice the countertransference pull to become the extra self he surrenders to; stay a facilitator of that surrender, not a rival savior.

2014-3.sentence: Right parietal damage leaves the left hemiplegia unrepresented: she cannot remember the limb as hers, so she repeats the loss by handing the arm to you. Anosognosia here is not stubborn denial; the body-self map is gone, and the dyad has to carry the missing half.

2014-4.sentence: Dysprosody is the melody stripped from speech, so affect is still in the room but the voice no longer carries it. That is a vertical split: feeling stays inside while the spoken line leaves the chair without tone.

2014-5.sentence: Fluoxetine as first-line asks whether her ego can wait through the lag and sit with early activation without bolting. Panic treatment tests affect tolerance: she has to hold weekly attacks while the SSRI slowly restores a margin of control.

2014-6.sentence: Serotonin syndrome after an SSRI plus tramadol is the body acting out what the mind cannot metabolize: too much transmitter, no leftover space. Naming clonus and hyperreflexia is not scolding the combo; it is refusing the defense of "just more pain meds" when the nervous system is already flooding.

2014-7.sentence: The team is already in an enactment: they are living a fight with the entitled patient instead of treating him. Model appealing to that entitlement so staff stop the punish-or-submit loop and still get the labs done.

2014-8.sentence: Non-REM sleep is the night's warehouse shift: the mind is less busy wrapping experience into a story you can later tell. Decreased recall of dream activity is the finding, not the absence of all mentation—NREM just does not package the night for morning report.

2014-9.sentence: The first job is the frame: name the rule, protect the staff, and keep treatment possible. Watching, referring, or charging a dollar for each "stupid" is dodge-work; limits are the intervention that stops the abuse from becoming the treatment.

2014-10.sentence: The proverb asks whether he can contain a concrete mess—spilled milk—until it becomes a thinkable rule. Abstract thinking is that containing work; a concrete answer leaves you holding only the puddle.

2014-11.sentence: Untreated mania is not a weekend of high self-esteem; the grandiose self can stay inflated for about three months. Counsel the family with that clock so they do not wait for a one-week crash that the untreated episode will not deliver.

2014-12.sentence: Triphasic waves with diffuse slowing mean the body is poisoning thought—metabolic encephalopathy—not a seizure storm or a dead brain. Read the EEG as failed metabolism, not as a hidden wish or a stroke's punch.

2014-13.sentence: Methylphenidate is not a personality transplant; it loans the eight-year-old a bit of prefrontal braking so energy, the short fuse, and homework slips do not have to live only as body-discharge.
