Video games already hold his attention, so the drug is aimed at the developmental gap between that locked-in play and the classroom demand to sit, wait, and finish.

2014-14.sentence: You asked for guns out of the house after a suicide attempt; the parent said no and you filed with child protective services, which is you holding the safety limit when the family would not. Autonomy is the ethical concept that fights that move: the parent’s claim to keep firearms and decide how they are secured, even when that claim collides with the child’s protection.

2014-15.sentence: The argument left something unsayable, so the throat went mute while a loud cough still proves the cords can close—conversion, not a torn larynx. The symptom is the fight relocated: speech is banned, but the apparatus is intact, which is why this is conversion disorder rather than injury or selective mutism.

2014-16.sentence: Sleep terrors start in childhood: a non-REM surge of terror and frantic movement, not a dream you can interpret at the bedside. There is no insight in the episode itself—eyes open, poorly organized thrashing, amnesia after—so you do not treat it as a REM nightmare or a seizure until the developmental picture fails.

2014-17.sentence: When an SSRI has only partly quieted PTSD, adding an atypical antipsychotic is a second lid on arousal that will not stay represented as words. Nightmares, hypervigilance, and paranoid-edged irritability are still being lived in the body; the antipsychotic is for that leftover storm, not a substitute for ending treatment on a clock.

2014-18.sentence: Four weeks is the outer wall of acute stress: startle, vivid memories, and pulling away from friends can still be the ego’s short-term scramble after the mugging. Past that window the same picture becomes PTSD, which means the nervous system did not metabolize the attack in the time we still call expected.

2014-19.sentence: After nocturia, many elders leave the night without leaving the bed: the body got up to pee, then the mind treats those minutes as if the whole night never happened. That vertical split—awake-for-the-bladder versus “I never sleep”—is why they ask for a hypnotic before anyone counts bathroom trips.

2014-20.sentence: The Wisconsin Card Sorting Test asks whether he can shift set after feedback, the same muscle he needs to take in a trial comment about his own impulsivity. A near-perfect MMSE can hide a frontal patient who cannot see his perseveration, so insight is not available to keep his meds safe.

2014-21.sentence: You hold the frame by having him listen to that song again and again with no alcohol until the pairing dies; that is extinction, not a new trick. Disulfiram-nausea or non-alcoholic beer would start a different pairing; they do not unpair the cue.

2014-22.sentence: They dump “declare my spouse the problem” into you as raw heat. You contain it—hold the blame long enough that it becomes thinkable as a fight between them, which is the common move in every couple and family therapy: difficulties named in relational terms.

2014-23.sentence: The Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule watches whether joint attention can appear in a structured play hour; you cannot rush a three-year-old into looking with you. Speech and relatedness have a developmental limit you observe, not force, once hearing is already cleared.

2014-24.sentence: If you keep demanding her name as if she is hiding it, you enact the assault’s erasure: two people repeating pressure on a mind that cannot retrieve episodic memory. Driving and fluent speech stay because procedural skill is not the file that went missing.

2014-25.sentence: The chart can split: one self writes a defensible plan, another self keeps treating by habit, and the two never meet. Incorrect-treatment claims pile up when that vertical split stays unowned—harm happened in the room while the official story stayed elsewhere.

2014-26.sentence: Sertraline in the gut is not just a side effect; it is the first feed, and nausea can feel like the pill is poisoning you. Name the GI hit before she leaves or the relationship to the medicine ends in the bathroom, not in the next visit.

2014-27.sentence: Do not let olanzapine become a convenient cover: that is denial, pushing the two-day drink-stop out of awareness while the EEG already shows withdrawal delirium. Name the tremor, fever, and inattention as alcohol leaving the body, or the defense will keep you treating the wrong fire.

2014-28.sentence: This man never built a reliable holding environment—the late-arriving capacity to stay in treatment without someone coming to him. Assertive community treatment is that missing developmental function: the team arrives so impulsivity and violence are not left to an exhausted family.

2014-29.sentence: The erection that works alone and fails with his wife is a conscience problem in the marriage bed: desire feels permitted only offstage. Bring her in for behavioral exercises so the couple, not a private guilt, becomes the site of the work.

2014-30.sentence: The sudden vertigo, diplopia, ataxia, and occipital pain during neck cracking is raw body-terror that has to be named before anyone can think. Contain it as vertebral artery dissection—do not evacuate it into “anxiety after chiropractic”—or the dread stays unthinkable and the artery keeps tearing.

2014-31.sentence: A same-sex night or a heterosexual fling is often the adolescent self trying on a version of itself before the self-concept is solid, not a failed gender identity. If parents treat that experiment as a disorder, they pull the mirroring—the admiring, confirming look—the kid still needs while sexual self-esteem is under construction.

2014-32.sentence: CAMS found combination sertraline plus CBT beat either monotherapy for pediatric GAD, separation anxiety, and social phobia. Sertraline can drop the arousal enough that a trial comment in CBT—“notice how your mind just predicted catastrophe”—can actually land instead of bouncing off a flooded nervous system.

2014-33.sentence: Disulfiram blocks aldehyde dehydrogenase so acetaldehyde piles up and drinking becomes a bodily crisis, not a negotiation. That is a hard external limit for a person who cannot yet hold “I stop” inside themselves; the pill is doing the ending they keep postponing.

2014-34.sentence: Lithium is at its best in acute mania and in maintenance, which is why the “how soon can I stop?” question is not only pharmacokinetic. You are being recruited as either the jailer who will never let the high return or the accomplice who will unlock the door too early; name that pull before you write the taper.

2014-35.sentence: Two doses of mirtazapine, then euphoria and standing on a chair, with no prior mood history, is substance-induced bipolar disorder, not a lifetime Bipolar I sentence. The team’s rush to brand him is a superego move: conscience wanting a hard, moral diagnosis instead of sitting with the more modest fact that a drug flipped the switch.

2014-36.sentence: On a locked unit, the wish to belong and the discharge clock collide every day, so cohesion never has time to form. Turnover is the real impediment: members leave before the group can metabolize either the longing to get close or the fear of it.

2014-37.sentence: New burning pain that makes her clamp down, which then makes the burn worse, can look like a body repeating something she has no words for. Still send her to gynecology first: an unrepresented state is a hypothesis, not a license to skip the exam that would find infection, vestibulitis, or endometriosis.

2014-38.sentence: The cerebellum's job is to land a movement you already planned, not to start it. A coarse, irregular 3 Hz oscillation that grows as the finger nears the target is that late-correction system failing in public—cerebellar intention tremor, not the 4–6 Hz rest tremor of Parkinson disease.

2014-39.sentence: Nonmaleficence is the first frame rule: do not manufacture a phobia in an 11-month-old to prove classical conditioning. Little Albert could not refuse the pairing of the stimulus and the loud bang, so Watson treated the baby as apparatus rather than a subject with a right not to be harmed.

2014-40.sentence: Amphetamine can flood the ED with persecutory objects: the computers become flashing accusers and a knife is recruited as a hard, external protector. That split is the drug collapsing inner threat into the machines in the room—check the urine before you baptize this as a primary psychotic break.

2014-41.sentence: A lithium level of 4.5 with creatinine 3.0, stupor, twitching, and diarrhea is not a moment for interpretation; the ion is a concrete bad object the kidney cannot metabolize. Emergent hemodialysis is the repair: you extract what he cannot hold or excrete.

2014-42.sentence: Lithium on the ECT list is a frame problem: the same ion that steadies mood also prolongs the seizure and thickens post-ictal confusion. Hold it so the treatment stays a treatment and not an iatrogenic delirium.

2014-43.sentence: This sits on identity versus role confusion: lithium holds the mood-self together while psoriasis makes the body a public, shaming badge of “the psychiatric patient.” The task is to keep both identities in one person—well enough to live, and not defined by the rash the medicine wrote on her skin.

2014-44.sentence: Ketamine’s NMDA antagonism briefly loosens the ego’s lock on a frozen, suicidal state; that is a borrowed hit of affect tolerance, not a new personality. Reality testing and impulse control can wobble in that window, so you use the drug as a short scaffold while the mind relearns holding despair without acting it.

2014-45.sentence: He used his spouse as a regulator—someone nearby to dump rage into—then broke the hand that reached for her. Naming that the violence is his job to stop protects the attachment system from turning proximity into a license to hit.

2014-46.sentence: You, the stimulant, and the biofeedback are one working pair: the pill is still pushing drive while the sessions ask for more self-control. Turn the methylphenidate or amphetamine down so the two of you are not amplifying each other into irritability and rebound hyperactivity.

2014-47.sentence: This mind has already shown it cannot use more of the same antipsychotic pressure; high-dose haloperidol or stacked second-generation drugs are just louder technique. Clozapine is the supportive choice—containment of treatment-resistant schizophrenia rather than more uncovering of residual psychosis.

2014-48.sentence: A cross-sectional survey is a still photo of who is currently in the untreated-depression relationship with the clinic, not a story of who later accepts the pill as feed or poison. You are counting how many people sit in that need-state today, not proving that treatment changed them.

2014-49.sentence: Hiding behind confidentiality here is denial: you treat a seven-year bond—and a husband you already know—as if it never existed so you do not have to feel the death. Calling him is ordinary grief work, not a lawsuit dodge or a chart leak; the relationship already left the consulting room.

2014-50.sentence: He and the family were already living one scene: he insisted the house smelled foul, they argued about a smell that was his medial temporal lobe talking. HSV encephalitis makes that two-person story; the T2 temporal signal and the seizure are the same circuit, not a private hallucination you can ignore.

2014-51.sentence: He wants DDAVP so overnight camp can stay a secure base instead of a wet sleeping bag that would push him out of the group. Father’s bedwetting until 12 is attachment data, not a lab cue: the family already knows this body, and desmopressin is a short bridge so he can stay close to peers.

2014-52.sentence: After 65, ego strength slips first in the workday—judgment, impulse, reality testing—and other physicians see it because they stand next to the change. Peer report is the group’s coping: colleagues name the impairment so a board can hold what the doctor can no longer hold.

2014-53.sentence: Opioid intoxication is a vertical split you can see: the person is still in the chair, but arousal has left—nodding, slurred, miotic. Pinpoint pupils name opioids, not alcohol or benzos; those sedate without that constricted, gone-while-present look.

2014-54.sentence: A bright, blistering, sunburn-like sheet after a new mood stabilizer is the pair already in an enactment: a rushed start of lamotrigine instead of a talked-about, slow titration. Stevens–Johnson is the body answering that broken frame; lithium and olanzapine do not write this letter.

2014-55.sentence: Asking for the Boston Naming Test can be a clean use of suppression: you set the word-finding worry aside long enough to measure it, instead of arguing about whether the substitutions “count.” Naming is the work of getting a word out, so this test tracks the gap between knowing and saying.

2014-56.sentence: Glycine is the spinal cord’s no: an inhibitory transmitter that quiets motor and sensory traffic the way a good feed can quiet a screaming need. When you teach why some drugs sedate or stop seizures, you are also saying the nervous system can take in a stop signal without being poisoned.

2014-57.sentence: School-age kids start to recognize racial and ethnic stereotypes; that is a developmental fact, not proof the family has failed the frame. Your job is to hold the limit: name the stereotype as something children now notice, without turning the visit into a confession or a lecture that shames the parent out of the room.

2014-58.sentence: Moderate ID here is not a verdict on insight; she already shows what she can use—self-care with a spotter, a greeter job with a supervisor, second-grade academics. A trial comment stays concrete: “You do better when someone is nearby,” which she can take in, rather than asking her to narrate her own disability.

2014-59.sentence: Amnestic MCI is a limit you cannot rush past: delayed recall of four words is failing while driving, cooking, and living alone still hold. Termination talk here is about time—this is not yet Alzheimer dementia, and naming it MCI protects her from a premature ending of independence.

2014-60.sentence: Varenicline is a half-feed at the α4β2 nicotinic receptor: it gives a little dopamine so the craving is not a famine, and it occupies the site so a cigarette cannot deliver the full reward. The wish to smoke and the prohibition against smoking meet in that partial agonist, which is why it can feel like both comfort and a slammed door.

2014-61.sentence: Drug court is not just a sanction; it is a borrowed parental function that says your self-worth is still being watched and can be restored by showing up. Two nights in jail after two missed counselor visits is a blunt competence demand: stay in treatment or lose status, rather than a lecture about cocaine.

2014-62.sentence: The truck driver’s ulnar lesion—numb little and ring fingers, wasted hypothenar, weak grip—can quietly recruit you into the role of the one who must keep him on the road. Notice if you feel hurried to clear him or oddly responsible for his livelihood; that feeling is countertransference, not a neurologic finding.

2014-63.sentence: The poisoning-the-dog conviction is unrepresented terror parked in the neighbor; you cannot argue a hole that never became memory. Empathize with the fear and skip confrontation, house surveys, and cameras—those moves reenact the watch at the window instead of holding what cannot yet be thought.

2014-64.sentence: Major depressive disorder as the leading U.S. disability cause from ages 15 to 44 lands on the years when identity and intimacy are supposed to lock in. When that developmental stretch stalls, work and love do not just feel sad; they fail to arrive.

2014-65.sentence: A no-harm contract soothes the psychiatrist’s conscience more than it protects anyone; the chart that actually stands up is an assessment of suicide risk and protective factors. Skipping that work for a signature is a sanctioned moral shortcut: you feel dutiful while the real judgment is missing.

2014-66.sentence: Projective identification is not ordinary projection; the disowned self or object is planted in you and you are nudged to live it, which is why you later snap at the nurse. Erikson’s intimacy-versus-isolation task is on the table: the patient cannot hold the rage inside a two-person relationship, so you become the container that briefly fails.

2014-67.sentence: Pictures of the nanny keep her as a usable inner object, so the preschooler can miss her instead of erasing her. Avoiding her name is not mercy; it makes the loss unthinkable, and unthinkable losses come back as clinginess, night fears, or sudden tantrums.

2014-68.sentence: The family and the consult team keep handing the high-arched feet and onion-bulb biopsy around as if someone in the room caused them. That is an enactment: a two-person (or two-generation) repetition of CMT1A’s PMP22 duplication, a myelin-gene copy-number error, being treated as a moral or parenting failure instead of a fixed Schwann-cell lesion.

2014-69.sentence: Aerosol huffing (glue, paint, solvents) gives this 13-year-old a cheap vertical split: red eyes, rhinorrhea, perioral sores, and that dazed “out of it” look while the body stays in the chair. The vacancy is the point—the solvent high is a chemical leave-without-leaving, not garden-variety sleepiness or garden-variety cannabis.

2014-70.sentence: The freshman on blotter LSD is recruiting you as the last sane object who can make “things aren’t right” stop. Meet that transferential plea with 20 mg of diazepam and a calm, present person—not isolation in the dark, not hourly haloperidol—because a bad trip is panic clinging to you, not a need to be abandoned or neuroleptically crushed.

2014-71.sentence: An overvalued idea is a stubborn, self-defining conviction—here the “Neanderthal” brow that exams call normal-range—that still yields a millimeter to reality, unlike a delusion. The harsh conscience has found a single facial ridge to prosecute; surgery would only feed that prosecutor, not settle the case.

2014-72.sentence: Clonazepam 0.5 then 1 mg bid finally quieted the panic, and the fading benefit is the old wish–prohibition fight: stay calm versus stay off a “bad” benzo. The right move is 1.5 mg twice daily, not a toxicology hunt or a shorter-acting switch—the dose is still climbing the therapeutic curve, not chasing a forbidden high.

2014-73.sentence: Alcohol use disorder is the diagnosis that most reliably turns unremembered rage into a body that hits: intoxication evacuates what cannot be thought, so the old scene is acted on someone else instead of being known. Schizophrenia gets blamed because psychosis looks like danger; the data say the bottle is the more common weapon.

2014-74.sentence: Unequal motivation means one partner is trying to dump raw panic into the room and the other will not hold it, so you cannot do the Bion job: contain a feeling until it becomes thinkable. Past affairs, sex trouble, co-parenting fights, and stuck arguments can still be metabolized together; a one-person project will evacuate as blame, not as thought.

2014-75.sentence: Low-income families carry the highest IPV rates because chronic scarcity starves the self of reliable mirroring and competence—the felt sense that someone sees you as worthwhile and that you can keep a life together. Screen everyone, but do not pretend poverty is psychically neutral: it erodes the idealizing and self-esteem cushions that keep rage from becoming a partner’s injury.

2014-76.sentence: Frontal-lobe atrophy takes the very capacity this lens needs: the person can no longer see their own part or use a trial comment, because initiative and affect have gone dull. You are not meeting resistance; you are meeting missing cortex, so insight work waits while you name the apathy as illness, not character.

2014-77.sentence: Symptoms present before age 3 is the clock you cannot rewind: autism’s social-communication break is a developmental limit, not a feeling the parents or school failed to notice soon enough. IQ 68, aggression, infant inhibition, and parental unconcern do not make the diagnosis; early onset does, and you cannot terminate or rush a capacity that never arrived on time.

2014-78.sentence: CBT for insomnia has the better long-term prognosis because it teaches a mind that can use uncovering of bedtime catastrophizing, not just a pill that supports sleep from the outside. Zolpidem, trazodone, diphenhydramine, and biofeedback may quiet the night now; they do not leave a technique the patient can keep after the prescription ends.

2014-79.sentence: When two SSRIs have already failed, the next move is imipramine, and the relationship work is helping the patient stay in a treatment that will feel older, drier, and more medical than the pills they already tried. You and the patient are co-authoring a third trial, not hunting a “cleaner” drug: bupropion, mirtazapine, gabapentin, and phenelzine are the ways the pair can dodge the TCA together.

2014-80.sentence: Serial sevens fails as a concentration test because it also demands arithmetic skill, so a stumble may be a school-age competence gap, not a here-and-now attention deficit. Erikson’s industry-versus-inferiority task is whether the person ever owned numbers as something they can do; if they did not, WORLD backwards is a fairer window on concentration.

2014-81.sentence: Winnicott’s holding environment is the caregiver’s job of keeping the child safe enough that spontaneity can happen—assertiveness grows from surviving a little frustration, not from never meeting it. The hovering parent who finishes every task is doing the opposite of holding: she is erasing the struggle that would have built a sense of competence.

2014-82.sentence: The suicide signal in epilepsy tracks comorbid psychiatric illness more than seizure type, seizure burden, AED black-box fear, or lifestyle limits. Developmentally, the mind that never quite arrived at a durable way to bear mood, despair, and impulse is the risk factor—not the temporal lobe’s electrical weather itself.

2014-83.sentence: Ovoid periventricular plaques in a 35-year-old with hemicorporeal numbness are multiple sclerosis, not ALD, Lyme, mets, or lacunes, and the conscience trap is treating the MRI as a moral verdict. A rigid inner judge can convert demyelination into “I am damaged / I caused this”; your job is to keep the finding neurologic so guilt does not become the unofficial diagnosis.

2014-84.sentence: Parents who still see explosions after a moderate stimulant are recruiting you to be the person who finally “stops the badness,” usually by adding an atypical or swapping to divalproex. That pull is countertransference: you feel pressured to become the punitive or sedating parent. The clinical move is to stay the optimizing doctor and push the long-acting stimulant first.

2014-85.sentence: Restless legs are an unrepresented state: the urge is lived in the limbs at night because there is no thought yet, only a demand to move. Check iron first so you treat the body's missing substrate instead of throwing pergolide, bromocriptine, or L-dopa at a complaint that has not been metabolized.

2014-86.sentence: Fluoxetine carries the wish to lift the depression; SIADH is the prohibition, dumping sodium until the elderly mind goes confused with a normal neuro exam. Urea and electrolytes name that collision; CT, EKG, CPK, and a hepatic panel do not.

2014-87.sentence: Amitriptyline is the bulky parent; nortriptyline is the usable self after demethylation, less anticholinergic fog and more room for a coherent self-experience. Knowing that metabolite is a competence mirror: you can offer a cleaner version of the same TCA instead of leaving the patient merged with dry mouth and confusion.

2014-88.sentence: Oxybutynin plus climbing diphenhydramine open a vertical split: animals and children appear while the body sits dry, mydriatic, tachycardic, and 101°F. Physostigmine, not dantrolene or bromocriptine, puts acetylcholine back so the person can occupy the stretcher instead of the hallucination.

2014-89.sentence: Ego strength shows up as whether three or four hours of sleep still leave a depleted self or a wired one. Asking how well rested they feel in the day tests affect tolerance and reality testing of need; awakening time, meds, nightmares, and sleep paralysis do not.

2014-90.sentence: The cohort design follows Agent Orange exposure forward and matches combat so the toxin is not used as a dumping ground for every wartime terror. That is depressive-position work: compare cognitive tests without projective identification of all damage into the exposed veterans.

2014-91.sentence: Refusing wound care while asking nurses to feed him splits the staff into two objects: the all-bad pain-givers and the all-good feeders. Reward for helping with dressings and calories keeps those functions in one relationship instead of letting him park all the good in the spoon and all the bad in the debridement.

2014-92.sentence: This is not a headache to interpret; bilateral papilledema plus a normal MRI is idiopathic intracranial hypertension until the lumbar puncture shows raised pressure. Support the body first—acetazolamide, weight, and the opening pressure—because uncovering conflict will not drop intracranial pressure.

2014-93.sentence: The OCD and the tic are working as a pair, not as one lonely ritual. An SSRI aimed only at the obsessions often stalls because the tic partner is still running the interaction, which is why pediatric OCD plus a tic disorder responds poorly to SSRI monotherapy.

2014-94.sentence: At the curb the three-year-old has acquired a new capacity: he reads the mother's face before he moves. That is social referencing—using the caregiver's expression as a safety signal—not stranger anxiety or object permanence.

2014-95.sentence: The slowness is doing the diagnostic work here: early HIV-associated neurocognitive change is subcortical, so processing speed drops while language, praxis, and recognition still hold. Alzheimer starts in cortex; this virus shows up first as a mind that is still articulate but late.

2014-96.sentence: Psychiatry's old identity problem was that two good clinicians could not name the same illness. DSM-III earned industry—shared competence—by standardizing diagnostic criteria, not by prototypes, axes, or being atheoretical.

2014-97.sentence: Alpha-1 blockade from a second-generation antipsychotic such as quetiapine drops vascular tone; the heart answers with reflex tachycardia, so a pulse of 110 after a dizzy stand is compensation, not a new psychotic storm. If you treat that number as “agitation,” you miss the body’s bargain and reach for more dopamine blockade when the fix is slower titration, fluids, and checking orthostatics.

2014-98.sentence: The wish to “wake him up” with methylphenidate or bupropion is acting out: doing something stimulating instead of sitting with residual cognitive dullness on clozapine. Fluoxetine is the indicated add-on here—it can lift negative and cognitive complaints and bump clozapine levels—so you stay with the only antipsychotic that already worked rather than chasing speed.

2014-99.sentence: Her lateness-equals-disgust story is transference: she installs a hating you in the five-minute gap. Tactical disclosure—briefly showing your real mind (“I ran late; I’m curious what you imagined”)—is the MBT move that restores two separate minds instead of a Socratic fight about who is right.

2014-100.sentence: Amitriptyline can hold both the neuropathic fire and the low mood in one object, so the consult does not have to split “real diabetic pain” from “just depression.” Bupropion, fluoxetine, and mirtazapine do not carry that same analgesic pedigree; the TCA is the relationship that treats the body and the affect together.

2014-101.sentence: Hippocampal tau tangles mean this mind is losing the apparatus that would use insight-oriented uncovering. Name Alzheimer disease, then shift technique toward support, orientation, and caregiver structure—you cannot interpret your way out of neurofibrillary degeneration.

2014-102.sentence: The pair co-authored the monster until one child’s shriek made pretend feel real, and the second child’s ego could not bind the surge. Withdrawal is the relationship saying the affect got too hot—not cheating, not a moral veto on harm themes, just too much anxiety for a four-year-old to stay in the game.

2014-103.sentence: The caretaker is this patient's last secure base — the person who still maps reality when Lewy-body fluctuations and visual hallucinations scramble it. Two days of risperidone 0.25 mg that produce rigidity and sedation steal that attachment channel: a rigid, obtunded patient cannot use proximity to the caretaker to settle.

2014-104.sentence: The polyuria is lithium's tax on the collecting duct — night thirst that can feel like the medicine is attacking the body. Amiloride blocks the ENaC channel lithium uses to injure those cells, so it treats the symptom without yanking the lithium level and taking away the mood-stabilizing relationship.

2014-105.sentence: At thirty this man sits on Erikson's intimacy-versus-isolation task: finding a partner and a people to belong to. Native Americans carry the highest U.S. suicide rate, so isolation is not only personal — it is a population wound that makes that intimacy task more lethal when depression and intoxication hit.

2014-106.sentence: The Santería curse is a live third in the room: faith, homeland, and family sit between you and the suicide risk. Learn from them the expected course of a curse-illness so you treat their map of danger, not a lecture on neurotransmitters.

2014-107.sentence: Empathy is taking in the patient's inner scene without dumping your own shoes back — you grasp their experience, not what you would feel. That is depressive-position work: you stay with their mind instead of splitting into a rescue of 'I'd feel the same.

2014-108.sentence: The old story treated the beta-blocker as a poison pill that would steal mood after an MI. Recent studies do not support that association, so the relationship task is naming the fear of the pill rather than withholding a cardiac drug that is not the depressant they imagined.

2014-109.sentence: Following commands during the thrashing means she is still in a two-person field with you, not in a cortical electrical storm that has taken the self offline. The ethical job is to hold that limit without a public unmasking in the bay: treat the events as a communication you will work with later, not as a lie you expose.

2014-110.sentence: Paranoia is what amphetamine psychosis does for the person: it turns a catecholamine flood into a plot, so the terror has an author instead of being formless. That is why you see intense suspiciousness after a stimulant binge, not the alogia and flattening that mark a primary process illness.

2014-111.sentence: At thirty the Erikson task is intimacy versus isolation, and another SSRI that steals appetite, gut comfort, and sexual function would push him further out of the body that has to stay in relationships. Bupropion is first-line here because it treats the depression without repeating fluoxetine’s GI and sexual side effects, so the medicine does not become another isolation.

2014-112.sentence: The acute combativeness is doing work the history cannot: it is announcing an acute brain-state change on top of old dementia, not just “more of the same.” EEG is the test that can show that change as diffuse slowing of delirium, which a normal chest film, EKG, or MRI will not settle when vitals and exam are already quiet.

2014-113.sentence: Psychological mindedness already arrived; what is late is the capacity to stay inside a good-enough relationship without treating vague inadequacy as a verdict that he must leave. Twelve sessions of brief psychodynamic therapy use that observing ego on the old sense of not-enough, which CBT, IPT, or supportive work would not target as cleanly.

2014-114.sentence: Café-au-lait spots, subcutaneous neurofibromas, and axillary freckling are childhood skin findings that were already writing neurofibromatosis type 1 on the body long before this first seizure. The developmental miss is that nobody read those signs when they arrived, so the diagnosis waits for a seizure at twenty-five to make the old skin language count.

2014-115.sentence: They keep recruiting you as either the scolding parent or the buddy who says drinking is fine. Motivational enhancement therapy holds the ambivalence itself—the two wishes at once—so you do not become either figure.

2014-116.sentence: The adult sibling is still inside the consult frame, even two years later; attraction that feels new is often leftover heat from that triad. APA ethics therefore bars romance with any third party, not only the identified adolescent.

2014-117.sentence: Haloperidol blocked dopamine so hard the motor wish could not move—that collision is NMS: rigidity, 104 fever, CK 9,000. After you stop the neuroleptic, a dopamine agonist such as bromocriptine returns a little of the blocked drive so the body can unfreeze.

2014-118.sentence: The primary team is already living a two-person pattern: they need psychiatry to turn a worship state into a diagnosis. Worldwide, those ‘taken over’ episodes are usually normal pieces of religious and ritual events, not depersonalization or psychosis.

2014-119.sentence: The CAG trinucleotide expansion on huntingtin is a developmental clock: childhood looks intact, then midlife the inherited script arrives as chorea. Irritability is not a new character; it is that genome timetable coming due.

2014-120.sentence: Cycling through the ED is doing a job: it is asking for a container big enough that the child does not have to leave home. Wraparound services exist to hold that dysregulation in the community and prevent hospitalization or residential placement.

2014-121.sentence: Integrity versus despair is the late-life task here: this attorney still works and still knows the people and animals are not real, so the ego has not given up a coherent self just because macular degeneration stole the visual field. Charles Bonnet is the cortex filling in a blind world; it is not a collapse of reality testing, and that distinction is what keeps this from becoming despair dressed up as psychosis.

2014-122.sentence: When mother answers every question and calls ulcerative colitis "our disease," her conscience has moved into his gut; he is not allowed a private body or a private illness. Enmeshment, in Minuchin's sense, is that sanctioned gap in boundaries: guilt and loyalty replace a child's right to speak for himself.

2014-123.sentence: The aging kidney's job of discarding free water never quite keeps up the way a younger one does, and a month of paroxetine can tip that late-arriving, fragile osmoregulation into SIADH. Urine osmolality is the test that shows the kidney is holding water when sodium is 117 and the patient is lethargic.

2014-124.sentence: The 2-year-old with a car next to the toddler with a truck is holding two separate play-worlds side by side; good and bad, mine and yours, are not yet mixed in one shared scene. Parallel play is object relatedness at arm's length: near enough to feel another mind, not yet ready to assign roles or feed the same doll.

2014-125.sentence: Transient psychosis in borderline personality is a mind that cannot hold itself together under abandonment pressure, not a new primary psychotic illness. Uncovering interpretations will shred that mind further; you support, name the stressor, and wait for reality testing to come back before you go deeper.

2014-126.sentence: After the house is gone, hopelessness is the mind saying agency itself has been destroyed, not a buried feeling that needs to be excavated. Structured steps that rebuild self-efficacy, and CBT that challenges the conviction that nothing will ever improve, restore a usable ego before you chase terror or start an SSRI or propranolol for prophylaxis.

2014-127.sentence: Topiramate is the daily wall you put up before the next storm, not the fire extinguisher you grab once the head already pounds. Projective identification is the same move: the patient parks the unbearable pressure in you so you will hold it first, then they can take a calmer version back.

2014-128.sentence: Conservation is the child's proof that amount survives a change of shape; Piaget will not let you skip that stage by coaching. Endings work the same way: time has to elapse until the person can keep the relationship when the hour, the cup, or the therapist looks different.

2014-129.sentence: Methadone maintenance holds the pregnant patient's opioid need so street heroin and a crash detox do not dump raw withdrawal into the fetus. That is containment: you metabolize the dread first so it becomes a thinkable plan instead of nameless evacuation.

2014-130.sentence: Dilated ventricles in the wet-wacky-wobbly triad mean CSF is pooling where thought and gait should be organized. Containment fails the same way: pressure builds in a closed space until walking, memory, and continence cannot be thought, only leaked.

2014-131.sentence: Capacity here turns on appreciation: she can name pills and needles, but she cannot take in that oral antibiotics already failed and sepsis is next. Some limits will not wait for family, a proxy, or a better MMSE; the consequence is already in the room.

2014-132.sentence: A June handoff has to carry the treatment course and a risk assessment, or the wish to be done collides with the duty not to abandon. That collision is the drive conflict: get out clean versus stay responsible long enough to name who is suicidal.

2014-133.sentence: Oxybutynin is an anticholinergic: it dries up the acetylcholine that donepezil is trying to spare, so the patient's mind cannot use the drug as a reliable helper. In self-psychology terms, that is a failed mirror—the pill promised more competence and self-esteem, then quietly cancelled the very signal it was supposed to amplify.

2014-134.sentence: Storytelling with words at age four is not just a language milestone; it is the child offering you a narrative feed instead of only play-next-to-you silence. When a parent asks if this is “normal,” the hidden question is whether talk can still nourish the relationship, or whether they need a pill to prove the child is behind.

2014-135.sentence: Object constancy is the late Mahler capacity to keep a good-enough picture of the other while you are frustrated, not Piaget permanence and not conservation. When that fails, the session after a vacation becomes splitting: you are all-good one hour and all-bad the next because the mind cannot hold both feelings at once.

2014-136.sentence: Low CSF serotonin tracks with IED’s punch-the-wall, smash-the-phone bursts that look mindless from the outside. A trial comment still matters: “You explode, then you feel sorry—can you see the split second you choose the wall instead of the words?” tests whether they can own their part or only the chemistry.

2014-137.sentence: Once you find this 88-year-old incompetent, the durable power of attorney names the assigned decision maker—not the attending, the spouse, or the nearest relative by default. That person holds the frame: they approve the agitation plan so you do not quietly seize the limit because it would be faster.

2014-138.sentence: Atomoxetine is the first-line ADHD pick when the adolescent already misuses cannabis or stimulants, because it is not a scheduled booster they can crush or sell. Ego strength here is impulse control: you treat attention without handing them a diversion-ready drug their coping cannot yet hold.

2014-139.sentence: When your mind keeps leaving a flat patient, treat the drift as a signal that you have lost your function as a secure base — the person they use to stay regulated in the room. Sit still and scan what you feel toward them before you apologize, take notes, or cut time; that inner check is how you come back into range so they do not have to protest a therapist who already left.

2014-140.sentence: Todd paresis after a seizure is the cortex briefly failing affect tolerance at the motor or language map — the same tissue that just fired cannot yet hold a limb or a word. Use that transient weakness or aphasia to localize the focus, not to invent etiology, prognosis, or a new stroke until the deficit overstays its welcome.

2014-141.sentence: Full erection starts in excitement, but seminal fluid appears in plateau — a vertical split in the cycle where the body is already leaking toward emission while the person is still “not quite there.” Name that split when they worry about premature emission so the fluid is a phase marker, not proof they left the chair.

2014-142.sentence: In prefrontal cortex, dopamine mostly wanders off by diffusion instead of DAT reuptake, so blocking DAT with methylphenidate cannot finish the job the way it does in striatum. That is an enactment already in the teaching: you keep reaching for the transporter while the synapse is ending the message by walking away.

2014-143.sentence: Acute ethanol is NMDA antagonism plus GABA-A agonism — a pharmacologic denial that both slams the brakes and unhooks the alarm. Sedation, ataxia, and disinhibition are that defense in wet form: the cortex is told nothing urgent is happening while inhibition floods the room.

2014-144.sentence: Wallenberg’s lateral medullary stroke arrives as vertigo, hoarseness, ipsilateral face pin loss, limb ataxia, and veering — a body that suddenly cannot take in food, voice, or balance. Offer the aspirin and the stroke workup as care, not as a pill that must prove they are sick enough, because the lesion already named the need.

2014-145.sentence: Anticipation names a real biological clock—CAG-repeat expansion in Huntington disease—so the clinic cannot pretend time is a negotiation. The ethical limit is who holds the result: you do not rush predictive testing, and you do not leak a parent’s diagnosis to a child who has not asked.

2014-146.sentence: Conduction block on NCS is the nerve failing to fire through a demyelinated patch; the axon is still there, the insulation is not. A trial comment works the same way: you test whether the patient can still conduct a thought about their own part, or whether insight is blocked at that spot.

2014-147.sentence: A Type I error is calling the new antidepressant a winner when the signal is noise—p=0.04 in a tiny trial is not a license to stay forever. Ending the claim is a termination: the study’s power and time are finite, and you stop treating a false positive as if it were a lasting capacity.

2014-148.sentence: Valproate’s job here is not mood only: it blocks glucuronidation and roughly doubles lamotrigine, which is how a helpful add-on becomes a rash risk. The symptom of “I need both” is doing work—covering residual depression—while quietly raising Stevens–Johnson risk unless you cut the lamotrigine dose.

2014-149.sentence: T2 myelopathy from degenerative cervical spondylosis is an integrity problem: discs and osteophytes squeeze the cord the way late adulthood squeezes Erikson’s integrity-versus-despair task. The clumsiness and gait change are not character; they are a body that will not let the person pretend aging is only psychological.

2014-150.sentence: Cervical dystonia with a geste antagoniste is a two-person circuit: her sternocleidomastoid pulls left, and the fingertip on the chin is the other party that briefly stops the pull. Botulinum toxin is the treatment of choice because you interrupt that muscle–person loop at the synapse, not by medicating “anxiety” as if she were alone in it.

2014-151.sentence: A motivated smoker who already failed nicotine patches needs a technique that matches current ego capacity: varenicline plus concrete quit support, not an uncovering hunt for what the cigarette “means.” Save interpretation of oral need or self-attack for later; right now the mind can use a receptor-level assist more than insight.

2014-152.sentence: Giant cell arteritis asks you to hold two pictures of the same patient at once: the treatable temporal headache and the ophthalmic artery that can go black overnight. Splitting into “just a headache” versus “hopeless catastrophe” drops the bad object out of awareness—the very split that delays steroids and costs the eye.

2014-153.sentence: A percentage of the plaintiff’s award is projective identification in a fee: the attorney parks winning into you so your opinion is no longer yours. Stay in the depressive position—concern for a true report you could repair if you were wrong—rather than a paranoid-schizoid merger with the verdict.

2014-154.sentence: Keeping quetiapine going forever because the ward is finally quiet is an enactment: staff and physician are living “silence the dangerous elder” instead of reviewing the chemical restraint. OBRA 1987’s every-three-month taper attempt is the formal interruption of that two-person (really two-system) repetition.

2014-155.sentence: Supportive work’s job is to stabilize functioning and strengthen defenses, not to pry at a vertical split the patient cannot stay present for. Insight that asks a fragile mind to watch itself from the other side of that split is how they leave the room without standing up.

2014-156.sentence: Methadone was carrying impulse control and affect tolerance; carbamazepine induces CYP3A4, drops the level, and that borrowed ego strength evaporates into craving and irritability. Treat the interaction as a sudden loss of scaffolding, not as the patient “deciding” to relapse.

2014-157.sentence: Criticism, blame, and hostility are high expressed emotion: the family stops being a secure base and starts being a threat the patient has to monitor. Psychoeducation lowers that heat so proximity can regulate the psychosis again instead of triggering another relapse.

2014-158.sentence: That pale midbrain stripe is lost neuromelanin in the substantia nigra: the dopaminergic cells that should have matured and stayed put are gone. Parkinson disease is a late failure of that nigrostriatal line, not a glioma or a plaque you would see in MS.

2014-159.sentence: The family is recruiting you as the person who can time the storm; your job is not to soothe them with a story, it is to name the clock. Oral amphetamines peak around two hours, so that is when the agitation, BP, and pulse—and your urge to discharge or over-control—will be worst.

2014-160.sentence: Registration is taking the three words in; recall is whether they still exist after you look away. The Folstein MMSE adds that hold-in-mind step to orientation, attention, calculation, and language—abstraction and insight are someone else's test.

2014-161.sentence: A pure liaison stance is supportive technique aimed at the team, not uncovering work on the nurse or a grab of the case. Advise them how to evaluate depression; if you offer to see the patient yourself you have switched into consultation.

2014-162.sentence: The “younger man” is the third in the marriage: an 80-year-old’s sexual and generational place is under threat, and the children siding with mother seals him out. Delusional disorder (jealous type) keeps identity intact by locating the injury in her betrayal rather than in aging, and the rest of his mind—no hallucinations, intact cognition—stays organized around that one idea.

2014-163.sentence: A sleep terror is NREM panic with no dream text: the scream, sweat, and inconsolable fear never become a story the patient can own the next morning. That is the paranoid-schizoid position in the body—raw dread dumped into the night, with no depressive-position work of remembering, naming, or repairing.

2014-164.sentence: Cocaine writes a two-act script in the neonate: first hypertonia, hyperreflexia, and tremor, then a dull, poorly interactive lull. The second act is not “a baby who will not attach”; it is the stimulant leaving, and the infant’s only available meaning is a nervous system that cannot yet meet a face.

2014-165.sentence: REM sleep behavior—screaming, kicking, chased-dreams that leak into the limbs—plus gait falls is a late-life threat to integrity: the old man can no longer keep night and body inside one reliable self. Parkinson disease is the condition that risk tracks, so the chase is becoming a motor fact, not a private nightmare.

2014-166.sentence: Lamotrigine is for bipolar depression, not acute mania: it covers the long, heavy pole without handing her a manic escape hatch. The superego often treats that depression as earned punishment after highs; this drug stays with the guilt-soaked pole instead of sanctioning a flight into elevation.

2014-167.sentence: Heavy smoke induces CYP1A2, so olanzapine is cleared faster than the dose on the bottle implies; quit on a smoke-free unit and that extra clearance vanishes. The “mature” metabolism was never a finished developmental achievement—it was a cigarette-built shortcut, and the leftover olanzapine then sedates and stiffens him.

2014-168.sentence: ADHD plus ODD in a young child is mostly lived in the body and the home–school loop, not stored as thoughts you can interpret. A rewards program built on what the child actually enjoys is how you represent that storm: same clear contingency at home and school, instead of insight or imagery the child cannot yet hold.

2014-169.sentence: When the veteran asks why his brain is stuck on exits and slammed doors, notice the pull to become the one who either dismisses the scanning as 'just PTSD' or joins him in treating the world as permanently unsafe. That is the countertransference: you are being recruited as either a naïve civilian or a fellow sentry, and naming the hypervigilance as an old threat-detector still firing can keep you from enacting either role.

2014-170.sentence: IPSRT treats the relapse as something two people (and a whole household) keep making: late nights, red-eyes, and overnight shifts knock the social zeitgeber off its peg, and the mood follows. Lifestyle regularity is the interpersonal prescription—stable sleep, meals, and social timing—so the relationship stops being the place where the clock gets smashed.

2014-171.sentence: A large-volume tap that clears the gait is your clue to stay supportive and medical, not to start uncovering 'why this mind is falling apart.' Enlargement of the frontal horns on the pre-LP CT is NPH anatomy, and that finding tells you how much insight work this brain can use right now: very little until the hydrocephalus is treated.

2014-172.sentence: The toddler's language grows from the parent's affect-holding talk—frequent conversation and thinking aloud—more than from drills, because the child is borrowing the adult's words to bind impulse and name feeling. That is ego strength in the making: the parent who narrates the room is lending regulation, not just vocabulary.

2014-173.sentence: GHB can look like a gym 'supplement,' and the ED visit is often the moment he finally lets someone else hold the danger he has been managing alone. Attachment-wise, the euphoria-plus-vision-loss-plus-hallucinations hour after the liquid is a bid for proximity: he used a chemical to regulate, and now he needs a person.

2014-174.sentence: The fitness-for-duty eval is already an enactment: the impaired physician who refuses treatment pulls you toward being the secret-keeping colleague, and the system pulls you toward being the cop. You are not bound by usual confidentiality because this is not a treatment frame—if you protect him like a patient, you are living the cover-up instead of naming it.

2014-175.sentence: Confusion plus urinary retention is the mind leaving the room while the body stays in the chair: anticholinergic toxicity from benztropine, not a new schizophrenic episode. Switch to amantadine so you treat the parkinsonism without another vertical split between awareness and the bladder.

2014-176.sentence: The Stroop Color Word Test is the pill as demand: ink says one word, habit says another, and you have to refuse the overlearned feed. You are not asking how well they name or copy; you are asking whether they can inhibit the first automatic answer.

2014-177.sentence: Alcohol is the most common prenatal neurotoxin here, and the hesitation when you ask about pregnancy is often denial: the fact stays out of awareness so guilt does not land. A smooth philtrum and thin upper lip are the body keeping the history the story cannot yet hold.

2014-178.sentence: Look at the patient and say you, not he: insight starts when they are a subject in the room, not a third-person case the interpreter is reporting on. A trial comment lands only if it is offered to the person, not narrated about them.

2014-179.sentence: Sertraline is first-line in most guidelines because the treatment frame includes the infant at the breast, not only the mother's mood. You hold the limit: treat her depression and keep milk exposure low, rather than making her choose between being a patient and being a mother.

2014-180.sentence: Acute migraine is a self that cannot think until the pain stops; sumatriptan is the mirroring that says I take the attack seriously right now. Propranolol, valproate, and topiramate protect later; they do not restore competence in the emergency department.

2014-181.sentence: Peek-a-boo is the infant playing a forbidden pair of wishes at once: make the face vanish, and keep it. Object permanence is what lets that game stay a game instead of a catastrophe—the object can go, so the wish to send it away does not have to be disowned.

2014-182.sentence: The body is telling the history the chart cannot: hypokalemia, hypochloremia, metabolic alkalosis, and a high amylase with a normal lipase after vomiting, not pancreatitis. Purging is an unrepresented state acted in the gut—what cannot be remembered as hunger, shame, or rage is repeated as emptying.

2014-183.sentence: Memantine, the NMDA partial antagonist you add when donepezil is no longer enough, puts you in the role of the person who still remembers how the brain is being injured. Watch the countertransference of grim rescue: you are being recruited as the last intact memory, not as a glutamate receptor.

2014-184.sentence: MDMA is what ties bruxism, anorexia, diaphoresis, hot flashes, and anorgasmia into one night, and the frame question is whether anyone named the drug before the rave. Confidentiality still holds in the ED, but you hold the limit on what is safe to hide: this is not a private experiment once teeth and orgasm are already collateral.

2014-185.sentence: Insight here is not a clever comment about death wishes; it is whether the family can see their part in leaving a firearm in the house. Reducing gun access is the prevention step that does not wait for the teen to become psychologically minded.

2014-186.sentence: Recent alcohol abuse is the limit that outpatient cutting cannot absorb: intoxication collapses the pause between 'to feel something' and a lethal slip. Admission is not a personality diagnosis; it is the ending of a plan that assumed she could still stop herself sober.

2014-187.sentence: Bilateral mammillary-body and medial-thalamic lesions leave a mind that cannot hold a new day, so the gap gets dumped as confabulation rather than felt as loss. Nameless dread is what happens when memory cannot contain experience; Korsakoff’s cheerful denial is evacuation of that dread, not insight.

2014-188.sentence: AIP dumps porphobilinogen into urine while the mind dumps the same crisis as paranoia and hallucinations timed to menses. That is a vertical split: the attack leaves the chair as psychosis and proximal weakness so the person never has to sit with one story.

2014-189.sentence: Cimetidine blocks CYP and suddenly methadone hits harder; the clinic pair is already in an enactment, living “who sedated whom” instead of naming the interaction. The reflux pill is not a side plot. It is the two-person scene repeating as over-sedation.

2014-190.sentence: Escitalopram plus ERP is support first: you damp the OCD engine so uncovering does not flood a mind that already lives in ritual. Technique here is dose of SSRI, not depth of interpretation, until the person can think without washing.

2014-191.sentence: OSA with enuresis, snoring, and large tonsils is fragmenting sleep, so the child cannot hold a good-enough night and looks impulsive by day. Fix the airway first; ADHD as a split-off “bad child” label is the relationship story you do not buy until breathing is restored.

2014-192.sentence: Negative reinforcement is the nagging stopping when the bow moves; the child projects the harsh parent into the room and then practices to repair the threat. Depressive concern would be practicing because the music matters, not because the aversive object must be made to go away.

2014-193.sentence: When the group starts risking self-disclosure and questioning your competence, they are recruiting you as the parent who will either collapse or punish. Name that testing—that is transference: an old authority scene lived in the room—rather than proving you are a good leader or slamming the lid back on Forming-level politeness.

2014-194.sentence: Fluctuating ptosis and jaw fatigue are not a conversion of conflict into a body story; acetylcholine-receptor antibodies are blocking the neuromuscular junction. Do not treat the weakness as a symbolic symptom until you have ruled out myasthenia.

2014-195.sentence: Not recognizing the family after the partner's assault is the mind's emergency exit: dissociative amnesia erases the people who make the trauma real. Intact identity, intact cognition, and a normal CT say this is protection by not-knowing, not a left temporal contusion.

2014-196.sentence: Prazosin blocks alpha-1 receptors so the nocturnal noradrenergic surge cannot restage the trauma as a nightmare. You are damping the body's night alarm, not handing the veteran a benzodiazepine that blurs sleep without metabolizing the scene.

2014-197.sentence: Tinnitus plus deep, rapid breathing names aspirin, not acetaminophen or lorazepam. In a young overdose that household pill can be the superego's sentence—the harsh conscience that punishes the body with a medicine everyone keeps in the cabinet.

2014-198.sentence: After a first break the family will try to make you either the oracle of cure or the prophet of inevitable decline. Emphasizing staying on antipsychotics is the transference job: you become the steady object who holds schizophrenia as treatable, not a verdict of chronic collapse.

2014-199.sentence: Lung cancer reaching the brain is the body saying what speech never could: a silent invasion that shows up as headache, seizure, and a personality that no longer feels like the person. Metastasis is unrepresented experience made flesh—the tumor writes itself into cortex because nothing in the history was ever given words.

2014-200.sentence: Five-year-olds sit on the hinge between initiative and industry: kindergarten asks them to produce, wait, and belong in a group, and home is where leftover baby-need is allowed to leak. The clinginess and regression are not a diagnosis; they are the child parking the leftover of the old stage so the new psychosocial task can start at school.

2014-201.sentence: Anhedonia in melancholia is not just a sad mood; it is a shutdown of wanting, as if pleasure itself had become dangerous or pointless. The symptom empties the day of incentive so the person does not have to risk desire, appetite, or morning hope.

2014-202.sentence: Naltrexone is an opioid antagonist: it occupies the receptor and refuses the high, which is a developmental capacity some patients never quite grew—saying no to a need that once felt like life itself. You are asking an adult ego to do what a child could not: tolerate craving without a chemical parent.

2014-203.sentence: Paroxetine next to lithium can keep punching holes in the mood stabilizer’s work; stopping it is the conscience of the regimen, the part that admits the helper became a saboteur. The superego move is not adding more drugs for guilt about “not doing enough,” but withdrawing the agent that licensed the cycling.

2014-204.sentence: Poor insight after a first schizophrenia diagnosis recruits you into the role of the only one who still believes there is an illness, while the patient lives in a world where the antipsychotic is an insult. Notice the countertransference pull to argue or abandon; that heat is the dyad acting out the lost awareness instead of naming it.

2014-205.sentence: Pathologic gambling, hypersexuality, and binge spending on a dopamine agonist such as pramipexole are not “just a choice.” They are an unrepresented state: a drive that never becomes a thought, so it is acted in the body and the marriage. Name the agonist and the ruin out loud, or the couple will keep repeating the crash instead of mourning what the medicine took.

2014-206.sentence: Taijin kyofusho sits at the collision of a wish to be seen and a prohibition against offending the group, so the odor becomes the compromise. Social phobia, body dysmorphic disorder, and somatic delusional disorder are the DSM neighbors because each is a different intensity of that same wish–shame fight.

2014-207.sentence: Low CSF hypocretin is a hole in the self’s continuity: sleep slams the door mid-meal, mid-talk, mid-drive, so mirroring and competence collapse without warning. The spouse’s report is the missing mirror—hold that humiliation as the real injury, not only the orexin number.

2014-208.sentence: Playing doctor, naptime masturbation, bathroom peeking, and asking to see a peer’s genitals are thinkable curiosity. Mimicking intercourse is raw, undigested adult sexuality dumped into play—contain it as possible exposure or enactment, not as “just preschool.”

2014-209.sentence: Down syndrome is the most common genetic cause of intellectual disability, and that fact is also a termination: some timelines cannot be rushed or parented away. The work is mourning the child they imagined so they can stay with the child they have.

2014-210.sentence: Fluvoxamine is the SSRI most likely to jam CYP and spike tacrolimus, warfarin, and theophylline. Ego strength here is knowing your own limits: pick a quieter SSRI rather than proving you can “handle” a metabolic pileup.

2014-211.sentence: Carbohydrate-deficient transferrin (CDT) can hold the drinking that the patient has split off: a vertical split, meaning the mind keeps the daily five-plus drinks in a separate compartment so they can sit in your office and mean it when they say they cut back. You are not catching a liar so much as offering a lab that lets the dissociated part of the story re-enter the room without forcing a confession.

2014-212.sentence: Before you and dermatology lock into treating imaginary lice, ask about recreational alcohol and drugs—stimulants especially—because the infestation fight is already an enactment: two people living the old pursuit-and-refusal instead of naming what is happening. Substance-induced formication is the exit from that two-person repetition; antipsychotic mandates and forced psychiatry only thicken the chase.

2014-213.sentence: Habit reversal therapy trains the child to notice the premonitory urge and swap in a competing movement—suppression used as a skill, not as white-knuckle denial. The tic is not being psychoanalyzed away; the ego is learning a pause between urge and discharge, which is why this is first-line for mild-to-moderate tics before meds.

2014-214.sentence: Lorazepam is the first-line medicine here because catatonia with waxy flexibility is the mind holding two impossible objects at once: the need to act and the terror of acting, frozen as a statue. You do not add an antipsychotic that can worsen catatonia; you give a benzodiazepine that loosens the freeze so the person can rejoin a living relationship with food, meds, and you.

2014-215.sentence: A reflective statement exists to ensure that what the patient said was understood—support first, not challenge, not interpretation, not a hunt for more details. Early in the work this mind can use a mirror more than a probe; if you keep firing questions you raise the uncovering dose past what the interview can metabolize.

2014-216.sentence: Kleine-Levin syndrome—the adolescent hypersomnia with megaphagia and a dull, withdrawn presence despite a structurally normal sleep EEG—pulls the family into a two-person pattern of watching a child vanish into sleep. You treat the diagnosis as a shared interpersonal event: parents stop moralizing laziness, and you stop chasing narcolepsy or Klüver–Bucy, so the boy is not left alone inside a syndrome everyone else is arguing about.

2014-217.sentence: College-plus-hardship is a double bind: two contradictory messages at once, so Betty cannot move toward school without feeling she is injuring the people who are supposed to be her secure base. Attachment-wise, proximity to the parents then costs autonomy, and staying close costs the future they just praised—so protest and freeze make more sense than “indecision.”

2014-218.sentence: Clozapine is not only an antipsychotic here; it is the one agent shown to cut suicide in schizophrenia, so the “meaning” of the prescription is a concrete bid to keep the person alive. When other atypicals have failed that job, staying on olanzapine or quetiapine can function as a quiet bargain with risk rather than a treatment of it.

2014-219.sentence: This sits on Erikson’s integrity-versus-despair: late life is the work of keeping dignity while accepting real limits, and driving is often the last symbol of adult competence. Consulting state reporting law is how you hold both sides of that stage—you do not steal autonomy by fiat, and you do not abandon the public (or the patient) to a failing ego function.

2014-220.sentence: Inattentive ADHD next to a reading disability is often wrapped in denial: the child (and sometimes the school) treats “I just don’t like reading” as if attention and decoding were intact. Naming ADHD, inattentive type, undercuts that defense so the delay is treated as a brain-and-skill problem, not as laziness or a character flaw.

2014-221.sentence: Modeling is already an enactment in the waiting room: fear shrinks when another child lives the ride as fun, and the phobic child borrows that regulation instead of arguing with the fear. You are not just teaching a learning principle—you are staging a two-person scene where courage is caught by watching, which is why peer demo beats a lecture about bikes.

2014-222.sentence: IPT’s frame is present-tense relationships, not schemas, childhood insight, relaxation drills, or Rogerian reflection—so the limit you hold is “we work the interpersonal problem.” Increasing contacts and strengthening the friendships she already has is the technique that keeps that frame, instead of sliding into CBT, psychodynamic excavation, or nonspecific warmth.

2014-223.sentence: The clock that dumps every numeral onto one half of the circle is not just a visuospatial fail; it is a unilateral world the parietal lesion has edited out, so the empty side never even becomes a demand. Treat the bedside clock as a relationship to space: the neglected half is the part of reality the patient cannot use you to hold.

2014-224.sentence: Modafinil once in the morning is a reliable wake-anchor, not another stimulant binge like methamphetamine twice daily or leftover cocaine. Give it as a secure base for alertness so the year of being clean does not have to be held together by naps, caffeine, or a hypnotic that never treats sleep-onset REM.

2014-225.sentence: Malpractice is a two-person story the court will hear under a preponderance of the evidence, not beyond a reasonable doubt: more likely than not that duty, dereliction, damages, and direct causation sit between you. The suit is the relationship continuing in a new room—the plaintiff and you are still arguing about who failed whom.

2014-226.sentence: Fifty milligrams of trazodone can knock someone out on H1 while the serotonin transporter is barely touched, so the antidepressant job is still split off and unoccupied. Pushing the hypnotic dose as if it were already an SSRI is pretending the two functions live in the same place when they do not.

2014-227.sentence: A thiazide just added for blood pressure can shove a years-stable lithium level to 1.6 and take the ego with it: tremor, dysarthria, and confusion are impulse control and reality testing failing in real time. Acetaminophen and energy drinks do not do this; the new diuretic is the change the coping system could not metabolize.

2014-228.sentence: The side effect you must name first in a 78-year-old referred for ECT is cognitive dysfunction, not fractures or dental trauma. Memory gaps after treatment can leave the illness as something that happened to the body while the story of the depression cannot be held in words.

2014-229.sentence: Hope and the wish to be well are still colliding with a hard prohibition: she must now accept that treatment has failed and only dying remains. Validating the grief as a normal reaction treats that collision as work, not as a suicidal plan or a “distorted” thought you need to CBT away.

2014-230.sentence: The emergency-department frame includes a sequence you do not skip: give thiamine before or with glucose, not D5W alone. Once ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and confusion appear, the limit is medical, not optional vitamins like niacin or folate.

2014-231.sentence: A well-defined parent–child boundary is the family’s way of knowing who holds authority and who can still speak. That structure lets people see their own part without the kids running the marriage or the parents collapsing into peers.

2014-232.sentence: Directed masturbation, sometimes with a vibrator, treats female orgasmic disorder by taking orgasm out of the couple’s gaze so inhibition can loosen. The defense is often a freeze of excitement under a partner’s eye; practice alone lets sensation return before it has to survive another person.

2014-233.sentence: A lesion of the inferior frontal gyrus (Broca’s area) leaves the wish to speak intact while chopping the words into effortful, telegraphic scraps. The relationship here is with the damaged motor-speech cortex, not with a pill you offer as comfort.

2014-234.sentence: The church group is a selfobject: it mirrors her as more than a caregiver and props up a self that Alzheimer care is grinding down. Telling her to keep going protects that source of esteem; cheerleading or blaming her frustration would leave her more depleted.

2014-235.sentence: Asking for a clozapine or haloperidol plasma level is the collision of two drives: the wish to know the drug is actually in the body, and the wish not to be caught, dosed, or found out. Those two agents earned the level because the wish for certainty and the prohibition against guessing both have a number you can name.

2014-236.sentence: Three lifetime major-depressive episodes is a hard stop, not a negotiation: the illness has already shown it will return if you treat remission like a finish line. Maintenance pharmacotherapy is the limit you hold so the patient does not have to test ending one more time.

2014-237.sentence: The older camper took in the child's raw jealousy of the gifted sibling and handed it back as something thinkable: a martial-arts skill instead of nameless rivalry. That is sublimation after containment—the envy got metabolized into practice rather than dumped back onto the brother or sister.

2014-238.sentence: Clang associations let sound police the sentence when meaning would have to answer for itself: a strong song, a throng, who do not belong. In mania the conscience loosens its grip on sense, so rhyme becomes the new rule and you document the music, not a thought.

2014-239.sentence: Interferon can knock out a mood-holding capacity that adulthood assumed was already there, especially in melanoma or hepatitis C protocols. New depression here is not a late developmental arrival of insight; it is an immunomodulator stripping a function the patient still needs.

2014-240.sentence: A trial comment about desire, partnership, or 'what sex means now' is fair, and it does not replace testosterone when the finding is postmenopausal hypoactive desire. Psychological mindedness includes seeing that this symptom has a hormone you can name, not only a story you can interpret.

2014-241.sentence: Valproate is the only common mood stabilizer that roughly doubles lamotrigine by blocking its glucuronidation, so the usual titration is not a neutral “start low, go slow”—it is the frame holding the rash-and-SJS risk you now share with the patient. Write the halved schedule into the plan before the first lamotrigine tablet, the same way you would write a fee or a session length: the limit is what keeps the add-on from becoming a stealth overdose.

2014-242.sentence: The pill you are asked to “do something with” on this C-L bed is not a feed or a poison yet—the EMG already named the illness: slow conduction, long distal latency, and conduction block of acute inflammatory polyneuropathy, Guillain-Barré. Your job in the relationship is to refuse a psychotropic just to look useful, and to stay with the patient while neurology watches the diaphragm; the demand for a medicine is often a demand not to feel helpless.

2014-243.sentence: Those cartoonish, fantastic “hallucinations” of conversion are a defense: the mind stages a childish scene so the fight with the partner never has to be felt as rage or loss. Unlike a psychotic hallucination, the vision is psychologically meaningful theater with intact reality testing—the patient is not reluctant, not multi-modal-psychotic, and not describing a single dry sensory fragment.

2014-244.sentence: Lithium overdose hits the cerebellum hard enough to leave lasting ataxia; the wish to end the pain and the prohibition against dying collide in a tremor that may not fully go away. The leftover dysarthria is not only neurology—it is the body keeping the record of a drive that broke the dose instead of speaking the wish.

2014-245.sentence: An 85-year-old with dementia who newly screams “fire” at the bedside lamp is not asking you to restore a grandiose self with lorazepam; the first competent, esteem-protecting move is a urinalysis for delirium. Naming a UTI as the thief of mind is mirroring: you treat the insult to the self instead of sedating the person who is already losing coherence.

2014-246.sentence: A BAC of 0.425 with stupor is nameless dread poured into the brainstem: respiratory failure is the immediate container you must hold, not DTs, seizures, or tomorrow’s liver. Sit with the airway first so the raw fact “this dose can stop breathing” becomes a thinkable plan rather than an evacuation into “he’ll sleep it off.”

2014-247.sentence: The referring doctor's "special patient who needs really good treatment" is already a demand that you skip an ordinary start and become the extra-good object overnight. Hold the limit: you cannot rush a new therapy into "taking," and that hurry is how splitting between the old psychiatrist and you gets lived instead of named.

2014-248.sentence: The anterior cerebral artery feeds the medial frontal lobe and paracentral lobule, the tissue that lets a person initiate a step, a void, or a willed thought. After an ACA infarct that capacity drops out as contralateral leg weakness with a spared face and arm, incontinence, and abulia: initiative that had arrived is suddenly gone.

2014-249.sentence: Factitious disorder is a conscience bargain: being the patient is the allowed identity, so symptoms are produced to be recognized as ill, not to collect a check. Malingering uses the same conscious deception for external gain; the distinguishing motive is whether the sick role has been sanctioned as the moral solution.

2014-250.sentence: When the parents bolt without a warm goodbye, they dump the pain of leaving into the ten-month-old instead of holding it. The infant then cannot keep one parent who is both loved and departing, so clinging and avoidance appear together—the paranoid-schizoid split of a needed caregiver and a dangerous one.

2014-251.sentence: The patient cannot hold "we were both at fault," so the other driver becomes all-bad and slashing the tires is revenge that restores a clean split. Tarasoff is not triggered by a property threat with no identifiable serious bodily harm, so there is no legal duty to warn, hospitalize, or call the employer.

2014-252.sentence: rTMS is a supportive, non-uncovering treatment: you stimulate cortex; you do not excavate conflict. The technique has a hard ceiling—push intensity or frequency past what this brain can take and the most serious adverse effect is a seizure, not a headache or a scalp burn.

2014-253.sentence: The outbursts and morning stomachaches live in the child–school pair, not only in the parents’ story of a well-behaved home. A release to speak with the teacher is how you get the other person in the pattern, instead of treating the child as a one-person mind.

2014-254.sentence: Wernicke encephalopathy from thiamine (vitamin B1) knocks out gaze, gait, and orientation—the tools a person uses to stay aimed at another human. Give IV thiamine first so you become a usable secure base while the mammillary-body circuitry comes back online.

2014-255.sentence: Saying “Hi Daddy” into a toy phone is symbolic representation: the ego can let one object stand for an absent person. That is affect tolerance in action—the child holds Daddy in mind instead of needing the real body in the room.

2014-256.sentence: Specific phobia is the anxiety disorder that most often starts in childhood, when the mind is still sorting real danger from imagined danger. Binding fear to one object (dogs, dark, needles) is a developmental bargain: one fenced-off threat so the rest of the child’s world can stay usable.

2014-257.sentence: Bleuler coined “schizophrenia” to name a split in associations, not Kraepelin’s dementia praecox of inevitable decay. Keep saying dementia praecox with the student and you two are already in an enactment: living Kraepelin’s hopeless script instead of thinking with Bleuler’s word.

2014-258.sentence: A case-control study starts with babies who have Ebstein’s anomaly and looks backward for psychotropic exposure, including lithium. That is isolation of affect in research clothes: you reconstruct the feared heart defect after the fact so you do not have to sit inside a prospective pregnancy and wait.

2014-259.sentence: The hypnotic already felt like poison: it knocked her out and left her groggy, so she stopped trusting anything you put in her mouth. EEG biofeedback for insomnia, beating progressive muscle relaxation in the trials, offers a different feed—she trains her own rhythms instead of swallowing proof that she is helpless.

2014-260.sentence: Crushing, snorting, or injecting the prescribed opioid is already an enactment: the two of you are living the old fight—more drug versus more control—instead of talking about pain and fear. Tolerance, late-dose withdrawal, and climbing milligrams are expected physiology; the route change is the relationship going underground.

2014-261.sentence: A subpoena is a demand at the door, not a court order; without the patient's consent you oppose it and hold the frame—the agreed boundary of who hears what.
