Calling the lawyer or handing the chart to a surrogate still leaks the session and teaches that the room collapses when the system knocks.

2014-262.sentence: Folic acid looks like a kind feed: the MCV comes down and everyone feels they did something. It is also a poison of reassurance, because the red-cell numbers normalize while B12 deficiency keeps chewing the cord and the mind.

2014-263.sentence: Staying on valproate while he still thinks about dying can be denial: the suicide risk is treated as already handled because the mood looks quieter. Lithium is the one mood stabilizer with the firmest long-term anti-suicide signal, so naming it is the opposite of that defense—you look at the lethal wish instead of covering it.

2014-264.sentence: He wants sildenafil as a clean fix and may not see his own part: the sublingual nitroglycerin already in his pocket. A trial comment is simple—“that nitrate plus a PDE5 inhibitor can drop the pressure dangerously”—and you watch whether he can use the fact or only want the pill.

2014-265.sentence: Wraparound holds the frame by refusing the usual office-only contract: formal mental health sits next to informal community support, and the team—not the court or the school—owns the limit. That is ethics in action: you treat the child’s serious emotional disturbance inside a web of people who can actually keep time, safety, and care going between sessions.

2014-266.sentence: Internuclear ophthalmoplegia is the unthinkable sensation—vertigo, diplopia, one eye that will not adduct—until you name the medial longitudinal fasciculus lesion. That naming is containment: the raw dread of “something is wrong with my eyes” becomes a thinkable diagnosis of multiple sclerosis instead of nameless neurologic chaos.

2014-267.sentence: Avoidant personality wants the relationship and still cannot take the last step; schizoid personality does not want it, so there is nothing to wait for. Termination thinking helps here: desire is present, but the capacity to bear rejection cannot be rushed, and the work is staying at that limit without calling the stall indifference.

2014-268.sentence: Copropraxia is an intrusive obscene gesture from chronic tics, not a cultural message aimed at you, your gender, or the class of the room. If you treat the gesture as identity or insult, you invent a third that is not there; the live third is the tic disorder, and the documentation should say copropraxia, not echopraxia or a parapraxis.

2014-269.sentence: At nine, the job is industry versus inferiority: grades, being “good enough,” and a voice that says he is bad all sit on that task. Major depressive disorder with a mood-congruent hallucination is the collapse of that work, not childhood-onset schizophrenia and not a character problem of never being pleased.

2014-270.sentence: The consult arrives as if the intravenous methamphetamine and the sad story were the feed you were hired to swallow. The real demand is the spinal epidural abscess at L2–L3—fever, percussion tenderness, paraparesis, saddle sensory loss, incontinence—and sending you a “depression” request can be a way to poison the work by asking psychiatry to metabolize a neurosurgical emergency.

2014-271.sentence: The frame here is honesty: you do not “protect” a dying child by keeping the diagnosis off the table. Silence leaves him alone with what he already senses, and it steals the last bit of autonomy he has left.

2014-272.sentence: The unit is already in an enactment: everyone is treating the low mood as if it were a depression that needs another psychotropic. Name the snoring and the unrefreshing sleep, then get the CPAP on—positive pressure is the treatment, not another antidepressant debate.

2014-273.sentence: Calling every lawyer a demon is not just a delusion; it is a defense that walls off the helper so he never has to face the court. That refusal wrecks the Dusky second prong: he cannot consult with counsel, so he is incompetent to stand trial.

2014-274.sentence: Quitting asks more ego strength than a patch can supply: he has to tolerate craving without acting. Bupropion plus group therapy is the pairing that actually holds the affect and the habit at the same time.

2014-275.sentence: Most new tics in a 7-year-old are a brief, self-limited twitch of the developing motor system, not a hidden self that has left the room. Start with clinical monitoring; habit reversal and meds wait until the tic proves it is staying.

2014-276.sentence: The flu-shot reminder is something you and the patient do together before anyone is sick—that is primary prevention, not a rescue after the fact. You are using the relationship as a public-health tool: you keep showing up so the shot actually happens.

2014-277.sentence: Hypnotizability is not a trait you infer from gender, ethnicity, WAIS-IV IQ, or the MMPI-2; it tracks the capacity to engage imagination, which is how a person lets another mind become a temporary secure base. In hypnosis the voice of the clinician is used the way an attached child uses a caregiver: to regulate attention and body state from the outside until the inner scene can hold.

2014-278.sentence: Nocturnal pins-and-needles that shake out of the hand is carpal tunnel until proven otherwise, and the countertransference trap is letting yourself be recruited as the doctor who treats it as anxiety or “neuropathy.” That recruitment is the old medical-psych split: you become the dismissive listener while the median nerve keeps waking her.

2014-279.sentence: Rerouting the commute away from the usual bar is stimulus control, a CBT relapse-prevention move that outsources conscience to the map so the patient is not left alone with a brittle “just don’t drink” command. The superego here is too thin to win a nightly stare-down with the tavern; changing the route is the ethical work done in geography instead of guilt.

2014-280.sentence: Federal 42 CFR Part 2 holds substance use treatment records to a stricter confidentiality bar than suicidality, homicidality, psychosis, or ECT notes, because the law treats SUD shame as a special risk of exposure. That extra legal conscience exists so a subpoena cannot casually turn treatment into public punishment.

2014-281.sentence: Asking the enrolled MS patient’s spouse to join as a healthy control threatens voluntarism: free, uncoerced yes, not autonomy, capacity, or the information sheet. In the room you are being recruited as the kindly researcher who “just needs one more control,” while the spouse is pressured into the loyal-partner role and cannot easily refuse.

2014-282.sentence: Mood is the one MSE heading that lives in the patient’s words (“I feel empty”); affect, appearance, insight, and even much of thought content you infer from what you see and hear. After trauma, the named mood can be a thin label over what the body is still repeating, so quote the report and separately describe the observed affect.

2014-283.sentence: Normalization names the collision without forcing a confession: the wish to discharge tension (scream, hit) and the prohibition against harming a partner sit in the same sentence. By saying stressed people sometimes do things they did not intend, you give the suicidal patient and spouse a way to report intimate-partner violence without first having to own the forbidden impulse as uniquely theirs.

2014-284.sentence: Childhood absence with fast eyelid flutter steals seconds of being-seen; valproic acid (or ethosuximide, if that were a choice) is what restores a continuous self the parent can actually mirror. Competence and self-esteem in a six-year-old are built in those unbroken stretches of attention, not in the blank stares.

2014-285.sentence: A K-complex is the cortex briefly containing a knock at the door of sleep so the stimulus can be registered without becoming full waking; sleep spindles then hold the night together as N2. Nameless dread evacuated as arousal would be a wake-up; these waveforms are the brain metabolizing the raw hit into something stay-asleep-able.

2014-286.sentence: Progressive supranuclear palsy announces a limit you cannot coach away: early falls, axial rigidity, knees locked, and an en-bloc pivot because the body will not make a gradual turn. Termination here is neurologic, not motivational—the downward gaze and the flexible step are capacities that will not arrive if you just give more time.

2014-287.sentence: This patient can already hold a trial comment: the chest burning might be benign, and still the mind snaps back to a missed infarct. CBT has the best evidence because it uses that sliver of psychological mindedness—seeing one's own catastrophic appraisal as a move, not as a coronary—rather than more reassurance or fewer cardiology visits.

2014-288.sentence: Effect size is the size of what the two intervention groups actually do to each other, the magnitude of their difference, not the p-value's permission slip that they are 'related.' Journal club is a two-person sport: significance says the pattern is unlikely to be noise; effect size says how much the treatment and the control really moved apart.

2014-289.sentence: This is not a mind that can use uncovering tonight: metoclopramide’s D2 blockade in the basal ganglia is writing the protruding tongue and torticollis, so interpret the gesture and you miss an acute dystonia. Support means name the drug, give anticholinergic rescue, and only later ask what the nausea story was.

2014-290.sentence: The myoclonus and rapid collapse are not a symbolic protest; prion protein is punching cytosolic vacuoles through neurons and glia until the cortex cannot hold a self. Treat the finding as meaning-of-the-lesion, not meaning-of-the-wish: spongiform change explains why the person is disappearing faster than grief can organize.

2014-291.sentence: Twenty years of drinking has parked adult life on the far side of generativity—the Erikson task of caring forward—so the bottle, not a vocation, has been the organizing project. Withdrawal seizures at twelve hours come in clusters, multiple brief generalized runs, which means the first job is to hold the body through that barrage before you ask what generation he never quite joined.

2014-292.sentence: Marginalization is the cultural third in the room: no live allegiance to the native culture and no real uptake of the host, so there is no group ego to borrow when despair hits. That nowhere-identity is why suicide, alcohol, and other substances cluster here—not because someone “chose” the wrong customs, but because no we remains to metabolize shame.

2014-293.sentence: Years of low-grade gloom is already a stuck depressive position: he works, but concern for damaged objects never quite turns into repair. The last month’s bedbound hopelessness and suicidal pull is double depression—a major episode stacked on dysthymia—when that thin capacity to mourn collapses into a more ruthless attack on the self.

2014-294.sentence: Temazepam does not bury a night in repression; as a benzodiazepine it blocks encoding, so the hours never become a memory that could be retrieved. That is an unrepresented state made by the pill: anterograde amnesia, not trauma dissociation, which is why you do not pick it when the mind already cannot hold a continuous self after dark.

2014-295.sentence: That lens-shaped epidural clot is recruiting you as the one who must notice the lucid interval before the crash—countertransference here is the urge to reassure because she looks fine. Name the feeling and stay with the CT: a biconvex extra-axial bleed after trauma is not a time to become the soothing bystander.

2014-296.sentence: An alcohol blackout is anterograde amnesia while the person stays awake and talking—the superego, the inner judge, often treats that gap as a moral loophole rather than a memory failure. The conscience then either pummels him for what he cannot recall or quietly licenses the next binge because 'I wasn't really there.

2014-297.sentence: Prenatal maternal tobacco is a perinatal hit on attention systems that should have come online more cleanly in childhood. ADHD here is not only genes: a capacity for sustained focus arrived late, or thinner, because nicotine exposure in utero taxed that developmental line.

2014-298.sentence: Declining the Facebook request protects the frame: fee, time, and a one-way window, not a mutual social feed. Ego strength in the psychiatrist is the capacity to tolerate the patient's disappointment without collapsing into friend-mode or hiding behind 'privacy' as the only reason.

2014-299.sentence: A pure sensory lacune in the lateral thalamus can split the body at the midline—half the self is numb, as if sensation left without the person leaving the chair. That is a neurological dissociation of the somatosensory map, not a conversion; the VPL/VPM relay is offline.

2014-300.sentence: Kohlberg's highest stage judges action by universal ethical principles, not by the social contract or keeping order. The frame question is who holds the limit when principle and institutional rule collide—you still name the law, but you do not pretend Stage 4 is the ceiling.

2015-1.sentence: Nonmaleficence is the frame holding the limit when the ICU wants a drug and the heart cannot take it: you refuse the antipsychotic because QT prolongation plus bradycardia is already a harm waiting to happen. The team’s urgency can pull you into doing something; the ethic is to stay still until a safer plan exists.

2015-2.sentence: If you and the patient spend the hour proving alters, you are already in an enactment: living the hidden-self drama instead of talking about what is missing. Track the amnesia—the extensive inability to recall personal information—because that gap is the illness, not the performance of other personalities.

2015-3.sentence: Reaching for methylphenidate or modafinil is acting out: swapping one chemical booster for another so the deadline never has to meet withdrawal. Cut caffeine by 25% weekly and the ego stays in charge—he still works, and the dependence comes down on a schedule instead of a crash.

2015-4.sentence: The Eye opener on CAGE is the drink as a morning feed: alcohol has become the first object that proves the body cannot start the day. That is not a hangover tip; it is the relationship announcing that the bottle now holds the wake-up function.

2015-5.sentence: You hold the limit before the refill: valproate and a planned pregnancy do not share a prescription pad because neural tube defects are the known fetal cost. Stability on the drug is not a reason to keep the frame; it is the reason to change the regimen first.

2015-6.sentence: Nihilistic delusions in late-onset psychotic depression capture insight: if the bowels have stopped and the self is already rotting, there is no “I am depressed” left to work with. A trial comment about mood will bounce; you treat the delusion and the not-eating first, then see whether a mind that can look at itself returns.

2015-7.sentence: Tic severity usually crests in school years and starts to ease in adolescence, so the nine-year-old’s worsening is still on the typical clock, not a signal that time has run out. Hold the parents’ panic without rushing a med jump: the developmental limit here is that you cannot force the tic course to finish early, only contain the year until adolescence does some of the work.

2015-8.sentence: The finding that keeps showing up is the therapeutic alliance, not the diploma or the fancier manual. That alliance is Bion’s container: you take in the resident’s (and the patient’s) raw dread that nothing is working and give it back as a thinkable problem—stay in the relationship—rather than evacuating the feeling by switching therapies.

2015-9.sentence: Clozapine is the antipsychotic tied to fewer completed suicides, including after risperidone and olanzapine have failed. Prescribing it can restore a bit of idealizable competence: the patient gets a real, evidence-backed protector instead of another empty promise that leaves self-esteem in pieces.

2015-10.sentence: Awake EEG beta often means sedatives—benzodiazepines and barbiturates—not a hidden seizure focus. The team’s hunt for something more exotic can be a harsh superego: a need to prove they did not miss a crime, when the conscience-saving move is the boring one of reading the med list.

2015-11.sentence: Homosexuality left the DSM as a disorder only with DSM-III-R in 1987; the 1970s cut in DSM-II still left ego-dystonic homosexuality on the books. Notice the countertransference pull to be the resident’s reassuring historian who erases that leftover stigma, instead of naming who you are being asked to become—the clean 1970s rescuer.

2015-12.sentence: In chronic PTSD with childhood-abuse dissociation, hypnosis is for volitional control of leaving the body, not for burying, rewriting, or amnestizing the abuse. Unrepresented trauma returns as lost time and dangerous driving; the work is to put a hand on the switch so the body does not have to repeat what cannot yet be remembered as a story.

2015-13.sentence: Do not treat this as a wish colliding with a prohibition. The malar rash, proteinuria, fever, pancytopenia, and pleural effusions name lupus cerebritis, and the visual-plus-auditory hallucinations with disorientation and one-of-three recall are a failing sensorium, not a neurotic compromise. Interpreting “persecution” as drive conflict here would miss the brain on fire.

2015-14.sentence: Pseudocyesis puts gender and the cultural demand to become a mother in the room as a third: her body produces amenorrhea, nausea, breast fullness, and a swollen belly as if that script were already true. The negative pregnancy test and empty ultrasound do not end the conviction because the identity stake is “I am supposed to be pregnant,” not a lab result.

2015-15.sentence: Alcohol hallucinosis sits on a later Erikson task: keeping a coherent self in time. Voices can roar and the person can still stay oriented, which is the intact sensorium that separates this from delirium tremens. Fever, seizure, agitation, and tachycardia mark the collapse of that holding function, not the diagnosis you want.

2015-16.sentence: The suicidality is doing work: it marks the pain of a lifelong female identification colliding with a body that still has male genitals despite breast implants. That is gender dysphoria, not schizophrenia, transvestic disorder, or body dysmorphic nitpicking of a single feature.

2015-17.sentence: Sensate focusing is homework that rebuilds a childhood capacity: curious touch without a performance goal. By banning breasts and genitals at first, you let the couple recover exploratory play before intercourse became a pass/fail exam.

2015-18.sentence: The family and the patient are now a two-person persecution system: they experience a hostile, withdrawn elder, and the patient experiences alien thought insertion and control. A MOCA of 28/30 and an MRI with only age-related involution keep this as late-life schizophrenia, not a dementia the relatives can carry alone.

2015-19.sentence: Recurrent major depressive episodes are a signal to stay supportive and keep the SSRI going rather than to peel back more history once the patient is well. Each extra episode is the mind telling you it cannot yet hold the depression without a chemical scaffold, so maintenance is technique, not a vote of no confidence.

2015-20.sentence: Ages one to three are Freud’s anal window: the child wants it now, and the parent has to teach delay of gratification around toileting and “by myself.” That tug-of-war is how a toddler first learns a mind can wait, not a trauma to erase.

2015-21.sentence: Imipramine’s overdose punch is voltage-gated sodium-channel blockade, which widens the QRS and can drop the heart—you are not being asked to be the calm interpreter of a suicide attempt until the ECG is safe. The countertransference pull is to moralize or to soothe; the job first is to treat the channel block, then to sit with whoever you just became in that room.

2015-22.sentence: Naltrexone blunts alcohol’s reward so craving does not keep humiliating a self that already wants to stay sober. You are lending a bit of borrowed competence: the medicine holds the urge while self-esteem rebuilds in the intensive outpatient work.

2015-23.sentence: Race on the form tracks visible physical categories; ethnicity is the thicker mix of language, religion, nation, and family practice—Haitian, Catholic, Creole, not just “Black.” Keep both, or you flatten a person into a checkbox and miss how they actually live.

2015-24.sentence: REM sleep behavior disorder with dream enactment points to synuclein inclusions, often years before Parkinson disease or Lewy body dementia shows its face. You cannot rush that clock; name the protein and the limit, then plan for a long neurodegenerative arc rather than a one-visit sleep fix.

2015-25.sentence: Lithium does not just "lower the seizure threshold" in a tidy way; with ECT it can keep the fit going past what the brain can finish, so you abort it and then take lithium off the list. That extra, unstoppable discharge is like raw dread that never gets named: the stimulus arrives and cannot be metabolized into a thinkable, bounded event.

2015-26.sentence: They asked you to manage suicidal ideation; your job is to hold that request and still name the real emergency: serotonin syndrome from linezolid plus sertraline (lithium and fever just muddy the picture). The frame is who sets the agenda—you do not treat the consult question while the MAOI-like antibiotic and the SSRI keep cooking the patient.

2015-27.sentence: A delusion of reference means the TV is not just on; it is aimed at them, so there is no leftover "maybe I am reading myself into this." You cannot trial-comment that until they can stand a sliver of ownership; right now the message lives entirely outside, in the news anchor.

2015-28.sentence: Disulfiram works when someone else actually watches the swallow—classically the partner—so the pill is not left to a lonely good intention that evaporates by evening. The partner holds both sides of the object: care that wants you sober and a limit that will not let you sneak the drink and the tablet apart.

2015-29.sentence: Intellectual disability is the comorbidity you plan around in autism, not a side note, because it sets how much the mind can use interpretation versus structure. You support function, language, and safety; you do not uncover conflict as if this were a neurotic child who just needs insight.

2015-30.sentence: Circumstantial speech still lands the job description; the long detour through the boss and coworkers is the cost of getting there. The extra stories buy time so a simple question does not feel like a demand to be pinned down in one clean sentence.

2015-31.sentence: Denial is doing the work here: the year of “successful” weight loss after bariatric surgery is treated as proof nothing is missing, so cobalamin depletion never becomes a worry until the cord speaks. The finding itself is the punchline of that defense—spasticity, clonus, extensor plantars plus lost vibration and joint-position sense—because B12 is what the dorsal columns and corticospinal tracts needed all along.

2015-32.sentence: Parents often have insight only into the loud half of combined ADHD—the oppositional-defiant fights—and none into the child’s own anxious part. A trial comment that names both comorbidities (“the arguing we see, and the worry he may not show”) tests whether they can use that second piece, not just the behavior chart.

2015-33.sentence: The frame is the evidence, not the gadget: EEG biofeedback is an efficacious option for generalized anxiety disorder, not a free pass for PTSD, OCD, agoraphobia, or acute stress. You hold that limit when a patient who hates pills asks for neurofeedback—you can offer it for GAD, and you do not stretch the indication to keep them in the chair.

2015-34.sentence: Valproate holds lamotrigine in the body by blocking glucuronidation, so the usual titration is already too much raw drug for the skin to metabolize. Containment here is concrete: cut the start and the target dose in half so the load stays thinkable, instead of evacuating as a rash.

2015-35.sentence: Mid-adolescence has a sexual timetable you cannot rush: a typically developing 15-year-old boy’s masturbatory fantasy is of explicit sexual acts, not the romantic stories or partner-response scenes of later years. The parent’s wish to end that rawness is a wish to terminate a phase that still has time left on the clock.

2015-36.sentence: The wish is to treat; the prohibition is that this is not your patient. What distinguishes the forensic exam from a general psychiatric evaluation is maintenance of confidentiality—you do not keep the usual clinical seal, because the evaluee was never in a treatment relationship with you.

2015-37.sentence: Each escape from the grocery aisle is negative reinforcement: the panic drop rewards flight, so the self never has to stay present while anxiety peaks. In self-psychology terms she is protecting a shaky sense of competence—better to be the person who “handles it by leaving” than to risk a public collapse that would shatter self-esteem.

2015-38.sentence: Gelastic seizures are usually hypothalamic (often a hamartoma), so the laugh is a motor stereotype, not a joke aimed at anyone. Do not treat the mirthless burst as an object-relations message—good or bad objects are not laughing at the team; the hypothalamus is firing.

2015-39.sentence: A family history of depression is the factor this item links to a better late-life course—more “classic” affective illness, less lonely vascular or empty-house collapse. Klein would hear that history as an internalized depressed object the patient already knows how to live with and, sometimes, repair, rather than a first, unrepresented disaster.

2015-40.sentence: Lithium needs about five days (roughly five half-lives) after a 900-to-1200 mg bump before a level is at steady state, so the day-two “it’s not working” call is premature. That call is an enactment: the two of you are repeating breakthrough panic in the frame instead of waiting for the salt to equilibrate.

2015-41.sentence: The biggest risk here is a biological parent with bipolar disorder, not race difference, open adoption, or infant placement. The parents’ worry about those other stories is a defense—displacement—so they do not have to sit with genetic loading they cannot adopt away.

2015-42.sentence: Looping back to an earlier medication answer is perseveration: a thought-process problem, not insight, speech, perception, or new thought content. The pill keeps returning as unfinished business—a demand or proof of need that hijacks the interview the way a hungry infant hijacks every topic back to the feed.

2015-43.sentence: The frame here is not “is alprazolam allowed.” It is who holds the limit after a new PCP refused to keep writing it without a psychiatrist in the room. A past misuse history of other drugs or alcohol is the finding that turns as-needed alprazolam from a treatment contract into a substance you may be asked to become the new supplier for.

2015-44.sentence: Restless legs is a two-person night: the urge to move arrives, and whoever shares the bed gets drafted into the ritual of walking it off. Pramipexole treats the dopamine-sensitive limb restlessness so the couple is not stuck performing the syndrome together instead of sleeping.

2015-45.sentence: The breakup ripped away the person she was using as a secure base, and the sertraline-overdose thought was a protest at that sudden loss of proximity. Seeing her the next day keeps you as a temporary base after she has already calmed, agreed to stay with family, and allowed you to speak with them—without turning the call into a late-night dose change.

2015-46.sentence: This child’s ego can handle school, friends, and play dates at home; what it cannot tolerate is distance from the attachment figures. Separation anxiety is the diagnosis because the feared catastrophe is getting lost or kidnapped—being away—not a global worry machine or a social-evaluation fear.

2015-47.sentence: The “depression” after amiodarone can be the thyroid leaving the room while the patient stays in the chair: energy, weight, and sleep change without a new psychological story. Check TSH and free T4 before you treat a mood that may be the drug’s effect on thyroid hormone, not a split-off self.

2015-48.sentence: l-Methylfolate is preferred because it crosses the blood-brain barrier better than plain folate—the already-reduced form that can actually reach CNS one-carbon metabolism. Identity is not in this item; the live third is the molecule that gets into brain, not race, gender, or class.

2015-49.sentence: When the child can hold one caregiver who is both feeding and frustrating, Klein calls that the depressive position: concern for a whole person replaces the split into all-good and all-bad. Repair becomes possible because the “bad” object is no longer a separate enemy you have to evacuate.

2015-50.sentence: Reality testing is intact here: culturally shared spirit-visions are not the same as a mind that cannot tell inner from outer. Ego strength is the schoolwork collapse—treat the function that failed, not the gift the family can still use.

2015-51.sentence: In REM sleep behavior disorder the body acts the chase dream because REM atonia is gone; the “assailants” are not a waking attachment figure you can protest toward. The spouse at the pillow is an accidental target, not a secure-base failure you treat with proximity work.

2015-52.sentence: Disulfiram only works if both of you keep the contract: you watch the transaminases at baseline and at two months while the patient keeps the bottle. Hepatotoxicity is a two-person problem—miss the labs and the pair has quietly dropped the frame.

2015-53.sentence: What predicts adult relating is the parent’s capacity to perceive and think about the child’s intentions—mentalization, not infant temperament or sibling drama. Uncovering “why I pick the same partner” only helps if that mind can still use another person as a thinking partner; otherwise stay supportive.

2015-54.sentence: The mother is splitting the parental pair: you may evaluate ADHD with her consent, but treatment without the father would enact her all-good/all-bad custody story. Ask for the divorce decree so you are not recruited as the good object who erases the other parent.

2015-55.sentence: The shrinking-body panic is not just vanity; it is a Kleinian dump of a hated small, weak self into the mirror so the patient can stay identified with a hard, inflated body. Anabolic-androgenic steroid abuse keeps that split going: the muscles are a paranoid-schizoid fortress against the soft, shrinking object he cannot yet mourn or repair.

2015-56.sentence: Falls plus housebound anxiety can become a story about frailty or gender, but the live third here is age: old bodies get read as “just Parkinson’s” or “just afraid,” and the vertical-gaze exam gets skipped. Progressive supranuclear palsy names the identity trap: do not let the cultural picture of a timid elderly patient stand in for the midbrain finding.

2015-57.sentence: At eighty-four this is Erikson’s integrity-versus-despair hour: the mind is trying to hold a life story together while the body is on fire. Benztropine toxicity hijacks that task—fever, dry mouth, tachycardia, visual hallucinations—so despair looks like delirium until you stop the anticholinergic.

2015-58.sentence: On a medical floor, “I’m fine” can be a symptom that keeps the ward moving and keeps terror off the chart. The Joint Commission’s primary risk factor—lack of proper assessment for suicide risk—means the missed ask is doing work: it protects staff from knowing how close the patient is.

2015-59.sentence: A six-week partial lift on venlafaxine XR 150 mg is a developmental stall, not a failed child: the antidepressant capacity has arrived, just not fully. Increasing the dose is waiting for that function to come online instead of switching parents because growth was incomplete.

2015-60.sentence: After Roux-en-Y, “just two drinks” is already an enactment: the old drinking story is being lived in a new gut that cannot buffer it. Alcohol now hits faster and harder, so the two of you are repeating the bypass of limits rather than talking about what the drinks are for.

2015-61.sentence: Varenicline can become a reaction formation in the quit attempt: the patient turns craving into its opposite, a ritual of taking the pill that says “I do not want this.” The drug still has to do the receptor work; the defense just makes sticking with it feel like a moral flip rather than a daily fight with nicotine.

2015-62.sentence: The oxytocin surge at orgasm is a brief window of affect tolerance: closeness floods in and the ego can hold it without having to act or flee. When that pulse is missing or frightening, the person may copulate but cannot stay present for the bonding the hormone is built to mark.

2015-63.sentence: “Tell me more about how all this started” keeps the story in one room so the patient does not dissociate—leave without leaving the chair—into why-questions, shame, or a mid-life-crisis label. Open invitation holds both the affair and the repair in awareness; closed or moralizing probes push half the material offline.

2015-64.sentence: Naming the federal government and IDEA is a trial comment about agency: the parent can see their own part as advocate, not as the person who failed to make the school move. Psychological mindedness here means using the mandate instead of only raging at the building that cannot, by law, be the last word.

2015-65.sentence: Exploitativeness in narcissistic personality is a limit problem: other people are treated as extensions, so endings and “no” never quite arrive. The work is not to rush empathy they do not have yet, but to hold time and refusal until using staff and family stops being the only way to feel whole.

2015-66.sentence: Bromocriptine after NMS is not just a dopamine agonist; it is the relationship saying the last pill became poison and the body must be unfrozen. Early benefit comes from treating rigidity and the 50,000 CK as a demand the drug made, then offering a different feed that restores the receptor instead of pushing more antipsychotic.

2015-67.sentence: You hold the frame when you refuse to treat “coma plus cirrhosis” as a seizure until the tracing shows triphasic waves—broad, frontally predominant complexes—not PLEDs or spikes. The ethical limit is the EEG itself: it decides whether you chase hepatic encephalopathy or start an anticonvulsant you do not owe.

2015-68.sentence: The wish is a clean efficacy trial: random assignment, tight inclusion, a circumscribed sample that makes the antidepressant look strong. The prohibition is the clinic, and the symptom of that collision is the effectiveness question—will the same drug still work under real-world conditions, with the patients you actually treat.

2015-69.sentence: In this Southeast Asian dhat picture, nocturnal ejaculation is not remembered as ordinary sexuality; it is lived as a leak of vital essence through semen. What cannot be represented as ordinary desire or loss is repeated in the body as fatigue, abdominal pain, and weight loss.

2015-70.sentence: Citalopram plus lithium already taxes serotonergic regulation; St. John's wort is the extra load that ego strength cannot metabolize, and the body shows it as fever, clonus, and confusion. The lesson is capacity: one more serotonergic agent can overwhelm a system that was barely holding.

2015-71.sentence: ECT is a brief parasympathetic drop then a catecholamine surge; congestive heart failure is the organ that cannot use that surge as a secure, time-limited event. You treat the failing heart as the attachment problem in the room: it cannot borrow regulation from a procedure that spikes rate and blood pressure.

2015-72.sentence: A healthcare professional with meperidine access is already in an enactment: the workplace supplies the drug and then admits the seizure. Normeperidine—not withdrawal from alcohol, butalbital, oxazepam, or fentanyl—is the metabolite that makes that two-person pattern visible as a fit.

2015-73.sentence: The commitment hearing can feel like two minds in one room: the frightened, dangerous patient you just saw, and the citizen whose liberty you are asking a judge to take. Clear and convincing evidence is the legal wall that keeps you from evacuating your own anxiety by overselling danger—or from splitting off the risk and understating it.

2015-74.sentence: You are holding two objects at once: the cold spouse in the story and the you who ended last hour before the patient finished. An interpretation names that they are one relationship in two rooms, so the patient can hate and need the same person without splitting you into “good listener” and “dismissive other.”

2015-75.sentence: Guanfacine’s presynaptic α2 stimulation quiets the noradrenergic alarm so the child’s mind is less flooded by impulse and evening rebound. Think of it as help toward the depressive position: less evacuating tension into a tic or a blow-up, more room to notice the other person and try to repair.

2015-76.sentence: After a sudden maternal death, the surviving parent and the school-aged children will co-create the next attachment field—silence, over-caretaking, or honest mourning. Ensuring psychosocial supports keeps that field from collapsing into one isolated dyad that has to carry the whole loss.

2015-77.sentence: Calling you by mother’s name is a parapraxis: the unconscious used a slip instead of a sentence. How far you unpack it depends on this ego—if the childhood was brutal, name the slip lightly and stay supportive; if the patient can play with it, the slip is already doing the uncovering.

2015-78.sentence: Transient global amnesia dumps a few hours of unthinkable confusion and then returns the mind intact; recurrent episodes are rare, so you do not have to treat it like a seizure or a stroke warning. Contain the family’s nameless dread—the repeated questions, the missing time—by naming the syndrome so the raw fear becomes a story they can keep.

2015-79.sentence: Schizotypal oddness (auras, crystals, the surgeon’s “aura”) is not a phase you can talk someone out of in a consult; it is a lifelong temperament that has already set the limit on how close people get. Your job is to respect that ceiling: treat the appendicitis, do not try to force intimacy or “normalize” the magical thinking overnight.

2015-80.sentence: Fluoxetine is the long-half-life partner that stays in the room after a short-acting SSRI like paroxetine slams the door. You are not just swapping molecules; you are using one drug’s lingering presence to buffer the shock of the other one’s sudden absence.

2015-81.sentence: Midlife friendship loosens the childhood rule that your secure base has to be the same age as you. The fifteen-years-younger confidante can still be the person she turns to for regulation; proximity of soul matters more than proximity of birth year.

2015-82.sentence: Optic neuritis that remits in six weeks is a test of ego strength: can this person tolerate a body that suddenly fails, then seems fine, while MS still waits in the wings? Name the risk plainly so they can plan, not so they panic; reality testing includes holding a future diagnosis without collapsing now.

2015-83.sentence: VTA dopamine to the nucleus accumbens is the circuit that hijacks wanting so hard the person can feel gone while still sitting there. Addiction is that split: the reward path fires as if the drug is life itself, while the rest of the self watches from a distance.

2015-84.sentence: Morning-coherent, afternoon-disorganized speech is the ward already enacting sundowning: the system “forgets” at 4 p.m. what it knew at 10 a.m. Treat the fluctuation as the diagnosis talking, not as two different patients, and do not argue with the afternoon exam as if it were a character change.

2015-85.sentence: The cough is nothing, and he still makes you the aggressor: that is splitting, holding you as all-bad so the good-you cannot exist in the same hour. Transference-focused psychotherapy names that pattern out loud instead of soothing it or arguing about your throat.

2015-86.sentence: Paroxetine is the SSRI most likely to put a serotonergic brake on ejaculation, so the tablet becomes a demand that he last longer for someone else. He slips it in at the door because needing a pill for sex can feel like proof he is defective, not just a 5-HT reuptake effect.

2015-87.sentence: The protective factor is not 50/50 custody or same-gender parenting; it is cessation of conflict between the divorced parents. You hold that limit: the child is not the mediator, the audience, or the courier for the fight.

2015-88.sentence: Cluster headache likes REM sleep, so the attack often clocks in at night with boring pain into one eye. The symptom has a timetable of its own: it wakes him on a schedule he did not choose and cannot bargain with.

2015-89.sentence: High reliability here means ratings are similar among different raters, not that the scale has already found the true depression. Two clinicians scoring the same patient and landing near each other is a late developmental capacity: a shared view of the same object, not two private movies.

2015-90.sentence: Childhood-onset schizophrenia carries similar deficits in attention, learning, and abstraction as adult-onset illness, so youth is not a milder inner world. The good and bad objects are already as hard to hold together as they are in the adult; age does not spare the relationship to reality.

2015-91.sentence: An accurate interpretation is a good object they did not invent, and that can stir Kleinian envy—the wish to spoil what the therapist just did well. Getting worse is the attack: they stay in the paranoid-schizoid position (split, all-bad, no repair) rather than feel depressive concern, which is ordinary guilt and a wish to make it right.

2015-92.sentence: Lithium can hold the mood while the body still speaks: psoriasis plaques are the symptom that got evicted from affect and parked on the skin. Name the drug in the room so the flare is not read as moral failure or “noncompliance,” but as a known cost of the salt that is keeping them sane.

2015-93.sentence: This is Erikson’s last task, integrity versus despair: the older body is asking whether a narrowing canal has to mean a narrowing life. Spinal stenosis pain that eases with sitting is a concrete limit; the psych work is whether he can use sitting, pacing, and help without treating every block walked as proof he has already lost.

2015-94.sentence: A faster benzo cut asks more of the ego than a brittle nervous system can hold—affect floods, sleep breaks, impulse control thins. Valproic acid is borrowed cortex: it raises the seizure and withdrawal threshold so the daily reduction is a planned change, not a daily trauma.

2015-95.sentence: Attachment lives in shared memory: names, routes, the face that is the secure base. Early Alzheimer PET with bitemporoparietal hypoperfusion is that map dimming, so the spouse becomes both navigator and lost object at once.

2015-96.sentence: The frozen house is a two-person (really four-person) pattern: Dad’s need for quiet and the kids’ fear of harming him lock together. A strategic task—a real visiting schedule—changes the dance without a speech about feelings; friends can come at agreed hours so guilt and protection stop running the clock.

2015-97.sentence: An acutely psychotic mind already cannot use uncovering; risperidone-driven akathisia makes it worse by flooding the body with restlessness that will be read as danger. Treat the motor side effect with propranolol 10 mg three times daily first, then support and contain—do not interpret or push the dose.

2015-98.sentence: When the story cannot be told in words, it shows up as a body emergency: radiating neck pain, a failing gait, and new incontinence. Get the MRI of the cervical spine now to rule out cord compression; the unrepresented state here is neurologic, not a metaphor you sit with.

2015-99.sentence: Two wishes collide: treat the depression with fluoxetine and keep the psychosis quiet with risperidone. Fluoxetine’s CYP2D6 blockade raises risperidone and the prohibition arrives as acute dystonia—the conflict lands in muscle, not in speech.

2015-100.sentence: If the patient cannot even register “apple, table, penny,” you do not have a partner for uncovering work. Technique follows that finding: support, simplify, and treat the sensorium before you ask this mind to remember or interpret.

2015-101.sentence: Families often split the pharmacy into a good new object and a bad old one, as if perphenazine were the rejecting parent and a second-generation drug the rescue. CATIE undercuts that split: second-generation antipsychotics were no more effective than first-generation ones, so keep both the good and the bad of any one agent in the same relationship.

2015-102.sentence: Attachment does not require bruises to break; emotional neglect still removes the person who should have been the secure base. Every form of early life stress, not only physical or sexual abuse, independently predicts adult psychiatric illness, so take the ‘it wasn’t that bad’ story as a clue, not a clearance.

2015-103.sentence: Beneficence is the ethical name for a two-person rescue: delirium has dropped him out of a peer conversation, so you and he briefly become a caretaker-and-cared-for pair. Overriding the refusal is not you being paternal alone; it is the two of you living a temporary parent–child setup until capacity returns and autonomy can re-enter the room.

2015-104.sentence: Blepharospasm is the body slamming the shutters: orbicularis oculi closes vision without her consent. Botulinum toxin is the treatment that interrupts that local “I will not look” at the neuromuscular junction, so the lids can stay open long enough to drive.

2015-105.sentence: Reality testing is the ego function that failed: a man who believes he is a wizard with diplomatic immunity cannot appraise the actual courtroom. Competency to stand trial needs that function intact so he can understand the charges and work with counsel, not negotiate from a delusional embassy.

2015-106.sentence: Cryptococcus hides behind its polysaccharide capsule the way denial hides a fact: the immune system (and the examiner) can miss what is right there. India ink makes the capsule’s empty halo visible, and the CSF pattern—lymphocytosis, high protein, low glucose—is the body finally admitting opportunistic meningitis.

2015-107.sentence: Prader–Willi hyperphagia pulls the family into a kitchen-policing war: lock the pantry, chase the forage, ride the tantrum. That is an enactment—you and the parents are living a food-control struggle instead of naming the sequence (neonatal hypotonia, then insatiable seeking) and treating the 15q11–13 paternal-deletion physiology.

2015-108.sentence: The TAT’s person-by-a-window is a blank enough other that she will cast someone—often you—into the scene. Who she makes that figure be is a transference rehearsal, and the feeling the story leaves in you is the countertransference sample.

2015-109.sentence: Intercourse with a stuffed animal is not curiosity; it is a script the child cannot put into words, so the body and play stage what memory cannot hold. Watch for other unrepresented material—night terrors, sudden freeze, or sexualized play that looks rehearsed rather than exploratory.

2015-110.sentence: Seasonal depression pulls her inward just as she is trying to make a new attachment, so light therapy is a secure-base intervention: it restores circadian proximity to the sun without putting a fetus in the middle of a medication decision. When winter darkness isolates her from her husband, timed bright light can re-regulate the pair before they lose each other as co-regulators.

2015-111.sentence: Twenty minutes of dying-feeling panic is more affect than this ego can bind, so lorazepam buys minutes of impulse control and reality testing while the cortex comes back online. Fluoxetine is the long game; you do not ask a flooded ego to wait six weeks for containment.

2015-112.sentence: Homework and holidays keep him a father, not a visitor, which is the supportive structure this child’s mind can actually use after the family frame broke. Uncovering his grief or making him her companion loads her with adult affect she cannot metabolize.

2015-113.sentence: Postpartum psychosis is often bipolar bursting into the mother–infant pair, so two people are suddenly living inside one person’s mood episode. Treat the bipolar diathesis fast; the infant cannot wait while you sort whether this is “just” depression or trauma.

2015-114.sentence: The attack is projective identification in action: unbearable rage is forced into you so you feel the danger he cannot think. Call law enforcement first; you cannot interpret a split until the room is safe and the projection is no longer landing on your body.

2015-115.sentence: Interferon is a good object that can flip into a persecutor: it treats hepatitis C and can also deepen depression into suicidal ideation. You keep both faces of the drug in one mind so hepatology does not split the consult into “just start it” versus “psych said never.”

2015-116.sentence: The fight over med times, food delivery, and who is “abusing” him is an autonomy-versus-shame crisis, not a failed capacity exam. Name that he is hard to work with and plan the behavior so the team can hold limits without shaming him into another lawsuit threat.

2015-117.sentence: “I’m being left out again” is an automatic thought: a snap appraisal that arrives before a core belief even speaks. You catch it at the surface so a roommate’s phone call does not have to become a lifelong story of exile.

2015-118.sentence: Toddlerhood is when “no” first has to mean something, and limit setting is that parental task. Attachment already happened; now the child needs an ending to the impulse, not more stimulation or instruction.

2015-119.sentence: Neurosyphilis invariably starts as meningitis, inflammation of the membrane that should contain the brain. Before arteritis or myelitis, that covering fails first: the container that makes experience thinkable is already inflamed.

2015-120.sentence: Aripiprazole is the other evidence-backed choice after risperidone for irritability and self-hitting in autism. The aggression is affect the child cannot put into words; you pick the agent with data rather than cycling quetiapine or olanzapine on hope.

2015-121.sentence: The pass is not a bribe; it is a real privilege that only holds if the patient's ego can still take lithium and keep impulses in check. Naming the trade-off is coercive in the everyday sense, and it is still the right move if you believe a home visit off meds would blow through affect tolerance and put the patient back in mania.

2015-122.sentence: A holding environment is the parent's reliable presence that lets the infant protest, settle, and come back—attachment as a secure base, not a lecture. When you recreate that predictability in treatment, the patient can use you to regulate instead of scattering every time the hour ends.

2015-123.sentence: You two still have a conversation even when Broca's area has wrecked speech: the patient can close the eyes on request because comprehension is relatively spared. The interpersonal task is to wait, not fill the silence, so the pair of you do not turn a language lesion into a false story that the person 'doesn't understand.

2015-124.sentence: Clang associations—'real, meal, deal'—are a thought-process break; the words link by sound, not by sense. You hold the frame by writing that accurately on the MSE instead of collapsing it into 'obsessions' or 'preoccupations,' which are thought content.

2015-125.sentence: Histrionic lability treats the pill, the compliment, and the appointment as proof that someone is still watching. The relationship task is not to feed the flourish or withhold it as punishment, but to notice that the feeling is intense, shallow, and gone the moment the audience leaves.

2015-126.sentence: The calm after 'dumped me' is isolation of affect, a defense that parks the feeling so the story can be told. Confrontation here is not a fight; it is you naming that split so the patient can look at the gap instead of living only in the words.

2015-127.sentence: Bilateral vestibular schwannomas are already an enactment: the genome is living NF2 in both ears at once, and you and the patient are stuck in that two-sided scene before anyone says the name. Café-au-lait spots are just extras; the pair of acoustic neuromas is the relationship that has already happened on the MRI.

2015-128.sentence: Asking "Why a 3 and not a 0?" is a mirroring response: you reflect the scrap of self-esteem that already wants change instead of demanding an idealized 10. A 3 is competence, not failure; push toward 5 or 10 and you steal the patient's own voice.

2015-129.sentence: The fired doctor could not contain the dread, so the patient evacuates it as certainty of stomach cancer after ordinary gurgling. Illness anxiety is nameless dread parked in a normal exam: you have to hold the fear long enough that it becomes thinkable, not another specialist.

2015-130.sentence: The syrinx is a hole down the center of the cord, a sanctioned gap: pain and temperature drop out in a cape over the shoulders while light touch, the letter of the law, stays. Syringomyelia punishes sensation the way a rigid conscience can go blank in the middle and still look intact at the edges.

2015-131.sentence: Collecting feedback from the patient is the developmental move that actually arrives: the observing function that says how the hour felt, not how faithfully you stuck to a method. Technique, transference accuracy, and demographic fit matter less than that late-arriving capacity to hear whether the work is helping.

2015-132.sentence: Split treatment lets everyone pretend the pill and the psychotherapy live in different people, so liability can be sliced 50/50 or limited to the script. The symptom of the arrangement is that dodge; the prescribing psychiatrist still keeps full responsibility for the patient's care.

2015-133.sentence: At fifty this firefighter is on Erikson's generativity-versus-stagnation task: he is supposed to still be the one who runs into the fire, and the infarct has put that identity on the floor. Sertraline is the drug that treats the depression without adding nortriptyline-level cardiac conduction risk or a phenelzine hypertensive surprise while he tries to rejoin the crew.

2015-134.sentence: The vomit is not a random habit; it is the ritual that empties the unbearable fullness so she never has to sit with it. Holding her after the meal until that dysphoria fades is extinction: the escape response is blocked until the urge dies on its own, so abdominal fullness stops predicting a purge.

2015-135.sentence: The note said "I am sorry," but she still cannot feel regret for surviving, which is Klein's paranoid-schizoid position: the lost partner is evacuated in a near-lethal act rather than mourned. Inpatient hospitalization is the container that keeps the attack from being finished while a sliver of depressive concern—the wish to repair—has a chance to appear.

2015-136.sentence: The unnamed anxiety pill (almost certainly an SSRI or SNRI) was held as purely good, and the restlessness was split off as a separate bad object that earned another 5 mg of intramuscular haloperidol. Cyproheptadine 8 mg PO treats the serotonin syndrome that split created: one serotonergic story, not two diseases.

2015-137.sentence: He already knows each click buys a brief lift against loneliness, so this mind can use that insight; you do not need a deep excavation of childhood before you name the loop. Operant conditioning is the technique-level truth: the purchase is positively reinforced, and therapy works by weakening that payoff rather than uncovering a hidden conflict first.

2015-138.sentence: The family and you are making the story of this death together; it is not only a one-person depression sitting in a dead football player's skull. Name the finding they came for: chronic traumatic encephalopathy is a tauopathy from repeated hits, not amyloid plaques, spongiform change, or hippocampal sclerosis.

2015-139.sentence: After one choking panic at the table, this teen treats food as a threat and the parents as the people who might shove calories back at them. Specific phobia here is also a bid for a safer base: stay near the family by shrinking the meal, not by saying the eating itself now feels like it could kill them.

2015-140.sentence: The Trendelenburg waddle of muscular dystrophy is two bodies working as one: the pelvis drops on the swing side and the trunk throws itself over the stance hip so the pair can stay upright. You and the patient are doing the same thing if you lean in to "help" the weak side instead of naming the hip abductors that failed.

2015-141.sentence: Creutzfeldt-Jakob with myoclonus and spongiform microvacuolation of glia and dendrites is not a mind that can use uncovering; the cortex is vanishing week by week. Stay supportive: name the course, protect the family from wild interpretation, and do not hunt for hidden meaning in a brain that is dissolving.

2015-142.sentence: Her ego is already using a bilingual friend as extra reality-testing against a husband who may be the source of the bruises. Start with the professional interpreter and that friend, keep him in the parking lot, and do not ask her limited English or his presence to carry the truth.

2015-143.sentence: Stopping your pretend 911 call is the child using you as a secure base to check: the dollhouse fire is symbol, not catastrophe. That pause marks preoperational into concrete operational—two people can now share that it is play and still stay regulated.

2015-144.sentence: Prepubertal kids need higher mg/kg doses of liver-metabolized drugs because their livers clear faster, not because they are "small adults." The cultural third is age itself: if you dose them like adolescents you undertreat the child sitting in front of you.

2015-145.sentence: This finding sits on integrity versus despair: after an upper-motor-neuron lesion, the body no longer yields smoothly to another person’s hands. Spasticity is that late-life bargain made visible—velocity-dependent resistance in antigravity muscles, clasp-knife give-way, brisk reflexes—so the exam is not just tone; it is whether the patient can still let a helper move a limb that now fights back.

2015-146.sentence: A good-enough other has to stay whole in the mind while the patient chooses an action. The stamped-envelope hypothetical tests judgment because it asks whether they can treat the unknown owner as a real person with rights, not as a discarded object they can ignore or exploit.

2015-147.sentence: Expert-wisdom diagnosis invites the paranoid-schizoid move: the guru’s certainty is split off and put into the patient as if it were a fact. The Feighner criteria (Washington University, 1972) are a depressive-position repair—operationalized checklists you can test, argue with, and revise instead of projecting “illness” by charisma.

2015-148.sentence: Split treatment tempts you to forget you are half of a pair. Your job is to evaluate and prescribe while keeping regular contact with the therapist; a trial comment is, “If we never talk, we will each treat a different patient.”

2015-149.sentence: The frame here is the correction rate, not the bed rails. When sodium of 99 is pulled up too fast, central pontine myelinolysis is the iatrogenic cost of dropping that limit—flaccid quadriparesis, dysarthria, dysphagia, mind still intact—so ethics means who holds the speed of change.

2015-150.sentence: Ego strength is whether feeling can be held without flooding or breaking reality. In ataque de nervios the affect spills as shouting, crying, trembling, and rising heat, yet it still maps to an anxiety disorder: impulse and affect overflow, reality testing holds.

2015-151.sentence: Lorazepam is the benzo that actually lands from muscle, so at 2 a.m. you are not just picking a sedative—you are choosing a way to stay with the person when the body is too split to take a pill. Dissociation here is a vertical split: the agitated patient has already left the room without leaving the chair, and a reliable IM route is how you keep a body in the same place as the mind long enough for anyone to arrive.

2015-152.sentence: Bilateral parotid sialadenosis is the body advertising self-induced vomiting while the interview still says 'I barely eat.' Two people are making that pattern: the patient hides the purge and you, if you blame weight gain or refeeding, join the hide instead of naming the vomit.

2015-153.sentence: Habituation is what you are after: anxiety after the doorknob falls on its own when washing is blocked. Attachment-wise the ritual was a homemade caregiver; you become the secure base that stays nearby so the patient can sit with contamination without fleeing into the sink.

2015-154.sentence: Reactive attachment disorder is the child who will not use you: little smile, no comfort-seeking, unexplained irritability after a string of foster homes. If someone then reaches for a pill as the 'feed' that will make bonding happen, the medicine becomes proof of need rather than a relationship the child still cannot risk.

2015-155.sentence: Normal-pressure hydrocephalus is the wet-wobbly-wacky triad with ventricles too big for the modest atrophy; that is a shunt conversation, not a shrug. The ethical frame is who holds the limit: family brought an 80-year-old to the ED, and you do not let 'just aging' or 'just dementia' cancel a treatable gait-incontinence-confusion package.

2015-156.sentence: Word knowledge holds last in normal aging while perceptual speed, inductive reasoning, numbers, and spatial skill slip earlier. The enactment is already in the room: she comes fearing dementia and you, if you only chase the complaint, rehearse the catastrophe instead of showing her the one ability that is still standing.

2015-157.sentence: The age-12 cutoff blocks a tidy story that ADHD began last semester under graduate pressure. Denial—pushing childhood inattention out of awareness—lets the student stay the competent adult who only just broke, instead of the kid who always lost the assignment.

2015-158.sentence: A Facebook friend request is evacuation: the patient dumps leftover need into your personal page so it does not have to be thought in the room. Containment means you take that raw leftover, turn it into words about the frame, and bring it back next session instead of clicking Accept or Ignore.

2015-159.sentence: Inhalants already hijacked the teenager's sense of a coherent self; a benzo or antipsychotic can feel like another takeover. Watchful waiting, when he is cooperative, mirrors a self that can come back online as the solvent clears.

2015-160.sentence: The SSRI treats mood in words the mind can use; restless legs dump what is left into the body at night. That crawl-and-pace is an unrepresented state: agitation that cannot be remembered as feeling, so it is repeated as a limb that must move.

2015-161.sentence: War psychiatry wanted to restore soldiers; the old asylum ethic wanted them locked away. NIMH was founded after World War II treatment of soldiers because that collision—heal versus warehouse—finally funded a research institute instead of more custodial beds.

2015-162.sentence: Clozapine is the last-resort ideal that can restore a shattered self, so it is easy to ignore dyspnea, tachycardia, and eosinophilia. A troponin level tests whether that ideal is inflaming the heart, protecting competence instead of clinging to the miracle drug.

2015-163.sentence: Gut-directed hypnosis works when someone can take the raw belly panic of irritable bowel syndrome and hold it long enough for it to become a thought instead of a spasm. That is containing: you metabolize the nameless dread so the bowel does not have to evacuate it as pain and urgency.

2015-164.sentence: DSM-5 will not call two weeks of work-stress sleeplessness insomnia disorder; the clock has to run three months. Ending cannot be rushed: the diagnosis waits until time itself proves the difficulty is not a passing stretch.

2015-165.sentence: A trial comment the day after the crane collapse is that numbness, flash images, and a sleepless night are a human stress reaction, not proof he is breaking. Psychological mindedness starts here: he can use that naming to reach coworkers and family instead of swallowing critical-incident debriefing, a benzo, or early trauma-focused CBT.

2015-166.sentence: Hoarding disorder lives in a broken frame: the home has no usable rooms, neighbors call police, and still the patient holds the limit that every pile is worth keeping if only there were time. You hold the other limit—safety, egress, and that insight without sorting is not treatment.

2015-167.sentence: Haloperidol was the demand that settled the nocturnal agitation of delirium; once he is awake and the workup is negative, the pill is no longer feed. Keeping it until orientation returns treats disorientation like a toxin you must keep poisoning, instead of stopping the antipsychotic when the storm has passed.

2015-168.sentence: Graduated vaginal dilators treat genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder by letting her approach the feared sensation in measured doses rather than freeze or flee. That is undoing in the service of mastery: each larger size rewrites the reflex that said penetration equals injury.

2015-169.sentence: The team and the patient have already been living a two-person loop: another dopamine blocker, same psychosis, more despair about suicide. Naming clozapine breaks that enactment—the old pattern of “more of what already failed”—instead of acting it out one more time with aripiprazole, olanzapine, or fluphenazine.

2015-170.sentence: Vygotsky’s zone of proximal development is the strip just beyond what the infant can do alone, where a parent’s toy or prompt still makes sense. Stimulation that sits there builds a new capacity; toys dumped below reflex or far above grasp leave development stuck.

2015-171.sentence: Cigarette smoke (polycyclic aromatics, CYP1A2) had been quietly metabolizing the clozapine so the same milligrams stayed a usable good object. When smoking stops, that object turns persecutory—oversedation, ataxia—because the relationship between dose and brain is no longer the one you thought you were holding.

2015-172.sentence: This mind and this consult do not need an uncovering confrontation about “hidden benzos.” Sertraline can light up an immunoassay; technique here is supportive: confirm with a specific assay before you treat a false positive as character.

2015-173.sentence: Voluntary pizza money is a two-person (really many-person) bargain: each resident can silently let someone else pay. A meeting that includes every club member makes the free-rider problem a shared conversation, which is why that strategy beats a private ask, a single collector, a guilt pitch, or a threat.

2015-174.sentence: After carbon monoxide, the globus pallidus can declare a delayed lesion on CT at two weeks—a capacity that looked present in the garage and then failed to arrive. Cherry-red skin and coma mark the acute hit; the pallidum is where the later developmental loss shows up.

2015-175.sentence: TMS lets the patient keep a waking mind while current is applied to cortex, so the treatment does not require the surrender of consciousness that anesthesia for ECT demands. For someone whose depression already feels like a loss of control, that intact awareness is the real advantage: they can accept stimulation without handing the body over to a procedure they cannot watch.

2015-176.sentence: Transient global amnesia hits in late adulthood and wipes new memories for hours, so the patient cannot finish the day's story even though identity and alertness stay intact. Erikson's integrity-versus-despair task is exactly that work of holding a continuous life narrative; a TGA spell briefly steals the last chapter while the person is still old enough to feel the hole.

2015-177.sentence: Voices arguing about the patient in the third person are Schneider's first-rank finding: the mind is no longer the sole speaker of the self. Culturally, that is a live third in the room—an alien chorus that comments on him as if he were already an object of public debate rather than a private subject.

2015-178.sentence: Childhood ADHD often shows the motor wish in the open: the body cannot sit still. In adults the same drive remains, but the prohibition against looking like a bouncing kid has usually won, so hyperactivity recedes while impulsivity and unfinished projects keep the conflict alive.

2015-179.sentence: At 80–120 mg, methadone does more than quiet withdrawal; it occupies the receptor so the old high cannot land and the body stops repeating the craving it cannot put into words. Under-dosing at 40 mg leaves that unrepresented hunger intact, and the patient acts it out with the next illicit opioid instead of remembering why they started.

2015-180.sentence: The tics are visible, so you can feel recruited into the worried-watcher role, scanning every blink and bark. The school failure is usually ADHD riding along with Tourette, and that quieter inattention is what is actually costing him grades while you are still watching the movements.

2015-181.sentence: Serial sevens is concentration, not memory: the patient who keeps losing the thread is showing what cannot be held in mind as a lapse in the body of the exam. Chart the drift as unrepresented attention, not as a forgotten seven.

2015-182.sentence: Complex partial seizure is a capacity that never quite arrived as a continuous self: awareness drops, automatisms run, and the interval is blank. Treat the voice-then-stare-then-amnesia as a developmental failure of consciousness, not as a late-arriving hallucination.

2015-183.sentence: Imipramine is the TCA whose plasma level is allowed to speak for the dose; the rest of the list is treated as if blood work were morally optional. Draw the level instead of punishing a nonresponse with another blind increase.

2015-184.sentence: This DMDD picture sits on Erikson’s industry versus inferiority: the work of school, teams, and bedtime collapses into daily rage. The adult correlate is anxiety, not bipolar I, because the psychosocial task failed as competence, not as mania.

2015-185.sentence: First same-sex attraction in early adolescence is the symptom doing the work of naming a desire that was already there. It reassures him that coming out at fifty-five is a late announcement, not a late onset.

2015-186.sentence: Skipping informed consent for depot antipsychotic dumps the decision into the patient as if they had already agreed. Repair is naming autonomy out loud: risks, benefits, and alternatives, instead of leaving the split in the syringe.

2015-187.sentence: The last usable self is not speech or limbs; it is lid opening and vertical gaze after a basilar occlusion. Goals-of-care talk that skips that channel treats a still-present person as already gone.

2015-188.sentence: At eighty, a TCA is only usable if it leaves enough cognition for the work of recovery. Desipramine is the least anticholinergic of this list, so you are not trading residual mood for a clouded mind that cannot use support.

2015-189.sentence: Purging is evacuation of something felt as intolerable, and the body keeps the ledger: hypokalemia flattens T waves and raises U waves. The EKG is not a side show; it is the relationship with the bad stuff written on the heart.

2015-190.sentence: Missed social cues in autism are not a child refusing your frame or testing a limit. You hold the assessment differently: you do not interpret inattention as defiance, because the social-cue channel never came online the usual way.

2015-191.sentence: Apathy that cannot organize a clock is not the same as sadness that will not try. If clock drawing fails, a trial comment about their part in the emptiness will bounce; the executive gear for self-observation is what is broken.

2015-192.sentence: Using after a clean screen is acting out: feeling gets discharged as a behavior instead of being named. Contingency management puts the $20 and the three-negative lockout outside the patient so the impulse does not have to be held by will alone.

2015-193.sentence: Rizatriptan is a 5-HT1B/1D agonist that aborts migraine; it is not a hug, a narcotic, or a daily preventive like topiramate. Offering it at the first throb can feel like being fed on time instead of being handed hydromorphone as if pain were a demand you have to shut down.

2015-194.sentence: A specific acetaminophen plan plus no doctor, no supports, and impulsivity is a mind that has already stepped out of the chair: dissociation, a vertical split where the self who would call for help is not the one holding the bottle. Inpatient hospitalization keeps a body in the room until that split can close enough to use an outpatient frame.

2015-195.sentence: Childhood separation anxiety disorder is the childhood illness with the strongest genetic tie to adult panic. In the room the panic can become an enactment: two people living a reunion-and-abandonment sequence instead of naming the old alarm that someone is about to leave.

2015-196.sentence: Shared (integrated) care means the pediatrician, psychiatrist, and psychologist stay in one circuit around the child's asthma, ADHD, and oppositional behavior. That circuit is a secure base: the family uses nearby adults to regulate, instead of being bounced between offices like a separation they have to protest.

2015-197.sentence: Lithium raises serum calcium independent of the kidney, often via hyperparathyroidism; fatigue and constipation are not automatically a mood relapse. Checking calcium is ego strength in action: tolerate the affect of 'maybe I'm missing something' instead of impulsively raising the lithium or the antidepressant.

2015-198.sentence: Erikson's midlife task, ages 40–60, is generativity: feeling useful by protecting the next generation, not integrity-versus-despair. With a 55-year-old who feels useless after the last child leaves, stay supportive and concrete about contribution; this is not a mind asking you to uncover every old wish.

2015-199.sentence: AZT turned AIDS from a short fatal episode into a long relationship between clinic and patient: two people keep showing up because treatment works, so the roster grows even when new infections fall. Prevalence here is the living partnership, not a one-person “more cases” story.

2015-200.sentence: Hypnagogic music and hearing his name live in N1, the slip from waking into sleep, not in REM or deep N3. That edge is like losing the secure base of full wakefulness for a second; name it as sleep-onset hallucination so he can use you to settle instead of fearing he is losing his mind.

2015-201.sentence: Divalproex can drop the platelet count in a dose-related way, so the CBC line that protects her is platelets, not hemoglobin or WBC. Ego strength here is affect tolerance with a lab: she can stay on a useful mood stabilizer if you watch the number that actually bleeds.

2015-202.sentence: Winnicott’s good-enough parent is attuned enough that the child can feel her own drives, not a perfect mirror and not a Kohut selfobject. Technique follows prognosis: this mother needs support that “snapping once” is ordinary failure, not an uncovering hunt for the moment she “ruined” him.

2015-203.sentence: Malpractice still needs harm: this patient found a new psychiatrist and did well, so the best defense is no appreciably bad outcome, not the signed letter or the 30-day pill bottle. The two of you made a clumsy last session together; the court still asks whether that relational mess injured him.

2015-204.sentence: Night-worse unilateral headache plus jaw claudication is giant cell arteritis until proven otherwise; start prednisone now, not sumatriptan or oxygen. Denial would say “just a headache”; naming GCA and treating it is the opposite of that defense.

2015-205.sentence: The clean syringe is a feed, not a demand that he stop wanting heroin. You stay in the relationship by reducing HIV and hepatitis risk first, so the clinic is not experienced as a poison that only loves him if he is abstinent.

2015-206.sentence: Formication is a vertical split: part of him is still in the chair while another part is already being eaten by bugs. Stimulant intoxication floods the skin and mouth with that split—picking, oral stereotypies, paranoia—so he leaves his body without leaving the ED.

2015-207.sentence: WHO mhGAP is an enactment of scarcity already in the room: three psychiatrists per million cannot be the only pair of hands. Training non-specialists to identify and treat is the system living the treatment gap instead of pretending a US fellowship pipeline will close it.

2015-208.sentence: Prednisone mood change has a clock the ego cannot rush: tearfulness, irritability, and sleeplessness arrive before you get a neat story. Mood disorder is the most common psychiatric complication of corticosteroids, so you name the limit of the drug rather than wait for delirium or frank psychosis to make the ending obvious.

2015-209.sentence: Forty cigarettes a day is nameless dread in the body until a dose can hold it. A 21 mg patch cannot contain that hunger, so 42 mg/d is the container that turns raw withdrawal into something thinkable instead of a relapse he has to evacuate.

2015-210.sentence: The wish is to discharge rage through the wrist; the prohibition is to call it nothing. Confrontation names that collision without interpreting why: the cut was not lethal, and it still says he is not doing well.

2015-211.sentence: The toddler is discovering a body that can generate pleasure, not announcing trauma. Your job is mirroring: you reflect that this is ordinary toddler competence so the parent can keep a sturdy, non-shaming self around the child’s genital curiosity.

2015-212.sentence: Habit reversal asks the child to notice the premonitory urge and swap in a competing response, so you become the coach who names the tic instead of the audience that flinches. Watch the countertransference of wanting to suppress or look away; that urge in you is what the kid already expects from every classroom.

2015-213.sentence: Paranoid personality lives the unremembered injury as if it is happening again in every memo and peer review. What cannot be thought as old betrayal is repeated in the doctor–hospital dyad as certainty that administration is exploiting him.

2015-214.sentence: Sydenham chorea after group A Streptococcus is a body fact, not a conversion you interpret. Do not hunt for the child’s “part” in the writhing until you have named the post-strep brain; psychological mindedness starts after the organism is on the table.

2015-215.sentence: Alpha is the awake posterior rhythm that blooms when the eyes close and fades when they open. Hold that technical frame or you will call a normal tracing drowsy, photic, or benzodiazpine-drugged.
