2015-216.sentence: Specificity is the 85 percent: among elders who are truly well, the screen correctly says well. Sensitivity is the other number, the 75 percent of true mild cognitive impairment you catch; do not let the vendor evacuate that distinction into one reassuring percentage.

2015-217.sentence: The first one to three years after arrival is the real limit: the immigrant’s hope of a new life meets a country that will not instantly confer language, work, or belonging. Demoralization there is a time problem, not a character problem—you cannot rush the ego’s adaptation any more than you can rush mourning.

2015-218.sentence: Her wish to taper methadone fast is a Kleinian repair fantasy: evacuate the “poison” so the fetus is no longer a damaged object she must atone for. The actual repair is staying on the current methadone dose, which holds mother and fetus instead of acting out the purge.

2015-219.sentence: Cognitive impairment—anterograde and retrograde memory trouble—is what most often stops ECT, because memory is how the self stays continuous. When recall frays, the person feels less like a subject and more like a collection of gaps, so families refuse even when mood would improve.

2015-220.sentence: Topiramate (carbonic anhydrase inhibition, acidosis, stones) recruits you into the ED as the doctor who “should have seen this coming.” Name that countertransference so you treat the hematuria and the missed risk, not just your guilt.

2015-221.sentence: M’Naughten asks only whether, at the moment, he knew the act was wrong—the law’s stand-in for a working conscience, or superego. A combat flashback that wiped that knowledge (and left no memory) is what the defense must show; PTSD, hyperarousal, or a DSM label will not do.

2015-222.sentence: Tuberoinfundibular D2 blockade (classically risperidone) takes the dopamine brake off prolactin, as if a regulatory capacity never quite arrived at the pituitary. Aripiprazole’s partial D2 agonism puts a little of that brake back, so galactorrhea and amenorrhea can recede without waiting for full adult “arrival” of unblocked dopamine tone.

2015-223.sentence: Empathic validation names the affect first—here, humiliation—so the patient feels held rather than analyzed. Avoiding coworkers after the staff meeting is doing protective work: it keeps the shame from being restaged in the hallway before either of you has put words to it.

2015-224.sentence: Separation anxiety and worry that the surviving parent will get sick are age-typical grief in an eight-year-old, not a new attachment diagnosis. The cling is nameless dread looking for a container: a mind that can take in the raw fear and return it as thinkable mourning instead of letting the child evacuate it as panic.

2015-225.sentence: Paraphasia is a language-output miss—read for meet—not a neologism, not stuck perseveration, not flat dysprosody. Treat it as a finding about the speech network, not as a self-esteem slip or a witty selfobject failure.

2015-226.sentence: Small, irregular, asymmetric pupils that accommodate but ignore light are light-near dissociation; diabetic autonomic neuropathy belongs on that list, not only the syphilis eponym. Third-nerve palsy would dilate and weaken extraocular movement—this exam is the opposite shape.

2015-227.sentence: Social anxiety disorder here is fear of scrutiny: the messy signature feels like a public stain, so cash for a car becomes the workaround. What cannot be thought as “just handwriting” gets repeated in the body of daily life—avoid the pen, avoid the audience.

2015-228.sentence: Semantic memory stores a shared fact: the town parade is every July 4th, with no “I was there” timestamp. First grade, grandma’s summer, first sled, a TV gag—those are episodes; do not call a calendar fact a personal scene.

2015-229.sentence: Your job is to hold the limit against a stroke-or-tumor workup when the story is still a young adult's attack: bilateral heat-off-asphalt visual change, vertigo, dysarthria, tingling in hands, feet, and both sides of the mouth, then occipital headache. That is basilar migraine, and chasing cerebellar tumor, fourth-ventricle ependymoma, or vertebrobasilar ischemia would break the frame by treating your anxiety as if it were the diagnosis.

2015-230.sentence: Binge-purge is a drive collision: the wish to take food in meets the prohibition that it must not stay, and the body acts both sides. Fluoxetine is the drug with evidence here; it does not settle the wish versus the rule, but it can quiet the binge-purge enough that the fight is no longer only in the bathroom.

2015-231.sentence: Caffeine blocks the adenosine receptor, which lifts the brake on dopamine, so the first cup can feel like a borrowed spark of competence and brightness. When the self starts to need that chemical mirror every morning, withdrawal is the crash of esteem once adenosine is allowed to work again.

2015-232.sentence: The Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (WCST) keeps changing the rule, so the patient has to sit with the raw 'wrong' long enough for it to become a new thought instead of dumping it as the same old sort. That is containment: holding nameless frustration until executive function can name the new category, which Grooved Pegboard, Boston Naming, Benton Visual Retention, and Rey Auditory Verbal Learning do not ask.

2015-233.sentence: Twenty minutes are already gone, and the remaining hour cannot be spent on martinis, the marital fight, or lateness while forearm cutting is on the table. DBT's hierarchy holds that limit: self-injurious behavior is the first target, and you do not rush past it to work on anything that can wait.

2015-234.sentence: Four weeks at clozapine 200 mg with partial gain and good tolerability is still a trial in progress, not a failed case that needs aripiprazole, divalproex, quetiapine, or depot risperidone. A useful comment to the team is that the urge to add or switch is their impatience, not evidence the patient has used the clozapine trial yet.

2015-235.sentence: When she asks whether abuse “changed her brain,” the ethical limit is to name the finding without turning the MRI into a life sentence: adult childhood-abuse samples more often show a smaller hippocampus, the memory-binding structure that also sits in the HPA stress loop. Hold the frame there—structure can shrink under chronic stress and still be talked about as plastic, not as proof she is permanently broken.

2015-236.sentence: REM is the hour when the body rehearses without acting: eye movements rise, skeletal tone falls, and heart rate climbs and turns irregular, as if the scene is still running. Read the tachycardic epochs as meaning, not noise—the autonomic system is living the dream while muscle atonia keeps it off the ward floor.

2015-237.sentence: Validity is the check against denial: the comforting claim that a scale “is depression” because it looks official. Reliability only says the numbers repeat; validity asks whether those numbers actually measure the construct you named.

2015-238.sentence: The community already handed you a bipolar child; that is an enactment—the system is living the old “difficult kid = mania” story instead of testing it. AACAP still requires a distinct abnormal-mood episode with episodic symptoms, not chronic tantrums and hyperactivity wearing a mood-disorder badge.

2015-239.sentence: Psychoanalytic work is after the part that left without leaving the chair: unconscious conflict kept out of awareness by a split, not just better coping. Other therapies can improve relationships and alliance; this one is specific because it tries to bring that sequestered conflict into the room so it can be known.

2015-240.sentence: Nightly trauma dreams are a two-person problem once she is in treatment: sertraline and therapy hold the day, but the nights still replay the assault. Adding prazosin—an alpha-1 blocker used for PTSD nightmares—is you joining her against nocturnal hyperarousal rather than leaving her to face the flashbacks alone.

2015-241.sentence: Alzheimer disease first shreds the autobiographical memory that lets this person keep a spouse or child inside as a secure base—the inner map of “someone is there.” Once that map fails, language and tool-use go next, so the family becomes the only remaining regulator; the cling and the panic are attachment, not mere “confusion.”

2015-242.sentence: Observed methadone is the good object—the clinic that keeps him alive—while disulfiram is the deliberately bad object that will punish a drink with an acetaldehyde crash. Giving both at the window, with consent, lets one relationship hold craving and consequence instead of splitting them into “kind clinic” versus “kicked-out drunk.”

2015-243.sentence: In someone over 65, gut absorption of a psychotropic is the part of pharmacokinetics you can still lean on; GFR, hepatic blood flow, and volume of distribution are the systems that have already aged. Technique follows: do not “uncover” a dosing mystery in the stomach—support the failing clearance and distribution and leave absorption alone.

2015-244.sentence: The family’s hush after his myocardial infarction is the symptom, not a waiting room: silence is how they keep a feared truth (death, blame, who will carry what) out of the air. Naming the inability to talk as one of the family’s problems puts that mute pact on the table instead of filling it with a lecture or deputizing a spokesperson.

2015-245.sentence: The mute, posturing body is dumping terror into the team, who then reach for haloperidol as if they could kill the badness—classic projective identification, the other person is made to feel and act the split-off state. Lorazepam is the repair: it loosens the freeze so concern and speech can return, instead of answering the projection with a neuroleptic that can deepen catatonia.

2015-246.sentence: Atrophy plus fasciculations with brisk reflexes and extensor plantars means the finding is doing one job: announcing simultaneous lower- and upper-motor-neuron death of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, not a depressive bargain or a conversion script. The “fatigue” consult is the psyche trying to rename a dying anterior horn and corticospinal tract as mood; the exam refuses that story.

2015-247.sentence: Midlife sits on Erikson's generativity task: can she keep others well without sacrificing her own skin. High-dose fluvoxamine, 200 to 300 mg daily, is the pharmacologic stand-in for that work—enough SSRI, long enough, that washing no longer has to do the caring.

2015-248.sentence: Impaired prosody means the music of speech is off: stress, pitch, and melody do not carry feeling the way grammar still does. A trial comment lands only if they can hear how you said it; if they cannot, you name the flat or sing-song delivery itself rather than expecting them to infer their part from your tone.

2015-249.sentence: Carbamazepine induces its own CYP3A4 clearance, so a good week-two level is not the ending. You wait several weeks and often raise the dose; you cannot rush autoinduction any more than you can rush a real goodbye.

2015-250.sentence: Triangulation parks the bad object—Dad's dangerous drinking—in the 15-year-old so Mother never has to hold both love and complaint in one adult relationship. The boy is asked to be the safe messenger; that splits the couple's conflict across a child instead of keeping good and bad in the marriage.

2015-251.sentence: Urgent-not-emergent distress has to go somewhere; if you vanish, the patient may dump it into 911 or the ED as if only catastrophe exists. Arranged clinical coverage is the container: someone named who can take the projection of need without forcing a paranoid-schizoid choice between abandonment and disaster.

2015-252.sentence: Idiopathic Parkinson disease typically starts and stays worse on one side; you and the patient discover that asymmetry together on the exam table. Vertical gaze palsy, early autonomic failure, no levodopa response, or dementia in year one are other syndromes—and those findings belong to the body, not to a one-person story of 'just depression.

2015-253.sentence: A threat of court and commitment is already a technique choice: you have moved from negotiation to force, so this 18-year-old cannot use uncovering or a real yes. Support the frame by naming the legal limit plainly and offering what is still optional (who visits, meds discussion, safety plan) rather than dressing coercion as “voluntary insight.”

2015-254.sentence: Withdrawal and forgotten phone numbers look like mood, but right hemiparesis, left limb ataxia, and field cuts mean ego functions—attention, praxis, reality testing—are failing as JC-virus PML chews white matter. Do not interpret the irritability; a bland LP plus multifocal T2 lesions means you support cognition and treat the infection, because this mind cannot use insight until the brain can hold a thought.

2015-255.sentence: A first seizure in a teen with autism and intellectual disability is not separation protest or a bid to pull caregivers closer. Autism’s bimodal epilepsy risk (early childhood and adolescence) is neurologic; keep the attachment system as a secure base after the event instead of reading the fit as acting-out of dependence.

2015-256.sentence: “I’ll stay a girl even if I wear blue or cut my hair” is gender constancy: the self-label holds when clothes and hair change. That is a developmental achievement, not an enactment with you; do not treat the insistence as a fight about the clinic’s rules.

2015-257.sentence: Mute, not eating, psychotic depression in a 70-year-old is ego collapse, not a dissociative split you wait out in the chair. ECT is the next step because this mind cannot use words, TMS, VNS, or DBS while starvation and psychosis are running the show.

2015-258.sentence: Rorschach and TAT are for what the patient cannot say on a structured interview: unrepresented, odd linkages leak onto an inkblot as subtle thought disorder. They do not screen cognition, certify developmental level, or cancel uncooperativeness; they catch psychotic process that has no words yet.

2015-259.sentence: Desipramine can flip bipolar I because the TCA lifts inhibition faster than the wish to feel alive can stay inside a stabilizer. The collision is drive versus brake: more catecholamine drive, weaker prohibition, and the switch is the symptom.

2015-260.sentence: Contempt and stonewalling are the divorce already happening in the chairs, not a later outcome. That is an enactment: they live “you are worthless / I am gone” instead of saying the smaller hurt.

2015-261.sentence: He splits the field into the saved and “the devil’s workers,” so mixed, ordinary people cannot exist. Hold schizophreniform: about two months of psychosis is still inside one-to-six months, not a finished schizophrenia story.

2015-262.sentence: A history of violent behavior is the finding that sets the limit, not how hot the 2 a.m. rage feels. You hold the frame: past acts decide dangerousness more than tonight’s anger, the gun at home, or your own fear.

2015-263.sentence: Depression is the most common psychiatric picture after stroke, including a left MCA insult three weeks out. The ethical limit is to treat that depression so rehab can start, not to call withdrawal “unmotivated” and drop the consult.

2015-264.sentence: Kohut’s cause is absence of age-specific mirroring responses, not unmet drive or failed good/bad integration. A trial comment names the miss—“you felt unseen when I looked away”—so he can notice his shame as a reaction, not as proof he is nothing.

2015-265.sentence: The endometriosis is already named and treated; what cannot be rushed is her capacity to live with leftover pain without converting it into a cancer emergency. Illness anxiety would be fear without the symptom; here the body is loud, and the work is to hold time—hours of research, daily calls—until worry can wait instead of demanding a new treatment tonight.

2015-266.sentence: Postherpetic neuralgia is nameless dread in a dermatome: raw burning that never got a thinkable ending after the rash left. Capsaicin is a crude container—it burns the C-fibers on purpose so the pain can be located, dosed, and stopped, instead of being evacuated into yet another systemic drug.

2015-267.sentence: Bonding is the parent's selfobject need: she wants to feel like a competent, loving mother, and she is measuring that against an imagined instant rush. Attachment is the infant's side; what she needs mirrored is that her tie can grow after the critical-period myth, not that she failed at first sight.

2015-268.sentence: The wish is to erase the crash with a pill—prazosin, propranolol, escitalopram—so nobody has to approach the memory. Trauma-focused CBT is the collision with the prohibition: the child must revisit the story in words, not bury the drive to forget under a first-line medication that pediatric PTSD does not have.

2015-269.sentence: The mentor cannot be remembered as a teacher anymore; dementia repeats the old hierarchy in the body of the admission, and you feel it as discomfort instead of a narrative. Finish urgent care, then transfer: if you stay, the unrepresented dual relationship will be acted in the dyad rather than named and ended.

2015-270.sentence: Social learning is ego at work: she copies mother's clothes because that is the available model, not because hormones or a triangular oedipal plot required it. Dress-up and 'I am a girl' are practice in identifying with a real person, which is ordinary coping with a new gender role at three and a half.

2015-271.sentence: The daughter’s call is not only a risk question; it is proximity-seeking after you put quetiapine 50 mg into her 82-year-old parent—she is using you as a secure base to metabolize the black-box fear. Name the real trade-off in that same attachment language: atypical antipsychotics raise mortality, and you will stay close enough to weigh that harm against the agitation you were asked to contain.

2015-272.sentence: An overvalued idea lives in the marriage, not only in one skull: he keeps assigning adultery to her, and she is now cast as the one who must disprove a charge that he already admits has no evidence. The interpersonal move is the half-open door—he concedes he might be wrong—so the couple stays locked in interrogation instead of grief, jealousy, or a clean delusion that would end the debate.

2015-273.sentence: Fever plus lead-pipe rigidity is the sign that this mind-body system cannot use interpretation; it needs you to stop the neuroleptic and treat NMS, not to hunt meaning. Tachycardia, myoclonus, or more EPS are noisier and less specific—those findings invite a long differential, while rigidity-with-fever tells you support and medical rescue come first.

2015-274.sentence: Bilateral leg weakness, abulia, mutism, and incontinence are the brain saying the medial frontal “starter motor” is offline after anterior cerebral artery occlusion—drive and initiative drop out with the legs and the bladder. That is not stubborn silence or a pill that poisoned will; it is a vascular cut of the circuits that let a person want, speak, and hold urine.

2015-275.sentence: The scale is undoing: he tries to cancel the pancreatic-cancer identification with his dead parent by proving, ounce by ounce, that he is not wasting away. Avoiding the annual physical is the paired defense—keep the feared confirmation out of the room—so illness anxiety stays a private ritual instead of a diagnosis he would have to hear.

2015-276.sentence: When the family asks you to “declare” Father incompetent, the enactment has already started: they want you to live the takeover with them instead of sending the question to a judge. You assess capacity; a judicial hearing decides competency—stay in that role or you become the extra relative with a prescription pad.

2015-277.sentence: Reciprocal inhibition works because she vertically splits the hour: one channel stays at the party while another rehearses a competing pleasure so the anxiety never owns the whole field. She leaves without leaving the chair—same room, two tracks—and the feared scene has to share the mind with something that is not fear.

2015-278.sentence: A middle-cerebral infarct empties the lateral convexity so speech and the right body drop out before they can be named; that is evacuation, not a metaphor. Containment here is the scan itself: the wedge of hypodensity gives the nameless deficit a territory so the team can think MCA instead of drowning in mute panic.

2015-279.sentence: Motivational enhancement therapy treats readiness as a limit you do not rush: empathy, discrepancy, no argument, roll with resistance, support self-efficacy. You end the fantasy that confrontation can terminate ambivalence on your timetable; change starts when he can hold the gap between his drinking and his values.

2015-280.sentence: Eliciting and testing automatic thoughts is Kleinian work in cognitive clothes: the thought I am worthless is a projected bad object, not a fact. You help her take it back inside and look at the evidence, moving from paranoid certainty toward depressive concern—repair instead of evacuation.

2015-281.sentence: Sertraline lets you hold both objects—seizure control and the depression—without sacrificing one to treat the other. Bupropion, amoxapine, or desipramine attack the good epilepsy object by lowering threshold; the SSRI keeps the pair in one relationship.

2015-282.sentence: This is Erikson’s identity-versus-role-confusion year: a first-year mind asked to be student, child, friend, and future all at once. Generalized anxiety disorder is the stage stalling as worry—the mind going blank, the restlessness—floods every role so no single identity can settle.

2015-283.sentence: American Indian and Alaska Native suicide rates are not a demographic footnote; they walk in as a cultural third—colonization, poverty, and intergenerational loss sitting between you and this patient. Use that knowledge to widen the safety plan (kin, tribe, IHS, elders), not to flatten the person into a category.

2015-284.sentence: Alprazolam had become the stand-in attachment figure: a chemical other that damped panic when no person was available. Flumazenil unhooks that GABA-A clamp, so if you give it, stay at the bedside—the nervous system may have no other regulator and can seize.

2015-285.sentence: The child's ego learned to hold fear with a small dog in a quiet room; that is a narrow window of affect tolerance, not a cured phobia. A large dog at a birthday party is a new context and a bigger stimulus, so renewal of clinically significant fear is expected until exposure is practiced more broadly.

2015-286.sentence: She can still write because the language motor program is intact, but a lesion involving the splenium of the corpus callosum (classically with left occipital cortex) cuts vision off from language, so her own script is unreadable. The symptom is a disconnection: production without recognition—do not treat it as conversion or “not trying.”

2015-287.sentence: Sudden inability to sit, crossed cranial signs (left VI, weak corneal, facial weakness), and vomiting mean the postural and brainstem apparatus has been hit, not that two people are “making a pattern.” Hypertensive hemorrhage in cerebellum or pons can wipe ego-level motor control in minutes—get the CT and neurosurgery, not a relational formulation.

2015-288.sentence: Years of backward falls, vertical ophthalmoplegia, axial rigidity, and dementia are the late-life ego losing midbrain programs that keep the body oriented. Autopsy in progressive supranuclear palsy shows tau-positive neurofibrillary tangles, not Lewy-type alpha-synuclein inclusions.

2015-289.sentence: Depersonalization is the psyche’s way of getting out of a body that still holds what cannot be remembered as a story. The person does not recall the trauma; they watch themselves from the hallway so the unrepresented state never has to arrive as “I was there.”

2015-290.sentence: Inattention that outlasts childhood hyperactivity sits on Erikson’s industry versus inferiority: the task of being able to work, finish, and feel competent. When that task never quite lands, adulthood keeps the same unfinished school-desk problem—not the running, the inability to stay with the work.

2015-291.sentence: The bilateral sixth-nerve palsies and that CSF (protein 223, glucose 25, mixed cells) are Mycobacterium tuberculosis announcing itself in a man whose drinking has already thinned his body’s defenses. The syndrome is doing the work his history would not: forcing a stop, a hospital, and a name for years of self-erasure.

2015-292.sentence: The cake binge is a paranoid-schizoid moment: the good, needed object is attacked by devouring it whole so it cannot leave. Hours of compensatory exercise are the depressive attempt at repair—trying to put the ruined, “too much” self back together so she can still look good and keep the object.

2015-293.sentence: The MCMI-III (here labeled MCMI-OD) is not a Rorschach or a WCST; it is a structured inventory built to put a personality diagnosis on paper. Ordering it is a frame move: you refuse to let the chaos of the relationship be the only “test,” and you get a score you can share instead of an enactment.

2015-294.sentence: Tetrabenazine depletes vesicular dopamine (VMAT2) when guanfacine and antipsychotics have already failed, and the family will recruit you as the last adult who can finally stop the tics. Notice the countertransference pull to become the magic fixer; prescribe the drug, but do not become the tic-suppressing parent they are handing you.

2015-295.sentence: An unsigned “Dr. Empathy” blog is a frame problem: the reader cannot locate who is speaking, so the usual limits of credential, liability, and accountability never get named. The Federation of State Medical Boards is asking you to keep the identity of the doctor representable—name and credentials visible—so the relationship does not stay an unowned, unremembered voice on the internet.

2015-296.sentence: A 16-year-old on probation still needs a parental coalition that can hold one set of expectations; that developmental capacity lives in the parents first, not in a more “egalitarian” family meeting. Structural work is the late arrival of hierarchy: both parents define rules they can actually back, so the adolescent is not left to organize himself around two competing grown-ups.

2015-297.sentence: Point tenderness at T5 plus a nipple-level sensory cut and new incontinence is spinal epidural abscess until proven otherwise—do not let a heroin history become a sanctioned gap in urgency. The team’s conscience fails here when “this is just withdrawal” or “they did this to themselves” delays the scan; that is a moral loophole, not a neurologic differential.

2015-298.sentence: Frequent hospitalizations after adequate antipsychotic trials are an evacuation: the unthinkable chaos of missed meds and lost follow-up gets dumped into the ED instead of being held. Assertive community treatment is the container that goes to the patient, so the raw disorganization can be metabolized in the community rather than only in a hospital bed.

2015-299.sentence: After subarachnoid blood, CSF clearance at the arachnoid granulations has a hard time limit the brain cannot rush; headache, vomiting, and falling alertness mean acute hydrocephalus, not a mood you can wait out. The CT of enlarging ventricles is the system hitting that limit: absorption failed, pressure rose, and consciousness is already ending.

2015-300.sentence: Two attendings deadlocked over depression versus delirium freeze the clock; residents and nurses will not speak while the hierarchy still pretends it does not need them. Leaders have to say, out loud, that they need help and value other opinions—otherwise the conflict never becomes thinkable and the workup of delirium stays stalled.

2016-1.sentence: The steep-road detour is already a private rule about what they will not enter, and the clinic should not quietly adopt that same detour by treating every panic as an emergency to be routed around. Keep the hour pointed at that one avoided stretch so the fear stays locatable instead of turning the frame into endless accommodation.

2016-2.sentence: Those inner figures of self and other are what get parked on staff when the patient flips from idealizing to devaluing. The flip is a change of which mental representation is on stage, not a random mood.

2016-3.sentence: The cousin's Mexico trip is a defense: they leave your mania questions by sliding onto someone else's story and never return. Tangentiality here is not only a thought-form; it keeps their own impulsivity off the table.

2016-4.sentence: The wish is to abolish a sodium of 95 in one heroic push; the prohibition is the pons, which shears if you obey that wish. Central pontine myelinolysis is that collision: rescue speed versus the brain's need for a slow climb.

2016-5.sentence: Using a banana as a phone is a small competence win: the child can make the world fit an inner picture and feel effective. Symbolic play is the self practicing “I can make meaning” without needing the object to already be the thing.

2016-6.sentence: Paroxetine's short half-life means a missed pill is not a quiet gap; the brain dumps the unprocessed withdrawal as dizziness and zaps. That is failed containment: the drug usually holds the raw state, and when it vanishes overnight the feeling returns unnamed.

2016-7.sentence: Fluoxetine 20 mg has not had its four-to-six-week trial yet, so the dyad is bumping into a hard limit: mood recovery cannot be rushed just because the patient is impatient with three weeks of leftover mild symptoms. Hold the dose and reassess in two weeks; switching or adding buspirone now is a flight from time, not treatment.

2016-8.sentence: A three-year-old’s sense of herself as female is not a solo milestone; it is named, mirrored, and used between her and the people who dress, bathe, and talk about her. Tying laces or copying a square can wait; this identity is already a two-person fact in the room.

2016-9.sentence: In a school-age child with tics, major depression is the comorbidity that is still uncommon; ADHD, OCD-spectrum worry, and learning trouble are the ones that usually ride along. Do not dig for a hidden depressive narrative the child’s mind has not yet organized; screen those neighbors and stay supportive until adolescence, when mood disorders actually catch up.

2016-10.sentence: This is a case-control study: the researchers started from adults already labeled schizophrenic and looked backward at daily adolescent cannabis, then compared them with people who never earned that diagnosis. Watch the conscience in the design: once you sample from the ‘sick’ column, cannabis can look like a moral cause rather than an exposure you still have to measure without judging it.

2016-11.sentence: Periodic limb movement syndrome is the overnight EMG story the patient never owned: bursts under five seconds, every twenty to forty seconds, while the mind reports only ‘sleep problems.’ Body-self awareness of those legs never quite arrived; the bed partner and the tracing hold the history the sleeper cannot tell.

2016-12.sentence: Pramipexole, the D3-preferring agonist, can dump an unrepresented urge into the room as compulsive gambling the Parkinson patient does not experience as a remembered wish. The spouse is left living the wreckage in the bank account; treat the drug, not a sudden character flaw.

2016-13.sentence: An interpersonal psychodynamic group lives on ordinary transference: people try you on as parent, rival, or longed-for friend and then talk about it. Antisocial personality disorder tends to recruit you and the other members into exploitation or legal-risk suspicion instead, so the room becomes a hunt rather than a place to notice who you are being asked to become.

2016-14.sentence: The postsynaptic cell cannot wait for the presynaptic terminal to be a reliable selfobject, so it makes endocannabinoids on demand and sends them backward to say “enough.” That retrograde signal is a competence move: the receiving cell protects its own equilibrium instead of drowning in glutamate or GABA it did not ask for.

2016-15.sentence: The old medical wish is to lead, diagnose, and decide; recovery principles put a prohibition on that grab for control. Collaborating in partnership with consumers to support their goals is how you hold the collision: you keep your expertise without discharging the wish to be the one who knows.

2016-16.sentence: A suicidal crisis does not wait for insight, media guidelines, or a school screen to ripen. Restricting access to lethal methods is the limit you can actually hold: you buy time when the capacity to stay alive cannot be rushed.

2016-17.sentence: The fury about the move arrives as something to dump: end the relationship and get the loss of control out of the body. Your job is containment—holding that raw anger until it can become thinkable as Erikson’s intimacy versus isolation, the late-twenties task of staying coupled without dissolving.

2016-18.sentence: ECT only works if someone holds the frame on seizure threshold. Lorazepam has to come off before the first treatment; leaving a standing benzodiazepine in place is not kindness, it is letting a sedative quietly veto the procedure.

2016-19.sentence: Case management’s honest job in addiction is retention: a person who can stay in the room long enough to notice their own part. If you sell reduced use or HIV rates as the first win, you invite a false insight—the service looks like it failed when the real trial comment is, “Can we keep showing up together?”

2016-20.sentence: A point mutation is a tiny rewrite—one base swapped, inserted, or deleted—and the psyche treats it the same way: one letter can change the whole sentence. Families often want the change to mean destiny; the clinical meaning is smaller and sharper—this is a local edit, not a whole-chapter copy-number rewrite.

2016-21.sentence: Hearing is a developmental achievement that NF-2 can take back: bilateral vestibular schwannomas steal a capacity that had already arrived. The late loss is not “noncompliance with listening”; the auditory channel itself is being dismantled by the tumor biology.

2016-22.sentence: REM atonia is the night’s conscience: the body is forbidden to act the dream. When polysomnography shows REM without atonia, that brake is off and punching or yelling is the dream leaking into muscle, not a moral lapse.

2016-23.sentence: “Worst headache of my life” recruits you as the doctor who must not miss the bleed, and a normal CT tempts a countertransference of premature reassurance. Lumbar puncture is staying in that role: you look for xanthochromia instead of becoming the person who waves the danger away.

2016-24.sentence: When reality testing is thin and splitting is the main way good and bad objects are held, uncovering therapy asks for a integration the ego cannot yet do. Supportive work is the holding environment: you lend structure and impulse control so the relationship stays in one piece.

2016-25.sentence: A cerebellar hemisphere lesion does not throw the deficit across the midline; skilled movement fails in the arm and hand on the same side as the damage. That is the opposite of projective identification—evacuating an unwanted state into the other—because the clumsiness stays in the ipsilateral limb instead of being put into the contralateral one.

2016-26.sentence: Intimate partner violence is not a soft “relationship factor” you fold into female orgasmic disorder; gendered coercion is already a third in the room. Orgasm that fails while she is being hit is adaptive silence, not a disorder of her sexuality.

2016-27.sentence: At forty-three the Erikson task is generativity: staying reliably present without a heroic new consult. Regular visits with an actual exam give a holding schedule so the lump, bloating, and chest pain do not have to escalate to keep the doctor from leaving.

2016-28.sentence: DSM names cannot be dropped into a rural clinic and expected to finish the work; local culture sets a hard limit on how far those labels travel. You do not end the idiom—“thinking too much,” spirits—by replacing it with a faster Western diagnosis.

2016-29.sentence: Trail Making Test B asks the depressed adolescent to stay put and switch sets; major depression can make that sequencing fail while she never leaves the chair. That is a vertical split: executive function—the part that alternates letters and numbers—has stepped out.

2016-30.sentence: A true tonic-clonic seizure dumps prolactin; a nonepileptic convulsion does not, because the motor storm is a bid for a person, not a cortical discharge. Lack of that rise is the lab’s way of saying this was proximity-seeking in seizure clothing.

2016-31.sentence: A hypersensitive infant has thin affect tolerance: ordinary sound and touch hit like threat, so startle and crying are the only available regulators. That is not “being difficult”; it is a nervous system that cannot yet hold stimulation long enough to settle, so the adult’s job is to shrink the world until the baby can use it.

2016-32.sentence: Disorganized speech is a vertical split you can hear: thought leaves the sentence the way a person leaves without leaving the chair. When delusions and hallucinations are missing, that derailment is still Criterion A because the mind has lost the thread that keeps one speaker, one topic, one reality in the room.

2016-33.sentence: Prostaglandin D2 raising extracellular adenosine is the body’s way of saying “you already stayed up”; the crash is not optional, it is chemistry collecting the debt. Calling that an enactment fits the insomnia consult: she and the night keep repeating wired-then-crash instead of treating adenosine as the signal to stop.

2016-34.sentence: Fewer available dopamine receptors after 70 means a usual antipsychotic dose is already a big occupancy, so EPS show up as if you overdosed. Denial here is treating the 82-year-old like a young adult receptor map—same milligrams, same story—while the aging nigrostriatal system has less slack.

2016-35.sentence: Acyclovir is not a negotiation; HSV in medial temporal and orbitofrontal cortex with left temporal periodic discharges is a clock, and the pill is the only feed that can still save memory. Delay turns the drug into proof of need you waited too long to meet—confusion and command-following already tell you the temporal lobe is on fire.

2016-36.sentence: Dissociative identity disorder asks you to hold the frame for more than one occupant: travel amnesia, lost job skills, childhood gaps, out-of-body watching, sudden feeling, and a child’s voice are switches, not “poor memory.” Confidentiality and time still belong to one treatment; you do not let an alter, or your curiosity, rewrite who consented or how long the hour lasts.

2016-37.sentence: The urine-tampering already answers the insight question: they can plan and hide the production of illness, so they are not lost in a delusion. A trial comment is something like, “Part of you needs to be a patient here,” because factitious disorder is intentional falsification of medical or psychological signs without the obvious payout that would make it malingering.

2016-38.sentence: Fear of becoming his father arrived before any dementia did, so the adult capacity you are counting on is still intact: he can use foresight instead of waiting for damage. Primary prevention is that move—tighten blood pressure, diabetes, and lipids now, while cognition is still normal, rather than screening for early disease or rehabbing a stroke that has not happened.

2016-39.sentence: Those headaches, dizziness, and gut symptoms may be carrying the migration story he cannot yet put into a Western word like depression. “What do you think is causing your symptoms?” lets the symptom keep its meaning—neurasthenia, family strain, shame about work—before you translate it into a DSM checklist.

2016-40.sentence: Shared DNA is the starting genome, not the finished person; methylation and other epigenetic marks keep rewriting expression after the split. You cannot rush that clock: the twins’ environments write different chromatin over years, which is why one can develop schizophrenia while the identical twin does not.

2016-41.sentence: The agitation and appetite crash are not a request to stack another cholinesterase inhibitor; galantamine or rivastigmine would only double the same acetylcholine bet. A trial comment to the family is: the disease has moved past what donepezil can hold, so we add memantine, an NMDA antagonist, rather than pretend more of the old drug will restore the person they remember.

2016-42.sentence: Cortical acetylcholine is not a single “on” switch; those muscarinic receptors can excite or inhibit, which is why boosting ACh with donepezil can sharpen attention and also drop the heart rate. The self-esteem trap is thinking more transmitter always means more competence—Alzheimer cortex has fewer, not more, of these receptors, so you are supporting a fading system, not restoring a youthful self.

2016-43.sentence: Without thiamine, glucose sits in the neuron unused, so the mammillary bodies and periaqueductal gray cannot turn raw sensation into a thinkable scene. Confusion, locked lateral gaze, and a body that will not stand are the evacuation: experience is dumped as nystagmus and ataxia instead of being contained into words.

2016-44.sentence: IPT opens on the quality of social connections because withdrawal after a role transition is often the working defense: isolation keeps the grief from being shared and therefore from being felt. You map who is still in the room with the patient so that defense has less cover, not so you can interpret childhood or the unconscious.

2016-45.sentence: Two IDs at every visit is an enactment: the clinic is already living its fear of the wrong body in the chair rather than only discussing safety in committee. That ritual belongs to the IOM safe domain because identity mix-up is a harm event, not a courtesy or a throughput trick.

2016-46.sentence: The Caspi finding is MAOA plus maltreatment, not a gene that lets you drop the abuse story. If a parent says the boy’s aggression is “just genetic,” you hold the ethical limit: low-activity MAOA does not cancel the duty to name maltreatment and to protect.

2016-47.sentence: Chronotherapy for circadian rhythm sleep disorder is a prescribed clock, and the delayed-phase student often treats that clock as a demand to defy or a feed that finally organizes the day. You are not handing a hypnotic; you are asking them to take in an outside rhythm—light and wake time—as something that can set them rather than as poison.

2016-48.sentence: Tactile anomia for the left hand means the callosum is the missing secure base between the feeling hemisphere and the naming one. The left hand still knows the key; it just cannot borrow language from the left hemisphere, so the parts of the self cannot use each other to regulate into a word.

2016-49.sentence: Mood reactivity is a two-person sign: the low mood is not sealed inside her; another person’s warmth can still lift it. Lead-limb hypersomnia and binge-weight gain sit next to that interpersonal brightness, so the depression is organized around contact and rejection, not a one-person vegetative lock.

2016-50.sentence: She needs you as a mirroring other who can still see her as a patient, not as a damages calculator. The ethical limit is clinical presentation only—impairment ratings, causation, and dollar disability would collapse that selfobject function into a courtroom verdict on her worth.

2016-51.sentence: The wish is to stay in the play; the prohibition is time-out. Cleaning up to dodge that aversive is negative reinforcement: the behavior is strengthened because the feared stop is removed, not because a prize is added.

2016-52.sentence: A body has a caffeine-and-taurine ceiling that adolescence cannot negotiate away. Energy-drink restlessness, flush, twitching, and rambling speech are the physiology saying stop when he tried to outrun a limit.

2016-53.sentence: “What brought you to the hospital today?” is a container: you hold the unshaped mess long enough for it to become a sentence. Closed questions evacuate the dread into yes/no pellets; this open-ended prompt asks the patient to think the arrival instead of dump it.

2016-54.sentence: The FDA QTc box on paliperidone is the field’s conscience in print—you do not get a moral holiday because the patient needs an antipsychotic. With a 470 ms baseline and another QT drug already on board, that label is the prohibition you obey, not a footnote you waive.

2016-55.sentence: Hemispatial neglect after a right parietal stroke is not just “not looking left.” The parietal map that was supposed to hold the left half of the world never comes online, so the left side of the body and space never quite arrives as something that belongs to the self. Anosognosia is that developmental failure in adult form: the patient cannot mourn a loss he has no representation of.

2016-56.sentence: In Lesch-Nyhan, the X-linked HPRT defect leaves uric acid and self-biting as the story the child cannot tell in words. The lips and fingers become the site of an unrepresented state: pain that is enacted on the body instead of remembered as a wish, a fear, or a thought.

2016-57.sentence: On the Stroop Test you ask for ink color and the printed word recruits you to become the easier, automatic object. When he reads the word instead of naming the color, you feel the pull to finish the sentence for him—that tug is countertransference to a frontal system that cannot inhibit the first, louder stimulus.

2016-58.sentence: Reliability means the interview yields the same result across examiners and times; validity is a different question. When you and your co-resident split on the same patient, the instrument is dissociating—two vertical halves of the assessment that never occupy the same chair at once.

2016-59.sentence: Clouded sensorium is the ED’s way of saying the medical process is already in the room with you, not waiting for labs. Calling it “psych” while attention waxes and wanes is the enactment: the system repeats the split between mind and body instead of treating the delirium in front of you.

2016-60.sentence: JC virus in progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy invades oligodendrocytes when CD4 is this low; the white-matter lesions are tissue that can no longer hold a continuous story. What cannot be myelinated cannot be remembered as a coherent self, so the decline is lived as patchy, unrepresented gaps rather than a named illness.

2016-61.sentence: Neurosyphilis inflates the self into grandiose delusions while a broad-based gait tells the truth the cortex can no longer keep. The mind is not inventing late-onset schizophrenia; it is papering over a dying brain.

2016-62.sentence: Socratic questioning is a mirroring move: you treat her as someone who can think, not as someone who needs your reassurance. An automatic thought like “I bombed it, so I’m worthless” loses its grip when she finds the hole in it herself, and that finding is a self-esteem event.

2016-63.sentence: The false-belief marble test is a container in miniature: the child has to hold the doll’s wrong idea as a thought, not as the actual marble. Fail that, and the other person’s mind is not a mind—it is just the world, unmetabolized.

2016-64.sentence: Continuous quality improvement is a limit, not a lawsuit: you track satisfaction because the work can get better, not because someone is about to sue. Joint Commission will not give the unit a capacity it does not already practice between surveys.

2016-65.sentence: When a high-dose antipsychotic flattens craving and pleasure, the ventral striatum is not being moralized—it is being blocked. Insight here is noticing that the missing motivation is mesolimbic dopamine, not a character defect.

2016-66.sentence: Naloxone in the film is the frame you cannot personally sit in the room to enforce: under the tongue it stays quiet; injected it precipitates withdrawal. The ethics are in the molecule—buprenorphine treats, naloxone holds the IV line.

2016-67.sentence: Recent heavy drinking is not just a risk factor on a list; alcohol is already in the relationship as feed and poison at once, numbing the body while thinning the ego’s shock absorbers. When the crash comes, that same bottle has already taught the mind that safety lives outside the self, so the trauma sticks instead of being metabolized.

2016-68.sentence: A crossover design lets the first drug leave a residue in the second period—the leftover good or leftover bad of one object contaminating the next. Parallel groups keep each treatment in its own relationship so you are not measuring last month’s pill still sitting in the room.

2016-69.sentence: Early first intercourse that then tracks with more partners is not only epidemiology; it can be a paranoid-schizoid solution, using bodies to evacuate anxiety instead of holding one person with mixed feelings. The developmental task is depressive concern: staying with one relationship long enough to care what it costs the other person.

2016-70.sentence: Checking HLA-B*1502 before carbamazepine in a patient of Asian ancestry is the conscience of the prescription: a rigid, earned limit, not optional courtesy. Skipping the allele is a sanctioned gap in morality dressed up as efficiency, and Stevens–Johnson syndrome is what that gap can cost the skin.

2016-71.sentence: Graded task assignments treat the garage as a developmental load the ego cannot yet carry whole, so you lend the missing capacity in small, sequenced pieces. You are not cheerleading motivation; you are building the child’s-eye skill of starting when the whole job still feels like too much mother to take in at once.

2016-72.sentence: Those four extra weekly CBCs after the WBC climbs back above 3,500/mm³ are not leftover bureaucracy; they are the afterimage of clozapine’s near-miss, the symptom of how close the marrow came to vanishing. The ritual of blood draws keeps the danger in view so neither you nor the family can pretend the agranulocytosis was only a number that already got better.

2016-73.sentence: An SSRI can strip the muscle atonia that usually cages REM, so the dream gets acted in the bed instead of stayed in the mind. That is a developmental misfire on Erikson’s integrity-versus-despair task: the older self cannot keep night-time aggression inside a story and has to punch it out.

2016-74.sentence: Social anxiety here is a mirroring wound: the stutter already taught the self that other eyes will not reflect competence, so the promotion and the restaurant feel like public proof of being inept. The solid marriage shows the need is not for a holding partner but for an audience that can still admire skill.

2016-75.sentence: Methyl groups on a promoter keep transcription factors off the DNA, so the gene cannot speak. Drive-wise that is a prohibition winning: the wish to mount a glucocorticoid stress response is silenced at the nucleotide, the same way a harsh inner no can shut a feeling before it is ever thought.

2016-76.sentence: Oxytocin is the neurohormone of social bonding; when a traumatic delivery and missing skin-to-skin starve it, attachment stays unrepresented—felt as emptiness rather than a rememberable story. What cannot be encoded as “we are a pair” then repeats in the body as numbness toward the infant.

2016-77.sentence: MHPAEA says psychiatric copays and day limits cannot be tighter than medical/surgical ones, so the denial of inpatient psych days while medicine gets a bed is the plan recruiting you as the stingy parent. Notice the countertransference: irritation at the insurer is useful data that someone is being asked to absorb the patient’s worthlessness.

2016-78.sentence: Hoarding most often rides with major depression, so the pile is not a solo ritual but a two-person bargain: keep the stuff and we never have to face the deadness between us. The distress at discarding is interpersonal—someone would have to stay present while the object, and the mood, leave.

2016-79.sentence: Hyperpigmentation plus collapse of energy is the body announcing it cannot keep itself upright without an adrenal partner. The ACTH stimulation test asks whether that partner still answers when you call—attachment measured at the gland, not only in the waiting room.

2016-80.sentence: Lithium’s frame is the kidney’s clearance; celecoxib (like other NSAIDs) quietly tightens that clearance and the level climbs. You hold the limit by treating the new analgesic as a frame break, not a harmless add-on.

2016-81.sentence: A cortical column is a vertical stack that already works as one processor, not a spare part waiting for later use. Development of cortex is the stacking of those functional units so information can be handled in place.

2016-82.sentence: Dopamine in the mesolimbic path is the signal that the high should not stop. Drugs of abuse hijack that signal, so ending the use feels like ending the only clock the reward system will honor.

2016-83.sentence: Rationalization is a story that makes embezzling sound like bookkeeping: the company still profits, so nothing was taken. Insight starts when they can hear that sentence as a cover, not as an audit.

2016-84.sentence: Abrupt audiovisual hallucinations with tachycardia and sweats, while still oriented, is alcohol withdrawal—not a new self coming apart from inside. Alcohol had been propping mood and arousal; when it drops, the borrowed cohesion fails in hours.

2016-85.sentence: The EEG’s bilateral triphasic waves are the liver’s ammonia made visible: a raw metabolic storm that the cortex cannot bind into thought, so it arrives as confusion and asterixis instead of words. Your job on the C-L note is containment: name the wave pattern so the team can think hepatic encephalopathy rather than evacuate the case as “just delirium.”

2016-86.sentence: Step one—admitting powerlessness over the addiction—is not piety; it is saying out loud a state that has lived only as using, blackout, and the body repeating what cannot yet be remembered as a story. Until that unrepresented helplessness is spoken, the twelve-step program has nothing to work on but another enactment of control.

2016-87.sentence: Care managers win in primary-care depression because they sit in the collision between the wish to be well and the prohibition against needing more than a ten-minute visit. Guidelines and CME stay on the shelf; a person who calls, tracks PHQ-9s, and pulls the patient back is the compromise formation that actually treats.

2016-88.sentence: Glycine (or D-serine) as obligate co-agonist means the NMDA channel will not open on glutamate alone—the synapse needs a second “yes.” That second yes is what the finding is doing: it licenses plasticity, which is why ketamine and glycine-site drugs can change mood instead of just blocking a receptor.

2016-89.sentence: Winnicott’s mirroring is the parent’s face giving the infant their own feeling back, so a self can begin to exist as something seen rather than only raw affect. Holding keeps the body safe; mirroring is the developmental move that arrives when the parent is attuned most of the time and shows it.

2016-90.sentence: Mental health court increasing engagement in community treatment is the system stepping out of the usual jail-and-drop enactment: the two-person repetition of “you’re dangerous / you’re abandoned.” Diversion names the illness in a courtroom so the defendant and the clinic can stay in a treatment relationship instead of another booking.

2016-91.sentence: Wanting the psychiatrist parked in the clinic is a kind of denial: it treats proximity as if it were the treatment, so nobody has to feel how much care actually falls through the cracks. Collaborative care works when a non-physician care manager holds that anxiety and coordinates the work, instead of pretending co-location undoes the split.

2016-92.sentence: A tic shows leftover ego strength: the patient can briefly suppress the jerk, which is impulse control, then the urge wins and relief follows. That premonitory urge-and-relief loop is not myoclonus (no warning) and not a compulsion (no feared thought the ego is bargaining with).

2016-93.sentence: Pathological laughter or crying is a vertical split: the face leaves the feeling without anyone leaving the chair. Lesions in the frontal–pons–cerebellum loop uncouple displayed affect from mood, so the family sees a storm the patient does not own.

2016-94.sentence: Split treatment is a two-person pattern: psychiatrist and unaffiliated therapist each quietly assign the other the job of knowing how suicidal the patient is. After the job loss, that unsaid bargain is an enactment—living the disconnect instead of sharing the condition—and the law treats both as having a duty to know.

2016-95.sentence: After TBI, the tablet is not a gadget so much as a borrowed secure base: an external mind that holds appointments when the injured one cannot. Monthly sessions are proximity on purpose—the therapist stays close while the patient learns to use that object to self-regulate, which is cognitive rehabilitation, not cheerleading.

2016-96.sentence: Anti-Yo turns the cerebellum into a hated stand-in: the immune system cannot hold tumor and Purkinje cell as separate objects, so it attacks both. Order the chest CT next to find the hidden bad object (occult cancer in this long-time smoker) rather than treating a normal MRI as proof that nothing malignant is in the relationship.

2016-97.sentence: Last observation carried forward is a conservative move: when a third of an antidepressant trial vanishes before week 8, you keep the last measured score instead of pretending the missing weeks will keep improving. That is the same clinical judgment as support over uncovering—do not invent a deeper ending the patient never stayed long enough to give you.

2016-98.sentence: The REM sleep behavior—shouting and punching in sleep—is not a random neurology extra; it is the body acting a dream it can no longer contain, the same leak that later becomes visual hallucinations in dementia with Lewy bodies. Transient help from levodopa/carbidopa then fading tells you the motor gain was never the point of the illness; the fluctuating mind and the dream-enactment are.

2016-99.sentence: Low CSF 5-hydroxyindole acetic acid (5-HIAA), the main serotonin breakdown product, is the most consistent chemical footprint of a violent, impulsive suicide attempt—aggression that never got bound into thought. That is a drive problem, not a stage problem: the impulse fires before the person can use any Erikson task to name what they want to live for.

2016-100.sentence: Organizational culture theory says the unit runs on shared meaning and 'how we do things here,' not on the seclusion protocol you posted. A trial comment to staff—'we treat the policy as the outsider and protect the old ritual'—tests whether they can see their own part instead of only blaming the written rule.

2016-101.sentence: Light does not negotiate with the clock: intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells project to the suprachiasmatic nucleus and drag the circadian day into alignment. Bright light for seasonal depression or delayed sleep phase works because that nucleus will not be rushed; you give time a reliable cue and wait for the phase to move.

2016-102.sentence: An advance directive is the frame written while the 60-year-old with early bipolar-related cognitive change is still lucid: who speaks, and what care is refused, when mania or incapacity arrives. Guardianship, conservatorship, guardian ad litem, and a representative payee are later substitutions by the court or the system; they are not the patient's own prior consent.

2016-103.sentence: Telephone consultation is part of the DBT frame, not a favor you grant when you feel generous. You hold the limit by teaching skills in the crisis call instead of becoming the after-hours soother.

2016-104.sentence: The ACA territory is the homunculus’s foot and leg, so a left ACA infarct writes contralateral foot–leg weakness on the exam before the patient can tell you the story. Read the body as a map of the vessel, not as a vague “stroke.”

2016-105.sentence: Frotteurism is touching or rubbing a nonconsenting person for sexual arousal; here the “exam” is the cover for the act. A wish for genital contact collides with the prohibition of the professional role, so the contact is staged as an accident of knees and a stool.

2016-106.sentence: Financial stress is a real risk factor for child abuse, not a moral footnote. When money panic cannot be contained—held long enough to become thinkable—it can be evacuated into the child as hitting, screaming, or neglect.

2016-107.sentence: School age is industry versus inferiority: the self wants a mirror that says “you can do this,” not a pep talk about identity. When competence is not recognized, irritability and school refusal are often the self collapsing, not a primary mood disorder.

2016-108.sentence: The 5-HT3 receptor is a ligand-gated ion channel, so ondansetron can shut nausea in minutes, not after a G-protein cascade. Fast receptors mean the body can dump a feeling as retching before anyone has time to think it.

2016-109.sentence: A personal feed is not a secure base; it is your private life, and the patient cannot use it to regulate without collapsing you into a friend. A separate professional account keeps proximity available (hours, policies, psychoeducation) without inviting them into your vacation photos, which is the attachment version of a locked office door.

2016-110.sentence: Biofeedback works by operant conditioning: the tone or graph is a reward when EMG or heart-rate variability moves the right way, so the body learns control the way a hungry infant learns that a cry brings milk. The screen is not magic and not a pill; it is a feed that proves the patient can change a physiological signal on purpose.

2016-111.sentence: Calling later-life desire 'over anyway' is often suppression: the person knows the wish is still there and parks it to avoid shame or a limp erection. A majority of middle-aged and older adults stay sexually active, so the work is naming the wish instead of using age as a polite gag.

2016-112.sentence: A trial comment that lands is: the brain laid down the most synapses in the first four years, so early neglect hit during construction, not after the house was built. Insight here is whether the parents can own that timing without collapsing into fatalism—early intervention still uses leftover plasticity rather than waiting for a later 'growth spurt' that never peaks the same way.

2016-113.sentence: The frame is the interview you actually do: CATIE found alcohol, not cocaine or cannabis, was the most common substance in that schizophrenia sample. You hold the limit by screening beer and wine with the same seriousness as street drugs, because the missed drink is what quietly wrecks the antipsychotic trial.

2016-114.sentence: Evoked potentials test whether the visual pathway still fires when the person cannot 'see'—a check on reality testing, not a moral verdict. If the cortex answers and the exam is clean, the ego is using blindness to manage affect it cannot yet bear, and the finding lets you treat function without pretending the eyes are dead.

2016-115.sentence: The prefrontal cortex is the region whose neurons remodel most in old age, so planning and multitasking get leakier even when memory networks are still decent. Attachment-wise, that loss of an internal executive often shows up as leaning on a spouse or adult child as a secure base—the other person becomes the borrowed frontal lobe that holds the day together.

2016-116.sentence: Hyperactive deep tendon reflexes mean the upper motor neuron has stopped putting a lid on the stretch reflex, so the limb fires too big and too fast. That is an enactment in the body: the old spinal circuit is living the movement instead of waiting for cortical commentary, the same way a dyad can act a pattern instead of thinking it.

2016-117.sentence: Maternal smoking tracks with decreased birth weight, not bigger heads or faster lungs. Dissociation is the split that lets a person light another cigarette while knowing the fetus is already paying in grams—the knowledge sits in one stream and the habit in another, so quitting feels optional until you name both at once.

2016-118.sentence: Cohort studies bleed power through loss to follow-up: the people who vanish are not a random leftover, they are often the sicker, the angrier, or the ones who never attached to the study. Object relations shows up in the dataset—the “good” subjects who stay and the “bad” objects who disappear leave you holding a cleaned-up relationship that no longer matches the original cohort.

2016-119.sentence: Ideomotor apraxia is tested by asking the patient to pretend to light a match—the skilled gesture has to be summoned from memory, not rescued by a real object in the hand. In Kleinian terms the pantomime is a small act of depressive concern: you have to hold the idea of the match and still try to do right by it, instead of only managing the concrete thing in front of you.

2016-120.sentence: Adolescence is the phase that packages idealism with a sense of invulnerability, which is why a 16-year-old can floor it drunk and mean it when they say nothing bad would happen. Drive conflict is the collision: the wish to feel omnipotent and unbound runs into a still-thin prohibition against death, so the risky act is the compromise, not a random lapse in judgment.

2016-121.sentence: When a postpartum woman cannot remember or think the terror of harming the infant, the unrepresented state shows up as a poison delusion and a demand to leave—the body and the dyad act it instead of naming it. That is why you treat this as an infanticide emergency: the baby is already inside the unthinkable scene, not a metaphor you can interpret from the doorway.

2016-122.sentence: She is recruiting you as the doctor who will not add another pill—watch the countertransference wish to be the kind, non-pharma one who hands her an “natural” out. You can still name SAMe honestly: it has some evidence in depression, and your job is not to become either the withholding MD or the supplement pal.

2016-123.sentence: The APA rule is a hard superego: no sexual relationship with current or former patients, period—not after discharge, not after “consent,” not after a clean termination. The flirtatious text is the moment conscience either holds or invents a sanctioned gap (“treatment is over, so it is private life”).

2016-124.sentence: Insight here is whether they can use a trial comment that sedative-hypnotic withdrawal (alprazolam, not opioids or cocaine) can seize and kill, while opioid withdrawal mostly just feels like dying. If they cannot see their own part in daily benzo use, they will leave against advice and you are left holding the medical emergency they refuse to own.

2016-125.sentence: TMS is a limit, not a shortcut: the coil sits over prefrontal cortex because that is the reachable depression circuit after meds and after ECT is off the table. You cannot rush prefrontal recovery the way a resident wants a last-session cure; the time course belongs to the target, not to the wish to be done.

2016-126.sentence: The raw fact that oxcarbazepine induces enzymes and can drop oral contraceptive levels has to be contained—named, held, thought—before it becomes an unplanned pregnancy you both “never saw coming.” If you evacuate the anxiety into a quick script change, the unthinkable stays in the body instead of in words.

2016-127.sentence: Slower visual processing in this healthy 75-year-old is a real limit, not a moral failing, and the adult child's push to take the keys can land as a collapse of the parent's competence, the feeling of being able and seen as able. Name the aging fact first so you can still offer a mirroring response: you see the parent's wish to stay a capable driver, and you also see the accidents.

2016-128.sentence: A single nucleotide polymorphism is a one-base swap, the common sequence variation, and it is easy to treat the CYP2D6 letters as a bad object stuffed into the patient. Hold the finding as ordinary genomic noise first so paranoid-schizoid splitting, all-or-nothing good gene versus cursed gene, can give way to depressive concern: this variant is one fact to use, not a verdict to evacuate.

2016-129.sentence: Methylmalonic acid rising when serum B12 is only borderline is the confirming lab for this gait, hyperreflexia, and lost vibration and position sense. The body is holding the good and the bad of malnutrition in one pathway: not enough cobalamin, and a metabolite that will not lie about it.

2016-130.sentence: Fluorescent in situ hybridization, not a routine karyotype, is what confirms the 22q11 microdeletion of velocardiofacial syndrome when psychosis shows up after cleft palate and learning trouble. Until that name is in the room the family is left with nameless dread, raw terror with no thinkable shape; FISH contains the dread by turning it into a locatable deletion.

2016-131.sentence: Complete sentences usually arrive at 3 years, not at 2 and not because a parent wishes them earlier. Language has a termination-like limit: you cannot rush the clock of syntax any more than you can rush an ending that has not ripened.

2016-132.sentence: Same-sex groupings regardless of activity are the dominant playground pattern in third and fourth grade, so a 9-year-old who only plays with boys is often developmentally on script. A trial comment that invites insight: I wonder if the worry is more about our wish for mixed-sex ease than about what his mind can actually do with peers right now.

2016-133.sentence: The frame of hospice is not only morphine and a new bed; it is a planned rupture of the old holding environment—home, spouse, the chair by the window. Name the feared loss of the loved ones, or the consult becomes a polite discussion of pain while the real goodbye stays unspoken.

2016-134.sentence: The clock that cannot stop repeating is the mind asking for another dose of structure when set-shifting has failed in prefrontal cortex. The pill, like the examiner’s prompt, can become a demand to “do it right again,” so you treat the perseveration as a relationship to the task, not just a lesion.

2016-135.sentence: She is not hiding the grief; she is using suppression—she keeps the tears in the room and still thinks about adoption. That is the defense of a phase-of-life problem: the wish stays conscious, so you do not need to diagnose a disorder to make the sadness legitimate.

2016-136.sentence: Friedreich ataxia’s GAA expansion keeps copying itself; the consult can do the same if everyone only talks gait and cardiomyopathy and never the patient’s fear of disappearing into the diagnosis. That is an enactment: the system repeats “more neurology” instead of sitting with the person who is losing the body.

2016-137.sentence: Hyperprolactinemia from an antipsychotic can steal cycles, milk, and bone density—osteoporosis—while the patient still sits there looking “fine.” That is a dissociation of the body from the story: the skeleton is leaving without anyone leaving the chair, so you name the prolactin, not only the psychosis.

2016-138.sentence: Rizatriptan is abortive care for a young adult whose migraine keeps interrupting work—the Erikson task of generativity and industry in miniature. A pill that stops the attack says the body can be an ally again, so she is not stuck in a monthly crisis of competence.

2016-139.sentence: Creatinine clearance falling while the serum creatinine still looks tidy is the kidney's quiet bargain with age: less muscle makes less creatinine, so the lab number stays polite while clearance drops. The symptom of a “normal” 0.9 is doing cover work—it lets everyone dose like the GFR is young unless you name the decline and calculate it.

2016-140.sentence: Pedigree analysis is the frame that says the family is the unit of observation: markers that travel with the phenotype across generations are the only data that count. You do not recruit convenience cases or sib pairs here; you hold the limit of who is in the pedigree and who is not, because co-segregation only means something inside that bounded tree.

2016-141.sentence: When he can say the nausea is from the drug and he wants out, that is usable insight: he sees his body and his wish as his own, not only his wife's. A trial comment is to treat that statement as competent dissent—proxy consent started the trial; his present mind ends it.

2016-142.sentence: Binge-purge anorexia leans on acting out: the impulse is discharged into a binge, a purge, or a weekend stimulant rather than held as a feeling. Substance use rides the same discharge channel; restriction more often uses denial and control, while this subtype uses the body and the bottle to evacuate the conflict.

2016-143.sentence: She wants you as the couples pill: the same good object who already feeds her individual work, now prescribed to the marriage. Impartiality is the dose limit—if you swallow that request you become her proof, not a third who can hear both of them.

2016-144.sentence: The year of shoplifting, sugar craving, and hoarding is not a new character who “left”; it is a frontal split in which the person who used to inhibit is gone while the body stays in the chair. SPECT is useful because it can show the hypoperfusion that matches that vertical cut—behavior unmoored from the self that used to own it.

2016-145.sentence: The psychoeducation hour can become an enactment: you and the room are already living a medicalizing script instead of talking about fear of the person. Naming mental illness a brain disease does not buy more tolerant attitudes; it can keep the public one step further from relationship.

2016-146.sentence: Jail is forced separation from every usual attachment figure, so suicide is the protest when there is no secure base left. Federal courts therefore require a suicide prevention program as the institution's duty of proximity, not optional counseling or a forensic specialist on staff.

2016-147.sentence: Five days off lamotrigine is not a small slip the ego can just power through; the immune system has lost its titration and Stevens-Johnson is the cost of rushing. Restart at 25 mg and walk the full initial schedule, even if mood still looks intact.

2016-148.sentence: The default mode network is the mind off-task, reprocessing what already happened rather than tracking new stimuli. That is the technical warrant for leaving some sessions less goal-directed: this circuit uses rest to rework old experience, not to idle cheaply.

2016-149.sentence: In the prison clinic the pair is never only two people; the institution is in the room with you. Imminent plans to escape or create disorder break confidentiality here in a way HIV status, inmate threats, and old crime details do not.

2016-150.sentence: In DBT the cutting, rage, or crisis call is treated as a behavior that already has a job, not as a riddle to interpret. The therapist uses contingencies and skills to replace that job, rather than holding the feeling until its meaning arrives.

2016-151.sentence: This sits on Erikson's initiative-versus-guilt years: a four-and-a-half-year-old is supposed to invent a world, not yet police it. The dinner-table monkey is practice at taking the lead in play; worry more if the child cannot leave the companion when reality needs them.

2016-152.sentence: In group CBT the pain is allowed to stay real; the work is to stop organizing a whole life around waiting for it to vanish. Functioning despite pain means the symptom can be a fact without remaining the only story the person is allowed to tell.

2016-153.sentence: A trial that enrolls the wrong people cannot be honestly offered to the people you treat; that is a frame problem, not a p-value problem. If the sample is not the population to be treated, the result is a closed conversation that only looks like it includes your clinic.

2016-154.sentence: Numb fourth and fifth digits plus weak intrinsic hand muscles name an ulnar lesion at the elbow, not a stroke the two of you have to keep fearing together. Once you localize, the consult can stop colluding with catastrophe and start talking about a nerve at the funny bone.

2016-155.sentence: A just-turned-two-year-old who can kick a ball is using what this mind can actually do; asking for a copied circle or a tricycle is asking for a later ego. Support the parent with that milestone instead of interpreting delay they have not shown.

2016-156.sentence: The long recap of who broke the rules is school-age ego strength: the child is using story and the rulebook to bind impulse instead of hitting. Latency lives on that identification with the grown-up order; it is coping, not just tattling.

2016-157.sentence: Asking what they think is causing the pain invites them to use you as a secure base: a person they can stay near while they put a private theory into words. Homesickness and “what are you hiding” close that distance; the explanatory-model question keeps attachment available for regulation instead of turning the visit into a test of loyalty to the workup.

2016-158.sentence: Mild intellectual disability hits later-emerging social cognition harder than color names or a practiced bedtime script, so peer cues fail first. Treat that as a developmental mismatch, not willfulness: the child can do the household routine and still miss the glance that says “we’re joking now.”

2016-159.sentence: Hypocretin (orexin) from the lateral hypothalamus is the glue that keeps wake, REM, and muscle tone in one piece. When it is gone, the mind can drop into sleep or lose tone in a laugh the way a dissociative split leaves the chair without leaving the room— narcolepsy with cataplexy is that split written in peptides.

2016-160.sentence: Advanced paternal age tracks de novo mutations that raise the child’s risk of schizophrenia, a illness that later makes good and bad objects hard to hold in one person. Name the epidemiologic fact in counseling: older fathers, schizophrenia—not depression, ADHD, or antisocial personality as the robust signal.

2016-161.sentence: This restless, strictly unilateral periorbital attack with ipsilateral ptosis, miosis, tearing, and rhinorrhea is cluster; high-flow oxygen is the abortive that meets the mind where it is—in unbearable autonomic storm. Do not uncover “meaning” in the forty-minute window; support first, then talk when the attack has actually stopped.

2016-162.sentence: Localized amnesia—blanking a whole stretch of time, not a category of facts or one’s entire autobiography—is the usual bargain after trauma: the relationship-event is gone, the rest of the self stays. Reconstruct that interval with another person at a tolerable pace; forcing the missing hours recreates the original overrun.

2016-163.sentence: Upbeat nystagmus on primary gaze is the secure base: stay next to the medulla instead of wandering toward occult lung cancer or a chiasmal craniopharyngioma. The urge to chase a flashier lesion is separation protest—the exam already told you whom to stay close to.
