2016-164.sentence: In a job-loss flood you lend ego strength: affect tolerance and a bit of structure so the patient can stand the hour without more uncovering. Supportive therapy is that loan; psychoanalysis and IPT wait until impulse control and reality testing can hold the work.

2016-165.sentence: Classroom ‘checking out’ can look like a vertical split—the child leaves without leaving the chair—but treating only the anxiety with an SSRI abandons the ADHD half of the case. Combined psychostimulant plus behavior therapy (the MTA start) keeps both halves present instead of dissociating one diagnosis from the other.

2016-166.sentence: Haloperidol plus olanzapine on an already crowded med list is the enactment: the system is living ‘more dopamine blockade’ instead of talking about the rigidity. NMS—fever, CK 15,000, lead-pipe stiffness, mutism—is the body finishing that sentence; stop the neuroleptics rather than add another.

2016-167.sentence: The gait–incontinence–cognition triad tempts denial: call it Alzheimer and stop looking. Enlarged ventricles name NPH, a shunt-possible hydrocephalus, so the defense to name is premature foreclosure, not more cortical-atrophy storytelling.

2016-168.sentence: The team’s ‘dementia means incompetent’ is an unrepresented state: they repeat incapacity in the consult instead of remembering to test the actual decision. The legal standard is the opposite—the law presumes the person is competent until a court rules otherwise.

2016-169.sentence: Relative risk asks you to hold two people in mind at once—the one with chronic pain and the one without—and feel how much more likely the first is to err. Notice if you start identifying with the pain patient as doomed or with the pain-free worker as the real employee; that pull is countertransference, your feeling of being recruited to take a side instead of reading the ratio.

2016-170.sentence: Substance P from C-fibers cannot be hurried into silence by opioids; neurogenic inflammation keeps firing after the original injury is gone. That is a limit: the pain system has already ended its useful alarm and will not terminate on your timetable, so you treat the peptide cascade rather than demanding the hand “get over it.”

2016-171.sentence: Botulinum toxin works at the neuromuscular junction; insight will not uncurl the fingers of writer’s cramp. A trial comment about anxiety can still help her see she is not “just nervous,” but psychological mindedness here means knowing which part of the problem can use words and which part needs toxin.

2016-172.sentence: DSM enuresis waits until age five—or equivalent developmental age—before you name the wetting a disorder. Holding that age cutoff is the frame: you protect the four-year-old from a premature diagnosis instead of treating the mother’s alarm as the criterion.

2016-173.sentence: Intraneuronal tau, not the amyloid plaque outside the cell, is the protein piled up inside cortical neurons. When you offer that fact, the family may treat the biomarker like a feed or a poison—proof you still care, or proof nothing can be done—so name tau clearly and then notice which meaning they assign the result.

2016-174.sentence: Illness anxiety lives in the idea of disease, not in a felt symptom; after the acquaintance’s death the tumor cannot be remembered as someone else’s story, so it is repeated as hours of searching and a demand for PET. The unrepresented loss shows up in the dyad as “prove I am not dying,” while the body stays neurologically quiet.

2016-175.sentence: Multisystemic therapy puts helpers in the home and neighborhood so the teenager’s delinquent wish—to rule, steal, or blow up—meets a live prohibition that is not another locked ward. The conflict stays in the family and street where it is already being lived, instead of being evacuated into a hospital that only repeats the same fight.

2016-176.sentence: A 5000-word vocabulary at age 7 is a semantic shortfall: the child’s word-store is too thin to name what he feels, so self-esteem has little language to lean on. Mirroring then has to come through the few words he does have, or he looks dumb next to peers who already own about 14,000.

2016-177.sentence: The sandwich generation—teen applying to college and a father with new dementia—dumps two raw claims into one mind before they can be thought. If nobody helps him hold both, the insomnia is nameless dread leaking out as nights that will not metabolize the stretch.

2016-178.sentence: Extinction means you withdraw the attention that was the stimulus, so the scream-to-get-staff-over response weakens—not punish, not reinforce by rushing in. Attachment-wise, the patient is using proximity as regulation; if you vanish the rush without a plan, expect protest before the scream dies down.

2016-179.sentence: The thalamus-to-amygdala shortcut startles the veteran at a slammed door before cortex can say “just a door,” so two people in the room can already be in a threat dance. You name the fast path so the pair of you are not treating the flinch as a character problem.

2016-180.sentence: An IEP can change the academic requirement itself, not just extra time like a 504, so the child with ADHD and a learning disorder is not asked to hold a load his ego cannot yet carry. Modification is a scaffold for impulse control and self-esteem, not a license for the school to ignore disruption.

2016-181.sentence: Trinucleotide expansion analysis is the test that ends the vertical split: the CAG repeat is already writing the diagnosis in the DNA while the family still lives in the other room, calling it maybe something else. Dissociation here is not leaving the chair; it is keeping the father's state-hospital death and this patient's chorea in two unjoined files until the expansion count forces them together.

2016-182.sentence: Death from abuse peaks from birth to three years because the pair is not two people yet: the infant cannot protest, flee, or recruit a third, so the caregiver's rage has nowhere to go but the body. The changing story in the PICU is the relationship still being written by one person; your job is to stop that two-person script from finishing.

2016-183.sentence: Little Hans's horse phobia is attachment work in costume: the boy keeps the father close by fearing a stand-in he can avoid, so he never has to lose the real secure base. The symptom is a clumsy proximity strategy, not a random animal fear; he regulates distance to dad by putting the danger on the street.

2016-184.sentence: Kin selection says the childless aunt is not failing to reproduce; she is feeding her own genes through nieces and nephews, so the devotion is an investment, not a leftover life. The meaning of the altruism is inclusive fitness: her care is the family line's way of staying alive when she has no child of her own.

2016-185.sentence: Carbohydrate-deficient transferrin (CDT) is the frame you hold when self-report will not: it is the lab that names a return to heavy drinking without arguing about last weekend. Using CDT is an ethical limit, not a gotcha; you are the one who keeps time and truth when the patient cannot.

2016-186.sentence: Early Huntington disease is already an enactment in the exam room: GABA-producing medium spiny neurons are dying, and the son's irritability and fidgeting restage the father's fatal script before anyone says the name. You are not watching a one-person illness; the pair is repeating the family's last chapter in movements and mood.

2016-187.sentence: Parents who insist on a full toothbrushing ritual are often using denial: they cannot stand seeing the child as able to do only a sliver of the task. Shaping works because you reward the next approximation—open mouth, then tolerate the brush—so the demand stops being all-or-nothing.

2016-188.sentence: The family's panic after dense retrograde amnesia is a raw evacuation: they want the ECT out of the room so they do not have to think. You contain that dread—hold it long enough to make it thinkable—and then space the treatments farther apart so memory can recover without abandoning an effective course.

2016-189.sentence: Her amusement and intact insight are a preserved grandiose/cohesive self: the visions do not shatter competence the way a true psychotic process would. Name posterior cerebral artery ischemia so you do not strip that self-esteem by calling formed, silent, colorful children-playing hallucinations 'psychosis.

2016-190.sentence: Allelic exclusion and X-inactivation are not one genome acting alone; they are a two-party deal between DNA sequence and epigenetic marks (methylation, histone change). The identical-twin discordance is the same idea: two lives write different expression on the same letters.

2016-191.sentence: The baby who pulls the blanket and finds the ball can hold an object in mind when it is gone—so clinginess is a developmental achievement, not a lesion to uncover. Stay supportive: explain object permanence to the mother instead of interpreting her worry as if the infant already had a neurotic conflict.

2016-192.sentence: Ego strength here is reality testing after male-to-female reassignment: gender dysphoria and suicidality often ease, but general health problems rise and need watching. You do not treat the surgery as a magical wipe of the body; you keep medical surveillance while the psyche is doing better.

2016-193.sentence: Grapefruit juice irreversibly occupies intestinal CYP3A4, so the usual first-pass “goodbye” never happens and the benzo or statin stays in the blood like a guest who will not leave. Think of CYP3A4 as a secure-base enzyme that metabolizes the drug away; the juice blocks that base, and the patient cannot regulate drug levels without naming what they drink every morning.

2016-194.sentence: Salivating to the smell of dinner is an unconditioned response: the body already knew how to drool before anyone paired a bell with food. The junior resident needs that distinction so exposure is not sold as inventing a new reflex, only as teaching the learned CS–CR pair to fade.

2016-195.sentence: Eighty percent engaged in the substance program is a process measure: it counts whether people are doing the work of treatment, not whether they got sober. On Erikson’s map that is industry in action—showing up for the task—whereas an outcome measure would ask if identity as “in recovery” actually stuck.

2016-196.sentence: Antiphospholipid antibodies are the lupus finding most consistently tied to neuropsychiatric hits and clots, including miscarriage. They treat the vessel wall as all-bad object: the lining is attacked rather than held as a mixed, living surface that can both protect and fail.

2016-197.sentence: Short REM latency plus sleep attacks while driving is narcolepsy, so you reach for modafinil, not CPAP or zolpidem. The waking ego cannot contain the REM state; sleep is projected into daylight as a sudden takeover, and modafinil is the pharmacologic attempt to keep that split from winning the road.

2016-198.sentence: Mid-life’s job is to see that personal time is finite and death is not optional—not to rewrite the résumé or re-do intimacy. A trial comment names his part: the friend’s death made the clock his, and insight is whether he can sit with that limit instead of only managing it.

2016-199.sentence: Universal intervention treats the whole veteran population as the patient, so the limit is public messaging, not a private hour. You still hold confidentiality at the chair: a TV ad can name warning signs, but it cannot become your excuse to report, chase, or treat someone who never entered the frame.

2016-200.sentence: PCP with nystagmus, hypertension, and blunted pain puts the room in a paranoid-schizoid state: everyone is a threat, so swinging is self-defense. That is projective identification: the patient dumps terror into staff until you feel you must "take him" by force instead of thinking.

2016-201.sentence: When an SSRI only half-works, lithium as the best-supported augmenter besides atypicals is not a class story; it is a chemistry story. Skip the cultural-third reading here and stay with meaning of the symptom: leftover depression is unfinished work, not a failure of identity, and lithium names that remainder in ions rather than in who the patient is.

2016-202.sentence: Self-help groups set goals that ignore intragroup dynamics, so they stay supportive: same problem, shared hope, no excavation of how members use one another. Your process group can uncover those uses; AA-style meetings cannot, and promising personality change there overloads a mind that only asked for a room of peers.

2016-203.sentence: Adult neurogenesis in the hippocampus, especially the dentate gyrus, is where new cells can hold a new version of a relationship. Exercise and an SSRI do not just clear "fog"; they give the mind extra room to keep a good object and a bad object in one person instead of splitting them.

2016-204.sentence: Williams syndrome is a multi-gene deletion, and the overfriendly child treats every stranger as a secure base. Attachment is inverted: there is almost no stranger wariness, so proximity is used to regulate anxiety with anyone, not with a chosen caregiver.

2016-205.sentence: The sodium correction is a two-person event: the team’s urge to “fix the number fast” and the patient’s fragile pontine myelin meet and make osmotic demyelination together. Slow the shared tempo—you are not just replacing Na+; you are negotiating how much change the relationship between brain and serum can survive.

2016-206.sentence: Fear of abandonment in borderline personality disorder is often a vertical split: one self stays in the chair while another self already lives in the empty room after you leave. The frantic clinging is not only neediness; it is an attempt to keep both selves in the same body when the bond feels about to vanish.

2016-207.sentence: A year of outbursts despite real outpatient work means this patient’s ego cannot yet hold affect, impulses, and daily change in an unstructured week. Partial hospitalization adds scaffolding—hours of structure without a locked unit—so affect tolerance can grow before you ask the self to manage it alone again.

2016-208.sentence: Looking at the face on the screen while the camera sits elsewhere is a quiet denial: you feel present; they experience averted gaze. Put the webcam next to their image so your eyes actually meet the lens—then the relationship is not defending against contact, it is making it.

2016-209.sentence: Journal club and the ward are already in an enactment: the RCT proves efficacy under tight rules, and the clinic keeps living the leftover story of effectiveness. Name the split instead of repeating it—praise the internal validity, then ask what the trial excluded that your real patients still have.

2016-210.sentence: A trial comment on day four—“this timing fits alcohol withdrawal more than a new psychosis”—tests whether the team can see its part in missing the drinking history. Psychological mindedness here is the capacity to use that comment: delirium tremens at 72–96 hours, not schizophrenia arriving after an uncomplicated anesthetic.

2016-211.sentence: The midbrain is a hard stop: CN III and the corticospinal fibers share a few millimeters, so you cannot stretch this into a cortical or pontine story. Extra time and extra tests will not uncross a right third-nerve palsy plus left hemiparesis with a clear mind.

2016-212.sentence: Pramipexole is a feed: it tops up D2/D3 tone so the evening crawl does not have to be soothed by walking the floor. Watch the relationship to the pill—augmentation and new impulses can turn that same dopamine gift into a demand.

2016-213.sentence: A prior withdrawal seizure is the limit you hold, not a preference the patient negotiates for home. Sending that person out for detox would collapse the frame: you would leave a known seizure risk unsupervised because outpatient feels kinder.

2016-214.sentence: Psychomotor disturbance is already an enactment: the two of you are living the illness in tempo—frozen or restless—before anyone names severity. Fatigue and insomnia stay inside the report; retardation or agitation takes over the interview itself.

2016-215.sentence: A perceived sense of community works against isolation, the defense of sitting in the room without belonging. When members feel a we, they stop treating leadership as someone else's job and identify with the group instead of waiting to be empowered from above.

2016-216.sentence: The orbital frontal cortex is where ego strength lives as a brake: it holds a wish long enough to feel the cost. After that lesion, IQ and memory can look intact while risk-taking rises because the person can no longer wait out an impulse.

2016-217.sentence: Fluoxetine is a strong CYP2D6 inhibitor, so it quietly stacks risperidone and prolactin while the chart still looks like “just the antipsychotic.” Galactorrhea is the split-off channel: the body leaks milk because the drug-drug story was filed in another drawer.

2016-218.sentence: An MMSE of 21/30 is mild cognitive impairment, not “normal aging,” and that number only arrives because a daughter who lives with her father could not keep carrying the forgetting alone. The score is a two-person event: her protest makes the deficit visible before you recode it as ordinary old age.

2016-219.sentence: Linkage mapping hunts alleles that stay next to the illness as they travel through a pedigree, the way a child stays near a caregiver when the room gets scary. The method is about co-travel: disease and marker refuse to separate across generations, so you infer they sit close on the chromosome.

2016-220.sentence: After haloperidol this woman goes rigid and mute, then chorea, seizure, and respiratory failure because CSF anti-NMDA receptor antibodies are attacking the receptor, not because she is purely “paranoid-schizoid.” Find the ovarian teratoma and remove it: that is the Kleinian repair—you locate the actual bad object instead of escalating the neuroleptic.

2016-221.sentence: Low serotonin is the named chemical for this triad: depressed mood, broken sleep, and poor impulse control. The symptom cluster is one language: the 5-HT system is failing to hold mood, night, and the brake at the same time.

2016-222.sentence: DHEA rises as an anti-glucocorticoid and tracks with milder PTSD, so the body is not only flooding cortisol after trauma. Erikson’s task after horror is to keep a self that can still trust and mean something; DHEA is the hormone that buffers the cortisol so that task is not chemically washed out.

2016-223.sentence: Unresponsive caregiving is doing the real work here: the infant learns that protest will not bring a mind, so insecure attachment becomes the cheapest way to stay near a caregiver who does not answer. Poor-quality daycare only bites when that home pattern is already in place; the extra hours are not the meaning of the insecurity.

2016-224.sentence: Déjà vu is a paramnesia: the mind slaps a false “I have been here” stamp on a new scene so the stranger-room does not feel like a full separation. The familiarity is not memory; it is a homemade secure base when the actual one is missing.

2016-225.sentence: Clozapine is not only quieting voices; it is changing the two-person field so the patient needs cannabis and alcohol less as a third party that manages terror and emptiness. Typicals like haloperidol left the addiction relationship intact; clozapine is the one that has shown less psychosis, less use, and more abstinence together.

2016-226.sentence: Kant’s gift is not a therapy technique but the ethics that decide how much uncovering you are allowed to do: treat the person as an end, not a means to your formulation. Autonomy and duty set the ceiling on interpretation; you do not strip defenses just because the history of psychiatry is interesting.

2016-227.sentence: A verbal score far above the nonverbal one is a split, not a high IQ: words hold one picture of the child while doing-in-the-world holds another, and the composite papers over that gap. Further assessment is how you stop treating the “good verbal object” as the whole mind.

2016-228.sentence: The wish to order another scan collides with the prohibition against delaying while the eye is dying: temporal-artery biopsy is the act that serves the body, not the wish to look longer. ESR 96, scalp tenderness, vision loss, and proximal stiffness already name giant-cell arteritis; more imaging would be the compromise symptom.

2016-229.sentence: Bazett’s formula is a bad mirror at high rates: it inflates QTc and hands the tachycardic patient a false verdict that their heart is more broken than it is. Before you treat the number as a blow to the self, remember tachycardia overcorrects the interval; the monitor is flattering danger, not competence.

2016-230.sentence: Epigenetics is mitotically or meiotically heritable change in gene function without a DNA-sequence rewrite—methylation and histones, not a new genome. That is the dose of uncovering this story can use: trauma can mark expression across cell divisions, but you do not have to tell the patient their identity was edited at the base pair.

2016-231.sentence: ALS and frontotemporal dementia often travel as a pair; TDP-43 pathology can sit in both motor neurons and the circuits that hold social tact. The family and the patient then write depression together when the real two-person fact is FTD-type apathy and disinhibition arriving inside the ALS relationship.

2016-232.sentence: In school-age kids, self-regulation—managing affect, attention, and impulse—tracks competent social life better than athletics, looks, or SES. That is attachment work on the playground: the child who can use an inner brake (and later a grown-up as a secure base) can stay near peers without exploding or vanishing.

2016-233.sentence: Since the late 1980s, CDC and Medicare data show more elderly patients dying at home, not fewer hospice users or more hospital deaths as the headline trend. Ego strength here is affect tolerance: can this family bear the dying in the living room, or do they need the ICU’s walls to hold what home cannot.

2016-234.sentence: A week of two-hour sleep, quitting to travel the world, and an erotomanic claim on the President usually walks in wearing the mania: bright clothes and an expansive mood, not retardation or poverty of thought. The costume is the drive on display—libido and grandiosity spilled onto fabric—so you read the outfit as mood, not as a dissociative costume change.

2016-235.sentence: Those early depressive symptoms are already recruiting you into an enactment: family and clinic start treating him as a case to manage rather than a man who just lost his wife. Name the two-person pattern in the room—rescue versus collapse—or you will treat normal longing and her “presence” as pathology while the real risk (major depression right after the death) gets missed.

2016-236.sentence: The ipsilateral intention tremor, dysdiadochokinesia, and dysmetric tapping point to cerebellum, not putamen or medulla; denial here is the wish that a “clumsy hand plus headache” is functional so nobody has to look at the scan. Suppression is the adult move: hold that wish, order the MRI, and let the cerebellar finding land.

2016-237.sentence: Pain relievers—not benzodiazepines, sedatives, or stimulants—are the prescription class most often abused, so the pill is often offered as feed: take this and the ache (and you) will be managed. In clinic that same opioid can flip into poison or proof of need the moment you hesitate to refill, which is why your relationship to the script matters as much as the molecule.

2016-238.sentence: Erikson’s integrity-versus-despair task at 75 is finding meaning in what he has done, not inventing new hobbies or saving the world. He is recruiting you as the last witness who will either confirm the life added up or sit in the despair with him—watch the countertransference urge to cheerlead or close the chart.

2016-239.sentence: Neglect is the most prevalent maltreatment, and the team’s hunger for bruises or a sexual-abuse story is a sanctioned gap: conscience lights up for commission and goes quiet for omission. Your job is to keep the superego honest—failure to feed and supervise this 6-year-old is already the crime, even when the exam is “only” malnutrition and no one is holding a stick.

2016-240.sentence: Synaptic pruning, not synaptogenesis or extra dendritic branching, is why adult abstract thinking outruns the 15-year-old’s. The frame is the limit you hold with the parent: you do not promise adult reasoning on a still-pruning cortex, and you do not pathologize impulsivity that development has not yet edited.

2016-241.sentence: Velocardiofacial (22q11) already wrote a story before you offered a pill: cardiac disease, cleft repair, and a nasal voice that staff hear as “odd,” then psychosis at baseline. An antipsychotic can land as feed (someone finally treats the need), as poison (another assault on a damaged body), or as proof that the face and the heart were always a demand for psychiatry—ask which of those the family is handing you.

2016-242.sentence: The ventromedial hypothalamus is the satiety brake; a craniopharyngioma can cut it, and bingeing plus sixty pounds in four months is the body without an ending. You cannot interpret that hunger into stopping, and you cannot rush a limit that tissue no longer supplies.

2016-243.sentence: Decreased REM latency means dream sleep arrives too soon, before the night has done its slow work—like affect showing up before the person can look at it. A trial comment is not “your EEG is depressed”; it is whether they can notice the same rush in waking life: feeling arrives first, reflection late.

2016-244.sentence: Selection bias here is a vertical split in the sample: the specialty-clinic cohort stays in the study chair while the ordinary anxious person is left outside. You have not measured “anxiety disorders”; you have measured the sicker, more comorbid slice that already found tertiary care.

2016-245.sentence: Szasz called mental illness a myth and renamed it a problem in living—conflict with rules, roles, and other people, not a lesion. Ego strength is still the test at the bedside: if reality testing, affect tolerance, and impulse control have collapsed, you are not merely judging nonconformity.

2016-246.sentence: Denial would say left-handers are “the other hemisphere,” so you skip the Wada or fMRI; the number is that about 75% of them are still left-dominant for language. You name the defense and then keep the 25% in view—the ones for whom a left-sided cut is not the safe default.

2016-247.sentence: When he asks for his 'schizophrenia gene,' the two of you are already repeating a hunt for one hidden culprit instead of sitting with messy, noncoding risk. Name that enactment—the old pattern of certainty-seeking playing out in the consult—and then teach that GWAS hits sit in intronic or intergenic regions, not a single candidate gene.

2016-248.sentence: Acute mania is not the hour for an underpowered experiment; this mind needs containment first, uncovering later. Skip oxcarbazepine—the weakest evidence among these—and reach for quetiapine, risperidone, divalproex, or carbamazepine while the ego is still flooded.

2016-249.sentence: Aggression here may be the only way a fragmented self can say that something inside the body is bad and unbearable. Do a pain assessment before imaging, a restraint vest, memantine, or PRN benzos, so the 'bad object' can be located in a treatable ache rather than dumped into staff.

2016-250.sentence: Wariness at first contact is often a boundary, not a delusion, and you cannot rush trust across a cultural gap. Say that doctors and patients of different backgrounds sometimes misunderstand each other and ask if he has been concerned about that, rather than labeling him paranoid or hunting for strange beliefs.

2016-251.sentence: After a left anterior temporal contusion, raw affect pours forward because the cable that usually helps hold it is torn. The uncinate fasciculus links anterior temporal and ventral prefrontal cortex—the anatomical container—so impulsivity here is unmetabolized feeling, not 'personality.

2016-252.sentence: The frame includes how you treat a broken pledge: shame from the chair collapses the work. Praise the half-cut in smoking rather than starting bupropion, voicing disappointment, threatening to stop, or reciting residual cancer risk.

2016-253.sentence: A trial comment that lands in a 15-year-old is one they can own as their own face in the mirror this week, not a lecture about a future heart they do not yet feel is theirs. Name bad breath and yellowing teeth and you are asking for insight they can actually use: they can see their part in how they look, so the warning is about the self they already care about.

2016-254.sentence: Impairment often lives as an unrepresented state: what the physician cannot remember or say is repeated in late notes, missed pages, and a ward that starts covering. The administrative psychiatrist is not bound by the usual parameters of confidentiality because the institution has to put words to what the body and the schedule have already been acting out.

2016-255.sentence: Students will recruit you as the all-knowing parent who can make late-adolescent collapse feel tidy; notice the pull to over-explain or to go cold when the story stays messy. Hold the actual finding: excess synaptic pruning links Fragile X and schizophrenia, so the work is to stay with that one process instead of becoming either the savior or the empty lecturer.

2016-256.sentence: One cooked meal a week is a small competence experience: she gets to feel effective in her own kitchen instead of waiting for a mirrored “you’re ready” that never quite arrives. Behavioral activation here is self-psychological, not just a schedule—it rebuilds esteem through a doable act after symptoms are gone and the self still feels too thin for the “real world.”

2016-257.sentence: An illusion is a wish and a fear colliding on a real stimulus: the IV pole is actually there, and the mind conscripts it into a person at the bedside. Name the finding—misinterpretation of genuine sensory input—so you do not confuse this drive-laden rewrite of the room with a hallucination born of no object at all.

2016-258.sentence: School-based care works because it puts a clinician where the adolescent already is, so help does not require a separate trip that feels like abandonment of the only secure base they have—school itself. The advantage is improved access for youth who otherwise never arrive: proximity is the treatment, not a nicer office across town.

2016-259.sentence: Cortisol's dawn peak is a daily load test of affect tolerance: the ego has to absorb a surge of arousal without falling apart. When that HPA clock is off, early waking is the body dumping a chemical tide the mind cannot yet contain.

2016-260.sentence: Dressing apraxia is a competence injury: strength is intact, but the self can no longer run a once-automatic sequence that held the feeling of being able. Mirroring the effort will not restore the motor plan; what failed is praxis, not the wish to look put together.

2016-261.sentence: Saying "Because girls don't have wee wees" is containment: you take the boy's raw astonishment and hand it back as a thinkable fact. Delay or scolding evacuates the question and leaves him with nameless dread about bodies instead of a name.

2016-262.sentence: Countertransference here is a limit on a new hour: your old sister-feelings arrive before the alliance has time to exist. You cannot rush them out; you name them privately so you do not live the old relationship instead of ending that impulse in the chair.

2016-263.sentence: Sleep-onset REM on the polysomnogram is the lab's trial comment: dream intrudes before thought can form. Cataplexy is the same collapse while awake—emotion arrives faster than insight, and the knees buckle instead of a sentence.

2016-264.sentence: Prednisone is the limit you hold: giant cell arteritis does not wait for a prettier workup while the optic nerve is at risk. Delay for gabapentin or a longer interview abandons who is supposed to keep the frame—the physician who starts steroids now.

2016-265.sentence: Clozapine’s low D2 affinity means the pill does not clamp the striatum like a typical neuroleptic, so it is less easily felt as a poison that steals movement. The same molecule can still feel like a feed or a proof of need—you are asking the patient to swallow something that works precisely because it does not occupy D2 the way a high-potency blocker does.

2016-266.sentence: Denial is the defense that says “he is already on an antipsychotic, so the suicide problem is covered,” while the overdoses keep happening. Clozapine is the one agent with the strongest evidence that it actually lowers suicide rates in schizophrenia, so the work is to drop the denial and name the risk instead of recycling risperidone and aripiprazole.

2016-267.sentence: Keeping lithium through ECT is already an enactment: the pair of you are living a fight between “do not drop mood coverage” and “do not lose control of the seizure,” instead of deciding it in words first. Lithium is the agent most likely to stretch the post-stimulus seizure past three minutes, so the system then has to abort what it helped create.

2016-268.sentence: The live third in the room is not diagnosis or the drug pamphlet; it is the court and the hospital’s power to hold or release him. Bargain-discharge for swallowing the antipsychotic strips voluntariness, the consent element that was missing, and turns “informed choice” into a class-and-custody deal.

2016-269.sentence: This sits on identity versus role confusion: the field wants schizophrenia to have a single-gene name, and GWAS refuses that tidy identity. Those studies assay common genetic variants across the genome, not one candidate gene that would let you stop looking.

2016-270.sentence: At sixty-eight the psychosocial task is integrity versus despair: a continuous life story versus a hole you cannot narrate. Transient global amnesia typically lasts only a few hours, then the self comes back, which is why the evening exam and normal MRI fit the diagnosis instead of a stroke story.

2016-271.sentence: Deployment is a third party in the family: the military’s schedule, not the child’s wishes, decides who is home. That institutional absence is why anxiety symptoms rise in the kids during the tour and stay up after reunion, not only on the day dad leaves.

2016-272.sentence: The offense is often a dump of unwanted sexual and aggressive bits into another person—projective identification, meaning he makes the victim carry what he cannot own. Cognitive behavior therapy is the usual program because it forces him to keep those thoughts in his own head and track them, rather than evacuate them again.

2016-273.sentence: He wants you as an exclusive good object who hides him; the officers want you as their informant. HIPAA lets you tell them he is ready for discharge without his consent, so you have to hold both the patient’s trust and the legal demand in one relationship instead of splitting them.

2016-274.sentence: He is recruiting you as the one adult who already understands the campus world, so the farm family can stay the ones who will not. Name it acculturation difficulty: two cultures are arguing inside him, and your warmth can become a stand-in for leaving home rather than a place to think about telling them.

2016-275.sentence: Ventral tegmental neurons dump dopamine into the nucleus accumbens, and that spike does not wait for a guilty verdict. Conscience can lecture later; the circuit has already stamped the drug as worth repeating.

2016-276.sentence: The forehead learned a backup plan: both hemispheres drive the upper face, so a cortical stroke usually leaves wrinkling intact. When upper and lower face go out together, that bilateral cortical capacity never gets to help—the lesion is peripheral, so tPA is the wrong rescue.

2016-277.sentence: The so-called panic is doing a job: it yanks her home before delay can mean her dying mother is gone. Separation anxiety here is not random fear of crowds; it is a last-ditch way to stay glued to the only person she has ever leaned on.

2016-278.sentence: MOC’s required medical knowledge is the part of you that must stay current so you do not split off from what you once knew. Board recertification is a vertical split in the other direction: you cannot leave the chair of practice while the facts walk out of the room.

2016-279.sentence: Ordering the multiple sleep latency test after an overnight PSG is already a two-person play: the clinic and the 19-year-old are staging how fast sleep hijacks the day. Cataplexy at a laugh is the same enactment in the body—wakeful muscle tone collapsing the moment affect arrives.

2016-280.sentence: Dendritic spines are the little handshake between two neurons: they change number and shape when two sides of a synapse keep meeting. Therapy and antidepressants work there because the relationship, not a lone cell body, is what remolds the contact.

2016-281.sentence: The BOLD signal tracks changes in deoxyhemoglobin, an indirect whisper, not a neuron shouting. That is your technique cue: fMRI supports a guess about perfusion chemistry; it does not uncover the mind’s contents, so do not interpret the activation map as if it were free association.

2016-282.sentence: ICU “psychosis” is usually delirium: the ego’s reality testing and sleep–wake scaffolding have collapsed under medical insult. Agitation and ceiling-tile spies are not new schizophrenia; they are what a mind does when it can no longer hold a coherent day.

2016-283.sentence: When NMS follows a neuroleptic like haloperidol, the body has lost its autonomic secure base and needs another person plus a procedure to do the regulating. ECT is proximity in medical form: you stay, stop the drug, and let the current hold while fever, rigidity, and that CK over 5000 come down.

2016-284.sentence: The fire-setting is already an enactment in the room: he is inviting you to chase, contain, or get scorched instead of naming the rising tension. Pyromania is the diagnosis because the excitement-then-relief cycle around fire is the point, not the stolen hardware or the broken curfew.

2016-285.sentence: Your report can split the defendant into mad versus bad and feel as if you have left the witness chair for the verdict. Insanity stays a finding by the jury: you describe mind, they decide whether he lacked the required state of mind.

2016-286.sentence: Before you push a depressed new mother back toward friends, map who actually functions as her secure base. The initial phase of IPT is collecting information about significant relationships so you know whom she uses to regulate, not yet reconnecting or rewriting expectations.

2016-287.sentence: A T-test or ANOVA is denial of complexity: it pretends one predictor at a time can explain adult major depression. Regression analysis lets childhood trauma, family history, low income, and chronic illness sit in the same model so you do not repress three of the four risk factors.

2016-288.sentence: Parents often treat visible puberty as a moral alarm, as if breast buds already mean sexual responsibility. Reproduction starts at menarche and first nocturnal emission; the rest is Tanner theater that a rigid conscience can mistake for permission or crime.

2016-289.sentence: The referral for “seizures” recruits you to become the epilepsy doctor, and the few bilateral jerks after collapse can hook that countertransference—your urge to treat a spell as a complex partial seizure. Stay with the collar, pallor, and faintness: carotid sinus syncope is mechanical hypersensitivity, not a performance you have to interpret as conversion.

2016-290.sentence: Retirement stirs a wish to stay mentally potent and a prohibition against becoming the sedentary man who “doesn’t bother”—so the news story arrives as both hope and self-reproach. Name that collision and still give the evidence: late-life physical activity, even newly adopted, is more likely than not to aid cognition.

2016-291.sentence: Imprinting is a silenced parent-of-origin mark: methylation of the paternal or maternal allele leaves the other allele speaking unopposed, which is why the same 15q region can become Prader-Willi or Angelman. What cannot be expressed on one chromosome is not forgotten; it is lived as the phenotype, the way an unremembered state gets repeated in the body.

2016-292.sentence: The friend’s omega-3 tip is an evacuation: raw dread of becoming the sibling with Alzheimer disease is handed to you as a pill request so no one has to think it. Contain that—hold the feeling until it is thinkable—and say the studies do not show omega-3s prevent cognitive decline, even if they may have other benefits.

2016-293.sentence: Kohut’s self psychology is the school that says a child’s sense of worth is built from parental empathy—mirroring that says “I see you,” plus room to idealize and feel competent. Without that, the self stays hungry for admiration and shatters at a slight; that is a selfobject need, not merely a defense.

2016-294.sentence: A trial comment can restore psychological mindedness: “Not remitting on the first SSRI is the STAR*D story—fewer than one-third got well at step one—not proof you are a hopeless case.” If she can see her discouragement as one failed trial rather than a verdict on her character, she can stay in the sequence instead of quitting the whole project.

2016-295.sentence: The five-day authorization is a real ending; you cannot invent leftover suicidality to stretch time the depression has not yet used. Charting SI that is gone turns the record into a fake clock, so the next clinician cannot tell when danger actually stopped.

2016-296.sentence: Hand-feeding has become the feed that proves he still needs to be a patient, not a tool that helps a burn body heal. A reward for self-feeding puts the spoon back in his hand so care is earned function, not family as the only nourishment.

2016-297.sentence: The parent who names the wish to stay out and still takes privileges is the one holding the frame: curfew is the fee for belonging, not a mood. Grounding for a month with no talk, or sliding the hour later, either drops the limit or drops the relationship.

2016-298.sentence: Amnestic MCI cannot keep yesterday’s conversation as a living other; that hole is the one that most often becomes Alzheimer disease, not FTD, DLB, or Parkinson. Repair in the depressive position needs a remembered person to mourn; when recent memory is the first piece gone, that work has no object left.

2016-299.sentence: Working memory in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex is how you hold two bits—a number and the next digit—without one wiping the other out. After a frontal injury he looks whole, but he cannot keep good and next instruction in the same mind long enough to dial.

2016-300.sentence: A Medicaid health home after the 2010 ACA is supposed to hold the whole person: primary care, mental illness, community, social, and family in one relationship, not a menu or two equal silos. Split services leave diabetes and psychosis as rival objects; the home is the place that refuses that split and still has to be cost-aware.

2017-1.sentence: Quality of social support is the real holding environment after a spouse dies: other people carry the grief so the treatment hour does not have to become a substitute marriage. Your ethical job is to find who still shows up and to refuse the quiet invitation to fill the empty chair yourself.

2017-2.sentence: When panic enters the conference, both of you can start living the alarm instead of thinking about it—that is an enactment, a two-person rerun of the fear circuit. The central nucleus of the amygdala is the output station that turns a remembered threat into freeze, flee, or a rush to intervene before anyone names the structure.

2017-3.sentence: Calling one-to-two-minute chewing spells with amnesia a 'dissociative state' is denial: it keeps a seizure in the safer category of mind so nobody has to say brain. Complex partial seizures will not yield to interpretation; they are uninterruptible automatisms, and a normal MRI does not talk them out of existence.

2017-4.sentence: The opening jab tests whether your ego can hold heat without counterattacking, taking a history detour, or proving you are the good doctor. Saying you are sorry they felt unheard and asking them to describe it is affect tolerance in action: you stay with the rupture long enough for an alliance to form.

2017-5.sentence: The pup does not store licking as a memory it can tell; DNA methylation of the glucocorticoid receptor keeps early care in the body while the genetic code stays untouched—a split between experience and sequence. High licking and grooming lowers that methylation so the offspring can feel stress and recover; low care leaves the receptor quieter and the HPA axis louder.

2017-6.sentence: Her breezy 'sure, no problem' already recruits you: she offers a perfect patient and you are invited to believe her so neither of you feels how hard a year without self-harm actually is. DBT answers by naming that the commitment would be extremely difficult, so the two of you hold the limit together instead of colluding with a wish.

2017-7.sentence: Carbamazepine had been this patient's quiet secure base: CYP3A4 kept a steady level and the seizures stayed put. Erythromycin then parks in that same enzyme and crowds the attachment figure, so carbamazepine piles up as nausea, ataxia, and diplopia—the nervous system's separation protest when the regulating other is no longer reliably there.

2017-8.sentence: She is holding two versions of herself that will not sit in one room: the administrative-assistant life as all-bad 'settling,' and the unlived graduate degree as the only good object. Ego integrity, Erikson's last crisis, asks her to keep both the missed path and the real decades in one mind instead of letting despair split the whole story.

2017-9.sentence: Cognitive dissonance is already doing the work: two attitudes, or an attitude and a behavior, grinding against each other. Do not interpret it away; stay supportive enough that they can feel the contradiction, because that tension is the leverage, not a deficit you need to uncover.

2017-10.sentence: The medial prefrontal cortex is the regulating other; the amygdala is the alarmed child. In major depression and OCD that link is off, so a pill that restores top-down mPFC–amygdala connectivity is less a chemical trick than handing the frightened part a mind that can hold it.

2017-11.sentence: The old clinic used professional omnipotence—the defense of acting as if only we can know—to keep families out of the plan. System of care names that defense and undoes it: families sit at the table as decision-makers, not as visitors to the expert's room.

2017-12.sentence: A left superior homonymous quadrantanopia—'pie in the sky'—means Meyer's loop in the right temporal lobe, or the right optic radiation, is gone, so that slice of the world never arrives. Insight works the same way: a trial comment only lands if they can still see that quadrant of their own mind; if the loop is out, you describe the field, you do not interpret the missing piece.

2017-13.sentence: The frame here is who holds the limit when the body freezes: you do not open with a neuroleptic just because the chart says bipolar. Lorazepam is first-line for catatonia (immobility, posturing, echopraxia) because it treats the syndrome and keeps you from enacting a rush to dopamine blockade that can tip into NMS.

2017-14.sentence: Fluctuating cognition in dementia with Lewy bodies is an ego-strength problem in the neurologic sense: some hours the person can reality-test and stay upright, then alertness and visuospatial mapping drop out. Early unilateral resting tremor plus increased arm tone tell you the same apparatus that holds a self together is already leaking, so you treat the fluctuation as illness, not as will.

2017-15.sentence: Attachment here is staying with the body instead of abandoning the patient to “functional” when they develop foot drop. Weakness of ankle inversion (tibialis posterior, L5) is the finding that keeps you as a secure base: it localizes a radiculopathy and stops you from using psychology to regulate your own uncertainty.

2017-16.sentence: Journal club often enacts the old wish for one culprit gene, as if schizophrenia were a single object you could catch. A GWAS’s real advantage is the opposite: it can detect common variants that each nudge risk only a little, so you stop repeating the hunt for a master gene and sit with many small effects.

2017-17.sentence: Walking into a first AA meeting with social anxiety is a near-dissociation: the person can leave the room without leaving the chair, splitting off into analysis or mindfulness to avoid the group. Twelve-step facilitation names the one thing that keeps them present—“you went to the meeting; it will get easier”—so the vertical split does not become the treatment.

2017-18.sentence: In major depression the night cannot hold the line between waking self and inner objects, so REM arrives too soon. Short REM latency is that failure in numbers: the dream world, with its unmetabolized good and bad, breaks in before slow-wave sleep has done any containing.

2017-19.sentence: Doubling lithium because she “wasn’t getting better fast enough” is paranoid-schizoid thinking: get rid of the bad, now, and ignore what the dose does to a real body. Depressive concern would have meant holding the lithium, checking a level, and repairing rather than evacuating the illness into diarrhea, tremor, and confusion.

2017-20.sentence: Relief at the abortion does not cancel the older collision: a wish to survive an abusive partner and a prohibition against ending a pregnancy. Pre-pregnancy depression is the track record of that same fight, so it outpredicts the procedure as the source of later collapse.

2017-21.sentence: Chronic glutamate at the NMDA receptor is trauma that never becomes a memory: calcium keeps pouring in and the neuron dies instead of representing anything. Memantine’s job is to blunt that unrepresented flood so the cell is not asked to live the injury on a loop.

2017-22.sentence: Childhood sexual abuse is an established risk for bulimia because the binge-purge can recruit you as the one who either looks away or takes over the body again. Watch the countertransference urge to police food or to go numb; that is the old pair trying to staff the room.

2017-23.sentence: A clomipramine overdose is often a superego attack: conscience trying to punish the self with a lethal dose. The same drug then enacts the sentence in the body, so you watch for seizures and cardiac toxicity, not just “sedation.”

2017-24.sentence: A PTSD scale that never asks whether a traumatic event occurred fails content validity: it left the defining piece of the domain off the page. That is the same failure as a patient who can list arousal and avoidance but cannot look at what actually happened.

2017-25.sentence: A disorganized patient asking “are you a real psychiatrist?” is testing whether you can hold the limit of who you actually are. Naming that you are a resident—a physician in specialty training—ends the scramble to be more, less, or someone else, and that honesty is what makes the interview thinkable.

2017-26.sentence: Fear is one of the first raw affects an infant can have before envy, shame, pride, or guilt exist as ideas. Containment is the caregiver taking that nameless dread—terror without a word—and giving it shape so the baby can think “something is dangerous” instead of only evacuating panic.

2017-27.sentence: Bilateral temporal-lobe loss in Kluver-Bucy strips away the inner object that once said “this is too much,” so the patient becomes placid, hyperoral, and sexually indiscriminate. Self-esteem here is not vanity; without temporal modulation there is no mirroring of appetite as “mine to regulate,” only drive without a self that can refuse.

2017-28.sentence: The 13-year-old who dropped from the 75th to the 20th percentile and still wants five to ten more pounds is not “healthier”; restriction is a Kleinian attack on a body treated as a bad object. Anorexia nervosa holds the paranoid-schizoid split—control is all-good, hunger and parents’ worry are all-bad—so there is no depressive concern, no wish to repair what starvation is doing.

2017-29.sentence: Major depressive disorder ranks in the WHO top ten for years lost to disability and death because the good internal object goes silent and the world feels emptied of usable others. Burden-of-disease numbers are the public face of that private collapse: when relatedness cannot hold good and bad together, whole lives go unused.

2017-30.sentence: The fourth question about a presentation font is not curiosity; it is evacuation of a belief that “I cannot be trusted to make a good decision.” Roomates (and you) get recruited as containers for that nameless incompetence until someone names the dread instead of answering the font again.

2017-31.sentence: Heroin withdrawal peaks around 36 hours, not at the first 8-hour yawn or the day-5 malaise. That peak is a hard limit: you cannot rush a nervous system off a mu-agonist, and the demand to leave “tomorrow morning” is often the wish that time would skip the worst stretch.

2017-32.sentence: Orbitofrontal injury can leave a person who still talks fluently but cannot use a trial comment—cannot see their own crude joke, the spend, the odd euphoria as theirs. Psychological mindedness is not IQ; it is frontal enough restraint to notice, “I just did that,” and this lesion takes that noticing offline.

2017-33.sentence: In girls the first usual marker is acceleration of linear growth, not menarche and not “secondary characteristics” as the opener. The ethical frame here is the clock you hold with the parent: you name the real sequence so a 9-year-old’s height does not become a premature diagnosis or a premature reassurance.

2017-34.sentence: She walks around the garbage can, so the visual system is working; conversion is the mind borrowing blindness as a solution when a conflict cannot be spoken. The “pill” she is asking for is not an ophthalmology drug—it is someone to take the symptom as communication rather than as a lesion to cut out.

2017-35.sentence: Daily sumatriptan is the habit to stop first; that is medication-overuse headache, not a new migraine genotype. Denial is working here: she still calls them “chronic migraines” and keeps dosing the abortive, so the drug can stay the problem she does not have to name.

2017-36.sentence: The move that actually cuts completed inpatient suicide is taking down hanging anchors, not a no-suicide contract or more 1:1s. The unit is already in an enactment: after a near-miss, staff want a ritual of watching or locking that soothes anxiety while the ligature points stay in the ceiling.

2017-37.sentence: Microglia do not just mop up debris; they dump TNF-α and IL-1 into the synapse, so the mind is chemically unplugged while the body still sits in the chair. That is a vertical split: the person is gone from the thought without having left the room, and the cytokine storm is how the brain evacuates itself.

2017-38.sentence: Urine is the easiest matrix to swap, dilute, or warm, so the screen becomes a test of whether the resident can still be seen as trustworthy. Erikson’s task here is identity versus role confusion: the sample is not just chemistry, it is a bid to keep two selves—the clean patient and the using one—from having to meet.

2017-39.sentence: Cobalamin loss steals the dorsal columns first, so vibration and position vanish and the person cannot locate the body in space. The fluctuating irritability and somnolence are the mind’s protest that the map of the self has gone blank; the deficiency is doing the work of making the world untrustworthy underfoot.

2017-40.sentence: A registry tracks the whole panel, not only the patients who show up hurting, so the clinic faces the wish to rescue and the prohibition against endless individual heroics. The conflict lives in the list itself: you want to hold every case, and the population method says you must count them instead of devouring them one by one.

2017-41.sentence: Leptin leaves fat, crosses into hypothalamus, and says stop eating—a signal the body writes when the mind cannot keep the hunger story. What cannot be remembered as satiety is repeated as drive: adipose tissue speaks the unrepresented ‘enough’ that words never held.

2017-42.sentence: Jumping and hopping should already be automatic in a school-age child; if they are not, the body is still dumping raw motor panic instead of a usable skill. That is failed containment: nameless dread stays in the legs instead of becoming a thinkable ‘I can leave the ground and come back.’

2017-43.sentence: MDMA’s warmth is a rented mirror: the drug plus a night of water-loading tries to swell a depleted self until it feels loved and competent. Hyponatremia is that swell gone literal—ADH plus free water dilutes the self the way an idealizing binge dilutes judgment.

2017-44.sentence: Low SES and rural life do not just raise lifetime MDD risk; they also starve psychological mindedness, the capacity to see one’s own part instead of calling the mood “just how it is here.” A trial comment that names both the zip code and the self-attack often lands better than either fact alone.

2017-45.sentence: Rising pre-movement potentials (the Bereitschaftspotential) mean the cortex prepared the jerk; conversion has a time course you cannot rush into “just stop it.” The EMG is a limit: some agency is already there, and naming that without forcing ownership is the termination work of the consult.

2017-46.sentence: The ACA’s ban on preexisting-condition denials for a mental-disorder history treats coverage like a needed feed, not a poison you earn by being well. When a bipolar patient shops the marketplace, the policy is the relationship: it says need is allowed to show itself.

2017-47.sentence: Cognitive theory puts negative evaluations of self at the center of depression; that schema is the patient’s private fee schedule—“worthless” is what they charge themselves every hour. Your job is to hold time and the frame while those verdicts get tested, not to argue the patient into a refund.

2017-48.sentence: Cutting clozapine to stop pillow-soaking sialorrhea is an enactment: the ward repeats the patient’s shame by discarding the thing that works. Glycopyrrolate treats the drool so the two of you can stay with the needed antipsychotic instead of living the rejection.

2017-49.sentence: Calling the elopement-plus-hip-fracture a Joint Commission sentinel event is also a way to keep denial from swallowing the night: the system names the harm so nobody can treat a walk-off as “just a wander.” Report it, then sit with the staff guilt rather than undoing the event with extra paperwork that never faces the unlocked moment.

2017-50.sentence: Dopamine-β-hydroxylase turning dopamine into norepinephrine is the chemistry of a secure base in a crisis: the synapse finally has the signal that says stay close and brace. When that step fails, the student sees why a MAOI–tyramine surge feels like panic without a person to hold onto.

2017-51.sentence: The dip in sharing from two to three is not the child becoming mean; it is two people renegotiating who owns the toy now that the toddler has a felt autonomous self. Parents who keep insisting on “be nice” are still playing the old we-are-one game, and the child is answering with mine.

2017-52.sentence: Cognitive impairment is the victim factor that tracks elder abuse most reliably because the mind can go missing while the body stays in the chair, and bruises then have no witness inside. The overwhelmed daughter is left with a person who is there and not there, which is why the risk sits in dementia more than in race, income, or extra diagnoses.

2017-53.sentence: A GWAS that hunts hundreds of thousands of SNPs will throw false positives unless ego strength holds: you tolerate not knowing instead of grabbing the first p-value the pharma rep waves. Reality testing here means remembering multiple testing, not rewriting antidepressant choice on one overfitted hit.

2017-54.sentence: Anxious parents treating missed shoe-tying at four as pathology is reaction formation: worry dressed as high standards, because a healthy kid who already runs, kicks, rides a tricycle, and zips a coat is allowed to wait on laces. Name the defense gently so they can stop “fixing” a milestone that has not come due.

2017-55.sentence: The team arguing for day hospital, groups, or family psychoed is already in an enactment: they keep asking a high-utilizer with schizophrenia to come to them, which is the same miss-and-readmit loop they hate. Assertive community care is the two-person correction—staff go out, hold housing and meds, and stop repeating the door.

2017-56.sentence: Your job on this TBI consult is the frame: depression is the most common psychiatric complication, so you screen for it even when the team wants psychosis, aggression, or PTSD. You hold that quieter limit; you do not let the dramatic sequelae steal the work.

2017-57.sentence: When a charming patient wrecks your thinking, the first move is supervision: borrow another mind before you act. Changing the hour, transferring her, or confessing the crush treats the attraction like a fact you must manage alone instead of a signal you cannot yet metabolize.

2017-58.sentence: Learned helplessness is a limit: after inescapable shock, the animal stops trying because agency itself feels gone, and you cannot talk or wait that capacity back. Antidepressants reverse those behavioral deficits; they restore the possibility of ending the trial, not the memory of having been trapped.

2017-59.sentence: Arm flailing and a tonic fencing posture look like theater, so the temptation is a trial comment about conflict or secondary gain. Video-EEG showing a frontal-lobe seizure is the check on that habit: hypermotor night spells can be cortex, not a story, until the tracing says otherwise.

2017-60.sentence: The identical-twin pair holds two stories at once: a shared genetic “bad object” that raises risk, and a still-open environmental story that is not the illness. The two-hit model is how you keep both in one relationship instead of splitting into “doomed because genes” or “safe because the other twin is well.”

2017-61.sentence: The Patient Health Questionnaire is a support-level instrument: it names the depression so the clinic can track it without asking the patient to uncover why they are sad. Recommend it when the mind, and the setting, can use a five-minute map more than an hour of interpretation.

2017-62.sentence: Fragile X is inherited through the mother’s FMR1 expansion, so the disability lives in a two-person genetic conversation, not only in the child’s chromosomes. The uncle’s intellect and the boy’s language delay are the same pattern passing between relatives, not a one-person accident.

2017-63.sentence: Childhood physical abuse is the most common backdrop for DID because the child cannot use the caregiver as a secure base and must split to stay near the person who hurts them. Dissociation here is proximity management: stay attached by leaving the self that was hit.

2017-64.sentence: Hydrochlorothiazide cuts lithium’s renal clearance, so the same daily dose now floods a mind that had been holding bipolar affect with lithium’s help. Ego strength drops with the tremor and ataxia: the patient can no longer metabolize either salt or feeling at the old rate.

2017-65.sentence: Cortisol production falls at sleep onset, which is the nightly vertical split: arousal leaves without the body leaving the bed. If a C-L cortisol curve ignores that dip, you will misread a physiologic leave-taking as pathology.

2017-66.sentence: Innate feelings, not chromosome complement or parental mirroring, are the stronger source of gender identity, so the family’s enactment—living the assigned gender instead of talking about the felt one—cannot write over that inner sense. The work is to stop repeating the assignment in the room and hear the identity that was already there.

2017-67.sentence: Picking Trails B over Boston naming or Rey figure is a small act of suppression: you set aside the tempting “let’s just scan everything” impulse and hold one question—can this person shift set? That restraint is the bedside analog of cognitive flexibility itself: keep the unused tests in mind without letting them run the consult.

2017-68.sentence: First panic in late adolescence often arrives as a body that screams “heart attack” because the mind has no usable story for the surge. What cannot be represented as feeling or memory gets repeated as palpitations, chest tightness, and dying-fear that peaks in minutes—unrepresented affect using the autonomic system as its only language.

2017-69.sentence: 22q11.2 microdeletion plus congenital heart repair, cleft palate, and a nasal voice can recruit you into becoming the “it’s just schizophrenia” doctor, as if the genes were an afterthought. Notice the countertransference pull to treat the psychosis and ignore the syndrome; that feeling is the cue to name 22q11.2 rather than collapse into a generic first-break story.

2017-70.sentence: Choosing against paliperidone in moderate-to-severe CKD can feel like you are the withholding parent who will not give the “easy” once-monthly option. Name that countertransference: the wish to be the rescuer who still prescribes it is how renal clearance gets denied in the room.

2017-71.sentence: Capacity for mental health court is not insight that bipolar “caused” the break-in, and it is not waving away counsel. What cannot stay in words—the fact that opting in means waiving certain constitutional rights—will get enacted as a nod in court if you never ask him to say the waiver out loud.

2017-72.sentence: Orexin A from the hypothalamus holds the wish to stay up against the drive to drop into sleep and atonia. When that peptide is lost, the collision is no longer negotiated: sleep attacks and laugh-triggered cataplexy are the wish and the shutdown arriving in the same instant.

2017-73.sentence: Walking and talking can come back and still leave the self feeling incompetent, because the fronto-subcortical loops that organize planning, sequencing, and stopping an impulse are what used to give a person a felt sense of agency. Family praise for “recovery” then lands as a failed mirror: they are admiring the body that works, not the executive self that still cannot hold a plan.

2017-74.sentence: Six to eight years from first mood symptoms to a diagnosis is enough time to miss Erikson’s identity work in late adolescence and then stall intimacy in the twenties. The delay is not just untreated illness; it is years of a self that never got a name for what was happening, so role and closeness get built around unexplained shutdowns.

2017-75.sentence: Lorazepam is the right first agent because bath-salt (synthetic cathinone) agitation is a sympathetic, hyperthermic storm, and GABA calm is what the body is screaming for—not a dopamine blockade. The symptom is doing something: it is forcing the room into a fight; benzos lower the drive so staff do not have to become the restraint the drug already invented.

2017-76.sentence: Latency (roughly 6–11) is when sexual curiosity goes quiet and the child’s energy pours into same-sex teams, skill, and school—here, basketball as the main job. Teasing girls while playing mostly with boys is the expected social map of that stage, not a failed genital arrival.

2017-77.sentence: SPECT is the test that can split Alzheimer-type from frontotemporal patterns by showing where blood flow has dropped, not just where the MRI looks thin. Think of the frontal hypoperfusion of FTD as a hole in the superego—the inner brake and social conscience—so disinhibition is not “personality” so much as a missing judge.

2017-78.sentence: Paroxetine is the SSRI with the strongest birth-defect signal, so the same pill that once proved she could be held together now reads as a possible poison to the fetus. The clinical bind is relational: stopping it can feel like being abandoned by the only feed that ever worked, while continuing it can feel like harming the baby to keep herself alive.

2017-79.sentence: HIPAA already lets you and the PCP share what you need to treat this shared patient. The hallway freeze is often isolation of affect: you turn the person into a legal object so you do not have to feel the ordinary anxiety of being a real teammate.

2017-80.sentence: Normal aging is a stooped posture and a slower walk, not rest tremor and a shuffle. The consult is an ego-strength job: help the family keep reality testing so they can metabolize ordinary decline without inventing Parkinson's to make the change feel more containable.

2017-81.sentence: Parental criminality is the risk factor that should change how you hear the fighting and lying. The child is still in a developmental window where the parent's act is the curriculum, so he practices the attachment figure's lawlessness as his working model of how people get what they want.

2017-82.sentence: Haloperidol unmasks dementia with Lewy bodies by worsening the parkinsonism, falls, and confusion. That overnight dose is often a two-person pattern: the agitated patient and a frightened ED make a demand for stillness, and the high-potency antipsychotic becomes the relationship's answer.

2017-83.sentence: Ketamine infusions commonly raise blood pressure, which is why you sit with the cuff during and just after the drip. Attachment is in the protocol: the nurse and the monitor are the secure base while a dissociative drug takes the floor out from under ordinary self-regulation.

2017-84.sentence: A one-time consult becomes treatment when you write a prescription and then keep talking symptoms and side effects on the phone. The pill is already a feed: once you have been the person who supplies and titrates it, walking away without a handoff is abandonment, not 'just a consult.

2017-85.sentence: Exposure only works inside a firm frame: same safe setting, enough time, no improvising mid-session. That frame is what lets the medial prefrontal cortex lay down new inhibitory learning over the old fear memory instead of just restimulating it.

2017-86.sentence: Persistent toe-walking at four is already a two-person scene: the child keeps going up on toes and the adults keep calling it intensity or habit. Name the finding in the room rather than living the family story that this gait is just temperament.

2017-87.sentence: Denial is the wish to treat descending paralysis, constipation, and fixed unreactive pupils as anxiety or a 'stomach bug.' Botulinum toxin has already blocked acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction; the defense is refusing that fact until the airway forces it.

2017-88.sentence: Beneficence here is containment: you hold the overdose and the wish to leave until the suicide can be thought instead of acted. You do not evacuate the raw dread back onto the street because the patient demanded autonomy in the moment.

2017-89.sentence: Those brief stare-and-blink spells are not a child checking out of the relationship; they are three-cycle-per-second spike-and-wave cutting the self offline for a few seconds. The teacher's noticing is a piece of mirroring: someone sees the interruption instead of calling the child lazy or spacey.

2017-90.sentence: Family psychoeducation is not a lecture to the identified patient; it is two (or more) people agreeing to stop the relapse dance together. The joint task is concrete: help the family encourage medication adherence rather than chase ambitious goals or ignore substances.

2017-91.sentence: A crossover design is already a statement about technique: you give one drug its full eight weeks, then a four-week washout, then the other, because this mind (and this receptor) cannot use two active interventions at once. If you skip the washout you are not “more uncovering”; you are contaminating the next trial with leftover drug, the research version of piling interpretations before the last one has cleared.

2017-92.sentence: Ego strength is uneven here: impulse control and affect tolerance hold at school, then collapse at home when a parent sets a limit and rage, threats, and all-night curfew-breaking appear. That home-only pattern is oppositional defiant disorder, not conduct disorder—the ego can still spare strangers, property, and the classroom; it just cannot metabolize parental authority without a tantrum.

2017-93.sentence: Adult neurogenesis lives mainly in the dentate gyrus of the hippocampus, the same circuit that encodes new relational memory—who is safe, who left, what happened next. Attachment is not only a feeling; it is a dentate job: a usable other becomes a secure base so the brain can actually lay down new cells and new maps instead of replaying the old ones.

2017-94.sentence: The live third in the room is the patient’s age and sex: a 58-year-old woman with retardation quietly invites estrogen, as if the story were menopause. The finding that should drive the choice is psychomotor retardation, and the augmentation with evidence for that picture is liothyronine (T3), not a gendered hormone you reached for because she is midlife and female.

2017-95.sentence: This sits on Erikson’s integrity versus despair: you already judged inpatient care necessary for suicidality, and integrity means you admit and appeal rather than shrink the plan to match the reviewer’s partial-hospital suggestion. Role confusion would be treating the insurance denial as a new clinical exam; the task is to keep the doctor’s word and fight the denial, not invent extra risk factors or send the patient home.

2017-96.sentence: A bitemporal field cut is the symptom of a lesion at the optic chiasm (usually label B), where nasal fibers from both eyes cross: the patient loses the outer half of each visual world. The meaning is anatomic, not “personality”—when both temporal fields go, think midline at the chiasm (classically pituitary), not a cortical story farther back along the tract.

2017-97.sentence: Washing for three hours is a Kleinian evacuation: he tries to push a persecutory “contaminated” bit of self into the sink so it cannot stay inside him. Exposure and response prevention asks him to keep that badness in mind without the ritual, which is how he moves from paranoid-schizoid panic toward ordinary depressive concern—and a chance to repair rather than purge.

2017-98.sentence: Rapid onset after the crash means the mind can still point to an event: “this started then,” which is the first cut of insight. A trial comment lands better here than in the smoldering, childhood-layered picture, because he can still see his symptoms as a reaction rather than as who he has always been.

2017-99.sentence: IDEA eligibility is a legal frame, not a favor you write because grades are poor or a parent is desperate. You hold the limit: special education requires a documented disability that actually blocks progress—not a failed grade, a psychiatrist’s name on the chart, or a pill.

2017-100.sentence: The SSRI is not a snack you drop into “the brain”; it first hits autoreceptors on the raphe nuclei, the clustered cell bodies that make almost all central serotonin. That is why the pill can feel like a mute button for weeks before it becomes a feed, and why serotonin syndrome is whole-body when those raphe axons fire everywhere at once.

2017-101.sentence: Occasional masochistic heterosexual fantasies at sixteen are homework, not a diagnosis: she is trying on intensity to find what belongs to her. Excitement plus anxiety is the developmental signal that she is sorting a pattern, not announcing a paraphilia, a hidden assault, or a secret orientation.

2017-102.sentence: The ward may treat the opioids and the delirium as acting out—behavior used to discharge feeling instead of naming an illness. Order urine porphobilinogen anyway: acute intermittent porphyria hides behind that “drug-seeking” story with the same belly, weakness, and confusion.

2017-103.sentence: Adding memantine onto donepezil is already a two-person scene: the clinic is acting out the wish to plug the NMDA excitotoxic leak the family cannot stand watching. Name that enactment—you and the system are living the rescue instead of saying the moderate-affinity block will not restore the lost self.

2017-104.sentence: A trial of young healthy volunteers is a vertical split: the paper stays in one room while your geriatric, multimorbid clinic is left outside the sample. External validity fails when the mind of the study never meets the body you actually treat.

2017-105.sentence: The locus coeruleus is ego strength in a nucleus: norepinephrine from that pontine source is what lets you hold arousal without flooding. Panic and opioid withdrawal show the same failure of affect tolerance when that noradrenergic generator fires without a brake.

2017-106.sentence: Risperidone or aripiprazole can quiet aggressiveness; they will not grow a secure base or buy gaze, prosody, or pragmatic talk. Parents are asking medicine to do attachment work—keep the child close enough to regulate without demanding a social self the drug cannot install.

2017-107.sentence: You and the nurses write the contingency together: reinforce a behavior incompatible with pacing-for-PRNs, not just punish the old one. Operant decrease is relational here—the pair of you stop feeding the demand cycle and pay attention to something else.

2017-108.sentence: A tissue and a walk to the elevator can be a crossing the conscience can own; sex, money, or secrecy is a violation because it exploits. The superego test is simple: did you use the patient, or did you stay a clinician who can still say no.

2017-109.sentence: Starting from “serotonin is dysregulated in PTSD” and then testing the homozygous S-SERT genotype is a candidate-gene approach: you already have a person in mind and you go looking for that person. Watch the countertransference, the feeling you get pulled into, of wanting SERT to be the villain so the hypothesis can stay the hero.

2017-110.sentence: Last observation carried forward treats the last recorded visit as if it were the real ending. That is a false termination: dropout is a stop you did not finish, and you cannot rush a completed outcome by freezing the last score in place.

2017-111.sentence: Hyperpigmentation plus salt craving is the body evacuating a crisis you cannot yet think: Addison’s adrenocortical failure, not “treatment-resistant depression.” Contain that nameless dread—the raw, unnameable sense that something is dying—by naming cortisol and mineralocorticoid collapse before you reach for another antidepressant.

2017-112.sentence: Fluoxetine can strip hydrocodone of its analgesic punch by inhibiting CYP2D6, so the patient loses the O-demethylated active metabolite and the pain comes roaring back. That is a self-esteem injury, not automatically drug-seeking: the person who felt competent and soothed by a working analgesic now feels failed by the medicine and by you.
