2017-113.sentence: The first move is to name the jurisdiction’s insanity test—M’Naghten, ALI, or whatever this court actually uses—before you interview anyone. That is the collision of a wish (to exonerate, to heal) and a prohibition (you do not get to invent the legal question); the standard is the frame that keeps the evaluation from becoming a rescue fantasy.

2017-114.sentence: Acting out is the 16-year-old’s defense here: he puts the dare and the vape into the body instead of sitting with the wish and the fear. The nucleus accumbens is loudest in adolescence on anticipated-reward fMRI, so the acting out is not “he forgot he knows better”—it is the reward system grabbing the steering wheel before thought can catch it.

2017-115.sentence: Internuclear ophthalmoplegia (failed adduction plus abducting nystagmus) is the MLF speaking in a dialect you can localize: a plaque, not “just dizziness.” In a 36-year-old, that finding means multiple sclerosis until you prove otherwise, because the young brainstem is where those plaques like to announce themselves.

2017-116.sentence: The frame of an intake is that you hold the limit: you do not argue the neighbors’ wiring, endorse it, or promise it will melt. You name the feeling the delusion carries so the patient is met as a person, not recruited into a debate that would collapse the interview.

2017-117.sentence: The trial comment here is aimed at you: adding fluvoxamine while the patient is on clozapine is your part in the seizure, not “bad luck.” Fluvoxamine blocks CYP1A2, clozapine climbs, and the brain declares the interaction with a convulsion.

2017-118.sentence: Fibromyalgia pain is not a joint sending an SOS; it is the CNS turning the volume knob up so ordinary input feels like injury. That is what the symptom is doing: central, non-nociceptive amplification that NSAIDs and opioids never reach, which is why the workup stays clean and the frustration grows.

2017-119.sentence: Sexual violence hits Erikson’s intimacy-versus-isolation task in the body: another person used closeness as the weapon. That is why its conditional PTSD rate outruns flood, crash, or witnessed death—the developmental work of trusting a partner is what got torn.

2017-120.sentence: Infancy is when axons and synapses exist in maximal number, so the infant’s mind is literally over-wired to take the caregiver in as good and bad objects. Pruning comes later; the first relationship is written on a brain that has more connections than it will ever have again.

2017-121.sentence: Papilledema is the moment raised ICP stops being a private inside story and shows on the disc—you cannot keep splitting “just anxiety” from a body that is actually swelling. That is depressive concern in Klein’s sense: you stay with the damage and try to repair it (funduscopy, imaging) instead of evacuating the threat back into “stress.”

2017-122.sentence: Neuroticism is not a solo trait sitting in her head; it is a two-person loop: her catastrophizing meets your next workup, and together you keep minting new somatic complaints. Name the dance early or the clinic becomes the other half of the personality risk factor.

2017-123.sentence: This mind in bipolar depression cannot use an uncovering, activating SSRI like paroxetine; it needs a holding, mood-stabilizing first-line agent with RCT backing—quetiapine. Technique follows prognosis: support the bipolar apparatus first, do not ask it to metabolize more affect than it can.

2017-124.sentence: The amygdala firing to subliminal emotional faces is the symptom doing its job: tagging threat before “I” ever sees a face. Implicit bias lives there first—fast, unseen, and already deciding who feels dangerous.

2017-125.sentence: Piaget mapped when a mind can construct how the world works—not when it can walk, detach, or repress. The four-year-old who thinks the tall glass holds “more” juice has not yet grown conservation; that capacity arrives later, and you wait for it instead of arguing with preoperational logic.

2017-126.sentence: Abstract reasoning is the ego’s later-arriving skill of moving from proverb to instance and back—grass greener, apple and orange. If it never quite arrived, you stop asking for metaphor and speak in concrete, same-level examples.

2017-127.sentence: This sits on Erikson’s autonomy versus shame and doubt: consent is the grown-up form of “my body, my will.” The Nuremberg Code names that task in law so an IRB cannot treat a captive ward as a sample you get to use.

2017-128.sentence: A five-year-old still fuses wish and cause: “I hate you” and the crash feel like one event. That is preoperational egocentric thinking, not an unremembered trauma leaking into the body, so you reassure Mom instead of hunting for a hidden scene.

2017-129.sentence: Dopamine from the substantia nigra is the fuel that turns a wish to move into a reach. When those nigrostriatal cells die, the wish is still there and the caudate–putamen cannot carry it—Parkinson rigidity is a drive with no motor yes.

2017-130.sentence: REM-like active sleep starts in utero, so the first “sleeper” is already a pair: fetus plus mother’s body. The NICU baby is not waiting to invent dreaming after birth; the two-person rhythm was already running.

2017-131.sentence: Dry at four, wet again at six is secondary enuresis: the night symptom arrived after a secure-enough stretch. That timing often marks a hit to the attachment system—loss, a new sibling, a shaken base—rather than the genetic deep-sleep pattern Dad and the uncles had.

2017-132.sentence: He can hold only one piece of the clock-object, the circle, and cannot keep numbers and hands in the same picture. Perseveration is that stuck partial object: the whole clock will not stay assembled in mind, so the hand just retraces what it already has.

2017-133.sentence: The Beck Depression Inventory asks the patient to rate herself; that only works if she has enough observing ego—the part that can look at feeling instead of just being flooded by it. If she cannot name sadness without collapsing or blanking, skip uncovering and start with a clinician-rated scale plus support until that observing function is stronger.

2017-134.sentence: Prosopagnosia after a fusiform gyrus lesion can pull you into an enactment: the two of you are living “I do not recognize you / you do not see me” instead of talking about it. Name that pull in the room so the consult does not become another missed face.

2017-135.sentence: The teen’s one-word answers are often suppression: he knows more than he will say and holds it out of the hour. Parental interviews are how you get the history his defense will not give you, not a courtesy add-on.

2017-136.sentence: Long-term potentiation is a calcium-driven, lasting boost of AMPA transmission—the synapse getting stronger with use. Ego strength grows the same way: repeated, tolerable practice of feeling and impulse, not a single insight.

2017-137.sentence: Erikson’s identity diffusion is a lack of continuity of self across relationships over time; it can feel like dissociation, a vertical split where she leaves without leaving the chair. One self shows up for one person, another for the next, so no single “I” holds.

2017-138.sentence: Anatomical work in schizophrenia shows no change in neuronal density; the tissue is not “punished” by cell death the way a harsh superego wants a corpse to blame. Hold the finding: volume loss is neuropil and connectivity, not a moral wipeout of neurons.

2017-139.sentence: Childhood-onset OCD arrives before the ego has a reliable way to keep a thought as a thought, so rituals recruit more of the developing mind and travel with ADHD, tics, and anxiety instead of sitting as a discrete adult illness. Early onset is not a milder chapter; it is a capacity that never quite separated obsession from the rest of personality.

2017-140.sentence: The lucid interval after the baseball is not a restored self; it is consciousness coming back for a short window while an arterial epidural hematoma expands under the temporal bone. Treat that interval as a capacity that returned and then failed—headache, vomiting, and falling arousal mean mass effect, not a kid who is “fine now.”

2017-141.sentence: Motivational interviewing does not argue, prescribe, or sell change; it holds the gap between drinking through the kids’ events and wanting to be a present father until that contradiction is thinkable. That is containment: you metabolize the raw shame into a named discrepancy instead of evacuating it with a lecture.

2017-142.sentence: Adoption changes the nursery, not the heritable risk: a birth mother’s completed suicide still raises this child’s risk of completed suicide relative to other adoptees. That is a limit love cannot rush past—name the elevated completed-suicide risk so the family can watch and plan rather than hope the new home erased the ending.

2017-143.sentence: An EHR tobacco prompt is a trial comment aimed at the clinic, not the patient: it asks providers to see their own part in skipping both the diagnosis and the referral. Once the record forces that look, documentation of use and cessation counseling both rise.

2017-144.sentence: Clinical exome sequencing reads the coding letters one at a time, so it is built for single-nucleotide substitutions after a microarray has already missed a diagnosis. It will not reliably catch long insertions, repeat expansions, or structural chromosomal rearrangements—know what the test can actually see.

2017-145.sentence: She is recruiting you the way she now recruits her mother: someone who will bless the newlywed choices so she does not have to own them. That is transference, not dependent personality—her earlier out-of-state college move already showed she can decide alone; the phase-of-life stress is what collapsed her back into seeking parental approval.

2017-146.sentence: You may forcibly give antipsychotics in jail for emergency danger, for symptoms that threaten safety, or to restore competency to stand trial—not to extract a confession and not because a forensic psychiatrist or a benefit–risk note says so. The frame is the court, not the dyad: you are treating so he can face the charge, which is a legal use of the body, not a clinical alliance.

2017-147.sentence: Ask how he would describe the problem to a family member or friend; that pulls the complaint into his own idiom instead of your guess about “his people” or spirituality. The wish to be understood collides with your unfamiliarity; the question lets him name the conflict rather than you filling it with a cultural stereotype.

2017-148.sentence: The license that counts is only in the state where the patient sits, not yours and not “any state.” Crossing a state line for telepsychiatry is a frame issue: the treatment relationship is legally located in the patient’s body, not in your office.

2017-149.sentence: Pedigree linkage is what finds rare variants of large effect that run through one family; GWAS case–control and sib-pair designs are built for common small effects and will miss that signal. The illness is inherited as a lineage, not as a crowd average—you study the pedigree the way you study a developmental line, not a population mean.

2017-150.sentence: Kraepelin treated psychiatric disorders as categorically distinct “natural disease entities,” not as a continuum between dementia praecox and manic-depressive illness and not as personality styles. The symptom, in his view, pointed to a disease kind, not to a meaning or a philosophical stance—that is why our manuals still split categories instead of drawing one mood–psychosis line.

2017-151.sentence: His complaint of slowness is also a recruitment: he is handing you the role of the person who will either certify him as demented or hold the line that he is still himself. Notice your countertransference—the urge to rush, finish his sentences, or over-reassure—because information processing speed is what actually slows after 65, and your impatience can become the proof he came in fearing.

2017-152.sentence: Transference is not a trivia term; it is the old relationship walking into the room and using you as the stand-in. Name it as reenacted feeling in the pair of you, not as her being “difficult,” so the wary please-don’t-abandon-me intensity can be talked about instead of lived.

2017-153.sentence: Mood regulation and clear thinking are ego capacities she already had; they do not vanish because of “stress” or a stable prednisone dose. When discoid lupus suddenly brings fatigue, inflamed joints, myalgias, depression, and cognitive fog without focal signs, those capacities are being knocked offline by disease-induced cerebritis.

2017-154.sentence: The preference for the human voice at birth is not a cute extra; it is the newborn’s first job—finding a speaker and locking on. Talking to the baby is already doing something: it offers a living object before words mean anything.

2017-155.sentence: A nine-year-old lives in industry versus inferiority: school competence is how he decides whether he is a capable kid or a failure. After years of good methylphenidate response that is now fading, mixed amphetamine salts is the next stimulant move that protects that task before you abandon the stimulant class.

2017-156.sentence: The six-hour inability to hold new information, with fluent speech and a later blank for the day, is not a meaningful “escape” from the vacation or a dissociative wipe. Transient global amnesia is the brain briefly failing to encode; treat the finding as neurology, not as a symbol of not wanting to go.

2017-157.sentence: Alcohol’s brief quieting of essential tremor can feel like a Kleinian repair: the shaky, persecuting hand is briefly made good again, so the self can reach for coffee without being attacked by its own body. Watch the flip: when the drink becomes the only way to evict the bad tremor, you are in paranoid-schizoid logic (split good/bad, get rid of the bad) rather than depressive concern that the tremor is part of him.

2017-158.sentence: Parenting training after a child’s conduct problems is indicated prevention: the family already has the symptom, so the work is undoing—doing something concrete now to cancel the damage already in motion. Universal classroom games and age-cut tobacco rules sit earlier; here the defense is repair after the fact, not pretending the conduct never arrived.

2017-159.sentence: Autism’s high heritability can turn a future pregnancy into a pill-as-proof-of-need: they want a gene test or a guarantee to feed the terror that they poisoned the child. Your job is to hold that demand without treating genetics as either a clean feed or a verdict of parental poison.

2017-160.sentence: Thanking her for saying she cursed, then working on alternatives, is mirroring: you reflect a mother who can still be competent, not a monster. If you only dump your anger or rush to CPS talk, you shatter the idealizing/self-esteem need that brought the confession.

2017-161.sentence: A two-year-old right MCA infarct on CT is already contained: hypodense, CSF-like, volume-lost—thinkable history, not nameless acute blood. Your consult job is the same Bion move: take the family’s raw dread of “stroke now” and name the old, residual left weakness so it can be thought instead of evacuated into panic.

2017-162.sentence: A translocation is genetic material broken off and stuck to another chromosome—unremembered rearrangement that still shows up in the body as dysmorphism plus new psychosis. What the karyotype cannot narrate gets repeated in the phenotype and then in the consult: the family lives the break they cannot recall.

2017-163.sentence: Valproate is the prohibition in this pairing: it blocks lamotrigine glucuronidation and roughly doubles the level, so the usual titration has to be cut in half. The wish is fuller mood coverage; the collision lives in the liver, not in the chart, and ignoring it is how you write a rash.

2017-164.sentence: Piaget maps the lone scientist and leaves conscience out of the lab: guilt, shame, and the wish to please never get a stage. That is why his model cannot explain a withdrawn adolescent whose thinking is intact and whose learning is still frozen by a harsh inner judge.

2017-165.sentence: Physicians who die by suicide are less likely than other completers to have been on an antidepressant; the white-coat identity recruits you into being the one who never needs the pill. That transference is lethal when it also lives in the treating doctor, who under-prescribes rather than sit with a colleague as a patient.

2017-166.sentence: Once complex partial seizures quiet, the mind can park the old storm in a paranoid story that the neurologist means harm—interictal psychosis, not a new personality. The symptom is doing the seizure's old job: keeping danger outside the self after months of control.

2017-167.sentence: At five she is not mixing parade with circus fantasy; she is using the circus to build a category of big public shows that might include clowns. That is categorical thought arriving on time: yesterday's experience becomes today's working class, not a failure of reality testing.

2017-168.sentence: Glutamate cannot open the NMDA channel by itself; glycine (or D-serine) has to sit on the co-agonist site or the door stays shut. The clinical meaning of that pairing is simple: ketamine-class blockade and glycine-site drugs only make sense if you remember both keys.

2017-169.sentence: This sits on Erikson’s industry versus inferiority: the asymptomatic child of a parent with serious mental illness is already being sorted into “at risk” before they have failed or succeeded at school-age competence. Selective prevention names that extra load without treating the kid as already sick, so the family can still build skill instead of inheriting a premature identity of defect.

2017-170.sentence: Duration of untreated psychosis is a limit you cannot rush away: first-generation immigrant status often stretches the time before anyone names the break, so language, stigma, and access keep the person in raw experience longer. Shorter DUP is the clinic’s time-boundary; longer DUP here is not “worse character,” it is delayed recognition that the illness has already started.

2017-171.sentence: Two-word phrases (“more milk”) are the toddler’s first container: a raw want gets held in a tiny sentence instead of only a scream. If the two-year-old cannot yet combine words, the feeling stays closer to Bion’s nameless dread—evacuated as noise rather than thinkable speech strangers could even half-understand.

2017-172.sentence: Accuracy of a marketed genetic test for a neurodegenerative disorder is a frame question: you need a cross-sectional study of sensitivity and specificity against a reference standard before you sell hope or dread. Cohort, crossover, and RCTs answer prognosis or treatment; they do not hold the ethical limit of “is this test true enough to use.”

2017-173.sentence: Holding a phone number just long enough to dial is working memory in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex—the same mental muscle that lets someone keep a trial comment in mind without acting. The hippocampus files lasting episodes; DLPFC is whether they can still see their own part for the next thirty seconds.

2017-174.sentence: Stopping or reducing lithium before ECT is suppression used well: you consciously set aside a useful mood stabilizer because it can worsen post-ECT delirium and potentiate succinylcholine blockade. That is not denial of the bipolar or unipolar illness; it is choosing a temporary gap so the seizure treatment can proceed without a confusional overlay.

2017-175.sentence: Sertraline may already be doing quiet work as a feed: proof someone is watching the heart so he does not have to carry the brother’s infarct alone. Still treat the exertional, rest-relieved pain as a real coronary demand first, or the pill becomes a poison that says his chest is imaginary.

2017-176.sentence: Methadone started in prison keeps the body from splitting: the inmate does not have to leave the craving in the cell and then meet it, unbuffered, at the gate. Transfer-only or NA-after-release asks a vertical split to hold until discharge, which is when most people fall out of the chair.

2017-177.sentence: Peak striatal dopamine-receptor density in adolescence is already an enactment: the teen’s reward system and the adult world’s “just say no” are repeating a two-person fight about who owns the impulse. Name the receptor peak in the room so you are talking about the chase, not living it as a power struggle.

2017-178.sentence: The hour in the bathroom is attachment work gone solitary: the mirror is being used as a regulating other, a secure base that never answers back. Body dysmorphic disorder, not excoriation disorder, means the protest is “look at this ruined face,” not “I cannot stop picking.”

2017-179.sentence: A visible hockey-crooked nose plus “I want to look normal again” is ego strength: reality testing is intact, affect is contained, and the wish is repair, not a new self. Quality of life often rises after that kind of surgery because the ego is not being asked to metabolize a phantom defect.

2017-180.sentence: PCP’s NMDA blockade dumps unmetabolized sensation into the room: nystagmus, hypertension, and violence are nameless dread that cannot be thought. Your job is containment, holding the NMDA-off brain until a feeling can become a word instead of an evacuation.

2017-181.sentence: Tobacco use disorder is already on a clock you do not get to reset later in the hour. Deferring the two-pack habit as “after the schizophrenia is stable” treats preventable death as something you can postpone; the limit is that this cause of death does not wait for a better session.

2017-182.sentence: Insight here starts in your own body: where you stand, how close you sit, and whether you can see the patient’s hands and path as clearly as your own. A trial comment is silent first—you notice if you have boxed yourself between the patient and the door, or squared up like a threat, before you say a word about consequences or demand cooperation.

2017-183.sentence: Fludrocortisone is the frame-holder when levodopa, pramipexole, or entacapone drop standing blood pressure: you do not keep pushing dopaminergic dose past what the vasculature can stand. Prednisone is not that limit; mineralocorticoid support, after hydration and med review, is how you keep treating Parkinson disease without pretending orthostasis is the patient’s problem to tough out.

2017-184.sentence: Adolescence is when the cortex does its biggest synaptic prune, so circuits that will stay are the ones that get used. That is why this window can unmask schizophrenia: the brain is deleting connections, not adding a childhood surplus, and unused pathways do not get a later do-over.

2017-185.sentence: When this five-year-old turns mother’s gentle help into fear and aggression, she is using a defense: she treats comfort as danger so she does not have to need anyone. That is not autism’s social-communication pattern and not PTSD’s re-experiencing; reactive attachment after neglectful foster care is the child refusing consolation because depending once already failed.

2017-186.sentence: Starting another antipsychotic on a patient already on QT-prolonging drugs is an enactment: the team is living “one more agent, we will watch it” instead of naming the shared cardiac risk. The mechanism is potassium channel blockade, so the repetition to stop is stacking IKr block until the QTc lengthens, not hoping sodium, calcium, or the ATPase will save the tracing.

2017-187.sentence: Flavor preference hangs on cognitive associations: the mind has already decided what the food means before the tongue finishes the bite. That is a vertical split—the person stays in the chair while the craving leaves for a memory, a person, or a rule about who is allowed to eat.

2017-188.sentence: Industry versus inferiority is the work of latency: make something, get good at it, and let peers and a father see the competence. Ego strength here is that he can take pride in the basketball cards instead of collapsing into inferiority when the parents ding his grades.

2017-189.sentence: Generalized theta and delta activity is the EEG of a cortex that can no longer hold a continuous self. Reality testing fails with those slow waves, so the confusion and fluctuating consciousness are not a mood—they are lost ego functions until the pneumonia clears.

2017-190.sentence: DSM-III (1980) put explicit diagnostic criteria and the multiaxial system on the page so a wish to tell the whole story would not swallow the need to name a syndrome. That is a drive conflict in the field itself: hunger for meaning colliding with a prohibition against untestable inference.

2017-191.sentence: The FDA requires bioequivalence—same rate and extent of absorption as brand lamotrigine—not a new efficacy or side-effect trial. What cannot be represented, the unremembered difference in fillers, gets repeated in the body as “this is not my drug.”

2017-192.sentence: Head injuries, especially abusive head trauma, are the leading cause of child maltreatment deaths—ahead of burns, starvation, or retroperitoneal bleeds. In that consult you are recruited to become either the adult who will not see the head or the one who must carry the rage; name that countertransference before you write.

2017-193.sentence: GABA is the local conscience of the mesolimbic reward circuit: it usually sits on the VTA and says no to extra dopamine. Many addictive drugs work by a sanctioned gap in that morality—they quiet those GABA brakes so dopamine can fire without asking permission.

2017-194.sentence: Constricted affect means the feeling is still there but the window is narrowed—sad, little smile, yet some normal prosody. That leftover inflection is your opening: a small trial comment can land because this is not a flat, sealed-off mind.

2017-195.sentence: The real limit on videoconference telepsychiatry is not the rural patient; it is physician dissatisfaction with a thinner frame. You cannot rush a clinician into a new ending of the old office ritual if they still experience the screen as a loss of the work.

2017-196.sentence: In bipolar imaging, the prefrontal cortex loses its line to the amygdala—so raw affect never gets contained, meaning held long enough to become a thought. What cannot be thought is evacuated as a mood swing instead of a nameable feeling.

2017-197.sentence: Caffeine (those energy drinks) can drop a lithium level from 0.9 to 0.6 while the patient is trying to feel competent enough to study. The self-esteem bid quietly unmirrors the stabilizing drug that was holding the bipolar self together.

2017-198.sentence: The room is already in an enactment: after the separation news, everyone treats the thigh cuts as the story and lets the patient say, “My parents can provide additional information.” That two-person script hides the real diagnosis—autism spectrum disorder, with lifelong noise intolerance, stereotypy, and social awkwardness that did not start three days ago.

2017-199.sentence: At two to three the tantrum is acting out: the child discharges frustration in the body instead of holding it. A good-enough attachment lets the toddler borrow the parent's calm so waiting can start to replace the meltdown.

2017-200.sentence: Genomic imprinting means the same 15q13 deletion can write two different syndromes depending on whether the missing copy came from father or mother. Ego strength in that counseling hour is affect tolerance for that uncertainty—the genotype is not a verdict, and reality testing has to hold both 'same deletion' and 'different story.

2017-201.sentence: Process metrics (call-light speed, med rec, suicide screens, note lag) let a unit stay in a vertical split: the paperwork is present while whether anyone got better is not felt. A change in depression score from admission to discharge is the indicator that pulls the team back into contact with the actual stay.

2017-202.sentence: After a shooting, the family's 'does his depression mean the guns go?' is already an enactment: panic is being lived as a blanket ban instead of thought as risk. The APA position—restrict firearms for people with increased violence risk, not for a diagnosis or a past hospitalization—keeps you from joining that scene.

2017-203.sentence: Cataplexy is humor failing as a defense: laughter, which should bind feeling, instead dumps tone in the arms and legs. Venlafaxine treats that collapse; modafinil and methylphenidate wake the patient up but do not restore motor control when affect spikes.

2017-204.sentence: Chronic physical illness can install the body as a bad object—the unreliable other that never quite goes away. Somatic symptom disorder grows when good and bad cannot be held together: real diabetes or COPD and the catastrophic inner doctor cannot share one relationship to the self.

2017-205.sentence: Lateral orbitofrontal cortex is the circuit that tags a stimulus as potentially harmful—the mind’s early-warning evaluator, not the motor, eye-movement, or planning loops. Uncover fear and contamination themes only as much as this patient’s OFC can stand; if harm-evaluation is already on fire, more interpretation just feeds the loop, so you stay more supportive until the alarm can be named without acting on it.

2017-206.sentence: Clozapine is the only atypical that has consistently beaten typicals for treatment-resistant psychosis—the two of you, and the family, are not shopping for a ‘stronger’ brand. The relational move is to stop the search for a magic pill and share the hard work: agranulocytosis monitoring, weekly labs, and staying in the room when hope and disappointment keep trading places.

2017-207.sentence: The necessaries doctrine says we treat because prison takes away the person’s power to seek care—an imposed separation from the usual secure base of choosing a doctor. When the charge nurse says ‘he’s a prisoner,’ you answer that deprivation of access, not worthiness, is why the SSRI and weekly therapy are required, same as in the community.

2017-208.sentence: The nightly glass of wine is not a secret dementia engine in this story; it has been a stable, moderate ritual that never needed to be the symptom. Advise her to keep the pattern if it does not change—parental dementia plus aging is not a reason to turn a long-held dinner habit into a new self-punishment.

2017-209.sentence: Gray matter volume peaks in late childhood, then pruning begins—so the ‘wall’ before the teen years is biology meeting Erikson’s industry-versus-inferiority, not a kid who suddenly stopped trying. Help the parent see competence as still being built while the cortex is remodeling; late childhood is when the brain is fullest before adolescence asks for identity.

2017-210.sentence: Carbamazepine, not an opioid or a migraine triptan, is the drug for classic trigeminal neuralgia—lightning jabs in the jaw set off by shaving or brushing. You and the patient make the pattern together when you refuse to chase the MRI-negative pain with narcotics and instead name a treatable nerve syndrome you can sit with until the stabs ease.

2017-211.sentence: Hyponatremia with mild confusion and lethargy is a support-first mind: the ego is metabolically soggy, so you correct sodium and water, not chase an unconscious conflict. Uncovering talk lands as more noise until the BMP is normal and thirst is no longer running the interview.

2017-212.sentence: The five-month-old’s gurgle-wave-kick and the mother’s tickle are how a good object gets built: mother is taken in as someone who answers excitement with pleasure, not as a temperament trait sitting inside the baby alone. Attachment here is a two-person holding of good feeling, not a one-person setting on a dimmer switch.

2017-213.sentence: A single day-long workshop dumps the algorithm into the CMHC as if staff should swallow a perfect object and feel grateful; leftover hatred of the change then has nowhere to go. Return visits after a focused workshop let you take in their projected incompetence and resistance—projective identification, meaning they put the “this will fail” feeling into you—and hand it back as problem-solving instead of abandonment.

2017-214.sentence: The NMDA channel stays shut behind a magnesium plug until the membrane depolarizes; ligand alone is a knock with no door opening. That coincidence rule is why ketamine and memantine matter: they occupy a gate that only works when the cell is already excited.

2017-215.sentence: Asking when in the day the cutting thought first showed up treats the patient as someone in autonomy versus shame: map the chain, do not put them in the dock. “Why would you inflict pain?” is a shame move; the timestamp question gives industry back—here is a sequence you can work.

2017-216.sentence: Ocular jerks to the optokinetic drum mean the visual pathway still tracks stripes; the “blindness” is doing psychic work, not reporting a dead retina. The symptom keeps something unseeable out of awareness while the OKN reflex quietly admits the eyes still work.

2017-217.sentence: Opposite-gender clothes and play at six often sit in a still-plastic developmental window, not a finished identity. Gender dysphoria that starts prepuberty most often remits on its own by adulthood, so the work is to hold the child through latency without treating play as destiny.

2017-218.sentence: The weekly ANC is the field's conscience after the 1975 Finnish Lancet epidemic of clozapine agranulocytosis. Skipping labs is not a small rebellion; it is a hole in that shared superego, and the marrow does not forgive it.

2017-219.sentence: When a parent recruits you as the judge of a seven-year-old 'loner,' notice the pull to become either the harsh critic or the reassuring grandparent. School age is about peers and group play, so your job is to name that task without joining the parent's panic or dismissing it.

2017-220.sentence: Ego strength needs a continuous self: who I was an hour ago still has to be me. Bilateral damage to the hippocampal formation and parahippocampal cortex wipes new encoding, so amnesia is not just a memory bug—it is the mind losing the thread that holds identity together.

2017-221.sentence: Depersonalization is a vertical split: the person leaves without leaving the chair, watching a body that no longer feels like theirs. Name it apart from derealization (the world goes unreal) so the patient can locate the cut inside the self, not in the room.

2017-222.sentence: PTSD risk is not only the crash; it is the old relational weather the person already lived in. Prior childhood adversity means the nervous system learned, with actual other people, that help does not come—so the new trauma lands on a two-person template already built for terror.

2017-223.sentence: Quetiapine is the clingy roommate who barely sits on the D2 receptor and then leaves, so the body does not have to protest the hold with akathisia and rigidity. You are offering a secure base that stays nearby without gripping—proximity without a death-grip on dopamine.

2017-224.sentence: The “new personality” and the weak contralateral leg are one sentence from the anterior cerebral artery, not a character assassination or a request for a pill. Medial frontal cortex plus paracentral lobule went offline; treat the infarct as the speaker before you treat the person as the problem.

2017-225.sentence: Taking the flowers is a boundary crossing: you bent the usual no-gifts rule so she could enter the room, then you keep the frame by documenting it and thinking about it. A violation would have been becoming her friend; here the limit still belongs to you, and the gift is allowed to mean “I can risk being known.”

2017-226.sentence: Selective abstraction is already happening between you: she hands you a stack of glowing evaluations and you are invited to live only inside the one mild note about questions. That is an enactment—the two of you repeating her habit of treating one blot as the whole self instead of naming the filter.

2017-227.sentence: He is using intellectualization: a confusing surge of arousal around male friends gets turned into a courtroom question—“am I gay?”—so the feeling never has to stay in the body. You answer the facts (these feelings are common at fourteen; preference is still consolidating) so the defense can loosen without you assigning him a lifelong verdict.

2017-228.sentence: She is handing you nameless dread—poison the fetus with sertraline, or ruin the pregnancy by staying depressed—and your job is containment: hold both facts until they can be thought. SSRIs are associated with neonatal adaptation syndrome, a usually transient jittery withdrawal picture, not a mandate to stop treatment that itself raises preterm birth.

2017-229.sentence: The paraphrase is the mirroring the speaker just earned: a partner who can repeat the specific behavior and the feeling back, without fixing it yet, tells the self it was heard accurately. Jumping to change, confession, or brainstorming would skip that reflection and leave one person feeling incompetent in the room.

2017-230.sentence: Wernicke aphasia after a hit to the posterior third of the left superior temporal gyrus is a two-person failure of meaning: fluent empty speech meets a listener who cannot decode it, and the patient does not notice the mismatch. The consult becomes a shared pattern of talking past each other until you stop asking for content and start testing comprehension and repetition.

2017-231.sentence: When pro-inflammatory cytokines rise with a rheumatoid flare, the mind has less spare capacity for uncovering work; support and treating the immune load come first. Insight-heavy technique during that inflammatory window asks a metabolically taxed ego to do more than it can hold.

2017-232.sentence: A 3½-year-old who walks in on the shower and asks why Dad’s penis is “fat” is using age-typical curiosity, not a collapse of impulse control or reality testing. The father’s alarm is the ego under strain; the boy’s is handling genital difference with ordinary preschool interest.

2017-233.sentence: HIPAA lets you call the primary care doctor to keep prescribing safe even when she will not sign a form, as long as she does not object. That call is proximity work: you use the other clinician as a secure base so the treatment pair is not left alone with a dangerous interaction.

2017-234.sentence: A single odd remark after bupropion in schizotypal personality disorder can get treated as “the drug caused psychosis” when it may just be the old personality speaking. A cohort follows the exposure forward into new psychotic symptoms, so the meaning of the change is timed to the drug instead of read into every quirk.

2017-235.sentence: A pedigree is a generativity problem: who passed what, and to whom. Linkage analysis is the tool that treats that inheritance as a map, tracking which chromosomal region travels with the illness instead of leaving lineage as a family myth.

2017-236.sentence: Diabetic feet and a low mood often get split into a “bad body” and a “good mind,” as if one relationship cannot hold both. Duloxetine treats neuropathic pain and depression in the same agent, so the patient does not have to keep the damaged part and the hopeful part in separate rooms.

2017-237.sentence: Contamination is the paranoid-schizoid version of OCD: dirt is not just dirt; it is a persecutor that must be kept out. Washing is an attempt to evacuate that projected badness from the skin rather than to mourn ordinary mess and stay in the depressive position, where concern and repair replace endless purification.

2017-238.sentence: Insight here is the capacity to own the simple subtraction, not hide in a fancier ratio. Attributable risk is that 12-point gap (28% minus 16%): the slice of progression the drug can actually claim, the way a trial interpretation names the patient’s real part instead of a relative story.

2017-239.sentence: The frame is not only the fifty-minute hour; it is also sleep and movement, the limits that keep the organ of memory from shrinking. Adult neurogenesis in the hippocampus is the biological reason those boring rules matter: new cells form there, and chronic stress plus insomnia is how the treatment setting quietly fails that tissue.

2017-240.sentence: Rapprochement is the toddler crisis of needing the parent and hating that need; in this adult it returns as closeness that feels like a crime. A harsh superego—conscience after abuse—treats intimacy as disloyalty or danger, so she cuts the tie before guilt and terror can be named in the room.

2017-241.sentence: A GWAS finding is not a destiny that finally arrived in the genome; it is a statistical crowd of tiny risk markers, not the missing parent who explains the child. When the family asks to test their son, they are hoping a lab result will complete a developmental story that association studies were never built to finish.

2017-242.sentence: The cyanosis and fainting are not background color; they are the body saying the heart cannot safely carry the extra work methylphenidate would demand. Holding the script protects the child from a treatment whose 'help' would be a cardiac risk, not a personality problem.

2017-243.sentence: MHPAEA sits on the industry-versus-inferiority problem of a whole system: mental health was treated as the lesser sibling of medical care. Equalizing visit limits for behavioral health and similar medical coverage is the statute's way of saying that psychiatry is not a second-class task.

2017-244.sentence: Dextromethorphan in OTC cough syrup is how some teens borrow a dissociative exit without naming a 'drug' in the family story. Class and pharmacy-aisle identity sit in the room: the parents can stay respectable while the adolescent leaves the self by NMDA blockade.

2017-245.sentence: DNA methylation is how early abuse can keep writing the same terror into gene regulation decades later, a molecular version of projective identification: the past is still being put into the present body. The patient is not imagining a scar; the stress axis was marked, not merely remembered.

2017-246.sentence: Deinstitutionalization split the hospital's holding function from the person who needed holding, then left the bad object—the untreated patient—on the street and in jail. The higher ratio of mentally ill people in prisons versus hospitals is what happens when society cannot keep good and bad care in one place.

2017-247.sentence: Myasthenia gravis is a fatigable mind–body: the lesion moves (right abduction this morning, left ptosis this afternoon) and then vanishes, so you cannot treat today's deficit as the whole story. Uncovering work that hunts a single hidden meaning will overshoot; stay supportive, re-examine, and let the fluctuating exam—not a clever interpretation—set the pace.

2017-248.sentence: Andropause really drops penile rigidity, not desire, sperm count, or the refractory period—so when he and you both lean on 'it's my depression,' you are co-authoring a two-person story that erases the vascular-androgen fact. Name the rigidity change in the room so the pair of you stop treating a mechanical shift as a moral or mood failure.

2017-249.sentence: Wraparound is an individualized, family-driven and youth-guided team—not a court, not 24/7 ACT, not a peds–psychiatry handshake. After serial placements, the family becomes the secure base again: the kid uses a known caregiver to regulate, and the team exists to keep that proximity from being taken over by the system.

2017-250.sentence: High-dose folic acid before conception is the intervention that can still reduce major malformations on antiepileptics; waiting until a pregnancy is already 'remembered' is too late. The unborn injury is still unrepresented—nothing to recall, only a risk in the body—so you act on folate now rather than wait for a tragedy the couple cannot yet picture.

2017-251.sentence: Acetylation of lysine on histones relaxes chromatin so transcription can happen; the 'wish' is expression, the condensed nucleosome is the brake. Valproate, as a histone deacetylase inhibitor, keeps that acetyl mark on—drive without the usual silencing—which is why the same chemistry that opens genes also carries teratogenic cost.

2017-252.sentence: In precontemplation, 'Have you heard about the health benefits of quitting?' offers a small mirror of competence: he can take in a fact without being told he is reckless or ready. Scare lines, pep talks, and quit-date questions puncture self-esteem; curiosity about benefit leaves his ideal self intact long enough to listen.

2017-253.sentence: Three documented bursts of aggression toward ED patients are not a private lapse; they are evacuation, dumping raw, unthinkable affect into whoever is in the room. Sending the colleague to the physician health program is the institution doing what Bion called containing: holding that heat long enough for it to become thinkable instead of living in the next patient's body.

2017-254.sentence: The sexual-side-effect veto is doing work: it protects a last intact piece of potency so the antidepressant cannot take that too. Escitalopram is the listed agent least likely to induce treatment-emergent sexual dysfunction, so you can treat the depression without stripping the function that still feels like self.

2017-255.sentence: Adaptive mourning is a developmental capacity, and it arrives only if someone lets the child put loss into words. Rapid remarriage, a stoic surviving parent, parentification, or a push for closure all stall that capacity; opportunities to express the loss let it come online.

2017-256.sentence: The overactive cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical loop is a rigid conscience with a motor: dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and striatum keep sending unfinished business, and the thalamus is the third station that bounces it back as another obligatory check. The SSRI that 'takes the edge off' is quieting that thalamic return ticket, not erasing real guilt.

2017-257.sentence: A dying 34-year-old with under three weeks will recruit you as the last person who can still do something fast, and that pull is countertransference you should name, not act out as heroic delay. Methylphenidate is the treatment that matches the time left; sertraline, duloxetine, or mirtazapine would leave you and the patient waiting for an antidepressant that will not arrive.

2017-258.sentence: Losing identity after 'walking away from something horrible,' with a clean EEG, urine, and scan, is the mind splitting off a bad object so the self does not have to hold both. Dissociative amnesia is that split in action: the person stays, the intolerable relationship is gone from memory.

2017-259.sentence: Trail-Making Test asks the mind to hold a sequence and jump between sets without falling apart—that is the same work as depressive concern: keeping two positions in play instead of splitting them. When frontal stroke wrecks that sequencing, the patient cannot “repair” the trail; they evacuate the task into chaos rather than integrate attention, scanning, and order.

2017-260.sentence: Prader-Willi hunger is not just calories; it is a self that never got a reliable mirror of “enough,” so food-seeking becomes the only way to feel held. Short stature, small hands and feet, hypogonadism, and OCD-like rigidity sit beside that void: competence and bodily pride never got idealized into a stable self-esteem.

2017-261.sentence: Habituation is the drive going quiet: the wish to startle at the train collides with the office’s demand that you keep working, and the alarm loses. The train still arrives; the prohibition against reacting wins, so the stimulus stays and the reaction fades—not extinction of a learned pairing, just the nervous system giving up the fight.

2017-262.sentence: Laxative abuse is the limit the binge cannot keep: the purge is a forced ending when satiety will not arrive on time. Binge eating disorder can sit with the overflow; bulimia installs a hard stop—vomiting, laxatives, or exercise—because the capacity to wait cannot be rushed.

2017-263.sentence: Diffusion tensor imaging follows water along white-matter tracts so a raw “wiring is broken” dread can become a thinkable map of connectivity. Without that container, TBI personality change stays nameless evacuation—feeling dumped into the room—rather than a pathway you can name and study.

2017-264.sentence: Basal ganglia procedural learning keeps the frame when hippocampus cannot: tennis still improves even if the patient cannot report the hour. The limit is held by a different structure—skill accrues in silence, so you do not demand explicit recall as the fee for learning.

2017-265.sentence: IMPACT works because someone keeps looking: screen most primary-care patients, then a care manager tracks scores so depression cannot hide as “just being tired.” A trial comment to the clinic is the same move—“we miss half of these unless we measure”—and it doubles treatment effectiveness versus usual care.

2017-266.sentence: Calling this a stroke in the first five minutes is acting out: discharging fear through action instead of watching the clock. Migraine with aura marches over about thirty minutes—vision, then lips and hands, then unilateral headache with osmophobia—so hold the anxiety until the tempo declares itself.

2017-267.sentence: When a surgeon cannot name the anatomy of a case he still “does,” the symptom is pointing at the fact store, not yesterday’s case. That is semantic memory: shared knowledge of parts and words, gone even though the hands may still find the plane.

2017-268.sentence: The blood–brain barrier is a frame: capillary endothelial cells with tight junctions decide what is allowed in. Astrocytes brace that wall; they are not the wall, which is why some drugs reach cortex and others never get a seat.

2017-269.sentence: Do not throw lithium out because a fine tremor showed up; that is paranoid-schizoid splitting, all-bad object, no room to repair. Keep the mood stable and add propranolol—depressive-position repair: the good treatment stays, the harm gets tended.

2017-270.sentence: A prion is a protein that teaches the next protein to fold wrong; staff can catch the same contagion as panic and start treating the room as cursed. Name the spongiform illness and the myoclonus so the enactment—isolation theater as if this were a virus—can stop.

2017-271.sentence: The incontinence arrives and she barely shrugs—that is a vertical split: the body event happens while the observing self has already left the chair. In normal pressure hydrocephalus the magnetic, shuffling gait and that indifferent wetness travel together because urgency never gets bound to shame; the loop is flooded, not forgotten.

2017-272.sentence: Staff praise or withhold on a schedule, and that schedule is the feed: the child learns the world will answer the action, not the wish. Behaviorism here is a promise that the same move always gets the same reply, safer than a parent whose care arrives as demand or proof that you are too much.

2017-273.sentence: A smaller amygdala is a thinner alarm, so trait aggression can fire before fear has time to veto it. Name that in the plan and you treat the next blow-up as a failed signal, not as a personality you have to argue with.

2017-274.sentence: Choosing bupropion over venlafaxine, duloxetine, or a tricyclic is the trial comment: can the depression move without the self flipping into a mixed or rapid-cycling storm. If they can say, a week later, “I feel a half-step too fast,” they are using insight, and lithium is no longer a spectator.

2017-275.sentence: The family dragged her in, so the first limit is whose hour this is: she stays if she wants the chair, not if they want a less embarrassing daughter. Avoidant personality disorder lives on the certainty of humiliation; a predictable fee and a closed door are the first proof you will not join the critics.

2017-276.sentence: The Wisconsin Card Sorting Test asks the mind to hold a rule that just died and make a new one from the tester’s “wrong”—that is containment: a raw I-failed becomes a thinkable next strategy. When that function is gone, the feeling is evacuated as perseveration instead of thought.

2017-277.sentence: A microarray that finds a CNV is not a verdict; it is a limit on what genetics can finish for the family in one visit. You hold that ending: like SNPs, copy number variants are common in healthy people, so you refuse to let a lab slip become a destiny.

2017-278.sentence: Sumatriptan plus 60 mg fluoxetine is not a private chemistry problem; it is a two-party handshake that can become serotonin syndrome. The fever, diarrhea, and tightening muscles are the pair speaking together—5-HT1 agonist meeting an SSRI—so you treat the combination, not a migraine drug in isolation.

2017-279.sentence: Highest lifetime IPV among Native American women sits on a trust-versus-mistrust terrain: safety with another person was never a given. Screening is not a census item; it is asking whether this woman has ever been allowed a basic Eriksonian hold that violence keeps tearing up.

2017-280.sentence: Variable-ratio payout is the worst schedule for insight: the next pull might be the one, so uncovering “why you gamble” rarely outruns the lever. Support the frame first—limits, money, time—because a slot machine trains persistence better than interpretation does.

2017-281.sentence: Orexin from the lateral hypothalamus is the night-watch that keeps two states from collapsing into each other. When those cells are gone, sleep and wake stop holding a partnership: daytime sleepiness and cataplexy are the pair failing to take turns.

2017-282.sentence: Case-control design is how you stay close to a rare event without waiting years for enough new cases to appear. You start with the people who already have the outcome and look backward for exposures—the epidemiologic version of using a known pair to study what went wrong, because incidence is too low to follow a huge cohort forward.

2017-283.sentence: Broca's aphasia leaves comprehension standing while the ego loses its usual exit ramp for affect: naming, repeating, and answering yes or no. That is a hit to affect tolerance and impulse control in speech, not to reality testing—he still follows verbal and written commands, so sit with the frustration instead of filling every silence.

2017-284.sentence: Erikson's tasks keep moving if one parent still supplies a reliable world: trust, industry, and later identity do not require a second spouse at the table. Remarriage is not a developmental rescue; stable parental functioning and money are what keep the child from stalling on the stage they are actually in.

2017-285.sentence: A healthy child's HPA axis is on a developmental clock: cortisol peaks in the morning and falls at night. Draw the level at the wrong hour and you will invent an adrenal story that the child's ordinary circadian rhythm never told.

2017-286.sentence: Illness anxiety parks the persecutor in one feared diagnosis; that is closer to paranoid-schizoid thinking, where one bad object is hunted, not a body full of complaints. Somatic symptom disorder floods the field with many damaged parts, so multiple physical complaints belong there, not in illness anxiety.

2017-287.sentence: The FMR1 CGG repeat, macroorchidism, and hand-flapping are one boy, not a 'good child' split off from a 'bad gene.' Hold both sides of him in the same room so the family does not love an imaginary intact object and exile the actual adolescent.

2017-288.sentence: Mesocortical dopamine is the tract for cognitive processing; an antipsychotic that over-blocks it can steal thinking while you chase psychosis. Holding the dose limit is the ethical frame: do not trade the patient's working cortex for a quieter ward.

2017-289.sentence: A trial comment is: “When I leave, it is as if a piece of you walks out with me.” If they can use that, they see the rage as loss of a self-object—another person doing a needed function for the self—not as you being a careless doctor.

2017-290.sentence: Corticotropin-releasing hormone is the hypothalamus turning nameless dread into a signal the pituitary can read as ACTH. Containment is the same job: you hold the raw panic until it becomes a thought instead of an evacuation down the HPA axis.

2017-291.sentence: Sleep paralysis is REM atonia locking the body while the mind is still half awake—the sleep–wake border will not be rushed. You name that limit the way you name the end of an hour: willpower does not shorten a narcoleptic attack.

2017-292.sentence: A trial comment is: “You are already paying a mood tax even if the checklist is one item short.” If they can own that an SSRI is for that suffering and not a verdict that the cancer has won, they have enough psychological mindedness to start.

2017-293.sentence: Self-assessment CME holds the frame: keyed answer, citation, and how you stacked against peers—no hidden examiner in the room. The ethical limit is yours: the credit only counts if you sit with the miss instead of shopping for an easier activity.

2017-294.sentence: Ten percent can land like a pill: feed if it names a real risk, poison if it feels like proof he is already next. Hand the sibling the number as a dose of need for monitoring, not as a demand that he become a patient today.

2017-295.sentence: Undoing is the defense here: the compulsion tries to magically cancel the forbidden thought, then the thought returns and the loop restarts. Neurosurgical work on cortico-striatal-thalamo-cortical circuitry interrupts that cancel-and-repeat circuit when SSRIs, clomipramine, and ERP have already failed.

2017-296.sentence: The argument already replayed in the body: complete right-arm 'paralysis' after a fight invites you into a two-person debate about who is right. The face-hand drop answers a different question—if the falling hand still protects the face, the pair of you are living a conversion scene, not a clean corticospinal lesion.

2017-297.sentence: A prior puerperal psychosis is a vertical split waiting to reopen: after delivery the mind can leave ordinary reality without leaving the bed. Age, parity, and a hard labor matter less than that last postpartum break plus bipolar I—plan sleep, meds, and watchers around that history, not around the delivery note.

2017-298.sentence: This sits on Erikson's first task, basic trust versus mistrust: the infant has to learn that hunger can be named and soothed. A 15q copy-number variant in Prader–Willi hijacks that task—hyperphagia, hypotonia, and intellectual disability mean the body never becomes a trustworthy signal.

2017-299.sentence: The thank-you is doing work: it keeps you as a usable good object so the marriage can stay improved. Supportive technique accepts that gift—'I'm glad our work has helped'—instead of interpreting the credit or assigning homework that asks for more ego than this patient has.

2017-300.sentence: The mesolimbic path through the nucleus accumbens is a craving engine; cue plus dopamine outruns insight. Uncovering childhood will not hold this mind in early stimulant recovery—use support, cue control, and structure until that circuit is quieter.

2018-1.sentence: When the floor team reaches for a benzodiazepine the moment the withdrawing patient gets shaky, you are already in an enactment: two people repeating the old GABA-A solution instead of talking about it. Alcohol calmed anxiety, stole motor control, and put the lights out at that same receptor; the unit is now doing the same job with a pill.

2018-2.sentence: The frame here is the overnight study, not the patient's story: periodic limb movement disorder only shows up when someone else holds time, lights, and the recording while the sleeper is unconscious of the jerks. You do not treat "insomnia they report" as the whole case; you protect the limit that the polysomnogram—not self-report—names the arousals.

2018-3.sentence: The steroid is both feed and brand: it inflates the body while leaving hirsutism as a mark that will not reverse when the cycle stops. Infertility, impotence, gynecomastia, and testicular atrophy can recede; the hair does not, so the relationship to the drug outlasts the dose.

2018-4.sentence: Peek-a-boo only works once object permanence is in place: the parent can vanish and still be expected back. That is a limit you cannot rush—an infant who cannot hold the hidden other cannot yet use an ending, only a disappearance.

2018-5.sentence: Cerebellar damage shows itself mid-reach: intention tremor, dysmetria, and poor rapid alternating movements on the right, not at rest. Insight is the same skill—can they notice the miss while the hand is moving, and use a trial comment about the clumsy reach rather than wait for the nose.

2018-6.sentence: Mirroring here is not letting someone declare a "learning style" and skip the reading; that protects a brittle self-picture at the cost of competence. Add supplemental material aimed at every learner so esteem can rest on actually knowing the material, not on opting out.

2018-7.sentence: That line is not a passing worry; it is a schema, a standing rule that already “knows” she must outwork everyone before the hour can even be thought about. Your question about necessity is an attempt at containment—holding the raw dread of being seen as inadequate long enough for it to become a thought instead of more unpaid labor.

2018-8.sentence: Confidentiality is the barrier because school-based care sits where parents, teachers, and peers already have a claim on the adolescent’s story. What cannot be remembered or named as family shame is repeated as a refusal to walk in: the unsaid stays in the body of the program as empty appointment slots.

2018-9.sentence: Supportive psychotherapy names the goal as better ego functioning and self-esteem because this patient cannot yet stand a wish and a prohibition colliding in full view. You lend ego—structure, praise, reality testing—so drive and guilt do not tear through when memory work or exposure would only flood.

2018-10.sentence: Letter D is the habenular nucleus: epithalamus, posterior third ventricle, just above the pineal, not a nearby thalamic blob. Anatomy is a frame issue here—you hold the limit of what that letter is allowed to mean, the same way you hold time and the chart when a tumor board wants the structure named, not guessed.

2018-11.sentence: Fasciculations are whole-motor-unit pops on EMG with preserved strength and bulk; fibrillations are single-fiber noise and belong to a different story. Insight here is the capacity to use that finding as a trial comment: the twitch is visible firing, not proof of wasting, and the patient can look at the data instead of collapsing into the fantasy of ruin.

2018-12.sentence: Selective abstraction keeps only the unnoticed misstep and throws away the Broadway acclaim, as if the night had no other content. Termination thinking is useful here: she cannot yet let the performance end as a whole; the hour has to stay open around the one flaw so she never has to stop and take in that it was enough.

2018-13.sentence: A mental health court is a container: it holds the raw mess of psychosis-plus-trespass so the system can think instead of dump the person into jail. When the court cannot metabolize nameless dread about “the crazy offender,” it evacuates him into incarceration.

2018-14.sentence: Isolation of affect, intellectualization, and reaction formation keep the self from needing a mirroring other; the obsessive-compulsive patient feels competent by staying dry and precise. Warmth would feel like a leak in self-esteem, so the story of the divorce stays brilliant and bloodless.

2018-15.sentence: Following lorazepam users and nonusers forward for new dementia is a prospective cohort: exposure first, outcome later, no randomization. The drive-level wish is “benzos will soothe me now”; the prohibition is “they may steal my mind later,” and the design lets that collision show up as incidence.

2018-16.sentence: When contamination terror cannot be remembered as a story, the cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical loop repeats it as washing. OCD lives in that circuit because the unrepresented threat keeps firing as a motor ritual instead of a thinkable memory.

2018-17.sentence: Disulfiram plus alcohol recruits you into the punishing parent: flushing, headache, hyperthermia, tachycardia, and hypotensive collapse after a drink. Your countertransference may be “he got what he deserved,” which is the old alcohol-shame script, not a clinical thought.

2018-18.sentence: Ainsworth’s Strange Situation scores reunion after brief separation, not Piaget stages or theory of mind. A harsh inner conscience often sits in the toddler who cannot protest and then cannot be comforted—guilt already policing the attachment bid.

2018-19.sentence: Anti-Yo cerebellar degeneration is a late unmaking of coordination the child spent years building—gait and limb control drop out after the skill had already arrived. Order CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis next, because the hidden ovarian or breast tumor is what is stripping that capacity, not another brain picture.

2018-20.sentence: A nine-year-old whose attentional control never quite arrived on methylphenidate still has a stimulant-shaped gap, not a need to abandon stimulation. Try dextroamphetamine next; it is a different amphetamine mechanism, so you give that developmental function one more real chance before clonidine or guanfacine.

2018-21.sentence: Integrity versus despair in later life is whether this man can accept a longer male refractory period as ordinary aging rather than as proof that desire is over. Name that change plainly: the wait between orgasms lengthens; libido, sperm count, and testosterone are not the story you need to tell.

2018-22.sentence: Intimacy in a psychodynamic group is whole-object relating: members can hold good and bad in the same person instead of splitting the room into allies and enemies. That is the working group, after engagement and subgrouping, when people risk real disclosure and still stay in relationship.

2018-23.sentence: Laughing while children torment a cat is a collapse of depressive concern—the capacity to feel for the damaged other and want to repair. Frontotemporal dementia then fills the gap with paranoid-schizoid contamination fear about germs in food, while memory stays, which is why this is not Alzheimer disease.

2018-24.sentence: Biofeedback is a two-person loop: you and the patient watch the same autonomic signal and slowly change it together. Heart rate variability is that marker; the pattern is co-made in the room, not a number the body produces alone.

2018-25.sentence: A block used as a train means this 22-month-old can already hold “as if,” not just bang and mouth. That symbolic capacity is what later lets play and words carry feeling; until it is there, you stay more supportive and concrete than interpretive.

2018-26.sentence: In MS, bigger lesion volume tracks depression risk—this is wetware, not only grief about disability. Treat it as a hit to ego strength: less neural reserve for affect tolerance and impulse control, so you treat the mood aggressively rather than waiting for insight about illness.

2018-27.sentence: Primary process is unconscious thought that ignores logic, time, and contradiction—wish and image first. You listen for it in dreams and free association so you do not “correct” it as if it were a toddler’s attempt to control feeling or a map of attachment figures.

2018-28.sentence: Behavioral inhibition is temperament: this child withdraws from novelty and will be the one most at risk for later anxiety. Mirror the wariness without shaming it, and stay a calm idealizable presence so the toddler can borrow courage instead of collapsing into “I am defective.”

2018-29.sentence: The reporter wants you to metabolize nameless political dread by diagnosing a candidate you have never examined. The Goldwater Rule is refusal of that evacuation: no professional opinion on a public figure without a face-to-face evaluation.

2018-30.sentence: Untreated depression during pregnancy is the strongest risk factor for postpartum depression—stronger than hormones, SES, or marital strain. Treat now: the same depleted mind will be the infant’s first regulator, and you do not wait for delivery to start that work.

2018-31.sentence: The pair can enact an all-or-nothing night: you and the patient treat every hormone as equally wrecked by the schedule, instead of naming the split. Growth hormone rides sleep itself, not the clock the way melatonin and cortisol do, so the enactment is arguing about circadian doom while the real variable is whether they can still get a consolidated slow-wave stretch.

2018-32.sentence: At a lithium level of 4.2 you are no longer the secure base; nephrology and the dialyzer become the regulating other because the kidney cannot hold the ion. Lithium is dialyzable because of low molecular weight, not high protein binding, so proximity here is extracorporeal: you stay with the patient while the machine does the holding the proximal tubule failed to do.

2018-33.sentence: Iproniazid was an antitubercular that lifted mood before anyone had a depression indication, which is a lesson in ego strength: the mind sometimes uses a side effect as a new coping tool before theory catches up. Teaching that MAOI history is not trivia; it models affect tolerance for surprise, the same capacity you need when a patient's lift arrives from an unexpected channel.

2018-34.sentence: A positive Hoover sign (pressure under the “paralyzed” heel when they lift the good leg) means the pathway still works and the mind is converting exam-week conflict into a limp, not faking it. Early on, support the function and do not interpret the conflict hard; this ego is using a body story because it cannot yet use words, so uncovering the graduate-school fight can wait until the leg is walking.

2018-35.sentence: Stroking the sole and the patient yanking away is a two-person fight: you chase a plantar response and they make withdrawal the whole exam. Switch to downward scraping of the shin (Oppenheim) so you stop wrestling the foot and let the two of you cooperate on a stimulus that still asks the same corticospinal question.

2018-36.sentence: Parents and the 23-year-old can dump the unlived physician into each other: they carry his ambition, he carries their disappointment, classic projective identification until someone owns both halves. The developmental task is identity, not generativity; Klein would add that he cannot choose medicine or the coffee shop until he can feel depressive concern for the parent he might disappoint rather than split them into persecutors.

2018-37.sentence: The listener treated the radio voice as a whole good doctor-object—someone who already knew him and had prescribed—while parking the reckless four-milligram alprazolam binge in that same imagined pair. The court will not complete that split for him: without a real doctor–patient relationship, there is no containing other to sue, only a public comment and a friend with tablets.

2018-38.sentence: Working memory is the self’s brief holding tank: you keep the running serial-7 total (or WORLD spelled backward) in mind and still do the next operation. When that tank leaks, the patient does not just “forget a fact”; he loses the felt competence of staying organized in the moment, which is why the exam feels humiliating as well as cognitive.

2018-39.sentence: In a young adult, this internuclear ophthalmoplegia—failed adduction plus abducting nystagmus—is the body announcing multiple sclerosis, not a pontine infarct or a third-nerve story. The wish to treat it as a one-off toxin or stroke collides with the prohibition against denying a demyelinating disease that will keep returning.

2018-40.sentence: Slow titration of the antidepressant is the conscience of the prescription: you refuse the omnipotent start-high rescue that can spike activation and suicidal events in adolescents. Close early follow-up then lets the family use you as a thinking adult rather than as a guilty parent who either withholds all medicine or dumps a full dose overnight.

2018-41.sentence: The request to restore competence so the inmate can be executed recruits you into the executioner-healer: treat just enough psychosis to make death legally tidy. Your countertransference may be to “help” or to prove you are not soft; the AMA line is the interpretation—decline that restoration role unless a commutation is already in place.

2018-42.sentence: An illusion is a real stimulus—the rustling leaves—bent into hearing his name; nothing was generated from empty air. Name that misperception so you do not treat wind as a hallucinated other, and so a trauma-shaped mind is not forced to argue with you about whether the morning sound “really happened.”

2018-43.sentence: Sensitization is the nervous system turning the volume up: after a real harm, a weaker cousin of that stimulus now fires the same full fear response. The wish is to stay safe; the prohibition is on ever relaxing, so ordinary noise gets drafted as proof that danger is still coming.

2018-44.sentence: Naltrexone blocks opioid receptors so the drink no longer delivers the glow that props up a shaky self. Craving here is also a bid to borrow that glow instead of finding esteem in staying sober.

2018-45.sentence: Intellectual disability is the most common comorbidity in autism spectrum disorder, so you get cognitive and adaptive testing early rather than waiting for speech to 'catch up.' The child's raw overwhelm can look like nameless dread until someone contains it—holds the feeling long enough to name it as a thinkable skill gap, not a void.

2018-46.sentence: An indel is a small insertion or deletion in the DNA sequence, not an SNP and not a poetic RNA rewrite. Some facts just take the time they take: you cannot rush the genome into a cleaner story.

2018-47.sentence: Acknowledge the patient's fear without agreeing the plot is true; that is the trial comment you can make when insight is not available. Confrontation, buddy-talk, and locked-on eye contact all ask for a mind that can still look at itself—this one cannot yet.

2018-48.sentence: This is anorexia nervosa: restriction, low BMI, fat-phobia, and purging; regular menses do not cancel the diagnosis. The frame holds the medical limit—weight and safety—when the patient cannot hold it herself.

2018-49.sentence: The insula is where the patient first feels a pill as feed or poison: it is the cortex of interoception, folded in the lateral sulcus under the opercula, that registers gut, craving, disgust, and “something is wrong inside.” When you name that fold on the scan, you are locating the tissue that will later decide whether clozapine, lithium, or a sugar tablet is experienced as care or as an attack.

2018-50.sentence: Weekly CBC with differential after starting clozapine, with a baseline ANC of 2200, is not only REMS math; it is a ritual that says the drug is both lifesaving and capable of wiping out neutrophils. The blood draw does psychic work: it proves the patient is worth watching, and it binds the terror of agranulocytosis into a calendar instead of a nameless dread.

2018-51.sentence: At sixteen the job is identity versus role confusion: finding a self that can stand with peers and still be yours. Texting the same friends and a romantic partner, plus looking up sexual health, is how this kid is doing that work, so the likely outcome is continued socialization in the current peer group, not a collapse of individuation.

2018-52.sentence: One week after the crash, nightmares, insomnia, dizziness, pain, and fear of driving are the nervous system replaying what it cannot yet file as a finished story. That is acute stress disorder, not PTSD: the unrepresented impact is still happening in the body before a month has passed.

2018-53.sentence: Asking for a vitamin is often a bid to repair something felt as depleted rather than to dump the antidepressant. Vitamin D3 is the adjunct with evidence; you can join the wish to repair without handing over a magical object that replaces the work of the SSRI.

2018-54.sentence: Delirium is an unrepresented state: the old brain cannot make a narrative, so confusion shows up as pulling lines and a sudden change in attention. The Confusion Assessment Method is the quick bedside net for that, not MoCA or MMSE, which ask the patient to perform a mind they no longer have.

2018-55.sentence: Randomization already assigned you a role: chance, not a sneaky imbalance, produced any age gap in Table 1. The p-value column recruits you into a false countertransference—treating a lucky draw as a finding you must explain or correct.

2018-56.sentence: A harsh conscience often treats needing people as a moral failure, so the widower may hear 'stay independent' as the good path. Remaining in contact with friends is the healthier ethic: connection is not a lapse of character.

2018-57.sentence: Reading is a later-wired skill that can drop out while writing, an earlier motor-language habit, stays online. A left posterior cerebral artery stroke can disconnect visual word forms from language and leave alexia without agraphia.

2018-58.sentence: APOE*E4 raises risk for late-onset Alzheimer disease; it does not issue a date of death for memory. Testing cannot rush the ending she wants named in advance.

2018-59.sentence: The observational story soothed nameless dread—'the pill works'—instead of holding the messier thought that healthier people already take it. The RCT contained that raw hope long enough to show an unknown confounder, not failed blinding or company money, best explains the split.

2018-60.sentence: Her inner critic treats an imperfect note or shared slide as a crime, so highlighting and rewriting become atonement. Obsessive-compulsive personality disorder is that rigid conscience running the rotation: duty-hour violations and doing the group project alone feel safer than depending on peers.

2018-61.sentence: When a borderline patient misreads every pause as abandonment, they are recruiting you to become the mind that can hold both of you—the one who can still think “what is she feeling?” while they cannot. Mentalization theory is that capacity: using your own and the other person’s inner states as the explanation for the blow-up, instead of treating the blow-up as a fact about who they are.

2018-62.sentence: After an acute cortical insult, microglia do not sit still: their processes retract and the cell body swells so they can crawl, eat debris, and stand watch. That shape-change is the brain’s first immune act—the finding is doing emergency cleanup, not waiting for astrocytes or peripheral cytokines to take the lead.

2018-63.sentence: Parkinson psychosis is often a serotonergic story riding on a dopamine-starved motor system, so blocking D2 to quiet the hallucinations taxes the very circuits that still need dopamine. Pimavanserin is a 5-HT2A inverse agonist: it can take the edge off the visions and paranoia without stealing more motor function.

2018-64.sentence: High hypnotizability means the self can loosen its edges on command—attention, body, and “I” slide apart more easily than in schizophrenia or ADHD.
