In a dissociative disorder that same talent for absorption is already the illness: the person can leave the self so completely that memory and continuity do not hold.

2018-65.sentence: Adolescence is when unused synapses get cut so leftover feelings can become thinkable thoughts instead of raw discharge. Synaptic pruning in that window—not ventricular growth or less myelin—is the brain learning to contain impulse rather than evacuate it.

2018-66.sentence: A covering doctor who expects every long-term benzodiazepine to “creep up” is treating a fear as if it were a fact the body will enact. The finding is the opposite: most patients on chronic benzos, including a stable clonazepam, keep the same dose over time.

2018-67.sentence: Transient global amnesia blanks a few hours of new episodes while driving and ordinary answers stay intact—that is the finding doing a narrow job, not a faint, a seizure, or a posterior stroke. The three-hour return to baseline is the point: the hippocampus briefly stops filing the trip, then comes back online.

2018-68.sentence: Envy at the end of year two is a two-person emotion: the toddler can now hold “me” next to “the baby being held” and feel the gap. That grab for the toy is the dyad teaching comparison, not a plot to manipulate Mom.

2018-69.sentence: HIPAA already carved a hole in the frame for payment: the insurer can get what it needs to process the claim without a fresh authorization. You release billing-necessary PHI, not a teaching file or a research dump, and you do not treat the clerk’s ask as permission to uncover the whole chart.

2018-70.sentence: On this MMPI-2, high F and low L are not comments on the test’s construct validity; they are the evaluee’s test-taking attitude—over-reporting distress, little fake-good. L, F, and K exist to show how the person sat down to the booklet, which is the meaning of those flags in a forensic report.

2018-71.sentence: He is already well on bupropion SR 100 mg BID after many failed antidepressants, and the epilepsy has stayed quiet. Technique here is to support a working regimen, not to uncover a “safer” swap the insurer prefers—continue bupropion SR.

2018-72.sentence: Chronic inhalants punish the body while the habit keeps a sanctioned gap in conscience: diffuse atrophy, renal tubular acidosis, CPK 3120, hematemesis. The solvents were tolerated as if they were not a crime against the self until the CT and the kidneys objected.

2018-73.sentence: Pain (and temperature) rides the spinothalamic tract; vibration and joint position stay in the dorsal columns. That split is a developmental achievement: the cord learns two different ways to carry the body, and a hemicord lesion shows you which channel never made it through.

2018-74.sentence: Keeping the still-suicidal patient in hospital is the duty to treat, not the duty to cooperate with utilization review. Object relations here is simple: you stay the holding object while managed care becomes the abandoning one, and you do not split the patient out to please the payer.

2018-75.sentence: On the MSLT, narcolepsy shows itself as decreased REM latency: REM arrives almost as soon as sleep does. Technique follows the same rule—this is not a mind you uncover slowly; REM (and affect) break the surface before a supportive delay can form.

2018-76.sentence: The brain’s jump in size through year two is synaptogenesis, not more neurons or myelination as the main driver. Developmentally that is capacity arriving as connections, not as new cells: the toddler’s mind gets denser, then later pruning will thin what never got used.

2018-77.sentence: Patients stop SSRIs early most often for GI distress, not jitteriness or insomnia. Klein would hear the gut as the first stage for a bad object: the serotonergic pill is taken in as poison, and nausea is the body trying to spit the helper back out.

2018-78.sentence: Pathological laughing and crying is reported most in ALS (pseudobulbar affect), not MS or TBI. Ego strength fails at the output valve: the feeling inside is intact, but the cortex cannot hold or meter the laugh or sob, so affect spills without a self to own it.

2018-79.sentence: A two-year-old who prefers trucks and boys' clothes is trying on roles, not leaving her body or her sex. She still says she is a girl, so the work is with the parents' panic, not a diagnosis of a split in the child.

2018-80.sentence: Serial 7s asks whether this ICU patient can still hold a sequence in mind, which is the self staying assembled. When attention collapses, the self fragments: nurses become bank clerks and the night never ends.

2018-81.sentence: Endorphins in the periaqueductal gray take raw nociception and hold it so it can be felt as pain rather than dumped as panic. That is containment: the PAG's opioids metabolize an unthinkable sensation into something the mind can stay with.

2018-82.sentence: Lithium's useful act is putting a stop on glycogen synthase kinase-3, a kinase that does not know when to quit. The drug works by enforcing a molecular limit, not by adding more drive.

2018-83.sentence: Adrenal androgen production, adrenarche, is the first pubertal move, before gonadal estrogen or a GnRH pulse train. Pubic hair and odor without breasts is that early adrenal chapter, not a premature full story.

2018-84.sentence: GWAS hunts single nucleotide polymorphisms, one-letter spelling differences, not a gene that can be blamed. The conscience wants a verdict; SNPs only give a statistical crowd of tiny variants.

2018-85.sentence: When a 19-year-old is finally in the genital stage—libido up, parents down, a more adult self coming online—he will try to recruit you as either the parent he is leaving or the lover he is approaching. Notice who you become in the room: overprotective advisor or excited accomplice both tell you which old bond he has not finished renegotiating.

2018-86.sentence: The subcallosal cingulate is where unworded despair lives as a loop, not a memory: the mood cannot be recalled as a story so it keeps firing as a state. DBS there is an attempt to interrupt a somatic repetition the patient cannot represent, which is why talking about “why I’m depressed” often fails until the circuit quiets.

2018-87.sentence: Orexin deficiency lets the sleep-wish win the fight with the waking prohibition: REM barges in as sleep attacks, sleep paralysis, and hypnopompic hallucinations. The collision is physiologic drive versus the demand to stay upright at the wheel—same structure as a neurotic compromise, written in hypocretin instead of conflicted affect.

2018-88.sentence: Cluster headache splits the night: one side of the face weeps, injects, and stabs while the rest of the person is “asleep,” as if the body left without leaving the bed. The ipsilateral tearing and restlessness are not metaphor—they are a vertical split you can see, pain sequestered in one autonomic half while consciousness is only half present.

2018-89.sentence: Depersonalization/derealization is the ego thinning out: she keeps reality testing (she knows she is not a robot) but loses affect tolerance and ownership of thought and body. “Head full of cotton” and out-of-body spells mean the observing ego is still there while the experiencing self has gone offline—that is why it is not DID, PTSD, or BPD as the first call.

2018-90.sentence: Meaningful Use’s third pillar—electronic exchange of health information—is how an unremembered medical story gets carried by the system instead of being acted out as lost labs, repeated histories, and fractured care. When notes do not travel, the patient’s unrepresented illness gets repeated in the dyad: another doctor, same gaps, same body having to speak for what the record never held.

2018-91.sentence: The student's question recruits you as the one who will make dopamine in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex feel personally useful, not just a receptor lecture. Notice the countertransference tug to overpromise a clean story: working-memory fine-tuning is real, but it does not make you the savior of the patient's disorganization.

2018-92.sentence: The commercial panel arrives as a conscience-soother: if you order pharmacogenomics, you have done the thorough, guilt-free thing. Your job is to keep a working superego—promise of utility is not the same as replicated outcome data—so you do not buy moral cover for a test that still lacks that evidence.

2018-93.sentence: A well-demarcated CSF-density hole with ex-vacuo dilatation is a developmental leftover: the infarct finished years ago, and the brain never rebuilt that territory. New right-hand numbness is today's complaint; the CT is showing a capacity that already left the building.

2018-94.sentence: The five-minute curbside is doing work for everyone: the PCP gets an expert voice, you get to feel helpful, and the patient never has to become yours. Keep that meaning honest by leaving direction and prescribing with the PCP, so the consult stays advice rather than a stealth treatment relationship.

2018-95.sentence: REM sleep behavior disorder sits on Erikson's integrity-versus-despair line: the body enacts dreams while the person is losing the continuity of a coherent self. Years of dream-enactment before the Lewy-body memory drop is the stage announcing itself before the daytime identity can name it.

2018-96.sentence: Apraxia is a late loss of a skill that once arrived without thinking: blow-out-the-match is gone even though strength and sensation still work. You are watching praxis fail as a developmental achievement that old age can unmake, not as a motor or language deficit.

2018-97.sentence: Splice variants are one gene putting on different outfits: the same DNA sequence can be cut and joined in more than one way, so you get different proteins—and different psychiatric risk stories—from a single locus. In Kleinian terms that is not a mutation so much as a need to repair a split: the genome holds one object, then parcels it into isoforms so the mind (and the lab) can keep both a ‘good’ and a ‘bad’ protein in play without destroying the gene.

2018-98.sentence: Fluoxetine is the antidepressant you can actually defend in a seizure-prone patient; bupropion, maprotiline, amoxapine, and clomipramine all lower the threshold and invite a fit. Naming that risk is suppression, not denial: you keep the seizure danger in mind and choose the safer pill instead of acting as if depression were the only emergency.

2018-99.sentence: Erikson’s school-age task is industry versus inferiority: the child needs to feel personally worth something because he can do something, not because he is loved or looks right. When a nine-year-old quits every imperfect task, he is stuck in inferiority; the work is to restore competence as the currency of self-esteem, not to soothe him back into earlier attachment.

2018-100.sentence: Buying a stake in a patient’s startup is a boundary violation: money and treatment become the same relationship, and you can no longer hold the frame. Dual roles (small-town pharmacist, a holiday scarf, a sliding fee, talking about erotic transference) can be managed; becoming her investor cannot.

2018-101.sentence: Fragile X goes silent when the expanded CGG tract lets the FMR1 promoter’s CpG sites get methylated—the gene is still there, but the switch is taped off and FMRP is not made. Insight here is seeing your own part of the story: the sequence is not rewritten; the expression is. A trial comment to the family is just that—can they use the idea that ‘genetic’ and ‘epigenetic’ can sit in the same boy?

2018-102.sentence: Delayed ejaculation tracks the aging body: fast sensory fibers drop out and sex steroids fall, so climax—the ending—takes longer or does not arrive. That is a limit you cannot rush; naming the physiology keeps you from treating time itself as a character flaw or an SSRI until you have checked both.

2018-103.sentence: IBS is a classic evacuation: the gut dumps a feeling that never got a name, so mood and anxiety ride along at higher rates than they do in something as purely nociceptive as low back pain. Your job with the gastroenterologist is Bion's container—hold the dread in words long enough that the patient can think 'this is panic in the belly' instead of hunting another clean colonoscopy.

2018-104.sentence: The amygdala–hypothalamus–periaqueductal gray path is the self's emergency brake: when mirroring or competence collapses, the person cannot keep self-esteem together and the body fires a defensive strike. Remorse after the lash-out is the self coming back online and noticing it just tried to restore cohesion with a punch.

2018-105.sentence: The wish is to stay euthymic without another crushing depression; the prohibition is every agent that would wreck the kidneys, weight, or glucose—lithium, divalproex, olanzapine, quetiapine. Lamotrigine is the compromise formation that lets the wish live without paying the metabolic or renal price.

2018-106.sentence: The baby already holds more than one attachment, and they are not equal in intensity—so dad is not a spare part just because the cry still prefers mom. What cannot be remembered as a story is already being repeated in the body of each dyad; his daytime hours still write a second, usable bond if he stays reliably present.

2018-107.sentence: The dorsolateral prefrontal cortex is what lets you drop yesterday's sorting rule when the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test changes the game; when it fails, the patient keeps dealing you the old deck. In the room you feel recruited to be the rigid examiner who 'keeps changing the rules'—name that countertransference instead of joining the perseveration.

2018-108.sentence: HIPAA's conscience is strict here: identifiable charts for epidemiological research need specific authorization; treatment, payment, and operations do not cover a colleague's study. The temptation is a sanctioned gap in morality—'it's just QI-adjacent science'—and the superego job is to refuse the shortcut.

2018-109.sentence: Sensitivity is the developmental capacity of a screen: it grows so that almost no truly ill person is left unseen. A suicide-risk tool that maximizes that capacity accepts extra false alarms rather than leaving a real risk child off the list.

2018-110.sentence: Denial would say “any neuron could be hit,” and skip the enzyme. Tyrosine hydroxylase is the rate-limiting step to L-DOPA, so when it crashes the toxin is hitting dopaminergic cells, not GABA, glutamate, histamine, or serotonin.

2018-111.sentence: The consent ritual can become an enactment: the team performs autonomy while the patient still feels like a subject being processed. Belmont’s respect for persons is the brake on that repetition—informed consent only if the person is treated as an end, not a means.

2018-112.sentence: At five, typical sexual behaviors peak; that is not a child “leaving the room” into pathology. Dissociation would be a later split—the body acting while the mind goes blank—not preschool self-stimulation or curious looking.

2018-113.sentence: Ego strength in late life includes still being able to knit sleep. Spindle density falling most in frontal and occipital cortex is the biology of thinner affect tolerance and less restorative sleep, not a character flaw.

2018-114.sentence: Acetylation of histone tails is generally rapid and reversible; it is a limit you cannot rush past with one talk. Stress can loosen chromatin now, and the same mark can be taken back—PTSD is not a locked DNA sentence.

2018-115.sentence: The request to assay sertraline in milk and infant blood is often less about pharmacokinetics than about whether she can bear being a mother who needs a pill. A trial comment—“You want numbers so you are not the one deciding it is safe to treat yourself”—tests whether she can see her guilt instead of outsourcing it to the lab.

2018-116.sentence: After corpus callosotomy the left hand still knows the object; the speaking hemisphere never gets the report. That is a frame problem in tissue: the commissure was the only channel that let private knowing become shared, nameable experience.

2018-117.sentence: Pramipexole is not only a D2/D3 agonist for restless legs; it is a feed you hand the nervous system at dusk when it cannot settle. Watch whether she treats the tablet as proof her body is real, or as a demand that she finally be still.

2018-118.sentence: When mammillary bodies and the dorsal (mediodorsal) thalamus die from thiamine loss, the past cannot be laid down, so the mouth fills the gap with confabulation. What cannot be remembered gets repeated as a story invented on the spot, in the body and in the interview.

2018-119.sentence: CBT for persistent voices and delusions does not erase the drive; it asks what wish or threat the belief is carrying. The work is to let the forbidden idea be examined instead of lived as persecution.

2018-120.sentence: The Wisconsin Card Sorting Test asks whether a mind can bury a working rule and invent a new one when the world stops rewarding the old one. That flexibility is a developmental achievement: some people never quite got a parent who could change the game without collapse.

2018-121.sentence: Sickness behavior after pneumonia is not just “being tired”; microglial cytokine propagation is the brain’s way of forcing rest so energy goes to fighting the peripheral infection. When that signal overstays its welcome, the same withdrawal that once protected healing starts to look like depression.

2018-122.sentence: The family is not only asking for a pamphlet; they are asking you not to leave them holding the psychosis alone. Pointing them to the National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) names a third party that can absorb their rage, grief, and lobbying energy so you do not become the only parent in the room.

2018-123.sentence: Shortened REM latency is the night’s confession: the dreaming mind rushes the stage before the rest of sleep has done its work. That early REM surge often tracks a conscience that will not let the patient stay in the quiet of slow-wave sleep.

2018-124.sentence: A 22q11.2 deletion is not a moral failure, but it can feel like one to a teenager whose heart, palate, and thinking all “came up short.” The wish to be ordinary collides with a genome that already wrote a prohibition into development.

2018-125.sentence: Rescue benzodiazepines in the control arm are the unremembered extra: a hidden soother that never got named in the protocol. That is a confounding variable, and it is also how trauma studies fail—something calming happens offstage, then both groups look the same.

2018-126.sentence: FDG-PET is a picture of whether tissue can still metabolize glucose—whether the mind still has fuel to think. When frontal and temporal hypometabolism show up, raw affect has fewer cortical containers and more nameless evacuation.

2018-127.sentence: The family is asking the 2% that is the exome to do mirroring work: they want a coded, protein-level story that says this child’s mind still makes sense. Whole-exome sequencing can name a variant, but it cannot restore the parent’s shaken ideal of a competent, “complete” genome—so you hold that self-esteem wound while you explain how small the coding fraction actually is.

2018-128.sentence: Histrionic attention-seeking is proximity work: the other person has to stay visually locked on or the attachment system reads it as abandonment. Theatrical affect and provocative dress are not vanity first; they are a loud bid to use you as an external regulator when inner continuity is thin.

2018-129.sentence: Competency to stand trial lives in present ego strength: can this person still reality-test the charge and tolerate enough affect to work with counsel. Intent at the theft, Miranda, and treatment consent are other legal questions; here you are asking whether the observing ego can sit in a room with a lawyer without falling apart.

2018-130.sentence: After stimulants wrecked sleep and appetite, the family recruits you as the calm alpha-2 presence—guanfacine instead of another activating agent. Notice if you feel pressured to be the perfect non-stimulating parent: that countertransference is the wish that someone finally tone down arousal without taking food and rest away.

2018-131.sentence: Progressive supranuclear palsy writes the unremembered fall into the body: voluntary downward gaze is gone while doll’s-head maneuvers still move the eyes, so the brainstem, not a story, is repeating the drop. Mild rigidity without tremor and a normal MRI leave you watching a motor script the patient cannot put into words.

2018-132.sentence: Validity is the developmental arrival of “this tool actually sees depression,” not the earlier skill of giving the same number twice. Reliability across visits and raters can show up on time while the capacity to measure the intended construct still has not quite arrived.

2018-133.sentence: The anterior mesial frontal cortex talking to the insula is how we feel another person’s affect in our own body, which is also how a harsh conscience can hijack empathy and turn it into guilt. Watch that loop in yourself: you are not just naming their feeling, you are borrowing it, and the superego loves to punish what it just borrowed.

2018-134.sentence: OCD sitting with other anxiety disorders is Erikson’s industry-versus-inferiority leftover: the child who never trusted that good-enough work would be good enough keeps checking. The ritual is not only a symptom; it is a stalled attempt to prove competence so shame does not win the stage.

2018-135.sentence: The paraventricular nucleus dumping CRH is the body saying this moment is too much, so the HPA axis will carry the story the person cannot yet put into words. In clinic that surge is not just biology; it is the symptom doing the work of signaling danger when language has gone offline.

2018-136.sentence: Multiple copies of wild-type CYP450 alleles turn risperidone into smoke while the ward still looks at the patient as if he is refusing care. That is the paranoid-schizoid snap: the bad object is split off into “nonadherent him,” instead of staying in the depressive position long enough to repair the dose with genotyping.

2018-137.sentence: No two-word sentences by age 2 is a hearing-test moment, not a verdict on the family’s culture or how they talk at home. Identity can sit in the room as a third, but you still protect the child by testing ears first so class or language bias does not get to rename a medical delay as “how they are.”

2018-138.sentence: A cross-over design raises precision because the same person is both the treated body and the control body, which is how the pill becomes a relationship instead of a coin flip. Each subject swallows both arms; the study is asking them to be their own proof that the drug is feed, not just noise.

2018-139.sentence: Humor lets you say the hard thing without the ego collapsing: nicotine hijacks the α4β2 nicotinic receptor, so the “reward” is chemistry, not character. Name the receptor and varenicline’s partial-agonist trick, and the patient can laugh at the craving instead of denying it or acting it out with another pack.

2018-140.sentence: After a disaster the child’s wish is to stay glued to the parent; the prohibition is “you have to go back to life.” Peer support is the compromise that holds both: other kids let the wish for attachment live without turning the parent into the only safe object, which is why peers beat relocation, counseling access, or media validation as protection against post-traumatic symptoms.

2018-141.sentence: What you cannot remember about failing to get your alcoholic parent to quit is being repeated in this room: you lean, they stall, and the body of the treatment is the old scene. Countertransference is that leftover urgency—not the patient’s resistance—and it is why you insist “we are making progress” when the only change is your pulse.

2018-142.sentence: You are being recruited as the doctor who will finally name the unnamed child: after a normal microarray, exome sequencing is the study most likely to catch a rare-disease single-nucleotide variant. Notice the countertransference tug to overpromise a gene and stay the omniscient parent; the real frame is a next test, not a rescue.

2018-143.sentence: The dying patient’s conscience is already working overtime; a sudden move can feel like abandonment they “deserve.” An identified care person is the external ego that keeps the handoff moral and practical, which is why that person predicts a better transition more than older age, a non-cancer diagnosis, or a sudden change in health.

2018-144.sentence: Legal responsibility asks whether the person can see their own wish and still choose. The man with severe alcohol use who robs a liquor store for vodka is most likely responsible: intoxication he sought does not erase the act the way command hallucinations, severe intellectual disability under a father’s demand, or statutory-age mistake can.

2018-145.sentence: Tertiary prevention is the admission that the limit already arrived: quetiapine has already given this person diabetes, and you cannot rewind that. Metformin is the work you do after the ending you hoped to postpone — treat the damage, do not pretend the clock can be reset.

2018-146.sentence: Linkage analysis is a container: it holds the raw fact that some unknown gene is traveling with nearby markers until that fact becomes thinkable as a map. It does not sequence the gene; it watches how consistently variants pass from parent to offspring inside families, so the dread of “we have no idea where it is” can be metabolized into a locus.

2018-147.sentence: Collaborative care exists because specialty mental health cannot mirror every patient’s need for an available, competent other — the workforce simply does not have that capacity. The care manager and weekly caseload review restore a bit of idealized competence in the primary-care home instead of sending people into a waitlist that cannot hold them.

2018-148.sentence: When you and the patient are already living the split — one hour you are all-good, the next you are trash — that is an enactment: the old Kleinian pattern is happening between you, not just being described. The depressive position is the later capacity to hold one mother, one therapist, as both helpful and frustrating at the same time, which is exactly what this enactment has not yet allowed.

2018-149.sentence: High-voltage delta with slow rolling eyes on the PSG is N3, the stage where the cortex has almost gone quiet. Think of it as a massive suppression: waking thought is pushed down so far that only slow-wave sleep remains, which is why night terrors and sleepwalking live here rather than in REM.

2018-150.sentence: Intensive case management, with a caseload up to twenty and ACT-style outreach, contains the hospital as a dumping ground for unthinkable crisis. The evidence is modest and specific: length of stay shortens; suicide deaths, jobs, and metabolic syndrome do not magically improve just because someone is holding the panic.

2018-151.sentence: Spasmodic torticollis does not wait for insight or for gabapentin to slowly “settle” the neck; the muscle is already locked in a fight you cannot talk down. Botulinum toxin works by ending that motor demand at the neuromuscular junction, a hard limit: some contractions have to be chemically stopped, not waited out.

2018-152.sentence: Ask the parents one trial comment: “So the storm starts when a no lands, not out of the blue?” If they can use that, they are seeing a protest at a limit, which is oppositional defiant disorder, not a bipolar switch. Psychological mindedness here is noticing the trigger is the word no, not an endogenous mood cycle.

2018-153.sentence: You asked a CBT meaning question and she filled the hour with a chain that runs from one physics exam to exile from the family; that is catastrophic thinking, not a request to cancel the exam. Hold the frame: stay with the thought, name the leap, and do not collude by rescheduling reality so she never has to sit the test.

2018-154.sentence: Histamine from the tuberomammillary nucleus is the brain’s “stay awake” signal; an antihistamine sleep pill is not just sedation, it is taking away that wake feed. The next-day grogginess is the relationship cost of borrowing sleep by blocking histamine: you paid with arousal.

2018-155.sentence: Normal CT and MRI can become a defense of denial: “the pictures are clean, so the headache cannot be dangerous,” while the discs show papilledema. Idiopathic intracranial hypertension asks you to treat the pressure you cannot see on the scan, not the reassurance the empty images offer.

2018-156.sentence: Vertical nystagmus plus a clouded, agitated eighteen-year-old is phencyclidine, and the ED often answers with matching force: more holds, more shouting, more bodies. That is an enactment: the room starts living PCP’s fight instead of containing it with quiet, space, and benzos.

2018-157.sentence: He starts the sexual story, then blanks—the mind leaves the chair while the body stays. “You’re doing fine. Go on.” is a tether: you keep him in the room with the words instead of letting the split finish the sentence for him.

2018-158.sentence: The urge to invent a new handoff tonight is impulse, not ego. A protocol that counts missed shift-change handoffs is reality testing first—measure the hole before you try to fill it.

2018-159.sentence: Tying shoelaces is last because the child must sit with two hands, a knot, and frustration while you stay nearby as the secure base. Velcro and snaps let the parent finish the job; laces ask the child to use you for regulation, not for the bow.

2018-160.sentence: Major depression’s global burden is years lived disabled, not years cut short. The symptom’s “job” at scale is to keep people functioning just enough to stay alive and still too flattened to recover.

2018-161.sentence: Standard TMS for depression hits the left prefrontal cortex—the side that starts a plan instead of withdrawing from one. That is generativity versus stagnation in hardware: you are trying to restart the cortex that still says “I can do something.”

2018-162.sentence: In acute refeeding the starving superego—the inner prosecutor—is already running the unit; insight work just hands it more charges. Coach, support, and reinforce calories so conscience is not recruited as another reason she does not deserve food.

2018-163.sentence: Transvestic disorder is not a late-arriving gender identity; the erotic charge still lives in the garment, and that is a different developmental line from wanting to be the other sex. Distress here is shame about the fetish, not a child’s-then-adult’s conviction that the body is the wrong one, which is why gender dysphoria does not fit.

2018-164.sentence: Asking how the parents respond when the child is afraid of the bus locates the payoff: the symptom is doing work, not just ringing an old alarm. If fear reliably brings closeness, exemption, or a cancelled ride, the crash fantasy is being reinforced as a family signal, which is the operant story.

2018-165.sentence: An adolescent with anorexia often cannot yet use individual uncovering; the family has to hold the meals and the fight until that capacity returns. Family therapy beating individual work at 6–12 months is the clinical translation: more support now, better autonomy later, not a forever family treatment for adults.

2018-166.sentence: He is using projection, putting his own disowned doubt and hostility into the wife’s inbox and the friends’ “side,” then policing them as if the threat were outside. That pattern without a mood drop or a true delusion is paranoid personality, not delusional disorder: the jealousy is a character habit, not a break with reality.

2018-167.sentence: Noncontrast CT is a frame question first: do not lyse until you know you will not flood the brain. Excluding hemorrhage is the only job that scan must finish before you act; site of ischemia and salvageable tissue wait for later studies.

2018-168.sentence: Low energy, foggy concentration, and extra weight already tax this ego’s coping; bupropion leans on drive and attention without adding sedation or kilos. Mirtazapine and amitriptyline would buy sleep and appetite at the cost of the very functions that feel most depleted.

2018-169.sentence: Microglia stay in the cortex and still leave their day job: they flip from quiet housekeepers into inflammatory attackers without changing seats. That is a vertical split in tissue—same cells, another mode—so infection can rewrite cognition while the anatomy looks unchanged.

2018-170.sentence: The harsh conscience says methadone is a moral stain and that a “good mother” must detox for the fetus. Continuing methadone maintenance is the sanctioned gap: you refuse that guilt ritual because withdrawal and relapse hurt mother and baby more than staying on the agonist.

2018-171.sentence: Asking you about a bipolar mood app is a recruitment: you are being invited to become either the all-knowing endorser or the scolding parent who forbids it. Reviewing the app yourself, then discussing it, keeps you as a thinking partner instead of acting out that transference.

2018-172.sentence: Amnesia for everyday events is not just trauma-forgetting; it is the symptom doing identity work, carving ordinary hours into unowned time. PTSD can blank the assault; dissociative identity disorder blanks Tuesday, so another part can carry the day.

2018-173.sentence: Histamine H1 blockade puts the adult observing ego to sleep and hands the body back to appetite and drowsiness. Sedation and weight gain are that developmental rollback: food and rest become the available soothers once wakeful self-regulation is pharmacologically dulled.

2018-174.sentence: Non-judgmental noticing of inner and outer stimuli is a mirroring function: you treat each sensation as legitimate instead of grading it. That stance props up self-esteem until the patient can hold experience without the inner critic collapsing the self.

2018-175.sentence: Metacognitive therapy is a container: it takes raw, unthinkable fragments—jumping to conclusions, missed social cues, no sense of what your own mind can and cannot do—and names them so they can be thought instead of evacuated. Without that naming, the patient is left with nameless dread, the feeling that something is happening in the mind that cannot be known, only acted out as certainty or withdrawal.

2018-176.sentence: Lithium started as a gout salt and only later, via Cade, became a mood stabilizer; the body carried a use the mind had not yet represented. That is how unrepresented states work: what cannot be remembered as a story of mania and collapse gets repeated in urate, in tremor, in a metal that quiets the soma before anyone has a word for bipolarity.

2018-177.sentence: The six-year-old wants contact—friends, jokes, the teacher's greeting—and the prohibition is the missing pragmatic code: turn-taking, greeting, nonliteral speech. Social (pragmatic) communication disorder is that collision as a symptom: the wish to join stays intact, while the social rule that would make joining work is the part that cannot be used.

2018-178.sentence: Next-generation sequencing finds rare variants the way a second person hears the odd, once-only detail that pedigree charts, karyotypes, sib-pair studies, and GWAS average away. The method is interpersonal in spirit: you sequence this family, this rare event, not a one-person population mean.

2018-179.sentence: Cisplatin's distal sensory polyneuropathy is the body's unthinkable residue of treatment; the cotton-walking feet arrive before mood has a story. Uncovering “depression” first would miss the unrepresented state: what cannot be remembered as platinum toxicity is repeated as tingling, numbness, and a consult that looks psychiatric.

2018-180.sentence: Entrainment—tapping one hand at a different rate until the tremor locks to that beat—shows the body repeating what cannot be remembered from the family meeting. Psychogenic tremor is that unrepresented state in the dyad: the examiner's tap becomes the missing memory, and the limb follows instead of telling the story.

2018-181.sentence: Gerstmann’s cluster—agraphia, acalculia, right–left confusion, finger agnosia—can recruit you into becoming the patient’s missing angular-gyrus secretary: you start writing, calculating, and orienting for him. Name the countertransference when irritation rises (“he’s not even trying”); the dominant-parietal lesion is failing the task, not the man.

2018-182.sentence: Dextromethorphan sits in a sanctioned moral gap: cough syrup is “medicine,” so the adolescent’s conscience does not file “I’m walking on air,” hallucinations, and tachycardia as getting high. The superego (the inner prosecutor) stays quiet precisely because the bottle is OTC, which is why you ask about Robitussin before you write first-break psychosis.

2018-183.sentence: Fitness-for-duty is not therapy; the frame is a three-person room—you, the officer, and the department—so secrecy cannot be the usual clinical promise. Informed consent about the limits of confidentiality is how you keep from sliding into double agentry: serving two masters while pretending you have only one.

2018-184.sentence: The crack house is not a “temptation” speech; it is a conditioned stimulus that fires craving before intention shows up. Classical conditioning means the block does the wanting for him—Pavlov’s bell, not a character flaw—so the work is cue exposure and route change, not more lectures on willpower.

2018-185.sentence: The subiculum is the hippocampus’s exit ramp: CA1 hands the trace to it, and it ships the memory toward entorhinal cortex. On the schematic, that transition zone is c—miss it and you lose how a formed memory ever leaves the circuit.

2018-186.sentence: Morning headache, night sweats, and fighting sleep all day are not “more depression”; they are the airway collapsing and the brain paying the tax. Obstructive sleep apnea is the symptom doing metabolic work—hypoxia, arousals, unrefreshing sleep—so another antidepressant will not treat the pharynx.

2018-187.sentence: In Kleinian terms this is projective identification: the patient dumps the “I caused this” part into you and then swats away every return of it, so the shame never has to live in him. Narcissistic structure needs you to stay the stupid, attacking object; if you stay curious instead of collapsing or counterattacking, you are doing the repair he cannot yet do.

2018-188.sentence: Source monitoring—whether the news came from TV or the paper—is the first memory to wobble in healthy late life; suturing and his life story stay. Calling that slip “dementia” is displacement: he parks the surgeon’s terror of losing the knife-hand on a source-memory miss so he does not have to name ordinary aging.

2018-189.sentence: Event-related potentials can show that the sensory pathway still fires when the limb “cannot feel,” which unmasks conversion as a body-language of conflict, not a cut nerve. The finding is useful because it refuses the either-or the team wants: the symptom is real and it is meaning, not a fake and not a lesion.

2018-190.sentence: Epigenetic drift is age-linked change at genomic sites, not a family curse, and it is invoked for sporadic late-onset Alzheimer disease. The children’s question—“why her, why us?”—is attachment work: they want a heritable plot that keeps them either doomed-together or safely exempt, and drift answers that nobody’s loyalty caused this.

2018-191.sentence: Offering a quiet room or a calming med is two people rewriting the crisis instead of one mind “managing” a bad object. If you jump to IM haloperidol, threats, or restraints first, you and she co-author the old scene—someone overpowers, she proves the world is assaultive.

2018-192.sentence: Nonmaleficence here is technical humility: after failed psychotherapy and adequate med trials, more uncovering or another cocktail by guesswork is harm. The consult is the supportive move this treatment can actually use—another mind, not another probe.

2018-193.sentence: Linezolid is a weak MAOI, so pairing it with fluoxetine can dump two serotonin-boosting systems into one body and produce serotonin syndrome. In object-relations terms the medicine team holds only the “good” of treating the infection and you are handed the “bad” of the interaction; name both parts in the same conversation so the patient is not split into a safe infection and an unseen neurotoxic risk.

2018-194.sentence: Hyperactivity is the ADHD feature most likely to fade with age; inattention, impulsivity, school strain, and peer trouble often linger. Parents who hear that running-and-climbing will quiet can slip into denial, treating the quieter teen as “cured” while the sitting-still, homework, and social costs still need scaffolding.

2018-195.sentence: The suprachiasmatic nucleus, just above the optic chiasm, is the clock that sets and holds circadian sleep timing. A delayed-phase student who “just tries harder” at 10 PM is already in an enactment with the clock: the SCN will not negotiate, and the missed 8 AM class is the two-person fight between biology and the academic schedule.

2018-196.sentence: Genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder is involuntary spasm plus fear of penetration after a normal pelvic exam, not low desire or anorgasmia. In the room she leaves without leaving the chair: talking about the spasm itself is dissociated, so stay with the body fact (tightening, anticipatory anxiety, avoidance) until speech can rejoin sensation.

2018-197.sentence: Poverty of speech is brief, one-word answers with almost no spontaneous elaboration; that is not latency, echolalia, or a paraphasic slip. Ego strength here is thin affect tolerance and a shrinking working-through capacity: the 80-year-old cannot hold enough feeling or thought to fill a sentence, so you lengthen the pause instead of piling on open-ended demand.

2018-198.sentence: HIPAA allows you to share information when the patient lacks capacity and disclosure is likely to benefit care, even over a Capgras-like refusal that the parents are imposters. Developmentally this 21-year-old has not yet held a stable adult self who can use parents as allies; the delusion freezes that late-arriving capacity, so you speak with them as needed while you keep treating the psychosis that stole consent.

2018-199.sentence: The conscience in this search is the wish for a clean, sanctioned answer: pick the antidepressant that “works best” and you have done your duty. Effectiveness trials are the moral counterweight—they study messy adherence and comorbidity—so your guilt about imperfect patients gets a real-world study design instead of a purity contest with efficacy RCTs.

2018-200.sentence: CATIE’s “most effective” was not a solo-drug miracle; it was olanzapine surviving the two-person grind of stay-on-it versus stop-it, with the lowest discontinuation and longest time to stop. Effectiveness here is relational: the patient and the pill keep making a tolerable pair, not just a bigger PANSS drop in a vacuum.

2018-201.sentence: Do not interpret clumsy motor play in a two-year-old as if the corticospinal tracts were already fully myelinated and the child were “refusing” skill. Support first until about age 3, when those tracts typically finish myelinating; uncovering meaning of the clumsiness can wait until the hardware can carry the demand.

2018-202.sentence: The parents split “good boy” from “girly boy” and hand you the bad half as if the child’s play were a damaged object in the family. When the ten-year-old has no distress or impairment, the diagnosis is nonconformity to gender role—keep the good and the unconventional in one child instead of pathologizing the doll play as gender dysphoria.

2018-203.sentence: The spouse’s complaint that he “won’t get up and care” can feel like a projected deadness dumped into you—classic projective identification: you are made to hold the lifelessness. Name it as Parkinson apathy with stable slowness of thought on carbidopa/levodopa, not depression, so you repair the couple’s story instead of treating imagined guilt and sadness that are not there.

2018-204.sentence: The relapse two weeks after discharge is already an enactment: hospital no-smoking plus clozapine, then home plus cigarettes, and the old psychosis walks back in. Resumption of heavy smoking induces CYP1A2 and drops clozapine levels—talk about the smoke, not a mythical treatment failure.

2018-205.sentence: Sleep that will not stay put is a nightly uncoupling: the mind leaves the night without leaving the bed, so the day never gets a continuous self to work with. Persistent SWAN depression tracks that split more than obesity, marriage, menopause, or even childhood maltreatment, because the body keeps rehearsing absence instead of rest.

2018-206.sentence: Late life often buys a thicker ego: more affect tolerance, slower impulse, better reality testing when the old storm starts. That is why personality disorders, not anxiety, depression, substances, or somatic symptoms, drop with ordinary psychosocial maturation—your 60-year-old borderline did not vanish; she can stand the feeling longer.

2018-207.sentence: Attachment is a wiring problem: the other person is the secure base that lets you risk a new link instead of a new cell. Synaptic connectivity, not neuronal number, size, pruning, or migration, is how learning and memory actually rewire—therapy is proximity that changes which synapses get used.

2018-208.sentence: The superego is the inner inspector that also patrols energy production: methylation enzymes sitting in mitochondria, not only the nucleus, Golgi, ER, or vesicles. Conscience can mark the power plant itself, so guilt is not just a nuclear memo—it can change how the cell pays its bills.

2018-209.sentence: Those long, suppressible, talking limb-shakes recruit you as the neurologist who must either catch a seizure or catch a lie. Insidious onset—not mood comorbidity, a clear stressor, high IQ, or a short wait to treatment—predicts a worse functional-neurologic course, because the two of you inherit a symptom that never announced itself as a conflict.

2018-210.sentence: Late light is a failed coping move: the ego tries to treat winter mood and instead shoves the clock later, so sleep onset and wake time drift the wrong way. Morning light advances phase; evening exposure from the borrowed box delays it—impulse to 'just use it whenever' overrode the timing that change actually requires.

2018-211.sentence: Levetiracetam can sit next to carbamazepine and your planned mirtazapine without joining their enzyme conversation. That is a vertical split in the pharmacy: the new drug occupies its own lane while the old metabolic systems keep running as if nothing else is in the chair.

2018-212.sentence: Moving the hour to a coffee bar after hours is already an enactment: the two of you are living the wish to make treatment feel less clinical instead of talking about why the clinic feels unbearable. The frame is the treatment; once you leave it, you are no longer doing the work you were hired to do.

2018-213.sentence: Handing over the PHQ-9 is a quiet use of suppression: you park the gut-level “I think they are better” so nine DSM depression items can speak first. The score is not the person, but it keeps you from treating hope as evidence that sertraline is working.

2018-214.sentence: A four-month-old who still wakes through the night is not rejecting the mother’s feed; adult-like circadian sleep is not due until about six months. The pill here is time itself: the body has to mature its clock before night can feel like a reliable holding.

2018-215.sentence: Atomoxetine’s black-box warning for suicidal ideation in children is the limit you hold with the parent, not a detail you bury because stimulants “always work.” You name the risk in the same breath as the tic-friendly reason you chose a non-stimulant, so consent stays a frame, not a sales pitch.

2018-216.sentence: Ask whether he can see that the fear arrived after a successful bone marrow transplant, when leaving the unit means losing the staff who kept him alive. If a trial comment like that lands, you have adjustment anxiety with some insight, not a personality that was always this dependent.

2018-217.sentence: Anxiety in boys can work as a developmental brake: it holds first intercourse until after 18 instead of letting peer time set the clock. That delay is a limit, not a failure—the capacity for a sexual beginning cannot be rushed just because a father wants his son caught up.

2018-218.sentence: A posterior cerebral artery infarct takes one occipital field and leaves a hole in seeing, not a vague “neuro change.” The hemianopia is doing work: it drops half the world, and the patient may fill that hole with denial unless you name the PCA territory.

2018-219.sentence: At 25 this body-dysmorphic preoccupation sits on Erikson’s intimacy-versus-isolation task: you cannot bring a face to someone if that face feels like a fake. Fluoxetine treats the obsessive grip on the imagined defect so identity can stop organizing around the mirror.

2018-220.sentence: Avoidance is the defense: skip the cafeteria seat and the speech and you never have to survive being looked at. The blushing and twitching still leak the shame social anxiety is trying to hide, which is why the picture is not panic, phobia, or schizoid withdrawal.

2018-221.sentence: Calling Broca’s aphasia “confusion” is already an enactment: the two of you are living the old pattern of treating a stalled speaker as lost rather than as a man who understands but cannot get the word out. If you finish his sentences, you repeat that rush instead of waiting for the nonfluent, poorly repeating speech.

2018-222.sentence: Once you feel flattered and attracted, the frame is already under load—fee, time, and the incest taboo of the dyad no longer hold themselves. Consultation is who holds the limit: you do not decide alone whether to lean in, pull back, or end, and you do not tell her the erotic transference “isn’t real.”

2018-223.sentence: In a crossover, the first pill is never fully gone when the second arrives, so residual effects turn the drug into leftover feed or leftover poison still sitting in the body. That carryover is the design’s real cost: you cannot tell whether today’s response is today’s treatment or yesterday’s unfinished demand.

2018-224.sentence: Response inhibition lives in the anterolateral orbitofrontal cortex–anterior putamen–thalamus loop, and it is a limit, not a pep talk. You cannot rush that circuit the way you cannot rush an ending: the stop signal has to arrive in time, or the compulsion keeps going.

2018-225.sentence: Schizotypal personality sits on the schizophrenia spectrum, so odd beliefs in the patient may be a family signal, not just a private quirk. A trial comment tests insight: can they look at their own magical thinking, or does naming it feel like an attack?

2018-226.sentence: The Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale is an interview, so the clinician’s gaze does the mirroring that a checklist cannot. In active psychosis, self-report (SCL-90, BSI, MCMI, MMPI) often fails because the self that would rate itself is not stably there.

2018-227.sentence: Fear of dying in pain is raw sensation that has not yet become a thinkable thought, so it arrives as nameless dread. Containment here is naming the pain plan, not a vague “we’ll take care of you,” so the dread can be held instead of evacuated into the team.

2018-228.sentence: Depression is the most common neuropsychiatric symptom in mild neurocognitive disorder, and it often shows up as lost interest before a story of loss can be told. What cannot be remembered as “I am slipping” is repeated as a flat mood in the body and in the family.

2018-229.sentence: The body is not being lazy at 4 a.m.; the wish to stay on shift collides with a hard physiologic veto when melatonin peaks and core body temperature hits its nadir. That collision is the crash—temperature, not pulse or saccades, is the clock that wins.

2018-230.sentence: Informed consent is an adult capacity: a real yes and a real no. “Sign in voluntarily or I will commit you” treats the manic patient as if that capacity never arrived, so the signature is not consent—it is a child’s forced choice.

2018-231.sentence: A WISC full-scale IQ of 60 names a score, not a life. The Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales ask what the low IQ is doing in daily function—communication, self-care, social skill—because intellectual disability is that lived deficit, not the number alone.

2018-232.sentence: A candidate-gene paper is recruiting you to become the parent who says “yes, that one gene explains everything.” Your countertransference hunger for a clean cause is the same bias that makes those studies throw off false positives.

2018-233.sentence: Extreme delta brush plus anti-NMDA antibodies is not a moral collapse you should punish with more seclusion. Look for the ovarian teratoma; the conscience that wants a “bad patient” story is the part that misses the tumor.

2018-234.sentence: The wish is to be the kind neighbor who fixes the fluoxetine while his doctor is away. Advising a dose increase is where that wish beats the prohibition—and that specific medical order, not the barbecue chat, is what creates a doctor–patient relationship.

2018-235.sentence: An underpowered trial cannot hold the effect in mind; the real difference stays unrepresented and only “shows up” later as a failed study you keep repeating. Power analysis is the pre-enrollment act of giving the sample a body big enough to remember an effect of known size and variance, instead of evacuating it into another null RCT.

2018-236.sentence: The arcuate nucleus is the container: it takes raw nutrient and gut-pancreas-liver-fat-brainstem signals and metabolizes them into a thinkable hunger or satiety command. When an antipsychotic floods that circuit, appetite becomes nameless dread in the body—weight gain you cannot think until you name the arcuate.

2018-237.sentence: Calling you a “wise and loving doctor” is an idealizing selfobject need: she is borrowing your shine to hold a shaky self together. In supportive work you use that idealization to strengthen the alliance; you do not puncture the mirror just to prove you are modest.

2018-238.sentence: Psychological mindedness here is yours: can you trial-link sertraline to SIADH instead of treating fluctuating attention as “new dementia”? Serum electrolytes are the insight test—hyponatremia is the patient’s part of the story that a plasma level or DST will not show.

2018-239.sentence: After 65, sleep’s frame has already ended: more fragmentation, more arousals, less slow-wave sleep. You cannot terminate aging with a hypnotic any more than you can rush a capacity that time has already limited.

2018-240.sentence: Saturday-night palsy recruits you as either the scold or the neurologist: the radial nerve was compressed on the chair, wrist and finger extension gone, grip spared. Notice the countertransference pull to moralize the drinking; name the radial lesion first so you are not living the lecture instead of examining the wrist drop.

2018-241.sentence: Epigenetics is how an unrepresented trauma still writes on the body: methylation and histone marks change what genes fire without rewriting the DNA sequence. The patient is not inventing a genetic scar; she is describing a memory that never became a story and so lives in regulation instead.

2018-242.sentence: PMDD is timed to the late luteal week because that is when the hormonal swing and the wish–prohibition clash land in the same body: irritability and mood drop as a conflict, not as a random PMS week. Charting across cycles keeps you from treating one angry fortnight as character when the drive pressure is cyclic and nameable.

2018-243.sentence: Erikson’s stages are sequential because the self needs a new mirroring job at each crisis; identity versus role confusion is the adolescent’s need to be seen as a coherent someone, not a pile of roles. If that mirroring fails, she withdraws not from “laziness” but from a self that has no confirming other to lean on.

2018-244.sentence: Incidence is the new-case rate over a defined interval, which is how you contain a raw QI panic—how many people fell ill again—into something thinkable. Prevalence just counts who is already in the bed; it evacuates the question instead of holding it.

2018-245.sentence: Conservation of volume arrives in Piaget’s concrete operational years, roughly seven to eleven; you cannot rush a six-year-old past that limit any more than you can terminate a treatment before the work is thinkable. The taller glass “winning” is not stubbornness; it is a mind that has not yet got time and quantity as durable facts.

2018-246.sentence: A glucocorticoid receptor is nuclear: the steroid has to go inside, bind DNA, and wait hours, unlike a benzo’s ligand-gated ion channel. Insight works the same way—a trial comment only lands if the patient can take it in and rewrite a bit of inner text, not if you expect a same-second flip.

2018-247.sentence: The C-L request for a fast benzodiazepine is the ward asking you to drop the frame: a pill that quiets the nurse more than it protects the lungs. Buspirone is how you hold the limit—you treat the anxiety without handing COPD a respiratory depressant.

2018-248.sentence: The visit cap is not a clinical judgment; it is the insurer shrinking the treatment frame for psychiatry while medicine stays open-ended. MHPAEA is the statute that says you do not accept a thinner benefit just because the illness is in the mind.

2018-249.sentence: By four, the child can keep two objects of the same toy: the one she sees and the one still sitting in the other person's mind. That is theory of mind as object relations—good enough development means she no longer assumes her inner picture is the only reality in the room.

2018-250.sentence: Rett is not a child “checking out”; MECP2 failure erases skills the girl already owned. Development here runs backward: speech, hand use, and autonomic regulation fall away after a period of ordinary growth.

2018-251.sentence: Pregnancy trained everyone to chase a higher lithium dose; delivery suddenly returns the old clearance and that old dose becomes a toxicity script. Cut the lithium when the placenta comes out so the postpartum kidney does not finish a story written for a larger plasma volume.

2018-252.sentence: The mind walls off the ambush and leaves the rest of memory standing—that is repression working locally, not a global amnesia. Dense gaps limited to a few traumatic episodes are the defense succeeding: the war is gone from recall while new learning still works.

2018-253.sentence: Schwann cells wrap one peripheral axon apiece; oligodendrocytes share many CNS axons. That is two different kinds of feed: a one-to-one wrap that can remyelinate, versus a shared wrap that, once lost, is much harder to restore.

2018-254.sentence: Corticosteroids turn up physiologic tremor; they do not create a new tremor disease. Name the steroid first and support the alarmed patient; do not uncover “hidden anxiety” in a hand that is pharmacologically faster.

2018-255.sentence: Core gender identity is usually in place by three years, so the child’s consistent self-label is already a two-person fact, not a future maybe. The work is with the parents’ alarm, not with “correcting” a three-year-old who has already told you who she is.

2018-256.sentence: The fusiform face area (ventral temporal, choice E) is how the cortex knows a particular face, not a voice or a name. Attachment needs that patch: without it the secure-base person is still there by sound, but the face that should regulate you will not light up.

2018-257.sentence: Two yes/no boxes—parental depression and child anxiety—want a chi-square, not a t-test or a Pearson r. Ego strength here is affect tolerance for a simple association: do not reach for logistic regression just to look more powerful than the data.

2018-258.sentence: A thunderclap plus a red, mid-dilated, painful eye is acute angle-closure until intraocular pressure says otherwise. Measuring pressure is a mirroring move: you take the catastrophic self-state seriously and then show the patient the actual organ that is screaming.

2018-259.sentence: Quality of parenting is the adult who can hold the child’s rage and need without collapsing, so the wish to be kept safe does not have to fight a parent who is also the source of danger. Resilience is not IQ or an easy temperament winning; it is that collision getting metabolized in a real relationship.

2018-260.sentence: PACAP is the molecule that keeps the cell from executing itself when NMDA and PARP have already started the death cascade—containment at the membrane. Nameless dread in the dish is apoptosis: raw excitation that never gets named as a survivable signal, only evacuated as cell death.

2018-261.sentence: The Conners CPT is a clock you cannot charm: it asks the child to stay with boredom for the full run, not to look smart on the Wisconsin or pretty on the Rey–Osterrieth. Sustained attention is a limit; you measure whether the mind can endure time, not whether you can rush a diagnosis from a school note.

2018-262.sentence: The wish to protect the child and the prohibition against “harming” them with a shot collide; CDC facts do not dissolve that fight. Tie vaccination to the group’s own values and the wish and the rule can sit in the same sentence instead of splitting into anti-vax versus science.

2018-263.sentence: Decentration is the child giving up the grandiose job of having caused the divorce; the self no longer has to be the omnipotent center to feel real. He can stay sad and angry and still keep a self that is not wrecked by blame—mirroring that he is a person in the story, not the engine of it.

2018-264.sentence: Alcohol hits the nucleus accumbens the way a perfect feed would: dopamine says the relationship just happened, even if the bottle is the only other party. The pill—or the pour—becomes proof of need and poison at once; craving is the demand that this object keep supplying the bond.

2018-265.sentence: The team is using acting out: they dump the terror of untreated first-episode psychosis into a steep titration instead of naming how hard it is to wait. Rapid dose escalation is what turns that enacted urgency into akathisia.

2018-266.sentence: A trial comment can ask whether she can own both parts of the story: estrogen falling and inflammatory cytokines rising, plus whatever meaning she gives the perimenopausal or postpartum window. Psychological mindedness is seeing that the cytokine shift is real without using it as a way to skip her own feelings about the drop.

2018-267.sentence: The mental health court holds the limit: legal leverage is the frame that gets participants into community treatment faster, not a cheaper system. Ethics means saying that out loud so families are not sold cost savings or a guaranteed drop in re-arrest as the proven outcome.

2018-268.sentence: Reality testing has to take in a three-month collapse, startle myoclonus, and 1-Hz periodic sharp waves, not the years-long Alzheimer's story the family brought in. Ego strength here is affect tolerance: you sit with Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease without rushing them into false hope or frantic, useless procedures.

2018-269.sentence: Atropine is a bodily secure base: it blocks the vagal surge at the electrical stimulus so bradycardia and asystole do not take the patient down. You stay the regulating other in the suite so they are not left alone with that parasympathetic crash.

2018-270.sentence: A wish to have Hindu meanings count collides with a prohibition against bringing those explanations into a Western first visit. Asking what he believes explains the weakness, palpitations, and suicidal ideation lets that wish speak instead of forcing the conflict into an instant major-depression script.

2018-271.sentence: A heavier burden of CNVs is the genome’s version of an unrepresented state: too much structural damage, not a tidy named lesion you can remember as a story. The body and the family then repeat what cannot be narrated—disability, dysmorphism, the need for microarray—because the injury never became a thinkable memory.

2018-272.sentence: Content validity is containment: the test has to hold the whole raw domain, not just one loud fragment, so the feeling can become thinkable instead of being evacuated as a single item. If your depression screen never samples anhedonia, sleep, or suicidality, the leftover bits stay nameless dread and leak out of the instrument.

2018-273.sentence: Illness anxiety here is a failed idealizing search: the cousin who died of a brain tumor is the terrifying parent-object, and each new MRI is a bid to restore a competent, mirroring doctor who can make the self feel intact. Almost no somatic symptoms means the wound is in self-esteem and safety, not in a body part asking to be interpreted.

2018-274.sentence: After about age six, the growth of neural language synapses slows, so the child’s capacity to take in an entirely new language arrives late or only in part. Vocabulary, grammar, and context-guessing can still thicken; the missed window is the deep synaptic readiness that once made a first language feel effortless.

2018-275.sentence: Leptin from adipose tissue is the body’s telegram that stores are full; olanzapine muffles that signal, so hunger becomes the symptom that does the talking. The extra eating is not only drive—it is a message that the satiety line from fat to brain has been cut.

2018-276.sentence: USPSTF data put the highest depression prevalence in the previously married; the divorced patient who minimizes mood may recruit you as the leftover spouse who must not notice the grief. Your countertransference urge to shrug it off is the old couple’s pact: do not name the loss.

2018-277.sentence: The grocery store is now a stand-in for danger, and the conscience can treat avoidance as a moral duty: stay out or you were reckless. Lorazepam soothes the panic, but it also licenses a tidy gap—chemical permission not to face the store, while the crash and the panic remain the unconditioned truth.

2018-278.sentence: De novo mutations let a devastating illness appear with no family story, and the consult can become an enactment: you and the parents start hunting a hidden ancestor instead of sitting with chance. That is an enactment—the two of you are living a blame-search instead of naming a new mutational event that fertility never selected against.

2018-279.sentence: Calling the 10 percent uniquely broken is denial: the mind erases how common suicidal ideation is among medical students so the group can stay exceptional. Humor or suppression can hold the same number later; first the defense has to stop pretending the statistic does not apply here.

2018-280.sentence: Memantine’s NMDA-receptor antagonism is not just a synapse trick; it is a damper on glutamatergic noise so the remaining self can still recognize a face. The pill’s meaning is a modest holding of chaos—less excitotoxic flood, more room for donepezil’s acetylcholine to do its work.

2018-281.sentence: When Winnicott’s holding environment never quite arrives, the infant builds a false self: a compliant surface that manages the mother instead of showing real need. Grandiosity and idealization of self-objects belong later; here the developmental failure is early, and the defense is to become what the caregiver can bear.

2018-282.sentence: Suicide as the leading trigger of psychiatric malpractice claims is also a superego crisis: the field treats a death as proof the doctor failed a duty of care. Sexual misconduct shocks the conscience louder, but the common lawsuit is the one that says you should have prevented the unpreventable.

2018-283.sentence: When D2 blockade barely moves the negative and cognitive picture, you can feel recruited into the old dopamine-only doctor: do more blockade, or give up. Glutamate dysfunction (NMDA hypofunction) is the more complete model of the syndrome; name that so your countertransference of futility does not become another untreated negative symptom in the room.

2018-284.sentence: A normal CT plus new aphasia can pull the team toward calling it functional, which is a collapse of reality testing under time pressure. Diffusion-weighted MRI is the early test of cytotoxic edema; hold that finding as the ego function that checks the impulse to diagnose by vibe.

2018-285.sentence: The attack that you are controlling and uncaring is projective identification: the patient evacuates a harsh internal object into you and then treats you as if you already are it. In Kleinian terms this is paranoid-schizoid transference, not a request that you prove you are nice; interpret the need to park the bad object in you rather than argue the charge.

2018-286.sentence: Lowest 12-month alcohol use disorder in Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders, partly via ALDH2 variants, is a group statistic, not a permission to under-screen the person in front of you. Race and culture sit as a third in the room: if you assume this patient 'doesn't drink,' you have used the epidemiology as a stereotype instead of a prior.

2018-287.sentence: Freud's latency lines up with Erikson's industry versus inferiority: the job is competence at school and with peers, not another oedipal showdown. School refusal at eight often means the child is losing that industry battle and taking on inferiority; frame the work as restoring mastery, not just getting him through the door.

2018-288.sentence: A positive allosteric modulator like a benzodiazepine only boosts GABA-A when GABA is already there; it does not fire the receptor on its own the way a barbiturate can. Think of ego strength the same way: you amplify affect tolerance and impulse control that exist, you do not replace a missing signal with a knockout dose.

2018-289.sentence: Dissociative amnesia with major depression is a proximity move: the mind drops an unbearable stretch of autobiography so the attachment can stay intact. Unlike Alzheimer retrograde loss, Wernicke-Korsakoff anterograde loss, or the anesthetic gap, this forgetting is reversible once the relationship can hold the affect again.

2018-290.sentence: Williams syndrome (7q11.23 microdeletion) wires a mind that treats almost every face as already familiar. Developmentally that hypersociability is not “good personality”; it is a missing brake on stranger-approach, so you still have to teach safety even while you enjoy the warmth.

2018-291.sentence: A preschooler facing leukemia does not yet live in Klein’s depressive position, where death is a real, permanent loss you can mourn. Absence of the caretaker still feels like annihilation of the good object, so the fear to name is separation, not afterlife or disappointing the parents.

2018-292.sentence: Ninety percent of U.S. girls reach menarche by 14, so a 13-year-old without a period is still inside a normal timeline, not a “broken” body. Hold the girl’s sexual body as ordinary and unfinished rather than splitting it into a good child versus a late, defective one.

2018-293.sentence: Malpractice needs the whole chain: duty, breach of the standard, damages, and that the breach caused the harm—not malice and not a deviation sitting there unused. After a complaint, support the working ego with that four-part test; do not uncover “what kind of doctor am I” as if intent were the legal question.

2018-294.sentence: A microarray for CYP sequence variants names a two-person mess you were both living: she looks intolerant, you look like a clumsy prescriber. Once poor metabolism is on the table, the pair can stop repeating “nothing works / I cannot help you” and dose to the enzyme instead of to the drama.

2018-295.sentence: By five years a typical child can answer why, when, and how because language has become a way to keep a caregiver close as a thinking partner, not just a body in the room. Those questions are proximity-seeking with words: the child uses you as a secure base while the mind goes out to explore cause and time.

2018-296.sentence: This man has already shown failed impulse control and thin affect tolerance: bipolar illness, cardiac ischemia, a violence record, and a named plan to hunt an ex and “teach her a lesson.” Most states require you to inform the police because his ego cannot be trusted to hold the rage, so the frame has to hold it for him.

2018-297.sentence: “If I didn’t smoke, I could use the money for music” is change talk because the patient is giving the habit a competitor that actually matters to him. Smoking is no longer just a habit; it is a symptom with a price tag, and music is the meaning that starts to argue against it.

2018-298.sentence: Valproate inhibits histone deacetylase, so acetyl groups stay on histones and the DNA stays loosely packed enough to be read. That is a developmental story at the chromatin level: genes that would have been locked shut stay available for transcription.

2018-299.sentence: Parental death by suicide, homicide, or accident in early childhood hits before mourning is a usable defense, so the child often relies on denial or identification rather than grief that can be thought. By young adulthood that unfinished loss shows up as depression because the mind never got a chance to metabolize the death in words.

2018-300.sentence: Absent gross negligence, dereliction of duty is not proved by a bad lithium outcome or by the injured patient’s story; it is proved by expert witnesses saying what a reasonable psychiatrist would have done. The courtroom borrows the field’s superego—the shared conscience of the specialty—and asks another doctor to speak it aloud.

2019-1.sentence: Lack of insight is doing work: it keeps the gangrene from becoming *his* problem, so he never has to authorize losing the limb. Appreciation fails first because knowing would collapse the last defense against a mutilating choice.

2019-2.sentence: A pedigree is built to catch a rare high-penetrance variant—the mutation that behaves like a family fate, not a common SNP that only slightly tilts risk. That is development written in DNA: one lineage handing the child a nearly unavoidable illness instead of a probabilistic nudge.

2019-3.sentence: Left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex is the strip that can still plan, inhibit, and stand a little outside the mood. rTMS is asking that executive self to come back online; you are not zapping the amygdala or the ventral striatum.

2019-4.sentence: Attentional bias toward threat is a drive compromise: a wish is still scanning for an object, and the prohibition has turned every frown into possible punishment. Depression does not hunt that way; it has already declared the wish hopeless and stopped looking.

2019-5.sentence: Label B, the insula, is the cortex that maps the inside of the body when there is still no story. What cannot be remembered often shows up here first—as raw interoception folded in the lateral sulcus, not as a narrative.

2019-6.sentence: The Jendrassik fist-clench recruits the patient as an ally so a silent reflex can appear. Notice your need for their body to answer you; that is countertransference, and the maneuver uses it instead of letting you over-call areflexia.

2019-7.sentence: Cardiovascular disease is the conscience of this visit: the “good patient” on clozapine who never missed a refill can still die of BP 158/96, glucose 142, high LDL, and a pack a day while you and he treat those numbers as optional extras. That is a sanctioned gap in morality—psychosis gets the full ethical heat, and the heart is allowed to fail off-stage.

2019-8.sentence: Sumatriptan four days a week is a trial comment she already answered: she can see each attack, not the pattern that made prophylaxis necessary. Offer topiramate as the next trial—can she use a daily preventive instead of living only in the abortive moment?

2019-9.sentence: Methylation is a termination you cannot hurry: it closes the DNA so the transcriptional machinery cannot get in, and gene expression stays down. Heritability without a sequence change is the same limit—some vulnerabilities are shut, not rewritten, and waiting will not open them.

2019-10.sentence: In Lewy body disease the visual hallucinations and overnight agitation are doing work: they keep the night team reaching for haloperidol, which this brain cannot tolerate. The symptom is a warning, not an invitation—severe extrapyramidal side effects are the price of treating the picture instead of the diagnosis.

2019-11.sentence: Daily OTC analgesics and triptans are a developmental stall: the capacity to wait out pain never quite arrived, so the bag of pills became the only regulator. Medication overuse is that late arrival made chronic—the strongest risk for daily headache is the rescue that never stopped.

2019-12.sentence: Glycine is the inhibitory conscience of the synapse: it says no so the cell does not fire without limit, the way GABA does when benzos or alcohol are on board. Glutamate has no such brake—agitation and seizures are drive without that inner “enough.”

2019-13.sentence: The team is recruiting you as the one who can promise the patient will wake—or as the one who will confirm he is gone. Notice the pull in your own body to over-reassure or to shut down; that feeling is data about how unbearable uncertainty about the ascending reticular activating system can become in the room.

2019-14.sentence: Intense fear of gaining weight is not just a DSM checkbox; it is terror that has no story yet, so it is enacted in starvation instead of remembered as a thought. The body becomes the place the unthinkable is repeated: if she cannot put words to the dread, she will keep living it at BMI 16.

2019-15.sentence: Formal operations means he can now hold a wish (feel better) and a prohibition (do not take a mind-altering drug) as ideas at the same time. Abstraction lets the conflict become thinkable—risks, hypotheses, a future self—instead of a mute yes or no to the SSRI.

2019-16.sentence: Prader-Willi rage often erupts when the self cannot borrow a calm, admiring other to regulate hunger and frustration. The microdeletion is biology; the outburst is also a collapse of self-esteem when competence fails and no idealized caretaker is felt to be there.

2019-17.sentence: The stria terminalis is the cable that dumps amygdala alarm into septum and hypothalamus before anyone can name it. Your job is Bion’s: take that nameless dread—raw, evacuative panic—and give it a word so it stops living only as hyperarousal.

2019-18.sentence: Family psychoeducation strengthens the household’s ego: more affect tolerance, less blame, better impulse control around meds. Relapse after stopping antipsychotics is often a family system that cannot hold change; teaching them is building a container the patient does not yet have alone.

2019-19.sentence: A first depression is a snapshot; bipolarity shows itself over time, so the reliable test is staying close long enough to see a manic switch, not a one-visit MDQ or family tree. Longitudinal follow-up is the attachment move: you become a secure base, not a screening stranger, before you bet the farm on an antidepressant.
