2019-20.sentence: Empathy and a real best friend mean the conscience has someone it can disappoint. The unkind blurt is the elementary-school gap: the superego—the inner rule-giver—can feel the standard and still lose to impulse before guilt brakes the mouth.

2019-21.sentence: Schizophrenia lands in the years when work, intimacy, and adult identity are supposed to lock in, so the WHO top-ten ranking is a developmental stall, not just a diagnosis count. Lost productive years from 15 to 44 name a mind that should be launching and instead is fragmenting.

2019-22.sentence: When speech is gone, the wish that was never fully spoken will get acted out as a family fight at the bedside unless it already lives on paper. Advance directives are that written memory: they carry the patient's instructions about interventions so the dyad does not have to invent them under terror.

2019-23.sentence: Smoke induces CYP1A2 and lowers olanzapine; quitting or a smoke-free ward suddenly raises the dose the body actually sees. The page for new sedation and rigidity is also a transference test: you are recruited as either the one who tracked the enzyme or the neglectful prescriber who 'overdosed' them after they did the healthy thing.

2019-24.sentence: Veracity is putting the whole contested triad in the chart: her wish to conceive, his doubt she is ready, and the valproate she already stopped. The live third in the room is the potential pregnancy—gendered, never discussed outpatient—and writing it down keeps that third from being edited out of the record.

2019-25.sentence: Living with a brain that seizes can feel like an inside attacker, a Kleinian persecutory object you cannot flee. Major depressive disorder is the most common psychiatric partner of epilepsy because many patients finally drop into depressive-position grief: sadness and a wish to repair a damaged self rather than only rage at the seizures.

2019-26.sentence: The tuberomammillary nucleus is the brain’s histamine wake-switch; an antihistamine that crosses the blood–brain barrier turns that switch off, so sleep arrives as a side effect with a job. The drowsiness is doing something: it is telling you that wake-promoting histamine, not “just sedation,” is what those neurons were supplying.

2019-27.sentence: Winnicott’s holding environment is Erikson’s autonomy-versus-shame stage made physical: the adult stays close enough that the toddler can bang pots without catastrophe. Spontaneity with a safety net builds competence; hovering that removes all risk, or vanishing that leaves real harm, both collapse the same psychosocial task.

2019-28.sentence: ACT’s 24-hour-a-day coverage is the treatment frame when the usual office hour is a limit the patient cannot keep. The team holds time and availability so care does not depend on the person with schizophrenia arriving at a clinic; the frame moves to the street instead of punishing missed appointments.

2019-29.sentence: In myotonic dystrophy the dangerous story is often silent conduction disease, so the electrocardiogram is the test that hears what the young man does not feel. The ECG is doing the noticing for a body that advertises myotonia and cognition while the heart’s rhythm slips unannounced.

2019-30.sentence: The weakest joint in the EMR is a person who does not yet see their own click as the door. Training staff to recognize threats is a trial comment to the whole hospital: you have a part in the breach, and psychological mindedness here means spotting the phish before the firewall ever gets a vote.

2019-31.sentence: The coordinator is breaking the frame by recruiting the spouse in the patient's presence: that is a pressure on voluntarism, the right to say no without feeling you will harm the marriage or the trial. You hold the limit by taking the spouse out of the room and asking later, so consent is not a performance for the partner.

2019-32.sentence: The parent dumps a raw “I am a terrible parent” feeling into you; that is evacuation, getting rid of a state that cannot yet be thought. Goodness of fit is the container: you name the mismatch between this toddler’s intensity and the parent’s pace so the dread becomes a workable idea instead of a verdict.

2019-33.sentence: Normal-pressure hydrocephalus will not be hurried: ventricles are big, opening pressure is normal, and the walk still will not start. Look for gait apraxia, the magnetic feet that cannot initiate a step; some capacities, like a termination date, do not come online just because you want them now.

2019-34.sentence: Adolescent cortex is already enacting a two-person fight: excitatory synapses get pruned first, so the “go” connections die faster than the brakes. The teen and the household then live that biology as drama—more inhibition, less raw drive—instead of talking about a brain that is remodeling on a deadline.

2019-35.sentence: Two weeks of fluoxetine and a foggy seventy-year-old with a clean neuro exam is SIADH hyponatremia, not a new lesion. Check urea and electrolytes: the mind has left without leaving the chair because sodium, not structure, split thinking from the body in the room.

2019-36.sentence: Kindergarten is the new demand; extra cling and regression at home are the feed the child asks for after a long day of holding it together. The teacher’s calm classroom is the proof the “pill” is not illness but a normative bid for more parent, and you do not medicalize a successful school transition.

2019-37.sentence: Persistent pain downregulates dopamine receptors in the ventral striatum, and that is denial in tissue: the reward system stops registering pleasure so the person does not have to keep hoping for a fix that never arrives. Name that finding on the C-L note so the anhedonia is not written off as 'mood' or as another failed opioid trial.

2019-38.sentence: Cholecystokinin from the small intestine is a two-person message: the gut tells the brain the meal is over, the way a steady other can say 'that's enough' without a fight. When that CCK satiety line is ignored, the unit often restages it—one person pushing intake, the other refusing the stop signal.

2019-39.sentence: This starved system cannot use aggressive uncovering yet: slam the calories and you get refeeding hypophosphatemia, the medical version of flooding an ego with more than it can metabolize. Phosphate checks, paced feeds, and a supportive frame come first; insight work waits until the labs and the person can hold a load.

2019-40.sentence: L-methylfolate regenerates tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4), the cofactor that lets the neuron actually make serotonin, norepinephrine, and dopamine—so the SSRI is no longer shouting into an empty shop. You and the patient are restocking that BH4 conversation together; the pill only works if both of you treat the factory, not just the receptor.

2019-41.sentence: Glutamate has to land on the AMPA receptor for the next cell to feel anyone is there—that is proximity at the synapse, a secure-base ping. Ketamine's fast antidepressant story rides that same AMPA–glutamate contact: a new signal after a stretch of nobody home.

2019-42.sentence: The song now elicits a conditioned response—nausea without the coaster—which means affect tolerance has collapsed and the ego cannot sort 'then' from 'now.' Name the pairing out loud (loudspeaker, vomit) so the person can keep the feeling and still know the ride is over.

2019-43.sentence: Around four, the child can keep a picture of the other person in mind long enough to care what they feel, so sharing stops being a parent demand and becomes a small act of concern. Before that, “mine” is not selfishness so much as a self that is still assembling.

2019-44.sentence: Dopamine turns up wanting; serotonin, especially on a high-dose SSRI, turns it down. When he is ready to throw the pill away rather than talk about a flattened libido, the pair of you are already in an enactment: living the deadened desire instead of naming it.

2019-45.sentence: Calling cannabis “natural and harmless” is denial: she shuts out the finding that in-utero exposure tracks with later cognitive deficits so she can keep using. The consult’s job is to put that fact back in the room without shaming her into a tighter clamp.

2019-46.sentence: Sedation and analgesia are not extras; they are the relationship’s first feed, the proof that someone will not leave the child alone with the needle. Skip that prophylaxis for bone marrow biopsies and the body files it as trauma, which is why PTSD, not garden-variety worry, is the likely sequela.

2019-47.sentence: One in four people with 22q11.2 deletion develop schizophrenia, so the frame here is not wait-and-see charm; it is honest risk talk, close follow-up, and who gets told what. Holding that limit—without treating the teen as already doomed—is the ethical work.

2019-48.sentence: A harsh conscience wants one guilty party: depression or alcohol, pick a sinner. Regression analysis refuses that moral shortcut; it keeps both independent variables on the page and asks how they jointly move suicide risk.

2019-49.sentence: The song still owns a piece of childhood-style pairing: drink and cue fused before the mind could keep them separate. Extinction is the late-arriving capacity—hear that song again and again with no alcohol until the pairing finally dies of neglect.

2019-50.sentence: Aging quietly subtracts a physiologic capacity the younger liver took for granted: hepatic blood flow falls, first-pass clearance slows, and the same benzo or antidepressant hangs around. Dose as if the body has less room to metabolize, because it does.

2019-51.sentence: Microglia do the mind’s dirty work in tissue: they prune circuits in development and later scavenge dead neurons, plaques, and invaders so the rest of the brain is not flooded with debris. That is Kleinian cleanup in cells—taking in the damaged bits so the whole can stay livable.

2019-52.sentence: The church group is not a luxury hobby; it is her cultural third, a place she is a person and not only a daughter of Alzheimer dementia. If she quits it, caregiving swallows the last room that is still hers—so the first intervention is to protect that room.

2019-53.sentence: School-age work is Erikson’s industry: can I do the task, or am I the kid who cannot? A 504 plan keeps the same course and only changes access; an IEP can exempt the child from course requirements, which is a different message about what competence even means.

2019-54.sentence: Ego strength leans on a story the person can still tell: facts and events, declarative memory, which lives in the hippocampus. When that volume shrinks, the self loses the file cabinet, not the how-to of riding a bike.

2019-55.sentence: Cataplexy on a hard laugh is attachment gone motor: closeness and joy should help him hold himself together, but with orexin gone the Multiple Sleep Latency Test just clocks how fast that social arousal dumps him into sleep. The secure base here is a person who can stay with the feeling; narcolepsy collapses the same moment into atonia and a nap.

2019-56.sentence: Addington v. Texas sets clear and convincing evidence as the floor because commitment is a two-person fight over liberty, not a solo diagnosis you announce. You and the manic patient are already pulling opposite ways; the court refuses both a casual 'preponderance' shrug and a criminal 'beyond a reasonable doubt' lock so neither of you gets to win by force of personality.

2019-57.sentence: Donepezil only offers this 87-year-old a little extra acetylcholine to lean on; that is support, not uncovering, and her Alzheimer mind cannot use even that if you cancel it. Oxybutynin is an antimuscarinic that blocks the same receptors donepezil is trying to feed, so the technique fails before the neuron ever gets a chance.

2019-58.sentence: Forgetfulness, low energy, and poor concentration can be depression speaking as cognition instead of naming the mood. Neuropsychological testing is the first useful map: it shows whether memory is actually gone or just not being used, before you send him for a CT as if the story were already a lesion.

2019-59.sentence: She wants the new peer world and she also wants not to betray her parents; those two drives collide and the anxiety is the collision, not a failure of loyalty. Formation of a bicultural identity is the workable compromise: both wishes stay alive instead of one killing the other through total assimilation or total refusal.

2019-60.sentence: Cis-regulatory elements sit next to the gene and mediate transcriptional activity; they are the local context that decides whether a sequence actually speaks. Schizophrenia GWAS hits pile up in that non-coding neighborhood because risk often lives in the switch, not in the protein itself.

2019-61.sentence: The 450 ms QTc is the moment depressive concern wins: you refuse to pour more nortriptyline into a heart that already cannot finish a beat safely. Shorter cutoffs treat the ECG as an enemy to be denied; 450 ms is the repair line, not a paranoid veto of every TCA.

2019-62.sentence: Concurrent psychosis gives the aggression a job: the person is striking at a threat that is not in the room. Word-finding, late stage, and premorbid anxiety do not supply that motive; the delusion or hallucination does.

2019-63.sentence: This is Erikson’s first task, trust versus mistrust, not a gifts-and-boundaries seminar. Accepting the cookie and thanking them lets a guarded schizotypal patient complete a small act of basic trust instead of confirming that closeness is dangerous.

2019-64.sentence: Conscience here is starting acyclovir before the PCR comes back: temporal-lobe hemorrhage, fever, seizure, and lymphocytic CSF do not permit a moral holiday of “wait and see.” Prednisone, ceftriaxone, and the antifungals would soothe diagnostic pride and leave HSV chewing the medial temporal lobe.

2019-65.sentence: Analgesia is a developmental capacity the mu receptor has not been allowed to grow under buprenorphine’s high-affinity partial occupancy. Switching to methadone before femur repair is how full-agonist pain coverage finally arrives; lowering the buprenorphine or going to an NSAID leaves that capacity still unborn.

2019-66.sentence: The outburst is unrepresented state, not a remembered story: what never got words comes back as a body storm after a tiny slight. Serotonin is the system that most directly brakes impulsive and affective aggression, so the pharmacology is also a bid to give the dyad a pause long enough for the rage to become speakable.

2019-67.sentence: The mother is recruiting you to certify that a 10-year-old who already knows death is permanent is still “broken.” Your countertransference urge to over-work-up ordinary grief is her unheld death anxiety landing in you, not a delay in the child’s concept of permanence.

2019-68.sentence: After the screaming fight, speech itself threatened self-cohesion, so the self sacrificed the voice rather than risk another narcissistic crash in front of the spouse. The preserved cough shows conversion, not cord injury: mute to keep a scrap of esteem, not because the larynx failed.

2019-69.sentence: Naming the abandonment transference only stages the old wish-versus-prohibition collision; change is integration of insight, the ego holding the wish without having to repeat it. Transference is the theater, not the cure—shame and advice never metabolize that drive conflict.

2019-70.sentence: He splits the partner into an object who must stay innocent and you into the container of the dangerous HIV knowledge so the couple can stay all-good. Consulting state law refuses that split: the statute, not his denial or your rescue fantasy, decides partner notification.

2019-71.sentence: The wish to taper, clonidine-detox, or naltrexone-blast her is paranoid-schizoid: evacuate the bad heroin-object even if withdrawal attacks the fetus. Methadone maintenance is depressive-position repair—you keep an imperfect good object on board so mother and baby are not hammered by withdrawal.

2019-72.sentence: The hippocampal formation is where lived episodes with other people get bound into memory, so its size is not a solo hard-drive score. Successful global cognition with aging tracks that relational archive: more intact hippocampus, more of the two-person story still available to think with.

2019-73.sentence: Bonferroni is the conservative p-value: you divide alpha by the number of tests so twenty comparisons do not manufacture twenty little “discoveries.” Uncovering every subgroup is like interpreting every dream in one hour—the mind, and the dataset, cannot use that much raw significance without a support frame that protects against false positives.

2019-74.sentence: Aquaporin-4 antibody disease (NMO/NMOSD) hits ego hardware: a longitudinally extensive cord lesion plus optic-nerve enhancement can wreck motor control and vision, the substrates of affect tolerance and reality testing. Name the antibody so the consult does not treat collapsing legs and sudden visual loss as conversion until the water-channel attack is ruled out.

2019-75.sentence: Inflammatory cytokines upregulate serotonin reuptake transporters, so more 5-HT is vacuumed out of the synapse—interferon for hepatitis C can leave the person without the chemical “secure base” mood usually provides. Depression here is not only meaning; the attachment system is being unplugged at the transporter.

2019-76.sentence: Flumazenil reversed a benzo that enhances postsynaptic GABA-A inhibition in the amygdala; alcohol plus that same GABA push is the classic overdose pair. Giving the antagonist and then hearing “pills” is already an enactment: the system undoes the chemical mute button before anyone has talked about why the mute was needed.

2019-77.sentence: Clanging is thought chained by sound—sleep/deep/bed/fed/red, well/bell—not by the question you asked. That is a vertical split: associations leave semantic ground while the body stays in the chair, so you track rhyme as a dissociation of meaning, not as clever wordplay.

2019-78.sentence: Claims data show fewer substance-related events in males with ADHD while they are on stimulants—the pill as regulation, not as the first hit. Treat the mother’s “you will make him an addict” as a poison fantasy about the script; the relationship task is to hold that fear while the methylphenidate or amphetamine actually lowers, not raises, the substance-event rate.

2019-79.sentence: “Nothing can destroy me” is denial: he is shoving terror of being small and breakable out of awareness. Verbal de-escalation talks to the person still behind that shield instead of proving that only needles and restraints can hold him.

2019-80.sentence: Orgasm is a capacity that cannot be rushed by estrogen, bupropion, or flibanserin. Directed masturbatory training honors the time limit: she has to learn her own body's map, not borrow climax from a pill or an interpretation.

2019-81.sentence: Longer trauma overruns containment, Bion's word for holding a raw feeling until it can be thought. The mind evacuates the ordeal as dissociative amnesia rather than letting nameless dread stay long enough to become a memory.

2019-82.sentence: Reliability is empty mirroring: the scale says the same thing every time and feels sturdy, yet it may not see depression at all. Validity is real recognition—whether the instrument actually measures what it claims, so your competence is not built on a flattering echo.

2019-83.sentence: The wish for another child collides with the prohibition of handing on TSC1 or TSC2. Autosomal dominant inheritance makes that conflict concrete: each pregnancy carries about a 50% risk even when both parents look healthy.

2019-84.sentence: Higher education can work as a brittle reaction formation: looking capable to fend off any hint of collapse. When schizophrenia arrives, that armor fails, and the gap between the old résumé and the new illness raises suicide risk in transitional-age youth.

2019-85.sentence: Calling this disruptive mood dysregulation disorder, not bipolar I, can feel like refusing the mood stabilizer that would prove the rages are “real.” The parent may treat that pill as feed or as proof of need; stay with the chronic irritability instead of medicating a mania that is not there.

2019-86.sentence: Numbers jammed onto the right half of the clock are parietal hemineglect: half of space has dropped out of the mind, not out of effort. The drawing’s meaning is concrete — usually a right parietal lesion has erased the left field, so the patient cannot “try harder” to see what is gone.

2019-87.sentence: Polymerase chain reaction does one job: it copies a short stretch of DNA, including short tandem repeats, until the lab can see it. A Fragile X CGG assay can name a piece of the intellectual disability; it cannot make the whole child make sense in one result.

2019-88.sentence: Elevated porphobilinogen names acute intermittent porphyria as the driver of the paranoia, proximal weakness, hyporeflexia, and menstrual abdominal crises. She needs you as a regulating other who keeps medicine in the room so the voices do not become the only attachment on the unit.

2019-89.sentence: Vertebral artery dissection after chiropractic neck work strips affect tolerance in a second: dysarthria, ataxia, and occipital pain arrive before the mind can metabolize them. Ego strength here is whether the patient can use you to bear a body that just changed, rather than deny the tear because “it was only an adjustment.”

2019-90.sentence: The on-air disclaimer is aimed at duty, so callers cannot install him as their doctor by projective identification — the push to put their need into him until he behaves as if he is treating them. He is trying to stay in concern rather than omnipotence: offer a thought, not a repair a radio minute cannot finish.

2019-91.sentence: Linkage analysis is the family speaking as one organism: you track which chromosomal stretch rides with the autistic-like trait down the pedigree, not a hunch gene from the literature. Association maps, candidate-gene studies, pathway analysis, and CGH ask different questions; they do not use kinship as the instrument.

2019-92.sentence: Worldwide, trance and dissociation most often sit inside religious and ritual events, so they can be identity work, not a depersonalization or PTSD diagnosis. If you pathologize Pentecostal tongues as a disorder, you mistake a culture's way of becoming a self for a broken ego.

2019-93.sentence: The 'I want to quit / I don't' split is not a stall; it is the symptom doing its job, keeping both sides of the drink alive so neither has to die yet. Motivational enhancement therapy treats that ambivalence as the work, instead of arguing the patient into one voice.

2019-94.sentence: Frieda Fromm-Reichmann's 'schizophrenogenic mother' was a developmental fairy tale: the child's psychosis was imagined as a late arrival of toxic mothering rather than a brain illness. When a parent asks if she caused it, name that history so guilt does not become the unofficial diagnosis.

2019-95.sentence: Frequent conversation and thinking aloud give the toddler words that will later become an inner voice—self-talk that can soothe, forbid, and plan. Flashcards feed vocabulary; overheard parental speech is how a conscience starts to sound like someone kind in the room.

2019-96.sentence: Dropout often happens when the therapist gets recruited into an old role—rescuer, critic, abandoning parent—and acts it instead of noticing it. Greater therapist experience is what most reliably keeps that transference from ending the treatment; matching gender or ethnicity is not the finding.

2019-97.sentence: Early skill is not yet a memory you can tell; it lives in the corticostriatal and corticocerebellar loops as a sequence the body is still assembling. The cerebellum here is like an unrepresented state: timing and error are practiced in movement before they become a story the cortex can narrate.

2019-98.sentence: Storytelling with words at four lets a child put a wish, a fear, and a parent into one plot instead of only acting them. The drive gets a beginning, middle, and end; without that narrative wrap, the same impulse stays a tantrum or a grab.

2019-99.sentence: Low circulating GABA is a quieting system that has gone thin, so the self has less internal hush against shame and collapse. Mirroring then has to do extra work: another person’s calm becomes the brake the chemistry is not providing.

2019-100.sentence: Methadone maintenance can produce hypogonadism, so desire drops in the body before it becomes a sentence about loneliness or recovery. What cannot be remembered as loss of vitality gets repeated as low libido, fatigue, and a quieter erection—the endocrine system acting the unsaid chapter.

2019-101.sentence: Effectiveness asks what happens when the wish for a clean result meets the messy clinic—comorbidity, missed doses, ordinary life. Efficacy is the wish under prohibition of noise; naturalistic work studies the collision, not the fantasy of the perfect trial.

2019-102.sentence: The FDA boxed warning pairs death with stroke when antipsychotics are used for dementia-related agitation—conscience written as a black box, not a vibe. Prescribing anyway without naming that risk is a sanctioned gap: we quiet the ward and outsource the guilt to the label we never read aloud.

2019-103.sentence: The tau tangle on the slide is also a transference pull: the family is asking you to be the one who still recognizes the person they are losing. Your countertransference—urgency to name Alzheimer disease, or a wish to look away—is information about how unbearable it is to sit with a mind that cannot hold new memories.

2019-104.sentence: Tourette syndrome is defined by multiple motor tics plus at least one vocal tic; that combination is a limit, not a judgment about how hard the child is trying. You cannot rush the nervous system past that threshold any more than you can terminate a treatment before the work is done—the diagnosis waits on what is actually present.

2019-105.sentence: The Simpson-Angus scale asks you to look at rigidity and gait, not at whether the patient 'gets' how sick they are. Insight here is yours first: a trial comment about stiffness only helps if you have named the motor finding instead of treating it as attitude or lack of motivation.

2019-106.sentence: The bell-and-pad pairs a wet sheet with an alarm so the bladder cue itself starts to wake the child—classical conditioning, not another sticker for willpower. That pairing can restore a bit of competence: the self feels more intact when the body begins to signal before shame does.

2019-107.sentence: HLA-B*1502 in Asian Americans turns carbamazepine into a carrier of nameless dread: a rash that can become Stevens-Johnson before anyone can think it through. You contain that raw risk by screening first, so the fear becomes a named lab rather than something evacuated into 'just start the mood stabilizer.

2019-108.sentence: Long-term abstinence is the evidence-based cut that lowers her cancer risk, even after a father's heavy drinking and her own one drink a day. Object relations here is the split she is holding: father's lethal bottle versus her 'light' glass—both belong to the same alcohol-cancer object until she can keep the good wish to live and the bad data in one frame.

2019-109.sentence: Maternal mental illness already diagnosed before birth is the bigger developmental threat because the infant can become the container for what the mother cannot hold—that is projective identification: her unmetabolized fear or despair gets lived in the baby’s body. An SSRI in pregnancy is a smaller risk than a mind stuck in paranoid-schizoid mode, unable to offer depressive concern (worry about the baby as a real other you might harm and then want to repair).

2019-110.sentence: Excessive administration is the biggest healthcare waste, and it functions like a collective superego: a rigid conscience that treats more rules, forms, and managers as moral virtue. Fraud looks like the obvious sin; the sanctioned gap is the paperwork we call “good stewardship” while it outspends poor coordination or extra labs.

2019-111.sentence: Cognitive preservation is the capacity that has to keep arriving if successful older age—independent living, mastery, growth—is going to happen. Money, social life, and a working body help, but without memory, planning, and reality testing still online, those later ego achievements stall.

2019-112.sentence: Ketamine’s club high—“flying above the dance floor”—then withdrawal plus nystagmus is an unrepresented state: the self is not remembered as a body on the floor, so leaving the body is repeated chemically. Nystagmus is the somatic leftover of that exit; methcathinone, cocaine, and amphetamine give wired euphoria without this dissociative lift.

2019-113.sentence: Waxy flexibility, mutism, and not eating recruit you into the one who must move a frozen body—that is the countertransference pull: helpless handler versus enforcer. Give lorazepam for catatonia; benztropine treats EPS, not this still, unseeing patient.

2019-114.sentence: Dopamine in the nucleus accumbens is the vote-counter for acute reinforcement: the drive for the hit wins the moment the mesolimbic path fires. Cortisol, epinephrine, nitric oxide, and substance P modulate stress or pain; they do not write the “do it again” ticket the way dopamine does.

2019-115.sentence: In a rigid anorexia family, hunger and deadliness get put into the adolescent’s body and treated as hers alone—that is projective identification: the parents live off the projected control while she starves the “bad” object. Structural family therapy (and FBT after it) hands feeding back to the parents so the girl can move toward depressive concern: repair and shared worry instead of a paranoid war with food.

2019-116.sentence: Quitting two months before you graduate is the symptom doing a job: she leaves first so the abandonment is hers, not yours. Interpret that reversal now; arranging a transfer or politely allowing termination skips the meaning and lets the old loss go unspoken.

2019-117.sentence: The Joint Commission bans “1.0 units” because a missed decimal becomes 10 units—a tenfold overdose dressed as neat charting. This sits on Erikson’s industry versus inferiority: the written dose is the work product, and craft either holds or it humiliates everyone at the bedside.

2019-118.sentence: Low-intensity telemedicine is not a solo mind treating a patient; it is you and the rural PCP co-regulating one antidepressant over a curbside (in person, phone, or e-mail). The pattern is two-person: they borrow your judgment for a minute so they can stay the doctor who actually writes the dose.

2019-119.sentence: Histone acetylation loosens DNA–histone grip so transcription can start; valproate, as an HDAC inhibitor, tips the cell toward that open, readable state. Think attachment: the chromatin becomes a secure base—genes can approach and be expressed instead of staying silenced and out of reach.

2019-120.sentence: Multiple ring-enhancing lesions in AIDS are Toxoplasma gondii abscesses, not a single lymphoma or the white-matter fade of PML. The person is still in the chair while cortex goes offline—that is a medical vertical split: awareness drops because parasite-walled tissue has left the conversation, not because the mind chose to leave.

2019-121.sentence: Stigma is a hit to ego strength: people will not use help if walking in already means they are “the psych patient.” Putting personal counseling next to financial counseling at the same desk lets a burned-out physician ask for money help and still tolerate the feelings that come with needing a person.

2019-122.sentence: A seven-year-old with ADHD and ODD still uses the parent as a regulator, not as an insight machine. A home-and-school rewards plan built on what the child actually enjoys is a secure-base move: the adult stays close, names the target, and hands back a predictable yes when the child can stay in range.

2019-123.sentence: Appelbaum capacity is not a private IQ score; it is a conversation the twelve-year-old and the team can now hold together. Around that age the child can usually take in the facts, hold the choice, and answer you back, so her preference becomes part of the shared decision rather than something adults simply override.

2019-124.sentence: CB1 lives mostly on the presynaptic membrane, where endocannabinoids travel backward and tell the bouton to quiet the next release. That is a support-not-uncover fact: cannabis hijacks a brake already built to keep circuits from flooding, which is why it touches so many functions and still rarely kills by overdose.

2019-125.sentence: A locked-unit group never becomes a usable object if the faces change every day. Rapid patient turnover splits the room into a string of one-offs, so good and bad never get held long enough for cohesion to form.

2019-126.sentence: Hypocretin-1 (orexin) from the lateral hypothalamus is the chemical that keeps wake from collapsing into sleep. In narcolepsy type 1 those cells are gone, so laughter can drop the body into cataplexy: the symptom is a failed stay-awake signal, not a wish to escape the joke.

2019-127.sentence: Whole exome sequencing is the family's wish for a name that lives in the protein-coding exons, not a demand to read every silent stretch of genome. Gene panels are too narrow and whole genome sequencing is too much story; the exome is the compromise that lets the child's intellectual disability and dysmorphic features become a thinkable diagnosis.

2019-128.sentence: This study sits on Erikson's generativity task: caring for a fetus while a mother is already ill enough to need an antidepressant. Healthy unmedicated controls erase that task, so the reviewers flag an inappropriate control group rather than sample size or the mere fact of studying pregnant women.

2019-129.sentence: Those two-week stretches of 3–4 hours of sleep are doing different jobs: mania gives energy, insomnia steals it. Asking how well rested the person feels by day asks whether the missing sleep is a gift the mood is handing over or a wound.

2019-130.sentence: The seizures stay raw and unthinkable until the face and back hold them: angiofibromas in the nasolabial folds and a shagreen plaque make tuberous sclerosis a name instead of nameless dread. Neurofibromatosis and Sturge-Weber evacuate different skin stories; this plaque and these papules contain the childhood epilepsy as one disease.

2019-131.sentence: Catatonia was the last rigid bid for a cohesive self when no one could still mirror a fragmenting mind. In Western wards that bid has become less common; alogia and disorganized thought remain, but the body no longer has to freeze to keep a scrap of esteem.

2019-132.sentence: The 12-month-old's wish to answer the stranger's hello collides with caution; that is the drive conflict. Mother's smile and nod lift the prohibition, and social referencing is the baby checking whether affiliation is allowed before laughing.

2019-133.sentence: GABA in the ventrolateral preoptic nucleus is the brain’s off-switch: those neurons inhibit the arousal systems so sleep can happen. What cannot be remembered often shows up as a body that will not downshift—insomnia, startle, night watch—because the switch never gets a clean signal that it is safe to go off.

2019-134.sentence: Capacity is the first question, not the daughter’s signature: can this person with dementia understand, appreciate, reason, and choose about the wrist surgery. The pill-or-procedure as relationship shows up here as the team treating consent like a feed they can grab from a surrogate so they do not have to sit with the patient’s no.

2019-135.sentence: Syringomyelia hits the crossing spinothalamic fibers first, so pain (and temperature) go while light touch, vibration, and proprioception stay. The frame here is who holds the limit of what gets felt: the cord has already split sensation, and you do not paper over a painless burn by calling it “just neuropathy” and walking off.

2019-136.sentence: Rivastigmine is a cholinesterase inhibitor; more acetylcholine means more vagal tone, so bradycardia and near-faints are the expected hit, not constipation or weight gain. Insight is whether they can use a trial comment—“the medicine is slowing the heart, not just the memory”—instead of treating every faint as a mystery of aging.

2019-137.sentence: ECT is indicated for catatonia, NMS, and psychotic depression; it is not a personality-disorder or dysthymia tool. Some endings cannot be rushed with talk: when eating, rigidity, or fever have already taken over, the limit is biological, and waiting for “more insight” is not treatment.

2019-138.sentence: Preschool emotion regulation tracks language, not walking, guilt, or cooperative play. Ego strength here is a word that can hold the feeling long enough that the impulse does not have to become a tantrum.

2019-139.sentence: Dissociation is a vertical split: the person leaves without leaving the chair, and the genome does something similar—sequence stays put while expression steps out. Micro-RNAs are that third epigenetic lever, with DNA methylation and histone modification, so childhood trauma can mute or unmute genes without rewriting the code.

2019-140.sentence: G-banded karyotyping is the wish for a whole, countable chromosome story colliding with the prohibition against guessing from a face: you want the tidy Down-syndrome gestalt, but the test that actually sees an extra 21 is still the old banded karyotype, not FISH, SNP arrays, or CGH. The symptom of “we already know” is the drive to close the case; the prohibition is that only a visible extra chromosome, not a targeted probe, confirms trisomy 21.

2019-141.sentence: In X-linked dominant disease, females are twice as likely as males to be affected in a multigenerational pedigree, and that number can quietly bruise a family’s self-esteem: daughters look “marked,” sons look “spared,” and no father-to-son transmission means the father’s line cannot idealize itself as the carrier. Mirror the pedigree without inflating or shrinking anyone’s competence—twice as many women affected is a counting fact, not a verdict on whose genome is weaker.

2019-142.sentence: The patient who never goes to a gathering is recruiting you as the amygdala’s scout: if you lean in too hard you become the threat detector, if you back off you become the freeze. Name the circuit instead—amygdala talking both ways with the periaqueductal gray of the brainstem, the node that turns social alarm into freeze, flight, and “I just won’t go”—so the feeling in the room is anatomy, not your job to soothe or chase.

2019-143.sentence: Cleaning and checking are how unrepresented danger gets a body: contamination and an unchecked stove stand in for a threat that never became a rememberable scene. The hands keep repeating the unthought catastrophe so it does not have to arrive as memory.

2019-144.sentence: REM is the night-school where dreaming and nightmare work practice arriving; benzodiazepines suppress that stage even while they shorten latency and lengthen sleep. The capacity to metabolize affect in dream is delayed or shut off, so the call-room "good night" can be a developmental stall, not just sedation.

2019-145.sentence: Asking about her estrogen pill before you lock a lamotrigine target is a conscience move: you are refusing a sanctioned gap where “I prescribed something reasonable” lets you ignore that estrogen will glucuronidate the drug and cut her level roughly in half. Guilt here is useful—if you skip the contraception question, you are the one who left her unprotected from breakthrough mood episodes, not just from pregnancy.

2019-146.sentence: This item sits on Erikson’s industry-versus-inferiority: the 7-year-old’s job is to sit, try, and feel competent, and prenatal tobacco use specifically stacks the deck toward ADHD so school feels like failure. Naming maternal smoking is not blame theater; it tells you why industry is harder for this child and where you owe extra scaffolding so inferiority does not become his identity.

2019-147.sentence: Ethanol’s NMDA antagonism plus GABA-A agonism is the chemistry of a brief vacation from psychic pain: excitation drops, inhibition rises, and the person finally feels allowed to stop. The symptom is doing work—numbing conflict and demand—until the same two receptors rebound and the vacation turns into withdrawal.

2019-148.sentence: The family is already in an enactment: they treat the 16-year-old’s knife, fights, and stealing as a life sentence, and you are being pulled to join the courtroom instead of the clinic. The epidemiology is the interpretation you need—these adolescent-onset conduct behaviors most often decrease over the next decade—so you stop living the catastrophe and start talking about time, limits, and a future that is not already written.

2019-149.sentence: St. John’s wort can flip bipolar depression into mania, and that switch is a vertical split: one self is still “just treating sadness,” while another state takes the chair without anyone deciding to leave. The herb is not a gentle side door around mood instability; it is an antidepressant that can split the person into a high that does not remember the low.

2019-150.sentence: You are being recruited as the parent who can finally start the clock: delayed puberty and short stature make you feel you should produce the missing push yourself. Hold that countertransference and teach the fact instead—growth hormone needs gonadal hormones to launch the adolescent growth spurt—so you stay the doctor who names what the body still requires, not the rescuer who tries to be the hormone.

2019-151.sentence: The fitness-for-duty eval is a sanctioned leak in the usual confidentiality pact: the hospital’s physician-health committee is the real “patient,” and the surgeon’s secrets are not yours to keep. That is a superego bargain, not cruelty—you name the limit up front so your conscience and his both know the report is the work, not a private treatment alliance.

2019-152.sentence: Anterior cerebral territory hits the paracentral lobule’s homunculus for the contralateral leg and the medial frontal circuits that start movement and hold the sphincter—so the wish to stand and the wish to hold urine both fail while face and arm stay intact. Abulia is the drive going quiet: initiation itself is injured, not just strength.

2019-153.sentence: Another anxiety disorder is the usual roommate, not mood, personality, or substance use—panic that “got better” on an SSRI still leaves the body repeating unrepresented dread as store-avoidance and social dread. Screen the second anxiety syndrome instead of assuming residual panic; what cannot be named as a second diagnosis will keep getting lived as “the same attack.”

2019-154.sentence: Copper deficiency after gastric bypass can mimic B12 myeloneuropathy—spastic legs, hyperreflexia, lost toe vibration—while the serum B12 sits there looking innocent. Contain the consult’s nameless “this should be B12” panic long enough to think copper, or the raw picture gets evacuated as another useless B12 shot.

2019-155.sentence: Effect size is the magnitude of the difference between arms; a tiny p-value only says the finding is unlikely under the null, not that the antidepressant is clinically impressive. Journal club that treats p as a mirror for “we are smart and this drug is great” is an idealizing collapse—self-esteem needs the size of the effect, not the applause of significance.

2019-156.sentence: Ornithine transcarbamylase sequencing is the definitive test when protein loading unmasks late-onset OTC and the consult looks like delirium. A trial comment that lands is “the diet, the headaches, the old slow growth, and this encephalopathy are one story”—if they can take that as their part of the physiology, you have enough psychological mindedness to order the gene test instead of another vague workup.

2019-157.sentence: Paranoid ideation is the interpersonal speed limit of schizotypal personality: odd speech, thrift-store eccentricity, and constricted affect already mark a mind that cannot be rushed into ordinary closeness. Ideas of persecution keep people at a distance you cannot interpret away in one consult; you work inside that limit instead of trying to terminate the oddness.

2019-158.sentence: Identification floods the intern so she becomes the dying patient's daughter; empathy keeps an observing ego, which is the capacity to feel the room and still think. If she cannot retain objectivity, drop uncovering and teach containment: name the feeling, then step back, because that mind cannot use deeper technique until the observing part is back online.

2019-159.sentence: Clock drawing is a two-person task: you set ten past eleven and the patient has to negotiate with you on the page. Executive function places the hands while visuospatial skill builds the circle and numbers; when either partner fails, the drawing shows the breakdown between planner and map.

2019-160.sentence: Cumulative incidence is development in a population: new tardive dyskinesia cases that actually arrived during the year, divided by everyone who could have gotten it. Prevalence only counts who already has the finding; incidence asks whether the capacity for the event showed up on time in the at-risk group.

2019-161.sentence: Capitation pays one yearly sum per enrolled patient whether they come weekly or vanish, which quietly licenses a gap in the treatment conscience: less care still pays the same. Notice the superego squeeze—guilt if you spend, and a sanctioned excuse if you ration—before the contract starts writing the frame for you.

2019-162.sentence: Male gender is a hard risk marker for prolonged or complicated bereavement; the widower may recruit you as the lost wife, the stoic buddy, or the one who will not cry. Track that countertransference—what you feel pulled to become—because acceptance, money, a good marriage, and a calm first month do not protect him the way people wish they did.

2019-163.sentence: Carbamazepine induces hepatic enzymes and quietly empties the oral contraceptive of its protection; the first ‘memory’ of that fact may be a late period, not a thought she can report. If you skip the enzyme-inducer talk, the pair of you repeat an old trauma pattern: something happens to her body while nobody puts words to it.

2019-164.sentence: A 22q11.2 deletion is a real missing piece; in the paranoid-schizoid position the family may treat emerging psychosis as a bad object stuffed into the teen rather than a chromosomal gap. Depressive concern starts when you name the deletion, so they can mourn what is absent instead of splitting the child into defective versus intact.

2019-165.sentence: The EMG finding that diagnoses REM sleep behavior disorder is excess muscle tone in REM: the body is acting the dream instead of representing it. Punching a bed partner is unrepresented action leaking into the dyad because the usual REM atonia brake is gone.

2019-166.sentence: Thirteen sits on Erikson’s identity-versus-role-confusion task; huffing aerosols (perioral sores, dazed days, nausea) is a chemical shortcut to a self-state when the teen cannot yet say who they are. The rash at the mouth is identity work happening at the body’s edge instead of in talk with peers.

2019-167.sentence: Medicare Part B is the optional purchasable benefit that actually covers psychiatrist visits and sertraline; turning it down can be a protest that he is not yet ‘old’ or dependent. The paperwork overwhelm does work: it postpones claiming a senior identity he has not metabolized.

2019-168.sentence: High-dose interferon is the immunomodulator that can crash a cancer patient into major depression within weeks; vitality drops and so does the felt secure base that the body will hold him. On C-L he may use you as a borrowed regulator because the drug has stripped the internal caregiver.

2019-169.sentence: You and this 70-year-old with a QTc of 480 ms are already in a two-person bargain: the unit wants him quiet, his heart wants you not to chase him toward torsades. Picking aripiprazole (lowest QT risk among this list, not ziprasidone or thioridazine) is you refusing to enact the “just give him something strong” demand with him.

2019-170.sentence: Calling the EEG metabolic encephalopathy—generalized slowing with triphasic waves in acute liver failure—is suppression: you keep the team’s seizure-fear in mind without acting it out as an over-read of non-convulsive status. The defense works by naming the pattern and sitting with uncertainty instead of converting anxiety into a false emergency.

2019-171.sentence: The teen is not in the room, so the frame is a parent consult, not a gender exam of an absent adolescent. Asking “What pronoun do you want me to use when referring to your child?” sets a speaking rule with the people present and keeps you from grabbing the limit that belongs to the missing teenager.

2019-172.sentence: A CYP2D6 poor-metabolizer result on nortriptyline is a hard limit, not a suggestion you can charm past. Personalized CYP dosing is best established for tricyclic antidepressants, so the ethical move is to dose to the enzyme rather than to the wish to rescue refractory depression faster.

2019-173.sentence: After traumatic brain injury—the medical condition on this list with the highest suicide risk—the organ that watches itself is injured, so insight is not a reliable safety tool. A trial comment still matters, but you treat “can he see his own part?” as something the injury may have taken, not as a given you can talk him into.

2019-174.sentence: Holding is the mother’s slow work of taking in the infant’s state, mirroring it, and giving it back in a form the baby can use—not projective identification, where the feeling is dumped and left in the other. That capacity cannot be installed in one visit; you watch for it and wait, because rushing it is not teaching, it is crowding.

2019-175.sentence: The family has already been used as a dumping ground for raw violence and missed meds, so they refuse to be the container—the mind that can hold a feeling long enough to make it thinkable. Assertive community treatment is the next container: outreach that stays with the unmetabolized chaos instead of evacuating it back to the ward.

2019-176.sentence: Growth hormone is the body's night-time yes—the biological mirror that says the self is still growing. If he skips slow-wave sleep, that competence signal never fires, and the growth curve is the self-esteem chart you can actually plot.

2019-177.sentence: Calculation is a later-acquired cortical skill; when it is still there, the cortex has not yet been the main casualty. Subcortical dementia hits tempo and motor tone first, so preserved calculation is the developmental leftover that tells you this is not Alzheimer-type cortical collapse.

2019-178.sentence: Antipsychotic metabolic injury often lives as an unrepresented state: the body repeats the damage before anyone can narrate it. Number needed to treat of 50 (absolute risk 20% minus 18%) means metformin barely writes that story—you treat fifty people to spare one person diabetes.

2019-179.sentence: The gambler often recruits you as the last person who might still believe a win is coming, while the session itself is soaked in the crash. Major depression is the usual companion because the chase and the empty after-feeling are one sequence—screen for it before you become another bailout.

2019-180.sentence: Self-psychology (Kohut) treats the here-and-now idealizing or mirroring tie as co-created, not as a one-way projection you interpret away. That selfobject function has a clock you cannot rush; ending too soon is not insight, it is just withdrawing the borrowed self.

2019-181.sentence: A trial comment after an attempt is not “why did you do that,” but “mood was already squeezing the horizon before the act.” If they can hear that they had a part in the despair, not only in the method, you have a scrap of insight to work with; if they cannot, treat mood first and keep the comment short.

2019-182.sentence: DNA methylation is the body’s way of writing “the world was famine” onto the genome so later generations keep scanning for shortage. Self-esteem then gets organized around a body that never quite feels reliably fed; the hunger winter lives on as a competence injury, not as a story they remember.

2019-183.sentence: Hair-pulling is often an evacuation: the student dumps nameless study-dread into the fingers so it never has to become a thought. Habit reversal works because it contains the urge in awareness-plus-competing response long enough for the feeling to become thinkable instead of just yanked out.

2019-184.sentence: Avoidant infants look cool because they have already used suppression: they push the need for the parent out of awareness so reunion cannot hurt. Little overt attention is the defense working, not independence; the child is managing attachment by not needing, which is still needing.

2019-185.sentence: MRI is the most sensitive noninvasive watch on MS inflammation, and the consult can become an enactment if psych and neurology trade “your symptoms vs ours” instead of looking at the same scan. Name that two-person split in the room: you are repeating lesion vs mind while the MRI is already showing both need tracking.

2019-186.sentence: Fatigable ptosis and diplopia that reset overnight is myasthenia, and the frame job is to hold the limit: this is not “just depression” you can keep only in the hour. You do not collude with a morning-only story; you send them for medical workup and keep the therapy hour from swallowing a neuromuscular emergency.

2019-187.sentence: Fragile X is the syndrome: long face, large everted ears, high-arched palate, plus ID and autism—and now depression. The pill can land as feed or as proof he is broken; name the syndrome first so the med is care, not another demand on a body already marked as different.

2019-188.sentence: This is still normal grief: disbelief, day-long thoughts of him, a wish to be with him without a plan to die. Attachment is a secure-base system; after sudden loss the protest can last months, and wanting proximity to him is not yet MDD.

2019-189.sentence: NESARC 2001–2013: the steepest rise in high-risk drinking and AUD was in adolescents and older adults, not the young-male story your colleague is telling. Drinking is a two-person pattern—who pours, who looks away, who calls it just a nightcap—so miss those age groups and you miss the pair.

2019-190.sentence: Medically certified sick leave tracks perceived poor relationship with the supervisor more than workload or decision latitude. In object-relations terms, the boss becomes the all-bad object—one person holding all the poison—so the body clocks out instead of the conflict getting named.

2019-191.sentence: Best first move: validate a normal reaction to failed treatment and a palliative plan, not CBT for “distortions” or a locked unit. Prognosis and technique: this mind needs support and naming of the overwhelm; uncovering or treating hope as a cognitive error would be too much.

2019-192.sentence: That package—psychoeducation, validate the vulnerability, then push for change—is dialectical behavior therapy. Gender and “too much feeling” often sit as a third in the room; DBT’s validation says the intensity is real before anyone asks her to change it.

2019-193.sentence: Young adulthood to middle adulthood is when concern can leave the home and land on the larger social system—that is Klein's depressive position: you start to care that other people and institutions can be damaged and might need repair. Before that, politics is still mostly a self-object; after it, guilt and responsibility can attach to a world that is not you.

2019-194.sentence: The mesocorticolimbic neurons start in the ventral tegmental area, not the substantia nigra—so reward, salience, and prefrontal drive all share one origin. Ego strength is what happens when those projections stay usable: you can want something, feel it, and still test reality instead of being hijacked by craving or flattened by blockade.

2019-195.sentence: The literature's top barrier is the initial cost of introducing an EHR, not age, autonomy, or policy fog. Calling it 'just money' can be a neat isolation of affect: the clinic names the invoice so it does not have to name the shame of looking clumsy at a new keyboard.

2019-196.sentence: Day-three baby blues with a depressed mother in the history is a two-person storm: the infant's needs and the new mother's own maternal imago arrive together. Psychoeducation is the relational intervention—naming the blues as expected so the pair do not have to enact 'I am a failed mother' before anyone has slept.

2019-197.sentence: Googling to tell grandiose delusion from reality can be a last-ditch way to stay a secure base: you need the world to stay real so the patient can still use you. Searching out of curiosity, to police psychotherapy, or to check if they can pay is using the patient as a proximity object for your own unease.

2019-198.sentence: Asenapine is absorbed through the oral mucosa, so the dose has to live on the tongue instead of disappearing into a swallowed story. Cheeking and 'I can't swallow this' often repeat an unrepresented state in the mouth—the body stages take-in versus spit-out when words for the fear are not yet available.

2019-199.sentence: Tyrosine hydroxylase is the throttle on the catecholamine line: it decides how much norepinephrine can even be made from tyrosine. Dopa decarboxylase and dopamine β-hydroxylase only work with what that enzyme lets through.

2019-200.sentence: The anterior cingulate is the salience network's alarm: it tags which inner or outer signal is worth interrupting whatever you were doing. Posterior cingulate lives in the default-mode club, so it is the wrong neighborhood for that job.

2019-201.sentence: Three lifetime episodes means the depressive position—the capacity to hold a good object and repair after collapse—has already failed more than once. Maintenance pharmacotherapy is the ongoing repair, not a one-time making-good after this sertraline remission.

2019-202.sentence: The Continuous Performance Test is a long, boring watch: it asks whether attention can stay on station, not whether it can split or retrieve words. Elevated omission errors mean the watchman blinked and the target walked by.

2019-203.sentence: A family-based association study keeps ancestry inside one pedigree, so systematic population differences cannot masquerade as a disease allele. Case-control mixes ancestries first and then blames the SNP.

2019-204.sentence: The team's conscience races to suicide while cardiovascular disease is the actual most common premature killer in schizophrenia. That is a sanctioned gap in morality: we treat the voices and leave the blood pressure, weight, and glucose unjudged.

2019-205.sentence: Epigenetic marks sit in a dynamic three-dimensional chromatin fold, not a one-dimensional base-pair string, so a childhood that never quite arrived as a safe environment can still rewrite which genes stay open. The DNA sequence she inherited is the fixed score; the 3-D code is the late-arriving conductor that trauma can still train.

2019-206.sentence: Without emotional attunement the toddler’s hunger and night-waking never become a story; they stay as unrepresented states, raw body weather with no words. What the parent cannot feel with the child gets repeated in feeding and sleep instead of remembered as “I was scared.”

2019-207.sentence: Label A is the putamen, the lateral lens-shaped gray just under the insula, where practiced motor programs live once they have arrived. A new movement symptom means that automatic habit nucleus is being driven; development of skilled action has been hijacked, not invented from scratch.

2019-208.sentence: In the first two years the motor cortex outruns the sensory cortex, so reach-and-grab competence shows up before fine tactile discrimination. The mother’s self-esteem does not have to wait for perfect sensory mirroring; the baby’s agency arrives first, and that sequence is the real developmental gift.

2019-209.sentence: OCD is a wish colliding with a prohibition until the ritual never stops; the anterior limb of the internal capsule is the white-matter corridor that carries that fight. Humanitarian-exemption DBS there is not “erasing the wish”—it is interrupting the highway between the urge and the punishing loop.

2019-210.sentence: Working memory lives in dorsolateral prefrontal cortex: it holds the digits while you dial. When that board goes blank, the mind does a vertical split—it leaves the task without leaving the chair—and the number is gone even though “memory” as a file cabinet is intact.

2019-211.sentence: Donepezil plus a glutamate modulator (memantine) is added when Alzheimer dementia has already eaten into judgment and ADLs, which is another way of saying ego strength has thinned: affect tolerance, impulse control, and reality testing no longer hold the day together. The combo does not restore a lost self; it slows the next drop in attention and global function so the remaining coping can still be used.

2019-212.sentence: Brief spinning only when she rolls in bed or tips her head back is canalithiasis, not a stroke, and naming it BPPV is a clean use of suppression: you park the catastrophe fantasy long enough to do Dix-Hallpike. Denial would be waving away the red flags; suppression is the opposite—you keep dysarthria and facial droop on the differential, then set them aside once the trigger is purely positional and hearing is intact.

2019-213.sentence: Adding low-dose aripiprazole after a maxed SSRI plus exposure is already an enactment: the two of you are repeating the OCD loop of “one more ritual might finally settle this,” only now the ritual is a dopamine partial agonist. Name that pull in the room so the pill stays an adjunct to ERP, not a shared search for a perfect undo.

2019-214.sentence: A haplotype is a block of alleles in linkage disequilibrium inherited as one unit, the same way a treatment frame travels as a package: fee, time, confidentiality, and reporting ride together, not as free SNPs you can swap. If you break the block—leak one limit and keep the rest—you no longer know which “variant” the patient actually received.

2019-215.sentence: The neural tube is folded ectoderm; folate is the ordinary “feed” that helps that sheet close, and its absence can feel to parents like a poison they gave or a proof they failed. Hold the pill and the prenatal vitamin as care, not as a verdict on whether they deserved a closed tube.

2019-216.sentence: A type 1 error is calling a true null false—declaring an ending that has not happened—so p = 0.05 is a rule about not rushing termination. You wait for enough time and enough N before you announce that relapse is gone; the clock, not hope, decides when the claim can stop.

2019-217.sentence: When the MRI is clean but PET shows reduced perfusion in the bilateral lateral temporal lobes, invite a trial comment: “You still know these jokes land wrong, even if you cannot stop them.” If they can see their own part, you are looking at remaining insight; if they only blame the spouse, frontotemporal change has already eaten psychological mindedness.

2019-218.sentence: Aspirin overdose with tinnitus and Kussmaul breathing is also a collapse of self-esteem: the pills were meant to quiet a self that felt unmirrored, not merely to “get high.” After the bicarbonate, name the competence hit—surviving the OD does not restore the mirroring they needed, so safety planning has to include who can actually see them.

2019-219.sentence: Derealization is the mind evacuating a raw panic so the room becomes a movie set instead of a place you have to inhabit. Containment here means you name the feeling—“the world went fake so the fear would not stay inside”—until that nameless dread can become a thinkable sentence.

2019-220.sentence: The Stroop Color Word Test is inhibition of an overlearned pull: say the ink color, not the word you automatically want. In the room the same skill is relational—you and the patient keep catching the old automatic reply instead of one person “having” the frontal deficit alone.

2019-221.sentence: Iron deficiency restless legs at night is a body that cannot use rest as a secure base; the legs protest the moment proximity to sleep (and to stillness) arrives. Check ferritin before a dopamine agonist, and notice whether nighttime agitation also spikes when the ward feels empty of a regulating other.

2019-222.sentence: Hippocampal neurogenesis is why the SSRI waits weeks: ego strength—affect tolerance, impulse control, the capacity to sit with change—grows as new cells come online, not when serotonin first rises. Tell the patient the delay is the hippocampus rebuilding a place to hold feeling, not proof the medicine “isn’t working.”

2019-223.sentence: Habituation is staying in the chair while the charge drains: the same stimulus hits again and the reaction gets smaller, so she does not have to leave her body to survive it. Dissociation is the other exit—a vertical split where she is still sitting there but the feeling is gone; exposure works only if she habituates instead of checking out.

2019-224.sentence: Female sex is the risk factor that belongs on the board for rapid cycling, and the cycle often becomes an enactment: staff and patient start living the swings instead of thinking them. Four episodes a year pull everyone into the same rush—dose change, crisis call, next polarity—so name the risk and stop acting the rhythm.

2019-225.sentence: Amniocentesis for chromosomal analysis is timed at 20 weeks, and the wait is often held by suppression: she knows the genetic risk and lithium question, and she parks the dread until the needle date. Denial would skip the calendar altogether; suppression keeps 20 weeks as a real appointment, not a fantasy that the genes will wait forever.

2019-226.sentence: Adjustment disorder is the commonest psychiatric diagnosis in cancer, and an antidepressant offered too fast can feel like a demand that she become a psychiatric patient instead of a person absorbing bad news. The pill is not feed here unless neurovegetative major depression is actually present; most of this is a relationship to the diagnosis, not a receptor gap.

2019-227.sentence: Antagonism at the nociceptin (orphanin FQ) receptor is the analgesic move, and it marks a limit: more mu-opioid is not the only ethical next step when pain has already swallowed the frame. Escalating opioids can become the treatment that never ends; naming nociceptin keeps a boundary between relief and an open-ended demand for more of the same.

2019-228.sentence: Consent after a serum draw still has to name who to contact for a research-related injury; that line is the study's conscience, not optional courtesy. Without a named person after bruise, infection, or worse, the protocol leaves a sanctioned gap: harm is admitted, duty is not.

2019-229.sentence: Federal 42 CFR Part 2 treats substance-use records as if the patient's capacity to seek help is still arriving and will collapse if the room is leaky. Extra confidentiality is the holding environment that lets a late-developing willingness to be known grow without being handed to a primary-care fax machine.

2019-230.sentence: Competency is decision-specific, and making financial decisions sits at the highest legal threshold because money is the object that most easily splits into all-good rescue and all-bad exploitation. The law asks whether the patient can hold both sides of that relationship long enough to choose, not merely whether they can sign a will or name a proxy.

2019-231.sentence: Alogia is thought emptied out: brief concrete replies and echoing the question put your words back in your lap instead of taking them in. In Kleinian terms that is evacuation, not conversation—the mind treats a question as a bad object to spit back rather than something that can be held, chewed, and answered.

2019-232.sentence: A five-year-old can go to her mother's funeral if a familiar person stays beside her; that companion is the attachment figure who keeps the goodbye from becoming abandonment. Shielding the body, seating her in the back, or making her perform the service all miss the point: she needs a known adult who can stay when grief arrives.

2019-233.sentence: AA's first move is identity work in Erikson's sense: recognizing that they are an alcoholic consolidates a self that can then use a sponsor, a meeting, or a chip. Belief in God and weekly attendance matter later; without that identity the rest is role-play around a drink that still belongs to 'everyone else.

2019-234.sentence: When overwhelm exceeds affect tolerance, the binge-vomit cycle does the regulating the ego cannot, and elevated serum amylase is the lab echo of that repeated purge. Impulse control failed first; the parotids just keep the score.

2019-235.sentence: Oppositional defiant disorder often lives in the attachment system: the child uses argument and annoyance to keep a parent close when a calm bid for a secure base—someone they can rest on and return to—has stopped working. The talking-back is proximity-seeking with a sharp edge, a protest that says “stay in the fight with me” because quiet cooperation feels like being dropped.

2019-236.sentence: CATIE-AD’s week-12 win was reduced suspiciousness, not a better life for the caregiver or the patient, so the family and you can start chasing a calmer dyad instead of a miracle pill. The suspicion is a two-person event: when the drug takes the edge off paranoia, the caregiver’s hovering and the patient’s counter-attack can loosen together, if you name that pattern instead of only titrating milligrams.

2019-237.sentence: Evoking is the process where you draw out the patient’s own reasons to change, not the process where you deliver yours—support first, then just enough uncovering of their ambivalence. If you skip evoking and jump to planning, you are doing advice in motivational interviewing clothes, and an ambivalent mind will push back harder.

2019-238.sentence: The nucleus accumbens is where the hit lands as dopamine, a bodily surge that stands in for a story the person cannot yet put into words. Use gets repeated in the body when the original ache stays unrepresented—felt as craving rather than remembered as loss—so the circuit fires the old scene instead of thinking it.

2019-239.sentence: Declarative memory, facts and episodes you can say out loud, needs an intact medial temporal lobe; the wish to keep a life story collides with a brain that will not file new chapters. The conflict shows up as a blank where recall should be: the mind still wants the memory, the prohibition is neurologic, and the symptom is the failed negotiation between those two.

2019-240.sentence: Content validity asks whether the items actually cover the thing named—here major depression—so a screen that skips sad mood and asks about spending sprees is evacuating the construct, dumping the wrong contents into the measure. Bion’s move is containment: hold the raw idea of depression long enough to turn it into thinkable items, instead of letting mania-flavored questions leak in because someone could not sit with the real target.

2019-241.sentence: The child's self is looking for a competent witness: a parent who only sees the 'good kid' at home cannot mirror the school self that is failing and frightened. Get the teacher's release first so you can name that split out loud, then the stomachaches stop being a mysterious body event and become a bid for someone to see him accurately.

2019-242.sentence: Supportive therapy is the trial comment you do not make: you build self-esteem and a more cohesive self instead of asking whether they can see their own part. Insight-oriented work needs psychological mindedness; this frame assumes they do not have it yet and treats esteem as the first holding environment.

2019-243.sentence: Korsakoff's mammillary and diencephalic lesions end the session the patient never got to finish: new memories will not form, so insight cannot catch up. You stop rushing interpretation; confabulation is the mind filling a hole that time and teaching will not close.

2019-244.sentence: You may feel recruited to be the grim realist who confirms that aging is only loss; that countertransference misses the finding. Sense of well-being often rises even as body and cognition fall, so notice if you are becoming the voice of decline instead of the person who can hold both facts.

2019-245.sentence: Chronic corticosteroids turn down AMPA signaling in hippocampus the way a harsh conscience turns down the capacity to take in new experience. Memory and mood then fail not from more guilt but from less glutamate transmission at those synapses, so the 'shoulds' of recovery outrun what the tissue can actually encode.

2019-246.sentence: The wish is that this is depression and a hint will bring the memory back; Alzheimer will not take the cue. The deficit that stays after hints or recognition is the collision: you wanted a recoverable mind, and the cortex will not grant it.

2019-247.sentence: When collateral is gone, the EEG is how you hear the unremembered: delirium writes a diffuse slow wave (or triphasic waves) that dementia at this stage usually does not. The body is repeating the metabolic insult the history cannot tell you.

2019-248.sentence: Elevated blood pressure is the risk factor that most reliably pushes amnestic MCI toward Alzheimer disease—vascular load eats the remaining ego reserve. Treat the hypertension as if it were affect tolerance: the brain that cannot buffer a pulse-pressure hit also cannot buffer the next forgetting.

2019-249.sentence: Meperidine plus sertraline (and buspirone) floods the synapse until the person is still in the chair but gone—diaphoresis, clonus, fever, hypertension. That is a chemical vertical split: the serotonergic storm evacuates the mind from the body that remains.

2019-250.sentence: Filing with CPS after a suicide attempt when the parent will not remove the guns trades on the parent's autonomy—the right to refuse your safety plan. You can still see your part: you used a trial comment about lethal means, they declined, and the report is the limit when insight stops.

2019-251.sentence: COMPASS nurse case managers named patient non-adherence and lack of motivation as the hardest wall—not the PCP, not the note. The frame is a collaborative-care huddle; if the depressed diabetic will not take the antidepressant or the statin, you hold the limit by naming the drop-out instead of blaming the clinic clock.

2019-252.sentence: The mother's guilt and promise is raw beta-stuff she dumped in your lap; you soothed instead of thinking, and you did not report. Containing here means turning the bruise into a mandated report so the child's dread can become thinkable—and so legal sanctions do not land on you for the unreported earlier abuse.

2019-253.sentence: Hyponatremia after an SSRI in an 84-year-old is a hard stop: confusion, headache, and an unsteady gait are not a request to wait another two weeks for the antidepressant to “kick in.” Time here is a capacity you cannot rush—the sodium has already changed the patient’s mental status, so you correct the lab before you interpret the mood.

2019-254.sentence: When the managed-care reviewer cuts the days and the unit discharges anyway, you are already in an enactment: two parties living the old pattern of “someone else is in charge” instead of naming who actually decides. The lawsuit still lands on the psychiatrist because the clinical duty was never transferable, even if the company wrote the denial.

2019-255.sentence: Loss of slow-wave (N3) sleep in a healthy 70-year-old is a vertical split in the night itself: the person is still in bed, but the deep, continuous layer of sleep has thinned away. Lighter sleep and more awakenings are the architecture leaving without the body leaving the chair—not a hypnotic deficiency you must fill.

2019-256.sentence: Low birth weight corrected for gestational age is not a metaphor; it is the earliest “feed” that most strongly predicts later ADHD, not schizophrenia or autism. The pill and the IEP later can feel like proof of need because the first ration of growth already marked a nervous system that would have trouble holding attention.

2019-257.sentence: Adding methylphenidate to stable lithium is suppression, not denial: you keep the mood medicine in place and treat the inattentive ADHD that is actually failing the readings. Switching to lamotrigine, valproate, or an atypical, or adding venlafaxine, would be undoing a year of euthymia to avoid the stimulant you are afraid of.

2019-258.sentence: Jerky, cogwheel pursuit of your slowly moving finger is a two-person finding: your hand sets the pace and the patient’s eyes cannot stay with you in a smooth glide. That broken chase points to Parkinson disease, not MS, Wernicke, PCP, or a benzo—the exam is the relationship making the sign visible.

2019-259.sentence: This mind already found a high-level way out: jealous rivalry with the gifted sibling got turned into martial-arts skill, which is sublimation, not a displacement that just dumps the anger on someone else. Do not interpret the sibling envy yet; support the dojo as the treatment, because this ten-year-old can use a channel more than an uncovering hour.

2019-260.sentence: Magnesium sits in the NMDA pore at rest and only leaves when the membrane depolarizes, so calcium cannot flood in until the cell is already awake. That is coincidence detection: the synapse learns only when two signals arrive together, the same developmental rule that says a child cannot take in a hard truth until the ego is already online.

2019-261.sentence: SSRIs, SNRIs, and nortriptyline nick platelet serotonin and raise GI bleed risk; mirtazapine does not, so it is the antidepressant this body can actually tolerate. Ego strength here is somatic: pick the drug that matches what the platelets can hold, not the one with the prettiest receptor story.

2019-262.sentence: Prenatal alcohol is the most common biological neurotoxin tied to intellectual disability, more than lead, mercury, diabetes, or radiation. The fetus has no defense and no exit, so the developmental task is prevention in the mother, not later repair of a brain that never got a sober first trimester.

2019-263.sentence: The family will try to pull you into counting stims, restricted interests, and age of onset as if those numbers were the future; that is an enactment, the two of you living the restricted-focus pattern instead of talking about function. Verbal ability at age five is the predictor of later adaptive outcome, so name language, not the rituals they keep handing you.

2019-264.sentence: The oven and carbon-monoxide checks are manic repair: a frantic undoing of the fantasy that the patient's own hate will kill the children. Exposure and response prevention asks the patient to sit in that Kleinian depressive worry, the fear of having harmed the loved ones, without the ritual that magically puts the family back together.
