2019-265.sentence: After a left-hemisphere stroke the weak right leg stays stiff and is swung out in a circumduction arc instead of being flexed through the step. The damaged limb is held as the bad object that cannot be taken back into the gait cycle, so the intact side does the relating and the paretic side is carried around it.

2019-266.sentence: Ablation of the suprachiasmatic nucleus in the hypothalamus shreds sleep-wake, cortisol, and temperature clocks; there is no insight that puts the oscillator back. Support the mind with light, meals, and a fixed schedule rather than trying to uncover why the patient is awake at 3 a.m.

2019-267.sentence: Routine T1, T2, and FLAIR look at isolated tissue and miss mild TBI; diffusion tensor imaging maps the white-matter tracts that let regions talk to each other. The injury is in the relationship between nodes, not in one photogenic bruise.

2019-268.sentence: By about 18 months the typical child starts simple word combinations; complete sentences and verb phrases are later work. You cannot terminate the single-word stage on a worried parent's timetable—the capacity arrives when it arrives.

2019-269.sentence: Parents bring nameless dread—is this a phase?—and need you to hold it until it becomes a thought. Core gender identity, the basic sense of being a boy or a girl, is typically in place by age three, so the feeling is already organized rather than something to evacuate as temporary.

2019-270.sentence: Duration of posttraumatic amnesia tracks later cognitive deficit better than the rollover story, the admission Glasgow Coma Scale, or even the lesion map. Use that clock to decide how much demand this mind can take and how much scaffolding it still needs.

2019-271.sentence: ALDH2-related flushing turns a sip of alcohol into a bad object in the body—heat, nausea, pounding heart—so it is harder to keep drink as a purely good soother. That concrete split helps explain why U.S. studies find the lowest one-year alcohol-use-disorder rates in Asian Americans, not a moral difference.

2019-272.sentence: The gag and palatal lift are CN X (vagus) deciding what may be taken in and what must be spat out. After a stroke that dulls that reflex, the mouth cannot do Klein’s repair work of safely swallowing the good and ejecting the toxic, so meals become something to choke on rather than take in.

2019-273.sentence: At three, the body has usually arrived at reciprocal pedaling on a tricycle; skipping, tandem gait, and a copied triangle have not. If that motor capacity never quite shows up, you are looking at a developmental delay in the child’s use of the body, not a later “won’t cooperate” story.

2019-274.sentence: Erikson’s first task, basic trust, is lived in the mother’s care of the infant, not in a lecture about bonding. The medial preoptic hypothalamus is the nucleus that organizes that caretaking drive; when it is offline in the postpartum, generativity toward the baby can stall into emptiness instead of tending.

2019-275.sentence: Therapeutic misconception is the wish that the protocol is still your personal doctor, deciding only for your good. Naming the trial’s real job—answering a research question, with drop-out allowed—protects consent from that rescue fantasy.

2019-276.sentence: Chronic zolpidem (or trazodone, diphenhydramine) is a night-by-night crutch; it does not grow the sleep-regulating capacity. CBT for insomnia is the treatment that leaves that capacity in place after the course ends, which is why long-term outcomes beat the pills.

2019-277.sentence: His conscience is prosecuting slowness as if it were a crime against competence. Name the finding plainly: healthy aging only stretches the time to learn; complete learning still happens, so the superego does not get to turn a slower hippocampus into a moral failure.

2019-278.sentence: The frame here is not a benzodiazepine handshake at 11 p.m.; first-line for restless legs is ropinirole, a dopamine agonist, even when the spouse is already naming depression. You hold the limit by treating the nocturnal urge and periodic limb jerks rather than handing clonazepam as a comfort object that papers over the diagnosis.

2019-279.sentence: She is offering the MMR shot as a poison-pill story: if a vaccine did this, someone can still be blamed and the child can still be saved by undoing a dose. The validated risk factor is advanced parental age, not vaccination, so the medicine you give is that harder feed—age and biology, not a toxin she can extract.

2019-280.sentence: Skipping insulin to shrink the body is a trauma logic that never gets words: the scale must change or the self disappears, so the pancreas becomes the scene of the repeat. That is psychological factors affecting other medical conditions, not factitious illness—she is not faking DKA; she is using type 1 diabetes as an unspoken weight-control ritual.

2019-281.sentence: Oxytocin is recruiting you, in the room, to be a quieter amygdala: less threat-scan, more approach, when the hour gets emotionally charged. If your countertransference is to stay hypervigilant, you are fighting the same circuit the peptide is trying to dampen.

2019-282.sentence: Leptin receptors in the hypothalamus are the body's competence signal: energy stores are seen, hunger can stand down, self-regulation holds. When olanzapine hijacks that hypothalamic set-point, the self loses a mirroring of satiety and experiences hunger as a collapse of control, not just extra pounds.

2019-283.sentence: Tyrosine hydroxylase is the checkpoint: the wish to make dopamine cannot outrun the enzyme that turns tyrosine into L-DOPA. That is why we give levodopa with carbidopa—we bypass the bottleneck instead of pouring more fuel into a locked gate.

2019-284.sentence: Skin conductance falling is the body finally letting go of sympathetic sweat—relaxation you cannot hurry by staring at the number. Biofeedback only works when the patient stops chasing the readout and lets the arousal settle in its own time.

2019-285.sentence: Carbon monoxide hits the globus pallidus, and the flapping limbs are raw motor discharge that never got held and named. After a CO suicide attempt, those asterixis-like movements are the brain evacuating what it cannot yet metabolize into thought.

2019-286.sentence: Quetiapine, lurasidone, and olanzapine-fluoxetine are the three monotherapies with real evidence—the frame is not “treat the sad mood,” it is “do not treat this as unipolar.” An SSRI or bupropion here is a boundary violation of diagnosis: you are treating the story you wished you heard.

2019-287.sentence: Huntington’s CAG repeats expand more when the father transmits them—anticipation is a fact the family has to look at, not a feeling to soothe away. A useful trial comment names that paternal instability so the worry can become a plan instead of a fog.

2019-288.sentence: GWAS scans the whole genome with no favorite gene in mind; it does not split the field into the “good” candidate you already love and the “bad” rest you ignore. Candidate-gene papers often keep one object idealized—GWAS is the method that lets the data be mixed and still true.

2019-289.sentence: A mind in severe postpartum depression, when allopregnanolone—the progesterone metabolite that allosterically boosts GABA-A—has fallen off a cliff, cannot use uncovering first. Restore the GABA-A signal with brexanolone or zuranolone, then interpret; support is not a consolation prize here, it is the indication.

2019-290.sentence: Startle myoclonus plus rapidly progressive dementia is the cortex announcing it can no longer bind experience: cytosolic vacuolation of neurons and glia with prion protein, the spongiform signature of Creutzfeldt-Jakob. The “self” is not fragmenting as a defense; the tissue that holds a self is being emptied.

2019-291.sentence: The field had lithium for acute mania and still could not hold it: a naturally occurring salt that cannot be patented was treated as waste to be evacuated rather than as a treatment to be thought. Containment here is institutional—someone has to metabolize the unglamorous, unownable drug into a formulary instead of dumping the nameless dread onto “the market.”

2019-292.sentence: An eight-year-old who sexualizes play and is seductive with peers is not showing curiosity or precocious puberty; the abuse that cannot be remembered is being repeated in the body and the schoolyard. Treat the sexualized behavior as an unrepresented state until a history of sexual abuse can be thought, not as a character label.

2019-293.sentence: The wish to be rid of crime and the prohibition against saying “we chose this” collided, and the compromise formation was policy: mandatory minimum sentences, not a rise in crime, drove the post-1990 incarceration surge. The symptom is legislative repetition—more time locked, less thinking about who we are punishing and why.

2019-294.sentence: Inhibited, comfort-refusing, affect-flat behavior in a recently adopted three-year-old is not a conscience problem and not autism until you have the missing piece: serious neglect, the DSM-5 requirement for reactive attachment disorder. Without a caregiver who answered distress, attachment did not form; you are seeing the absence of a bond, not a guilty withdrawal.

2019-295.sentence: Once a 15-month-old can treat you as a mind that is not theirs, they start recruiting you: you become the one who knows, soothes, or withholds. Notice what role you feel pulled into in the visit; that countertransference is early evidence that other-minds have arrived.

2019-296.sentence: The nagging is doing a job: it keeps the patient as the household superego so the partner never has to want the chore. Warm, specific praise after a completed dish pile is a positive reinforcer; it tries to make cleanliness belong to the partner instead of to the complaint.

2019-297.sentence: Asking for APOE testing is a bid to grow up into a known future, as if a lab could finish the developmental work of waiting. You have to say the hard limit: in a symptom-free 45-year-old, APOE e4 only shifts risk and has limited predictive value for Alzheimer disease.

2019-298.sentence: Attention regulation is a childhood capacity that often never quite arrives on time and then travels forward. A significant number of children with ADHD become adults with ADHD, so you still hunt the childhood timeline instead of treating adult restlessness as a new self.

2019-299.sentence: The request to call lung cancer pneumonia is a plea that you absorb the spouse’s panic so the patient’s ego does not have to. You keep two functions intact: you will not lie, and you tell the spouse only that the patient has not given permission to discuss the care.

2019-300.sentence: Needle exchange is harm reduction: it treats the syringe as a life-preserving tool while the person cannot yet use abstinence as a thought. The finding is doing work—fewer abscesses, HIV, and hepatitis—without demanding that the craving already have a story.

2020-1.sentence: Ask the parents what they notice in themselves when the three-year-old says “I’m a boy” with no wiggle room. If they can hear their own startle or pride without correcting the child, you have a trial comment they can actually use.

2020-2.sentence: Generativity has a clock: the 40-to-60-year-old either puts something into the next generation or the hour just empties. You cannot rush a 52-year-old into Erikson’s later integrity work; first they have to find a use that outlives the career.

2020-3.sentence: Taste arriving in the anterior insula is already a feeling before it is a fact. When food “tastes strange,” the raw gustatory hit has not been contained—held long enough to become a thinkable flavor instead of nameless dread in the mouth.

2020-4.sentence: Construct validity is the scale’s self-esteem: it needs a theory of depression and a story of how the parts hang together. Without that model, the instrument cannot be mirrored as “really measuring depression,” only as a pile of items that look sad.

2020-5.sentence: Olanzapine feeds a hungry drive for more (weight, glucose, triglycerides) while the medical superego says stop. Metformin is the compromise that lets the antipsychotic stay and still answers the prohibition against metabolic harm.

2020-6.sentence: IDEA is federal law: the right to a free appropriate public education is not a school’s mood or a district’s memory. When the school “forgets,” the unrepresented disability gets repeated as delay in the building instead of named as a mandate.

2020-7.sentence: Kohut’s point is that childhood narcissism is not a character flaw you should shame; it is the raw material of a cohesive self that needs mirroring—being seen as special without being crushed. If you feel irritated or morally superior toward a patient’s grandiosity, you are being recruited as the parent who withdrew admiration, and that countertransference will teach them that self-regard is dangerous.

2020-8.sentence: Acknowledging the patient’s frustrations is support, not uncovering: you name the affect so the frontal lobes can come back online. This mind cannot use interpretation while it is still in fight-or-flight, so you lower stimulation—no staring contest, no standing over them, no touch that can be read as a grab.

2020-9.sentence: The hospital, the car ride, even the smell of the lobby have become paired with the unconditioned nausea of chemo, so two people—the child and whoever is driving—now live inside a conditioned scene. You treat the pair: change cues, space visits, and name the automatic body reaction so the family does not turn the trip into a battle about “being difficult.”

2020-10.sentence: Elevated plasma homocysteine is a medical finding, not a metaphor for “too much self.” Support first: work up the stroke, treat the homocysteine, and do not interpret the event as unconscious punishment until the brain is stable enough to use insight.

2020-11.sentence: Beck’s CBT is not object-relations work; it is a two-person laboratory for the thought that feels like a fact. You sit with her catastrophic self-other picture and test it, so the “bad” thought can be held without splitting you into the only good object.

2020-12.sentence: The confirming test is lumbar puncture for idiopathic intracranial hypertension, not another scan of a “normal” brain you already have. If you skip the LP because the headache feels like drama, you have dumped the feared badness into her body instead of containing it—projective identification in the workup.

2020-13.sentence: Nine P-words and twelve animals is not a shy, undereducated, or “not trying” patient. Letter fluency is a frontal generator task; category fluency still uses a stored semantic list, so the drop on P-words is the dorsolateral executive engine failing, not a personality.

2020-14.sentence: Withdrawal and irritability after an AIDS diagnosis invite a trial comment about shame or not wanting to know. When memory fails, the LP is acellular, and T2 white-matter lesions fit progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, JC virus has stolen the apparatus for insight—you are talking to injured oligodendrocytes, not a closed mind.

2020-15.sentence: Pulsatile hypothalamic gonadotropin-releasing hormone is the starter pistol for puberty; a GnRH agonist like leuprolide holds that pulse. The ethical frame is who may pause a child’s body: the clinic and the parent take the limit, and you name that openly so the medicine is not experienced as a secret punishment.

2020-16.sentence: An equivocal multiple sleep latency test leaves the stimulant looking like a demand, a crutch, or a character judgment. Low cerebrospinal fluid orexin is the missing feed: the assay authorizes replacement of a peptide the lateral hypothalamus no longer makes, not a personality upgrade.

2020-17.sentence: Cortical atrophy lets the brain sag away from the skull and stretch the bridging veins; a shrug-off bump then shears them. The chronic subdural is a two-party product: an older brain that has pulled back, and a dyad that treated the fall as nothing.

2020-18.sentence: A fishbone (Ishikawa) diagram is a container for the team’s urge to hand you one villain. You are being recruited as judge or scapegoat; sorting causes into bones keeps the transference on the paper instead of in your chest.

2020-19.sentence: The cough is not a comment; it is an unrepresented scrap of old attack that she cannot remember as a story, so she repeats it in the room by turning you into the aggressor. Transference-focused psychotherapy names that live replay instead of arguing about the cough.

2020-20.sentence: Each online art buy is a tiny ego dodge: a mood lift arrives fast enough that he never has to tolerate the loneliness underneath. Operant conditioning just names the mechanism—the purchase is rewarded—so the work is to grow enough affect tolerance that he can wait out the urge.

2020-21.sentence: The orbitofrontal circuit is the brake pedal: it lets you feel the insult and still not strike or rant. When that circuit is out, hostility is not “who he is”; it is impulse with no delay.

2020-22.sentence: Collaborative care is a three-person system: the care manager keeps the primary-care clinician and the patient from quietly losing each other between visits. Without that tracking person, the “integration” is just two offices hoping the other one will call.

2020-23.sentence: Morning logic and afternoon rambling is the ego’s hold on reality slipping across hours, not a new personality. You compare the two exams because delirium is a fluctuating failure of organization, not a fixed deficit like a stable Mini-Mental score.

2020-24.sentence: Involuntary outpatient commitment is only a paper object unless assertive community treatment keeps showing up as a real relationship that can hold both the well and the ill parts of the patient. Without that team, the court order has no one to be the container, and the hospital becomes the only “good” object again.

2020-25.sentence: Persecution is projection: hostility that cannot be owned is thrown onto coworkers, then felt as coming back. Do not interpret the denied rage yet; that mind needs you to hold the danger as real first, then slowly ask what part of the threat might live inside.

2020-26.sentence: The family recruits you to ratify a story that the widower prefers solitude, so you will stop noticing the arthritis and the fall. Your countertransference job is to refuse that role and keep naming reduced mobility as the thing that actually emptied the social world.

2020-27.sentence: The cigarette smell plus a request for cessation papers is contemplation: conscience is awake, but the habit still wins the hour. If you lecture or prescribe on the spot, you become either a scolding superego or a shortcut that lets him skip the conflict.

2020-28.sentence: Benztropine plus an 84-year-old brain is anticholinergic toxicity, not a new psychosis: fever, dry mouth, tachycardia, restlessness, visual hallucinations. Age has thinned the buffer that once absorbed that drug’s load, so the body now speaks the overdose the history may not.

2020-29.sentence: Fetishistic disorder stays off the police blotter because the arousal is tied to an object, not a nonconsenting person. The object can hold the sexual charge so the person never has to approach a live other who might overwhelm, refuse, or reopen old trauma.

2020-30.sentence: Hourly mood swings, bingeing, shopping, and “you are the only one who listens” in the first ten minutes is already an enactment: you are being installed as the perfect rescuer while everyone else is trash. Name the idealization as data, not as proof you are special, or you will live the abandonment story instead of treating borderline personality disorder.

2020-31.sentence: Basilar migraine briefly hijacks the whole visual field (heat-shimmer, both eyes), then the brainstem—vertigo, dysarthria, bilateral acral and perioral tingling—before the occipital headache arrives. Perception leaves without the patient leaving the chair: the posterior circulation territory goes offline as a reversible split, not a stroke, tumor, or sinus infection.

2020-32.sentence: Painful monocular loss, red washout, a relative afferent pupillary defect, and a swollen disc that remits in six weeks is optic neuritis announcing a later life as multiple sclerosis. The first attack is a developmental first chapter, not a pill story: the eye recovers, the demyelinating career is what you prepare them for.

2020-33.sentence: Rushing from an Alzheimer label to a surrogate is denial: the team treats the diagnosis as if it already answered whether he can refuse repair of a displaced radius. Capacity is decision-specific; you still have to see whether he can hold the fracture, the operation, and the risk of saying no.

2020-34.sentence: Dysdiadochokinesia is a timing failure: agonist and antagonist cannot trade places fast enough, so palm-to-knee, dorsum-to-knee becomes clumsy, off-beat, and edge-on. That is cerebellum, not apraxia (lost how-to) or chorea (random dance); the maneuver shows he cannot preview the next half-beat.

2020-35.sentence: Prolonged NMDA opening lets calcium flood mitochondria until caspases fire and the neuron dies—excitotoxicity, the same idea behind memantine and behind damage from status or ischemia. The receptor is supposed to open briefly; when stimulation will not stop, the cell cannot hold that limit.

2020-36.sentence: After the parent's pancreatic death, postprandial fullness never becomes a thinkable sensation; it stays nameless dread of the same cancer. The scale evacuates the feeling into a number, and avoiding the annual exam refuses the one person who might actually contain it.

2020-37.sentence: The snap “you must really hate me” is projection: the patient’s own hostility toward you is too raw to own, so it is thrown onto you and experienced as your hatred. Name the mechanism quietly rather than arguing your innocence; defending yourself only confirms the projected picture.

2020-38.sentence: The child’s wish to attach still collides with a history of lost foster homes, so the drive is shut down instead of risked again. Reactive attachment disorder is that compromise: comfort-seeking and smiling are inhibited so another abandonment cannot land as hard.

2020-39.sentence: Fragile X (FMR1, maternal uncle with intellectual disability, macrocephaly, hand-flapping) limits how much this toddler can use a parent as a mirror for a coherent self. Gaze aversion and social pull-back are not only “behavior”; they starve the self of the reflected delight self psychology says a two-year-old needs.

2020-40.sentence: REM sleep behavior disorder is a failure of the nighttime motor brake (lost REM atonia), not a daytime wish to punch. Ego strength can still look fine by day while Parkinson disease is already leaking through dream enactment.

2020-41.sentence: Psychiatry’s high suicide rank can sit beside a vertical split: the part that treats despair stays at work, and the part that is despairing is not allowed in the same hour. Wellness talk has to reach the split, not only the colleague’s caseload.

2020-42.sentence: Capgras is a prediction error: the face is recognized, the expected warm familiarity does not arrive, so the mind concludes “impostor.” The couple is already in an enactment—the wife is treated as a double—before anyone names the missing emotional signal.

2020-43.sentence: The periaqueductal gray and parabrachial nucleus pipe peripheral pain straight into the amygdala, so nociception and terror share a wire. When he represses—shoves out of awareness—the fear that his pancreas is failing, that unfelt dread still rides the same PAG–parabrachial–amygdala loop and a dressing change feels like catastrophe.

2020-44.sentence: Focal epilepsy splits him into a usable self and a seizing, “bad” body-object; major depression is when the damaged object colonizes the whole relationship to himself. Keep both in the room—the man who still works and the temporal lobe that dumps him—so the bad object is not the only object.

2020-45.sentence: IDEA is a supportive, not an uncovering, intervention: eligibility needs intellectual disability plus failed academic progress, not a deeper interpretation of the child. Interpret less and scaffold more—IEP, concrete skills—because insight will not close that achievement gap.

2020-46.sentence: Resilience after a hip fracture is a two-person job: the widow and her people invent new routines together. You are half of that pair; your expectation that she can adapt is part of what successful aging actually is.

2020-47.sentence: An SNRI can sit as a steady secure base; a benzodiazepine plus weekend wine is borrowing a disappearing other to dampen worry. You stay the predictable person so she does not have to use GABA and alcohol for proximity.

2020-48.sentence: Caudate atrophy in Huntington disease evacuates irritability and chorea as raw, unthinkable bits—Bion’s beta elements, feelings that cannot yet be named. Containment is taking in that nameless dread of a dying striatum, turning it into words (this is HD, this is the caudate), and handing it back in a form he can think.

2020-49.sentence: Cocaine and other psychostimulants flood the mesolimbic dopamine tract, so the high briefly supplies the missing selfobject: an outside source that makes the self feel whole, competent, and worth looking at. The dollar bill then works like a cheap mirror—it promises that same surge of cohesion without anyone actually seeing you.

2020-50.sentence: After meds, ECT, and TMS have already failed between you two, vagus nerve stimulation is the adjunct that stays in the patient’s body when the pair of you cannot generate another hopeful trial. The implant becomes a third party in the room: a pacemaker of mood that keeps working on nights neither of you is there.

2020-51.sentence: In a competency eval you drop the usual promise of confidentiality, so this mind cannot use uncovering the way a patient can. Stay supportive and factual; if you invite free association here, you are doing therapy in a courtroom and the material will not be held.

2020-52.sentence: A left posterior cerebral artery clot splits the written word from the speaking self: she talks fluently, but reading and writing—the objects that hold language on the page—are gone. Speech still has a good object; print does not, so the pair of functions that should live together (alexia with agraphia) fall apart.

2020-53.sentence: A positive Romberg means the posterior columns have failed, so when the eyes close the body cannot feel where it is. Vision was the containing other; take that object away and the self sways like a mind that cannot hold itself without being looked at.

2020-54.sentence: Duty-hour reform hits the cultural third in training: the resident as endlessly available laborer versus the resident as a mind that needs sleep. High-quality studies show cognitive performance improved, which undercuts the old class story that staying later is how you become a real doctor.

2020-55.sentence: At thirty, contamination OCD has already stolen the intimacy-versus-isolation years: rituals keep people out so the self never has to risk being known. When washing no longer holds that bargain, the leftover affect is major depression—the most common comorbidity—not a second random illness.

2020-56.sentence: Label C, the insula tucked in the lateral sulcus under the opercula, is the cortex that turns gut, heartbeat, and disgust into “this is happening inside me.” Finding it on the scan is finding where a feeling becomes a self-state instead of just a number on a vital-sign sheet.

2020-57.sentence: Eight weeks of sertraline 200 mg already asked a second-trimester mother to wait; continuous suicidal ideation with a plan means that waiting capacity never arrived. ECT is the intervention that does not depend on a developmental skill she does not have yet, while the fetus is still growing.

2020-58.sentence: The risk sits in the disadvantaged neighborhood, not in the adolescent’s failure to “see their part.” A usable trial comment names the block first: it is hard to use insight when the street is already choosing the high-risk move.

2020-59.sentence: Naloxone education and kits are harm reduction: you hold the limit on dying even when the patient will not hold the limit on using. The ethical frame stays intact—you do not make abstinence the price of care.

2020-60.sentence: Dopamine cell bodies in the ventral tegmental area project to the nucleus accumbens and briefly idealize the self: the high feels like being seen and competent. Relapse is that mirroring collapsing the moment the drug wears off.

2020-61.sentence: Semantic memory is the shared encyclopedia—state capitals, what a hammer is for—not the private film of a life. When those facts stay while the personal story goes, the conflict is often between wanting a coherent self and the ego's need to drop lived episodes first.

2020-62.sentence: General systems theory starts here: a change in one member is already a change in the whole family. You cannot close the case by discharging the teen as the only patient while the rest of the system still needs his depression as the organ that holds the limit.

2020-63.sentence: Competency is a court finding after a judicial hearing, not a stamp you write so the family can seize the checkbook. Hold their urgency as nameless dread—raw panic that something terrible will happen unless you evacuate it—and return a capacity opinion instead of their wished-for verdict.

2020-64.sentence: Ketamine's rapid lift is NMDA antagonism, not another SSRI-style wait. Watch for manic repair: the wish to smash the bad depression instantly, without the slower work of keeping both hope and damage in view.

2020-65.sentence: Next-generation sequencing starts with genomic DNA fragmentation, not exome enrichment or the flow cell. You break the whole genome into pieces before anyone can read the child's story; the lab does with DNA what you cannot do with a person—shatter first, assemble meaning later.

2020-66.sentence: The FDA flags paradoxical dissociative-like states with sedative-hypnotics, including chronic benzodiazepines. Before you name a new trauma diagnosis, treat the unreality as something the drug can write into the body when the original fear still has no words.

2020-67.sentence: An NNT of 20 for lithium and suicide can recruit you as the one who is supposed to make death stop. The countertransference sting when the number is 20, not 2, is you meeting the limit of that job: you treat twenty people so one suicide does not happen, and you still sit with the twenty-five who died on lithium.

2020-68.sentence: HIPAA does not require encryption for patient email if you limit how much and what kind of information you send; that rule invites a vertical split, a leaving without leaving the chair, in which the inbox doctor and the office doctor stop being one person. Keep refills short and non-clinical so the treatment does not migrate into a channel where you are only half there.

2020-69.sentence: Starting neuropsychological testing with language refuses the enactment of skipping the word-finding trouble because the battery feels long. If you rearrange the order to soothe the room, the two of you are already living the old pattern of not naming what is failing.

2020-70.sentence: The diencephalon becomes the thalamus, and students will recruit you as that relay: the person who filters messy embryology into one clean nucleus. Watch the urge to oversimplify; if you only say thalamus and drop hypothalamus, you have become the soothing filter instead of the teacher.

2020-71.sentence: Depersonalization/derealization is an unrepresented state shown in the body: numbness, the robotic self, watching life from outside so nothing has to happen to a “me.” Do not argue them back into the body; name the distance so the state can start to have words rather than only a numb field.

2020-72.sentence: The male excess of ADHD and OCD at ages six to twelve tracks grey-matter loss in the basal ganglia going off-script. Inhibition and the ability to stop a ritual are capacities that should be arriving then, and here they arrive late or arrive wrong.

2020-73.sentence: Multiple sclerosis can knock out the white-matter circuits that usually hold grandiosity and spendthrift impulse in check, so the conscience goes offline without anyone choosing to be bad. Secondary mania here is not a moral holiday the patient granted themselves; it is a lesion-sanctioned gap in the brakes we casually call a superego.

2020-74.sentence: Splitting is the mind’s way of keeping two stories from talking; commissural fibers, especially the corpus callosum, are the anatomic refusal of that split. When those fibers fail, each hemisphere can live as if the other never happened—denial with a tract name.

2020-75.sentence: The intern keeps hunting infection while dyspnea, tachycardia, eosinophilia, and T-wave changes sit in the first weeks of a clozapine titration: that is an enactment, the two of you repeating the old story that the psychotic patient’s heart is not the real patient. A troponin is how you stop living that story and treat the myocarditis.

2020-76.sentence: The wish is to stay one person who knows her own life; the prohibition is against knowing what another self already lived. Extensive inability to recall personal information is the compromise—identity can shift only if memory takes the hit.

2020-77.sentence: Donepezil’s 2.5-point MMSE bump is the actual feed, not the rescue fantasy a significant p-value invites. Effect size tells you how much cognitive mothering the pill really offered once you scale that 2.5 by the scatter (SDs 1.5 and 1.0).

2020-78.sentence: The referring psychiatrist is not a secure base if they insist on a 100 mg clozapine start when 12.5–25 mg is the dose that respects hypotension and seizure risk. You use the supervising attending as the nearby adult who can hold both of you so you do not comply your way into a crash.

2020-79.sentence: An efficacy trial and a clinic hour are two different interpersonal fields: one is a purified dyad, the other is you and this patient with missed doses, comorbidity, and a real alliance. Effectiveness work keeps that two-person mess—real-world conditions—so the result can speak to the pair you actually treat.

2020-80.sentence: Adolescence is Erikson’s identity-versus-role-confusion stretch: the kid is trying to know whose feelings these even are. A daily diary in CBT psychoeducation is a scaffold for that task—he rates moods and triggers so the self becomes something he can observe, not just act.

2020-81.sentence: Elementary sensation lives in earlier cortex; the posterior parietal lobe is where touch becomes a known object—astereognosis is that assembly step gone. Developmentally, the mind has to bind pressure and edges into “key” or “coin”; without that region, the parts never become a whole.

2020-82.sentence: In a Kleinian frame the motor tic can be an evacuation: unbearable tension is thrown into blinking, shrugging, grimacing instead of being held as worry. Persistent motor tic disorder (no vocal tics, more than a year) still flares when he is tired or anxious—the paranoid-schizoid moment of “get it out of me”—and brief suppression is a thin depressive attempt to contain it.

2020-83.sentence: Migraine often splits the body into a good, livable self and a bad, attacking vessel. Thermal biofeedback—watching distal digit temperature and learning to raise it—lets her practice a warmer, dilated periphery instead of living only with the constricted, persecutory object.

2020-84.sentence: This eight-year-old can use support, not a deep uncovering campaign: clinginess and fear for the surviving parent are age-typical bereavement, not a warrant to hunt hidden guilt or attachment failure. Stay with the living parent’s availability and the child’s questions; interpret less, hold more, and treat new depression as a later problem if it actually appears.

2020-85.sentence: When someone asks for N-acetylcysteine instead of another dopamine blocker, they are recruiting you as a partner against residual schizophrenia, not handing you a solo mind to fix. The glutathione-and-inflammation story becomes a shared project: you two try to change the oxidative milieu together rather than you pushing receptor occupancy at them.

2020-86.sentence: Donepezil works because Alzheimer disease has already torn down nicotinic receptor sites and the remaining ones are shouting to stay attached to acetylcholine. That is attachment at the synapse: the brain is clinging to a thinning cholinergic secure base, and the drug is a prosthetic companion so the circuit does not protest the loss alone.

2020-87.sentence: Derealization is the ego stepping back from the room so the fuzzy white-noise world does not flood her. That is affect intolerance wearing a perceptual mask: she stays seated, but reality-testing of the environment goes dim so depression and anxiety do not have to be felt at full volume.

2020-88.sentence: Lean methodology maps the clinic flow and cuts waste the way dissociation maps a day and cuts the parts that hurt. The delays stay in the building, but the non-value-added steps get split off and discarded so the team can keep working without living inside the bottleneck.

2020-89.sentence: Pointing at the subgranular zone of the dentate gyrus is already an enactment: you and the resident are growing a new cell of knowledge in the same niche you are naming. The stem cells are not only in the hippocampus; the two of you are repeating a repair story—antidepressants, exercise, neurogenesis—instead of only talking about it.

2020-90.sentence: Gabapentin stacked on opioids is a developmental failure of brakes: the child's later-arriving capacity to stay awake and breathe under load never quite showed up in this combination. Cumulative CNS depression is the immature nervous system of the pair of drugs, still unable to titrate sedation the way a grown cortex would.

2020-91.sentence: The SICU's push for benzos is a sanctioned moral shortcut: if we can just quiet the thrashing, we do not have to feel the guilt of an intubated person whose mind is failing. Name the chemistry anyway—delirium here tracks acetylcholine deficit, so sedation that further wrecks ACh is not mercy, it is the team buying a clean conscience.

2020-92.sentence: The daughter is recruiting you to be the loyal child who locates the danger in a 'crazy' 72-year-old and never in the household. Your countertransference—relief that the MoCA is 26, irritation at the nurse, eagerness to medicate 'aggression'—is the pull to join that story instead of asking who is actually being hurt.

2020-93.sentence: After the MI, closeness that cannot be put into words still arrives in the body as an oxytocin surge at orgasm. That hormone is the unrepresented state made chemical: bonding happens even when the couple cannot yet remember or say what the near-death did to them.

2020-94.sentence: Post–Roux-en-Y, alcohol is no longer a manageable bad object; a couple of drinks become a life-threat, which is the paranoid-schizoid world where the split-off 'just a drink' actually can kill. Repair in the depressive position means holding both: she is not a monster for relapsing, and the anatomy now makes alcohol uniquely dangerous.

2020-95.sentence: The salience network—anterior insula and dorsal ACC—is the mind's bouncer: it tags which stimulus even counts as 'this matters.' Knock those cortices out and attention, memory, and decisions still have a room; nothing important is allowed through the door.

2020-96.sentence: Dropping the PHQ-2 cutoff from 3 to 2 is a generativity move: the clinic chooses to catch more real depression (sensitivity goes up) rather than protect its own neat numbers. Stagnation would be clinging to a stricter threshold so fewer false alarms bother the system, while more despair walks out unlabeled.

2020-97.sentence: fMRI is useful because the BOLD signal is a stand-in: more local blood flow means that patch of cortex is working harder, not that you have photographed a feeling. Choose it when the question is “where does the brain change its work,” and remember PET can track flow too but with a tracer, while MRS, CT, and EEG are answering different questions.

2020-98.sentence: Midlife often means using the partner as a secure base in a new way: you look again at who you lean on, not only at the job or the empty nest. Reappraising the marriage is typical attachment work—testing whether proximity still regulates you—rather than a sudden impulsive break or a required depression when the last child leaves.

2020-99.sentence: The family and the patient are no longer in the same story: they still expect the lively man they knew, while Huntington-related frontal-subcortical change has left him apathetic, sparse of speech, and unbothered. That mismatch is interpersonal, not a shared depressive duet—he denies low mood, so this is personality change due to another medical condition, not MDD or adjustment.

2020-100.sentence: Awareness of the situation is the function that makes the rest of a competence exam usable: if the person cannot grasp the predicament, MSE findings, a mild dementia label, or whether they can pay bills sit in a vacuum. You are checking whether they can hold the facts of their life in mind, not whether they keep a tidy house.

2020-101.sentence: BDNF at TrkB (tropomyosin receptor kinase B) is how a growth capacity actually arrives in tissue: synapses get built and kept, the way a developmental achievement has to land in a real pathway. Antidepressants and exercise get interesting here because they recruit that same TrkB line, not NMDA, 5-HT1A, or IGF-I as the primary BDNF door.

2020-102.sentence: Conservation of volume is a capacity that has usually arrived by ten and not by five: the child can hold “same juice” while the glass changes shape. Right-and-wrong talk, ball skills, and a self-centered story can show up earlier; this one marks the concrete-operational shift, not a cultural third in the room.

2020-103.sentence: This is latency: sexual drive quiets from about age six to puberty so the school-age child can work the Erikson task of industry versus inferiority, learning to do things well with teachers and peers. If you treat that child as if they were still in oedipal heat or already in adolescent identity crisis, you miss the actual job of this period.

2020-104.sentence: A dropping carbamazepine level after a few weeks is CYP3A4 autoinduction, the drug inducing and then being eaten by its own enzyme, not a secret refusal of the medicine. Read the number before you read the relationship; otherwise you will chase “nonadherence” while the dose simply needs to go up.

2020-105.sentence: Trisomy 21 gives three copies of APP, so the brain is flooded with amyloid precursor it cannot metabolize, much as a Kleinian mind is flooded when it cannot metabolize what has been put into it. Early Alzheimer change here is that extra gene dose, not a failure of the family’s wish to repair.

2020-106.sentence: You and this elderly man have been keeping valproate in the picture together while bone density quietly falls; the pair of you can miss the enzyme-linked bone loss until a fall makes it undeniable. Name valproate as the agent to avoid here so the regimen stops collaborating with further osteopenia.

2020-107.sentence: The tics are classic Tourette and barely distress him; the school failure is most often ADHD riding along, so you treat attention, not more uncovering of the movements. Insight into blinking and barking will not raise grades if working memory and impulse control are what the classroom actually needs.

2020-108.sentence: Bucharest showed type of placement—foster home versus remaining in the institution—was what moved IQ at eight years, not extra nutrition, enrichment drills, or psychotherapy bolted on later. Ego strength grows in a mind that has a person, not a ward; tutoring cannot retrofit what early institutional care never built.

2020-109.sentence: Primary insomnia is defined by sleep dissatisfaction, not by daytime sleepiness, snoring, or restless legs. She is using that complaint as a bid for proximity: the night failed as a secure base, so she asks another person to help regulate what she cannot settle alone.

2020-110.sentence: Dissociative amnesia erases autobiographical memory while implicit, working, and procedural skills stay online. Conscience can sanction that hole: the personal story becomes unthinkable after the assault, but riding the bus does not violate the same rule.

2020-111.sentence: Fluoxetine treats both the new major depression and the bulimia; bupropion is off the table because purging-related seizures make it unsafe. You are supporting a late-arriving capacity: holding hunger and mood without evacuating them.

2020-112.sentence: Slow refeeding is how you keep phosphorus from crashing as starved cells suddenly start working again. What cannot be remembered as famine gets repeated in the body as hypophosphatemia on day two.

2020-113.sentence: Histone acetylation loosens chromatin and is the best mark of how hard that stretch of DNA is being transcribed. Watch the pull to become the journal club's amplifier: you are being recruited to certify intensity, not to recite telomere length or methylation.

2020-114.sentence: Normal developmental regression is a transient return to earlier behaviors while overall maturation still holds. The newly trained three-year-old who wets after a sibling arrives is grabbing for the mirroring that just left the room.

2020-115.sentence: Alcohol hallucinosis is the wish for drink colliding with a body that will not tolerate it: the forbidden object returns as voices, not as another sip. Clear sensorium is the leftover ego—still oriented, still tracking you—so the conflict stays a hallucination instead of dissolving into delirium tremens.

2020-116.sentence: Validity is a hard stop: the test either measures depression or it measures something else, and no amount of extra clinic time can paper over that. Reliability only says the number is stable; it does not grant the instrument the right to name the thing it never captured.

2020-117.sentence: Fights, online bullying, and stealing the classmate’s phone are evacuations: raw rage is dumped into action so nobody has to think it. Conduct disorder, not ODD or a one-off IED burst, is the diagnosis when the uncontained feeling keeps becoming another victim instead of a thought.

2020-118.sentence: Dehydroepiandrosterone, mostly as DHEA-S, is the most abundant circulating steroid in women, which is why the bottle on the shelf can sound like a medical fact. Your job is to hold the frame: you counsel on physiology and evidence, not on the ad’s promise for mood and libido.

2020-119.sentence: Valproate blocks lamotrigine’s glucuronidation and roughly doubles the level, so you start and titrate at half dose whether or not the patient “feels fine.” Psychological mindedness here is noticing their part in the risk—new rash, flu-like prodrome—and using that trial comment before a Stevens–Johnson surprise writes the note for you.

2020-120.sentence: Evoked potentials ask whether the sensory pathway still fires while the left leg “cannot feel.” Intact potentials say the finding is doing psychic work—keeping a conflict out of words—rather than proving a lesion on EEG or MRI.

2020-121.sentence: A developmental capacity that should arrive in adolescence—being held by a continuous adult world—never quite arrives when historical trauma, disrupted kinship, and reservation-level resource gaps keep cutting the line. That is why American Indian and Alaska Native youth carry the highest U.S. suicide rate: the holding environment failed before the self could use it.

2020-122.sentence: Histone phosphorylation is the cell’s instant conscience: a phosphate mark that licenses early-response genes within minutes of a hit, not the slower compacting or silencing of other histone codes. Guilt works on that tempo too—an acute stressor flips transcription on before the rest of the chromatin has time to argue.

2020-123.sentence: When tuberomammillary histamine neurons go silent in REM, the daytime watchman who kept you oriented to “who I am to this person” clocks out. Dreaming then recruits you as anyone—classic transference weather—while muscle atonia keeps the plot from walking into the room.

2020-124.sentence: You are being asked to hold two objects that will not sit in one mind: the capacitated patient as a separate subject who may choose aid in dying (autonomy), and the doctor who must not become an instrument of her overdose (nonmaleficence). Empathy that collapses those two into one “good” position is a split, not a synthesis.

2020-125.sentence: Linkage analysis follows a single major-effect locus as it co-segregates through one pedigree—the chromosomal segment that travels with the illness the way a projected part travels through related minds. You are not surveying strangers (association mapping); you are watching what the family cannot metabolize and keeps handing down.

2020-126.sentence: The muscle membrane never quite acquired a stable hold on potassium; a carbohydrate load dumps K+ inside the fiber and the limb goes flaccid while face and speech stay spared. Acetazolamide is the developmental patch: it acidifies and reduces attack frequency in familial hypokalemic periodic paralysis, the father’s same channel failing in the daughter.

2020-127.sentence: This sits on identity versus role confusion: the child still has to assemble a self from many identifications, and two mothers or two fathers do not skip that work or hand them a finished sexual orientation. Decades of data land on absence of adverse psychological consequences, which is Erikson’s point in clinic language—trust, industry, and identity keep unfolding if the caregiving is decent, not if the couple is heterosexual.

2020-128.sentence: Alternative splicing is a posttranscriptional limit: the gene has already spoken, and only then does the cell decide which exons stay and which get cut. You cannot rush a single transcript into one protein; the same gene keeps yielding several products, which is why one schizophrenia candidate can look like several diseases.

2020-129.sentence: MicroRNA does not carry the message and does not splice it; it regulates gene expression, a quiet down-tune after the cell has already written something. Insight works the same way: a trial comment does not rewrite the DNA of the history—it just turns the volume of a pathway up or down enough that you can see your own part.

2020-130.sentence: Guns enter as a cultural third: politics, fear, and identity sit between you and the patient the moment you ask who has a firearm at home. Courts protected that question as freedom of speech, not as a malpractice shield or a license-scope trick, so the gag law does not get to decide what you may name in the room.

2020-131.sentence: Diazepam before the EEG is a chemical evacuation of anxiety, and the tracing answers with increased beta rhythms—fast, busy activity rather than slow repair. In Klein’s terms the patient is still in a rush to get rid of the bad feeling; the machine records the speed, not the depressive work of holding the agitation and looking at it.

2020-132.sentence: “I am worthless” is a core belief: the whole self is painted with one bad object, not a passing automatic thought about today’s incompetence. In object-relations language the patient is not describing a mood; they are living as if the harsh internal figure is the only true picture of who they are.

2020-133.sentence: Rivastigmine is the cholinesterase inhibitor that stays mostly unbound in serum and barely joins the CYP/warfarin pile—so you can start it without turning polypharmacy into a second disease. Support first: in Alzheimer dementia the ego is already taxed by memory loss, so pick the agent that does not add interaction chaos the patient cannot metabolically or psychologically metabolize.

2020-134.sentence: Sensate focusing bans breasts and genitals on purpose so the couple can make a new interpersonal sequence: touch as curiosity, not as a pass/fail exam of desire. The homework is two-person work—each partner’s anxiety and demand used to live in the other’s body; taking the goal off intercourse lets them feel that pattern instead of performing it.

2020-135.sentence: Cannabis is the substance most tightly linked to converting a first drug-related psychosis into schizophrenia—so “just the weed” is not a safe story for a 19-year-old. Attachment is the other variable: when the family is used as the only secure base, continued cannabis use pulls the adolescent away from that regulating other and into a mind that cannot reassemble after the break.

2020-136.sentence: IED outbursts are triggered by anger, erupt in seconds, and are grossly out of proportion—not planned, not substance-timed, not dementia theater. Ego strength fails at the affect-tolerance step: anger floods before impulse control or reality testing can say “this slight is not a war,” and remorse after the fact does not count as control during it.

2020-137.sentence: Thiamine deficiency hits the mammillary bodies—the Wernicke triad of confusion, ophthalmoplegia, and ataxia is the clinical fingerprint, so IV thiamine goes in before glucose. Dissociation here is neurologic, not defensive: the person is still in the chair, but mammillary damage splits memory from the present so they “leave” continuity without walking out.

2020-138.sentence: Healthy melatonin starts rising about two hours before sleep and peaks mid-sleep, which is why you time exogenous melatonin to that dim-light window in delayed sleep phase—not as a knockout pill at lights-out. Self-esteem in a delayed-phase patient often hangs on “I am broken at night”; teaching the actual curve restores a competence story: the clock can be nudged, it does not have to be conquered.

2020-139.sentence: Kandel’s point is that the wish to stay safe by avoiding and the prohibition on facing the feared cue keep rewriting gene expression until the circuit is the habit. Exposure is unlearning: you ask the same synapses that learned the neurotic pattern to change their gene expression again, not just swallow a pill and hope the old wiring goes quiet.

2020-140.sentence: Anosognosia after bilateral PCA strokes pulls you into a two-person scene: he cheerfully names dim lights and missing glasses while you keep naming the blindness he cannot own. That is an enactment—the two of you are living the deficit (he insists, you insist) instead of treating the denial as the neurologic finding it is.

2020-141.sentence: When the amygdala is out, fear and anger drop out of faces and voices while happiness and disgust stay readable—a vertical split, not a mood. The person is still in the chair, but the threat channel has left the room, so you stop expecting them to “just know” when someone is dangerous.

2020-142.sentence: A dorsolateral prefrontal circuit injury leaves conversation intact and furniture-assembly plans in pieces; the pill then becomes proof of need, or a demand that you fix the strategy they cannot hold. Prescribe for the circuit, and say out loud that the drug is not a substitute for the stepwise scaffolding their working memory no longer supplies.

2020-143.sentence: An RR of 1.0 is the statistic saying this factor has no association with disease risk—yet journal club still wants caffeine to be the villain. That is denial: the number is allowed to sit on the slide while the wish for a culprit does the talking.

2020-144.sentence: Chromosomal microarray finds unbalanced translocations and copy-number change; it does not catch a single-nucleotide point mutation, so the test you pick is already a joint decision about what kind of answer the family can use. You and the parents make the next pattern together: a first-line array, or a hunt for a point mutation that this chip will never see.

2020-145.sentence: Split treatment only works if you know how much uncovering this mind can use: you hold the supportive medical frame so the therapist can go deeper, or you both stay concrete if affect tolerance is thin. Regular contact with the therapist is the technique that keeps the two of you from becoming the good object and the bad pill-pusher.

2020-146.sentence: An internal locus of control is ego strength in plain clothes: the child can feel a feeling, choose a next move, and believe the move matters. That is better armor than MAOA levels or gender when the outside world is chaotic.

2020-147.sentence: Association analysis finds common variants that nudge bipolar risk a little; it does not hand you a yes-or-no inheritance test. That probabilistic answer is what lets you stay a secure base—someone he can use to regulate terror about his kids—instead of joining a fusion fantasy that genes are destiny.

2020-148.sentence: In Piaget’s preoperational period the puppet can stand for mother, which means mother now lives as a symbol, not only as a body in the room. That is the cognitive hinge that lets a child play loss and reunion instead of only living them.

2020-149.sentence: Tetrabenazine, a VMAT2 inhibitor that empties dopamine from vesicles, is the next somatic move when antipsychotics and clonidine or guanfacine have failed. For an adolescent, that is identity work by other means: you quiet the public tic so industry and a usable self-image can form.

2020-150.sentence: Two-word combinations at age two are a competence the child can show you: more milk, mommy go. Accurate mirroring means you name that milestone to the parent instead of inflating or collapsing the child’s language self.

2020-151.sentence: Voices arguing are two inner claims fighting out loud: one accuses, one defends, and the listener is the battlefield. Schneider heard that as drive conflict made public—the wish and the prohibition no longer stay inside as thought; they speak as other people.

2020-152.sentence: Sertraline is the limit you can hold: lowest breastmilk passage, best infant-safety data, so treatment and feeding can both continue. Ending the wait for a “perfectly risk-free” drug is the termination here—you start the safer SSRI instead of leaving mother and baby in untreated depression.

2020-153.sentence: The dentate gyrus is where raw input first lands in the hippocampal formation before it can be stored as a usable memory. Think of it as Bion’s container in tissue: dentate, cornu ammonis, and subiculum hold what the amygdala and mammillary bodies cannot turn into a thinkable trace.

2020-154.sentence: Verbal ability is the old conscience of the mind: vocabulary and verbal reasoning stay, even when timed recall and new encoding slip. The 85-year-old’s worry that slowness equals dementia is a harsh superego verdict; crystallized words are allowed to remain competent.

2020-155.sentence: Age 55 is midlife, not late old age: empty nest and menopause arrive as a developmental demand the self may not have words for. Completed suicide risk in women peaks here, when the next stage is required and the psyche still treats it as a private failure.

2020-156.sentence: “I’m being left out again” is an automatic thought: a flash cognition the moment the roommate walks out, not a core belief or an idea of reference. Trauma lives in that instant replay—what cannot be remembered as a whole story repeats as the same leaving, in the body of the session.

2020-157.sentence: The laughing is not a joke aimed at you, but amitriptyline is treating a disconnected affect-release circuit, so your job is not to play the audience who must laugh along or shut it down. Notice the pull to feel embarrassed or to over-soothe the family; that countertransference, the feeling you are being recruited into, is a clue that the affect is happening without a person behind it.

2020-158.sentence: Linezolid plus sertraline is the interaction: MAO-A blockade stacked on an SSRI, so the tremor, hyperreflexia, myoclonus, and fever are serotonin flooding, not a hidden wish to die. Do not treat the consult as a personality crisis first; hold the medical meaning of the symptom or you will keep talking about suicide while the syndrome worsens.

2020-159.sentence: The hippocampus fails first, so new days do not stick while old self-stories stay fluent; the family then becomes the external memory. That is a developmental injury in reverse: the person cannot lay down the next chapter, so relatives start living as the archive instead of as children.

2020-160.sentence: Neck pain plus gait change plus new incontinence is the body announcing cord compression before anyone has a story for it; MRI of the cervical spine is how you listen. Delay for x-rays or urodynamics repeats the unrepresented state: something urgent is happening that cannot yet be remembered as words, only as legs and bladder.

2020-161.sentence: A positive therapeutic alliance is the finding that actually tracks outcome, because the wish to be helped and the prohibition against needing anyone collide in the room. When the patient feels rushed, the protocol becomes the prohibition; you restore the work by naming the wish, not by stacking more worksheets.

2020-162.sentence: WAIS Vocabulary holds because old word-knowledge is a stored self, not a fresh performance, so it is the best hint of premorbid functioning after trauma. Use that score as a mirror of who he was, not as a verdict on who he is now, or you flatten his remaining self-esteem into a single deficit number.

2020-163.sentence: Parents often dump the wet sheets and the shame into you as raw panic—nameless dread, a feeling with no name yet—because they cannot think “this runs in families” without it meaning they failed. Your job is containment: you take that mess, metabolize it into one thinkable fact (family history of enuresis), and hand it back so the child is a bladder-and-genes kid, not a moral emergency.

2020-164.sentence: He wants testosterone replacement to repeal time; the body will not rush. Sex hormone-binding globulin rises with age and mops up free testosterone, so declining responsiveness is a real limit, not a demand you can fill by pouring more hormone into the hourglass.

2020-165.sentence: A trial comment—“the cigarettes, not the nicotine, were inducing CYP1A2 and keeping your clozapine level down”—tests whether he can see his own part: smoking as a relationship with the drug, not just a habit. If he can use that insight, the smoke-free floor’s sedation and sialorrhea become thinkable pharmacology instead of a mysterious poisoning.

2020-166.sentence: HIPAA’s Privacy Rule lets patients see the chart but carves out psychotherapy notes kept out of the general medical record—that is the frame holding the work. You, not the records clerk, hold that limit: process notes stay private so the room can stay a place to speak, not a place to be exhibited.

2020-167.sentence: The family wants a pill-equivalent: one intervention that will “fix him” and keep him out of placement. Multisystemic therapy is the opposite of that feed—it is a demand that home, school, peers, and court all change together, so the “medicine” is the whole system showing up, not a substance you swallow.

2020-168.sentence: He still knows the watch (use, meaning) but cannot find its name—anomia, not a split in the object itself. Good and bad stay together in the thing; what is lost is the word-bridge between you, so you hold both the intact knowledge and the missing label in the same relationship.

2020-169.sentence: Wanting one gene that “caused” schizophrenia is a paranoid-schizoid move: dump the whole illness into a single bad object you can name and fight. Genome-wide mapping’s real gift is the opposite—novel, unexpected loci—so you help her stay in depressive concern, repairing the wish for a culprit instead of pretending GWAS already found one.

2020-170.sentence: Leaving the store is not just negative reinforcement—escape that removes panic and thereby trains more escape. A harsh conscience also blesses the exit: “good patients never stay with terror,” so the relief feels morally earned and the exposure work never starts.

2020-171.sentence: Greater mortality in widowers often means a self-care capacity that lived in the marriage and never quite arrived as his own. Cooking, pills, and cardiology were her ego functions; when she dies, the developmental job of being a body without her is still unfinished.

2020-172.sentence: The housebound “anxiety” is doing work: it keeps him off stairs and curbs that progressive supranuclear palsy has made treacherous because vertical gaze and axial tone are failing. Treat the symptom as a crude safety signal around falls, not as a phobia that insight will talk away.

2020-173.sentence: Testamentary capacity sits on Erikson’s last task: integrity versus despair—can he still author what his life meant. Asking whether he can make a will is asking whether he can leave a coherent last word, not whether he can gift money or refuse a procedure.

2020-174.sentence: Linkage disequilibrium flatters the trainee’s competence: the SNP that lights up feels like the gene you “found.” Idealizing that marker as the cause is a self-esteem shortcut; the real variant is the neighbor traveling with it, and humility is the adult move.

2020-175.sentence: The kick is a drive leaking past the night's usual veto: aggression or motor wish hits the prohibition of sleep atonia, and the couple lives the collision in bed. Polysomnography is the only test that watches that fight in real time—REM without atonia versus periodic limb movements—so you see which wish won, not just that someone got kicked.

2020-176.sentence: Anxiety here is not a side note; it is the unremembered middle, the body-state that carries what depression cannot yet say. Call it a mediator: behavior therapy has to change that felt tension first, and only then does mood move, because the pathway runs through what was never represented as a thought.

2020-177.sentence: The parents are handing you a role: become the adult who hears a monster and a running commentary and calls it psychosis. That is countertransference recruitment—you are being pulled to join their alarm instead of naming the speech as ordinary preschool private talk during play.

2020-178.sentence: CPAP is already a two-person treatment: patient and machine sharing the night so the airway stays a reliable other. When sleepiness persists after a controlled AHI, adding FDA-approved modafinil is admitting the pair still cannot regulate arousal alone and needs a third party in the room.

2020-179.sentence: Starting carbamazepine without HLA-B*15:02 in a patient of Asian descent is asking them to trust a caregiver who has not first made the environment safe. The allele test is attachment work: you become a secure base by checking for Stevens-Johnson risk before you ask them to swallow the drug.

2020-180.sentence: Negligence is the frame breaking: you stop being the reasonably prudent physician that the treatment contract assumed you would be. Duty, harm, and cause can all be present, but this word names the dropped limit—the standard of care you were supposed to hold.

2020-181.sentence: Ghrelin from enteroendocrine cells in the stomach and proximal small intestine is the body’s hunger signal, so a meal—or a pill that changes appetite—can feel like a feed, a poison, or a demand depending on the relationship, not just on kcal. When hunger surges before meals and in fasting, you are watching a gut peptide ask to be taken in; the same request often lands on the consult as “prove you need me.”

2020-182.sentence: Low serum iron marks a higher risk that a high-potency antipsychotic will tip into neuroleptic malignant syndrome—rigidity, fever, autonomic storm—so the limit is biological, not a matter of trying harder. You stop the drug and support the body; NMS is the system saying this capacity cannot be rushed past its metabolic ceiling.

2020-183.sentence: Circumduction after a left-hemisphere stroke is the weak right leg swinging out in an arc because it cannot lift cleanly—insight starts when the patient can see that compensation, not just “walk better.” A trial comment names the outward swing as the body’s workaround; if they can use that observation, they are psychologically minded enough to own the hemiparesis instead of only fighting it.

2020-184.sentence: Neuropeptide Y made in the arcuate nucleus is the hypothalamus’s appetite-on switch; rapid weight gain on an antipsychotic can land as a blow to competence and self-esteem, not only as a lab value. Mirroring the patient’s sense of a hijacked body—then locating the drive in arcuate NPY—restores a bit of idealizable expertise without pretending the hunger is a character flaw.

2020-185.sentence: Cholinesterase inhibitors in Lewy body dementia often quiet behavioral disturbances—hallucinations, fluctuation, apathy—before you risk an antipsychotic the DLB brain cannot contain. You are doing Bion’s job in pharmacology: holding raw, unthinkable percepts until acetylcholine tone makes them nameable instead of evacuating them with a neuroleptic.

2020-186.sentence: Schizophrenia carries the greatest economic burden of chronic disability among mental disorders, out of proportion to incidence, because so much of the illness lives as unrepresented states—blank years, repeated admissions—rather than a story that can be remembered. The body and the system then repeat what cannot be symbolized: a third admission this year is the dyad enacting the unthinkable cost until an ACT slot holds it.

2020-187.sentence: REM atonia is the night-time brake on motor wish; in Lewy body dementia that brake fails, so dream aggression walks out as kicking, while waking dopamine circuits leak visual scenes the ego cannot own. Treat the syndrome as a failed inhibition, not a new personality, and you will not reach first for a neuroleptic that can crash this brain.

2020-188.sentence: A manic mind cannot use uncovering talk while the drive is still flooding; lithium needs one to three weeks before the ego can even sit still enough to think. Until that window, you hold sleep, safety, and labs, and you do not interpret the grandiosity as if insight were already available.

2020-189.sentence: A Caesarean can split the birth into a rescue that also feels like a theft: the baby is delivered, but the mother's body did not complete the work she imagined. That split between the good saved infant and the bad unused body is a real risk for postpartum depression even when she has never been depressed before.

2020-190.sentence: You cannot terminate cognitive deficit by insight; working memory has a ceiling that interpretation will not raise. Cognitive remediation trains attention first so later talk, jobs, and endings have a mind that can hold them.

2020-191.sentence: Three months of rising alcohol is evacuation: dumping raw despair into a bottle so it never becomes thinkable grief about the marriage. Name substance-induced depressive disorder first, because the container you have to dry out is the drinking, not a two-month major-depressive episode standing alone.

2020-192.sentence: ECT's frame is a brief, planned seizure; lithium can stretch that seizure past what the team can hold and add neurotoxicity. You stop or hold the lithium so the stimulus stays inside the limit you actually consented to, rather than improvising anticonvulsants after the fact.

2020-193.sentence: Arguing, mood lability, sexual fantasy, and questioning family beliefs are the adolescent's first trial comments on the self: they can see a part that is not the parent's. Preferring parents over peers suggests that capacity has not come online—they cannot yet use a thought about themselves that would let them leave the old dyad.

2020-194.sentence: The calm report of a dump is isolation of affect: the story arrives, the feeling stays locked in the next room. Confrontation is you naming that split out loud so the missing feeling can come back into the sentence.

2020-195.sentence: Each extra admission can land as proof that the self is failing, so the next prescription or refill may feel like a demand to be sick rather than a feed. Weight multiple psychiatric admissions as suicide risk, and ask what the last hospital stay meant to this person before you add another pill.

2020-196.sentence: The drop-the-baby image is a vertical split: she is in the chair and also watching a scene she cannot own as hers. Silent prayer and delayed holding are the reunion ritual—she waits until the dissociated thought has left so she can be a mother again, which is OCD, not a delusion that the thought is true.

2020-197.sentence: You and the patient can enact a frantic fact-hunt: you keep asking for three words and last week’s news, and they keep failing, as if the whole person were gone. Name the split out loud—hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus hold declarative memory (facts), while the bike-riding self is still in the room—so the pair stops living the ‘empty mind’ scene and starts testing two memory systems.

2020-198.sentence: “Let’s get this over with” is doing work: it shrinks a coerced, job-threatening hour into something he can finish before anyone sees him as the angry guy. Clarifying the purpose of the interview and setting a mutual agenda answers that function—it gives him a say—instead of proving his anger, waving termination, or punishing the protest.

2020-199.sentence: This interview sits on Erikson’s first task, trust versus mistrust: the paranoid patient is asking whether you are safe before any history can happen. Prefacing a symptom question with a normalizing statement (“a lot of people in the ED feel watched”) offers a small piece of trust without demanding eye contact or chumminess they cannot use.

2020-200.sentence: At three and a half she is in the middle of identification: she puts on mother’s shoes to try on being a girl the way mother is a girl. Social learning names the modeling; the inner move is “I become like the person I need,” not a lecture about chromosomes.

2020-201.sentence: A case-control study of clozapine agranulocytosis starts with people the pill has already marked as poisoned and looks backward for who got the wound. The design treats the drug as a suspected toxin in a relationship: you do not wait years for a rare catastrophe; you begin with the ones the medicine already harmed.

2020-202.sentence: Vygotsky’s zone of proximal development is the stretch just past what the infant can do alone, held by a parent who does not flood or abandon the task. Toys and novel situations belong there so learning stays a two-person reach, not a solo test the child cannot yet pass.

2020-203.sentence: The parents and the clinic are already in an enactment: they are living the old story that major depression is a teenage-girl problem, so a 10-year-old girl’s low mood gets shrugged off. Pre-puberty the rates match in boys and girls; the two-person script is what hides the illness, not the epidemiology.

2020-204.sentence: AMA guidance treats the chart as a hard limit: a portal note about changing sertraline is still the treatment, so it has to live in the medical record. Ending the fantasy of a private side-channel keeps time, dose, and responsibility inside the official frame instead of in a disappearing thread.

2020-205.sentence: Association analysis is the container: it holds common, small-effect alleles until a population frequency becomes thinkable instead of evacuating the question into linkage, which only hears large effects shouting across a pedigree. Nameless dread in the methods meeting is grabbing GWAS, sequencing, or chromosomal scans when the hypothesis is modest inherited variants, not rare Mendelian thunder.

2020-206.sentence: CATIE held the treatment frame against the market story: second-generation antipsychotics were no more effective than first-generation ones, so novelty is not a clinical limit you owe the family. The ethical job is to keep the fee and the hope from writing the prescription when effectiveness is a wash.

2020-207.sentence: MECP2 is the genome’s psychological mindedness: it reads methylation marks so the cell can see which genes to quiet. Without that epigenetic insight you get Rett—regression, lost purposeful hands, wringing—not a structural deletion like Williams or cri-du-chat.

2020-208.sentence: Monozygotic concordance of 80–92% in autism can be held in the depressive position: high heritability and a wish to care for this child sit in the same room. The paranoid-schizoid move splits it—either we wrecked the next pregnancy or genes make us innocent—and dumps the badness into the sibling-risk question.

2020-209.sentence: WHO mhGAP locates the usable good object in the non-specialist who can identify and treat, not in a distant psychiatrist-hospital that never arrives. Splitting care into “real doctors abroad” versus “nobody here” leaves millions without a relationship that can actually hold illness.

2020-210.sentence: The out-of-body rush is a vertical split: the person leaves without leaving the chair, but depersonalization does not diagnose panic disorder. What confirms it is fear of recurrent unexpected attacks—the mind staying terrified the split will happen again.

2020-211.sentence: Reliability is a mind that keeps giving the same answer; validity is whether that answer still tracks the real world. Ego strength here is reality testing: a depression scale that only repeats itself (test–retest, kappa, ICC, internal consistency) is a sturdy defense against noise, not a measure of the illness.

2020-212.sentence: The clenched jaw is suppression failing: the patient never quite lets the affect into awareness, so the masseter keeps firing. EMG does not read “skin tension” or alpha; it records the electrical potentials of that leftover clench so they can finally suppress it on purpose.

2020-213.sentence: The room is already in an enactment: staff freeze at “paternalism” while the delirious patient refuses the line, and everyone rehearses either abandonment or a power struggle. Beneficence is the principle that lets you treat the incapacity instead of acting out that fight.

2020-214.sentence: A hypo-responsive ventromedial prefrontal cortex is a weak brake; the amygdala story is incomplete if the top-down regulator is offline. Go support-first: stabilize and titrate exposure rather than uncovering trauma while that vmPFC circuit still cannot hold the affect.

2020-215.sentence: Prosody is how a voice holds the other person—warmth, warning, “we’re okay.” Impaired prosody in autism leaves good and bad objects poorly signaled in tone, so relatedness sounds flat or sing-song even when words and enunciation are intact.

2020-216.sentence: After Streptococcus, Sydenham chorea turns the child’s body into a moving target, so the parent cannot serve as a secure base or a regulator. The writhing and lability are not “bad attachment”; they are post-strep neurologic noise that hijacks proximity-seeking.

2020-217.sentence: She is not hiding a memory from you; the two of you keep rehearsing an implicit model—a summed, nonconscious expect-to-be-left script that never needed hippocampus-style remembering. Name the pattern between you instead of hunting for a childhood scene she cannot retrieve.
